note: Consolidated evidence sets. Each artifact merges the asks of every framework requirement the control discharges; required_by cites them.

artifacts.name: AI Policy
artifacts.description: The documented AI policy with its approval records signed by designated management, the sub-policies supporting it covering AI resources, impact assessments and system lifecycle, and the approved organisational policies and procedures governing AI.

artifacts.name: Context Analysis
artifacts.description: The documented analysis of external and internal issues relevant to the organisation's purpose and ability to achieve its intended outcomes, the worksheet capturing legal, regulatory, cultural, competitive and other factors, the document identifying the organisation's roles as provider, producer, customer, partner, subject or relevant authority, and the context documentation covering intended purposes.

artifacts.name: AI System Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory listing AI systems developed, provided or used by the organisation with their intended purpose and the technology employed.

artifacts.name: Interested Parties Register
artifacts.description: The register of interested parties including AI subjects, customers, regulators, employees and suppliers with their requirements; the records of consultations, surveys or meetings used to elicit those requirements; the mapping document linking them to management system outputs; and the stakeholder engagement and feedback log.

artifacts.name: Management System Framework
artifacts.description: The top-level manual or framework document describing the AI management system, its processes and their interactions; the process map showing risk, impact assessment, lifecycle, data, supplier and operation processes and their sequence; and the implementation plan with milestones, owners and continual-improvement cycles.

artifacts.name: Leadership Commitment Records
artifacts.description: The signed top-management statement of commitment to the management system, its policy and objectives; the minutes of executive meetings where performance, decisions and continual improvement are discussed; the log of internal communications by top management; and the budget and resource allocations provisioned for the system.

artifacts.name: Communication Plan
artifacts.description: The communication plan specifying what, when, with whom and how communications are made internally and externally; the schedule of recurring communications; and the examples of executed communications including newsletters, public posts and incident notices.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The schedule defining planned intervals for AI risk assessments and the triggers for significant changes, and the documented results of all executed assessments per cycle and per significant change.

artifacts.name: Operational Planning and Control
artifacts.description: The catalogue of operational processes with criteria, control points and ownership; the register of externally provided processes, products and services with their associated controls; the records of planned changes with reviews of the consequences of unintended ones; and the indicators and audit notes monitoring effectiveness of implemented controls with the corrective actions arising.

artifacts.name: AI System Requirements Records
artifacts.description: The documented requirements and specifications for new AI systems or material enhancements including their rationale, and the traceability matrix linking requirements to design, development, testing and deployment artifacts.

artifacts.name: Human Oversight Design
artifacts.description: The human oversight and human-AI configuration design, the approved policies and procedures supporting the human oversight processes, and the documented evidence demonstrating the outcome.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Accountability
artifacts.description: The responsibility matrix defining AI risk management roles, the AI impact assessment, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, the documented evidence demonstrating each governance outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing them within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

AAT-01.notes: 45 asks across 2 frameworks. ISO 42001 clauses 4-8 supply the management-system scaffolding; each clause is a distinct artifact an auditor samples separately, so they stay apart rather than collapsing into one AI governance pack.

artifacts.name: Responsible AI Use Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for the responsible use of AI systems including required approvals, cost and approved sourcing; the approval records evidencing that procedure was applied before using particular AI systems; and the documented objectives covering fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, reliability, safety and robustness.

artifacts.name: Human Oversight Plan
artifacts.description: The plan defining where and how meaningful human oversight is incorporated in the AI system lifecycle and the training records and instructions for personnel performing those oversight activities.

artifacts.name: Intended-Use Conformance Records
artifacts.description: The procedure ensuring AI system deployment and use align with the associated documentation including the required human oversight, the records of concerns communicated to internal personnel and third-party suppliers regarding impact or legal exposure, and the event logs and documentation demonstrating use as intended.

artifacts.name: Customer Responsibility Records
artifacts.description: The documented allocation of responsibility between the AI system provider and the customer, the records of customer expectations and needs captured during design and through contractual or general terms, and the information pack provided to customers identifying the risks of the products and services and the limits of their valid domains of use.

artifacts.name: AI Objectives Register
artifacts.description: The register of AI objectives at relevant functions and levels with measurability, requirements and monitoring frequency; the plan specifying what will be done, resources required, responsibility, completion dates and result-evaluation method; the dashboard tracking objective progress and measurement results; and the evidence of those objectives being communicated within the organisation.

artifacts.name: AI System Design Records
artifacts.description: The design documentation covering the machine learning approach, learning algorithm and model, training plan and data quality, and evaluation; and the final system architecture.

artifacts.name: Leadership Commitment Records
artifacts.description: The signed top-management statement of commitment to the management system, its policy and objectives; the minutes of executive meetings where performance, decisions and continual improvement are discussed; the log of internal communications by top management; and the budget and resource allocations provisioned for the system.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Measurement Records
artifacts.description: The defined AI risk metrics and measurement methodology, the test, evaluation, verification and validation plans, the validity and reliability demonstration with generalisability limitations documented, the documented risk tolerance statement with its approval records, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the AI impact assessment, the incident response plan with the incident or error register, the documented evidence demonstrating each mapping outcome, and the periodic review records.

AAT-04.notes: 36 asks across 2 frameworks. The responsible-use decision, the human oversight it depends on and the customer-facing responsibility split are three proofs; each ISO 42001 Annex A control here answers a different question and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Asset Management Policy
artifacts.description: The approved asset management policy with its classification scheme, the bring-your-own-device provisions, top management approval, version control and review records, and the evidence it was communicated. MAS TRM requires an information asset management policy with the classification scheme documented separately.

artifacts.name: Asset Inventory and Register
artifacts.description: The asset inventory register with ownership assignments, classification records and tracking procedures, the IT asset register with lifecycle tracking, and the software licence management records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement to maintain baseline configurations and inventories.

artifacts.name: Software Inventory and Currency Records
artifacts.description: The software inventory database with its review records, the licensed software documentation, the end-of-life software tracking, the supported software verification records, and the documented risk acceptance for unsupported software still in use.

artifacts.name: Software Bill of Materials
artifacts.description: The inventory of bespoke and custom software with the third-party components it incorporates and their versions, the composition analysis tool reports, and the procedure governing maintenance of the inventory on every release.

artifacts.name: Asset Criticality Assessment
artifacts.description: The documented methodology for assessing and classifying asset criticality, the criticality register with ratings and justifications, the differentiated protection plans mapped to each tier, the application criticality classification, and the data criticality analysis behind them.

artifacts.name: Critical ICT Services and Continuity Register
artifacts.description: The inventory of critical systems with owners and recovery tiers, the register of recovery objectives and dependencies, the ICT continuity plan for restoring services within them, the failover architecture diagram, the technical failover runbooks, and the most recent recovery test report showing objectives achieved.

artifacts.name: Legal and Regulatory Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The register of applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations with requirements mapped to controls, the obligations matrix naming owner, controls and evidence, the periodic compliance monitoring reports, the horizon scanning report on upcoming changes, the legal counsel advisory records, and the legal review of cryptographic use across jurisdictions.

artifacts.name: Off-Premises Asset Controls
artifacts.description: The policy governing use of assets outside organisational premises, the management authorisation records for off-site equipment, the checkout log with expected return, the travel security guidelines including country-specific advice, the off-site equipment insurance, and the loss or theft incident log with response actions.

artifacts.name: Media and Device Movement Controls
artifacts.description: The device and media control policy, the hardware and media tracking procedures, and the movement authorisation records governing physical relocation of assets.

artifacts.name: Asset Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The media disposal policy with the documented disposal method, the disposal tracking logs, the certificates of destruction, and the asset disposal and decommissioning procedures and records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented sanitisation requirement.

artifacts.name: Wireless Access Point Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of authorised wireless access points with location, identifier, hardware address and business justification, and the records evidencing the inventory is maintained and updated.

artifacts.name: Payment Device Inventory and Inspection
artifacts.description: The inventory of point-of-interaction devices with make, model, serial number, location and responsible person; the inspection procedure with cadence and methods; the periodic inspection records; the personnel training records on detecting tampering and substitution; and the investigation outcomes for reported tampering.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Employment Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy with least privilege requirements, the access review and recertification records, and the human resources security policy covering the employment lifecycle through which asset custody changes hands.

artifacts.name: Asset Management Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented information asset management artifacts held under the national regulator's regime, the evidence of compliance, and the regulator's own assessment records.

AST-01.notes: 76 asks across 12 frameworks. ISO 27001 A.5.31 (legal obligations) and A.5.30 (ICT continuity) arrive here alongside the asset inventory demands; both are kept separate because they are governed and evidenced independently of the asset register.

artifacts.name: Asset Register
artifacts.description: The master inventory of information assets with owner, classification, location, custodian and retention; the hardware and software asset inventory export listing all assets with tags and owners; the cloud resource inventory; the technology asset inventory and register with lifecycle tracking; the information asset inventory; the automated discovery scan output reconciled against the configuration database; the evidence of formal asset ownership assignments and acknowledgements; the inventory review and reconciliation log showing assets added, retired and verified; the asset inventory update logs; and the periodic inventory reconciliation reports.

artifacts.name: Asset to Service Dependency Map
artifacts.description: The asset-to-service mapping and relationship diagrams, the system interdependency documentation, the dependency analysis report for recovery planning, the map of business-function interdependencies, the documented workflow analysis identifying process dependencies, and the technology system dependency mapping.

artifacts.name: Service Catalogue and Service Levels
artifacts.description: The technology service catalogue documentation, the service level and operational level agreements, the service level performance monitoring reports, and the service agreement review records with their improvement actions.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The comprehensive business impact analysis report covering all business functions, the assessment and prioritisation of business functions and processes including their interdependencies, the business impact analysis documentation, the application criticality classification, the data criticality analysis report, and the business impact analysis for availability requirements.

artifacts.name: Critical Service Recovery Records
artifacts.description: The inventory of critical systems with owners and recovery tiers, the register of critical services with agreed recovery objectives and dependencies, the plan for restoring services within those objectives, the recovery plan reflecting critical system interdependencies, the technical failover runbooks for each critical system, the architecture diagram showing redundancy and failover paths, the most recent test report showing achievement of the objectives, and the records of contingency tests incorporating system interdependencies.

artifacts.name: Availability and Capacity Records
artifacts.description: The availability and capacity management plans, the capacity forecasting and planning documentation, the performance baseline measurements and monitoring reports, the architecture review reports identifying single points of failure, and the system redundancy architecture documentation.

artifacts.name: Asset Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The critical asset identification with its protection measures, the software licence management records and compliance reports, and the asset disposal and decommissioning procedures and records.

artifacts.name: Financial Close Dependency Records
artifacts.description: The financial close process documentation, the close calendar with its deadlines and dependencies, and the annual review and update evidence keeping the dependency mapping current.

AST-01.1.notes: 45 asks across 7 frameworks. The asset register, the service catalogue and the dependency map between them are three proofs; the dependency map is the one this control exists for and is kept apart from the inventory it draws on.

artifacts.name: User Information Pack
artifacts.description: The user documentation covering purpose, notification that the user is interacting with an AI system, how to interact with or override it, and the technical requirements; the documented criteria for what information is provided covering intended use, reasonably foreseeable misuse and user expertise; and the records validating user access to the information and its completeness, accuracy and currency.

artifacts.name: Adverse-Impact Reporting Channel
artifacts.description: The documented and operational reporting channel through which interested parties can report adverse impacts and the register of received reports with their status, investigation and resolution.

artifacts.name: Incident Communication Records
artifacts.description: The plan covering the types of incidents to communicate, the notification timeline, the authorities to notify and the required content; the templates for notifying users and other interested parties including for personal data breaches; and the records of communications executed under that plan.

artifacts.name: Reporting Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The register of reporting obligations to authorities, customers, regulators and other interested parties; the procedure addressing jurisdictional requirements for information shared with law enforcement authorities; and the examples of executed reports to those parties.

artifacts.name: AI Human Resources Register
artifacts.description: The register of human resources covering data scientists, human oversight roles, trustworthiness experts and researchers; the documented education, training and experience for personnel involved in AI activities; and the plan ensuring diverse expertise and inclusion of relevant demographic groups where the system design requires it.

artifacts.name: Asset Register and Ownership
artifacts.description: The master inventory of information assets with owner, classification, location, custodian and retention; the hardware and software asset inventory listing all assets with tags and owners; the cloud resource inventory; the automated discovery scan output reconciled against the configuration database; the evidence of formal asset ownership assignments and acknowledgements; and the periodic review log showing assets added, retired and verified.

artifacts.name: Programme Management Records
artifacts.description: The programme management methodology and standards documentation, the programme charters with their business cases and authorisation records, the programme plans with milestones, timelines and resource allocations, and the programme status reports with benefits realisation tracking.

artifacts.name: Stakeholder Communication Records
artifacts.description: The stakeholder communication strategy and plans, the board and management reporting packages, the governance reporting templates and dashboards, and the stakeholder satisfaction survey results.

artifacts.name: AI Stakeholder Governance Records
artifacts.description: The elicited system requirements with their socio-technical design decision records, the legal and regulatory requirements register mapping applicable AI laws, the documented evidence demonstrating the governance outcome, and the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate.

AST-01.2.notes: 32 asks across 4 frameworks. ISO 42001 Annex A supplies four distinct stakeholder-facing obligations — user documentation, adverse-impact reporting, incident communication and reporting to authorities — and each is kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Asset Management Policy and Inventory Maintenance Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved policy and the implementing procedure/work instruction that govern inventories: what must be inventoried, the required attributes, who maintains it, the update trigger and the review frequency. Must include the maintenance procedure applied on every software release, the asset tracking procedure, and - where relied on - the parent framework document (board-approved ISMS/cyber security management framework) that contains the inventory requirement. Related policies cross-mapped here (HR security policy covering the employment lifecycle, access control policy with least privilege, teleworking policy) should be supplied where the assessor scope includes them.

artifacts.name: Hardware and Technology Asset Register (CMDB Extract)
artifacts.description: The master inventory of technology assets - servers, workstations, network devices, security appliances, databases and middleware - with make, model, serial number, owner, custodian, location, classification, lifecycle status, and where required warranty and support contract data. Must be current, complete and at a granularity that supports accountability and reporting; several sources want it as a direct CMDB export rather than a hand-kept sheet, and want the baseline configuration reference alongside it.

artifacts.name: Software Inventory, SBOM and Licence Records
artifacts.description: Inventory of installed and authorized software with version and business justification, the software bill of materials for bespoke and custom applications listing incorporated third-party components and versions, software composition analysis tool output mapping those components to known vulnerabilities, and the licence entitlement records and compliance reporting proving installed counts are licensed.

artifacts.name: Automated Discovery Scan Reports and Tool Coverage Documentation
artifacts.description: Output from the asset and software discovery tooling, plus the tool's configuration and a statement of its coverage - which network ranges, cloud accounts and endpoint estates the tool actually sees, and what is out of its reach and therefore inventoried by other means. The point is to show the inventory is discovered, not just declared.

artifacts.name: Inventory Review, Reconciliation and Update Log
artifacts.description: Evidence the inventory is maintained on the defined cycle: review and reconciliation logs showing assets added, moved, retired and verified, the reviewer, the date, observations and corrective actions, plus the system update log for the register itself. Frequency is organization-defined in most sources but must be stated and met; NIST 800-53/800-171 want the defined frequency evidenced as well as the reviews performed against it. Access review and recertification records are cross-mapped here by NIS2.

artifacts.name: Asset Ownership and Accountability Records
artifacts.description: Formal assignment of an owner and custodian to every asset and dataset, with the acknowledgement showing the assignment was accepted - asset owner assignment records, the data owner register naming who is accountable for confidentiality, integrity and availability, and supporting role mandates, RACI, job descriptions or committee charters covering all inventoried items with a last-update date.

artifacts.name: Information and Data Asset Register with Classification
artifacts.description: The data-side inventory: information assets and datasets with owner, classification, location, retention and lifecycle status, supported by the classification policy that defines the levels, the data identification procedure, and where maintained a metadata repository or data catalogue export with business glossary and data dictionary. Data quality and metadata management reporting is required by COBIT and NDMO alongside the register.

artifacts.name: Specialized Asset Inventories (Cloud, Endpoint, Wireless, IoT/CPS, Payment Devices, AI, Non-Production)
artifacts.description: The inventories that sit outside the core CMDB but are demanded by name: cloud resource inventory from CSPM export; endpoint/unified-endpoint inventory; authorized wireless access points with location, SSID, MAC and business justification, and the SSID/key rotation procedure; IoT and cyber-physical system registers; point-of-interaction payment device inventory with make, model, serial, location and responsible person; AI system inventory with owner, risk tier and lifecycle status; authentication and authorization system inventory; non-production environment inventory; cabling register; teleworking and personally-owned device inventories with the approval workflow and the access controls applied. Supply only those in scope for the assessment.

artifacts.name: Asset-to-Service Mapping and Dependency Diagrams
artifacts.description: Documentation linking each business service or product to the underlying assets and systems that deliver it, including network mapping for IoT/OT devices - current, version-controlled, dated and approved, showing components, interconnections, trust zones and data flows.

artifacts.name: Unsupported and End-of-Life Software Tracking with Risk Acceptances
artifacts.description: Records showing every inventoried software product is checked for vendor support status: the supported-software verification records, the tracked list of end-of-life or unsupported products with planned removal or upgrade dates, and signed risk acceptances (with compensating controls and expiry) for anything still running unsupported.

artifacts.name: Asset Movement and Chain-of-Custody Records
artifacts.description: Logs of hardware and media movement into, within and out of the organization, recording the item, the date, the destination and the individual accountable at each step, with chain-of-custody documentation for transfers. Required by HIPAA specifically for hardware and electronic media holding ePHI.

artifacts.name: Asset Disposal and Decommissioning Procedure with Records
artifacts.description: The procedure covering retirement, secure disposal and destruction of hardware and media (paper and electronic), the retention rules applied before disposal, and the completed evidence - decommissioning records and destruction or secure-wipe certificates - reconciled back to the assets removed from the register.

artifacts.name: Physical Device Inspection and Tamper-Response Records
artifacts.description: For devices requiring physical inspection: the inspection procedure setting cadence and method, the completed periodic inspection records checking for tampering and substitution, training records for the personnel who perform them, and investigation records for any reported tampering with its outcome. PCI DSS sets the frequency from a targeted risk analysis for point-of-interaction devices; QCB requires annual inspection reporting for cabling.

artifacts.name: Critical Asset Prioritisation Methodology and Register
artifacts.description: The documented method for identifying which inventoried assets are critical (criteria, weighting, risk tiering) and the resulting critical asset register with owner, CIA rating, location and the additional protection measures applied. Where AI systems are in scope, include the approved risk tolerance statement with its approval record.

artifacts.name: Inventory Awareness and Independent Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Evidence personnel were informed of the inventory obligations (awareness communications with attendee list, dates, content reference and completion status), plus independent checks on inventory accuracy - internal or regulator-led audit and compliance assessment records, including random site audits where remote working sites are in scope, with findings and remediation tracking.

AST-02.notes: 126 manual entries across 22 sources collapsed to 15 artifacts. No automated collectors are mapped, but most inventory artifacts are tool exports in practice, hence the hybrid marks. NIS2 Article 21(2)(i) and ADHICS AC 3.2 (teleworking) are loose cross-maps - their HR/access-control and teleworking items are kept under the policy and specialized-inventory artifacts rather than dropped.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Database
artifacts.description: The configuration management database with its documentation, the database extract with full asset details, the extract showing current system configurations, the system component inventory, the database records, the inventory of network devices, servers and workstations, the configuration baselines and controlled configuration item records, and the configuration status and change tracking reports.

artifacts.name: Asset Register
artifacts.description: The comprehensive asset register with make, model, serial number, owner, location, warranty and support contract details; the hardware and software asset registers; the asset inventory register with classification; the information asset inventory; the software inventory database; the licensed software documentation; and the asset-to-service mapping and relationship diagrams. HITRUST requires the approved inventory of assets policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Asset Discovery and Reconciliation
artifacts.description: The automated discovery reports, the software inventory tool configuration with its coverage documentation, the discovery scan report reconciled against the asset register, the periodic inventory reconciliation reports, the log of updates to the register covering additions, retirements and moves, the asset inventory update logs, the inventory review and update records, and the software inventory review records.

artifacts.name: Configuration Documentation Repository
artifacts.description: The documented configurations and settings for operating systems, software, databases and servers stored in a version-controlled repository; the standard defining required configuration documentation contents and format; and the change records evidencing the documentation is updated when configurations change.

artifacts.name: Configuration Baselines
artifacts.description: The policy defining configuration standards, baselines and change controls; the baseline configurations for each platform in use; the documentation of approved golden images for servers and workstations; the infrastructure-as-code repositories enforcing configuration consistency; the compliance scan results against the baselines; the alert configuration for drift with examples detected and remediated; the sign-off records for systems before production deployment confirming the baseline was applied; and the configuration audit and verification reports.

artifacts.name: Media Movement Records
artifacts.description: The hardware and media movement log, the chain of custody documentation, and the responsible person tracking records covering assets that leave their recorded location.

artifacts.name: Governance Framework Records
artifacts.description: The technology management framework documentation and policies, the organisational structure charts with technology roles and responsibilities, the responsibility matrices for technology processes, the capability maturity assessments with their improvement plans, the board and management reporting packages, the governance reporting templates and dashboards, the stakeholder communication strategy and plans, and the stakeholder satisfaction survey results.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the asset inventory requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

AST-02.9.notes: 50 asks across 9 frameworks. The asset register, the discovery that reconciles it and the configuration records the database holds are three proofs; COBIT's governance and management-framework asks arrive through an adjacent crosswalk and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Asset Owner Assignment Records
artifacts.description: The formal assignment of an owner to each asset with the owner's acknowledgement, the owner and custodian assignment evidence, the shared resource ownership documentation where a single owner is not possible, and the owner-defined control requirements they are accountable for. ADHICS requires the owner to define the control requirements and to review their adequacy periodically.

artifacts.name: Information Asset Register
artifacts.description: The master inventory of information assets with owner, classification, location, custodian and retention, the hardware and software asset inventory, the cloud resource inventory, the configuration database with its required fields, and the asset tracking procedures.

artifacts.name: Asset Discovery and Reconciliation Records
artifacts.description: The automated discovery scan output reconciled against the inventory, the periodic review log showing assets added, retired and verified, and the inventory update procedures that keep the register current.

artifacts.name: Asset Classification Records
artifacts.description: The classification assigned to each asset with the classification records and the register linking classification to the handling requirements it triggers.

artifacts.name: Access Authorisation by Asset Owner
artifacts.description: The access authorisation records showing the asset owner approved each grant, evidencing ownership carries decision rights rather than only a name in a register.

artifacts.name: Media and Hardware Movement Records
artifacts.description: The hardware and media movement log, the chain of custody documentation, and the records tracking the person responsible for each item as it moves.

artifacts.name: Data Stewardship Records
artifacts.description: The documented business data executive, IT data steward and metadata stewardship coverage specifications with their compliance evidence, the master and reference data categorisation with golden-record definitions, the data architecture artifacts, the metadata repository export, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Vendor Default Account Remediation
artifacts.description: The inventory of vendor default accounts across in-scope components with their status, the documented procedure for discovering and remediating them on new deployments, the evidence confirming default credentials were changed, and the configuration evidence showing unused default accounts removed or disabled.

artifacts.name: System Hardening Baseline Records
artifacts.description: The baseline configuration showing unnecessary services and functions removed or disabled, the service inventory per component showing only necessary services enabled, and the sample command output confirming removal or disablement.

artifacts.name: Insecure Service Justification Register
artifacts.description: The register of insecure services, protocols or daemons still in use with the business justification, the compensating security features configured for each, and the signed management risk-acceptance records for their retention.

artifacts.name: Post-Change Inventory Update Records
artifacts.description: The documented definition of a significant change, the sample completed assessment for a recent change, the updated diagrams, scope documentation and inventories following it, and the records confirming applicable requirements remain in place on new or changed systems.

artifacts.name: Acquisition and Vendor Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The acquisition documentation, the security requirements written into contracts, and the vendor security assessment results for assets brought in from outside.

artifacts.name: IT Governance Structure Records
artifacts.description: The IT management framework documentation and policies, the organisational structure charts with IT roles, the RACI matrices for IT processes, and the capability maturity assessments that place asset ownership within the governance structure.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of their asset ownership obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

AST-03.notes: 78 asks across 12 frameworks. PCI DSS 2.2 pulls in system hardening evidence that is adjacent rather than about ownership; it is kept as its own artifact so the ownership evidence stays clean.

artifacts.name: Asset Ownership Register
artifacts.description: The asset ownership register, the evidence of formal asset ownership assignments and acknowledgements, the owner and custodian assignment evidence, the shared resource ownership documentation, and the responsible person tracking records. HITRUST requires the approved ownership of assets policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Owner-Defined Control Requirements
artifacts.description: The owner-defined control requirements documentation, the access authorisation records granted by the asset owner, and the periodic control adequacy review records confirming those requirements still fit.

artifacts.name: Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: The master inventory of information assets with owner, classification, location, custodian and retention; the hardware and software asset inventory listing all assets with tags and owners; the cloud resource inventory; the configuration management database records with its columns; the system component inventory; the asset inventory register with classification; the automated discovery scan output reconciled against the database; and the periodic review log showing assets added, retired and verified.

artifacts.name: Asset Movement Records
artifacts.description: The hardware and media movement log and the chain of custody documentation covering assets whose custodian changes.

artifacts.name: Governance Framework Records
artifacts.description: The technology management framework documentation and policies, the organisational structure charts with technology roles and responsibilities, the responsibility matrices for technology processes, the capability maturity assessments with their improvement plans, the board and management reporting packages, the governance reporting templates and dashboards, the stakeholder communication strategy and plans, and the stakeholder satisfaction survey results.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the asset ownership obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

AST-03.1.notes: 33 asks across 7 frameworks. Overlaps AST-02.9; what is distinct here is the ownership record — the named owner, the controls that owner has specified, and the review confirming those controls are still adequate.

artifacts.name: Network Architecture Diagram
artifacts.description: Current-state network diagram showing security zones, trust boundaries, segmentation and every connection between the protected environment and other networks (corporate, partner, internet, wireless). PCI DSS scopes this to connections into and out of the CDE; HITRUST additionally expects firewalls and trust zones to be identifiable; QCB expects both high-level and low-level design diagrams.

artifacts.name: Data Flow Diagram
artifacts.description: Diagram tracing every ingress, processing point, storage location and transmission path for the data in scope, together with the inventory of transmission channels and storage locations it references. PCI DSS scopes this to account data (PAN/SAD); CIS CSC and CSA CCM extend it to service-provider and cloud data flows; SOC 2 expects information flows for critical processes.

artifacts.name: Diagram Currency and Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the diagrams reflect the environment as it is now: the update log showing refresh after every significant change, the periodic review records naming reviewer and date, and the corrective actions raised. PCI DSS and QCB tie updates to change events; QCB additionally requires a quarterly review cadence; NDMO requires reviewer, date and corrective action to be recorded.

artifacts.name: Asset and Network Component Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory the diagrams are drawn from: hardware, software and cloud assets with owner, classification, location and custodian, network component and cable registers, and the reconciliation log showing assets added, retired and verified against discovery scan output.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy and Hardening Standards
artifacts.description: The approved network security policy covering architecture, controls and operations, the implementing procedure or work instruction, and the device hardening standards applied to routers, switches, firewalls and wireless access points.

artifacts.name: Firewall and IDS/IPS Configuration and Review Records
artifacts.description: Firewall rule base export (source, destination, port, service, description) with the periodic ruleset review records showing justification and cleanup actions, plus IDS/IPS rule configuration and sample alerts investigated. HITRUST expects device configuration baselines alongside the ruleset review.

artifacts.name: Wireless Network Documentation and Configuration
artifacts.description: Documentation of all wireless networks with physical placement, SSIDs, encryption and whether they connect to the protected environment, together with the security configuration (WPA3/Enterprise, rogue AP detection, guest isolation).

artifacts.name: Data Architecture, Model and Governance Documentation
artifacts.description: Current-state and target-state data architecture with data models and ERDs, the data governance framework and classification/metadata documentation, data quality reports and metrics, retention schedules and the master/reference data register with golden-record definitions. NDMO requires each of its architecture specifications to be evidenced as a documented artifact plus implementation records.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing, Integration and Interface Documentation
artifacts.description: Data sharing agreements, interoperability standards and integration/API documentation, together with the interface inventory, interface monitoring and completion logs, reconciliation reports for transferred data and records of interface failure investigation and resolution.

artifacts.name: System Security Plan and Acquisition Documentation
artifacts.description: The System Security Plan with its approval, review and update records, plus the acquisition documentation, security requirements written into contracts and the vendor security assessment results that support it.

artifacts.name: Resilience and Redundancy Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: System redundancy architecture documentation and the architecture review reports identifying single points of failure, together with the crisis-time documentation pack and disaster-recovery plan describing assets, data and flows.

artifacts.name: Internet Banking Environment Description
artifacts.description: Documented description of the internet-banking business and technology environment (channels, products, customer segments, transaction volumes, geography), the current-state IB architecture diagram, the register of physical and logical locations where customer information is held, and the inventory of security measures deployed in its support.

artifacts.name: Standard Operating Procedures Library
artifacts.description: The central SOP library with procedure dissemination evidence, review and update logs, and the updated system diagrams that accompany each procedure set.

AST-04.notes: 115 asks across 15 frameworks. Three distinct diagram families are conflated in the raw list: network topology (PCI DSS, ISO 27001, HITRUST, ADHICS), data flow (PCI DSS 1.2.4, CIS CSC, CSA CCM, SBP ETGRMF) and data architecture/modelling (NDMO, COBIT). They are kept apart because an assessor asks for them separately.

artifacts.name: Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy
artifacts.description: The policy with its requirements, timing rules and enforcement mechanisms, the clean desk policy, the annual review records, the signed acknowledgements, and the awareness material, posters and signage supporting it. HITRUST requires the approved policy document and its annual review as separate artifacts.

artifacts.name: Screen Lock Configuration
artifacts.description: The group policy or device management configuration enforcing auto-lock and screen timeout, the auto-lock and screen-saver configuration evidence, and the workstation locking enforcement records.

artifacts.name: Clear Desk Compliance Audit Records
artifacts.description: The results of periodic walkthrough audits showing compliance rate and findings, the clear desk audit records, and the compliance audit records covering the same practice in areas holding sensitive information.

artifacts.name: Physical Storage and Disposal Provision
artifacts.description: The evidence that all staff have access to lockable drawers or cabinets, the map showing confidential waste bin placement throughout facilities, the privacy screen deployment, and the hardcopy shredding records with shredder logs.

artifacts.name: Off-Premises Asset Controls
artifacts.description: The policy governing use of assets outside organisational premises, the management authorisation records for off-site use, the checkout log with expected return, the travel security guidelines including country-specific advice, the off-site equipment insurance, and the loss or theft incident log with response actions. HITRUST requires the approved standard for security of equipment off-premises with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The endpoint security policy covering configuration, encryption, malware protection and remote wipe; the hardening baseline applied; the disk encryption coverage report; the endpoint detection and response deployment evidence; the device management enrolment report against workforce count; the mobile device compliance policies covering passcode, jailbreak detection and application restrictions; and the log of remote wipe actions on lost or stolen devices.

artifacts.name: Equipment Transport and Protection Records
artifacts.description: The equipment security procedures, the physical protection measures, the transportation security controls, and the work area security procedures covering equipment in transit and in use.

artifacts.name: Payment Device Inspection Records
artifacts.description: The inventory of point-of-interaction devices with make, model, serial number, location and responsible person; the inspection procedure with cadence and methods; the periodic inspection records; the personnel training records on detecting tampering and substitution; and the investigation outcomes for reported tampering.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Area Handling Controls
artifacts.description: The documented access criteria for areas holding sensitive information, the orientation records for personnel working there, the unattended-information detection controls, the print and share privilege restrictions with local-printer-only configuration, the cleaning staff access monitoring, the professional licence verification records, and the breach notification procedure to the regulator.

artifacts.name: User Responsibilities Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented user responsibilities for unattended equipment and the awareness training materials communicating them, with the surveillance and physical access records covering the areas where equipment is left.

AST-06.notes: 67 asks across 6 frameworks. Clear desk (physical), screen lock (technical) and off-premises equipment (custody) are three distinct ISO 27001 controls that all land here and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Equipment Disposal Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for secure disposal, reuse and destruction of equipment including interim storage, the media disposal policy, the disposal method documentation, and the approved standard for secure disposal or re-use with its implementing procedure. NIST 800-171 and CSA CCM accept configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Asset Retirement Workflow Records
artifacts.description: The asset management workflow showing retirement steps and approvals, the hardware decommissioning procedures, the disposal tracking logs, and the technology refresh policy and roadmap driving retirement.

artifacts.name: Data Sanitisation Records
artifacts.description: The records showing the sanitisation method used per device — overwrite, degauss or physical destruction — the sanitisation checklists, the wiping tool configuration and execution logs, the degausser usage logs, and the sanitisation records for faulty media that could not be wiped normally.

artifacts.name: Destruction Certificates
artifacts.description: The certificates of destruction from internal destruction or a disposal vendor with chain of custody, the physical destruction certificates, and the disposal records tying each retired asset to its certificate.

artifacts.name: Sanitisation Verification Records
artifacts.description: The pre-disposal verification records, the verification of non-recoverability, the wiping and destruction verification evidence, and the disposal verification confirming sanitisation completed before the asset left custody.

artifacts.name: Reuse Approval Records
artifacts.description: The records approving internal reuse after wipe with the verification attached, and the re-use authorisation documentation where equipment returns to service rather than being destroyed.

artifacts.name: Disposal Vendor Due Diligence
artifacts.description: The assessment of the disposal vendor's certifications and handling practices, and the off-site transfer authorisation policy and procedures governing equipment leaving the premises for destruction.

artifacts.name: Software Licence Reclamation Records
artifacts.description: The log of software licences reclaimed from decommissioned equipment and the licence deactivation records, closing the commercial as well as the security loop on retirement.

artifacts.name: Logical Data Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The information deletion policy, the retention and deletion schedule with its triggers, the procedures for secure deletion across database, file, cloud and backup systems, the deletion log with verification, the backup deletion records, the provider deletion attestations on termination, and the log of privacy erasure requests fulfilled.

artifacts.name: Physical Security over Disposal Areas
artifacts.description: The access control and surveillance evidence for the areas where equipment awaiting destruction is held, the perimeter protection evidence, the facility entry and exit records, the physical access logs and visitor register, and the camera evidence over them.

artifacts.name: Secure Media Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The records of secure destruction or re-use of physical assets holding classified information, held separately because the classification determines the destruction standard applied.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Deployment
artifacts.description: The data loss prevention deployment and media handling controls covering the window between an asset being retired and being destroyed.

artifacts.name: AI System Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The approved policies and procedures covering AI system decommissioning and deactivation, the documented decommissioning procedure, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, and the documented evidence of the outcome.

AST-09.notes: 74 asks across 15 frameworks. Overlaps DCH-09; the distinction kept here is the equipment lifecycle — retirement workflow, reuse approval, licence reclamation and disposal vendor diligence — rather than the media sanitisation method itself.

artifacts.name: Asset Removal Authorisation
artifacts.description: The asset removal and movement authorisation procedures, the authorisation approval records, the movement authorisation records, and the device and media control policy governing what may leave. HITRUST requires the approved removal of property policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Asset Movement Records
artifacts.description: The asset movement register and logs, the gate-pass records, the hardware and media tracking procedures, and the chain of custody logs for off-site equipment.

artifacts.name: Off-Site Asset Protection
artifacts.description: The off-site equipment procedures, the off-site protection measures documentation, the verification records for off-site assets, the equipment security procedures, the physical protection measures, and the transportation security controls. HITRUST requires the approved security of equipment off-premises policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Loading Dock Controls
artifacts.description: The access procedures for loading docks, the segregated delivery and loading area layout, the inbound and outbound material inspection logs, and the material registration records.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Controls
artifacts.description: The register of all managed removable media with owner, classification and status; the policy on approved media types, encryption, registration and disposal; the endpoint policy evidence restricting removable-device use to approved devices only; the endpoint or data loss prevention configuration enforcing encryption on removable media; the procedure for secure transport of media; and the records of secure media destruction including certificates from the disposal vendor.

artifacts.name: Facility Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the removal rules, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

AST-11.notes: 36 asks across 5 frameworks. The authorisation to remove, the gate-pass record of the removal and the protection of the asset while it is away are three proofs; the loading-dock controls are kept separate because they gate the physical route.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Policy & BCMS Documentation
artifacts.description: Approved business continuity / ICT continuity policy plus the management-system documentation that sits under it: BCMS scope and process documentation, document control procedure, document register and templates with version control, and the review and update records showing the set is current. Where a cloud or regulated variant applies, the same policy must evidence coverage of the cloud environment and of the national/sector regulation cited.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Plans
artifacts.description: The executable plan set: BCP / COOP, disaster recovery and ICT continuity plans, and the recovery runbooks. Must cover invocation criteria and activation decision authority, emergency-mode and manual workaround operating procedures, recovery and reconstitution steps per critical service, and the security requirements that continue to apply during recovery. Scope must include every critical service identified in the BIA.

artifacts.name: Continuity Risk Assessment & Treatment Records
artifacts.description: Business-disruption risk assessment with its methodology and evaluation criteria, the resulting risk register, the risk treatment plan and treatment decisions, documented residual risk acceptance, and the risk appetite/tolerance statement. Include insurance coverage documentation where relied on as a treatment.

artifacts.name: BCMS Objectives, KPIs & Performance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: Documented continuity objectives with the KPIs and effectiveness criteria used to measure them, plus the monitoring and review output: availability metrics against SLA, capacity and uptime reporting, operational effectiveness reports, and periodic plan/policy review records with reviewer and date.

artifacts.name: Board & Management Approval Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the plans and policy were formally approved and are re-approved on the required cycle - board or senior management sign-off (annual for several banking frameworks), management commitment evidence, and the oversight minutes. Include the compliance mapping or attestation to the specific circular/regulation where the regulator demands it, and plan distribution records.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis & RTO/RPO Register
artifacts.description: BIA identifying critical business processes and ICT services with their dependencies and disruption impact over time, the resulting recovery priority ranking, and a register of agreed RTO and RPO per service. Must be traceable both to the critical-service inventory and forward to the recovery strategy and plans, and must include the security requirements identified during the analysis.

artifacts.name: Continuity Strategy & Resilience Architecture Evidence
artifacts.description: The chosen continuity strategy with the options analysis behind it and traceability back to the BIA, supported by the technical evidence that the strategy is real: high-availability/failover architecture diagrams, redundancy implementation records, alternate site and alternate processing arrangements including their security assessment, supply-chain diversification, and the access control and encryption protecting data at the recovery site.

artifacts.name: Crisis Management & Communication Plan
artifacts.description: Crisis management plan with crisis roles and decision authority, and the communication plan under it: stakeholder communication matrix, notification procedures, pre-drafted communication templates, redundant communication channels, and any responsible-disclosure route.

artifacts.name: Backup Policy, Schedule & Restoration Verification Records
artifacts.description: Backup policy stating scope, frequency and retention per system class, the backup schedule, successful-completion logs for the period, and the restoration tests that prove the backups are usable. Frameworks differ on cadence and on whether restoration testing must be independent of DR exercises, so evidence should cover both routine verification and at least one full restore.

artifacts.name: BC/DR Test & Exercise Reports
artifacts.description: Reports from the continuity and recovery tests run in the period - scheduled annual tests at minimum, plus resilience/scenario tests where required - showing scenario, participants, results against RTO/RPO, and lessons learned. Detailed testing programme evidence sits under BCD-04; here it evidences that the BCMS is exercised.

artifacts.name: BCMS Roles, Governance Structure & Team Rosters
artifacts.description: Who owns continuity: appointment of the continuity lead, BCM committee charter and its meeting minutes, the governance structure and reporting lines, continuity focal persons and site-level recovery team rosters, documented roles and responsibilities, and evidence of the budget/resources allocated to the programme.

artifacts.name: Disruption Incident & Post-Incident Improvement Records
artifacts.description: Records of actual disruptions handled under the plans: incident handling records and tracking-system entries, post-incident review reports with root cause, and the improvement actions raised and tracked to closure.

artifacts.name: Continuity Training, Awareness & Plan Distribution Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that personnel know their continuity duties: continuity training records, awareness communications, plan dissemination to recovery teams, and policy acknowledgement records.

BCD-01.notes: 202 entries collapsed to 13 artifacts. The dominant duplication is one BCMS document set restated by ISO 22301, DORA, QCB, SBP, ADHICS, HITRUST and CSA CCM. Backup, availability metrics and failover architecture are marked hybrid because the control has live infrastructure collectors (DigitalOcean, Neon) that produce part of that evidence.

artifacts.name: Plan Alignment Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of alignment between incident management and continuity objectives, the documented governance linking incident reporting, the incident response plan and continuity objectives, and the detection, response, recovery and containment procedures showing how the plans hand over to one another.

artifacts.name: System Interdependency Map
artifacts.description: The documentation of interdependencies between critical systems, the report analysing those interdependencies for recovery planning, the recovery plan reflecting them, and the records of contingency tests incorporating them.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The continuity plan with recovery objectives and procedures, the plan including explicit information security considerations, the plan defining how security controls are maintained during disruption, the business impact analysis identifying security requirements during disruption, the contingency plan document with its review, approval and distribution records, and the approved crisis and continuity management plan document. HITRUST requires the approved continuity planning framework policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: ICT Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The plan for restoring services within the recovery objectives, the inventory of critical systems with owners and recovery tiers, the register of critical services with agreed objectives and dependencies, the technical failover runbooks for each critical system, the architecture diagram showing redundancy and failover paths, and the recovery time and recovery point objectives themselves.

artifacts.name: Plan Exercise Records
artifacts.description: The most recent continuity test report demonstrating security controls were maintained during the exercise, the test exercise records with their post-test review documentation, and the most recent disaster recovery test report showing achievement of the recovery objectives. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented business continuity exercises requirement.

artifacts.name: Recovery Communication Records
artifacts.description: The communication plan with formats and escalation routes aligned to the incident response plan and the documented communications and activities during recovery events or exercises.

artifacts.name: Incident Register
artifacts.description: The register evidencing all security incidents are reported and managed under the incident response plan, providing the link between incident handling and continuity invocation.

artifacts.name: Continuity Training and Awareness
artifacts.description: The training records for staff with continuity-related security responsibilities and the awareness communications informing personnel of the continuity planning framework.

BCD-01.1.notes: 34 asks across 7 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is that continuity, disaster recovery and incident response plans reference one another; the alignment evidence and the dependency map are kept separate from the plans themselves.

artifacts.name: Provider Continuity Plans
artifacts.description: The service provider's disaster recovery plan covering scope, recovery objectives, recovery teams and procedures; the approved plan covering the services in scope; the provider continuity and disaster recovery plans; the documented and tested supplier continuity plans for critical services; the inventory of provider recovery sites by type with capacity, location and activation procedures; and the provider-supplied documentation covering asset acquisition, deployment, maintenance, refresh and disposal.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objective Alignment
artifacts.description: The side-by-side comparison evidencing alignment of provider recovery objectives with the organisation's documented business requirements, the memo or matrix demonstrating that alignment, the recovery time and recovery point objectives themselves, and the register of critical services with agreed objectives and dependencies.

artifacts.name: Joint Recovery Testing
artifacts.description: The joint disaster recovery testing results with service providers, the records of joint walkthroughs or table-top exercises between the organisation and the provider, the periodic test reports from the provider with results, gaps and corrective actions, the records of participation in provider tests including offshore systems, the schedule of tests for offshore provider systems, the observer sign-offs, the supplier continuity test reports, and the continuity test reports. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented business continuity exercises requirement.

artifacts.name: Provider Capability Assessment
artifacts.description: The service provider disaster recovery capability assessment reports and the security assessment of hot, warm or cold alternate recovery sites.

artifacts.name: Provider Failure Fallback Plans
artifacts.description: The fallback plans to an alternate provider or on-premise environment, the plans for resuming operations if the provider is disrupted, the continuity plan specifically addressing provider service disruption scenarios, and the records of testing those scenarios.

artifacts.name: Organisational Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The contingency plan document with its review and approval records and distribution records, the continuity plan including explicit information security considerations, the plan defining how security controls are maintained during disruption, the business impact analysis identifying security requirements during disruption, and the most recent test report demonstrating security controls were maintained during the exercise.

artifacts.name: ICT Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The plan for restoring services within the recovery objectives, the inventory of critical systems with owners and recovery tiers, the technical failover runbooks for each critical system, the architecture diagram showing redundancy and failover paths, and the most recent test report showing achievement of the objectives.

artifacts.name: Continuity Awareness and Contract Records
artifacts.description: The training records for staff with continuity-related security responsibilities, the stakeholder communications and awareness campaign material, and the vendor security clauses obliging the provider to maintain and test its plans.

BCD-01.2.notes: 42 asks across 8 frameworks. The provider's own continuity plan, its alignment with the organisation's recovery objectives, and the joint test are three proofs; the joint test is what this control exists for and is kept apart from the provider's paperwork.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objectives Register
artifacts.description: The register of recovery time and recovery point objectives for each critical business function and system, with the management approval of the targets and the prioritised recovery list they drive. SBP ETGRMF requires a register at both business-function and IT-system level; SABIC CyberTrust and MAS TRM require the objectives to be documented alongside the recovery plan.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis with Tolerance
artifacts.description: The business impact analysis containing the maximum tolerable downtime per function, the acceptable loss estimates, the critical path recovery analysis documenting the recovery sequence, and the management approval records for the downtime thresholds.

artifacts.name: Objective-to-Plan Traceability
artifacts.description: The evidence linking the disaster recovery specification to the impact analysis findings and the recovery objectives derived from them, the justification document for the specification choices made, and the business resumption priorities they establish.

artifacts.name: Recovery Procedures Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented recovery and restoration procedures with step-by-step actions, the checklist-based action plans, the detailed continuity plans with all required elements, the reconstitution process documentation, and the contact lists and call trees supporting them.

artifacts.name: Recovery Test Results
artifacts.description: The system recovery and restoration test reports demonstrating the defined timeframes are actually achievable, the register of agreed restoration times with last-tested values, the design and test reports demonstrating objectives are met, and the joint resilience test reports with vendors and partners.

artifacts.name: Recovery Metrics Performance Reports
artifacts.description: The documented recovery and response metrics for critical systems and the reports measuring actual performance against them, distinguishing a stated objective from a demonstrated one.

artifacts.name: Backup Execution and Failure Records
artifacts.description: The backup schedule documentation, the execution and completion logs, the daily completion reports, the failure investigation records, the backup inventory with data ownership, and the off-site or remote storage evidence.

artifacts.name: Alternate Site Arrangements
artifacts.description: The alternate storage site agreements, the geographic separation documentation, and the storage site security assessment establishing that the recovery location is both distinct and adequately protected.

artifacts.name: Plan Activation Criteria
artifacts.description: The documented activation triggers including breach of the recovery objectives, the plan activation criteria documentation, and the records of plan activation whether in exercise or in a real event.

artifacts.name: Critical Services Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of critical business services and processes with their supporting system and application continuity plans, and the roles and contact information register attached to each.

artifacts.name: Continuity Strategy Records
artifacts.description: The documented business continuity strategy with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Data Recovery Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented disaster recovery and production data access control specifications with their compliance evidence and implementing procedures, the register with a named owner, the data security control evidence, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the approved data management strategy behind them.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the continuity requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

BCD-01.4.notes: 73 asks across 13 frameworks. The chain that matters is impact analysis → tolerance → objectives → test → measured achievement, and each link is its own artifact because a stated objective with no test result behind it is the common failure.

artifacts.name: Invocation Criteria
artifacts.description: The documented conditions prompting plan invocation and the immediate steps during disruption, the activation threshold criteria, the escalation procedures, the documented invocation procedure covering damage assessment, communications, recovery and restoration, and the recovery plan with defined activation triggers such as recovery objective breaches.

artifacts.name: Named Roles and Deputies
artifacts.description: The list of named individuals with primary and deputy responsibilities for the contingency plan, the responsibility matrix covering sign-off, update and activation, and the incident management team structure with its contact details.

artifacts.name: Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The written enterprise-wide continuity plan based on a comprehensive impact analysis and risk assessment, the continuity plan with recovery objectives and procedures, the evidence of plan flexibility to respond to unanticipated scenarios, the incident response plan, and the dissemination records confirming the plan reached the organisation. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented business continuity strategy requirement. HITRUST requires the approved continuity planning framework policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Plan Maintenance Records
artifacts.description: The version history and change log of the contingency plan documenting each update with its rationale, the records of periodic reviews with their conclusions and update decisions, the log of developments that trigger a feasibility reassessment, and the evidence of annual board review and approval.

artifacts.name: Invocation and Activation Records
artifacts.description: The logs of activities during plan invocation or exercise, the records of recovery plan activation whether real or exercise measured against the triggers, the plan activation rehearsal records, and the test exercise records with their post-test review documentation.

artifacts.name: Continuity Capability Readiness
artifacts.description: The continuity infrastructure readiness records and the continuity plan capability deployment evidence confirming the plan can be executed when invoked.

artifacts.name: Recovery Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented disaster recovery specification with its compliance evidence, the register or inventory evidencing disaster recovery with a named owner, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the continuity framework.

BCD-01.5.notes: 32 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps BCD-01.6; what is distinct here is the criteria and named roles that govern invocation, and the plan-maintenance evidence, rather than the communication that follows.

artifacts.name: Plan Activation Criteria
artifacts.description: The activation threshold criteria, the plan activation criteria documentation, the escalation procedures, the documented invocation procedure covering damage assessment, communications, recovery and restoration, and the early warning detection procedures.

artifacts.name: Contact and Escalation Register
artifacts.description: The call tree and escalation matrix, the roles and contact information register, the incident management team structure with its contact details, and the media spokesperson designation.

artifacts.name: Crisis Communication Plan
artifacts.description: The crisis communication plan, the communications strategy document, the communication plan with formats and escalation routes aligned to the incident response plan, the emergency notification system documentation, the press release and communication templates, and the command centre playbook.

artifacts.name: Communication Test Records
artifacts.description: The communication testing records, the communication drill records, and the records of continuity plan drill exercises exercising the communication paths. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented communication requirement.

artifacts.name: Invocation Communication Logs
artifacts.description: The logs of activities during plan invocation or exercise and the documented communications and activities during recovery events or exercises.

artifacts.name: Customer Outage Communications
artifacts.description: The incident communication procedures for availability events, the planned maintenance notification records, the unplanned outage notification and status update records, and the status page or system health dashboard through which they are published.

artifacts.name: Continuity and Recovery Plans
artifacts.description: The formal continuity and disaster recovery plan documents with their actions, roles, communications, training and drills; the emergency response plan; the evacuation procedures; the incident response plan; the information system and application continuity plans; the critical business services and processes inventory; and the annual review and update evidence.

artifacts.name: Recovery Test Records
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery test plans with their execution results and the gap remediation tracking arising from those tests.

BCD-01.6.notes: 36 asks across 7 frameworks. The activation trigger, the call tree and the external communication during a disruption are three proofs; the communication test is kept separate because a contact list that has never been dialled is not evidence.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The enterprise-wide business continuity plan built on the business impact analysis and risk assessment, covering governance, tiered recovery, alternate sites, remote working and supply-chain resilience. SBP ETGRMF requires the development methodology and a documented scope and sizing rationale reflecting the institution's size and complexity, and requires the plan to be scenario-agnostic rather than tied to named events; ISO 22301 expects plans per business unit or site; SBP Internet Banking requires alignment to BSD Circular No 13 with internet-banking services in scope.

artifacts.name: Disaster Recovery Plan
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery plan with its execution procedures, asset, data and flow descriptions, and the recovery procedures for each critical system. MAS TRM and SOX require documented management approval and an annual review; NDMO requires the DR specification to be evidenced as a documented artifact with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Board and Management Approval Records
artifacts.description: The board resolution or senior management approval adopting the plans, with the annual re-approval evidence. SBP ETGRMF and SBP Internet Banking require board-level approval specifically; PISF 2026 requires higher-management and, where applicable, sector-regulator approval of a realistic risk-based plan; SL CSF accepts senior management approval.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The business impact analysis categorising critical functions and their interdependencies, with the recovery time and recovery point objectives and maximum tolerable period of disruption it establishes. SBP Internet Banking requires internet-banking services to be in scope with RTO/RPO/MTPD defined; SOC 2 and HITRUST require RTO/RPO targets for critical systems to be traceable into the plan.

artifacts.name: BC/DR Test Records and Sign-offs
artifacts.description: The annual test schedule covering critical systems and scenarios, the test and drill reports with scenarios, results and lessons learned, and the sign-off by the business group or unit heads. SBP ETGRMF requires a documented sign-off process and a register tracking sign-offs across drills; SOX requires gap remediation from tests to be tracked to closure; SBP Internet Banking requires internet-banking-specific scenarios in the test set.
