artifacts.name: Plan Review, Update and Distribution Records
artifacts.description: The review and update log with version history, the records confirming dissemination across the organisation and plan accessibility, and the evidence that the plan remains aligned to business strategy. MAS TRM and SOX require an annual review specifically; SBP ETGRMF requires a scope change log tracking business growth and complexity.

artifacts.name: Invocation Procedure and Activation Criteria
artifacts.description: The documented conditions that prompt invocation, the immediate steps to take during disruption, the damage assessment, communication, recovery and restoration procedure, the checklist-based action plans, and the logs of activity during an actual invocation or exercise.

artifacts.name: Crisis Management and Emergency Response Plan
artifacts.description: The crisis management plan with its roles and responsibilities matrix, the command centre playbook, the emergency response and evacuation procedures, and the crisis-time documentation pack.

artifacts.name: Contingency Scenario Register and Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The register of identified contingency scenarios (system faults, hardware malfunction, operating errors, security events), the risk assessment performed for each, the response plan addressing each, and the records of scenario testing.

artifacts.name: Cloud Resilience Architecture Evidence
artifacts.description: The cloud contingency plan addressing provider disruption, connectivity loss and legal-action scenarios, the high-availability architecture diagram showing redundancy across availability zones, the architecture decision document justifying service and deployment model, health-check and monitoring configuration, redundant connectivity arrangements via diverse cables or providers, and the connectivity contracts carrying disruption penalty clauses.

artifacts.name: BCM Governance Structure and Roles
artifacts.description: The business continuity governance structure and framework, the appointment letter for the BCM head, the steering-committee designation of the body governing the programme, the register of departmental continuity focal persons, the roles and contact information register, and the call tree and escalation matrix.

artifacts.name: Critical Business Services Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of critical business services and processes with their supporting information systems and application continuity plans, and the documented criteria by which each plan is activated.

artifacts.name: Data Continuity Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy as it bears on continuity, the register evidencing the disaster recovery specification with a named owner, and the national regulator's assessment and compliance records.

BCD-01.7.notes: 107 asks across 14 frameworks. BCP and DRP are kept as separate artifacts because several frameworks approve and test them separately, and the approval evidence is held apart from the plan because SBP ETGRMF, QCB, PISF 2026 and SBP Internet Banking each test the approval as its own control.

artifacts.name: Critical Asset Register
artifacts.description: The enterprise information asset inventory classified by criticality with owner, confidentiality/integrity/availability rating and location, together with the documented methodology and criteria by which criticality is assigned. SBP ETGRMF requires the prioritisation methodology and an asset register review log; QCB requires per-asset classification with periodic refresh evidence; COBIT requires lifecycle tracking, disposal records and software licence compliance alongside the inventory.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The BIA report assessing and prioritising all business functions with their interdependencies, the workflow analysis identifying process dependencies, the interdependency map, and the disruption impact analysis. HIPAA requires an explicit data criticality analysis and application criticality classification; COBIT requires the BIA to establish availability requirements.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objectives Definition
artifacts.description: The documented and approved recovery time and recovery point objectives for each critical asset, with the backup design and periodic test reports demonstrating they are actually met.

artifacts.name: Disruption Scenario Register
artifacts.description: The register of uncontrolled and non-specific disruption events considered, the documentation of each scenario analysed in the impact assessment, and the measures documented to reduce the likelihood or impact of multi-source threats.

artifacts.name: Continuity and Recovery Plans
artifacts.description: The business continuity and disaster recovery plans built on the criticality assessment, the information system and application continuity plans, the contingency plan document with its distribution, review and approval records, and the plan activation criteria. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented risk assessment and impact analysis.

artifacts.name: Continuity Risk Register and Treatment
artifacts.description: The continuity management system risk register with the risk assessment methodology and its approval, entries with owners, ratings and treatment plans, the opportunity assessment records, the effectiveness evaluation criteria, and the risk treatment plans.

artifacts.name: Recovery Testing and Post-Incident Records
artifacts.description: The recovery testing and validation records, disaster recovery test results, the post-incident improvement action items with tracking, and the root cause analysis documentation behind them.

artifacts.name: Resource Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The control implementation plan prioritised by risk and criticality with management or regulator approval, the records prioritising resources to the assets that essential services depend on, and the strategy focused on continuity of those critical services.

artifacts.name: Asset Performance Monitoring
artifacts.description: The prioritised asset list with operational sensitivity ratings, the monitoring reports showing asset performance against operational goals, and the records of periodic priority reviews.

artifacts.name: Capacity and Availability Planning
artifacts.description: The availability and capacity management plans, capacity forecasting documentation, performance baseline measurements with monitoring reports, the IT service catalogue, service level and operational level agreements, service level performance monitoring, and the service agreement review records.

artifacts.name: Security Management Framework
artifacts.description: The board-approved information and cyber security management framework containing the asset prioritisation component, giving the governance context the register sits inside.

artifacts.name: Crisis Response Contact Records
artifacts.description: The call tree and escalation matrix, the roles and contact information register, the critical business services and processes inventory they map to, and the crisis-time documentation pack.

artifacts.name: AI System Inventory
artifacts.description: The AI system inventory register with named owners, the documented AI risk tolerance statement with its approval records, the documented evidence of the outcome, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Data Asset Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The documented data systems prioritisation, backup and recovery, and disaster recovery specifications with their implementation evidence, the register or inventory evidencing each with a named owner, the approved data management and personal data protection strategy behind them, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions, and the national regulator's assessment records.

BCD-02.notes: 95 asks across 14 frameworks. The control is about identifying what is critical, so the asset register and the business impact analysis are the two anchors; the continuity plans that consume them are one artifact rather than the focus.

artifacts.name: Contingency Training Materials
artifacts.description: The contingency training materials, the training schedule, the awareness training modules on incident reporting, and the documented roles and responsibilities for the testing programme with the responsibility matrix behind them. HITRUST requires the approved testing policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The training completion records, the evidence that assigned staff are trained for their testing roles, the records of staff assigned to testing roles, and the evidence of staff ability to execute the emergency and recovery procedures.

artifacts.name: Workforce Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The acknowledgement records from the recovery team and relevant staff confirming plan awareness, the evidence of recovery team and staff awareness of the plans, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the testing obligations.

artifacts.name: Exercise and Drill Records
artifacts.description: The annual test plan and results, the annual test reports validating recovery requirement effectiveness, the annual testing schedule, the sign-off records evidencing annual validation, the comprehensive test reports demonstrating all aspects covered, the evidence that tests cover people, processes and technology, the records of drill exercises, the fire and natural disaster drill records, the unplanned test records at the required frequency, the test exercise results with lessons learned, and the post-test review documentation.

artifacts.name: Independent Test Assurance
artifacts.description: The internal audit reports on testing and the external auditor continuity management report.

artifacts.name: Continuity Plans
artifacts.description: The formal continuity and disaster recovery plan documents with their actions, roles, communications, training and drills; the continuity plan with recovery objectives and procedures; the continuity policy and strategy documentation; and the backup and recovery procedures with their verification records.

BCD-03.notes: 32 asks across 6 frameworks. Training the recovery team, testing whether they can execute, and the independent audit of that testing are three proofs; the awareness of the wider workforce is a fourth and separate population.

artifacts.name: Continuity Testing Programme & Plans Under Test
artifacts.description: The approved testing programme document - scope, methodology, risk-based prioritisation and governance - together with the current approved BCP, DRP and ICT continuity plans and the recovery runbooks that the tests exercise. Auditors match the tested version to the approved version, so provide the plan revision that was in force at each test.

artifacts.name: Test Scenarios, Test Cases & Success Criteria
artifacts.description: The scenario library and the test cases derived from it, with defined success criteria and traceability back to the BIA and to the risks and threat scenarios being simulated - including severe-but-plausible and threat-actor/TTP-led scenarios where the framework requires them, and the tooling used.

artifacts.name: BC/DR Test Reports & Results
artifacts.description: The completed test reports for the period: what was tested, when, by whom, results against the success criteria and against RTO/RPO, and the deficiencies found. Must cover technical recovery and full or partial switchover as well as plan-level tests, and evidence the required frequency - annual at minimum for most frameworks, with several banking regimes requiring multiple unplanned or hot/cold tests per year.

artifacts.name: Tabletop, Simulation & Live Exercise Records
artifacts.description: Records of the non-technical exercises: tabletop and simulation reports, full rehearsals, parallel-operation and unplanned switchover exercises, and multi-party exercises involving providers or other entities, each with the objectives set and the outcome observed.

artifacts.name: Testing Schedule & Calendar
artifacts.description: The forward testing schedule showing each planned test, its type, scope and date, and covering every critical system and plan across the cycle. Frameworks differ on cadence - annual as the baseline, with quarterly or more frequent unplanned tests required by several banking regulators - so the schedule must show the applicable frequency and evidence completion against it.

artifacts.name: Post-Test Lessons Learned & Corrective Action Tracking
artifacts.description: After-action reports and the lessons-learned or deficiency register, with each finding assigned an owner, due date and closure evidence, plus root cause analysis for failed test objectives. This is the artifact that shows testing changes something rather than being performed for its own sake.

artifacts.name: Provider Exit Plan & Joint Testing Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that dependency on providers is exercised too: the documented exit or transition plan with its trigger events, RACI and transition playbook, the shortlist of alternate providers, escrow or continuity agreements, the exit plan test report, and the results of tests conducted jointly with the cloud provider or of provider SLA testing.

artifacts.name: Test Sign-off & Business Participation Records
artifacts.description: Attendance and participation records showing business users - not only IT - took part in each exercise, together with the business-head and test-owner sign-off confirming the test completed and the results were accepted.

artifacts.name: Testing Roles, Training & Competency Records
artifacts.description: The RACI for the testing programme and the roles documentation under it, plus training, awareness acknowledgement and competency records for the staff expected to execute recovery during a test or a real event.

artifacts.name: RTO/RPO Register & Recovery Objective Achievement Analysis
artifacts.description: The BIA-derived RTO/RPO register for critical services with the recovery dependency mapping, and the analysis comparing objectives to what each test actually achieved, including the explanation and remediation where an objective was missed.

artifacts.name: Alternate Site & Infrastructure Readiness Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence the recovery environment is ready to be tested against: alternate site readiness and security assessment, equipment location and siting records, failover architecture, and the hardening, perimeter and logging configuration of the recovery infrastructure.

artifacts.name: Plan Revision & Version History Records
artifacts.description: Version history for the continuity plans showing the revisions made as a direct result of test findings and of significant changes to the environment, with the reassessment of plan adequacy and the approval of each revision.

artifacts.name: Crisis Communication Drill Records
artifacts.description: Records of communication drills and call-tree tests run as part of the exercise programme, with the communication strategy, press or holding statements and spokesperson designation that were exercised.

artifacts.name: Backup Restoration Validation Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that backups were restored and verified as part of, or alongside, the test programme - restore job output, integrity validation results, and the backup/recovery verification procedure they were run against.

artifacts.name: Independent Audit Reports on Continuity Testing
artifacts.description: Internal audit reports covering the continuity testing programme and, where the regulator requires external assurance, the external auditor's business continuity report, together with the responses to their findings.

BCD-04.notes: 173 entries collapsed to 15 artifacts. SBP ETGRMF alone restates the testing programme roughly forty ways (schedule, calendar, RACI, sign-off, scenarios, reports); these are the same handful of documents a testing programme produces each cycle. No evidence collectors exist for this control, so only config-derived readiness and restore evidence is marked hybrid.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plans
artifacts.description: The current BCP and DRP documents with their governing policy and strategy, recovery procedures and RTO/RPO targets. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented plan; SBP ETGRMF requires board-approved policy references on the face of the documents.

artifacts.name: Plan Maintenance Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure governing how plans are kept current: the change management procedure for the continuity management system, impact assessment on proposed changes, change request records, and the criteria that trigger a reassessment of plan adequacy.

artifacts.name: Plan Review, Version History and Distribution
artifacts.description: The review and update log, the version history recording each change with its rationale, the sign-off on review completion, and the records confirming distribution and accessibility to the people who would use the plan. SBP ETGRMF requires an annual review with sign-off; SBP Cloud requires named individuals with primary and deputy responsibilities recorded against the plan.

artifacts.name: Test Schedule and Results
artifacts.description: The annual test schedule covering critical systems and scenarios, with the test reports and results. QCB requires a minimum of four unplanned hot/cold tests a year; SBP ETGRMF requires business group and unit head sign-off on the results; HITRUST requires post-test review documentation alongside the exercise records.

artifacts.name: Post-Exercise Evaluation and Lessons Learned
artifacts.description: The post-exercise evaluation reports, the lessons learned register, the post-incident evaluation records following a real disruption, and the root cause analysis behind each. ISO 22301 requires evaluation of both exercises and actual incidents; SOC 2 requires post-incident improvement items to be tracked.

artifacts.name: Corrective Action and Gap Remediation Tracking
artifacts.description: The corrective action tracker arising from exercises and incidents, the gap analysis comparing existing plans against required policies and procedures, the remediation plan with the linkage from each gap to the prioritised disruption it affects, and the closure records.

artifacts.name: Change-Triggered Plan Update Records
artifacts.description: The log of plan updates triggered by specific events — business, system or network changes, audit recommendations, test results — with the records linking each update to its triggering event. SBP Cloud requires a feasibility trigger log covering new availability zones, alternate providers and technology changes.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objective Achievement Analysis
artifacts.description: The analysis of whether recovery time and recovery point objectives were actually met during exercises and incidents, with the defined objectives for each critical system that the analysis measures against, and the procedure evaluation reports assessing continued fitness.

artifacts.name: Continual Improvement Programme Records
artifacts.description: The continual improvement programme documentation, the maturity assessment records for the continuity management system, and the improvement action tracker showing progress against it.

artifacts.name: Independent Audit of Continuity Management
artifacts.description: The internal audit reports on continuity testing and the external auditor's business continuity management report, giving assurance independent of the team that runs the exercises.

artifacts.name: Exit and Alternate Provider Planning
artifacts.description: The exit management plan, the identification of alternate providers, and the disaster recovery plan covering worst-case scenarios where the primary provider is unavailable.

artifacts.name: Cloud Contingency Governance Records
artifacts.description: The RACI matrix for the cloud contingency plan covering sign-off, update and activation responsibility, the list of named individuals with primary and deputy roles, the periodic plan review records with conclusions and update decisions, and the version history.

artifacts.name: Scenario-Based Resilience Testing Records
artifacts.description: Test plans covering broad scenarios including simulation of extreme but plausible cyber attacks, tabletop and simulation reports challenging response and recovery assumptions, records of tests specifically exercising governance arrangements and communication plans, staff exercise participation records for unfamiliar scenarios, and the lessons-learned register from them.

artifacts.name: Backup and Recovery Verification Records
artifacts.description: The backup and recovery procedures with the verification records demonstrating restores were actually performed and succeeded, rather than that backups were merely taken.

BCD-06.notes: 97 asks across 12 frameworks. This control is about keeping continuity plans current rather than about having them, so the maintenance cycle (test, evaluate, remediate, update, re-approve) is the organising structure and the plan documents themselves are one artifact rather than the centre of the set.

artifacts.name: Alternate Site Documentation
artifacts.description: The documentation of the geographically separated recovery site with location details and distance from the primary; the alternate processing site agreements; the site readiness assessment; the recovery time documentation; the alternate provider identification; and the exit management plan for the arrangement.

artifacts.name: Site Readiness Testing
artifacts.description: The recovery site testing and readiness assessment records, the failover test results showing recovery objective attainment, and the failover test results.

artifacts.name: Redundant Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture diagrams showing redundancy across clusters, load balancers and multiple availability zones or regions; the high-availability configuration screenshots; the register of services and their availability targets; the monthly report of service uptime against commitments; and the analysis of single points of failure with their mitigation plans.

artifacts.name: Network Path Redundancy
artifacts.description: The evidence of alternate network paths and different service providers and the plans for cross-border network redundancy covering offshore arrangements.

artifacts.name: Contingency Scenario Records
artifacts.description: The register of identified contingency scenarios covering system faults, hardware malfunction, operating errors and security events; the risk assessment for each scenario; the response plans addressing each; and the records of scenario testing.

artifacts.name: Provider Recovery Site Records
artifacts.description: The service provider's disaster recovery plan covering scope, recovery objectives, recovery teams and procedures; the inventory of provider recovery sites by type with capacity, location and activation procedures; the provider documentation describing the type and configuration of each site; the site activation procedures with their timelines; the operational evidence of each site through visit reports, photographs and infrastructure inventory; the geographic risk map showing site separation against single-event risks; the memo or matrix demonstrating alignment of the provider plan with the organisation's recovery objectives; and the provider-supplied asset lifecycle documentation.

artifacts.name: Continuity Plan and Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The comprehensive continuity plan covering tiered recovery, alternate sites, remote work and supply-chain resilience; the annual business impact analysis categorising critical functions and interdependencies; the disaster recovery plan with its worst-case scenarios; and the disaster recovery plan and procedures.

artifacts.name: Backup and Environmental Records
artifacts.description: The backup policy and schedule with its successful completion logs, the restoration test results and reports, and the environmental monitoring system configurations at the alternate site.

BCD-09.notes: 35 asks across 7 frameworks. The site itself, its geographic separation from the primary and its readiness to be activated are three proofs; the provider's own recovery sites are kept separate because the organisation does not operate them.

artifacts.name: Backup and Recovery Policy
artifacts.description: Approved policy defining backup scope (user-level data, system-level data, system documentation, device configurations), frequency, retention, encryption, storage locations, protection measures and testing obligations, tied to the recovery objectives. Must be current, management-approved with scope, roles, review frequency, approval signature and version history. Several sources want backup lifecycle management (retention through destruction) covered explicitly, and NDMO expects the approved data management strategy carrying its roadmap, owners, metrics and review cadence.

artifacts.name: Backup and Restoration Procedures
artifacts.description: The operational runbook implementing the policy: step-by-step backup and restore instructions, responsible roles, control points, exception handling, verification steps, and the pre-movement backup procedure to be run before equipment is relocated or decommissioned. Must reference the parent policy and be current.

artifacts.name: Backup Schedule and Job Configuration
artifacts.description: Live configuration from the backup platform (or cloud-native backup service) showing the defined jobs, what each covers, frequency, retention period and encryption settings - the evidence that the documented schedule is actually what runs. Export or screenshot must carry the date, system identifier and reviewer.

artifacts.name: Backup Job Execution Logs and Success/Failure Reports
artifacts.description: Backup completion evidence covering the full review period for both local and remote/off-site solutions: job execution logs, periodic success/failure reporting, and the remediation record for every failed job. Logs must be retained for the required period, tamper-protected, and show timestamp, actor, action and outcome.

artifacts.name: Restoration and Recovery Test Reports
artifacts.description: Signed reports from actual restore tests - scenarios exercised, data restored, restore time achieved against the target, integrity verification of the restored data, issues found and corrective actions. Must include recovery activities that failed as well as those that succeeded, and cover device configuration restores where those are backed up. Frequency differs by source: periodic/organization-defined for ISO, ADHICS and HITRUST; the last two cycles of half-yearly testing for cloud workloads under SBP; verification before equipment moves under HIPAA.

artifacts.name: RPO/RTO Definitions and Backup Design Justification
artifacts.description: Approved recovery point and recovery time objectives for critical assets and services, and the backup design showing how the chosen frequency, retention and replication meet them - including the backup schedule mapped to data classification, and documentation of recovery capability at individual system and cluster level. Test reports should be traceable back to these targets.

artifacts.name: Backup Encryption and Data-at-Rest Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration proving backup copies are encrypted at rest and in transit, together with the underlying data-at-rest encryption evidence for the source systems it covers (full disk, database and storage encryption) and the key management arrangements for those keys. Where regulated data types are in scope (CUI, ePHI, medical device data), include the policy or procedure asserting the confidentiality requirement and the records showing it operates.

artifacts.name: Off-Site, Immutable and Replicated Copy Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that a copy survives loss of the primary site and of the production credentials: off-site or cloud backup storage documentation, immutable/object-lock or write-once snapshot configuration, backup architecture documentation showing the 3-2-1 arrangement, replication implementation evidence at database, storage and cluster level with a replication health/lag view, and evidence of network segregation and physical separation between production and backup environments.

artifacts.name: Backup Integrity Verification Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the backed-up data is verifiably intact, not merely written: integrity check or checksum/hash verification output, the documented backup integrity procedure, file integrity monitoring deployment covering backup repositories, and data quality/validation reporting where the source demands it (profiling, validation rules, issue and cleansing logs). Records must be retained and tamper-protected.

artifacts.name: Backup Repository Inventory and Access Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The catalogue of what is backed up and where - backup sets and media with verification hashes, repository inventory with last-backup date, data ownership per backup set, and the media classification applied - together with the access controls restricting who can read, restore or delete backups, and the retention and destruction records for expired media. Email archiving and restoration capability is included where in scope.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plans
artifacts.description: The continuity and recovery plans the backup regime feeds: business continuity policy and strategy, BCPs covering critical services, DR plans with defined RTO/RPO, crisis management and communication plan, and - where cross-mapped by PCI DSS - the incident response plan containing the business recovery and data backup process, its roles and responsibilities, the payment brand and acquirer contact list and the legal/regulatory reporting map. Overlaps with IRO-01; collect the IR items once.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review and Programme Assurance Records
artifacts.description: Records closing the loop after a failed backup, failed restore or recovery event: root cause analysis, improvement actions with tracking to closure, and the periodic programme review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions. Include independent compliance or regulator assessment records where the regime requires them.

artifacts.name: Records Protection: Retention Schedule, Agreements and Awareness
artifacts.description: The organizational-records protection set cross-mapped to backups: approved policy and implementing procedure for protection of organizational records, the retention schedule with the access-control and integrity mechanisms applied to retained records, executed third-party agreements carrying the required security clauses with signatures, awareness communications showing personnel were informed, and operator qualification records where specialist staff handle the data.

artifacts.name: Hosting Environment and Email Platform Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: Supporting availability and platform-protection evidence cross-mapped into this control: environmental monitoring configuration for the facility holding primary or backup systems (temperature, humidity, fire suppression), and for the email platform, threat-protection and MFA configuration for administrative, remote and webmail access plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC records. Peripheral to backups - supply only if the assessment scope covers those requirements.

BCD-11.notes: 124 manual entries across 24 sources collapsed to 14 artifacts. Two evidence collectors are live (DigitalOcean, Neon), so backup schedule/config and job-result artifacts are marked automated or hybrid: the connectors cover part of the estate, the rest still needs tool exports. The IR-plan items (PCI 12.10.1) and the environmental/email items (SOC 2 A1.2, PISF 9.7) arrive via cross-mapped requirements and duplicate IRO-01 and other controls.

artifacts.name: Backup Policy and Schedule
artifacts.description: The policy defining scope, frequency, retention, encryption and testing, with the schedule and backup tool configuration showing jobs and retention per system. PISF 2026 requires the schedule to be aligned to data classification; CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented policy; SBP Cloud requires the policy to specify recovery point objectives, ransomware protection and a half-yearly restoration cadence.

artifacts.name: Backup Execution Logs
artifacts.description: The backup job execution and completion logs with the periodic success and failure report and the remediation applied to failures, evidencing backups actually run rather than only being scheduled.

artifacts.name: Restoration Test Records
artifacts.description: The restoration test plans, schedule and results with the scenarios exercised, restore times achieved and data integrity verified. Cadence differs: SBP Cloud requires half-yearly with signed reports from the last two cycles, QCB semi-annual, SOX and PISF 2026 periodic against a documented schedule. This is the evidence that distinguishes a backup from a recovery capability.

artifacts.name: Backup Integrity Verification Records
artifacts.description: The integrity verification records, hash records over backup sets, the integrity checks performed on restored data, the replica environment integrity tests, and the backup inventory and catalogue with its verification hashes.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objective Achievement Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented and approved recovery point and recovery time objectives for critical assets, with the evidence from testing that they were actually achieved and the recovery time verification records.

artifacts.name: Backup Encryption and Access Controls
artifacts.description: The configuration showing backups encrypted at rest and in transit, the access control documentation for backup systems, and the verification that the protection is applied to every backup set rather than a subset.

artifacts.name: Immutable and Offsite Backup Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of offsite replication or immutable object-lock copies following a separation rule, the immutability configuration on the backup repository, the offsite storage documentation, the network segregation and physical separation evidence for backup infrastructure, and the offsite backup location records.

artifacts.name: Failed Restoration Remediation Records
artifacts.description: The remediation records for failed restoration tests with root cause analysis and the post-incident improvement items tracked to closure.

artifacts.name: Single Point of Failure Register
artifacts.description: The documented register of single points of failure with the mitigation actions planned against each, establishing where a restoration would not be sufficient on its own.

artifacts.name: Cloud Data Residency and Exit Controls
artifacts.description: The register documenting the current data centre or region for every workload and dataset, the region enforcement configuration restricting deployment to approved locations, the contractual clause requiring advance notification of location changes with a right to reject, the deletion clause mandating secure removal from all provider and subcontractor storage on exit, and the sample deletion confirmation template.

artifacts.name: Cloud Data Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The information classification policy defining sensitivity tiers, the cloud asset inventory tagged with classification, owner and criticality, the enhanced controls matrix for high-value assets covering customer-managed keys, data-loss prevention, multi-factor authentication and enhanced logging, the data-loss prevention policy and rule export, the access security broker configuration showing inspection and blocking, and sample anomalous access alerts with triage records.

artifacts.name: Disaster Recovery Plan and Environment
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery and continuity plans the restoration supports, with the environmental monitoring configuration covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression at the sites holding the backup infrastructure.

artifacts.name: Data Backup Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented data backup and recovery specification with its implementing procedures and process workflows, the implementation evidence, the data quality profiling reports, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the backup requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

BCD-11.1.notes: 84 asks across 15 frameworks. The distinction that matters and is easily lost in a raw list: backups being taken, backups being protected, and backups being provably restorable. The third is what this control is actually about, so restoration testing is its own artifact rather than a line inside the backup policy.

artifacts.name: Offsite Backup Storage
artifacts.description: The offsite backup storage documentation, the off-site backup location records, the off-site or remote backup storage evidence, and the evidence of offsite replication or immutable object-lock backup copies.

artifacts.name: Backup Policy and Schedule
artifacts.description: The policy defining scope, frequency, retention, encryption and testing for backups; the backup policy and schedule; the backup policy, schedule and successful completion logs; the backup schedule documentation; the backup schedule aligned to data classification; the backup procedures; and the backup schedule and configuration from the backup tool showing jobs and retention.

artifacts.name: Backup Completion Records
artifacts.description: The backup completion logs, the daily backup completion reports, the periodic report showing backup job status and failure remediation, the backup failure investigation records, and the backup logs.

artifacts.name: Backup Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The configuration showing backups encrypted at rest and in transit, the backup encryption verification records, the backup integrity verification records, the catalogue of backup sets and media with verification hashes, and the evidence that backup media, storage and facility are secured and protected.

artifacts.name: Restoration Test Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of periodic restore tests with success criteria and outcomes, the restoration test results and reports, the recovery test results, the reports of recovery mechanism tests, and the disaster recovery plan and procedures they exercise.

artifacts.name: Backup Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The risk assessment of the backup and restore process with the controls it defines.

artifacts.name: Facility Protection Records
artifacts.description: The disaster protection measures documentation, the uninterruptible power supply and battery backup configuration, the generator and backup power testing records, and the environmental monitoring system configurations covering the site holding the copies.

artifacts.name: Credential Store Backup
artifacts.description: The password storage with hashing or encryption and the privileged password vault with its offsite backup.

artifacts.name: Retention and Classification Records
artifacts.description: The storage and retention policy with its documented compliance evidence, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the data lifecycle records covering retention schedules, the data security control evidence including access controls, and the data value realisation records.

artifacts.name: Backup Recovery Accountability
artifacts.description: The documented data backup and recovery specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the implementation evidence demonstrating the outcome, the data quality profiling reports, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

BCD-11.2.notes: 45 asks across 10 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is that backup copies sit somewhere the primary failure cannot reach; offsite and immutable storage is kept separate from the backup programme itself.

artifacts.name: Backup Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration showing backups encrypted at rest and in transit, the backup encryption configuration, the backup encryption verification records, the backup data protection verification, and the encryption configuration protecting the copies. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-backup-confidentiality requirement.

artifacts.name: Backup Key Custody
artifacts.description: The encryption key custody records, the key management for data at rest, and the backup access control documentation restricting who can decrypt a restored copy.

artifacts.name: Backup Policy and Schedule
artifacts.description: The policy defining scope, frequency, retention, encryption and testing for backups; the backup policy and schedule; the backup policy, schedule and successful completion logs; the backup procedures; and the schedule and configuration from the backup tool showing jobs and retention. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented backup requirement.

artifacts.name: Backup Completion and Integrity Records
artifacts.description: The backup completion logs, the backup logs, the periodic report showing backup job status and failure remediation, the backup integrity verification records, and the catalogue of backup sets and media with their verification hashes.

artifacts.name: Offsite and Immutable Copies
artifacts.description: The offsite backup storage documentation and the evidence of offsite replication or immutable object-lock backup copies.

artifacts.name: Restoration Test Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of periodic restore tests with success criteria and outcomes, the restoration test results and reports, the recovery test results, and the disaster recovery plan and procedures they exercise.

artifacts.name: Encryption at Rest Records
artifacts.description: The data-at-rest encryption configuration, the database encryption records, and the full disk encryption documentation covering the systems the backups are taken from.

artifacts.name: Environmental Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The environmental monitoring system configurations covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression at the site holding the copies.

BCD-11.4.notes: 33 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps BCD-11.2; what is distinct here is the cryptographic protection of the backup specifically — the encryption configuration, the key custody and the verification that both hold.

artifacts.name: Backup Policy and Completion Logs
artifacts.description: The backup policy and schedule with the successful completion logs, the backup and recovery procedures with their verification records, the backup management policy, the backup configuration evidence, the sample backup and restore job logs with completion status and durations, and the retention policy and procedures behind the schedule. HITRUST requires the approved backup policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Backup Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The backup encryption configuration, the backup access control documentation, and the backup data protection verification confirming the copies cannot be reached or altered by whatever compromised the primary.

artifacts.name: Restoration Test Records
artifacts.description: The backup restoration test records demonstrating recoverability, the periodic restoration test reports demonstrating the defined timeframes are achievable, the disaster recovery test results and reports, the data and system restoration verification procedures, the recovery testing and validation records, and the system recovery test results.

artifacts.name: Disaster Recovery Plan
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery plan with its procedures, the recovery procedures for critical systems, the plan with asset, data and flow descriptions, the crisis-time documentation pack, and the reconstitution process documentation. Where the plan is shared with continuity it is the recovery-specific sections that satisfy this control.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objectives Register
artifacts.description: The recovery time and recovery point objective definitions per system, the defined and measured recovery time objective documents, and the register of agreed restoration times per system with last-tested values against them.

artifacts.name: System Restoration Procedures
artifacts.description: The documented restoration procedures with detailed step-by-step recovery actions per system, the recovery and resumption procedures, and the recovery procedures documentation supporting them.

artifacts.name: Return to Normal Operations Records
artifacts.description: The return-to-normal criteria, the stand-down procedures, and the records showing the transition from recovery operations back to business as usual was made against defined criteria rather than by judgement call.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Plan and Invocation
artifacts.description: The business continuity plan covering critical services with the continuity policy and strategy documentation behind it, the documented invocation procedure covering damage assessment, communications, recovery and restoration, the logs of activities during invocation or exercise, and the crisis management framework and communication plan.

artifacts.name: Continuity Exercise Records
artifacts.description: The business continuity plan test and exercise results with lessons learned, and the joint resilience test reports with vendors and partners covering the dependencies the organisation does not itself control.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review and Improvement
artifacts.description: The root cause analysis documentation and the post-incident improvement action items with their tracking, closing the loop from a recovery event back into the plan.

artifacts.name: Environmental Monitoring Configuration
artifacts.description: The environmental monitoring system configurations covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression at the sites holding the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Data Retention and Classification Records
artifacts.description: The data retention policies with the backup and recovery procedures they drive, the storage and retention policy with its documented compliance evidence, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the data lifecycle records covering retention schedules, the data governance framework and policies, the data quality management reports and metrics, and the data security control evidence.

artifacts.name: Recovery Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented disaster recovery specification with its compliance evidence, the register or inventory evidencing disaster recovery with a named owner, the organisational artifacts covering role mandates, responsibility matrices, job descriptions and committee charters, the data value realisation records, and the awareness communications and periodic review records naming the reviewer.

BCD-12.notes: 63 asks across 13 frameworks. Backup, restoration testing and reconstitution-to-normal are separated because they are three sequential proofs — that copies exist, that they restore, and that the business resumes — and an assessor samples each differently.

artifacts.name: Redundancy Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture documenting redundant systems and infrastructure eliminating single points of failure, the high-availability architecture diagram showing redundancy and workload distribution across availability zones, the high-availability and redundancy architecture diagram across active-active or active-passive configurations, the network topology showing redundant paths and components, the core banking architecture design with its resilience provisions, the redundant mail infrastructure design, the architecture decision document justifying the service and deployment model, and the technical evidence of redundancy in critical systems. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented equipment redundancy and business continuity strategy requirements.

artifacts.name: Failover and Switchover Testing
artifacts.description: The failover test reports, the documented system switchover plan with its tested procedures, the periodic switchover test reports demonstrating operational readiness, the records of rapid backup and recovery capability testing, the reports of periodic resilience and stress testing of critical components, and the records showing test results used to improve resilience measures.

artifacts.name: Single Point of Failure Analysis
artifacts.description: The analysis identifying and addressing single points of failure and the documented register of those points with their mitigation actions.

artifacts.name: Replication and Backup Records
artifacts.description: The technical evidence of data replication at system and application cluster levels, the dashboard showing replication lag and health, the high-availability replication configuration, the offsite replication evidence, the backup architecture documentation, the documentation of recovery capabilities at individual system and cluster levels, the backup policy and schedule with its successful completion logs, and the restoration test reports verifying recoverability.

artifacts.name: Availability Monitoring
artifacts.description: The documented availability target for the platform with its measurement methodology and exclusions, the uptime monitoring dashboard export, the configuration of health and monitoring checks such as load balancers and uptime probes, the periodic operational effectiveness reports covering transaction success rates, response times and error rates, and the periodic capacity management reports demonstrating headroom against forecast load.

artifacts.name: Cloud Contingency Plan
artifacts.description: The comprehensive cloud contingency plan addressing provider disruption, connectivity loss and legal-action scenarios; the documentation and diagram of redundant connectivity via different international cables and providers with diverse routes; and the signed connectivity contracts containing penalty clauses for disruption and downtime.

artifacts.name: Disaster Recovery Records
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery plan and procedures, the restoration test results and reports, and the environmental monitoring system configurations at the sites the failover targets.

artifacts.name: Audit Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The compliance documentation against the applicable regulatory circular governing audits and switchover planning, and the information systems audit plan with the latest reports executed under it.

BCD-12.2.notes: 41 asks across 7 frameworks. Redundant architecture, the failover test that proves it works, and the single-point-of-failure analysis that finds where it does not are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Capacity Management Plan
artifacts.description: The plan covering current and forecast capacity for critical resources, with the growth forecasts used as inputs and the procedure for initiating and maintaining it. SBP ETGRMF requires internal factors (growth, acquisitions, new products and technology) and external factors (customer demand) to be addressed explicitly; CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented plan.

artifacts.name: Capacity Monitoring Dashboard
artifacts.description: The monitoring dashboard tracking processing, memory, storage and bandwidth utilisation, the monitoring tool configuration, the resource utilisation trends, and the technology resource monitoring reports covering platform processing, storage and bandwidth.

artifacts.name: Capacity Thresholds and Alerting
artifacts.description: The defined capacity thresholds with the alert configuration and escalation paths, the escalation matrix, the sample alert response and resolution records, and the log of capacity incidents with the mitigation taken.

artifacts.name: Capacity Trend and Forecast Report
artifacts.description: The trend report showing utilisation over time with projected breach points, the capacity forecasts, and the periodic capacity planning review records confirming the forecast remains current.

artifacts.name: Performance Monitoring Reports
artifacts.description: The performance targets per service with the monitoring dashboards measuring against them, the performance baseline measurements, the system availability reports, and the operational effectiveness reports covering transaction success rates, response times and error rates.

artifacts.name: Scaling and Load Test Results
artifacts.description: The evidence of load or scaling tests demonstrating ability to meet forecast demand, and the auto-scaling or capacity expansion procedures that respond when thresholds are approached.

artifacts.name: Availability Architecture and SLA
artifacts.description: The documented availability target for the platform with its measurement methodology and exclusions, the high-availability and redundancy architecture diagram, the uptime monitoring dashboard export, and the capacity management reports demonstrating headroom against forecast load.

artifacts.name: Denial-of-Service Resilience Evidence
artifacts.description: The distributed denial-of-service mitigation service documentation and protection configuration, the network monitoring for denial-of-service indicators, and the mitigation controls applied at API endpoints with their capacity planning.

artifacts.name: Change Capacity Impact Assessment
artifacts.description: The capacity impact section completed on each change request and the pre- and post-change capacity comparison confirming the change did not consume unplanned headroom.

artifacts.name: Resource Optimisation and Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The database optimisation and archival records and the decommissioning records for unused systems, evidencing capacity is reclaimed rather than only added.

artifacts.name: Service Level Agreements and Performance
artifacts.description: The signed internal service level agreements between IT and the business covering availability, performance and capacity, the periodic performance reports, the breach register with remediation actions, and the review meeting minutes.

artifacts.name: IT Service Management Framework
artifacts.description: The documented ITSM framework covering preventive maintenance, incident and problem management and capacity, with management approval, the detailed process documents, the tool screenshots evidencing operation, and the KPI dashboard across components.

artifacts.name: Technology Currency and Resilience Assessment
artifacts.description: The ICT systems inventory with its currency assessment, the system update and maintenance records, and the technology resilience assessment evaluating whether the estate can carry forecast demand.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis for Availability
artifacts.description: The business impact analysis establishing availability requirements per service, with the risk assessment methodology and risk register entries carrying capacity risk.

artifacts.name: Data Storage Forecasting Records
artifacts.description: The documented storage forecasting, data processing considerations and service level specifications with their implementing procedures, the data architecture artifacts, the performance metrics dashboard, the compliance audit reports, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

CAP-01.notes: 85 asks across 15 frameworks. Capacity planning (forward-looking forecast) and performance monitoring (current-state telemetry) are kept apart because they are produced by different teams and tested separately; denial-of-service resilience is a third, distinct demand that arrives under the same control.

artifacts.name: Capacity Management Plan
artifacts.description: The plan covering current and forecast capacity for critical resources, the capacity management policy, the capacity plan with its forecasts, the capacity planning documentation and forecasts, the capacity forecasts themselves, the trend report showing utilisation over time with projected breach points, and the peak-load capacity assumptions behind them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented capacity and resource planning requirement. HITRUST requires the approved capacity management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Capacity Monitoring and Alerting
artifacts.description: The monitoring dashboard tracking processor, memory, storage and bandwidth utilisation; the cloud monitoring dashboard exports; the capacity monitoring reports; the resource utilisation metrics; the capacity utilisation tracking; the alert thresholds configured for capacity metrics with their escalation paths; the capacity threshold and escalation matrix; the monitoring tool configuration with its alert thresholds; the infrastructure monitoring dashboards and alert configurations; and the capacity planning and monitoring records showing thresholds against forecasts.

artifacts.name: Capacity Review Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining capacity monitoring scope, thresholds, review cadence and escalation; the periodic capacity review meeting minutes with forecasts, threshold breaches and decisions; the log of capacity-related incidents with the mitigation actions taken; the incident-driven capacity diagnostics; and the sample alert response and resolution records.

artifacts.name: Capacity Expansion and Scaling Evidence
artifacts.description: The auto-scaling or capacity expansion procedures, the evidence of load and scaling tests demonstrating ability to meet forecast demand, the database optimisation and archival records, and the decommissioning records for unused systems that release capacity back.

artifacts.name: Change Capacity Impact Assessment
artifacts.description: The capacity impact section of the change request form and the pre- and post-change capacity comparison evidencing the assessment was made and checked.

artifacts.name: Availability Performance Reporting
artifacts.description: The system availability reports and the performance metrics and service level compliance reports showing whether the capacity provisioned met the commitments made.

artifacts.name: Denial of Service Protection
artifacts.description: The protection service documentation, the protection configuration, the network monitoring for denial-of-service indicators, and the high-availability design for the public-facing channels.

artifacts.name: Contingency Plan and Recovery Objectives
artifacts.description: The contingency plan document with its review and approval records and distribution records, the recovery time and recovery point objectives it commits to, and the disaster recovery and backup capacity sizing documents provisioning for them. HITRUST requires the approved continuity development and implementation policy and standard with its implementing procedure and its periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Storage Forecasting Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented storage forecasting specification with its compliance evidence, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The risk assessment methodology documentation with its approval records, the risk register with entries, owners, ratings and treatment plans, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the capacity management requirements.

artifacts.name: Cloud Training Records
artifacts.description: The training curriculum with distinct modules for end-users and privileged users covering cloud usage, security and administration; the completion records showing both groups completed within the required period; and the assessment results certifying privileged users on cloud administration and security.

CAP-03.notes: 62 asks across 11 frameworks. The plan, the live monitoring and the change-time impact assessment are three separable proofs. Denial-of-service protection arrives via NIST SC-5 and QCB availability requirements and is kept out of the capacity artifacts because it answers a different threat.

artifacts.name: Performance Monitoring Dashboards
artifacts.description: The monitoring dashboards tracking processor, memory, storage and network utilisation, the monitoring agents deployed to collect them, the utilisation trend reports, the system resource monitoring dashboards, and the defined performance targets per service they are measured against.

artifacts.name: Capacity Thresholds and Alerting
artifacts.description: The defined capacity thresholds with the alert configuration and escalation matrix, the service availability alerting, the monitoring tool configuration with its alert thresholds, and the sample alert response and resolution records.

artifacts.name: Capacity Management Plan and Forecasts
artifacts.description: The capacity management plan with its forecasts, the capacity planning documentation, the capacity management reports, the peak-load capacity assumptions, and the incident-driven capacity diagnostics performed when a threshold is breached. HITRUST requires the approved capacity management standard with its implementing procedure and the planning records showing thresholds and forecasts.

artifacts.name: Cloud Capacity Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining capacity monitoring scope, thresholds, review cadence and escalation for cloud workloads; the utilisation dashboard exports from the cloud monitoring service; and the periodic capacity review meeting minutes recording forecasts, threshold breaches and decisions.

artifacts.name: Availability and Resilience Architecture
artifacts.description: The high-availability architecture diagram showing redundancy and workload distribution, the resilience architecture decision document, the health-check and uptime probe configuration, the redundant connectivity arrangements, the connectivity contracts with disruption penalty clauses, and the denial-of-service protection.

artifacts.name: System Availability Reports
artifacts.description: The system availability reports measured against target, and the environmental and building management monitoring dashboards covering the facilities the systems depend on.

artifacts.name: Batch Job Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The job schedule documentation with its authorisation, the monitoring dashboard or alert configuration, sample evidence of successful completion, the failure logs with resolution documentation, and for period-end the processing schedule, cutoff control configuration, period lock evidence and batch completion evidence.

artifacts.name: Interface Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The interface inventory and documentation, the monitoring and completion logs, the reconciliation reports for transferred data, and the investigation and resolution records for interface failures.

artifacts.name: Asset Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The documented criteria for prioritising assets by operational sensitivity, the priority asset list with its ratings, the monitoring reports showing performance against operational goals, and the records of periodic priority reviews.

artifacts.name: Resource Optimisation Records
artifacts.description: The database optimisation and archival records and the decommissioning records for unused systems, evidencing capacity is reclaimed rather than only monitored.

artifacts.name: Cloud Training Records
artifacts.description: The training curriculum with distinct modules for end users and privileged users covering cloud usage, security and administration; the completion records within the required period; and the certification results for privileged users.

artifacts.name: Capacity Risk Register
artifacts.description: The risk assessment methodology with its approval records and the risk register entries carrying capacity and availability risk with owners, ratings and treatment plans.

artifacts.name: Data Operations Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The documented database monitoring, storage KPI and service level specifications with their compliance evidence and implementation records, the performance metrics dashboard with targets and review records, the business intelligence artifacts reporting them, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

CAP-04.notes: 77 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps CAP-01; what is distinct here is measurement of running performance rather than forward capacity planning, so the monitoring telemetry, alert response and batch-job assurance lead.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining configuration standards, baselines and change controls; the configuration management policy and procedures documentation; the secure configuration process document; the configuration management procedures; and the policy review records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented operating system and compatibility requirements.

artifacts.name: Configuration Baselines
artifacts.description: The baseline configurations for each platform in use, the configuration baseline standards, the system configuration baselines, the hardening standards documentation, the network device configuration standards and hardening guides, the documentation of approved golden images for servers and workstations, and the removed services documentation showing what the baseline strips out.

artifacts.name: Baseline Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The compliance scan results against the baselines, the hardening verification reports, the configuration monitoring and baseline comparison reports, the configuration audit and verification reports, the configuration review records, and the sign-off records for systems before production deployment confirming the baseline was applied.

artifacts.name: Configuration Drift Detection
artifacts.description: The alert configuration for configuration drift with examples of drift detected and remediated, and the infrastructure-as-code repositories enforcing configuration consistency.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Database
artifacts.description: The configuration management database with its documentation, the configuration baselines and controlled configuration item records, and the configuration status and change tracking reports.

artifacts.name: Change Control Records
artifacts.description: The change management procedure with advisory board approvals and back-out plans, and the change records with their risk classification. HITRUST requires the approved change control procedures policy and standard with its implementing procedure, its awareness communications and its periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Security Monitoring Configuration
artifacts.description: The security information platform configuration, the infrastructure monitoring tool configurations with their alert rules, and the vulnerability scanning schedules, tools and reports covering the configured estate.

artifacts.name: Access Restriction Configuration
artifacts.description: The matrix of permissions per role in each business application, the role-based access matrix, the attribute-based access control policy configuration with its attributes and rules, the evidence of row and column-level security in databases and data platforms, the access decision audit log showing granted and denied decisions, the access review outputs per application signed off by business owners, and the periodic assessment identifying over-privileged accounts with its remediation actions.

artifacts.name: Data Leakage Prevention Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining scope, detection strategy and response; the rule export covering mail, endpoint, web and cloud channels; the cloud storage configuration; the platform dashboard showing coverage; the endpoint control preventing or monitoring transfers to removable media; the log of alerts triggered, triaged and investigated; and the playbook defining response steps for confirmed leakage events.

artifacts.name: Security Programme Governance
artifacts.description: The security programme charter, the information security policy manual, the security violation incident log, and the corrective action records arising from it.

artifacts.name: Storage Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented storage management specification with its compliance evidence, the implementing procedures and process workflows, the implementation evidence demonstrating the outcome, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

CFG-01.notes: 60 asks across 11 frameworks. ISO 27001 A.8.3 access restriction and A.8.12 data leakage prevention arrive through adjacent crosswalks and are kept as their own artifacts rather than absorbed into configuration management.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Policy & Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved policy and supporting procedure for secure configuration: who defines baselines, what industry standard they derive from, how baselines are approved, applied, reviewed and retired, how deviations are requested and authorized, and how configuration documentation is itself maintained. Must require the most restrictive settings consistent with operational need and place baselines under configuration control across the system life cycle.

artifacts.name: System Hardening Standards & Baseline Library
artifacts.description: The documented secure baseline for every technology type in scope, each traceable to an industry-accepted source (CIS Benchmarks, DISA STIG, or vendor hardening guide) with documented justification for any local variation. Coverage must include server operating systems, workstations, mobile and endpoint devices, network devices and firewalls, wireless access points, databases, hypervisors and virtual machines, cloud services and cloud accounts, major and minor applications, containers and images, embedded and multifunction devices, and infrastructure services such as DNS, NTP, email and internet gateways. Each baseline must state the hardware, software, firmware and documentation it covers, the services and default accounts to be removed or disabled, and the approved services list. SCF requests these per asset class (E-AST-13 through E-AST-21).

artifacts.name: Golden Images & Infrastructure-as-Code Definitions
artifacts.description: The machine-readable form of the baseline: golden or gold-standard image documentation, baseline configuration files, infrastructure-as-code repositories and their commit history, and the CI/CD pipeline configuration that deploys them. Must show that the deployed baseline is the approved one and that changes to it go through source control rather than manual edit.

artifacts.name: Configuration Compliance Scan Reports
artifacts.description: Output from the tooling that measures live systems against the approved baseline: benchmark compliance reports, hardening verification and configuration compliance scans, baseline comparison reports, drift alerts, and vulnerability scan results where they evidence configuration weakness. Must cover the in-scope estate rather than a sample of convenience, show scan date and coverage percentage, and be paired with the remediation tracker for non-compliant findings.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Database Extract
artifacts.description: The CMDB or asset/configuration item inventory showing each in-scope asset, its type and owner, the baseline applied to it, its current configuration state and its change history. Must reconcile to the asset inventory so that no in-scope system is outside baseline coverage. Several frameworks pair the baseline requirement explicitly with maintaining inventories.

artifacts.name: Baseline Review & Hardening Sign-off Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that baselines are reviewed and that systems are approved as hardened before they go live: periodic baseline review records with reviewer, date and outcome, and pre-production or pre-acceptance hardening sign-off per system — including vendor-supplied equipment accepted into the estate. Review frequency varies by framework: at least annually in most, semi-annually or biannually in some banking frameworks, and on any significant change or life-cycle event. SCF requests the review evidence as E-AST-12.

artifacts.name: Configuration Deviation & Exception Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved departures from baseline: the system and setting affected, the business justification, compensating controls, the approver, and the expiry or review date. Must include insecure services, protocols and ports that remain enabled with their documented mitigations, retained default accounts, and any baseline setting relaxed for operational need. Open items must be tracked to closure.

artifacts.name: Endpoint & Device Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that endpoint baseline settings are enforced in practice, exported from the managing system (group policy, MDM or endpoint management): session lock and inactivity timeout, device lockout thresholds, autorun/autoplay disabled, removable media scanning and USB control, anti-exploitation and exploit protection features, host firewall enabled with default-deny, and endpoint protection deployment coverage. Must show both the configured policy and the deployment coverage across the endpoint fleet.

artifacts.name: Network & Perimeter Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration state for the network layer against its baseline: network security control rulesets with explicit deny, firewall configurations per host, VLAN and management-network segmentation, network architecture and DNS architecture diagrams showing trust zones, gateway and next-generation firewall configuration, wireless access point settings including disabling capabilities not in use, and hypervisor, virtual network and VM isolation controls. Must include the ruleset review records that show the configuration is periodically re-justified.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic & Transmission Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration proving the baseline's cryptographic requirements are enforced: TLS/SSL protocol and cipher configuration with certificate inventory, VPN and circuit encryption configuration, email encryption implementation, transmission integrity and message authentication settings, and the configuration protecting stored authentication secrets. Must show that deprecated protocols and weak ciphers are disabled on in-scope systems.

artifacts.name: Authentication & Access Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: The identity-related settings within the baseline, exported from the systems that enforce them: MFA coverage, conditional access policy, authentication protocol configuration, password and lockout settings, role-based access and segregation-of-duties configuration, application access control matrices and data access restrictions, default and built-in account handling, and failed-authentication monitoring. Must demonstrate least privilege as configured, not merely as intended.

artifacts.name: Logging & Time Synchronization Configuration
artifacts.description: Baseline settings for audit logging and time: audit log enablement across system components with a coverage map and SIEM source inventory, the log format standard with sample entries showing required fields, log retention configuration, and the time synchronization architecture — authorized time sources, NTP configuration and authentication on all systems, restriction of who may change time settings, and drift monitoring. Log review records evidence that the configuration produces usable output.

artifacts.name: Configuration Change Management Records
artifacts.description: Change records for modifications to baselines and to configured systems: raised change requests with risk classification, approval (including CAB minutes where used), test plans and results, back-out plans, emergency change handling with post-implementation review, and the version control history for configuration artifacts. Must show that configuration changes are controlled rather than ad hoc, and that the baseline documentation was updated to match.

artifacts.name: Secure Design & Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The design-side inputs the baseline derives from: security architecture documentation, secure design principles and security engineering review records, the application security requirements catalogue and API security standard, threat modelling artifacts, secure SDLC documentation with security review gates, and evaluation records for acquired software. Frameworks that require attack surface reduction expect the threshold to be stated here and reflected in the baselines.

artifacts.name: Secure Configuration Training & Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the people who build and operate systems know the baseline requirements: training program documentation and curriculum for administrators and developers, completion records, awareness campaign materials, and training effectiveness assessment. Required where frameworks tie configuration control to demonstrated personnel competence.

CFG-02.notes: 257 entries collapse to 15. The largest cluster is 'the hardening standard for platform X' repeated across servers, workstations, network devices, databases, hypervisors, gateways, DNS, NTP, email, wireless, printers, mobile and cloud — one baseline library, not 45 requests. The remaining clusters are the four things a baseline needs to be credible: the images/IaC that build it, the scans that prove drift-free state, the sign-offs that approve it, and the exception register for what deviates. This control has 17 mapped collectors (Security Hub, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps, Kandji, SentinelOne, Snyk, SonarCloud, Tenable, 1Password, Tailscale, Vercel, Render, DigitalOcean, ServiceNow, Semgrep), so scan reports, IaC state, endpoint settings and logging configuration are marked automated or hybrid accordingly.

artifacts.name: Baseline Review Records
artifacts.description: The baseline review and update records, the biannual review records, the process review records, and the configuration audit and verification reports evidencing the baselines were revisited on schedule.
