NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented review-and-update-logged-events requirement.

artifacts.name: Configuration Baselines
artifacts.description: The policy defining configuration standards, baselines and change controls; the baseline configurations for each platform in use; the baseline configuration documentation per technology product; the configuration baseline standards; the hardening baselines against recognised benchmarks; the hardening standards documentation; the system configuration baselines; the manufacturer and benchmark mapping; the documentation of approved golden images; the infrastructure-as-code repositories enforcing consistency; and the removed services documentation. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented change management baseline requirement.

artifacts.name: Baseline Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The compliance scan results against the baselines, the configuration compliance scan results, the hardening verification reports, the alert configuration for drift with examples detected and remediated, the sign-off records for systems before production deployment confirming the baseline was applied, and the configuration status and change tracking reports.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Database
artifacts.description: The configuration management database with its documentation, recording the configuration each managed component currently holds.

artifacts.name: Change Management Records
artifacts.description: The change management policy and procedures, the change request and approval records with the advisory board minutes, the change testing and validation documentation, and the emergency change procedures with their post-implementation reviews.

artifacts.name: Periodic Compliance Review
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence; the latest four quarters of review reports; the evidence that reviews are performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task being reviewed; the management sign-off records; and the tracker of issues identified with their closure status.

CFG-02.1.notes: 40 asks across 11 frameworks. Overlaps CFG-01 and CFG-02.2; what is distinct here is the review cadence itself — the record that baselines were revisited and updated on schedule.

artifacts.name: Security Configuration Baselines
artifacts.description: The security configuration baselines and benchmarks, the system baseline configuration documentation, the documented baselines for cloud-hosted systems, the configuration baselines and controlled configuration item records, the hardening guides, the hardening standards documentation, the system configuration baselines, the removed services documentation, and the baseline review and update records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented change management baseline requirement.

artifacts.name: Automated Compliance Scanning
artifacts.description: The configuration compliance scan results, the configuration compliance scanning reports, the periodic baseline compliance reports from cloud-native tooling, the dashboard export showing compliance scores against the baselines with trends, the configuration audit and verification reports, the configuration review reports, the configuration accuracy verification records, and the hardening verification reports.

artifacts.name: Drift Detection and Remediation
artifacts.description: The tracker of baseline non-compliance items with remediation status, the deviation remediation records, and the configuration status and change tracking reports. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented detection of baseline deviation requirement.

artifacts.name: Deviation Exception Records
artifacts.description: The deviation approval records recording the baseline settings deliberately not applied with their justification and expiry. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented exception management requirement.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Database
artifacts.description: The configuration management database with its documentation, recording what each managed component is currently configured to.

artifacts.name: Automated Security Tooling
artifacts.description: The inventory of cloud-native security tools deployed, the configuration export of security baselines and guardrails enforced by policy engines, and the automation workflows for automated response, remediation and notification.

artifacts.name: Change Management Records
artifacts.description: The change management policy and procedures, the change request and approval records with the advisory board minutes, the change testing and validation documentation, the change test plans and results demonstrating testing before production deployment, the pipeline configuration, and the emergency change procedures with their post-implementation reviews.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties in Configuration
artifacts.description: The role definition document, the identity and access configuration evidence showing segregation of duties across infrastructure, security and application roles, and the segregation of duties matrix with verification that no single role spans incompatible functions.

artifacts.name: Monitoring and Alerting Records
artifacts.description: The log monitoring and alerting evidence, the anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records, the alert triage and escalation procedures, and the operations centre procedures covering configuration alerts.

CFG-02.2.notes: 45 asks across 7 frameworks. The baseline, the automated detection of drift from it, and the exception process for approved deviations are three proofs; the exception register is kept separate because a low drift count means nothing without it.

artifacts.name: Rollback Plans
artifacts.description: The documented rollback plans for each change to production systems, the change records with their rollback plans, the defined rollback strategy for failed patches, the documented alternative recovery options for non-rollback scenarios, and the log of actual rollback invocations with their outcomes.

artifacts.name: Rollback Test Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of rollback plan testing and the records of vulnerability testing before patch deployment establishing that the rollback path was exercised before it was needed.

artifacts.name: Device Configuration Backup
artifacts.description: The policy mandating regular backup of all device configurations, the backup scheduler configuration with job completion logs for device configurations, the inventory of backed-up device configurations with last-backup date, and the evidence of periodic configuration restoration testing.

artifacts.name: Baseline Configuration Records
artifacts.description: The system baseline configuration documentation, the configuration management database, and the baseline review and update records preserving what the configuration was before the change.

artifacts.name: Version Control Records
artifacts.description: The version control repository access reports, the repository access control configuration, the commit history samples with ticket references, and the release baseline tagging evidence.

artifacts.name: Change Control Records
artifacts.description: The change management policy, the change management procedures, the change records, the change request tickets with their required fields, the business justification documentation, the approval documentation, the business impact assessment templates, the change log completeness verification, and the change management system reports.

artifacts.name: Production Data Access Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented production data access control specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures implementing it, and the data security control evidence including access controls.

CFG-02.3.notes: 32 asks across 7 frameworks. The retained previous configuration, the rollback plan that uses it and the test proving the rollback works are three proofs; device configuration backup is kept separate from application rollback.

artifacts.name: Hardening Baselines
artifacts.description: The system baseline configuration documentation, the system configuration baselines, the hardening standards documentation, the system hardening documentation, the application hardening checklists, the hardening template documentation, the security configuration documentation, the benchmark application records, and the baseline review and update records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented application security baseline requirements.

artifacts.name: Baseline Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The configuration compliance results against the baselines, the hardening verification reports, the feature enablement review, and the configuration management database recording what is deployed.

artifacts.name: Service and Port Restrictions
artifacts.description: The approved software and service list, the port and protocol restrictions, the unnecessary service removal records, and the removed services documentation showing what the baseline strips out.

artifacts.name: Network Security Control Configuration Standard
artifacts.description: The approved configuration standard defining ruleset baselines, defaults, naming, documentation requirements and review cadence; the sample configurations from production firewalls, routers and security groups demonstrating implementation; and the version history and maintenance records of the standard with reviewer and approver.

artifacts.name: Multi-Connected Device Controls
artifacts.description: The approved standard defining specific configuration settings for devices that connect to both trusted and untrusted networks, the evidence preventing devices from being actively connected to an untrusted network while concurrently connected to the protected one, the inventory of in-scope devices with their compliance status against the standard, and the device management configuration export showing the enforced settings.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Enablement Coverage
artifacts.description: The configuration export evidencing audit log enablement on all in-scope system components, the coverage map showing every component is producing audit logs, the inventory of integrated log sources feeding the aggregation platform, and the sample live audit logs.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Field Standard
artifacts.description: The documented standard listing the required fields per audit log entry including user identification, event type and date and time; the logging configuration export demonstrating capture of all required fields; and the sample log entries from in-scope systems showing every required field populated.

artifacts.name: Time Synchronisation Configuration
artifacts.description: The architecture document showing time-synchronisation technology deployed to all in-scope components, the configuration export from sample components, the sample output demonstrating active synchronisation, the documented standard specifying authoritative internal time sources traceable to a reliable external source, the configuration evidence showing all systems set to the correct and consistent time, and the time drift monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Time Source Access Controls
artifacts.description: The list of authorised internal and external time sources accepted by in-scope systems, the access control configuration restricting modification of time-sync settings to authorised personnel, and the audit logs of any modifications to those settings.

artifacts.name: Authentication and Session Configuration
artifacts.description: The password policy documentation, the system password configuration, the password compliance reports, the remote desktop and secure shell security settings, the remote access encryption configuration, and the session encryption evidence for the high-risk components.

artifacts.name: Data Leakage Prevention Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining scope, detection strategy and response; the rule export covering mail, endpoint, web and cloud channels; the cloud storage configuration; the platform dashboard showing coverage; the endpoint control preventing or monitoring transfers to removable media; the log of alerts triggered, triaged and investigated; and the playbook defining response steps for confirmed leakage events.

CFG-02.5.notes: 55 asks across 6 frameworks. PCI DSS 10.6 time synchronisation and 10.2 log field standards arrive here through the configuration crosswalk; they are genuinely configuration baselines for high-risk components and are kept as their own artifacts rather than merged into the hardening baseline.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Change Detection
artifacts.description: The configuration of drift detection tooling flagging unauthorised changes, the sample alert logs of detected drift events, the unauthorised change detection logs, and the configuration compliance scan results against the baselines.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Change Register
artifacts.description: The register listing unauthorised configuration changes detected with rollback or formal approval evidence, the register of identified policy violations with severity and remediation, the log of other conditions identified as potentially increasing breach risk with their mitigation actions, the incident response records for unauthorised changes, and the unauthorised software removal records.

artifacts.name: Change Restoration Records
artifacts.description: The change restoration records evidencing the configuration was returned to its approved state. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented change restoration requirement.

artifacts.name: Control Failure Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The procedure for detecting and addressing failures of each listed critical security control system, the service-provider variant of that procedure, the alert configuration covering those systems, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, the sample failure alert logs, the sample failure alerts with their triage and resolution records, the documented response procedure covering restoring security functions and identifying cause and duration, the response records demonstrating prompt addressing, the sample incident response records for past failures, the mean-time-to-restore metrics, and the lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Configuration Baselines and Exceptions
artifacts.description: The security configuration baselines and benchmarks, the system configuration baselines, the hardening guides and standards documentation, the hardening verification reports, the removed services documentation, the deviation approval records, the exception documentation, and the monthly review records.

CFG-02.8.notes: 32 asks across 7 frameworks. Detection of the unauthorised change, the register recording it and the restoration that reverses it are three proofs; PCI DSS 10.7's control-failure response is kept whole.

artifacts.name: Secure Baseline Configuration Standards
artifacts.description: The approved hardening baselines themselves, one per deployed technology type, stating which functions, ports, protocols, services, software and utilities are enabled and which are prohibited or removed. Coverage must span server-class and workstation-class operating systems, network devices, mobile devices, databases, hypervisors/virtual machines, cloud services, major and minor applications, and embedded technologies. Baselines must be traceable to a recognised source (CIS Benchmarks, STIG or documented internal equivalent) and be the most restrictive configuration consistent with operational need.

artifacts.name: Configuration Management Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: Board or management approved policy establishing least functionality as a requirement, plus the procedure implementing it: how baselines are authored, approved, applied, reviewed and changed; who owns each; how exceptions are handled; and the restrictions on use of system utilities and remote diagnostic/configuration ports. HITRUST expects the procedure as a distinct work instruction referencing the parent policy, plus awareness communications showing personnel were informed. NIST 800-171 expects records that least functionality is not just documented but operating.

artifacts.name: Baseline Review, Change Approval and Sign-Off Records
artifacts.description: Records showing baselines stay current and changes to them are controlled: the periodic review of each baseline for continued applicability, the change management records for configuration changes, version control evidence for baseline documents, reviews of newly enabled features or services, and the pre-production sign-off confirming the baseline was applied to a system before deployment. QCB requires the configuration review at least quarterly; other frameworks state a defined periodic cadence without a fixed interval.

artifacts.name: Approved Ports, Protocols, Services and Software Register
artifacts.description: A single authoritative register of everything permitted to run or traverse: each allowed service, daemon, port, protocol and software package, with the business justification, the system or network scope it applies to, the named approver and the approval date. Must also record allowed inbound flows with source, port, protocol and destination component. PCI DSS requires the business need and approval documented per entry; NIST 800-53 and CIS CSC require the approved software/service list to be the basis for restriction.

artifacts.name: Firewall and Network Security Control Ruleset Exports
artifacts.description: Live configuration exports of the network security controls enforcing the restrictions: perimeter rulesets at every trusted/untrusted boundary, inbound rules limiting untrusted traffic to authorised publicly accessible components and stateful responses, default-deny evidence for everything else, per-host or per-VM firewall configuration, and the register classifying each network as trusted or untrusted with its enforcement point. Rulesets must be accompanied by the periodic ruleset review records showing date, reviewer and outcome.

artifacts.name: Network Architecture and Defence-in-Depth Design Documentation
artifacts.description: Current, version-controlled network architecture and segmentation diagrams showing components, trust zones, interconnections, data flows and the placement of security controls at each boundary, including the dedicated management VLAN. Supporting design documentation must evidence defence-in-depth: IDS/IPS deployment points, monitoring coverage including any 24/7 SOC roster, and the single-point-of-failure review. Diagrams must be dated and approved.

artifacts.name: Completed Hardening Checklists and Removal Verification
artifacts.description: Per-system proof that the baseline was actually applied: completed hardening checklists naming the system, the person who applied it and the date; verification reports or command output confirming unnecessary services, daemons, functions, utilities and software were disabled or removed; documentation of what was removed; and the applied resource limits and role-based restrictions for virtual machines and hypervisors. PCI DSS accepts sample command or script output (for example service enumeration) as the confirmation.

artifacts.name: Configuration Compliance Scan and Drift Reports
artifacts.description: Automated compliance scan results measuring live systems against the approved baselines, with pass/fail per check, the systems in scope, and the remediation of failures. Include the drift detection alert configuration and worked examples of drift detected and corrected. HITRUST additionally attaches the vulnerability scanning reports with remediation timing and the patch deployment records with the exception register, as the corrective side of the same loop.

artifacts.name: Golden Image and Infrastructure-as-Code Evidence
artifacts.description: Documentation of the approved golden images for servers and workstations, and evidence of the infrastructure-as-code repositories (for example Terraform, Ansible, Chef) that enforce configuration consistency at build time, showing that the restrictive baseline is the default state rather than a post-build correction.

artifacts.name: Insecure Service and Configuration Exception Register
artifacts.description: Register of every deviation from the baseline still in use: the insecure or non-standard service, protocol, port or setting; the business justification; the risk acceptance and named approver; the compensating control applied to each (for example IPSec wrapping, IP allow-listing, application-layer protection); and the expiry or review date. PCI DSS requires configuration evidence of the compensating controls actually implemented, not just their description.

artifacts.name: Management and Diagnostic Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that administrative, diagnostic and configuration access paths are restricted to what is essential: the whitelist of permitted diagnostic and configuration ports, the list of workstations authorised to perform remote diagnostics, the access logs for remote diagnostic sessions, and the network access controls limiting who can connect at all (port security and MAC filtering, 802.1X/NAC, AAA server deployment, encrypted management protocols with multi-factor authentication). Includes the modem inventory showing dial-up/out-of-band access disabled by default with authorisation records for any enabled use. HITRUST additionally requires physical protection evidence for the ports themselves via badge/visitor logs and CCTV records.

artifacts.name: Removable Media and Peripheral Port Restriction Configuration
artifacts.description: Endpoint configuration restricting non-essential peripheral functionality: USB and removable media port disablement or monitoring policy and its enforced configuration, auto-run/auto-play disablement, the mandatory scanning requirement for removable media, and the isolated environment provided where media must be accessed.

artifacts.name: Data Egress Control and Web Isolation Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration and operating evidence for the controls restricting outbound data paths: the data leakage prevention policy defining scope, detection strategy and response; the DLP ruleset covering email, endpoint, web and cloud storage channels; the platform dashboard showing coverage; the alert and investigation log; the incident response playbook for confirmed leakage; and the documentation and assessment of any web browsing isolation solution deployed.

artifacts.name: Application and Data Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that application and data-layer capability is likewise restricted to what is needed: the permission matrix per role for each business application, configuration of row or column level restriction in databases and data platforms, any attribute-based access policy configuration, the periodic least-privilege assessment identifying over-privileged accounts with remediation, the business-owner-signed application access review outputs, and the access decision audit log showing grants and denials.

CFG-03.notes: 109 manual entries across 12 frameworks collapsed to 14 artifacts. No collectors are wired to this control, but most of the substance (baseline compliance state, firewall rules, service inventories, endpoint port policy) is genuinely connector-collectable, so several items are hybrid. Note that some source entries map loosely: ISO 27001 A.8.12 (DLP) and A.8.3 (application access) were mapped to this control by the crosswalk and are preserved as two clearly-scoped artifacts rather than being forced into the hardening items. QCB contributes a wide spread of network-layer restriction asks that cluster into boundary configuration, network design and management-port protection.

artifacts.name: Network Control Configuration Review
artifacts.description: The last two cycles of network security control configuration review reports at six-monthly intervals with reviewer, scope and conclusions; the reviewer and approver sign-off records; and the tracker of follow-up actions resulting from those reviews with closure status.

artifacts.name: Quarterly Compliance Review
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence; the latest four quarters of review reports; the evidence that reviews are performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task being reviewed; the management sign-off records; and the tracker of issues identified with their closure status.

artifacts.name: Annual Scope Review
artifacts.description: The annually-confirmed scope document including all data flows, the locations of regulated data and the identification of connected components; the documented scoping validation methodology aligned with the standards body's guidance; the validation results from data discovery scans, network analysis and interviews; and the records of scope reviews performed upon significant changes.

artifacts.name: Technology End-of-Life Review
artifacts.description: The inventory of hardware and software technologies in use with vendor, version and end-of-life information; the annual review report assessing each technology against vendor support, security advisories and emerging threats; and the action plans for technologies nearing end of vendor support or no longer adequately supporting security.

artifacts.name: Awareness Programme Review
artifacts.description: The annual review records of the awareness programme with reviewer and findings, the documentation evidencing programme currency including the most recent threat-landscape inputs, and the update records reflecting newly identified threats and vulnerabilities.

artifacts.name: Awareness Training Records
artifacts.description: The approved awareness training curriculum covering threats and vulnerabilities and the handling of regulated data, the learning management records evidencing training upon hire and at least once every twelve months, the personnel acknowledgments confirming understanding of the policies, and the phishing simulation campaign results with their remediation activities.

artifacts.name: Targeted Risk Analysis Library
artifacts.description: The library of targeted risk analyses for each requirement that specifies one, the documented methodology covering identification of assets, threats, impacted controls and the factors leading to likelihood and impact, the tracker of all analyses with last-review and next-review dates, and the management review and acceptance records for each.

artifacts.name: Payment Page Integrity Monitoring
artifacts.description: The configuration of the change and tamper-detection mechanism alerting personnel to unauthorised modification of payment pages, the records demonstrating the evaluation cadence, the targeted risk analysis defining that cadence where the default is not used, and the sample alerts with their response records.

artifacts.name: Configuration Restriction Records
artifacts.description: The approved software and service list, the port and protocol restrictions, the system hardening documentation, and the unnecessary service removal records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented application security baseline requirements; NIST 800-171 likewise for the restrict-nonessential-programs-and-services requirement.

artifacts.name: Secure Architecture Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented secure architecture principles, the reference architectures, the library of approved security patterns, the design documents for sample systems showing application of the principles, the architecture review board minutes showing security review, and the register of approved deviations from the reference architectures.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Review Records
artifacts.description: The vulnerability management policy covering scanning cadence, service levels, prioritisation and exception handling; the periodic scan reports covering internal and external assets; the remediation tracker showing open vulnerabilities with owners, service levels and closure status; the metrics showing remediation performance against those service levels; the annual penetration test reports with findings and remediation evidence; the records of patches deployed per system with success or failure and rollback; and the documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated immediately.

CFG-03.1.notes: 51 asks across 5 frameworks. PCI DSS contributes five separately-cadenced reviews — six-monthly ruleset, quarterly compliance, annual scope, annual technology, annual awareness — and each is kept distinct because an assessor samples each cadence on its own.

artifacts.name: Application Allow-List Policy
artifacts.description: The application allow-listing policy, the application allow-listing configuration documentation, the approved software and service list, the allow-list review records, and the whitelisting implementation with its exception records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented apply-allowlist-or-denylist requirement; CSA CCM likewise for the application and service approval requirement.

artifacts.name: Library Allow-List Controls
artifacts.description: The library allow-listing configuration, the authorised library inventory, and the library control testing results.

artifacts.name: Script Execution Controls
artifacts.description: The script execution policy configuration, the script inventory with its authorisation, and the digital signature verification records.

artifacts.name: System Utility Controls
artifacts.description: The system utilities inventory, the utility access control configuration, the authorisation records for utility access, and the utility usage monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Blocked and Removed Software Records
artifacts.description: The blocked execution logs, the unauthorised software removal records, the monthly review records, and the exception documentation for software permitted outside the allow-list.

artifacts.name: Service and Port Restrictions
artifacts.description: The port and protocol restrictions, the system hardening documentation, the hardening standards documentation, the system configuration baselines, the unnecessary service removal records, the removed services documentation, and the hardening verification reports. HITRUST requires the approved control of operational software policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the software restrictions, the periodic review records naming the reviewer, and the configuration baseline documentation with its hardening standards.

CFG-03.3.notes: 36 asks across 8 frameworks. Application allow-listing, library allow-listing and script control are three separate enforcement layers in CIS CSC and are kept apart; system utility control arrives via ADHICS and is a fourth.

artifacts.name: Change Management Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved policy and its implementing procedure covering change categories, assessment, approval paths, documentation, implementation and review. PCI DSS requires it to state the reason for change, the documented impact, approval by authorised parties, testing and a back-out plan; SOX requires annual review evidence and documented classification and prioritisation criteria; CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the document.

artifacts.name: Change Advisory Board Records
artifacts.description: The change advisory board or change management committee charter and membership, with the meeting minutes recording change review, decisions and approvals.

artifacts.name: Change Request and Approval Records
artifacts.description: Sample change tickets showing the full lifecycle: request, assessment, authorisation, implementation and closure, with approver identity and the workflow tool configuration behind them. PCI DSS additionally requires network security control change tickets to correlate to audit log entries from the management console.

artifacts.name: Change Impact and Security Assessment
artifacts.description: The impact assessment performed before approval, including the security impact analysis and business impact assessment template used. NIS2 requires security impact assessment on the change request form itself; SOC 2 extends this to business model and significant organisational changes with environmental scanning and threat intelligence input.

artifacts.name: Testing and Rollback Evidence
artifacts.description: Test evidence (UAT or regression) confirming control integrity after the change, the documented rollback or back-out plan for significant changes, and the change success metrics with failed-change analysis.

artifacts.name: Emergency Change Records
artifacts.description: The log of emergency changes with the post-implementation review evidence for each, showing the change was reviewed after the fact against the same criteria a planned change would meet.

artifacts.name: Post-Implementation Review Records
artifacts.description: Post-implementation review reports confirming the change achieved its intent and introduced no regression, with follow-up actions where it did not.

artifacts.name: Change Classification Scheme
artifacts.description: The documented scheme classifying changes by type, risk and urgency with the prioritisation criteria attached, and sample records showing changes classified under it.

artifacts.name: Software Installation Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The policy on permitted software, installation rights and the approval process, the approved software catalogue, the installed software inventory reconciled against it, the deployment tool configuration controlling distribution, evidence that standard users cannot install arbitrary software, and the shadow IT discovery report identifying unauthorised applications.

artifacts.name: Environment Separation Evidence
artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing separation between production and pre-production environments, the network security control configuration enforcing it, and the access control configuration preventing crossover.

artifacts.name: Post-Change Compliance Confirmation
artifacts.description: The documented definition of a significant change for this environment, a sample completed significant-change assessment, the records confirming all applicable requirements remain in place on new or changed systems, and the updated network and data-flow diagrams, scope documentation and inventories that follow.

artifacts.name: Quarterly Compliance Review Records
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence, the latest four quarters of review reports, evidence the reviews were performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task reviewed, management sign-off, and the remediation tracker with closure status.

artifacts.name: Management System Change Register
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for planning and controlling changes to the AI management system including impact analysis and approvals, the register of changes with rationale, impact, plan and post-implementation review, and the approval records signed by designated management.

artifacts.name: Data Model and Reference Data Change Records
artifacts.description: The documented change management specification for data architecture with its implementing procedures and process workflows, the reference and master data change request logs, the master register with golden-record definitions and stewardship records, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Change Tracking and Logging Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration or records demonstrating that system changes are tracked and logged, the change management technology in use, and the encryption change cost-benefit analysis where cryptographic changes are in scope.

artifacts.name: Security Programme Governance Records
artifacts.description: The information security policy manual and security programme charter under which change control operates, the security violation incident log, and the corrective action records arising from it.

artifacts.name: Upgrade Risk Assessment and Patch Compliance
artifacts.description: The risk assessment performed before upgrades and the patch compliance reports across asset classes that evidence the change programme is keeping the estate current.

CHG-01.notes: 108 asks across 18 frameworks — the widest crosswalk in the catalogue. The frameworks agree on the change lifecycle but each adds one distinct demand: PCI DSS a post-change compliance confirmation and environment separation, ISO 42001 a management-system change register, ISO 27001 software installation control, NDMO data-model change tracking. Those stay separate.

artifacts.name: Change Management Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved, current-version change management policy plus the implementing procedure. Must define which change types are configuration-controlled (system configs, security configs, patches, software updates, documentation, AI/AIMS changes where applicable), the request-assess-approve-implement-review lifecycle, roles and authorised approvers, change categories and risk classification, emergency-change handling and exception paths, and back-out requirements. Approval evidence differs by framework: HITRUST and SBP ETGRMF require board or executive management approval of the policy; PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and ADHICS accept documented management approval. Include the version history and the awareness communication that told personnel the requirement exists (HITRUST).

artifacts.name: Change Advisory Board Charter and Meeting Minutes
artifacts.description: The CAB/Change Control Board charter or terms of reference (membership, quorum, authority to approve or reject, escalation) together with meeting minutes for the audit period. Minutes must show the changes reviewed, the decision taken on each, attendees, and date. MAS TRM specifically requires the charter as a separate artifact; PCI DSS, ISO 27001, COBIT, SOC 2 and SBP ETGRMF require the minutes as approval evidence. SCF requests the CCB charter under its own evidence request list.

artifacts.name: Change Request Records with Approvals
artifacts.description: A sample of completed change tickets from the change system (ServiceNow, Jira, Remedy, Azure DevOps or equivalent) covering the audit period. Each record must show: reason for the change, documented impact, risk classification, approval by an authorised party before implementation, test results, back-out plan, and implementation date and performer. The sample must span the full declared scope - infrastructure and network/NSC changes, security configuration changes, patches and software updates, virtualisation and VM changes, production software releases and go-live events, encryption changes, and third-party-initiated changes. ISO 42001 requires the equivalent register for AIMS changes with rationale and post-implementation review.

artifacts.name: Change Impact and Security Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Documented impact and security risk analysis performed before approval, for a sample of changes. Must show the security consequences of the change were assessed, not just the operational ones - NIST 800-53 requires a formal security impact analysis and evidence of security engineering review against documented secure design principles and the security architecture; QCB requires a pre-implementation security assessment specifically for network changes; MAS TRM requires change risk and impact analysis with pre-implementation assessment documentation; SOC 2 extends the requirement to assessments of significant organisational and business-model changes, including the environmental scanning and threat intelligence inputs that trigger them.

artifacts.name: Change Testing and UAT Evidence
artifacts.description: Test evidence for a sample of changes demonstrating that control integrity was verified before promotion: UAT plans and results, regression or quality test output, a traceability matrix linking test cases to requirements, and user or business owner sign-off forms. PCI DSS requires the testing to confirm that in-scope security controls were not weakened by the change; QCB requires the signed user acceptance forms and traceability matrix as distinct artifacts; CSA CCM requires records showing quality testing actually operates in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Rollback and Back-out Plans
artifacts.description: Documented rollback or back-out plans for significant and high-risk changes, plus evidence of change restoration capability. Plans must cover activation criteria (when to invoke a back-out), scope, roles and responsibilities, escalation path and communication steps. ADHICS requires the plan to specify stakeholder responsibilities and escalation; COBIT requires rollback procedures inside release and deployment plans; CSA CCM requires records that change restoration is actually exercised in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Emergency Change Log and Post-Implementation Review Records
artifacts.description: The log of emergency and out-of-band changes for the period, with the retrospective approval and post-implementation review for each, plus PIR reports for significant planned changes. Records must show what was changed under emergency authority, who authorised it, and the review outcome including lessons learned and any corrective actions. Frameworks differ on trigger: ISO 27001 and SOC 2 require a PIR for every emergency change; COBIT, SBP ETGRMF, ADHICS and SL CSF require PIRs for major changes generally.

artifacts.name: Production Promotion and Test Data Removal Records
artifacts.description: The documented dev-to-production transition procedure together with promotion authorisation records for a sample of releases. Must include the production deployment or promotion checklist, evidence that test data and test accounts were removed before go-live (PCI DSS requires both the removal procedure and signed verification for recent deployments, plus a periodic scan of production for residual test accounts), authorisation records for each transition, and evidence that third-party developers are restricted to non-production environments. NDMO additionally requires the production data access control documentation and supporting access-control and encryption evidence.

artifacts.name: Change Tooling Configuration and Unauthorised-Change Detection Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration exports and screenshots of the change management workflow tool (approval routing, mandatory fields, gate enforcement) plus the technical detection layer that catches changes made outside it: change/configuration audit logs from NSC and management consoles correlated back to approved tickets, configuration version history, software installation approval logs, cloud change-detection tooling (AWS Config, Azure Policy, GCP SCC or equivalent) with its alert rules, and a sample of unauthorised-change alerts showing triage and remediation. NIST 800-171 requires records proving the track-and-log capability is operating, not just configured.

artifacts.name: Version Control and Migration Records
artifacts.description: Documentation of the version control system used to manage code and database migrations, plus records showing version control was applied to migrations into quarantine and production. Must show authorisation tied to each version via commit or tag (SBP ETGRMF), the branching and tagging naming policy, and the software repository with its version history (ADHICS). QCB additionally requires the migration policy, migration methodology, a migration runbook with timelines and owners, and stage-wise sign-off records for each migration stage.

artifacts.name: Software Installation Control Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that only approved software reaches endpoints and servers: the software installation policy (permitted software, installation rights, approval route), the approved software catalogue, the deployment tool configuration (SCCM, Intune, Jamf) that distributes it, proof that standard users lack local install rights, the installed-software inventory reconciled against the approved catalogue, approval records for non-standard installation requests, and a shadow-IT or CASB discovery report identifying unauthorised applications. ADHICS requires the authorised software installer list as a named artifact.

artifacts.name: Periodic Change Control Compliance Review Records
artifacts.description: Records of the recurring review that confirms the change process is being followed. PCI DSS service providers must perform this quarterly and produce the review procedure (scope, methodology, reviewer independence), the last four quarterly review reports, evidence the reviewer was independent of the task being reviewed, management sign-off on results, and a remediation tracker for issues found. ISO 27001 requires change success-rate metrics and failed-change analysis; NDMO requires periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions; QCB requires service-quality monitoring against the process.

artifacts.name: Third-Party and Cloud Provider Change Management Assurance
artifacts.description: Evidence that changes made by suppliers and cloud providers are governed to the same standard. Must include the change agreement or mutually agreed change management procedure signed by both parties covering request, approval, prioritisation, impact assessment, reporting and roles (SBP Cloud requires joint signature by the regulated entity and CSP), the documented patching and release timeframes by criticality, the CSP's advance change notifications with evidence of receipt and acknowledgement, the CSP's own change management control documentation as reviewed by the entity, and records demonstrating third-party adherence to the entity's change process.

artifacts.name: Post-Change Documentation Update Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that system documentation is updated as part of the change, not after the fact: the documentation standards to which updates must conform, the defined roles and responsibilities for documentation change management, records of documentation changes actually made against those standards with their approvals, updated process documents, and the CMDB or system documentation reflecting the post-change state.

CHG-02.notes: 146 manual evidence entries from 19 frameworks collapsed to 14 artifacts. Every input entry is assigned to exactly one artifact (verified: no duplicates, no gaps). The heaviest overlap was the policy/procedure layer (27 entries across 12 frameworks all asking for the same approved change management policy and its implementing procedure) and change ticket records (23 entries). Framework-specific specialisations kept separate because they are genuinely different documents to collect: software installation control (ISO/ADHICS), version control and migration records (SBP ETGRMF/QCB), CSP change management assurance (SBP Cloud), and PCI's quarterly compliance review cycle.

artifacts.name: Change Control Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved change control procedure covering reason for change, documentation of impact, approval by authorised parties and back-out planning; the change management policy and procedures; the change management policy applied to network connection changes; the change management procedures; and the approval authority matrix. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented change management technology requirement.

artifacts.name: Change Approval Records
artifacts.description: The change advisory board minutes and approval records, the change request and approval records, the change approval records in the ticketing system, the sample of changes with approval timestamps before deployment, the change records, the change request tickets with their required fields, the business justification documentation, and the parameter change approval records.

artifacts.name: Change Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The security impact analysis documentation, the change risk and impact analysis reports, and the pre-implementation assessment documentation preceding approval.

artifacts.name: Network Change Records
artifacts.description: The sample change tickets for network security control changes showing impact, testing, approval and back-out, and the audit log entries from the management consoles correlating actual changes to approved tickets.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Change Detection
artifacts.description: The reports from tools detecting unauthorised changes, the file integrity monitoring configuration with its alerts, the configuration monitoring and baseline comparison reports, the hash and integrity-check evidence on migrated programs, the change verification procedures for preventing unauthorised modifications, and the change verification records captured during migration. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented unauthorised change protection requirement.

artifacts.name: Software Installation Restrictions
artifacts.description: The software installation restriction policies and controls, the application allow-listing documentation, and the anti-malware and endpoint protection deployment evidence preventing unapproved software from running.

artifacts.name: Change Testing Evidence
artifacts.description: The test evidence confirming control integrity after change, the sample completed change tickets demonstrating all required elements, the change log completeness verification, and the change management system reports.

artifacts.name: Automated Calculation Controls
artifacts.description: The application configuration documentation, the automated calculation validation results, and the reconciliation of automated outputs to expected results confirming a change did not alter them.

artifacts.name: Management System Change Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for planning and controlling changes to the management system including impact analysis and approvals, the register of changes with rationale, impact, plan, approvals and post-implementation review, and the approval records signed by designated management.

artifacts.name: Production Data Access Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented production data access control specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures implementing it, and the data security control evidence including access controls.

CHG-02.1.notes: 47 asks across 10 frameworks. The control is that unauthorised changes are prevented and detected; the approval record and the detection of what bypassed it are kept apart because the second is the only proof the first is enforced.

artifacts.name: Change Management Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: Approved policy and the procedure implementing it, covering change categories and risk classification, the definition of a standard vs emergency change, request and approval paths, mandatory testing in a non-production environment before production, required documentation, back-out requirements, and post-implementation review. Must state the review cadence, name the approver with date, carry version history, and be supported by records showing personnel were informed of the requirement. Includes the production promotion SOP and system acceptance procedure where those are held separately.

artifacts.name: Change Records (RFC Sample)
artifacts.description: A sample of completed change tickets spanning the audit period, each showing the full lifecycle: reason for the change, risk classification, documented impact, approval by authorised parties with name and date, evidence of testing, and the back-out plan. PCI DSS requires all five elements present on every in-scope change; HITRUST additionally requires the risk classification and post-implementation review to appear on the record.

artifacts.name: Change Advisory Board Minutes
artifacts.description: Minutes of the CAB or Change Control Board covering the audit period, showing the changes reviewed, the attendees and their roles, the decisions reached and the conditions attached to approvals. Must be dated and traceable to the change records they approved.

artifacts.name: Change Impact and Security Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Completed impact assessments for a sample of changes, covering the security impact analysis required before approval, affected systems and dependencies, and the risk rating driving the approval path. Where the change is organisational or to the business model rather than technical, the assessment must show the same analysis was applied, informed by environmental scanning and threat intelligence.

artifacts.name: Rollback Plans and Pre-Change Backups
artifacts.description: Documented back-out or rollback plans for significant changes and the release/deployment plans that carry them, plus records of the backup taken before the change was applied and confirmation it was verified as restorable. Must be attached to or referenced from the corresponding change record.

artifacts.name: Test Plans and Test Cases
artifacts.description: Documented test plans and the test case library for changes and new systems: predetermined test data, processing-problem scenarios and business scenarios, UAT scenarios covering critical business cases, performance/load test plans for critical systems, and the traceability matrix linking requirements to test cases. Plans must be approved by management before execution.

artifacts.name: Test Results and User Acceptance Sign-off
artifacts.description: Executed test evidence from the non-production environment for a sample of changes, with the outcome recorded against each planned test case, the defects found and their closure status, and the signed acceptance by the business users and the testing owner before promotion. Must cover functional/regression testing confirming control integrity is preserved, UAT with named business-user sign-off, and performance test results for critical systems demonstrating acceptable operation prior to deployment. This is the single largest duplication in the input - every framework restates it.

artifacts.name: Software Installation Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The policy on permitted software and installation rights, the approved software catalogue and the deployment tooling configuration that distributes it, configuration proving standard users cannot install arbitrary software, the installed-software inventory reconciled against the catalogue, approval records for non-standard installation requests, and the discovery report identifying unauthorised or shadow applications.

artifacts.name: Emergency Change and Post-Implementation Review Records
artifacts.description: The log of emergency and expedited changes with the retrospective approval and post-implementation review for each, plus PIR reports and lessons learned for significant planned changes and the change success/failure metrics used to monitor the process. Must show the review actually occurred, who performed it and what corrective action followed a failed change.

artifacts.name: Secure Design, Code Review and Security Test Records
artifacts.description: Security architecture and secure design principles documentation, records of security engineering reviews, the secure SDLC documentation showing security checkpoints at design, code review and test, and the code review records and security testing results (SAST, DAST, penetration testing) produced before release.

artifacts.name: Significant-Change Reassessment Records
artifacts.description: The documented definition of a 'significant change' for this environment, and for a sample of such changes the completed reassessment confirming all applicable requirements remain in place on the new or changed systems and networks afterwards, together with the updated network and data-flow diagrams, scope documentation and inventories.

artifacts.name: Production Promotion and Release Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that promotion to production is gated on successful testing and explicit authorisation: the production promotion checklist, release and migration approval records tied to the test-completion confirmation, go-live sign-off, screenshots of the release tool showing the workflow and the enforced test gate, and the CI/CD pipeline configuration that blocks promotion until tests pass.

artifacts.name: Development, Test and Production Environment Separation Evidence
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure requiring separation of development, test and operational environments, plus the access control matrix and provisioning/review records showing that the same individuals do not hold conflicting access across those environments.

artifacts.name: Data Migration and Integration Testing Records
artifacts.description: For changes involving data movement or system interfaces: the documented data mapping and transformation specification, integration solution test evidence, data quality reports (profiling, validation rules, issue logs, cleansing records), the migration audit logs, and the data models/ERDs and API or interoperability documentation the migration was built against. Where data crosses organisational boundaries, include the data sharing agreements with their security, privacy and audit clauses.

artifacts.name: Configuration Baselines and Compliance Reports
artifacts.description: Documented configuration baselines (CIS Benchmarks or equivalent hardening standards) for the systems being changed, the configuration version history showing what changed and when, periodic baseline compliance reports from the scanning or cloud-native tooling, and the tracker of non-compliant items with owners and remediation status.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties in Change and Release
artifacts.description: The role definition document separating infrastructure, security and application configuration-management duties, the SoD matrix verifying no single role spans incompatible functions (notably that the person who develops or approves a change is not the person who promotes it), and the RBAC/IAM configuration export evidencing that separation in the live environment.

CHG-02.2.notes: 116 entries collapse to 16. The dominant duplication is testing: 21 input entries are all 'the test results and the sign-off on them' under different names (UAT, performance, system, regression, pre-production). Change tickets, CAB minutes and the policy account for another 30. Kept separate where the ask genuinely differs: significant-change reassessment (PCI-specific), environment separation (HITRUST 09.d), software installation control (ISO A.8.19), data/integration migration (NDMO, QCB) and cloud baselines/SoD (SBP Cloud). Git and ticketing collectors are connected, so PR/change records and pipeline test runs are partly automated; approvals and business sign-off are not.

artifacts.name: Security Impact Analysis Records
artifacts.description: The security impact analysis performed before a change is approved, the change risk and impact analysis reports, the risk analysis template used, the assessment of effects on upstream and downstream systems, and the pre-implementation assessment documentation. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement to analyse the security impact of changes.

artifacts.name: Change Management Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved change management policy and its implementing procedure covering assessment, approval, back-out and review. HITRUST requires separate approved standards for change management and for managing changes to third-party services; CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence for the change management technology and change agreements.

artifacts.name: Change Request Records with Impact Assessment
artifacts.description: The change request forms carrying the security impact assessment, the change records with risk classification, the tickets with their required fields, the change log completeness verification, and the business justification documentation.

artifacts.name: Change Approval Records
artifacts.description: The change advisory board minutes and decisions, the management approvals granted on the basis of the risk and impact analysis, the pre-implementation sign-off records evidencing assessment before implementation, and the approval workflow configuration.

artifacts.name: Rollback and Testing Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented rollback or back-out plans for significant changes, the pre-implementation testing results, and the configuration version history evidencing the prior state can be restored.

artifacts.name: Post-Implementation Review Records
artifacts.description: The post-implementation review records confirming the change achieved its intent without regression, the emergency change documentation with its after-the-fact review, and the reassessment triggers and outputs where conditions change after implementation.

artifacts.name: Post-Change Compliance Confirmation
artifacts.description: The documented definition of a significant change, a sample completed significant-change assessment, the records confirming applicable requirements remain in place on new or changed systems, and the updated diagrams, scope documentation and inventories that follow.

artifacts.name: Test Data and Account Removal Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for removing test data and accounts before production release, the deployment checklist covering it, sample sign-off records for recent deployments, and the periodic scan of production for residual test accounts.

artifacts.name: Cloud Provider Change Governance
artifacts.description: The change management procedure jointly agreed and signed with the provider covering request, approval and prioritisation; the provider's own change management control documentation reviewed by the organisation; the advance change notification records received and acknowledged; and the documented timeframes for patching and releases by criticality.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Change Detection
artifacts.description: The cloud change-detection tooling configuration, the automated alerting rules for unauthorised configuration changes, and sample unauthorised-change alerts with their triage and remediation records.

artifacts.name: AI System Impact Assessment Process
artifacts.description: The documented process covering the circumstances that require an assessment and its elements — identification, analysis, evaluation, treatment and documentation; the standard templates for performing and recording it; and the register of triggers and criteria such as criticality, complexity and sensitivity that initiate or rescope one.

artifacts.name: AI Impact Assessment Repository
artifacts.description: The repository of completed AI system impact assessments recording intended use, positive and negative impacts and predictable consequences, with the retention policy defining how long the results are kept.

artifacts.name: Business and Organisational Change Assessment
artifacts.description: The management of change procedures for significant organisational changes, the business model change impact assessments, the change management risk assessment process, the business impact assessment templates, and the environmental scanning and threat intelligence reports that trigger them.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Change Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses and right-to-audit, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records, covering changes the organisation does not itself make.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the change management requirements and their obligation to have changes assessed before implementation.

CHG-03.notes: 77 asks across 16 frameworks. Distinct from CHG-01 in that the demand here is the analysis performed before a change is approved, not the change process itself. Cloud provider-initiated change (SBP Cloud 10.1) is kept separate because the organisation assesses rather than authors it.

artifacts.name: Change Access Restriction
artifacts.description: The change access control procedures, the authorised change personnel list, the migration access privilege reports, the migration procedure documentation, the developer against migrator access privilege reports, the production access restriction evidence, and the compensating control documentation where separation is not achievable.

artifacts.name: Automated Pipeline Controls
artifacts.description: The automated pipeline configuration with its approval gates, the deployment logs with their change ticket references, the commit history samples with ticket references, the release baseline tagging evidence, the repository access control configuration, and the version control repository access reports.

artifacts.name: Migration Logs
artifacts.description: The logs of activities performed during migration processes, the evidence that logging is enabled during migration, the retention policy for those logs, the records of migration log reviews, and the migration log review for segregation-of-duties compliance.

artifacts.name: Change Access Audit Records
artifacts.description: The change access audit logs, the change activity logs, and the semi-annual change process review reports.

artifacts.name: Change Verification and Integrity
artifacts.description: The procedures for verifying changes and preventing unauthorised modifications, the records of change verification activities during migration, and the hash and integrity-check evidence on migrated programs.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Change Detection
artifacts.description: The reports from tools detecting unauthorised changes, the unauthorised change detection logs, and the incident response records for unauthorised changes. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented unauthorised change protection and change restoration requirements.

CHG-04.1.notes: 31 asks across 5 frameworks. The restriction on who may make a change, the pipeline that enforces it and the migration log that records what passed through are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Change Management Procedure
artifacts.description: The change management policy and procedure, the change management procedure with advisory board approvals and back-out plans, the change request records with their impact assessment, the change records with their risk classification, the change advisory board meeting minutes, the change request and approval records, the change testing and validation documentation, the roll-back plans for changes, the configuration version history, the emergency change procedures with their post-implementation reviews, and the post-implementation review records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented change agreements requirement. HITRUST requires the approved change management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Customer Change and Outage Notifications
artifacts.description: The planned maintenance notification records, the unplanned outage notification and status update records, the incident communication procedures for availability events, and the status page or system health dashboard through which they are published.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Change Notifications
artifacts.description: The procedure requiring notification of material changes to the sector regulator and response team within the prescribed period and the records and correspondence of those notifications with timestamps.

artifacts.name: Stakeholder Communication Strategy
artifacts.description: The stakeholder communication strategy and plans, the board and management reporting packages, the governance reporting templates and dashboards, and the stakeholder satisfaction survey results measuring whether the communication lands.

artifacts.name: AI Impact Assessment Process
artifacts.description: The documented impact assessment process covering the circumstances that require one and its elements of identification, analysis, evaluation, treatment and documentation; the standard templates for performing and documenting them; the register of triggers and criteria that initiate or rescope an assessment; the repository of completed assessments with intended use and predictable impacts; and the retention policy defining how long results are kept.

artifacts.name: Encryption Change Analysis
artifacts.description: The cost-benefit analysis performed before changing cryptographic arrangements. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Catalog Change Notifications
artifacts.description: The documented metadata and catalog notifications specification with its compliance evidence, the metadata repository or data catalog export, the register or inventory evidencing the notifications with a named owner, and the performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records.

artifacts.name: Data Governance Records
artifacts.description: The data governance framework and policies, the data classification and metadata management documentation, the data quality management reports and metrics, and the data retention policies with their backup and recovery procedures.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the change notification requirements that bind them.

CHG-05.notes: 42 asks across 8 frameworks. Notifying internal stakeholders, notifying customers of outages, and notifying a regulator of a material change are three different obligations with different clocks and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Post-Change Control Verification
artifacts.description: The control effectiveness verification, the control effectiveness assessment, the security validation test results, the detection rule updates confirming detection still fires, the side-effect monitoring evidence, and the requirements fulfilment validation.

artifacts.name: Significant Change Reassessment
artifacts.description: The documented definition of a significant change applicable to the environment, the records confirming all applicable requirements are in place on new or changed systems and networks following such a change, the updated network and data-flow diagrams, scope documentation and inventories, and a sample completed significant-change assessment for a recent change.

artifacts.name: Post-Implementation Review
artifacts.description: The post-implementation review records, the post-implementation review report, the post-implementation review reports with lessons learned, and the lessons learned documentation arising from them.

artifacts.name: Change Testing Records
artifacts.description: The test plans and test cases, the test execution results with sign-off, the user acceptance testing results with their sign-off documentation, the acceptance approval documentation, and the non-production environment configuration documentation the testing was performed in.

artifacts.name: Change Control Records
artifacts.description: The change management policy and procedures, the change request and approval records, the change advisory board meeting minutes, the security impact analysis documentation, the production promotion checklists with their authorisation records, and the release and deployment plans with their rollback procedures.

artifacts.name: Control Failure Response
artifacts.description: The documented response procedure covering restoring security functions, identifying and documenting cause and duration, and resuming monitoring; the sample incident response records for past control failures; the mean-time-to-restore metrics; and the lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Secure Design Records
artifacts.description: The secure design principles documentation, the security architecture documentation, and the security engineering review records against which the changed control is verified.

CHG-06.notes: 32 asks across 6 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is verification that controls still work after a change; the post-implementation review and the significant-change reassessment are the primary artifacts.

artifacts.name: Cloud Outsourcing Policy
artifacts.description: The board-approved cloud outsourcing policy covering the required areas, the cloud security policy covering acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit, the cloud computing policy, the outsourcing risk management policy governing identification, measurement, monitoring and control of outsourcing risks, the board minutes recording approval and subsequent reviews, the matrix mapping each framework requirement to the corresponding policy clause, the dissemination records with acknowledgements, the version-controlled review log, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Cloud Service Inventory
artifacts.description: The approved cloud application catalogue, the technology outsourcing risk register for all arrangements with risk ratings and controls, the list of all third-party service providers with which regulated data is shared with a description of the service, the documentation of which providers receive what data and through which channels, and the records evidencing list maintenance upon engagement of new providers.

artifacts.name: Provider Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment of each major provider including data residency, certifications and shared responsibility; the risk assessment reports conducted before onboarding and periodically for each provider; and the periodic management information on outsourcing risks, performance and incidents.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Posture
artifacts.description: The hardening baseline applied to the cloud estate, the posture management scan results showing misconfigurations and remediation status, the shared responsibility matrix mapping control ownership across the service models, and the review report of cloud console administrative users and privileged roles.

artifacts.name: Portability and Exit Records
artifacts.description: The documented plan to migrate data and workloads out of each provider if required. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented interoperability and portability policy and data portability contractual obligation requirements.

artifacts.name: Network Control Configuration Standard
artifacts.description: The approved configuration standard defining ruleset baselines, defaults, naming, documentation requirements and review cadence; the sample configurations from production network security controls; and the version history and maintenance records of that standard.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data on Public Systems
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence controlling regulated data on publicly accessible systems, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating.

CLD-01.notes: 31 asks across 7 frameworks. The cloud policy, the provider inventory and the portability arrangements that make exit possible are three proofs; the network-control standard arrives through an adjacent PCI DSS crosswalk.

artifacts.name: Tenant Isolation Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture document describing logical and physical segregation through dedicated accounts, subscriptions, virtual networks and tagging; the technical evidence of data separation and isolation at the provider covering tenant isolation and encryption keys; the test results validating that segregation; and the resource tagging standard with its compliance report.

artifacts.name: Provider Segregation Assurance
artifacts.description: The provider audit and assurance reports confirming data segregation controls, the contract clauses requiring segregation at the provider, and the cloud due diligence checklist covering the listed attributes.

artifacts.name: Provider Access Prohibition
artifacts.description: The contract terms prohibiting unauthorised provider access to the organisation's data, the confidentiality agreements with the provider covering all personnel with infrastructure access, the logs of provider access to infrastructure with the organisation's monitoring overlay, the evidence that the organisation retains sole discretion over data access through key and identity control, the executed clause explicitly prohibiting the provider from using the data for commercial purposes, analytics or model training, the configuration evidence showing opt-out of provider telemetry and model-training features, and the executed clause prohibiting disclosure to foreign governments, courts or law enforcement without prior written consent.

artifacts.name: Cloud Data Security Controls
artifacts.description: The board-approved data security policy for cloud workloads covering encryption, desensitisation, segregation and personal data handling; the cryptographic standard specifying approved algorithms and protocols; the configuration export showing encryption at rest enabled for storage and databases; the transport security scan reports for cloud-exposed endpoints; the procedure defining masking, tokenisation and hashing techniques with the approval workflow for moving production data; the execution logs from the masking tool; and the legal memorandum confirming the arrangements comply with applicable law.

artifacts.name: Personal Data Flow and Impact Assessment
artifacts.description: The data protection impact assessment and the personal data flow diagrams identifying data elements, residency and legal basis.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Policy and Posture
artifacts.description: The policy covering cloud acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit requirements; the hardening baseline applied to the cloud estate; the posture management scan results showing misconfigurations and remediation status; the assessment of each major provider including data residency, certifications and shared responsibility; the shared responsibility matrix; the review report of cloud console administrative users and privileged roles; and the documented plan to migrate data and workloads out of each provider.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data on Public Systems
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence controlling regulated data on publicly accessible systems, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating.
