CLD-06.notes: 31 asks across 5 frameworks. Tenant isolation, the provider's own segregation assurance and the prohibition on provider access to the tenant's data are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Shared Responsibility Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping security control ownership between the organisation and the provider across the service models, the responsibility matrix for the departments involved in migration covering requirement analysis, performance testing, acceptance testing and data handling, and the controls mapping showing which controls remain the organisation's despite outsourcing.

artifacts.name: Provider Service Level Agreements
artifacts.description: The signed service level agreements with all providers carrying service metrics, penalties and review cadence; the register of breaches with the remediation actions and penalties applied; the compliance monitoring records and periodic reports against agreed service levels; and the records of periodic review and update of those agreements.

artifacts.name: Data Ownership Records
artifacts.description: The cloud service contracts specifying data ownership terms, the board-approved policy confirming the organisation retains ultimate responsibility for data security, the register of hosted data with ownership attestation, and the due diligence records on the provider's data security practices.

artifacts.name: Migration Role Assignment
artifacts.description: The signed document agreeing roles and responsibilities for each migration prior to transfer of information assets, the migration runbook with role-by-role task assignments, and the pre-go-live sign-off records confirming the agreed roles were executed before cut-over.

artifacts.name: Executive Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The executive management charter establishing responsibility for the protection programme and its compliance, the executive sign-off records, the records of strategy and compliance reporting to executive management, and the governing committee minutes evidencing oversight of the outsourcing and its service levels.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Policy and Posture
artifacts.description: The policy covering cloud acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit requirements; the hardening baseline applied to the cloud estate; the posture management scan results showing misconfigurations and remediation status; the assessment of each major provider including data residency, certifications and shared responsibility; the review report of cloud console administrative users and privileged roles; the documented plan to migrate data and workloads out of each provider; and the cloud risk register.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Agreement Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit; the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records; and the awareness communications informing personnel of the arrangement. HITRUST requires the approved policy and standard on addressing security when dealing with external parties with its implementing procedure.

CLD-06.1.notes: 33 asks across 6 frameworks. The shared responsibility matrix, the service level agreement that gives it contractual force and the monitoring of provider performance against it are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Data Residency Register
artifacts.description: The register documenting the current data centre or region for every workload and dataset, the register listing every cloud outsourcing arrangement with provider classification and workload materiality, the cloud asset inventory tagged with classification, owner, criticality and applicable controls, and the data residency evidence held against each entry.

artifacts.name: Residency Enforcement Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export restricting resource deployment to permitted regions, the region enforcement policy configuration, and the screenshots from the provider portal showing data residency controls and region restrictions.

artifacts.name: Onshore Preference Policy
artifacts.description: The board-approved cloud outsourcing policy section articulating the preference for onshore providers with its rationale and criteria, the assessment report documenting why the selected onshore provider is deemed reputable including reference checks and track record, and the cloud usage restriction policy governing what may be placed off-premises at all.

artifacts.name: Jurisdiction Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The jurisdictional risk assessment for each offshore service location covering legal, regulatory and availability risk; the register of service locations with risk ratings, onsite-audit feasibility and approval status; the legal and compliance memo confirming no provider data-centre location falls within an unfriendly or hostile jurisdiction; the jurisdiction risk register; and the cloud data residency assessment behind them.

artifacts.name: Location Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The documented alternate assurance mechanism for locations where onsite assessment by the organisation, regulator or external auditor is impracticable; the updated enterprise risk management framework explicitly covering cloud outsourcing risks including sub-contracting; and the management or board approval records for that framework.

artifacts.name: In-Country Location Evidence
artifacts.description: The contracts specifying in-country data centres and operations, the verification evidence that providers and all physical servers are located in-country across the service models, the provider site attestation confirming service location, and the due diligence records confirming in-country operations.

artifacts.name: Location Change Controls
artifacts.description: The service level clause requiring the provider to give advance notification of data location changes with the right to reject or terminate, the clause mandating secure deletion of all data from every provider and sub-contractor storage location on exit, and the sample written deletion confirmation template covering those locations.

artifacts.name: Provider Certification and Controls Assessment
artifacts.description: The provider security certification pack reviewed, the register tracking those certifications with issue dates, expiry dates and scope of coverage, the assessment of provider physical security and internal controls against the intended workload's confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience requirements, the review report on provider corporate governance and entity-level controls, the assessment of the provider's ability to give the organisation control over data residency including shifting between preferred data centres, and the due diligence checklist covering the listed attributes.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Policy and Posture
artifacts.description: The policy covering cloud acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit requirements; the matrix mapping security control ownership between the organisation and the provider; the hardening baseline applied to the cloud estate; the posture management scan results showing misconfigurations and remediation status; the assessment of each major provider including data residency, certifications and shared responsibility; the review report of cloud console administrative users and privileged roles; and the documented plan to migrate data and workloads out of each provider if required.

artifacts.name: Cloud Data Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The information classification policy defining sensitivity tiers and handling requirements, the matrix of additional controls applied to high-value cloud assets, the data loss prevention policy and active rule export for cloud mail, storage and software services, the access broker configuration export showing inspection and blocking actions on uploads, downloads and sharing, and the sample anomalous-access alerts with their triage records.

artifacts.name: Cloud Backup and Restoration
artifacts.description: The approved policy specifying backup frequency, retention, recovery point objectives, ransomware protection and half-yearly restoration testing; the backup job execution logs; the immutability or object-lock configuration on backup repositories; and the signed restoration test reports from the last two cycles documenting scenarios, restore times and data integrity.

artifacts.name: External Service Provider Agreements
artifacts.description: The external service provider agreements, the service level agreements with security requirements, the third-party security assessments, the continuous monitoring of external services, the system integration review for cloud connections, and the sector authorisation records for information sharing where the regulator requires them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented data portability requirement.

CLD-09.notes: 55 asks across 7 frameworks. The residency requirement, its technical enforcement and the assurance that the provider honours it are three proofs; SBP Cloud 12.2 arrives here carrying a full cloud data-protection stack whose non-residency parts are kept separate.

artifacts.name: Legal, Regulatory & Contractual Obligations Register
artifacts.description: A single maintained register listing every statutory, regulatory and contractual obligation the organization is subject to (including sector rules, licensing conditions, IPR, records retention, data protection and cryptography law), each mapped to the systems, business processes and internal controls that satisfy it, with a named owner. Frameworks differ on form: ISO 27001, PISF 2026 and SBP ETGRMF expect a register/matrix in spreadsheet form; QCB additionally wants a per-system legal-requirements view; NIST AI RMF wants applicable AI law identified specifically. Show the register is current and owned, not a one-off snapshot.

artifacts.name: Compliance Management Policy & Procedures
artifacts.description: The approved policy and supporting procedures governing how compliance obligations are identified, assigned, implemented and monitored, with documented scope, objectives and management approval. HITRUST and SL CSF want both the approved policy and the work-instruction level procedure; NIST 800-53 PL-1 additionally requires evidence the policy is reviewed on a defined cycle; DoH ADHIE and SBP expect internal policy to be demonstrably aligned to the external rule set.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Change Monitoring & Register Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of the process that keeps the obligations register current: horizon-scanning or regulatory-watch output, a change log of new and amended requirements with impact assessment and actions taken, and dated periodic review records naming the reviewer. Review cadence is framework-specific — PISF 2026 and HITRUST expect a documented periodic review, DoH ADHIE expects periodic alignment reviews against participation criteria, SBP expects a maintained regulatory change management log.

artifacts.name: Compliance Assessment & Gap Analysis Reports
artifacts.description: Periodic assessments testing whether the implemented controls actually meet each applicable obligation, with identified gaps, risk-rated findings, remediation owners and due dates, plus the tracker showing closure. PCI DSS 12.4.2 demands this quarterly, performed by personnel independent of the reviewed activity and signed off by management; ISO 27001, DoH ADHIE and SBP accept a defined periodic cycle. Include the mapping showing which controls were tested against which requirement.

artifacts.name: Internal & External Audit Reports and Auditor Access Records
artifacts.description: Completed internal and external audit and regulatory examination reports covering compliance, together with the audit administration trail: engagement letter or audit plan, agreed testing procedure, audit impact assessment, the read-only account provisioned for auditors and its activity log, and management sign-off on findings. ISO 27001 A.8.34 specifically requires evidence that audit access to production was restricted, logged and time-bounded.

artifacts.name: External Certifications & Third-Party Attestations
artifacts.description: Current third-party validation of compliance where a scheme requires it: PCI DSS Report on Compliance or SAQ, PA-DSS/PCI-PTS/PCI-PIN validation for in-scope applications and devices, ADHICS audit and certification records, and ISO 22301 alignment evidence. Certificates must be in date and cover the actual in-scope environment.

artifacts.name: Legal Counsel Review & Legal Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Records of legal function involvement: advisory opinions on compliance interpretation, legal review of monitoring and logging activity, the legal-environment risk assessment covering specific statutory exposures (SBP cites Electronic Transactions Ordinance sections on documentation, burden of proof, liability and secrecy), the legal risk report to senior management or the board, and the legal function's charter and sign-off.

artifacts.name: Compliance Roles, Committee Charters & Resourcing Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that responsibility and authority for compliance activity is assigned and adequately resourced: terms of reference for the risk/compliance forums, the legal function charter, staffing and skills records for compliance personnel, and performance criteria that include security and compliance responsibilities. DORA additionally requires board-level ICT training — curriculum, schedule, completion and competency assessment.

artifacts.name: Management & Board Compliance Reporting and Sign-off
artifacts.description: Reporting packs presented to senior management and the board on compliance status and security KPIs, with the minutes or approval records showing the body received and acted on them, plus formal management attestations and sign-offs (compliance function annual attestation, board approval of outsourcing arrangements, sign-off on review findings).

artifacts.name: Contracts & Agreements Carrying Compliance Obligations
artifacts.description: Executed agreements that carry regulatory obligations through to third parties: HIPAA business associate agreements (template plus signed copies and the tracking list of all business associates), service level agreements containing security provisions, outsourcing agreements and the outsourcing policy governing them, platform licensing agreements with compliance clauses, and HITRUST-required security clauses with signature records.

artifacts.name: Compliance Awareness & External Disclosure Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that obligations are communicated internally and externally: internal communication procedures and awareness material covering compliance duties, the confidential/whistleblower reporting channel, the sanctions policy and its acknowledgement, complaint and investigation procedures, customer notification procedures for incidents, and published security/privacy disclosures and patient-facing rights material.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Controls Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The approved standard and procedure governing use of cryptography against legal restrictions on its use, export and import, plus the key management procedure and current key inventory/lifecycle records, and evidence of compliance with IPR, records-retention and data-protection obligations touching encrypted data. HITRUST 06.f expects both the policy layer and the operating key inventory.

artifacts.name: AI System Inventory & Regulatory Context Analysis
artifacts.description: For organizations running AI systems: the inventory of AI systems with each system's intended purpose, the documented determination of the organization's role (provider, deployer, user), the context/PESTLE analysis behind the AI management system's scope, and the elicited requirements and design decision records showing applicable AI law was translated into system requirements.

artifacts.name: Regulated Platform Participation & Compliance Attestations
artifacts.description: Where the organization participates in a regulated platform or scheme: the participation criteria checklist, approval and access-grant records from the operator, signed attestations of adherence to the operator's processes and privacy/security controls, records of compliance with specific supervisory circulars, and the sector-specific security framework the organization is required to follow with its maintenance log.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Regulatory Compliance Documentation
artifacts.description: The business continuity policy, plans and procedures held to satisfy continuity obligations imposed by regulation, mapped to the applicable circular or standard (QCB BCM circular, ISO 22301 alignment), together with the system switchover plan and its test reports required by SBP.

CPL-01.notes: 159 framework restatements collapse to 15 real artifacts. The bulk is one obligations register asked for by 12 sources under 12 names. Nothing in this control is currently automated (empty automated list), so almost everything is manual; the crypto-controls and platform-participation items are hybrid because key inventories and access-grant records can be pulled from systems while the governing documents cannot.

artifacts.name: Non-Compliance Register
artifacts.description: The nonconformity register, the control deficiency registers with their remediation tracking, the control deficiency tracking and remediation log, the register of identified policy violations with severity and remediation, the register listing unauthorised configuration changes with rollback or formal approval evidence, and the log of conditions identified as potentially increasing security breach risk with their mitigation actions.

artifacts.name: Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: The corrective action plans with evidence of implementation, the corrective action plans with their timelines and status, the corrective action plans with their follow-up tracking documentation, the root cause analysis records, the effectiveness review records, and the tracker of issues identified during review with their closure status. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remediation of audit findings requirement.

artifacts.name: Compliance Review Procedure
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence; the latest four quarters of review reports; the evidence that reviews are performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task being reviewed; and the management sign-off records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented audit management process requirement.

artifacts.name: Internal Control Framework Records
artifacts.description: The internal control framework documentation and policies, the control self-assessment reports and results, the internal control testing results and effectiveness reports, the conformance monitoring reports with target achievement records, the performance monitoring framework with its indicator definitions, and the performance dashboards and scorecards with trend analysis.

artifacts.name: Configuration Drift Detection
artifacts.description: The configuration of drift detection tooling flagging unauthorised changes and the sample alert logs of detected drift events.

artifacts.name: Compliance Gap Records
artifacts.description: The assessment identifying inability to meet audit or compliance requirements and the plan or records of migrating services to a compliant facility.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Determination Handling
artifacts.description: The procedure for handling a determination by the competent authority that safeguards are inadequate for a specific transfer, the log monitoring the continued implementation and operating effectiveness of the safeguards for each exempt transfer, and the periodic review records confirming those safeguards remain adequate so the exemption continues to hold.

artifacts.name: Management Reporting Records
artifacts.description: The management reporting on control exceptions and the board reporting on significant control deficiencies.

artifacts.name: Standards Alignment Records
artifacts.description: The standards mapping and alignment documentation, the gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

artifacts.name: Accountability Framework Records
artifacts.description: The accountability framework documentation, the performance evaluation criteria including security responsibilities, the incentive and reward programme documentation tied to control objectives, and the security performance dashboards and reports.

CPL-01.1.notes: 43 asks across 9 frameworks. The detection of non-compliance, the register that holds it and the corrective action that closes it are three proofs; the reviewer-independence evidence is kept separate because it is what makes the oversight credible.

artifacts.name: Management System Scope Statement
artifacts.description: The formal documented scope defining boundaries, locations, systems, organisational units and products, with the boundary diagram showing in-scope units and interfaces to out-of-scope areas, the justification for inclusions and exclusions, and the top-management approval authorising it.

artifacts.name: Regulated Environment Scope Document
artifacts.description: The annually confirmed scope document including all data flows, storage locations and connected or security-impacting systems; the documented validation methodology; the validation results from data discovery scans, network analysis and interviews; and the scope reviews performed after significant changes.

artifacts.name: In-Scope Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of in-scope system components with function, owner and scope classification, the update records evidencing it is kept current, and the configuration database integration or automated maintenance behind it.

artifacts.name: Legal and Regulatory Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The up-to-date register of applicable laws, regulations, standards, contracts and directives; the regulatory inventory with effective dates; the compliance register tracking adherence to each; and the log evidencing periodic update of the register. HITRUST requires the approved standard for identifying applicable legislation with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Change Management Log
artifacts.description: The log of regulatory changes received with the impact assessment, action plan and closure evidence for each, and the legal review records supporting the assessment.

artifacts.name: Compliance Attestation Records
artifacts.description: The annual attestation from the compliance or audit function confirming compliance with the applicable regulations, the compliance assessments, and the compliance requirements inventory they are measured against.

artifacts.name: Audit Universe and Scope Records
artifacts.description: The audit universe inventory, the approved per-audit plans with scope, objectives, tools, timelines and resources; the audit scope approved by the competent authority; the reference showing alignment to recognised standards; and the applicability statement and treatment plan provided to the auditor.

artifacts.name: Scope Exemption Records
artifacts.description: The exemption case files with the regulator notification, the head of department and risk approvals, and the justification recorded for each exclusion from scope.

artifacts.name: Sector Compliance Scope Records
artifacts.description: The written declaration to the exchange operator listing all covered facilities, the notification records for any change to that list, the group corporate structure documentation, and the compliance attestation with the sector processes.

artifacts.name: Sector Regulation Mapping
artifacts.description: The information security regulation mapping, the compliance assessment reports against it, the audit and certification records, and the implementation evidence for the system and process security controls it requires.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Mapping Configuration
artifacts.description: The documented information system regulatory mapping and the logging scope definition, with the records demonstrating each operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Assurance Scope and Follow-up
artifacts.description: The assurance initiative plans with scope and objectives, the review reports with findings and recommendations, the management action plans responding to them, and the follow-up tracking of recommendation implementation.

artifacts.name: AI Legal and Requirements Register
artifacts.description: The legal and regulatory requirements register mapping applicable AI laws, the elicited system requirements with socio-technical design decision records, the approved organisational policies and procedures, the documented AI risk tolerance statement with its approval, the context documentation covering intended purposes, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Data Management Scope Records
artifacts.description: The documented data management and personal data protection policy with its approved standard, the approved strategy and plan, the data security control evidence, and the privacy artifacts defining what the data programme covers.

CPL-01.2.notes: 69 asks across 13 frameworks. Two different scopes converge: the management-system scope statement (ISO 22301, ISO 42001) and the regulated-environment scope with its asset inventory and validation (PCI DSS). They are kept apart because the second requires evidence the first does not.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The regulatory compliance register with the applicable requirements, the legal and regulatory tracker, the change-monitoring process keeping it current, and the governance framework behind it.

artifacts.name: Conformity Evidence Pack
artifacts.description: The evidence of compliance with laws, regulations and contracts; the compliance documentation; the compliance status documentation; the compliance report templates; the compliance assessment reports with their gap analyses; the conformance monitoring reports with target achievement records; and the documented evidence of compliance with the platform access requirements.

artifacts.name: Processing Activity Records
artifacts.description: The records of processing activities, the processing inventories, and the regular updates keeping them current.

artifacts.name: Audit Trails
artifacts.description: The audit trails supporting the conformity claims and the external audit reports and regulatory examination findings tested against them.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Submissions
artifacts.description: The annual standards compliance report submitted to the regulator, the submission records, the regulator audit cooperation procedure, and the records of regulator audit engagements.

artifacts.name: Platform Access Compliance
artifacts.description: The participation criteria compliance checklist and the operator approval and access grant records evidencing entry was permitted.

artifacts.name: Performance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The performance monitoring framework with its indicator definitions, the performance dashboards and scorecards with trend analysis, and the corrective action plans with their follow-up tracking documentation.

artifacts.name: Privacy Communication Records
artifacts.description: The privacy notices, the communication templates, and the accessibility measures making the conformity information reachable.

artifacts.name: Compliance Audit Accountability
artifacts.description: The documented compliance audit results specification with its compliance evidence, the implementation evidence demonstrating the outcome, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, the business intelligence dashboards and analytics use-case register, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

CPL-01.3.notes: 33 asks across 6 frameworks. The obligations register, the evidence pack demonstrating each is met and the audit trail supporting the pack are three proofs; the regulator-specific submissions stay separate.

artifacts.name: Oversight Committee Charters and Board Minutes
artifacts.description: Charters for the executive steering committees performing oversight - risk, audit, and privacy/security - each showing purpose, membership drawn from cybersecurity, technology, risk, privacy and business leadership, decision authority and meeting cadence, plus the board or committee minutes evidencing that oversight actually occurred over the period.

artifacts.name: Compliance Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The catalogue of applicable laws, regulations, standards and contractual obligations, each mapped to the responsible owner, the controls that satisfy it and the evidence proving it. Must be current and include the horizon-scanning output on upcoming legislative and regulatory change with readiness status, supported by legal counsel advisory records - including, where cryptography is deployed across jurisdictions, the legal review of its permitted use.

artifacts.name: Control Assessment and Independent Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: Reports from the periodic assessment of security, compliance and resilience controls, both internal testing and independent/third-party assessments, at the frequency the organisation has defined. Must state scope, methodology, the controls tested, findings with risk ratings, and conclusions on operating effectiveness. Include the assurance initiative plans that scoped them and, where in scope, the specialised assessments frameworks call out separately such as the encryption and key management audit.

artifacts.name: Executive and Board Compliance Reporting Pack
artifacts.description: The recurring reporting pack delivered to executive leadership and the board showing the security, compliance and resilience status of the environment: the defined performance metrics (KPIs, KRIs) and dashboard trends tracking programme health, control monitoring results, open non-compliance and its remediation status, and internal audit conclusions. Must evidence the defined reporting frequency and identify the recipients, so that the oversight function's reporting line to executive leadership is demonstrable.

artifacts.name: Deficiency Register and Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: The POA&M, risk register or control deficiency register tracking each identified weakness from identification through remediation, with owner, risk rating, agreed treatment, target date and current status. Must cover deficiencies from all sources - assessments, audits, self-assessments, monitoring and non-compliance findings - and include the management action plans responding to assurance findings, the evidence that corrective actions were completed, follow-up tracking of recommendations, and formal risk acceptance records where a finding will not be remediated.

artifacts.name: Compliance Monitoring and Self-Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The schedule of manager-led compliance reviews by area and the completed self-assessment returns from each department or control owner, with reviewer, date, observations and corrective actions raised. Cadence differs by framework - ISO 27001 accepts quarterly or semi-annual, others expect at least annual - so state the cadence applied and show the schedule was met for the full period.

artifacts.name: Continuous Control Monitoring Strategy and Scan Output
artifacts.description: The documented continuous monitoring strategy - what is monitored, by what method, at what frequency, against which metrics, and how results are correlated and analysed - together with the automated output evidencing it runs: technical compliance scan results against internal standards and configuration evidence for the controls monitored continuously, including encryption and access controls.

artifacts.name: Security Event and Whistleblower Reporting Channel Evidence
artifacts.description: The procedure telling staff what, how, when and to whom to report security events and concerns, documentation and screenshots of each channel (hotline, portal, mailbox, in-product reporting button), the awareness material promoting their use, the configuration of the anonymous or third-party whistleblower channel, and the log of events reported with triage outcomes and volume metrics demonstrating the channels are actually used.

artifacts.name: Audit Management Records
artifacts.description: The audit charter defining the function's mandate and independence, and for each audit engagement over the period: the engagement letter setting scope, timing and access; management sign-off on scope and accepted risk; the impact assessment for testing against operational systems; the read-only audit account configuration; records of audit access granted with expiry; and the log of queries and actions performed during testing.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management and Penetration Test Reports
artifacts.description: The vulnerability management policy setting scanning cadence, prioritisation and remediation SLAs by severity, the periodic internal and external scan reports, patch deployment records with success/failure and rollback outcome, the remediation tracker showing open items with owners and closure status, SLA performance metrics by severity, and the annual penetration test report with evidence that findings were remediated.

artifacts.name: Critical Security Control Failure Detection and Response Records
artifacts.description: For each critical security control system - network security controls, IDS/IPS, file integrity monitoring, anti-malware, physical and logical access controls, audit logging mechanisms and segmentation controls - the documented failure detection procedure, the health-check/heartbeat and alert configuration with thresholds, and a sample of failure alert logs with triage. Plus the response evidence: security functions restored, cause and duration identified and documented, security issues arising during the failure addressed, risk assessment performed, preventive controls implemented, monitoring resumed - with mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records. PCI DSS applies part of this to service providers specifically.

artifacts.name: Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Records
artifacts.description: The code of conduct or ethics policy, the acknowledgement records showing employees have read and accepted it, and the disciplinary action records evidencing that violations are actually acted on.

artifacts.name: Internal and External Communication Records
artifacts.description: The procedures and artifacts for communicating security and compliance matters: internal communication procedures and security awareness programme materials, the awareness communications confirming personnel were informed of compliance obligations, customer notification procedures for security incidents, external audit communication protocols, security provisions in service level agreements, and public-facing security and privacy disclosures.

artifacts.name: Security and Compliance Programme Documentation
artifacts.description: The overarching programme documentation for the oversight function: the internal control framework and the information security and governance programme document, the approved policy and procedure requiring compliance with security policies and standards, the documented description of technical and organisational security measures, and records evidencing the programme has been implemented rather than only written.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Monitoring and Review Records
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are in scope: the RACI matrix defining AI risk management roles, responsibilities and communication lines, the records of ongoing monitoring and periodic review at the defined frequency with named performers, and the implementation artifacts evidencing this oversight across the AI lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Security Function Appointment and Independence Evidence
artifacts.description: The appointment letter for the CISO or Information Security Officer, the job description and the reporting-line diagram demonstrating independence from the CIO/CTO and a reporting line to executive leadership, plus the independence assessment records and the impairment disclosure log for the assurance function.

CPL-02.notes: 114 entries collapse to 16. Three clusters absorb most of it: control assessments (11), the deficiency/POA&M register (11) and PCI DSS's critical-control-failure regime (11, which is genuinely its own artifact and does not merge into generic monitoring). Framework refs pull in several adjacent oversight topics - whistleblower channels, audit management, vulnerability management, code of conduct, CISO independence, AI governance - each kept as one item because they are separately collectable. No connectors are configured for this control, so almost everything is manual; the two exceptions are scan-derived.

artifacts.name: Internal Audit Charter
artifacts.description: The charter establishing the internal audit function with its independence, reporting line, mandate and authority. PISF 2026 requires separate charters covering information security audits and compliance; SBP ETGRMF requires the technology audit charter to be board-approved; MAS TRM requires the IT audit charter with the function documentation.

artifacts.name: Auditor Independence and Competence Evidence
artifacts.description: The qualifications and certifications of the audit team evidencing competence, the periodic declarations of independence by the audit head and team, and the auditor selection criteria and impartiality records.

artifacts.name: Multi-Year Audit Programme
artifacts.description: The internal audit programme covering all management system areas with frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning and reporting requirements, and the audit universe it draws on. MAS TRM requires the technology risk audit universe documentation and audit planning risk assessment records; QCB requires an audit universe document.

artifacts.name: Annual Audit Plan and Approval
artifacts.description: The annual audit plan covering goals, schedules, staffing needs, budget and reporting requirements, with the audit committee or board approval and the budget and staffing documentation behind it.

artifacts.name: Audit Execution Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of audit activities executed against the plan, the per-audit documentation of objectives, criteria and scope, the audit plans and checklists, and the workpapers and evidence files retained. QCB requires application controls workpapers and data integrity test results specifically.

artifacts.name: Internal Audit Reports
artifacts.description: The completed audit reports with findings, evidence and recommendations, the records confirming results were reported to the relevant managers, and the reports presented to the board.

artifacts.name: Corrective Action Register
artifacts.description: The register of audit-driven corrective actions with owners, due dates and status, the finding tracker, the management review minutes reviewing results and directing action, the remediation action plans with status tracking, and the follow-up tracking of recommendation implementation.

artifacts.name: Audit Access and System Protection Records
artifacts.description: The controls protecting operational systems from the audit activity itself: the engagement letter defining scope, timing and access, the impact assessment for audit activities on production, management sign-off on scope and risk acceptance, the audit testing procedure, records of audit-specific access rights granted with expiry, read-only audit account configuration, and the log of audit queries and actions performed.

artifacts.name: Control Self-Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The internal control framework documentation and policies, the control self-assessment reports and results, the internal control testing results and effectiveness reports, and the control deficiency register with remediation tracking.

artifacts.name: Independent Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: The assurance initiative plans with scope and objectives, the assurance review reports with findings and recommendations, the management action plans responding to them, and the reports from external advisors or prior certification-body audits used as independent review.

artifacts.name: Periodic Control Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The documented policy or configuration evidence for assessing security controls periodically, with the records demonstrating the assessment is implemented and operating rather than only defined.

artifacts.name: Audit Management Process Records
artifacts.description: The audit management process documentation with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment it covers, and the encryption and key management audit records where cryptographic controls are in scope.

artifacts.name: Cloud Outsourcing Certification to the Board
artifacts.description: Internal Audit's independent certification to the board confirming regulatory and legal compliance of the outsourcing arrangements, the documented scope, methodology and sampling approach behind it, the regulatory compliance matrix mapping arrangement controls to the framework and applicable law with review conclusions, and the board or audit committee minutes receiving and discussing the certification.

artifacts.name: IT Strategy and Architecture Context
artifacts.description: The IT strategic plan aligned to business strategy, current-state and target-state architecture documentation, gap analysis reports with prioritised initiatives, and the strategy communication and roadmap material that scopes what the audit function covers.

artifacts.name: Data Compliance Function Records
artifacts.description: The documented compliance officer, compliance monitoring and compliance-and-audit specifications with their compliance evidence, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, the performance metrics dashboard, the privacy artifacts, and the open data publication records.

CPL-02.1.notes: 95 asks across 14 frameworks. Distinct from CPL-02.2 (periodic audits) in that the demands here are about the function — its charter, independence, competence and programme — rather than about individual audit engagements. ISO 27001 A.8.34 contributes a separate concern: protecting production systems from the audit activity itself.

artifacts.name: Audit Charter and Independence Evidence
artifacts.description: The board-approved charter establishing the audit function with its independence, reporting line and mandate, the periodic declarations of independence by the audit head and team, and the CVs and certifications evidencing competence. PISF 2026 requires a charter establishing an independent internal audit function for information security audits specifically; SBP ETGRMF requires the technology audit charter to be board-approved.

artifacts.name: Risk-Based Audit Plan and Schedule
artifacts.description: The annual and multi-year rolling audit plan with the audit universe it draws on, and the documented rationale linking audit frequency to risk assessment outcomes. MAS TRM and QCB require the frequency to be justified from a risk rating; SBP ETGRMF requires the annual plan to be board-approved and commensurate with the technology risk profile; PISF 2026 requires at least annual information security audits.

artifacts.name: Audit Reports and Workpapers
artifacts.description: The executed audit reports with scope, findings and conclusions, together with the workpapers and evidence files supporting them. SBP Internet Banking requires the information systems audit plan and reports to be executed in accordance with the applicable circular; QCB requires working papers and evidence files to be retained.

artifacts.name: Audit Coverage Matrix
artifacts.description: The coverage matrix confirming audit scope across all required control domains — IT strategy, business planning, IT operations, disaster recovery and continuity, outsourcing, information security and development — with the dashboard showing annual coverage achieved against it.

artifacts.name: Finding Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker of findings from all audit and testing activity with severity, owner, target date and closure status, the non-conformance tracker with remediation timelines, the corrective action records with closure evidence, and the remediation action plans with status tracking.

artifacts.name: Independent Third-Party Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The independent assessment or third-party audit reports covering physical, technical and operational controls, with the engagement records behind them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented independent assessment process; PISF 2026 requires at least one annual independent third-party audit of the data centre.

artifacts.name: Control Self-Assessment and Internal Control Testing
artifacts.description: The internal control framework documentation and policies, the control self-assessment reports and results, the internal control testing results and effectiveness reports, and the control deficiency register with remediation tracking.

artifacts.name: Security Testing Reports
artifacts.description: The annual security testing plan with the scope and frequency justification showing it is commensurate with system complexity and risk, the penetration test reports with findings and remediation status, and the independent security audit report covering the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Cloud Provider Audit Records
artifacts.description: The schedule of provider audits, the scope document for each engagement, the resulting audit reports on the arrangements, and the records of provider compliance findings and their remediation.

artifacts.name: Privacy Monitoring and Audit Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure for privacy monitoring and auditing, the audit plan and reports with scope, findings and remediation tracking, the audit logging configuration evidence, log review records with follow-up case documentation, and the published privacy notice with its version history.

artifacts.name: Independent Review of Information Security
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure for independent review of information security, the awareness communications informing personnel of it, and the change management records evidencing that review findings feed the change process.

artifacts.name: Data Compliance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The documented compliance monitoring and audit specifications with their implementing procedures and workflows, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, the performance metrics dashboard, the privacy artifacts, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the register evidencing each with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Security Measures Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented technical and organisational security measures assessed during audit — access controls, encryption implementation and the risk assessments behind them — evidencing the measures whose effectiveness the periodic audit tests.

artifacts.name: Backup and Environmental Audit Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that backup and restore effectiveness is included in regular audits reported to senior management, the documented mechanism for continuous monitoring of backup and restore activity, and the periodic test and inspection reports for environmental safeguards with the audit records verifying their effectiveness.

artifacts.name: System Switchover Plan and Test Reports
artifacts.description: The documented system switchover plan with tested procedures and the periodic switchover test reports demonstrating operational readiness, held with the audit evidence because the applicable circular tests them together.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Compliance Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The compliance assessment reports with findings management, the records of key audit results reported to management, and the records of audits triggered by material changes to critical infrastructure.

CPL-02.2.notes: 99 asks across 12 frameworks. Audit charter and independence evidence is separated from audit execution because SBP ETGRMF, PISF 2026 and SL CSF each test the independence of the function as its own control, not as an attribute of the reports.

artifacts.name: Audit Findings Reports
artifacts.description: The audit reports identifying control weaknesses with meaningful recommendations, the annual audit reports with their scope documentation, the findings and deficiency reports, the audit workpapers and test results, the compliance assessment reports with findings management, the internal and external audit reports with outcomes, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the self-assessment results and compliance status reports alongside them.

artifacts.name: Management Response Records
artifacts.description: The management plans for addressing identified weaknesses, the board-signed action plans submitted to the regulator, the remediation action plans with status tracking, and the remediation plans accompanying the findings.

artifacts.name: Corrective Action Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker of corrective actions arising from audits with closure evidence, the register of audit recommendations with status tracking, the register tracking recommendation implementation timelines against the approved procedure, the finding tracking and closure records, the non-conformance tracker with remediation timelines, the material gap register, the mitigation measures evidence, and the improvement tracking records.

artifacts.name: Follow-Up Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented follow-up processes for significant audit findings, the procedure approved by senior management for timely implementation of audit recommendations, the evidence of that senior management approval, and the evidence of the procedure being applied to actual audit recommendations.

artifacts.name: Closure and Validation Records
artifacts.description: The records confirming corrective actions completed with remediation validation, the follow-up reports on the status of significant finding remediation, the follow-up review records over management remediation plans, and the audit plan and schedule against which closure is tracked.

artifacts.name: Overdue Finding Escalation
artifacts.description: The log of overdue significant findings escalated to senior management or the governing committee, and the escalation records for items past their agreed remediation date.

artifacts.name: Findings Integration into Risk
artifacts.description: The evidence that audit findings are integrated into risk management practices and the lessons learned and enhancement implementation records showing the finding changed something beyond its own closure.

artifacts.name: Internal Audit Function Records
artifacts.description: The charter establishing an independent internal audit function for compliance and the records of key audit results reported to management.

artifacts.name: Technical Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The vulnerability scanning reports with their remediation tracking and timing, and the patch management records with deployment evidence and exception register. HITRUST requires the approved technical compliance checking policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Corrective Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented data quality issues resolution specification with its compliance evidence, the data quality profiling reports, the documented compliance audit results and compliance monitoring specifications with their implementation evidence, the open data publication records, the business intelligence dashboards and analytics use-case register, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, the performance metrics dashboard with targets and review records, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Compliance Awareness and Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the compliance obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved compliance policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

CPL-02.3.notes: 61 asks across 7 frameworks. The finding, the management response and the closure evidence are three distinct records; the escalation of overdue items is separate again because that is the control most often missing.

artifacts.name: Compliance Monitoring Mechanism
artifacts.description: The formally approved monitoring mechanism covering scope, methods, roles and reporting, with the schedule of manager-led compliance reviews by area and the coverage map showing which monitoring method covers each control area. SBP Internet Banking requires the mechanism to be formally approved with an effectiveness analysis of the methods chosen; HITRUST requires the approved compliance policy and its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Control Self-Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The documented self-assessment methodology, the completed self-assessment forms from department managers, and the results feeding continuous risk management. PISF 2026 requires the outputs to demonstrably feed risk management rather than terminate as a report.

artifacts.name: Control Testing Results
artifacts.description: The control testing programme with its results, the control effectiveness review reports, the IT control effectiveness assessment reports, and the re-testing performed after environmental change. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented periodic assessment.

artifacts.name: Security Assessment Plan and Results
artifacts.description: The security assessment plan, the assessment results report, and the plan of action and milestones arising from it.

artifacts.name: Technical Compliance Scan Results
artifacts.description: The automated compliance scan output against internal standards and benchmarks, with the compliance monitoring dashboard showing KPI trends across control families.

artifacts.name: Non-Compliance Register and Corrective Action
artifacts.description: The log of non-compliances detected with root cause and corrective action, the evidence of actions taken, the control deficiency register with remediation tracking, and the remediation plans behind them.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Detection Configuration
artifacts.description: Alert configuration covering failure of every critical security control system — network security controls, intrusion detection, file integrity monitoring, anti-malware, physical access controls, logging mechanisms and segmentation — with the health-check or heartbeat configuration and the sample failure alert logs. PCI DSS requires this both for service providers and, separately, for all entities.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Response Records
artifacts.description: The documented response procedure covering restoration of the security function, identification and documentation of cause and duration, root-cause remediation, assessment of further action needed during the outage and resumption of monitoring; with sample response records for past failures, triage and resolution records, mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Quarterly Compliance Review Records
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence, the latest four quarters of reports, evidence the reviews were performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task reviewed, management sign-off, and the remediation tracker with closure status.

artifacts.name: Continuous Monitoring Programme
artifacts.description: The continuous monitoring programme documentation and records, the internal audit plan and schedule, the security control testing results and reports, and the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports that corroborate the monitoring.

artifacts.name: Internal Audit Programme and Findings
artifacts.description: The multi-year internal audit programme, the completed audit reports with findings and recommendations, the auditor independence and competence evidence, the corrective action register, the management review of findings, and the external review reports used as independent assurance.

artifacts.name: Audit Access and System Protection Records
artifacts.description: The engagement letter defining scope, timing and access, the impact assessment for audit activity on operational systems, management sign-off on scope and risk acceptance, the audit testing procedure, records of audit access rights with expiry, read-only account configuration, and the log of audit queries performed.

artifacts.name: Independent Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The independent assessment process documentation with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment, the audit management process, the risk-based planning assessment, and the encryption and key management audit records.

artifacts.name: Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic access review reports and the remediation records arising from them, evidencing that the access controls being monitored are actually recertified.

artifacts.name: Architecture Review Reports
artifacts.description: The network architecture review reports with the vulnerabilities identified from them, testing the design rather than the running configuration.

artifacts.name: Sector Compliance Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The sector information security regulation mapping, the compliance assessment reports against it, the audit and certification records, and the implementation evidence for the system and process security controls it requires.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The RACI matrix defining AI risk management roles, the ongoing monitoring and periodic review records, and the implementation records and artifacts evidencing the governance outcome within the AI lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Data Compliance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The documented compliance monitoring specification with its implementing procedures and process workflows, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, the performance metrics dashboard with targets and review records, and the business intelligence artifacts reporting them.

CPL-03.notes: 94 asks across 16 frameworks. Two things sit under this control: whether controls are operating as designed (self-assessment, compliance scanning, management review) and whether the control systems themselves are still running (PCI DSS 10.7 failure detection). Both are kept, because a control that has silently stopped is a different failure from one that is operating poorly.

artifacts.name: Assessor Independence and Qualification Evidence
artifacts.description: The formally defined criteria for assessor independence, certification and qualification; the engaged assessors' credentials; the periodic independence declarations; and the impairment disclosure log recording anything that could compromise objectivity. QCB requires independence assessment records with an impairment disclosure log; PISF 2026 requires selection criteria to be defined before engagement.

artifacts.name: Independent Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The completed independent assessment or third-party audit reports with findings and recommendations, and the external review reports from advisors or prior certification-body audits used as independent assurance. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented independent assessment process.

artifacts.name: Assessor Engagement Records
artifacts.description: The engagement letter or contract confirming independence, scope and methodology, the records of the independent party's engagement, and the scope and methodology document agreed before work began.

artifacts.name: Audit Plan and Schedule
artifacts.description: The approved schedule of regular internal and external audits, the annual audit plan and reports, the review schedules, and the records of audits triggered by material change rather than by calendar.

artifacts.name: Finding Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: The corrective action register with owners, due dates and status, the follow-up tracker, the non-conformance tracker with remediation timelines, and the management review of findings directing the corrective action.

artifacts.name: Cloud Provider Independent Assessment
artifacts.description: The annual independent threat and vulnerability assessment report covering the provider data centres hosting material workloads, the engagement letter confirming assessor independence and scope across all relevant sites, the mapping of each material workload to the data centres where it resides, the coverage list confirming each site was assessed, and the finding remediation tracker carrying both provider-side and organisation-side actions.

artifacts.name: Cloud Provider Audit Programme
artifacts.description: The rolling biennial audit schedule for providers carrying material workloads with planned dates, the documented scope confirming coverage of the infrastructure and software delivering the service, the comprehensive provider audit report whether self, third-party or pooled, the third-party assessor engagement letter or pooled-audit agreement, and where onsite audit is not feasible the documented justification with a review of the certification's scope and methodology.

artifacts.name: Jurisdictional Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The political and economic climate risk report for each data-centre country, the supplementary assurance reports reviewed for material workloads, and the internal audit and information security function review records of the independent assessment results.

artifacts.name: Independent Continuity Assessment
artifacts.description: The reports from the independent assessment of the continuity testing programme and its results, the scope and methodology document, the engagement records, and the evidence of assessor independence from continuity management.

artifacts.name: Independent Project Quality Assurance
artifacts.description: The schedule of quality assurance reviews across major projects, the contracts engaging independent parties to perform them, the resulting review reports, and the reviewers' independence declarations.

artifacts.name: Continuous Monitoring Strategy
artifacts.description: The continuous monitoring strategy with its metrics and dashboards, the ongoing assessment reports, and the security status reports produced under it.

artifacts.name: Audit Charter and Programme
artifacts.description: The board-approved charter establishing the audit function with independence, reporting line and mandate; the multi-year internal audit programme; the internal audit charter; and the auditor competence evidence.

artifacts.name: Privacy Monitoring and Audit Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure for privacy monitoring and auditing, the audit plan and reports with scope, findings and remediation tracking, the audit logging configuration evidence, log review records with follow-up case documentation, and the published privacy notice with version history.

artifacts.name: Independent Review of Information Security
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure for independent review of information security, the awareness communications informing personnel of it, and the change management records evidencing review findings feed the change process.

artifacts.name: Security Testing Programme
artifacts.description: The annual security testing plan with the justification showing scope and frequency are commensurate with system complexity and risk, the penetration test reports, the self-assessment reports with control coverage, and the independent security audit report.

artifacts.name: Audit Management Process Records
artifacts.description: The audit management process documentation with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered, and the encryption and key management audit records where cryptographic controls are in scope.

artifacts.name: Indicator Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The audit or assessment reports over the defined resilience indicators, with the engagement letter for the independent assessor who produced them.

CPL-03.1.notes: 86 asks across 11 frameworks. The demand common to all is that the assessor be independent of what is assessed; the specialisations are what independence is required over — cloud data centres (SBP Cloud), the continuity programme (SBP ETGRMF 5.2.4.f), major projects (SBP ETGRMF 4.1.d).

artifacts.name: Technical Compliance Checking Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy and implementing procedure for technical compliance checking, the automated compliance scan output against internal standards and benchmarks, and the compliance monitoring dashboard showing KPI trends across control families.

artifacts.name: Compliance Review Schedule and Self-Assessments
artifacts.description: The schedule of manager-led compliance reviews by area, the completed self-assessment forms from department managers, and the self-assessment reports with control coverage for the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Control Testing Results
artifacts.description: The control testing results and documentation, the IT control effectiveness assessment reports, the continuous and periodic control review reports, and the internal control testing results and effectiveness reports.

artifacts.name: Network Security Control Configuration Review
artifacts.description: The last two cycles of six-monthly network security control configuration review reports with reviewer, scope and conclusions, the reviewer or approver sign-off records, and the tracker of follow-up actions with closure status.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The alert configuration covering failure of every critical security control system, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, sample failure alerts with triage, the documented response procedure covering restoration, cause and duration documentation and root-cause remediation, sample incident response records for past failures, mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Quarterly Compliance Review Records
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence, the latest four quarters of reports, evidence the reviews were performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task reviewed, management sign-off, and the remediation tracker.

artifacts.name: Standard Operating Procedure Adherence Records
artifacts.description: The register of technology SOPs with version, owner, approval and last review date, the signed and current SOP documents covering all areas of technology operations, staff acknowledgement records evidencing awareness, and the internal audit reports assessing adherence in practice.

artifacts.name: Internal Audit Programme and Findings
artifacts.description: The multi-year internal audit programme, the completed audit reports with findings and recommendations, the auditor independence and competence evidence, the corrective action register with owners and due dates, the management review of findings, and the external review reports used as independent assurance.

artifacts.name: General Controls Audit Coverage
artifacts.description: The coverage matrix confirming audit scope across all required general control domains, the annual coverage dashboard against those areas, the general controls audit reports, and the records of general control deficiency remediation.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability and Patch Compliance Evidence
artifacts.description: The vulnerability management policy, periodic scanning reports covering internal and external assets, the remediation tracker with owners and service levels, SLA compliance metrics by severity, patch deployment records with success or failure and the exception register, annual penetration test reports, and the documented risk acceptance for what cannot be remediated.

artifacts.name: Security Assessment Plan and Risk Analysis
artifacts.description: The security assessment plan, the assessment results report, the plan of action and milestones arising from it, the risk assessment methodology and report with its update records, and the threat and vulnerability analysis behind them.

artifacts.name: Periodic Technical and Non-Technical Evaluation
artifacts.description: The periodic evaluation reports covering both technical and non-technical assessment findings, with the remediation plans arising from each. HIPAA requires the evaluation to cover operational and environmental factors, not only technical configuration.

artifacts.name: Policy Compliance Monitoring Report
artifacts.description: The quarterly management report tracking adherence to technology policies and plan-versus-actual performance against targets, the master register of approved technology plans and policies with owner and review dates, the exception and deviation register with compensating controls and expiry, and the current-versus-future-state technology assessment behind it.

artifacts.name: Audit Management Process Records
artifacts.description: The audit management process documentation with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered, and the encryption and key management audit records where cryptographic controls are in scope.

artifacts.name: Architecture Review Reports
artifacts.description: The network architecture review reports with the vulnerabilities identified from them, and the gap remediation tracker arising from the review.

artifacts.name: Security Testing Programme Records
artifacts.description: The annual security testing plan with the justification showing scope and frequency are commensurate with system complexity and risk, the penetration test reports, the independent security audit report, and the tracker of findings from all testing activity with severity, owner and closure status.

CPL-03.2.notes: 94 asks across 12 frameworks. Overlaps CPL-03; what is distinct here is the functional review of whether a control still works — technical compliance checking, the six-monthly network security control review, and the SOP adherence audit — rather than whether a control exists.

artifacts.name: Right of Audit Clauses
artifacts.description: The service level clauses granting audit and onsite assessment rights to internal and external auditors, independent assessors and the regulator; the contract clauses granting audit access to the organisation and its regulator; the right-to-audit clauses in service contracts; the right-of-audit clauses in sub-contractor and affiliate agreements; the audit-non-impedance clauses; the clauses granting audit, access and information rights over the provider and its sub-contractors; and the matrix confirming each required area is covered in the executed contract.

artifacts.name: Provider Access Attestations
artifacts.description: The provider attestation confirming no restriction or prohibition on organisation, auditor or regulator access to cloud-related information; the attestation acknowledging the regulator's access rights; the documentation of the provider's audit facility and cooperation commitments; and the regulator notification records where access was impeded.

artifacts.name: Audit Access Exercise Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for initiating and fulfilling audit and access requests to the provider, the log of audit and onsite assessment access exercised with dates, scope and outcomes, the records of audit access exercised by the organisation or its regulator, the access request fulfilment records, the audit access logs, the audit cooperation procedure, the records of audit engagements, the audit cooperation records, and the audit support procedures.

artifacts.name: Provider Assurance Evidence
artifacts.description: The register and copies of provider certifications covering service delivery, continuity and information security; the assessment of provider data security controls; the review of the provider's contingency plan, recovery capability and exit support; the assessment of the provider's sub-contracting practices; the support services agreement covering response times, escalation tiers and availability; the provider-supplied security testing results reviewed by the organisation; the sub-contractor security testing results; the provider company and financial information; and the records of interactions with the provider's external auditors.

artifacts.name: Audit Finding Follow-Up
artifacts.description: The tracker of audit findings on the provider with target dates, owner, remediation status and closure evidence; the correspondence with the provider regarding remediation and status updates; the records of escalations of overdue findings to the governing committee; and the audit findings responses.

artifacts.name: Regulator Information Response
artifacts.description: The service level clause obligating the provider to timely provide any information requested by the regulator and the log of those requests with the provider and organisation responses and their timeliness metrics.

artifacts.name: Audit Data Protection
artifacts.description: The procedures protecting sensitive information during audits, the evidence of least-privilege access and data masking or watermarking for audit data, the non-disclosure agreements executed with auditors, and the confidentiality agreements covering audit information.

CPL-03.3.notes: 41 asks across 6 frameworks. The contractual right of access, its actual exercise, and the protection of what the assessor sees are three proofs; the last is kept separate because the audit itself creates an exposure.

artifacts.name: Audit Charter and Programme
artifacts.description: The audit charter or policy establishing the function, the multi-year internal audit plan covering all management system areas with frequency, the multi-year rolling audit plan reflecting the defined cycle, the documented audit cycle with frequencies based on risk assessment, the documentation linking audit frequencies to risk assessment outcomes, the continuous monitoring programme documentation, and the audit service level references. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented audit management process requirement.

artifacts.name: Annual Audit Plan
artifacts.description: The documented annual audit plan covering goals, schedules, staffing needs, budget and reporting requirements; the annual audit plan and its committee or board approval; the audit budget and staffing plan for the year; the internal audit plan and schedule; the documented approved per-audit plans with scope, objectives, tools, timelines and resources; the reference showing alignment of the plans to recognised standards; and the evidence of audit activities executed per the plan.

artifacts.name: Audit Universe and Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The audit universe document, the documented risk assessment methodology for determining audit scope and frequency, the risk assessment reports, the risk-rated audit cycle plan, the application risk classification, the audit plan derived from the risk register, regulatory obligations and incidents, the audit scope documents linked to risk assessment findings, and the records tying audit scope to business priorities and the threat landscape.

artifacts.name: Audit Execution Records
artifacts.description: The completed internal audit reports with findings, evidence and recommendations; the records of audits conducted per the defined cycle; the working papers and evidence files; the security control testing results and reports; and the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports produced under the programme.

artifacts.name: Auditor Independence and Competence
artifacts.description: The qualifications and independence declaration for internal auditors and the reports from external advisors or previous certification body audits used as independent review.

artifacts.name: Management Review of Audit Results
artifacts.description: The management review minutes reviewing audit results and directing corrective actions, and the register of audit-driven corrective actions with owners, due dates and status.

artifacts.name: Audit Testing Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure governing audit tests on production systems, the engagement letter defining scope, timing and access for each audit, the impact assessment for audit activities on operational systems, the management sign-off on scope, timing and risk acceptance, the records of audit-specific access rights granted with expiry, the read-only account configuration used for audit testing, and the log of audit queries and actions performed against operational systems.

artifacts.name: Audit Tool Controls
artifacts.description: The audit tool inventory with its access restrictions and authorisation records, protecting the tooling that holds the audit record. HITRUST requires the approved information systems audit controls policy and standard with its implementing procedure, its awareness communications and its periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The risk assessment methodology documentation with its approval records and the risk register with entries, owners, ratings and treatment plans feeding the audit universe.

artifacts.name: Data Governance Audit Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented compliance specification with its compliance evidence and implementing procedures and workflows, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, the business intelligence dashboards and analytics use-case register, and the privacy artifacts covered by the audit scope.

artifacts.name: AI Oversight Records
artifacts.description: The responsibility matrix defining AI risk management roles, the documented evidence demonstrating the governance outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the ongoing monitoring and periodic review records.
