CPL-04.notes: 58 asks across 9 frameworks. Distinct from CPL-02.3 in that the object is the audit programme rather than what it finds; ISO 27001 A.8.34 protection of systems during audit testing is kept separate because it protects production from the auditor rather than the reverse.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The approved policy on the use of cryptographic controls plus the technical standard beneath it: approved algorithms and minimum key lengths, approved protocols and versions, where encryption is mandatory (at rest, in transit, removable media, authentication factors, administrative sessions, VPN), prohibited/deprecated algorithms, and random number generation requirements. Must be management-approved with scope, roles, version history and sign-off; HITRUST requires annual review records naming reviewer, date and changes captured, and several sources require the standard to reference the recognised source it follows (FIPS, NIST, ISO, IETF).

artifacts.name: Key Management Procedure and Key Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The procedure covering generation, distribution, storage, use, rotation, archival, revocation and destruction of cryptographic keys, with named custodians and their responsibilities, plus the operating records: key inventory with lifecycle status, key rotation log showing rotations performed against the defined schedule, and custodian assignment/acknowledgement records. Where core banking or payment keys are in scope, include the specific key management evidence for those systems.

artifacts.name: HSM and FIPS-Validated Module Evidence
artifacts.description: Inventory of cryptographic modules in use with their FIPS 140 validation certificate numbers (or Common Criteria certification), the HSM configuration documentation including operator roles and separation of duties, HSM usage records, and the algorithm validation records evidencing that the implementations relied upon are the certified ones. NIST 800-171 requires this specifically where FIPS-validated cryptography is mandated.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Inventory
artifacts.description: A single register of cryptography actually in use: cipher suites and protocol versions deployed across the environment, the applications and services relying on them, the encryption practices in use per channel (TLS, SFTP, S/MIME, full disk encryption, database encryption), and the systems covered at rest and in transit. This is the source list the annual algorithm review is run against.

artifacts.name: Data-at-Rest Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: Live configuration proving stored sensitive data is encrypted: full disk encryption on endpoints and servers, database and storage-level encryption, and the algorithm and key length in force. Includes the configuration showing stored authentication factors are hashed or encrypted (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2 or equivalent) and, where cardholder data is in scope, that any sensitive authentication data held before authorization completes is encrypted with strong cryptography.

artifacts.name: Data-in-Transit Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: TLS, VPN and session encryption configuration for the systems in scope - protocol versions and cipher suites enforced, certificate binding, remote access and session encryption settings, email encryption implementation - together with the verification output (scan or configuration audit) confirming the enforced settings match the standard and that weak versions are refused. Include the evidence for authentication factor transmission specifically where PCI DSS applies.

artifacts.name: Certificate Inventory
artifacts.description: Inventory of TLS/SSL and code-signing certificates with issuer, subject, owner, expiry date and the system each is installed on, sufficient to show certificates are tracked and renewed before expiry.

artifacts.name: Encryption Coverage Assessment and Implementation Records
artifacts.description: The assessment that pulls it together: confirmation that every system holding or transmitting sensitive or regulated data is covered by the required encryption, with the deployment coverage report showing percentage of estate encrypted and any documented exceptions. Supporting records include implementation and verification reports, code review or storage scan records confirming no plaintext secrets remain at rest, CSPRNG implementation verification, security evaluations of internet-facing systems, and the general security-measures documentation used to demonstrate Article 32-style appropriateness of the measures chosen.

artifacts.name: Algorithm Review, Deprecation and Crypto-Agility Plan
artifacts.description: Evidence that the cryptography in use is re-assessed against current industry guidance: the review report assessing each cipher suite and protocol against NIST/IETF advisories and flagging weak or vulnerable algorithms, evidence of subscription to or monitoring of the industry sources used (NIST advisories, vendor PSIRTs), the migration plan away from deprecated algorithms with dates and owners, and the longer-range crypto-agility or post-quantum migration plan. PCI DSS requires this review annually; NIS2 and ISO require it periodically.

artifacts.name: Removable Media and Endpoint Encryption Evidence
artifacts.description: The policy requiring encryption of removable media and portable devices, the enforcement configuration that blocks or encrypts unencrypted media, the device encryption configuration applied to endpoints, and the removable media handling procedures governing their use and transfer.

artifacts.name: Integrity Verification and Change Detection Evidence
artifacts.description: Cryptographic integrity controls and their output: file integrity monitoring configuration and coverage, integrity verification tool reports, unauthorized change detection records for software, firmware and information, and transaction/activity logging configuration with the records showing it operates in the production (including cloud) environment.

artifacts.name: Secure Administrative Protocol Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence that administrative access uses strong cryptography on all system components - SSH v2, RDP over TLS, HTTPS management interfaces with approved cipher and protocol settings - and evidence that insecure management protocols (Telnet, FTP, plain HTTP) are disabled or blocked.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Roles and Data Stewardship Assignments
artifacts.description: Documented roles and responsibilities for encryption and key management - who approves algorithms, who holds and rotates keys, who authorises exceptions - and the assignment and communication of data stewardship to the individuals entrusted with sensitive or regulated data, with evidence the assignments were communicated and accepted, and the records showing the roles operate in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Cryptography Awareness, Training and Agreements
artifacts.description: Training and awareness material covering secure handling of cryptographic material and credentials, completion records, campaign materials and effectiveness assessments, plus executed agreements carrying the required security clauses and signature records where third parties handle keys or encrypted data.

artifacts.name: Application and API Security Requirements with Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: Cross-mapped from ISO 27001 A.8.26 and MAS TRM: the reusable catalogue of application security requirements (including cryptographic requirements), the API security standard covering authentication, authorisation, validation and rate limiting, sample project security requirement specifications with sign-off records from security or architecture, per-application risk assessments driving requirement selection, security evaluations of acquired COTS/SaaS software, and the risk assessments underpinning the choice of technical measures.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Architecture Documentation Supporting Encryption Scope
artifacts.description: Cross-mapped from SOC 2 CC6.1 and GDPR Article 32: the information asset inventory and classification defining what must be encrypted, the access control policy and procedures, identity and access management system configuration, and network architecture and segmentation diagrams showing the boundaries the transit encryption protects. Peripheral to cryptography itself - collect once and reuse across the access control and classification controls.

CRY-01.notes: 120 manual entries across 19 sources collapsed to 16 artifacts. A large collector set is live (AWS root-account checks plus ~30 SaaS evidence collectors covering IdP, source control, hosting and comms platforms), so TLS/at-rest configuration state for those platforms is largely automated; the policy, standards, key management and review artifacts are not. ISO 27001 A.8.26 (application security requirements) and SOC 2 CC6.1 (access control) are loose cross-maps kept as separate labelled artifacts.

artifacts.name: Cryptography Policy
artifacts.description: The approved, management-signed policy governing use of cryptographic controls, covering data in transit as the primary scope plus data at rest and in use where the frameworks extend it, with scope, applicability, roles and responsibilities, mandated use cases by data classification, and version history. Must state review frequency; several frameworks require documented annual review. Where transmission or information-transfer security is regulated separately (health data, payment data, cloud workloads), the policy must explicitly address the confidentiality of transmitted sensitive data and any prohibition on commercial use or onward disclosure.

artifacts.name: Approved Cryptographic Algorithm & Protocol Standard
artifacts.description: The technical standard listing permitted algorithms, minimum key strengths, protocol versions and cipher suites for data in transit - and explicitly naming the prohibited/obsolete ones - with the deprecation timeline for each. Must at minimum cover TLS version floor and permitted cipher suites and key exchange, the algorithms approved for authentication factors in transit and at rest, and the algorithm inventory showing what is actually in use against what is approved.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Policy & Secure Transfer Procedures
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised methods for transferring information outside the organisation and the procedures implementing each method - SFTP, managed file transfer, secure/encrypted email, encrypted removable media, secure credential and key delivery over separate channels, and physical media couriers - including required approvals before transfer and pre-exchange validation. Must include the awareness communications informing personnel of the requirement and the periodic review record for the procedures.

artifacts.name: Transmission Encryption Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Live configuration exports proving encryption is enforced on every channel carrying sensitive data: TLS settings on public-facing endpoints, load balancers, web servers and API gateways; server-to-server and integration API TLS; VPN and remote-access (RDP/SSH) encryption settings; email transport encryption (TLS/S-MIME/PGP) for external mail flows; application- and database-level encryption; wireless and network-device encryption; encrypting PIN pads and PCI-PTS certified payment terminals with their tamper-response evidence; medical-device and multifunction-device/fax encryption; and mobile app secure-transport and secure-storage settings. Each export must carry the date, system identifier and reviewer.

artifacts.name: TLS/SSL Scan & Encryption Verification Reports
artifacts.description: Independent verification that the deployed configuration matches the standard: external SSL/TLS scan reports for every exposed endpoint confirming only approved protocol versions and cipher suites are accepted and weak protocols/ciphers are refused, network encryption verification results, and vulnerability assessment/penetration test reports covering transmission security with remediation tracked to closure. Scans must be recent and cover cloud-exposed endpoints as well as on-premises.

artifacts.name: Certificate Inventory & Management Records
artifacts.description: The inventory of all TLS and code-signing certificates safeguarding data in transit, with issuer, subject/SAN list, key length, expiry date and owner, together with the certificate lifecycle procedure covering trust validation (CN/SAN check, chain validation, revocation checking), renewal and revocation. Must be complete enough to show no in-scope endpoint relies on an untrusted, expired or weak certificate.

artifacts.name: Key Management Procedure & Key Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure covering key generation, distribution, exchange, storage, rotation, escrow and destruction for the keys protecting data in transit, plus the records it produces: key inventory and lifecycle records, key rotation logs against the defined schedule, and secure key/credential exchange records. Include the HSM/KMS documentation showing FIPS certification level, operator roles and configuration, and the crypto-agility or migration plan for moving off deprecated algorithms.

artifacts.name: Encryption Coverage Inventory
artifacts.description: A system-by-system inventory recording, for each in-scope system or data flow, whether encryption in transit (and at rest, where the framework extends the ask) is implemented, by which mechanism, against which data classification, with owner, status and last review date. Must be complete across critical systems and reconcilable to the configuration evidence, including the transmission-security control inventory and the inventory of online transactions and encryption appliances/software in use.

artifacts.name: Data Flow & Network Architecture Diagrams with Encryption Points
artifacts.description: Current, version-controlled, dated and approved diagrams showing components, interconnections, trust zones, segmentation and data flows, with the encryption boundary marked at each point sensitive data crosses a network. Must cover external transmission paths, third-party interconnections and, where applicable, PII flows with residency identified. Supporting network device configuration baselines and ruleset review records evidence the diagrams reflect reality.

artifacts.name: Data Classification Register & Sensitive Data Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The register classifying data elements (for example account numbers, PANs, OTPs, PINs, PHI, PII) with the confidentiality control assigned to each, plus the evidence those controls operate: tokenisation and masking of sensitive fields, in-processing protections such as masked logs and secure enclaves, DLP policy and active rule set covering the relevant data flows, removable-media and MDM controls, and the access matrix and provisioning/review records restricting who can reach the data in transit or at its endpoints. Data desensitisation procedures and masking job logs belong here where production data moves to non-production.

artifacts.name: Secure Transfer & Connection Logs
artifacts.description: System-generated logs corroborating that transfers actually occurred over the approved encrypted channels: managed file transfer platform exports showing encrypted transfers with recipients, secure file transfer logs, connection monitoring logs for VPN/TLS sessions, and session integrity evidence for remote access. Logs must be retained for the required period, tamper-protected, and carry timestamp, actor identity, action and outcome.

artifacts.name: Transmission Security Clauses in Third-Party Agreements
artifacts.description: The executed agreements governing data transmitted to or through external parties: data transfer and data sharing agreement templates and signed instances, third-party connectivity agreements, service agreements with online transaction partners, information exchange agreements, and third-party ICT access agreements - each carrying security clauses, confidentiality obligations, breach notification, right to audit and signatures. For cloud, include the executed clauses prohibiting disclosure to foreign authorities without prior written consent and prohibiting commercial use or model training on the organisation's data, plus the associated legal review. Chain-of-custody receipts and vendor escort records evidence controlled physical handover where transfers leave the network.

artifacts.name: Application & API Transmission Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The security requirements applied to applications and interfaces that transmit sensitive data: the reusable requirements catalogue, the API security standard covering authentication, authorisation, validation and rate limiting, sample project security requirement specifications with sign-off by security or architecture, secure design documentation, and the SSDLC gate evidence (code review, security testing approval) confirming transmission controls were verified before deployment. Include the evidence that stored and transmitted authentication factors are protected by strong cryptography and the code or storage audit confirming no plaintext secrets.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Risk Assessment & Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented assessment of cryptographic risk driving control selection - including the application risk assessments and acquired-software security evaluations that determine which transmission controls apply - together with the periodic review records for the cryptography policy, the algorithm and protocol review, and the encryption coverage assessment. Reviews must name the reviewer, date, observations and corrective actions; annual review is explicitly required by at least one framework.

artifacts.name: Cloud & Tenant Isolation Evidence for Data in Transit
artifacts.description: Where transmission crosses a cloud provider: the tenant isolation architecture describing logical or physical segregation (dedicated accounts/subscriptions, VPCs, dedicated keys), the resource tagging standard and compliance report showing every resource carries owner and classification, provider opt-out configuration for telemetry/analytics/AI-training features that would ingest the organisation's data, the PII data-flow mapping and DPIA, and provider availability/SLA monitoring reports supporting the assured-channel claim.

CRY-03.notes: 161 entries collapse to 15 artifacts. Cloud/SaaS collectors already exist for encryption-at-rest defaults and provider settings, so live configuration state is marked automated; policies, standards, agreements and assessments remain manual. A handful of entries are mis-mapped in the source data (ATM CCTV/alarms, availability SLA reporting, general access provisioning) and are folded into the nearest genuine transmission-security artifact rather than dropped.

artifacts.name: Transmission Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The transmission integrity controls documentation, the transmission integrity verification evidence, the digital signature or keyed-hash configuration, the message authenticity and integrity requirements, the message integrity verification logs, the message authentication implementation, and the integrity controls applied to processing and transmission. HITRUST requires the approved message integrity policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Transport Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: The encryption configuration for data in transit, the transport layer security configuration with integrity verification, the encryption configuration for regulated data in transit, the transmission security controls inventory, the external transmission encryption evidence, the secure file transfer logs, the session encryption evidence, the remote desktop and secure shell security settings, the remote access encryption configuration, and the virtual private network encryption standards.

artifacts.name: Certificate Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of transport layer and code-signing certificates with expiry dates and owners, the certificate documentation, and the data flow diagrams marking the encryption points the certificates terminate.

artifacts.name: Cryptography Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The policy defining approved algorithms, key lengths, protocols and use cases; the technical standards naming the specific ciphers with their deprecation plans; the cryptographic risk assessment; the plan for migration to post-quantum or alternative algorithms; and the assessment confirming encryption coverage for data at rest and in transit across critical systems.

artifacts.name: Key Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedures for key generation, distribution, rotation, escrow and destruction; the key rotation log; the hardware security module setup with its certification and operator roles; the key retirement, replacement or destruction procedure with its triggers; the destruction records with method and witness sign-off; the archival evidence for retired keys retained only to decrypt legacy data; and the key management for data at rest.

artifacts.name: Encryption at Rest Evidence
artifacts.description: The data-at-rest encryption configuration, the database encryption records, the full disk encryption documentation, and the encryption-at-rest, in-transit and in-use evidence covering the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Online Transaction Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of online transactions, the transaction integrity and online transaction security controls, the service agreements with online transaction partners, and the network architecture diagram with the device configuration baselines and ruleset review records protecting them. HITRUST requires the approved online transactions policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Application Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The catalogue of reusable application security requirements, the standard for interface authentication, authorisation, validation and rate limiting, the per-application risk assessment driving requirement selection, the security evaluation of acquired and hosted software before purchase, the redacted security requirements specifications from real projects, and the sign-off records showing security or architecture approved them.

artifacts.name: Network Security Architecture
artifacts.description: The network security architecture documentation and the access control evidence, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records for the systems carrying the transmissions.

artifacts.name: Published Content Controls
artifacts.description: The public information policy, the information disclosure guidelines, the content approval workflow, and the website content review records governing what may be transmitted to the public.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the message integrity requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

CRY-04.notes: 65 asks across 10 frameworks. The control is transmission integrity, but several frameworks arrive here dragging their whole cryptography estate; the key-management and at-rest artifacts are kept separate from the transmission ones so the control is not answered by a key policy alone.

artifacts.name: Cryptography Policy & Encryption Standard
artifacts.description: The approved cryptography policy and the accompanying encryption standard defining which data classes must be encrypted at rest, the approved algorithms and minimum key lengths, where cryptography must be applied (storage, database, application, endpoint, removable media, medical device and payment data), and the roles owning cryptographic decisions. Must include the removable media encryption policy, the cloud data security policy where cloud is in scope, evidence that application-level implementations align to it, and approval plus periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Data-at-Rest Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence that stored data is encrypted across the estate: storage volume and object store encryption settings, database and column/tablespace encryption, application-level encryption, cloud encryption configuration exports, and encryption applied to regulated data categories specifically named by the frameworks (cardholder and sensitive authentication data prior to authorisation, payment data, CUI, PHI, medical device data). Must cover in-processing protection where required and show coverage across every listed data category, not a sample.

artifacts.name: Endpoint & Full-Disk Encryption Deployment and Coverage Report
artifacts.description: Full-disk encryption configuration for laptops, desktops and mobile devices, the MDM policy and configuration enforcing it, and a coverage report reconciling encrypted devices against the asset inventory so that unencrypted or non-compliant endpoints are visible with remediation status.

artifacts.name: Removable Media & Transported Media Encryption Controls
artifacts.description: The removable media handling procedure and encryption policy, the technical configuration enforcing encryption or blocking unencrypted media, and evidence that data on media in transport (including CUI) is encrypted — covering USB devices, backup media and any physically moved storage.

artifacts.name: Key Management Procedures & Key Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The key management procedure covering generation, distribution, storage, rotation, escrow, revocation and destruction, with the operating records that prove it: HSM configuration documentation, certificate inventory, key rotation logs, cloud key management arrangements including BYOK/HYOK evidence, and split knowledge/dual control where payment scope requires it. Must show keys protecting data at rest are managed separately from the data they protect.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Algorithm & Module Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of cryptographic implementations in use with the algorithms, modes and key lengths for each, evidence of validated modules where required (FIPS 140), documentation of the algorithms approved for each use case, and the crypto-agility plan describing how deprecated algorithms will be replaced.

artifacts.name: Encryption-in-Transit / TLS Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: TLS and transport encryption configuration for internal, external and third-party connections, TLS scan or posture reports showing protocol and cipher compliance, secure file transfer logs, encryption of access sessions to sensitive systems, and encrypted communications for medical devices and payment channels where in scope.

artifacts.name: Data Classification Register & Encrypted Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: The data classification register identifying which data classes require encryption at rest, mapped to the systems and stores holding them, including the cloud resource tagging standard and its compliance report used to identify which resources fall in scope of the encryption requirement.

artifacts.name: Secret, Credential & Password Storage Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that authentication secrets are cryptographically protected at rest: the standard governing cryptography for authentication factors, configuration showing passwords are hashed with an approved algorithm rather than stored recoverably, privileged credential vault configuration including its offsite backup protection, and code or storage audit records confirming no secrets are stored in the clear.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Policy & Configuration
artifacts.description: The DLP policy and deployed ruleset, tool configuration and coverage evidence, and the reports it produces — the compensating detection layer for sensitive data leaving encrypted stores.

artifacts.name: Tenant Isolation & Access Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that encrypted data is also access-segregated: the access control policy and procedures, identity and access management configuration governing who can decrypt or reach the data, the network segmentation supporting those boundaries, and the tenant isolation architecture where multi-tenant cloud services hold the data.

artifacts.name: Data Masking / De-identification Procedures & Logs
artifacts.description: The data desensitisation or masking procedure applied when production data is copied to non-production environments, and the masking tool job logs evidencing it ran on the relevant datasets.

artifacts.name: Privacy Records for Protected Data
artifacts.description: The published privacy notice with version history, consent records, opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, and the PII data flow documentation with the associated data protection impact assessment — evidencing the protected data that the encryption controls exist to safeguard is itself governed.

artifacts.name: Cloud & Third-Party Contract Clauses for Data Protection
artifacts.description: Executed agreements carrying the required security and confidentiality clauses, third-party connectivity agreements, and — for cloud arrangements under banking rules — the clause governing disclosure to foreign authorities, the prohibition on commercial use of the institution's data, evidence that provider data-use opt-outs are configured, and the legal opinion confirming compliance with applicable data residency and protection law.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Risk Assessment & Control Test Reports
artifacts.description: The cryptographic risk assessment identifying where encryption is required and what residual risk remains, plus the evidence that the controls were tested: control implementation evidence, control test reports, and the qualification records for operators of specialised encrypted equipment where the framework requires demonstrated competence.

CRY-05.notes: 110 asks collapse to 15 artifacts. 61 collectors are attached including an EBS default-encryption check and broad SaaS coverage, so configuration items are hybrid: connectors evidence the cloud and SaaS estate while on-premise databases, application-level encryption and medical/payment devices still need manual export. The single largest duplication was 'encryption policy / standard / cryptographic standard' restated by 13 sources, and 'encryption-at-rest configuration' by 13 more.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Key Management Policy
artifacts.description: The approved key management policy stating requirements for key generation, distribution, storage, access, use, rotation, backup, archival, revocation and destruction, with defined roles and responsibilities, scope of systems and data covered, and review frequency. Frameworks variously require board or management approval and version control (HITRUST), explicit reference to a recognised key management standard such as ISO/IEC 11770 (QCB), evidence of periodic review with reviewer, observations and corrective actions, and awareness communications confirming personnel subject to the policy have been informed.

artifacts.name: Approved Cryptographic Algorithm and Encryption Standards
artifacts.description: The technical standards baseline listing organisation-approved algorithms, modes, key lengths, protocols and permitted use cases for data at rest, data in transit and APIs, including IV/nonce handling, key strength and storage requirements, deprecation dates for weak algorithms, and a crypto-agility or post-quantum migration plan. SBP Cloud additionally requires a signed subject-matter-expert review of the algorithm and key-length choices mapped to NIST/ISO guidance, together with evidence of that reviewer's qualifications and independence from the implementation team.

artifacts.name: Key Lifecycle Procedures
artifacts.description: The working procedures implementing the policy across the full key lifecycle: generation, distribution, activation, storage, use (including single-purpose key restrictions), backup, archival, rotation, suspension, deactivation, revocation, destruction, compromise handling and recovery. Must include the key protection requirements (protection against disclosure and misuse, key-encrypting keys of equal or greater strength stored separately, storage in the fewest possible locations), named responsible roles and control points. QCB expects the lifecycle stages enumerated (a)–(k); cloud frameworks expect the same procedure to cover keys held in CSP key management services.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Key and Certificate Inventory
artifacts.description: A complete register of cryptographic keys with, for each key: identifier, purpose/single-use mapping, owner and custodian, algorithm and length, storage location, activation date, cryptoperiod and next rotation date, and status. Includes the TLS and code-signing certificate inventory with expiry dates and owners. Frameworks expect the inventory to be maintained and evidenced as current, and used to demonstrate key lifecycle records exist for each entry.

artifacts.name: Key Generation and Ceremony Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that keys are generated under the approved procedure: signed key generation ceremony records for master and key-encrypting keys performed under dual control/split knowledge with named custodians and witnesses, HSM/KMS generation audit log extracts showing operator and timestamp, verification that approved algorithms, key lengths and entropy sources were used, and equivalent activation and re-generation records where keys are re-keyed.

artifacts.name: Cryptoperiod Definitions and Key Rotation Records
artifacts.description: The documented cryptoperiod per key type (aligned to vendor direction and industry guidance such as NIST SP 800-57), the resulting rotation schedule, and records evidencing that each key was actually rotated within its cryptoperiod, including re-encryption of protected data where required. Where the platform supports it, provide the KMS/HSM configuration export showing automated rotation enabled; where rotation is manual, provide the dated rotation log.

artifacts.name: Key Revocation, Destruction and Archival Records
artifacts.description: Records of keys retired, suspended, deactivated, revoked or destroyed, showing the trigger (end of cryptoperiod, weakened integrity, suspected or known compromise, personnel change), the method used (cryptographic erase, HSM zeroise), verification of destruction and witness or approver sign-off. Include archival evidence for retired keys retained solely to decrypt legacy data, with justification and protection controls.

artifacts.name: Key Custodian Register and Dual-Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The register of designated key custodians, the key components or functions assigned to each, and their signed acknowledgement of custodian responsibilities. Includes the split-knowledge and dual-control procedure mandating that no single person can access or reconstruct a cleartext key, and evidence that manual cleartext key operations were performed by at least two custodians.

artifacts.name: HSM and Key Store Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence of where and how keys are protected: HSM/KMS deployment documentation and configuration exports showing FIPS 140-2/3 certification level and tamper response, the key hierarchy diagram showing data-encryption keys wrapped by key-encrypting keys of equal or greater strength held separately, HSM placement and integration architecture, key storage security assessment, and equivalent evidence for cloud key vaults. QCB requires FIPS-140 certified HSM deployment evidence specifically.

artifacts.name: Key Access Control Configuration
artifacts.description: Access policy exports from IAM/KMS/HSM showing that key management functions are restricted to the fewest custodians necessary, that key import, replacement and administrative operations require authorised custodians under dual control, and that unauthorised substitution of keys is prevented through integrity checks and change approval. For cloud deployments this must show CSP principals are denied key administration where sole administration by the organisation is required. Configuration is collector-supplied; the governing procedure and custodian approvals are manual.

artifacts.name: Key Management Audit Logs
artifacts.description: Audit log extracts from the HSM/KMS covering key lifecycle and administrative events — generation, import, replacement, rotation, export, use and destruction — recording actor, timestamp, action and outcome, with evidence the logs are retained and protected from tampering.

artifacts.name: Key Distribution and Transport Records
artifacts.description: The secure key distribution procedure (encrypted distribution, key wrapping/transport mechanisms, split-knowledge delivery, integrity verification on receipt) and records of actual distribution events showing method, recipients, dates and the integrity verification performed, plus configuration of the wrapping/transport mechanism used.

artifacts.name: Key Backup, Recovery and Compromise Response Records
artifacts.description: Key backup procedures and evidence that backed-up key material is protected to the same standard as production keys, plus records of key recovery tests demonstrating keys can be restored when needed, and records of any key compromise events showing detection, revocation, re-keying and impact assessment.

artifacts.name: Encryption Coverage Evidence for Data at Rest and in Transit
artifacts.description: Evidence that the approved cryptography is actually applied across in-scope systems: configuration of data-at-rest encryption (full disk, database TDE or column-level, storage/bucket encryption), in-transit encryption for applications and APIs, digital signing configuration where required, and an encryption coverage assessment reconciling the classified information asset inventory and network/system architecture against implemented encryption, with any gaps and exceptions identified. Includes verification reports confirming implementations match the standard.

artifacts.name: Cloud Key Ownership and BYOK/HYOK Evidence
artifacts.description: For keys protecting data hosted with a cloud provider: the signed document agreed with the CSP specifying key and HSM location(s), ownership and management responsibility; evidence of BYOK/HYOK implementation with key material generated by the organisation (external key store, customer-managed keys); verification that each workload or environment uses distinct keys with no cross-environment reuse; and evidence of the customer's ability to manage its own keys in the provider's platform.

CRY-09.notes: 131 entries collapse to 15 artifacts. The largest duplicate group is lifecycle procedure text (27 entries: CSA CCM alone restates generation, purpose, rotation, revocation, destruction, activation, suspension, deactivation, archival, compromise, recovery and inventory as separate asks) — one lifecycle procedure document satisfies all of them. This control has extensive collector coverage (54 SaaS/cloud checks), so key access control, audit logs, rotation state and encryption coverage are automated or hybrid.

artifacts.name: Key Lifecycle Procedures
artifacts.description: The procedures for key generation, distribution, rotation, escrow and destruction; the key lifecycle management documentation; the key lifecycle procedures; the key management policy and procedures; and the key generation, revocation and repair records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented key rotation, revocation, activation, suspension, deactivation, destruction and compromise requirements.

artifacts.name: Key Rotation Records
artifacts.description: The log of cryptographic key rotations performed per schedule, the key rotation logs, the key rotation schedules, and the key renewal procedures governing them.

artifacts.name: Key Compromise Response
artifacts.description: The key compromise response procedures and the key revocation and replacement records evidencing a compromised key was withdrawn and its traffic re-keyed.

artifacts.name: Key Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for retirement, replacement or destruction of keys triggered by end of cryptoperiod or integrity weakening; the records of retired and destroyed keys with method and witness sign-off; and the archival evidence of retired keys retained only where necessary to decrypt legacy data.

artifacts.name: Key Custodian Records
artifacts.description: The key custodian documentation, the key custody records, the escrow and recovery procedures, and the access policy export showing access to key-management functions restricted to the fewest custodians necessary.

artifacts.name: Key Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure governing protection of keys against disclosure and misuse covering access restrictions and key encryption, the key hierarchy diagram, the key protection mechanisms, the key strength and storage standards, and the hardware security module setup with its certification and operator roles.

artifacts.name: Cryptography Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The policy defining approved algorithms, key lengths, protocols and use cases; the technical standards naming the specific ciphers with their deprecation plans; the plan for migration to post-quantum or alternative algorithms; the assessment confirming encryption coverage across critical systems; and the cryptographic independence verification.

artifacts.name: Certificate Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of transport layer and code-signing certificates with expiry dates and owners and the certificate management records tracking renewal before expiry.

artifacts.name: Wireless Key Change Records
artifacts.description: The procedure governing wireless encryption key changes upon personnel changes or suspected compromise, the records identifying personnel with knowledge of wireless keys to enable timely change on departure, the records of key changes with date, trigger event and approver, the network identifier and key rotation procedure, and the wireless asset inventory the change must cover.

artifacts.name: Personal Device Approval Records
artifacts.description: The personal device approval workflow governing which devices may hold the keys in scope.

CRY-09.3.notes: 53 asks across 9 frameworks. The demand is the response to a key that is lost, compromised or must change; CSA CCM contributes eight separate lifecycle states which are grouped by what an assessor asks for rather than kept as eight documents.

artifacts.name: Key Management Procedures
artifacts.description: The procedures for key generation, distribution, rotation, escrow and destruction; the key management procedures; the key management policy and procedure; the key management policy; the key lifecycle procedures covering each defined stage; the key management policy referencing the applicable key-management standard; and the key management procedure with its key inventory and lifecycle records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented key generation, key purpose, key activation and key rotation requirements. HITRUST requires the approved key management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Key Custodian Records
artifacts.description: The key custodian documentation, the key custodian list, the key custody records, and the access policy export showing access to key-management functions restricted to the fewest custodians necessary.

artifacts.name: Key Distribution and Exchange
artifacts.description: The key exchange procedure documentation, the multi-channel credential delivery procedure, and the encryption configuration for data in transit protecting the exchange itself.

artifacts.name: Key Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure governing protection of keys against disclosure and misuse covering access restrictions and key encryption, the key hierarchy diagram, the key protection mechanisms, the key strength and storage standards, and the hardware security module setup with its certification and operator roles.

artifacts.name: Key Rotation Records
artifacts.description: The log of cryptographic key rotations performed per schedule, the key rotation logs, and the key rotation schedules governing them.

artifacts.name: Key Generation and Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The key generation, revocation and repair records and the key destruction records closing the lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Cryptography Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The policy defining approved algorithms, key lengths, protocols and use cases; the technical standards naming the specific ciphers with their deprecation plans; the cryptographic standards documentation; the plan for migration to post-quantum or alternative algorithms; and the assessment confirming encryption coverage across critical systems.

artifacts.name: Certificate Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of transport layer and code-signing certificates with expiry dates and owners.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the key management requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

CRY-09.4.notes: 45 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps CRY-09.3; here the object is control and distribution — custodian assignment, key exchange and access restriction — rather than loss or change.

artifacts.name: Data Protection & Classification Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy establishing the data classification levels in use (for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and the protection obligations attaching to each. Must define scope, applicability, roles and responsibilities including data owners and custodians, and the governance framework under which data management operates. Frameworks add specific coverage: sensitive data protection expectations for cloud environments, protection of critical information assets against unauthorised access, misuse and fraudulent modification or disclosure, and the data management process documentation describing how the classification programme runs end to end.

artifacts.name: Data Handling, Labelling & Process Control Procedures
artifacts.description: The handling matrix mapping each classification level to concrete rules for storage, labelling, transmission, sharing, retention and disposal, plus the labelling procedures and handling guidelines staff actually follow. Must cover handling, transmission and storage of data and demonstrate alignment with the applicable legal requirements. Information flow diagrams for critical processes and the business process control documentation showing where data protection controls sit in the flow are also required.

artifacts.name: Classified Information Asset Inventory & Register
artifacts.description: The master inventory of information assets and the systems holding them, each with an assigned owner, custodian, classification value, location and retention requirement, reconciled against the technical asset inventory. Must include hardware and software assets from the CMDB or asset management tool, cloud resource inventory from the CSPM tooling, and the register of confidential information specifically. Evidence of formal asset ownership assignment and acknowledgement is required, together with the periodic review log showing assets added, retired and verified and classifications reassessed where circumstances changed. Automated discovery scan output reconciled against the register is requested to prove completeness.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy, NDAs & Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The acceptable use policy defining permitted and prohibited uses of IT resources, email, internet and organisational data, with signed or electronically acknowledged acceptance records from employees and contractors, and executed non-disclosure agreements for both populations. Supporting evidence includes the training module completion report for the acceptable use content, the login banner reminding users of their obligations, and records of detected violations with the action taken (redacted as appropriate).

artifacts.name: Records Retention Schedule & Document Control Records
artifacts.description: The records management policy and the retention schedule listing each record type with its retention period, the legal or regulatory basis for that period, and the approved disposition method. Must be supported by evidence the schedule is enforced rather than aspirational: the retention policy configuration in the content management or email platform (for example retention labels), the documented storage, encryption and access controls protecting retained records, access logs to archived records for traceability, and the data archival procedures. One framework additionally requires control of documented information covering availability, distribution and version control, the access control settings and audit logs of the document management system, and a register of external-origin documents relied upon.

artifacts.name: Secure Disposal, Sanitisation & Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The media sanitisation and disposal policy and the hardware decommissioning procedure, together with the records proving disposal actually happened: destruction logs identifying what was destroyed, when, by which method and with witness or certificate of destruction from the disposal vendor, and the wiping or destruction verification evidence for each asset. Must cover records destroyed at end of retention as well as decommissioned hardware and media, and must show media is sanitised or destroyed before disposal or reuse.

artifacts.name: Media Protection Policy & Handling Procedures
artifacts.description: The media protection and device control policy covering approved media types, registration, encryption requirements and permitted movement, plus the procedures implementing it: media handling, secure transport (tamper-evident packaging, approved courier, chain of custody), hardware and media tracking, and physical securing of media holding regulated data. Must include the mobile device management policy where mobile endpoints carry protected data, and evidence the policy is reviewed on the defined cycle.

artifacts.name: Media Inventory, Movement & Endpoint Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The register of managed removable media with owner, classification and current status; the documented inventory of physical media storage locations with the controls applied to each (locked cabinet, safe, secure room) and inspection or photographic evidence of that secure storage; the authorisation records for any movement of hardware or media holding protected data; and the endpoint configuration enforcing encryption on removable media and restricting use to approved devices only.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Configuration & Alert Records
artifacts.description: The DLP policy defining scope, detection strategy and response, the deployed ruleset covering email, endpoint, web and cloud channels, dashboard evidence of the coverage achieved, and the alert log showing detections triaged and investigated to closure. Must include DLP configuration for cloud storage services and endpoint control over transfers to removable media, the incident response playbook for a confirmed leakage event, and the deployment and configuration records for the DLP tooling. Data theft detection mechanisms and the technical evidence of DLP and encryption applied to critical assets are additionally named.

artifacts.name: Encryption, Secure Transmission & Backup Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The approved cryptographic standard naming the algorithms, key lengths and modules permitted for data at rest and in transit, together with configuration evidence that it is enforced: TLS/SSL configuration for data in transit, encryption of external transmissions, secure file transfer logs, and encryption of backup data. Must cover sensitive data transfer specifically and the access controls protecting backup repositories, with verification evidence that backup data protection is operating. Connectivity agreements governing secure transfer with third parties are also requested.

artifacts.name: Data Access Restriction Evidence & Protection Control Audit Records
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence that access to classified data is restricted to those with a need to know: storage and data-store access control configuration, data ACL documentation, the access control matrix showing rights to critical information assets by role, and the multi-tier configuration (identity, network ACL, web application firewall) preventing unauthorised access. Must be accompanied by the access review records and the documented need-to-know justifications for granted access, and by independent verification - the audit report validating protection controls on critical information assets and the compliance verification records confirming handling aligns with legal requirements. Segregation of duties over data-handling privileges is named by one framework.

artifacts.name: Data Integrity Controls & Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented integrity standard and policy covering how data is protected from unauthorised or undetected modification across databases, application services and messaging, plus the technical controls implementing it: storage integrity controls and checksums, database integrity monitoring configuration, file integrity monitoring configuration on the in-scope servers, and database tamper-proofing through audit logging, row-level integrity hashes or write-once journaling. Must include the operating evidence: integrity verification procedures and their results, system-generated reports demonstrating integrity, FIM and integrity alert logs with triage outcomes, information processing validation and integrity check records, and error and exception handling logs with the corrective action taken. Change control documentation for systems holding regulated data, and data quality management procedures with their reports and metrics, are also required.

artifacts.name: De-identification & Anonymisation Documentation
artifacts.description: The de-identification policy and procedures, the documentation of the method applied (expert determination or the safe harbor identifier-removal method), the verification records confirming de-identification was performed correctly on each dataset, and the re-identification risk assessment demonstrating the residual risk of re-identification is acceptably small.

artifacts.name: Data Protection Training & Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The training curriculum and materials teaching staff how to classify and handle data correctly and meet privacy obligations, together with completion records for the whole workforce. Must evidence that new hires are trained within the required timeline after joining and that refresher training runs on a defined schedule, with the completion records to prove both.

artifacts.name: Transaction Authorisation & Anomaly Detection Controls
artifacts.description: For payment messaging environments: the relationship management authorisation review records and correspondent authorisation documentation with the change management log for authorisation changes, the transaction verification procedures, the configured payment limits, evidence of dual authorisation on transactions, and the anomaly detection rules applied to transaction flows. Cross-mapped into this control through the payment-messaging framework; the substantive evidence is normally owned by the transaction integrity control.

DCH-01.notes: 135 entries across 16 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts. Automated coverage is thin (storage encryption defaults, MDM and endpoint agents), so most artifacts are manual or hybrid. The payment-messaging transaction controls bucket is framework drift cross-mapped into this control and is normally satisfied by the transaction integrity control.

artifacts.name: Data Stewardship Role Assignments
artifacts.description: The documented appointments for each data governance role — governance officer, business data executive, business data steward, IT data steward, metadata steward and reference data steward — with their compliance evidence, implementation records, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Data Owner Register
artifacts.description: The register of information owners responsible for the confidentiality, integrity and availability of assigned assets, the data inventory by process with process owner classification responsibilities, and the ownership attestation for hosted data. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented ownership and stewardship requirement.

artifacts.name: Responsibility Assignment Matrix
artifacts.description: The documented and maintained matrix covering all data, systems and processes with the version or review log evidencing it is kept current.

artifacts.name: Information Asset Inventory and Classification
artifacts.description: The comprehensive inventory of information assets with owner, classification and retention schedule; the classification policy defining levels with handling guidelines; the asset inventory register with classification; and the data management process documentation behind them. HITRUST requires the approved asset ownership standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Data Ownership in Provider Contracts
artifacts.description: The cloud service contracts specifying data ownership terms, the board-approved policy confirming the organisation retains ultimate responsibility for data security, the register of hosted data with ownership attestation, and the due diligence records on the provider's data security practices.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The data quality accountability statement naming who owns quality, the data quality management procedure, the quality assurance review records, and the data quality management procedures supporting them.

artifacts.name: Sector Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The accountability statement and governance records for the regulated data category, the compliance mapping to the applicable regulation, and the evidence of compliance with the regulator's directions.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The data retention schedule, the disposal procedures, the secure disposal and destruction standard operating procedure covering paper and electronic media, and the disposal or destruction certificates from shredding or secure wiping.

artifacts.name: Physical Media Custody Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining controls for physically securing media containing regulated data, the documented inventory of storage locations with the controls at each, and the photographic or inspection evidence of secure storage.

artifacts.name: Metadata and Reference Data Registers
artifacts.description: The metadata repository or data catalog export, the master and reference data register with golden-record definitions and stewardship records, and the register evidencing each with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Information Flow Documentation
artifacts.description: The information flow diagrams for critical processes and the system-generated reports demonstrating data integrity across them.

artifacts.name: Correspondent Relationship Records
artifacts.description: The correspondent authorisation documentation, the relationship management change logs, and the periodic review records over the authorised set.

artifacts.name: Acquisition Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The acquisition documentation, the security requirements written into contracts, and the vendor security assessment results for systems that will hold the data being stewarded.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of asset ownership obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-01.1.notes: 68 asks across 12 frameworks. NDMO defines six distinct stewardship roles as separate specifications; those are merged into one role-assignment artifact because an assessor asks for the appointment set, not six documents.

artifacts.name: Data Classification & Protection Policy
artifacts.description: The approved, current policy defining the classification scheme (e.g. Public / Restricted / Confidential / Secret, or the NDMO / regulator-defined levels) and the protection required for each class wherever data is processed or stored. Must state scope, roles and responsibilities, review frequency and approval. Healthcare regimes require an explicit health information protection policy covering access criteria, ownership and sharing requirements; DoH ADHIE requires the policy to address confidentiality, integrity and availability of PHI.

artifacts.name: Data Handling & Labelling Procedures
artifacts.description: The working procedures that turn the classification policy into practice: labelling rules per class and step-by-step handling instructions covering access, processing, storage, transmission, printing and sharing, plus the data management process documentation and the business-process controls that enforce them. PISF 2026 and NDMO expect documented workflows with responsible roles and control points; DoH ADHIE additionally expects a documented misuse-prevention procedure.

artifacts.name: Sensitive & Regulated Data Inventory
artifacts.description: The register of sensitive and regulated data elements and where they live — data classification register naming each element (e.g. account number, national ID, OTP, PIN, PHI), its class, owner and assigned protection; the storage-location inventory for regulated data with the protection method applied at each location (PCI DSS requires this for every PAN storage location); and the labelled dataset register per the applicable classification levels. Must carry last-review dates and traceability to the source systems.

artifacts.name: Encryption & Cryptographic Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that sensitive data is cryptographically protected at rest, in transit and, where required, in use: the list of approved cryptographic solutions and modules; database/file/column encryption and tokenisation configuration with the KMS/HSM keys used; TLS configuration and scan results for all external and internal endpoints; secure file transfer evidence for external transmissions; and the key management procedures governing the keys. PCI DSS requires the documented method used to render stored PAN unreadable (hashing, truncation, tokenisation or strong cryptography); SBP additionally requires in-processing protections such as masked logs and application-tier tokenisation; DoH ADHIE requires encryption evidence specifically for PHI.

artifacts.name: Data Masking & De-identification Evidence
artifacts.description: The de-identification policy and procedures, the method applied (HIPAA expert determination or safe harbor) with its supporting documentation, verification records confirming de-identification was performed, and the re-identification risk assessment. Also covers the policy governing use of production data in non-production environments and the records showing masking was actually implemented there.

artifacts.name: Data Integrity Controls & Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The data integrity policy and the verification procedures that detect unauthorised alteration or destruction of regulated data, the integrity monitoring controls in operation, processing validation and integrity check records, and the change control documentation for the systems holding that data (ePHI systems specifically under HIPAA).

artifacts.name: Access Control, Stewardship & Segregation of Duties Evidence
artifacts.description: Who may reach the data and on what basis: documented assignment of data stewardship to named custodians, the access criteria applied to sensitive/regulated data, the access privilege records and segregation of duties matrix, document-management-system access settings and audit logs, and the live configuration restricting privileged actions such as printing and sharing (including printer restrictions in PHI areas).

artifacts.name: Transaction & Counterparty Protection Controls
artifacts.description: For payment and messaging environments: transaction verification procedures, payment limit configuration, dual authorisation evidence and anomaly detection rules, together with the correspondent relationship (RMA) authorisation documentation, periodic RMA review records and RMA change management logs.

artifacts.name: Platform Hardening & Segmentation Evidence
artifacts.description: Hardening evidence for the systems that store or process regulated data — payment card systems, core banking application and database hardening, magnetic stripe data protection controls — plus network segmentation evidence isolating the regulated environment, and the documented safeguards applied where the data is handled at alternate or secondary sites.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention & Physical Handling Controls
artifacts.description: Controls preventing regulated data leaving approved channels: the DLP policy and the active rule set covering the in-scope data flows (email, endpoint, network), plus the physical handling evidence — clear desk/clear screen audit records in areas holding sensitive records, detection of unattended sensitive material, monitoring of unescorted staff such as cleaners in those areas, and hardcopy shredding records and shredder logs.

artifacts.name: Retention, Disposition & Document Control Records
artifacts.description: The retention and disposition schedule for the regulated data and the documented information that supports it, the data lifecycle records covering retention, archival and secure disposal, the disposal procedures applied, and the document control policy plus external-origin document register governing controlled documents (availability, protection, distribution, version control, retention).

artifacts.name: Training & Awareness Records for Sensitive Data Handling
artifacts.description: Curriculum plus completion records showing everyone who handles the data has been trained: privacy/handling training content, completion records for all workforce members, evidence that new joiners were trained within the required timeline, the refresher schedule and its records, orientation records for staff entering PHI environments, and awareness communications confirming personnel were informed of the labelling and handling requirements.

artifacts.name: Confidentiality & Data Sharing Agreements
artifacts.description: Signed instruments binding others to the protection requirements: non-disclosure and confidentiality obligations for staff and third parties, data sharing agreements with interoperability and integration/API terms, and third-party connectivity agreements for external transmissions — each showing scope, term, security and privacy clauses, right to audit, breach notification and both parties' signatures. Include the referenced sanctions and disciplinary provisions applied when obligations are breached.

artifacts.name: Compliance Monitoring, Audit & Violation Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the protections are checked and enforced: compliance monitoring records for handling procedures, internal audit reports on adherence with findings and management responses, records of handling violations and the resulting incidents, disclosure monitoring records, error and exception handling logs with corrective actions, periodic review records naming reviewer, date, observations and corrective actions, professional licence/eligibility verification for staff granted access, availability and SLA/uptime monitoring reports, and the documented breach notification procedure to the regulator (DOH under ADHICS).

artifacts.name: Threat & Risk Assessment for Regulated Data
artifacts.description: The threat and risk assessment reports covering the environments holding sensitive/regulated data, the register of mitigating controls traced to each identified risk, periodic threat landscape review records, and the evidence that the selected threat-protection controls are implemented.

DCH-01.2.notes: 105 framework evidence asks collapse to 15 artifacts. No automated collectors are attached to this control; encryption, access and hardening configuration items are marked hybrid or automated because a connector could produce the live configuration state while the governing documents remain manual.

artifacts.name: Data Access Control Matrix
artifacts.description: The role-based access matrix enforcing least privilege for data, the access control matrix per system with the data owner's approval, the owner-approved business rules, and the access control list configuration over the data stores.

artifacts.name: Data Access Approval Records
artifacts.description: The documented data, document, database and metadata access approval specifications with their implementing procedures and process workflows, the access authorisation records signed by the asset owner, the register with a named owner, and the formal approval and socialisation records.

artifacts.name: Data Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The records of regular data access reviews and monitoring, the access control review records, the documented need-to-know justification for each grant, and the periodic control adequacy review by the owner.

artifacts.name: Data Classification Scheme
artifacts.description: The data classification policy and scheme with the labelled dataset register, the documented information handling procedures by classification level covering access, processing, storage, communication and printing, and the training records for those procedures.

artifacts.name: Asset Ownership Register
artifacts.description: The asset ownership register with the owner-defined control requirements they are accountable for and the shared resource ownership documentation where a single owner is not possible.

artifacts.name: Data Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The data retention schedule with the archival policy and its access rights, the data lifecycle records, the disposal procedures, and the data management process documentation governing them.

artifacts.name: Data Masking and Non-Production Controls
artifacts.description: The data masking implementation records and the production data usage policy for non-production environments, controlling exposure of regulated data outside the systems authorised to hold it.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Population Handling Records
artifacts.description: The handling policy for data on protected or high-profile individuals, the access control configuration enforcing it, the procedures aligned with the sector directions, and the compliance evidence against the participation criteria.

artifacts.name: Health Information Physical Protections
artifacts.description: The documented access criteria for healthcare information, the orientation records for personnel handling it, the professional licence verification records, the clear desk and screen audit records in areas where it is processed, the unattended-information detection controls, the print and share privilege restrictions with local-printer-only configuration, the cleaning staff access monitoring, the hardcopy shredding records, and the breach notification procedure to the regulator.

artifacts.name: Documented Information Control
artifacts.description: The document control policy and procedure covering availability, protection, distribution, version control, retention and disposition; the retention and disposition schedule; the register of external-origin documents; and the document management system access control settings and audit logs.

artifacts.name: Metadata Catalog Access Records
artifacts.description: The metadata repository or data catalog export with the access approval specification governing who may reach it, and the register evidencing it with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Business Process Control Records
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action, and the segregation of duties matrix with access privilege records.

artifacts.name: Cloud Documentation Records
artifacts.description: The documented information control requirement with the records demonstrating it operates in the cloud environment covered.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing and Security Control Records
artifacts.description: The documented security controls specification with its implementing procedures, the data sharing agreements and interoperability standards, the data security control evidence including access controls, and the approved data management and personal data protection strategy behind them.

DCH-01.4.notes: 76 asks across 10 frameworks. NDMO restates the access-approval artifact across four specifications (document, database, metadata, data) and those are merged. ADHICS HI 2.1 contributes physical protections for health information that are genuinely different evidence and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Data & Asset Classification Policy
artifacts.description: Board- or management-approved policy establishing that all data and assets must be classified. Must state scope and applicability (including BYOD and cloud), roles and responsibilities, the control objectives, review frequency, approval signature and version history, and be shown in its current approved version with the version-control/review record behind it. Several sources want the policy plus a separate documented procedure or work instruction implementing it, and evidence of top-management approval.

artifacts.name: Data Classification Scheme and Handling Matrix
artifacts.description: The classification scheme itself, naming each level (e.g. Public / Internal / Confidential / Restricted, or the NDMO or QCB restricted-private-public levels) with the criteria for assigning each, mapped to required handling rules per level: labelling, storage, transmission, access, retention and disposal. Must be specific enough for an owner to classify a new dataset without asking. Include metadata/labelling guidance where a data catalogue is used, and the handling guidance issued to staff.

artifacts.name: Classified Asset and Data Inventory
artifacts.description: The register showing classification actually applied - every information asset, dataset, application, database, cloud resource and (where in scope) AI system with its assigned classification, owner, custodian, location, criticality and last-review date. Must be traceable back to source systems, cover cloud as well as on-premises assets, and be current. Some sources want it broken out per business process or per application; others want the cloud subset tagged with owner, criticality and the controls applicable at that classification.

artifacts.name: Asset and Data Owner Assignment Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that named individuals are formally accountable for classifying and protecting each asset or dataset - assignment letters, acknowledgements, a data/system owner register, or a RACI showing owner and custodian per asset. Must show the assignment was accepted (acknowledged) and identify who is responsible for confidentiality, integrity and availability of the assigned assets, including classification responsibilities held by business process owners.

artifacts.name: Asset Discovery and Inventory Reconciliation Reports
artifacts.description: Output of automated discovery (endpoint discovery tooling, CSPM/cloud resource export) reconciled against the CMDB or asset register, plus the reconciliation log showing what was added, retired or corrected and by whom. Demonstrates the classified inventory is complete rather than a hand-maintained spreadsheet.

artifacts.name: Classification Criteria and Impact/Valuation Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The methodology and its worked output for deciding what classification an asset gets: asset criticality criteria, confidentiality/integrity/availability impact ratings, information valuation and financial impact tolerance criteria, protection-level assessments, and the justification records tying a given asset's classification to its assessed impact. Where a risk-tier model is used for AI systems, include the approved risk tolerance statement with its approval record. Assessments must show scope, criteria, methodology, findings, ratings and the acceptance decision.

artifacts.name: Periodic Classification Review and Reclassification Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that classifications are re-checked on a defined cycle and changed when they should be: review logs naming reviewer, date, assets reviewed, observations, reclassification decisions and corrective actions, plus the refresh evidence for the inventory itself. Frequency is set by the organization in most sources; several require review by the data or system owner specifically, and NDMO additionally expects compliance audit/assessment records with findings and remediation tracking.

artifacts.name: Media Classification, Labelling and Transit Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that classification is physically applied to media: the media classification matrix with the controls required per class, the media register with labels assigned, sample photographs or images of labelled physical media, the labelling procedure, and - for media moved off site - the transit procedure, transit tracking records, tamper-evident packaging evidence and signed courier agreements. PCI DSS scopes this to all media holding cardholder data.

artifacts.name: Retention Schedule and Secure Disposal Procedure with Destruction Certificates
artifacts.description: The records retention schedule tied to classification levels (with the access-control and integrity protections applied to retained records), the secure disposal and destruction SOP for paper and electronic media, and the completed destruction evidence - shredding or secure-wipe certificates, and, for cloud data, the provider's written deletion confirmation covering all storage locations including sub-contractor sites. HITRUST additionally wants the approved policy and implementing procedure for protection of organizational records.

artifacts.name: Classification Awareness and Communication Records
