artifacts.description: Evidence that staff were told how to classify and handle data: training or awareness material on the classification scheme, delivery records with attendee list, dates, module reference and completion status, and evidence the policy itself was communicated (e.g. the distribution mail or intranet publication). Where an effectiveness measure exists, include it.

artifacts.name: Confidentiality Agreements and Third-Party Classified Information Handling Records
artifacts.description: Executed NDAs/confidentiality agreements for employees and contractors, and executed third-party agreements carrying the required security clauses with signature records. For information classified by another entity, include the mapping of external classification schemes to your own, the procedure for interpreting inbound classifications, and records of the controls actually applied. For cloud, include the contractual clauses on advance notice of data-location change (with right to reject or terminate) and on secure deletion at exit.

artifacts.name: Technical Enforcement Configuration for Classified Data (DLP, Residency, Database Access)
artifacts.description: Live configuration proving classification drives controls: DLP policy and active rule set covering the sensitive data types in scope (PII, national ID, account and card numbers), CASB/cloud-native DLP inspection and blocking configuration for uploads, downloads and shares, the enhanced-control matrix applied to high-value assets (customer-managed keys, MFA, enhanced logging, privileged access management), the data residency register and the region-restriction policy configuration enforcing it, and for databases the classification of held data with the corresponding role and permission matrix. Include sample anomaly/UEBA alerts on unusual access to classified data with their triage records.

artifacts.name: Data Governance Framework, Data Quality and Data Flow Documentation
artifacts.description: The data governance framework and supporting policies, data quality management procedures with their reports and metrics, system-generated reports evidencing data integrity, and information flow diagrams for the critical processes that handle classified data - showing where classified data originates, moves and is stored.

artifacts.name: Backup and Retention Configuration Aligned to Classification
artifacts.description: Evidence that backup and retention treatment follows the classification: the approved backup and restoration policy stating frequency, retention, RPOs and ransomware protection, the immutability/object-lock configuration on backup repositories, backup job execution logs for the review period, and signed restoration test reports - SBP Cloud requires half-yearly restoration testing with the last two cycles evidenced. Overlaps heavily with BCD-11; collect once and reuse.

DCH-02.notes: 129 manual entries across 19 sources collapsed to 14 artifacts. No automated collectors are mapped to this control, so nothing is genuinely collected today; 'automated'/'hybrid' marks what a connector could produce. Backup, DLP/residency and data-quality items enter via cross-mapped requirements (SBP Cloud 12.2, COBIT APO14, SOC 2 CC2.1) rather than classification per se - keep them but expect overlap with BCD-11 and the data-protection controls.

artifacts.name: Media Access Control Procedure
artifacts.description: The media access control procedures, the authorised media access list, the device and media control policy, the hardware and media tracking procedures, the movement authorisation records, and the media storage access logs. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limit-access-to-regulated-data-on-media and control-the-flow-of-regulated-data requirements.

artifacts.name: Access Justification Records
artifacts.description: The need-to-know access justifications, the data access control list configuration documentation, and the access control review records evidencing the list is kept to those who require it.

artifacts.name: Media Inventory and Tracking
artifacts.description: The register of all managed removable media with owner, classification and status, the media tracking logs, the media handling policy, and the procedure for secure transport of media covering tamper-evident packaging, courier and chain of custody.

artifacts.name: Media Encryption and Restriction
artifacts.description: The endpoint or data loss prevention configuration enforcing encryption on removable media, the media encryption configuration, the policy on approved media types with encryption, registration and disposal, the endpoint policy evidence restricting removable-device use to approved devices only, the device password enforcement configuration, the device management platform records, and the portable device access authentication evidence.

artifacts.name: Data Classification Records
artifacts.description: The data classification policy and procedures, the confidential information inventory or register, the data handling and labelling procedures, the data management process documentation, and the non-disclosure agreements binding employees and contractors to the handling rules.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The data retention schedule, the data disposal procedures, the media disposal procedures, the disposal records, and the records of secure media destruction including certificates from the disposal vendor.

artifacts.name: Content Access Approval Records
artifacts.description: The approved document and content access approval policy or standard with its documented specification and compliance evidence, the documented procedures behind it, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the formal approval and socialisation records covering committee minutes, sign-off and workshops, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability.

DCH-03.notes: 41 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps DCH-06; what is distinct here is who may reach the media rather than how it is stored, so the authorised-access list and the access justification are the primary artifacts.

artifacts.name: Disclosure Scope Controls
artifacts.description: The minimum necessary disclosure procedure, the operator-defined minimum data set, the disclosure scope review records, the information access request and approval workflow, and the need-to-know access justifications behind each disclosure.

artifacts.name: Downstream Disclosure Verification
artifacts.description: The compliance verification procedure for downstream disclosures, the disclosure audit reports, and the legal and regulatory compliance attestation obtained from the recipient.

artifacts.name: De-identification Records
artifacts.description: The de-identification policy and procedures, the documentation of the expert determination or safe harbour method applied, the de-identification verification records, and the re-identification risk assessment.

artifacts.name: Restricted Subject Handling
artifacts.description: The handling policy for high-profile patient data, the access controls applied to it, and the procedures aligned to the regulator's participation criteria governing who may see it.

artifacts.name: Data Access Controls
artifacts.description: The data access control list configuration documentation, the access control review records, the role-based access controls for transaction validation, and the data classification policy determining what each disclosure tier permits.

artifacts.name: Data Retention and Disposal
artifacts.description: The data retention schedule, the data disposal procedures, and the data management process documentation governing what remains available to disclose.

artifacts.name: Correspondent Relationship Records
artifacts.description: The correspondent authorisation documentation, the relationship management change logs, the relationship review records, the data flow diagrams with their encryption points, the encryption configuration documentation, and the certificate inventory protecting those flows.

artifacts.name: Instrument Data Masking
artifacts.description: The receipt template review evidencing account number masking or truncation before the record leaves the organisation.

artifacts.name: Freedom of Information Records
artifacts.description: The documented request process implementation with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures behind it, the request log, the open data publication records, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability for what is released.

artifacts.name: Data Security Control Records
artifacts.description: The documented security controls specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the data lifecycle records covering retention schedules, the data security control evidence including access controls, and the data sharing agreements with their interoperability standards and integration documentation.

artifacts.name: Documented Information Control
artifacts.description: The policy and procedure for control of documented information covering availability, protection, distribution and versioning; the document control procedure; the access control matrix for the controlled documents with the document management system access settings and audit logs; the document distribution records; the version control records; the register identifying and controlling external-origin documents; and the retention and disposition schedule for the controlled set. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented documentation requirement.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Rights Records
artifacts.description: The personal data access, reversal, rectification and deletion records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

DCH-03.1.notes: 52 asks across 9 frameworks. Minimum-necessary disclosure, de-identification and downstream compliance verification are three separate proofs; ISO 22301 and ISO 42001 document-control asks arrive through an adjacent crosswalk and are kept apart from disclosure of data.

artifacts.name: Classification Scheme
artifacts.description: The data classification scheme, the classification policy, the classification scheme with its handling guidelines per level, the classification procedures, the confidentiality-integrity-availability marking scheme, the classification marking guidelines, and the default classification policy for unlabelled assets with the default private marking policy and templates.

artifacts.name: Labelling Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure specifying how to label electronic and physical information per classification, the asset labelling procedure, the labelling procedures, the media labelling standard, the media marking procedures, and the handling guidelines the label invokes. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented mark-media-with-regulated-data-markings requirement. HITRUST requires the approved information labelling and handling and information handling procedures policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Labelling Tool Configuration
artifacts.description: The sensitivity label and auto-labelling rule configuration in the labelling platform, the document label templates covering headers, footers and watermarks, the document templates with classification headers and footers, and the mail classification tooling.

artifacts.name: Label Coverage Evidence
artifacts.description: The report showing the percentage of documents and messages labelled correctly over time, the examples of labelled physical and digital assets, the photographs of physical media with applied classification labels, the media labelling examples, and the sample labelled documents.

artifacts.name: Physical Media Marking Controls
artifacts.description: The tamper-evident storage for the marked media and the disposal procedures closing out the labelled lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy and Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: The policy defining permitted and prohibited uses of technology resources, mail, internet and data; the signed or electronically acknowledged records from employees and contractors; the training module completion report; the acceptable use restrictions on organisational mail; the login banner reminding users of their obligations; and the redacted records of violations detected with the actions taken.

artifacts.name: Classification Metadata Records
artifacts.description: The documented data classification metadata specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the metadata repository or data catalog export, and the register or inventory evidencing the metadata with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Review Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the labelling and handling requirements, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-04.notes: 51 asks across 10 frameworks. The labelling procedure, the tooling that applies labels and the evidence that labels are actually present are three proofs; the coverage report is what an assessor uses and is kept separate from the templates.

artifacts.name: Media Storage Procedure
artifacts.description: The media storage procedures, the procedure defining controls for physically securing all media containing regulated data, the secure storage area documentation, the media handling policy and procedures, and the handling guidelines by classification. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-system-media requirement. HITRUST requires the approved information handling procedures policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Media Storage Location Inventory
artifacts.description: The documented inventory of physical media storage locations with the controls at each covering locked cabinets, safes and secure rooms; the media inventory records; the register of all managed removable media with owner, classification and status; the removable media inventory or register; the media lifecycle records; the media movement tracking logs; and the media tracking logs.

artifacts.name: Storage Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The photographic or inspection evidence of secure storage of media holding regulated data, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the storage security for sensitive instrument information.

artifacts.name: Media Encryption Controls
artifacts.description: The endpoint or data loss prevention configuration enforcing encryption on removable media, the encryption configuration protecting stored media, the removable media policy on approved types, encryption, registration and disposal, and the endpoint policy evidence restricting removable-device use to approved devices only.

artifacts.name: Handling Procedures by Classification
artifacts.description: The documented information handling procedures by classification level, the procedures covering access, processing, storage, communication and printing, the data handling procedures governing handling, transmission and storage, the handling procedure training records, the awareness training materials, and the records verifying handling aligns with legal requirements.

artifacts.name: Clear Desk and Screen Controls
artifacts.description: The clear desk policy, the clear screen policy, and the compliance audit records showing walkthrough results against them.

artifacts.name: Backup Media Security
artifacts.description: The evidence that backup media, storage and facility are secured and protected and the risk assessment of the backup and restore process with the controls it defines.

artifacts.name: Media Transport and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for secure transport of media covering tamper-evident packaging, courier and chain of custody; the records of secure media destruction including certificates from the disposal vendor; the media disposal procedures; the disposal records; and the disposal procedures closing the storage lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Retention and Classification Records
artifacts.description: The storage and retention policy with its documented compliance evidence, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the data lifecycle records covering retention schedules, the data security control evidence including access controls, and the data value realisation records.

DCH-06.notes: 51 asks across 12 frameworks. The storage-location inventory, the physical controls at each location and the handling procedures by classification are three proofs; overlaps DCH-07 and DCH-08 but the object here is media at rest rather than in transit or at disposal.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Data Inventory
artifacts.description: The sensitive data inventory, the inventory of all electronic media holding regulated data with location, custodian and classification, and the data inventory review records evidencing it is maintained.

artifacts.name: Data Flow Diagrams
artifacts.description: The data flow diagrams showing where the sensitive data originates, travels and rests.

artifacts.name: Inventory Reconciliation Records
artifacts.description: The procedure governing maintenance and reconciliation of the media inventory and the records of periodic reconciliation against actual media holdings.

artifacts.name: Data Identification and Register
artifacts.description: The documented data identification and data register specifications with their compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing them, the registers or inventories evidencing each with a named owner, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the formal approval and socialisation records.

artifacts.name: Data Catalog Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy or standard covering the automated cataloguing tool with its documented specification and compliance evidence, the metadata repository or data catalog export, and the register or inventory evidencing the tool with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Data Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The sensitive data transfer controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation, and the segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records.

artifacts.name: Handling and Access Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the handling requirements, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability. HITRUST requires the approved information handling procedures policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

DCH-06.2.notes: 34 asks across 6 frameworks. The inventory itself, the flow diagrams that show where the data moves and the reconciliation confirming the inventory is complete are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Media Transport Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for secure transport of media covering tamper-evident packaging, approved couriers and chain of custody; the procedure for transporting media holding regulated data including secure courier and tracking; the physical media transit procedures; the media transport procedures; the device and media control policy; the hardware and media tracking procedures; and the transport protection mechanisms documentation. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented control-media-during-transport requirement. HITRUST requires the approved physical media in transit policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Courier Arrangements
artifacts.description: The approved courier list, the courier service agreements, the courier handling standard operating procedure for the instruments carried, and the standard data transfer agreement templates with third parties receiving the media.

artifacts.name: Chain of Custody Records
artifacts.description: The chain of custody documentation, the signed receipts for physical media transfers via approved couriers, the sample courier or tracked-delivery records for media sent outside the facility, the delivery proof records, and the media transit tracking records.

artifacts.name: Movement Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The asset removal and movement authorisation procedures, the authorisation approval records, the movement authorisation records, the gate-pass records, and the asset movement register and logs.

artifacts.name: Media Protection in Transit
artifacts.description: The photographic evidence of tamper-evident or secure containers used for transport, the tamper-evident packaging evidence, the media protection in transit through encryption or tamper-evident controls, the backup encryption configuration for media leaving the site, the encryption key custody records, and the endpoint configuration enforcing encryption on removable media.

artifacts.name: Media Inventory Register
artifacts.description: The register of all managed removable media with owner, classification and status; the removable media inventory or register; the media lifecycle records; the media movement tracking logs; the media classification records; and the removable media management procedures maintaining them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented asset classification requirement. HITRUST requires the approved management of removable media policy and standard with its implementing procedure, its awareness communications and its periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Restrictions
artifacts.description: The policy on approved media types, encryption, registration and disposal; the endpoint policy evidence restricting removable-device use to approved devices only; and the media disposal records including certificates from the disposal vendor closing the lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Physical Protection Measures
artifacts.description: The equipment security procedures, the physical protection measures, and the transportation security controls covering equipment as well as media.

artifacts.name: Facility Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records covering the areas media passes through.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the mail encryption configuration; and the managed transfer platform log showing encrypted transfers and recipients — the electronic alternatives to shipping media.

DCH-07.notes: 58 asks across 10 frameworks. The transport procedure, the courier arrangement and the movement log are three sequential proofs; ISO 27001 A.5.14 information transfer covers electronic paths and is kept separate from physical media transport.

artifacts.name: Chain of Custody Records
artifacts.description: The chain of custody documentation, the chain of custody logs for off-site equipment, the signed receipts for physical media transfers via approved couriers, the sample courier or tracked-delivery records for media sent outside the facility, the delivery proof records, the media transit tracking records, and the verification records for off-site assets.

artifacts.name: Media Transport Procedure
artifacts.description: The media transport procedures, the procedure for transporting media holding regulated data including secure courier and tracking, the physical media transit procedures, the transport protection mechanisms documentation, the device and media control policy, and the hardware and media tracking procedures. HITRUST requires the approved physical media in transit policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Courier Arrangements
artifacts.description: The approved courier list, the courier service agreements, the courier handling standard operating procedure for the instruments carried, and the standard data transfer agreement templates with third parties receiving the media.

artifacts.name: Off-Site Equipment Custody
artifacts.description: The off-site equipment procedures, the off-site protection measures documentation, and the movement authorisation records governing who may take equipment off the premises and who holds it while it is gone.

artifacts.name: Media Protection in Transit
artifacts.description: The photographic evidence of tamper-evident or secure containers used for transport, the tamper-evident packaging evidence, the media protection in transit through encryption or tamper-evident controls, and the media classification records determining the protection required. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented asset classification requirement.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the mail encryption configuration; and the managed transfer platform log showing encrypted transfers and recipients — the electronic paths that avoid a custodian entirely.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Records
artifacts.description: The policy defining permitted and prohibited uses of technology resources, the signed or electronically acknowledged records from employees and contractors, the training module completion report, the login banner reminding users of their obligations, and the redacted records of violations detected with the actions taken.

artifacts.name: Facility Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records covering the custody points.

DCH-07.1.notes: 41 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps DCH-07; what is distinct here is the named custodian who holds the media at each hop, so the custody log and off-site verification are the primary artifacts.

artifacts.name: Media Sanitisation and Disposal Policy
artifacts.description: The media sanitisation and disposal policy, the media handling policy and procedures, the media sanitisation procedures with the recognised sanitisation-standard compliance documentation, the media destruction and disposal standard operating procedure, the media disposal procedures, the data disposal procedures, the media sanitisation documentation, the discreet disposal procedure, and the hardware decommissioning procedures. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented off-site transfer authorisation requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the sanitise-or-destroy-before-disposal requirement. HITRUST requires the approved disposal of media policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Destruction Certificates and Records
artifacts.description: The sample destruction certificates from internal destruction or a third-party vendor, the destruction certificates from authorised vendors, the media destruction logs, the media disposal records including vendor certificates, the shredding and wiping evidence, the witness records for destruction, the sanitisation records and certificates, the disposal certificates and records, the disposal records, the asset disposal and destruction records, and the data wiping and destruction verification evidence.

artifacts.name: Hard-Copy Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for destroying hard-copy materials by cross-cut shredding, incineration or pulping such that the data cannot be reconstructed, and the evidence of storage in secure containers prior to destruction.

artifacts.name: Media Inventory Register
artifacts.description: The register of all managed removable media with owner, classification and status, the removable media inventory or register, the media lifecycle records, the media movement tracking logs, the media tracking logs, and the removable media management procedures maintaining them.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Controls
artifacts.description: The policy on approved media types, encryption, registration and disposal; the endpoint policy evidence restricting removable-device use to approved devices only; the data loss prevention or endpoint configuration enforcing encryption on removable media; and the encryption configuration protecting media that leaves the site.

artifacts.name: Media Transport Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for secure transport of media covering tamper-evident packaging, approved couriers and chain of custody.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Disposal Contracts
artifacts.description: The third-party disposal contracts specifying the required destruction procedures, the standards the vendor must meet and the evidence they must return.

artifacts.name: Retention and Deletion Schedule
artifacts.description: The retention and deletion schedule defining periods by data category with deletion triggers, the data retention schedule, the data classification policy driving the categories, the data management process documentation, and the data lifecycle records covering the schedule. NDMO requires the retention and disposal specification with its documented compliance evidence and implementing procedures and workflows.

artifacts.name: In-System Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The information deletion policy defining when and how information must be deleted, the procedures for secure deletion across databases, file systems, cloud and backup, the log of deletions executed per the retention schedule with verification, the records showing expired backups purged, the log of privacy erasure requests fulfilled and verified, and the provider attestations confirming deletion on termination.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the media disposal requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-08.notes: 61 asks across 13 frameworks. Distinct from DCH-21 in that the object here is physical media rather than data in systems; the media register and transport controls sit with disposal because they are the chain of custody an assessor follows to the destruction certificate.

artifacts.name: Media Sanitisation and Disposal Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure governing sanitisation, disposal and secure re-use of media, covering both electronic and paper. HITRUST requires separate approved standards for disposal of media and for secure disposal or re-use; NIST 800-53 requires alignment to the recognised sanitisation standard; NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented procedure.

artifacts.name: Destruction Certificates and Records
artifacts.description: The certificates of destruction from internal destruction or a third-party vendor with chain of custody, the disposal and sanitisation records, and the physical destruction certificates for media that could not be wiped.

artifacts.name: Sanitisation Tool Configuration and Logs
artifacts.description: The configuration and execution logs of the secure wiping tooling, the degausser usage logs, and the tool effectiveness tests demonstrating the method achieves non-recoverability for the media type it is applied to.

artifacts.name: Sanitisation Verification Records
artifacts.description: The pre-disposal verification records, the data sanitisation checklists, the verification of non-recoverability, and the disposal verification confirming the sanitisation actually completed before the asset left custody.

artifacts.name: Retention and Deletion Schedule
artifacts.description: The schedule defining retention periods by data category with the deletion triggers, the information deletion policy defining when and how information must be removed, the data retention schedule, and the data lifecycle records covering it.

artifacts.name: Logical Data Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The procedures for secure deletion across different system types — database, file store, cloud, backup — the log of deletions executed against the retention schedule with verification, the backup deletion records showing expired backups purged, and the log of privacy erasure requests fulfilled and verified.

artifacts.name: Cloud Provider Deletion Attestations
artifacts.description: Attestations from cloud providers confirming data deletion on termination, and the off-site transfer authorisation policy and procedures with the records demonstrating they operate in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Equipment Sanitisation Before Maintenance or Release
artifacts.description: The procedure requiring removal or secure handling of classified media before equipment leaves for external repair, the records of media removal or sanitisation prior to dispatch, the data protection procedures during off-site movement, and the documented procedure or configuration evidence for sanitising equipment for off-site maintenance.

artifacts.name: Media Handling and Tracking Records
artifacts.description: The media handling policy and guidelines, the media tracking logs recording custody, and the handling guidelines by classification level.

artifacts.name: Information Asset Inventory and Classification
artifacts.description: The comprehensive inventory of information assets with owner, classification and retention schedule, the classification policy defining levels with handling guidelines, the data owner register, and the data classification and management process documentation.

artifacts.name: Hardware Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The hardware decommissioning procedures, the secure disposal and re-use procedures, the software licence deactivation records, and the asset disposal records tying each retired asset to its destruction certificate.

artifacts.name: Faulty Media Handling Records
artifacts.description: The sanitisation records for faulty media that cannot be wiped through normal means, and the re-use authorisation documentation where media is returned to service rather than destroyed.

artifacts.name: Data Retention Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented retention and disposal specification with its implementing procedures and process workflows, the approved standard covering it, and the compliance evidence for the specification.

artifacts.name: Physical Access and Surveillance over Disposal Areas
artifacts.description: The physical access logs and visitor register for areas where media awaiting destruction is held, the surveillance deployment with footage retention, and the data loss prevention deployment covering the same estate.

artifacts.name: Log Retention Records
artifacts.description: The documented log records requirement with the evidence demonstrating retention is implemented in the environment covered, held here because log media falls under the same retention and disposal regime.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the disposal requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-09.notes: 87 asks across 18 frameworks. Physical media destruction and logical data deletion are separated: they use different tooling, produce different evidence and are tested by different requirements (PCI DSS 9.4.7 destruction versus ISO 27001 A.8.10 deletion).

artifacts.name: Disposal Register
artifacts.description: The disposal register or database, the disposal record template with its required fields, the completed disposal records, the sanitisation records and certificates, and the media handling records supporting them. HITRUST requires the approved disposal of media and secure disposal or re-use policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Sanitisation Procedures
artifacts.description: The media sanitisation procedures, the media sanitisation procedure, the media destruction and disposal standard operating procedure, the procedure for destruction of electronic media via degaussing, secure wiping or physical destruction, the procedures for secure deletion across databases, file systems, cloud and backup, the information deletion policy, and the compliance documentation against the recognised sanitisation standard.

artifacts.name: Destruction Certificates
artifacts.description: The sample destruction certificates from internal destruction or a third-party vendor with chain of custody, the destruction certificates, the disposal verification, and the supervision records for destruction events.

artifacts.name: Sanitisation Tool Records
artifacts.description: The configuration and execution logs of the secure wiping tooling and the sanitisation tool effectiveness tests confirming the method achieves what it claims.

artifacts.name: Pre-Disposal Retention Check
artifacts.description: The retention verification checklist completed prior to disposal, the legal hold check records, and the data retention policy compliance evidence confirming nothing under obligation was destroyed.

artifacts.name: Disposal Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The disposal authorisation workflow, the management-approved disposal requests, and the disposal approval audit trail.

artifacts.name: In-System Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The log of deletions executed per the retention schedule with verification, the records showing expired backups purged from media, the log of privacy erasure requests fulfilled and verified, the provider attestations confirming deletion on termination, and the retention and deletion schedule defining periods by data category.

artifacts.name: Facility and Leakage Controls
artifacts.description: The data loss prevention deployment, the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer covering the areas where disposal occurs.

DCH-09.1.notes: 43 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps DCH-08; what is distinct here is the documentation of sanitisation — the register, the record template and the retention check before disposal — rather than the sanitisation itself.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Policy
artifacts.description: The policy on approved media types, encryption, registration and disposal; the portable media protection policy; the removable media policy with its encryption controls; the removable media restriction policy with its data loss prevention and encryption configuration; the removable media management procedures; and the media handling policy and procedures. HITRUST requires the approved management of removable media policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Media Use Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The removable media authorisation records, the user request and approval workflows, the management risk acceptance records for the exceptions granted, and the access justification behind each approval.

artifacts.name: Port and Device Restriction Configuration
artifacts.description: The endpoint policy evidence restricting removable-device use to approved devices only, the removable media whitelisting configuration, the port disable policy, the removable media control configuration evidence, the policy and configuration governing secure use of external and removable media, and the isolated media-access environment where media must be read before it reaches the estate.

artifacts.name: Media Encryption Controls
artifacts.description: The endpoint or data loss prevention configuration enforcing encryption on removable media, the content encryption evidence on the media in use, the encryption configuration, and the transport-layer encryption configurations protecting data moved by other means.

artifacts.name: Media Scanning Configuration
artifacts.description: The removable media scan policy, the removable media scanning configuration, the auto-run disable configuration and evidence, the real-time protection configuration, and the scheduled scan reports covering inserted media.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Protection Coverage
artifacts.description: The anti-malware deployment inventory, the deployment and update records, the signature update logs, the alert configuration, the endpoint protection tool reports, the coverage report showing no unprotected endpoints, and the endpoint patch compliance report.

artifacts.name: Media Inventory and Movement Records
artifacts.description: The register of all managed removable media with owner, classification and status; the removable media inventory or register; the media lifecycle records; the media movement tracking logs; the procedure for secure transport of media; and the media disposal records with certificates from the disposal vendor.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Records
artifacts.description: The data loss prevention tool configuration with its reports, the endpoint deployment of that tooling, and the device management policy and configuration governing what may be copied off the estate.

artifacts.name: Physical Media Access Controls
artifacts.description: The biometric access provisioning configuration protecting the location where removable media is held and the session timeout policy and configuration on the systems that read it.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The malware awareness training records covering removable media, the awareness communications informing personnel of the media restrictions, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-12.notes: 50 asks across 8 frameworks. The authorisation to use removable media, the technical restriction of what may connect, and the scanning of what does are three proofs; anti-malware arrives here because removable media is its principal vector and is kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals, with the information exchange procedures and the technical standards for packaging and transmission. HITRUST requires the approved exchange policy and its implementing procedure as separate artifacts; ADHICS requires the sanctions and deviation handling procedure alongside them.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing Agreements
artifacts.description: The executed information exchange and data sharing agreements with their security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit provisions, the standard transfer agreement templates, the non-disclosure and confidentiality agreement library, and the third-party risk assessment and monitoring records behind them.

artifacts.name: Secure Transfer Configuration
artifacts.description: The procedures for each specific transfer method — secure file transfer, secure email, encrypted removable media, managed file transfer — with the email encryption configuration enforcing protected external mail, the managed transfer platform log showing encrypted transfers and recipients, the transport encryption configuration, the certificate inventory, and the courier chain-of-custody receipts for physical media.

artifacts.name: Sharing Platform Security Records
artifacts.description: The inventory of information sharing platforms, the access control documentation for each, the secure connectivity configuration, the documented security requirements per platform, and the application integration security documentation.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing Request Process
artifacts.description: The documented data sharing process and request submission channel with their implementing procedures and process workflows, the internal and external sharing agreements with their compliance evidence, the register with a named owner, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Need-to-Know Access Controls
artifacts.description: The access control list configuration over shared data, the documented need-to-know justification for each grant, and the access control review records confirming the justification still holds.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Configuration
artifacts.description: The data loss prevention tool configuration and reports, the removable media policy with its encryption controls, the mobile device management policy and configuration, and the sensitive data protection records demonstrating the controls operate in the environment.

artifacts.name: Data Classification and Interpretation Records
artifacts.description: The data classification scheme with the labelled dataset register, the inter-entity classification interpretation procedure for data received under another organisation's scheme, the third-party classification mapping document, and the records of controls applied to third-party classified information.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Population Handling Records
artifacts.description: The handling policy for data on protected or high-profile individuals, the sharing procedure aligned with the sector directions, the access control configuration records enforcing it, and the compliance evidence against the participation criteria.

artifacts.name: Data Submission and Reconciliation Records
artifacts.description: The submission logs to the receiving platform, the completeness and accuracy verification reports, and the reconciliation records between the source system and the platform confirming what was shared arrived intact.

artifacts.name: Correspondent Relationship Records
artifacts.description: The correspondent authorisation documentation, the relationship management change logs, the periodic review records over the authorised set, and the data flow diagrams with their encryption points.

artifacts.name: Exchange Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The data-exchange risk assessments performed before a sharing arrangement is entered, and the incident response procedure for information exchange failures.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the information sharing requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-14.notes: 79 asks across 10 frameworks. Sharing agreements (the legal instrument), transfer mechanisms (the technical control) and the sharing request process (the operational workflow) are kept apart because an assessor asks for each separately.

artifacts.name: Public Content Publication Procedure
artifacts.description: The public information publishing procedure with the publication and approval workflow, the content review and approval records, the public content authorisation procedure, and the role-based access controls governing who may publish. HITRUST requires the approved standard for publicly available information with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Published Content Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic content audit results, the public domain validation records, the website content review records, the content sanitisation records, and the public website monitoring logs confirming nothing regulated has been exposed.

artifacts.name: Public Information Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of information deliberately placed in the public domain, the register of official social media accounts with defined ownership, and the default private marking policy and templates that make publication an explicit decision.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data Exclusion from Public Systems
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence controlling regulated data on publicly accessible systems, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating, and the public system integrity monitoring detecting unauthorised content.

artifacts.name: Storage Tier Isolation Evidence
artifacts.description: The network security control configuration showing components that store regulated data have no direct path from untrusted networks, the topology documentation showing the storage tier behind the perimeter and application tiers, and the reachability test results confirming those components are unreachable from outside.

artifacts.name: Open Data Plan and Processes
artifacts.description: The documented open data plan, identification, processes, publishing and metadata specifications with their compliance evidence, implementation records and implementing procedures and workflows; the approved data management and personal data protection strategy behind them; and the performance metrics dashboard.

artifacts.name: Open Data Publication Records
artifacts.description: The publication records for each open dataset, the metadata repository or catalog export accompanying them, the data lifecycle records covering retention, the data quality profiling reports, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Freedom of Information Process Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy or standard covering the request process design with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures, the data architecture artifacts supporting it, the request log, and the public entity publication evidence.

artifacts.name: Public Data Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The data security control evidence including access controls applied to published data, the privacy artifacts, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability for what is published.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping for the publishing systems, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the publication requirements.

DCH-15.notes: 67 asks across 8 frameworks. Two different things sit here: preventing regulated data reaching public systems (NIST 800-171, PCI DSS) and deliberately publishing open data well (NDMO). They are kept apart because one is a prohibition and the other an obligation.

artifacts.name: Data Retention & Disposal Policy
artifacts.description: The single approved policy governing how long media and data are kept and how they are destroyed, covering statutory, regulatory and contractual drivers, retention periods tied to data classes, disposal methods, and the scope of media covered including backups, archives and BYOD-held data. Must be current, carry management or board approval, and state scope, roles and responsibilities, control objectives and review frequency. Different frameworks anchor it differently — records management and information deletion policies under ISO 27001, account data retention and disposal under PCI DSS, archival and retention plus asset management under ADHICS, protection of organisational records and retention/disposal under HITRUST, storage and retention under NDMO, backup and archiving under QCB, and audit working paper retention under SBP ETGRMF — but it is one governing document set.

artifacts.name: Policy Approval, Version Control & Communication Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the retention policy is live and maintained: management, board or audit committee approval records, version history and periodic review records naming reviewer, date, observations and corrective actions, evidence the policy was communicated to staff, and the awareness communications confirming personnel were informed of the records retention requirement.

artifacts.name: Records Retention Schedule
artifacts.description: The schedule listing every record and data type with its retention period, the legal or business justification for that period, the disposal method and the trigger for deletion. Must cover the regulated data types in scope — PCI DSS requires justification per data element, HITRUST requires the protection mechanisms alongside the schedule, QCB requires a 15-year retention for financial records, NDMO requires the data lifecycle records covering retention, archival and secure disposal, and ISO 27001 requires the legal basis recorded against each record class.

artifacts.name: Retention Automation & Storage Lifecycle Configuration
artifacts.description: The live configuration that enforces the schedule without human intervention: storage lifecycle and tiering rules, retention labels and policies in the content or email platform, automated retention controls, and the storage access control and integrity-monitoring settings protecting retained data (including checksums or equivalent integrity verification of stored records).

artifacts.name: Log Retention Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that audit and event logs meet their own retention requirement: the log retention policy and storage configuration, an audit or report showing the age of the oldest retained logs meets the required period, and a test record demonstrating archived logs can be restored. PCI DSS requires at least 12 months of history with the most recent three months immediately available and the ability to restore months four to twelve within a reasonable time.

artifacts.name: Retention & Secure Disposal Procedures
artifacts.description: The working procedures beneath the policy: how data is deleted from each system type (database, file store, cloud, backup media), how hard-copy material is destroyed (cross-cut shredding, incineration or pulping so it cannot be reconstructed), how electronic media is destroyed (degaussing, secure wipe or physical destruction), the asset disposal triggers and criteria that start the process, and the workflow tying classification, retention and disposal together.

artifacts.name: Destruction & Deletion Records
artifacts.description: Proof that disposal actually happened at the end of the retention period: destruction certificates from internal or third-party destruction, secure wiping tool configuration and execution logs, records destruction logs naming method and witness, deletion records with verification, evidence that expired backups were purged from media, provider attestations confirming deletion on service termination, and the log of privacy erasure requests fulfilled and verified.

artifacts.name: Disposal Approval & Legal Hold Verification Records
artifacts.description: The controls applied before anything is destroyed: the disposal request and its approval, the retention verification checklist completed and signed prior to disposal with each control point ticked, the legal hold check confirming no hold applies, the regulatory or legal references relied on for the disposal decision, and evidence that material awaiting destruction was held in secure containers.

artifacts.name: Data Discovery & Retention Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: Periodic verification that persistent storage locations hold only what they should: data discovery scan results confirming regulated data resides only in approved locations and that data past its retention period has been removed, retention compliance audit results, verification records demonstrating the retention requirement is met, and the records showing retention and deletion controls are operating in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Data Classification Scheme & Dataset Register
artifacts.description: The classification scheme and the labelled inventory it is applied to — asset and dataset register with owner, classification, status and last review date — plus the data management process and metadata management documentation that keep the classification current. Retention periods are assigned by class, so this is the register the schedule is applied against.

artifacts.name: Records Protection & Archive Access Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that retained records stay intact and accessible for the whole retention period: storage, encryption and access controls documented for protected records, access logs to archived material for audit traceability, preservation evidence covering the archival period, the repository holding retained working papers and reports with their retention metadata, media classification and access controls, and the records showing reports were distributed and then retained per policy.

artifacts.name: Legal, Regulatory & Contractual Retention Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The register of retention obligations the schedule must satisfy: per-system legal requirements, compliance evidence for intellectual property, records, data protection and cryptography obligations, privacy law alignment for the retention periods chosen, executed third-party agreements carrying retention and protection clauses, the documented compliance position against the applicable national data management specification, and the legal risk reporting to senior management or the board.

artifacts.name: Data Governance & Value Records
artifacts.description: Supporting governance artefacts requested alongside retention: data quality management reports and metrics, the data products catalogue and value or monetisation model, and the evidence of personal data protection controls applied to retained data.

artifacts.name: Penetration Test Methodology & Tester Qualification Records
artifacts.description: Retained testing documentation mapped into this control by PCI DSS: the penetration testing methodology, the records of its periodic review and update, and the qualification and organisational independence documentation for the testers. Collect once for VPM-07 and reference here as records held under the retention schedule.

DCH-18.notes: 101 framework evidence asks collapse to 14 artifacts. No automated collectors are attached; lifecycle/retention configuration is marked automated because a storage or DMS connector could produce it directly, and discovery scan results are hybrid. The PCI DSS 11.4.1 penetration testing entries mapped into this control are retained as a separate item so nothing is dropped — they relate to test records held under the retention regime.

artifacts.name: Data Masking Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The policy prohibiting use of non-desensitised production data in testing, the procedure defining masking, tokenisation and hashing techniques with the approval workflow for moving production data, the standard operating procedure for masking when external parties are involved, the data masking procedures, and the test data management policy. HITRUST requires the approved protection of system test data policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Masking Execution Records
artifacts.description: The execution logs from the masking tool showing masked datasets provisioned to lower environments, the sample masking tool output evidencing desensitisation, the records of data desensitisation before use in testing, the evidence of masking validation before external testing, the anonymisation evidence for personal data, and the sample test data sets produced.

artifacts.name: Production Data Use Approvals
artifacts.description: The production data usage authorisation records and the information owner approvals recorded when desensitised production data is used in testing.

artifacts.name: Test Data Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The test data lifecycle records, the post-test data erasure confirmation, the test data access controls, and the data protection records covering the test estate.

artifacts.name: Provider Data Use Prohibition
artifacts.description: The executed service level clause explicitly prohibiting the provider from using the organisation's data for commercial purposes, analytics or model training; the configuration evidence showing opt-out of provider telemetry, analytics and model-training features; and the executed clause prohibiting disclosure to foreign governments, courts or law enforcement without prior written consent.

artifacts.name: Cloud Data Security Controls
artifacts.description: The board-approved data security policy for cloud workloads covering encryption, desensitisation, segregation and personal data handling; the cryptographic standard specifying approved algorithms and protocols; the configuration export showing encryption at rest enabled for storage and databases; the transport security scan reports for cloud-exposed endpoints; the tenant isolation architecture describing logical and physical segregation; the resource tagging standard with its compliance report; and the legal memorandum confirming the contract and operational arrangements comply with applicable law.

artifacts.name: Personal Data Flow and Impact Assessment
artifacts.description: The data protection impact assessment and the personal data flow diagrams identifying data elements, residency and legal basis.

artifacts.name: Testing Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented testing programme covering internal and external stakeholder participation and its data-masking requirements, the log showing participation of business line management, incident response and crisis teams, and the reports from programme exercises with results and improvement actions.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The data retention policy, the record retention schedule, the data disposal procedures, and the retention compliance verification records.

artifacts.name: Secure Design Records
artifacts.description: The secure design principles documentation, the security architecture documentation, and the security engineering review records governing how test environments are built.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the test data restrictions and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

DCH-18.2.notes: 42 asks across 6 frameworks. Overlaps TDA-10; what is distinct here is the extension to training and research, and SBP Cloud 12.1's prohibition on the provider using the organisation's data to train its own models, which is kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Schedule
artifacts.description: The retention and deletion schedule defining periods by data category with deletion triggers, the data retention and disposal schedule, the record retention schedule, the retention schedule by data type, the data lifecycle records covering it, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register that gives it categories, and the retention compliance verification records. NDMO requires the storage and retention policy and the retention and disposal specification with their documented compliance evidence and implementing procedures and workflows.

artifacts.name: Disposal Policy and Procedures
artifacts.description: The information deletion policy defining when and how information must be deleted, the data disposal procedures, the media sanitisation and disposal policy, the procedure for secure permanent disposal of data no longer required, the secure data destruction procedures, the deletion procedures across databases, file systems, cloud and backup, the discreet disposal procedure, and the hardware decommissioning procedures. ADHICS additionally requires the disposal triggers and criteria with the regulatory and legal disposal references behind them.

artifacts.name: Disposal Certificates and Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The destruction certificates from authorised vendors with the certificate templates, the media destruction logs, the shredding and wiping evidence, the witness records for destruction, the asset disposal and destruction records, the disposal verification and audit trail, the data wiping and destruction verification evidence, the media sanitisation records and documentation, and the disposal request and approval records preceding them.

artifacts.name: In-System Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The log of deletions executed per the retention schedule with their verification, the records showing expired backups purged from media, the log of privacy erasure requests fulfilled and verified, and the electronic data destruction tool configurations performing them.

artifacts.name: Physical Document Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The physical document shredding procedures and records, and the secure disposal procedures for personal information held on paper.

artifacts.name: Archival and Preservation Records
artifacts.description: The data archival and retention policy, the archival and destruction records, and the preservation evidence covering the archival period before disposal falls due.

artifacts.name: Cloud Exit Data Destruction
artifacts.description: The service level agreement clause requiring complete removal of data including logs from all provider storage locations on exit, the procedure for executing and verifying destruction across primary, replicas, backups, logs and archives, the verification records from past exits or test declarations, the sample written deletion confirmation from the provider covering sub-contractor locations, and the provider attestations confirming deletion on termination.

artifacts.name: Supplier Off-Boarding Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for secure off-boarding covering data return or destruction, access revocation and exit audit; the records evidencing completed off-boarding steps for exited suppliers; and the data destruction clauses in the contracts that make them enforceable.

artifacts.name: Data Inventory and Ownership
artifacts.description: The data inventory by process with the process owner classification responsibilities, the data security control evidence including access controls over the data awaiting disposal, and the data value realisation records.

DCH-21.notes: 63 asks across 10 frameworks. Disposal of media, disposal of data within live systems, and disposal at the end of a provider relationship are three different proofs; SBP Cloud's exit deletion and PISF's supplier off-boarding are kept out of the general media artifact for that reason.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved data quality policy with its management procedure and accountability statement naming who owns quality for each domain. DoH ADHIE requires an approved policy with a documented accountability statement; NDMO requires the quality prioritisation, rules development and monitoring specifications to be evidenced as documented artifacts.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Rules and Controls
artifacts.description: The documented quality rules with the controls maintaining accuracy, completeness and consistency across the data lifecycle, the standardised data entry field definitions, and the real-time validation and feedback loop configuration enforcing them at point of capture.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Profiling Reports
artifacts.description: The profiling reports measuring quality against the defined rules, the completeness and accuracy verification reports, the validation and reconciliation evidence, and the trend analysis showing whether quality is improving. NDMO requires trends to be evidenced as their own specification with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Data Quality KPI Dashboard
artifacts.description: The performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records, the data catalog KPIs, and the business intelligence dashboards and reports through which quality is monitored.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Issue Resolution Records
artifacts.description: The documented issue resolution specification, the erroneous information correction logs, the notification records to the receiving party when corrections are made, the patient or customer feedback intake records, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Service Level Agreements
artifacts.description: The documented quality service level agreements defining the standard each data product must meet, with the compliance evidence and the audit reports assessing adherence.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Tooling Records
artifacts.description: The documented quality tooling specification with its implementation evidence, the metadata repository or catalog export, and the register or inventory evidencing each with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Master and Reference Data Register
artifacts.description: The master and reference data register with golden-record definitions and stewardship records, establishing the authoritative source each quality rule is measured against.

artifacts.name: Data Governance Framework
artifacts.description: The data governance framework and policies, the data classification and metadata management documentation, the approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the retention policies with backup and recovery procedures.

artifacts.name: Quality Management System Records
artifacts.description: The quality management system documentation and policies, the quality standards and procedures for IT processes, the quality monitoring reports with defect tracking, and the continuous improvement plans with corrective action reports.

artifacts.name: Knowledge Management Records
artifacts.description: The knowledge management strategy and policies, the knowledge repository with maintained documentation, and the knowledge sharing activity records and training materials that keep data definitions consistent across teams.

artifacts.name: AI Data Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented data management processes for AI addressing privacy and security implications and the threats arising from the data itself, with the evidence of operational implementation such as pipelines, validation jobs and access controls.

artifacts.name: AI Data Provenance Records
artifacts.description: The documented process for recording provenance covering creation, update, transcription, abstraction and validation, with the provenance records — lineage logs and transformation history — for the data used in AI systems.

artifacts.name: AI Data Acquisition and Selection Records
artifacts.description: The register documenting categories of data needed, quantity and sources whether internal, purchased, shared, open or synthetic; the documented rationale for data selection including suitability for the intended task; and the contracts and licences for purchased or shared data including personal information and copyright terms.

artifacts.name: AI Data Quality and Preparation Records
artifacts.description: The documented data quality requirements for training, validation, test and production data, the reports measuring quality and bias against those requirements with the adjustments made to model or data, the documented criteria and methods for preparation covering exploration, cleaning, imputation and normalisation, and the logs of preparation steps applied to each dataset.

artifacts.name: Data Entry Quality Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The data entry quality assurance reports, the records audit findings, the staff training records on accurate recording, the submission logs to the receiving platform, and the reconciliation records between the source system and that platform.

artifacts.name: Data Migration Records
artifacts.description: The migration policy and methodology document governing how data quality is preserved when data moves between systems.

artifacts.name: Information Classification and Flow Documentation
artifacts.description: The information classification policy, the information flow diagrams for critical processes, and the system-generated reports demonstrating data integrity across those flows.

DCH-22.notes: 90 asks across 7 frameworks but dominated by NDMO, which states the same quality artifact once per specification across nine data-quality requirements. Those are merged. ISO 42001's data provenance and preparation demands are kept separate because they concern data used to train AI, not operational data quality.

artifacts.name: Transfer Legal Basis and Purpose Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping every transfer or disclosure outside the jurisdiction to a permitted purpose, the documented legal basis assessment per transfer, the memo justifying that a transfer is necessary for central processing operations, the extract from the processing records evidencing purpose, recipient, destination and data category, and the transfer documentation and records.

artifacts.name: Transfer Mechanism Evidence
artifacts.description: The mechanism relied on for each transfer: adequacy decision verification with the destination country identified, standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules, the certificate of accreditation, or the documented derogation justification with explicit consent records and necessity assessment. GDPR requires the third-country assessment behind whichever mechanism is used.

artifacts.name: Safeguards Implementation Register
artifacts.description: The documented selection of the appropriate safeguard per exempt transfer, the register mapping each transfer to its safeguard with status and validity dates, the monitoring log tracking continued implementation and operating effectiveness, and the periodic review records confirming the safeguards remain adequate.

artifacts.name: Transfer Condition Exemption Records
artifacts.description: The assessment confirming a transfer qualifies for exemption from the standing conditions, the register recording each exempt transfer with the condition exempted, the applicable case and the safeguard applied, and the evidence that appropriate safeguards remain in place notwithstanding the exemption.

artifacts.name: Inter-Governmental Transfer Authorisation
artifacts.description: The executed agreement or memorandum of understanding implementing the state-level agreement with its data protection provisions, the mapping confirming the required standard provisions are present, and the authorisation record confirming a public-body-to-public-body transfer implements that agreement.

artifacts.name: Limited Transfer Justification
artifacts.description: The documentation evidencing a transfer is non-recurring or for a limited period and involves a limited number of data subjects, the recipient's approval certificate where that route is relied on, and the record confirming the data is not sensitive.

artifacts.name: Onward Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The contractual provisions extending compliance obligations to any subsequent transfer by the recipient, the recipient attestation confirming onward transfers will comply, and the register tracking onward transfers with their destinations.

artifacts.name: Transfer Halt Procedure and Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure to promptly halt a transfer when an exemption is revoked or safeguards are found inadequate, the procedure for handling a competent authority determination to that effect, the log recording each halted transfer with its triggering condition and halt date, and the records of notifications sent to the entities that received the data.

artifacts.name: Pre-Transfer Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The register logging when a transfer risk assessment is required, the inventory identifying continuous or wide-scale transfers of sensitive data, the completed assessments evidenced as performed before the transfer took place, and the transfer impact assessments.

artifacts.name: Transmission Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The external transmission encryption evidence, the secure file transfer logs, the third-party connectivity agreements, and the anomaly detection rules, payment limit configuration, dual authorisation evidence and transaction verification procedures protecting the transfer channel.

artifacts.name: Data Residency and Use Restriction Controls
artifacts.description: The cloud usage restriction policy, the data residency evidence and enforcement records, the cloud-storage prohibition controls, the data-loss prevention rules preventing ingestion into unauthorised systems, the procedures restricting use to permitted purposes, the acceptable use policy referencing the exchange, the logs of permitted and non-permitted access flags, the system integration review for cloud connections, and the sharing authorisations from the sector regulator.

artifacts.name: Data Handling and Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The procedures governing handling, transmission and storage of data by classification, and the records verifying that handling aligns with legal requirements.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Controls
artifacts.description: The documented secure area policy and procedures with the records demonstrating they operate in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing Process Records
artifacts.description: The documented data sharing process with its implementing procedures and process workflows, the data classification scheme with the labelled dataset register, the data architecture artifacts, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the compliance audit reports.

DCH-25.notes: 70 asks across 8 frameworks. KSA PDP contributes a complete cross-border regime — legal basis, safeguards, exemptions, onward transfer, and a halt procedure — that is far more granular than GDPR's transfer mechanisms, so each of those instruments is kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Security Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering configuration, encryption, malware protection and remote wipe for endpoints; the endpoint devices policy and procedures; the acceptable use guidelines; and the workstation use policy with its placement and screen privacy requirements. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented endpoint devices policy and endpoint management requirements.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Inventory and Enrolment
artifacts.description: The inventory of endpoint devices in scope of protection, the report from the device management platform showing enrolled devices against workforce count, the inventory of devices with their compliance status against the security standard, and the evidence that endpoint controls are implemented across each device class.
