artifacts.name: Endpoint Hardening and Encryption
artifacts.description: The hardening baseline applied to the managed operating systems, the disk encryption coverage report for all managed endpoints, the mobile device compliance policies covering passcode, jailbreak detection and application restrictions, and the device management configuration export showing the enforced settings.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The detection and response platform coverage and policy screenshots, the anti-malware deployment evidence, the definition update logs, the scan reports, the malware incident records, the malware protection deployment and update records, and the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented malware protection policy requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the protect-against-malicious-code requirement.

artifacts.name: Remote Wipe Records
artifacts.description: The log of remote wipe actions performed on lost or stolen devices, evidencing the management platform can reach an endpoint that has left the estate.

artifacts.name: Multi-Connected Device Standard
artifacts.description: The approved standard defining specific configuration settings for devices that connect to both trusted and untrusted networks and the evidence preventing devices from being actively connected to an untrusted network while concurrently connected to the protected one.

artifacts.name: Authentication Controls
artifacts.description: The policy specifying authentication strengths per risk tier and use case, the evidence of secure protocols in use with deprecated ones disabled, the export of conditional and step-up access policies, the multi-factor enforcement coverage report across applications and user groups, the passwordless and biometric rollout metrics, the failed authentication anomaly monitoring, and the periodic review of authentication strength against the threat landscape.

artifacts.name: Clear Desk and Screen Controls
artifacts.description: The clear desk and clear screen policy with its requirements, timing rules and enforcement mechanisms; the configuration enforcing auto-lock and screen timeout; the evidence that all staff have access to lockable drawers and cabinets; the map showing confidential waste bin locations; the posters, signage and training content on the rules; and the results of periodic walkthrough audits showing compliance rate and findings.

artifacts.name: Media Access Controls
artifacts.description: The authorised media access list, the media access control procedures, and the media storage access logs governing what an endpoint may read from or write to.

artifacts.name: Network Service Access Controls
artifacts.description: The approved policy on the use of network services with its annual review records, the network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones, the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the access control lists with the user access review documentation.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Procedures
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configurations covering the endpoint estate.

END-01.notes: 55 asks across 10 frameworks. ISO 27001 A.8.5 authentication and A.7.7 clear desk arrive here through adjacent crosswalks and are kept as their own artifacts; the endpoint management artifacts stay grouped by what the management platform actually enforces.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Security Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering configuration, encryption, malware protection and remote wipe for endpoints, the workstation security standards, the physical security measures for workstations, and the workstation inventory with its security controls.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Inventory and Enrolment
artifacts.description: The inventory of endpoint devices in scope of protection, the report from the device management platform showing enrolled devices against workforce count, the inventory of devices with their compliance status against the security standard, and the evidence that endpoint controls are implemented across each device class.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Hardening Baseline
artifacts.description: The hardening baseline applied to the managed operating systems, the group policy settings documentation, the configuration compliance verification, the mobile device compliance policies covering passcode, jailbreak detection and application restrictions, and the device management configuration export showing the enforced settings.

artifacts.name: Encryption at Rest
artifacts.description: The disk encryption coverage report for all managed endpoints, the endpoint encryption deployment records, the encryption coverage assessment reports, the data-at-rest encryption configuration, the full disk encryption documentation, the database encryption records, and the key management for data at rest. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-regulated-data-at-rest requirement.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The detection and response platform coverage and policy screenshots, the malware protection deployment and update records, and the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports from the endpoint estate.

artifacts.name: Exploit Mitigation Configuration
artifacts.description: The anti-exploitation feature configuration, the exploit protection settings, and the feature compliance reports confirming they are enabled across the estate.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Controls
artifacts.description: The authorised storage media policy, the removable media control configurations, the auto-run and auto-play disabled configuration, the removable media scan configuration, the scan policy documentation, and the scan event logs from inserted media.

artifacts.name: Multi-Connected Device Standard
artifacts.description: The approved standard defining specific configuration settings for devices that connect to both trusted and untrusted networks and the evidence preventing devices from being actively connected to an untrusted network while concurrently connected to the protected one.

artifacts.name: Remote Wipe Records
artifacts.description: The log of remote wipe actions performed on lost or stolen devices, evidencing the protective measures can be enforced on a device that has left the estate.

artifacts.name: Authentication Controls
artifacts.description: The policy specifying authentication strengths per risk tier and use case, the evidence of secure protocols in use with deprecated ones disabled, the export of conditional and step-up access policies, the multi-factor enforcement coverage report, the passwordless and biometric rollout metrics, the failed authentication anomaly monitoring, and the periodic review of authentication strength against the threat landscape.

artifacts.name: Web and Cloud Access Controls
artifacts.description: The internet services usage policy and the web filtering and cloud access security controls applied at the endpoint.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configurations and the access control lists with the user access review documentation covering the endpoint management consoles.

END-02.notes: 49 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps END-01; what is distinct here is the protective measure rather than the management platform, so encryption at rest, exploit mitigation and removable-media scanning are kept as separate artifacts.

artifacts.name: Malware Protection Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy covering anti-malware controls across endpoints, servers, email and web, with the implementing procedure. CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the document; HITRUST requires the approved policy and standard plus the implementing work instruction.

artifacts.name: Anti-Malware Coverage Report
artifacts.description: The coverage report from the management console showing the agent installed on every applicable system, with the system component inventory carrying deployment status per component and the list of components determined not at risk following periodic evaluation. PISF 2026 requires the report to show no unprotected endpoints; MAS TRM and ISO 27001 require coverage across all managed devices.

artifacts.name: Anti-Malware Capability Evidence
artifacts.description: Vendor documentation evidencing the deployed solution detects all known malware types and removes, blocks or contains them, the configuration export showing those capabilities enabled, and independent test evidence — EICAR, atomic testing or breach-and-attack simulation — confirming the solution actually detects rather than merely being installed.

artifacts.name: Signature and Engine Currency Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration confirming automatic updates of engine and signatures are enabled, the update history logs showing recent successful updates, the status dashboard showing currency across the estate, and the definition update records.

artifacts.name: Scan Configuration and Reports
artifacts.description: The configuration export showing the periodic scan schedule and real-time or continuous behavioural scanning enabled, the scan policy documentation, sample periodic scan reports across covered systems, real-time detection logs, and the scheduled scan reports.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Scan Controls
artifacts.description: The policy governing use of removable media referencing the scan requirement, the endpoint configuration enforcing an automatic scan on insertion (or the alternative continuous behavioural analysis), sample insertion-triggered scan logs, the auto-run disable evidence, and the media restriction policy with its data-loss-prevention and encryption configuration.

artifacts.name: Malware Detection and Incident Records
artifacts.description: The log of malware detected, quarantined and incidents opened, sample quarantine and block logs evidencing detection and remediation, and the malware incident records with their response.

artifacts.name: Anti-Malware Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence showing anti-malware audit logs enabled across all components, the retention configuration meeting the applicable requirement, evidence of forwarding to the central log store, and sample audit log entries from the solution.

artifacts.name: Agent Tamper Protection Configuration
artifacts.description: The tamper-protection configuration preventing users from disabling or altering the agent, the endpoint privilege configuration supporting it, and the documented, management-authorised exceptions for case-by-case temporary disablement with time limits.

artifacts.name: Email and Web Gateway Filtering
artifacts.description: The email security gateway configuration with its malware-blocked report, the web gateway and content filter configuration, deep packet inspection enablement evidence, and the anti-phishing and anti-spam metrics.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Posture and Network Admission Evidence
artifacts.description: The network admission compliance reports and the posture check policy verifying personal firewall and anti-malware state before a device is admitted, with the endpoint, network and user-level control inventory behind it.

artifacts.name: Application Control and Integrity Monitoring
artifacts.description: The application allow-listing documentation, software installation restriction policies and controls, and the file integrity monitoring configuration and alerts.

artifacts.name: Malware Awareness Training Records
artifacts.description: The training content on recognising and avoiding malware with the attendance records and dates, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the controls.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configuration, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, the malware protection deployment and update records, and the access control lists and user access review documentation that scope the protected estate.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Patch and Session Controls
artifacts.description: The endpoint patch compliance report evidencing regular updates, and the session timeout policy and configuration limiting the exposure window on an unattended endpoint.

artifacts.name: Continuity Evidence for Malware Events
artifacts.description: The business continuity plan with recovery objectives and procedures and the test exercise records with post-test review, held here because HITRUST tests malware protection alongside recovery from a malware event.

END-04.notes: 96 asks across 17 frameworks. PCI DSS contributes the most granular set — coverage, capability, currency, periodic scanning, removable media, logging and tamper protection are each separately testable requirements — so those stay as distinct artifacts rather than collapsing into one anti-malware configuration.

artifacts.name: Automatic Update Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export confirming automatic updates of the anti-malware engine and signatures are enabled, the auto-update configuration, the real-time protection configuration, and the update configuration on the deployed agents.

artifacts.name: Signature Currency Status
artifacts.description: The dashboard export from the anti-malware console showing currency of signatures across the estate, the status showing all endpoints hold current definition and engine versions, the signature update compliance reports, the update compliance reports, the update distribution verification, and the update history logs showing recent successful updates.

artifacts.name: Definition Update Logs
artifacts.description: The anti-malware signature update logs, the signature update records, the malware definition update records, and the definition update logs from the management console.

artifacts.name: Anti-Malware Deployment Coverage
artifacts.description: The report showing an anti-malware agent installed on all managed devices, the anti-malware deployment inventory, the anti-malware controls inventory, the endpoint protection deployment records, the anti-malware deployment evidence, the anti-malware solution documentation, and the deployment and update records covering the estate. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented malicious code protection update requirement.

artifacts.name: Malware Protection Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering anti-malware controls across endpoints, servers, mail and web, with the security operations procedures and monitoring configurations implementing it. HITRUST requires the approved controls against malicious code policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The scheduled scan reports, the periodic malware scanning reports, the malware scan reports, the system scan reports with their schedules, and the scan reports from the deployed agents.

artifacts.name: Malware Detection and Response Records
artifacts.description: The log of malware detected, quarantined and incidents opened; the malware incident records; the anti-malware alert configuration; the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports; and the gateway threat detection records supporting them.

artifacts.name: Mail and Removable Media Scanning
artifacts.description: The report from the mail security gateway showing malware blocked, the endpoint configuration enforcing an anti-virus scan on removable-media insertion, the removable media scanning configuration, the pre-transmission scanning configuration, the auto-run disable evidence, and the removable media restriction policy with its data loss prevention and encryption configuration.

artifacts.name: Malware Awareness Training Records
artifacts.description: The training records on recognising and avoiding malware, the malware awareness training records, and the training attendance records with dates.

artifacts.name: Patch Management Records
artifacts.description: The patch management policy and procedures, the patch deployment records, the patch testing documentation, the vulnerability remediation tracking, and the patch status reports for remote-access servers and clients.

artifacts.name: Continuity Records
artifacts.description: The business continuity plan with its recovery objectives and procedures, the test exercise records with the post-test review documentation, and the session timeout policy and configuration accompanying them.

artifacts.name: Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The access control lists with the user access review documentation covering the consoles that manage the anti-malware estate.

END-04.1.notes: 62 asks across 14 frameworks. The narrow demand is that definitions update automatically and the estate is current; the deployment-coverage artifact is separate because an estate can be fully patched on the endpoints that have an agent while missing the ones that do not.

artifacts.name: Tamper Protection Configuration
artifacts.description: The anti-malware tamper-protection configuration preventing users from disabling or altering the agent, the endpoint privilege configuration restricting who can, and the documented management-authorised exceptions for case-by-case temporary disablement with their time limits.

artifacts.name: Real-Time Protection Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export showing the periodic scan schedule and real-time or continuous behavioural scanning enabled, the real-time protection configuration, the anti-malware deployment inventory, the anti-malware deployment, and the update configuration. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented anti-malware detection and prevention requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the perform-periodic-and-real-time-scans requirement.

artifacts.name: Scan Reports and Detection Logs
artifacts.description: The sample periodic scan reports across covered systems, the sample real-time and behavioural detection logs, the scheduled scan reports, the scan reports, the scan event logs, and the anti-malware alert configuration with the signature update logs behind it.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Scanning
artifacts.description: The policy governing use of removable media referencing the scan requirement, the anti-malware configuration showing automatic scan on insertion or an alternative continuous scan, the removable media scan policy and configuration, the sample logs evidencing scans performed on insertion, the scan policy documentation, and the auto-run disable configuration and evidence.

artifacts.name: Malware Protection Operations
artifacts.description: The malware protection deployment and update records, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, the security operations procedures and monitoring configurations, and the access control lists with the user access review documentation covering the management console.

artifacts.name: Malware Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The malware awareness training records covering why the protection may not be disabled.

END-04.7.notes: 36 asks across 9 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is that protection cannot be turned off — the tamper-protection configuration and the authorised-exception records are the primary artifacts, kept apart from the scanning evidence.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Agent Coverage
artifacts.description: The report showing anti-malware, detection and response coverage with no unprotected endpoints, the host-based prevention deployment documentation, the automated discovery reports, the software inventory tool configuration with its coverage documentation, and the endpoint patch compliance report.

artifacts.name: Prevention Policy and Action Logs
artifacts.description: The host-based prevention policy configuration, the prevention action logs, the removable media control policy and configuration, the exception documentation, the monthly review records, and the unauthorised software removal records.

artifacts.name: Integrity Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The file integrity monitoring configuration, the integrity verification tool reports, and the unauthorised change detection records produced by the endpoint agent.

artifacts.name: Agent Failure Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The procedure for detecting and addressing failures of each listed critical security control system, the service-provider variant of that procedure, the alert configuration covering those systems, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, the sample failure alert logs, the sample failure alerts with their triage and resolution records, the documented response procedure covering restoring security functions and identifying cause and duration, the response records demonstrating prompt addressing, the sample incident response records for past failures, the mean-time-to-restore metrics, and the lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Incident Handling Records
artifacts.description: The incident response plan and procedures, the security incident classification and prioritisation criteria, the incident investigation and analysis reports, and the post-incident review and lessons learned documentation covering what the endpoint agent detected.

END-06.2.notes: 31 asks across 5 frameworks. The agent deployment coverage, its prevention actions and the detection of the agent itself failing are three proofs; the last arrives via PCI DSS 10.7 and is kept whole.

artifacts.name: Security & Privacy Program Charter
artifacts.description: The charter establishing and resourcing the cybersecurity programme and, separately or in the same document, the data privacy programme: mandate, scope, objectives, authority, funding and staffing, the programme owner, and the reporting line into governance. Must be management-approved and current; where an ISMS is claimed, the charter must tie to the ISMS documentation set and to the recognised framework the programme is built on.

artifacts.name: Board-Approved Security Governance Framework
artifacts.description: The overarching framework document approved by the board or management body that defines how security, technology and risk are governed: leadership and organisational structures, decision rights, processes linking technology to enterprise strategy, and the mandated components (risk assessment, controls implementation, controls monitoring). Must be the current version, evidence formal board approval, and where required show how system complexity and customer/service considerations were factored into its design.

artifacts.name: Board Approval Records & Governance Minutes
artifacts.description: The approval trail for the programme, framework and policies: certified board resolutions with signatures of attending directors and the company secretary, board and committee meeting minutes showing the framework was deliberated with attendees, discussion points and voting outcome, and e-signature or workflow approval records for individual policy versions. Must cover both initial adoption and each subsequent review/re-approval.

artifacts.name: Information Security Policy & Topic-Specific Policy Library
artifacts.description: The master information security policy signed and dated by top management stating objectives, scope and commitments, plus the indexed library of subordinate topic-specific policies (access control, cryptography, backup, HR security, supply chain, cyber hygiene and so on) with owner, version number and review date for each. Must be the currently issued version with version history and management sign-off.

artifacts.name: Policy Communication & Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the policy set was published and received: intranet/email/town-hall communication evidence, and the HR or LMS export showing each employee acknowledged the current policy version with a timestamp. Where a code of conduct is in scope, include the employee acknowledgement records for it as well.

artifacts.name: Annual Policy & Framework Review Records
artifacts.description: Minutes or records of the scheduled review of the policy set and governance framework showing what changes were considered, the reviewer, the approval outcome and the next review date, plus the framework review log tracking each review cycle with dates, reviewers, changes made and re-approval reference. Review must be at least annual where specified, and additionally triggered by significant change; risk assessments carry their own annual review record.

artifacts.name: Governance Structure & Roles Documentation
artifacts.description: How accountability is structured and assigned: organisational charts showing the security function and reporting lines from board through committees to CIO/CTO/CISO, RACI matrices for IT and security processes, board and committee charters with composition and independence declarations, the security organisation charter, and documented management-body responsibility assignments. Must be current and reconcile to the people actually in post.

artifacts.name: Security Strategy, Roadmap & Resource Allocation Evidence
artifacts.description: The approved multi-year security/technology strategy with goals aligned to business objectives and applicable law, the implementation roadmap with periodic execution review records, the traceability matrix linking each initiative to a strategic objective with value metrics and resource allocation, and evidence that adequate skilled staff and budget were actually allocated. Include the mapping showing corporate governance and technology governance are aligned rather than parallel.

artifacts.name: Risk Management Framework & Risk Treatment Plans
artifacts.description: The documented risk assessment methodology, the ICT/technology risk management framework with its board approval record, the resulting risk treatment plans with prioritised actions and implementation evidence, and the annual risk assessment review record. Must show risk decisions are traceable from assessment through treatment to residual acceptance.

artifacts.name: Program Performance Reporting & Metrics
artifacts.description: The recurring reporting that demonstrates the programme is monitored: security KPI/metrics dashboards, ISMS monitoring reports, IT value delivery and benefit realisation dashboards, the integrated governance reporting pack consolidating corporate and technology MIS for the board, periodic governance effectiveness reviews, and the briefing records evidencing the management body was informed of programme effectiveness.

artifacts.name: Resilience Program Plans
artifacts.description: The continuity and response plans the programme must encompass: incident response plan with defined roles and escalation, incident classification/severity framework and handling playbooks, the incident log with post-incident review records, business continuity plan covering critical services, disaster recovery plan with defined RTO/RPO, backup management policy with testing records, and the crisis management and communication framework. Each must be current, approved and testable.

artifacts.name: Supporting Security Program Documentation
artifacts.description: The remaining constituent programme documents the framework must demonstrably cover: supply chain security policy with supplier risk assessments, contractual security requirements and supplier monitoring/audit reports; secure procurement and secure SDLC documentation with vulnerability handling/disclosure policy and pre-deployment testing results; cyber hygiene practices and the awareness/training programme with attendance records and phishing exercise results; cryptography and key management with the encryption inventory and algorithm review records; HR security, access control with least privilege, asset inventory/classification and access recertification records; and MFA policy, coverage assessment and secured/emergency communications documentation with testing records. Third-party agreements carrying security clauses, SLAs and right-to-audit, plus the third-party risk assessment and monitoring records, sit here.

artifacts.name: Operating Procedures & Document Control Set
artifacts.description: The operating procedure library that implements the programme - SOPs and runbooks for routine operations with version control log, distribution/acknowledgement records, on-call handover procedure and periodic review evidence - together with the document control procedure, template library, controlled repository, retention and disposition schedule and external-origin document register governing all programme documentation.

artifacts.name: Audit, Assessment & Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: Independent evidence that the programme operates: internal and external security audit reports with findings, penetration test reports, periodic and continuous control review reports, regulator or national-authority assessment records, certification evidence where held, and the gap remediation tracker showing findings driven to closure with owners and dates.

artifacts.name: Compliance Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The register of laws, regulations, standards and contractual obligations the programme must satisfy, with the applicable requirement, owner, how it is addressed and the last review date - including externally originated documents required for programme planning and operation. Must be current and traceable to the controls or policies that discharge each obligation.

artifacts.name: Management Commitment & Workforce Conduct Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that leadership visibly owns the programme and that expectations reach staff: the signed leadership commitment statement providing resources and directing enforcement, management review minutes of programme performance, the code of conduct/ethics policy with employee acknowledgements and any disciplinary records for violations, new-joiner security briefing records, employment contract security and confidentiality clauses, and the guidance issued to line managers on enforcing policy in their teams.

GOV-01.notes: 167 entries collapse to 16 artifacts. NIS2 Article 21(2)(b)-(j) alone contributes ~35 entries that are the constituent sub-programmes a security programme must cover rather than separate evidence asks; they are grouped into two bundle artifacts (resilience plans, supporting programme documents) with the coverage list in the description.

artifacts.name: Committee Charters & Terms of Reference
artifacts.description: The formal charter or terms of reference for every oversight body in scope - executive/security steering committee, board IT committee, information security committee or forum, technology risk committee, fraud review group, PMO and procurement oversight forum - stating mandate, scope, decision rights, composition requirements, quorum, meeting frequency and reporting obligations. Must be the current approved version with version history showing each update and its re-approval, and where cloud or outsourcing oversight is in scope the ToR must explicitly include SLA, KPI/KRI and incident review responsibilities.

artifacts.name: Committee Constitution & Composition Records
artifacts.description: Evidence each body was properly constituted and is properly staffed: the board resolution constituting it with effective date, the composition register naming members with designation, director type and the function they represent (IT, information security, risk, compliance, operations, business), member appointment letters, CVs and credential evidence for qualification requirements, annual independence declarations, the applicability assessment confirming the requirement applies to the entity, and an org chart showing cross-functional representation. Must evidence any mandated minimums such as member count, an independent director and an IT-qualified member.

artifacts.name: Committee Meeting Minutes, Attendance & Calendar
artifacts.description: The meeting record for each body: the annual meeting calendar evidencing planned cadence, attendance registers confirming quorum and cross-functional presence at each sitting, and minutes capturing attendees, agenda, matters discussed, decisions taken, action items, owners and target dates. Minutes must evidence the substantive oversight the frameworks require - strategy and policy deliberation, technology risk discussion, project implementation review, procurement governance by scope and size, incident review including cyber and cloud incidents, and internal control oversight - at the mandated frequency (quarterly for some bodies, at each meeting for project review).

artifacts.name: Management Review Records
artifacts.description: The formal management review of the management system: the procedure defining frequency, participants, required inputs and outputs; the compiled input pack covering status of prior actions, changes in context and interested-party requirements, performance trends (nonconformities, corrective actions, monitoring and measurement results, audit results) and improvement opportunities; and the documented outputs - decisions, directions and action items with owners.

artifacts.name: Oversight Reporting Packs & Performance Dashboards
artifacts.description: The recurring status reporting the committee receives and forwards upward: the quarterly business review or equivalent recurring programme status report, periodic reports from the committee to top management against a documented cadence, project status dashboards and monitoring reports covering all technology projects, PMO reports, KPI/KRI and CSP performance dashboards, cyber security effectiveness metrics, cloud incident packs with trends and actions, and the board reporting evidence closing the loop. Reports must be dated, attributable and traceable to the meeting at which they were tabled.

artifacts.name: Committee-Approved Roles & Responsibilities Assignment
artifacts.description: The formally approved definition and assignment of cyber/information security roles and responsibilities - including the ICT function responsibility matrix, the entity designated to govern the business continuity programme, and departmental focal persons - together with the committee minutes approving those assignments and the conflict-of-interest review confirming no incompatible duties were created.

artifacts.name: Risk Appetite Statement & Risk Acceptance Decisions
artifacts.description: The board- or committee-approved technology/ICT risk appetite and tolerance statement, plus the records showing it is actually applied: IT and ICT decisions reviewed against the stated appetite, and documented risk acceptance decisions taken by the management body with the accepting authority, rationale and review date.

artifacts.name: Strategies & Policies Reviewed and Approved by the Committee
artifacts.description: Evidence the committee performs its pre-approval and approval role: the IT/digital strategy and policy drafts bearing committee review comments and sign-off, the standard review checklist used, the pre-submission approval log tracking each item and its board submission date, the resulting committee-approved information security policies and procedures, and the management-body approval records for cybersecurity policies. Must show the committee reviewed before board submission where that sequence is mandated.

artifacts.name: Dissemination & Awareness Records for Committee Decisions
artifacts.description: Records evidencing that committee-approved policies, procedures and directives were communicated to the stakeholders they bind, with acknowledgements captured, plus the awareness communications demonstrating personnel were informed of the governance requirement itself.

artifacts.name: Resource Allocation & Management Commitment Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that leadership backs the programme with more than minutes: the documented management commitment statement, leadership communication records, evidence of adequate funding and skilled resources allocated (including specifically for critical infrastructure information security), records of top-management decisions on critical security matters, executive or board minutes evidencing leadership accountability for risk decisions, and the accountability framework documenting where that responsibility sits.

artifacts.name: Deficiency & Action Item Remediation Tracking
artifacts.description: The tracking record proving oversight produces closure: the control deficiency and exception log with management reporting, corrective action plans with owners, timelines and current status, follow-up tracking of assurance and audit recommendations, project escalation and procurement issue logs handled by the committee, and test deficiency trackers. Must show open items ageing and escalation to the board for significant deficiencies.

artifacts.name: Assurance, Audit & Compliance Reports Reviewed by the Committee
artifacts.description: The independent assurance material the committee is required to review: assurance initiative plans with scope and objectives and the resulting review reports with findings and recommendations, security audit and penetration test reports, compliance assessment reports and gap analyses, external audit and regulatory examination findings, evidence of compliance with laws, regulations and contracts, and - for outsourced or cloud services - post-incident review reports received from the provider and the annual incident response plan test report.

artifacts.name: Committee Member Competency & Training Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the oversight body is competent to oversee: board and committee member competency profiles demonstrating technology and technology-risk knowledge, and the training records showing members received briefing or training on technology risk topics.

artifacts.name: Governance Process & Oversight Procedure Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented processes the oversight function runs on: transparency and oversight reporting procedures, PMO and procurement governance operating procedures with reporting cadence and escalation rules, the human oversight process design with override and appeal mechanisms where automated decisioning is in scope, the performance monitoring framework with KPI definitions and conformance monitoring, the regulatory compliance register, and the data governance and business process control documentation the committee is accountable for.

artifacts.name: Stakeholder Engagement, Impact & Feedback Records
artifacts.description: Where the committee's remit covers impact on external parties: the stakeholder engagement and feedback log with adjudication and integration records, impact assessments documenting likelihood and magnitude of beneficial and harmful outcomes with risk ratings and treatment decisions, and the context documentation covering intended purpose, deployment setting, users and assumptions that the committee reviewed. Records must be retained, timestamped and attributable.

GOV-01.1.notes: 166 entries collapse to 15 artifacts. The input repeats one committee lifecycle across many named bodies (board IT committee, IT steering committee, information security committee, security forum, fraud review group, PMO, procurement forum, management review) - those are consolidated by artifact type (charter, composition, minutes, reporting pack) with the bodies named in the descriptions. Some COBIT entries (APO14 data governance, DSS06 process controls) are mis-mapped in the source data and are folded into the governance-process documentation item.

artifacts.name: Governance Committee Charters and Terms of Reference
artifacts.description: The charters or terms of reference for every forum that exercises oversight of security, privacy, risk and technology: the cybersecurity steering committee, the data privacy steering committee, the audit committee, the risk committee, the Data Management Board, the board IT committee (BITC) and the information security committee. Each must state mandate, membership, quorum, meeting cadence, decision authority and reporting line to the board. Include the cyber governance charter establishing board and senior management responsibility, the RACI or accountability matrix defining the chain of accountability for cyber actions, and the fraud review group ToR where applicable. NIS2 requires documentation of the management body accountability framework.

artifacts.name: Board and Committee Meeting Minutes
artifacts.description: Approved minutes for the audit period from the board, audit committee, risk committee, IT/board technology committee, information security committee and executive management, evidencing that security, privacy, risk and compliance matters were actually presented, discussed and decided. Minutes must capture attendees, agenda, the material presented, decisions taken and direction given. Must cover each responsibility assigned to the committee (QCB), receipt and deliberation of committee reports by the board (SBP ETGRMF), management review decisions on continual improvement (ISO 42001), leadership accountability for AI risk decisions (NIST AI RMF), and management oversight of cybersecurity (NIS2).

artifacts.name: Board Reporting Policy and Reporting Calendar
artifacts.description: The board-approved policy defining the format, contents and cadence of management information reported to the governing body - covering IT strategy implementation, policy exceptions, major project status and cyber security matters - together with the reporting calendar or schedule showing the agreed cadence to the board, board technology committee and audit committee. Include the board-approved cyber security policy and its version control log (QCB), and the HITRUST-required approved policy and implementing procedure for management commitment to information security.

artifacts.name: Periodic Cyber Security Status Report to the Board
artifacts.description: The recurring briefing pack submitted to the board and top management on the security programme: action plan progress and implementation status, the threat landscape and a summary of major threats and attacks faced with estimated operational impact, programme performance metrics and indicator dashboards, and the board MIS pack with its submission log. Cadence differs by framework - QCB requires semi-annual board indicator dashboards and an annual review report; SBP ETGRMF and PISF 2026 require periodic reports with a documented cadence. Include the formal measures of performance used to track programme health (SCF).

artifacts.name: Consolidated IT and Operations Reports to the Audit Committee
artifacts.description: The periodic consolidated reports submitted to the audit committee, with evidence that each mandated subject area is actually covered in the report content, plus the submission records proving they were delivered. SBP ETGRMF requires separate consolidated coverage of: information and cyber security; IT service delivery and operations; IT outsourcing and cloud service arrangements; IT project management, acquisition and development; IT procurement; performance management with KPIs; and BCP/DRP including test results. Also includes the board technology committee's consolidated reports to the board on technology activities and digital initiatives.

artifacts.name: Board Oversight Records for Major Technology Projects
artifacts.description: Evidence that the governing body approves and tracks major technology investments: the board-approved criteria defining what qualifies as a major project (cost threshold, strategic significance, risk), board resolutions approving each major project with its business case and risk assessment, the register or tracker of major projects with status, budget and impact on operations, earnings and capital, and the periodic project status reports submitted upward (IT steering committee to board technology committee to board) covering progress, budget, risk and issues. COBIT additionally requires the programme management methodology and standards, programme charters and authorisation records, and programme plans with milestones and resource allocations.

artifacts.name: Risk Reporting to Executives and Board-Approved Risk Appetite
artifacts.description: The risk reporting methodology showing how high-exposure systems, processes and infrastructure are surfaced to management, the register of risk events, regulatory requirements and audit observations that feed it, management's approval of the methodology, and a sample of the resulting risk reports tabled at senior management and the IT steering committee. Must include the board-approved cyber risk appetite statement (QCB), documented risk acceptance decisions taken by the management body (NIS2), reports on major risks escalated to the steering committee, results of risk process testing and control reviews, and the annual legal-risk impact assessment with the per-system legal requirements register and IPR, records-retention, data-protection and cryptography compliance evidence.

artifacts.name: Significant Incident and Post-Implementation Review Escalation Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that material incidents and project outcomes reach executive level: the matrix defining which incidents are significant enough to require steering committee review, the records of those escalations, and the MIS reports on incidents, logs and breaches reviewed periodically by senior management. Also the post-implementation review material presented to executives - the PIR executive summary tabled at senior management and the register of identified deficiencies with corrective action tracking.

artifacts.name: Audit Findings and Remediation Status Reported to the Governing Body
artifacts.description: The centrally managed repository of internal audit findings and control deficiencies with owner, rating, agreed corrective action and closure status, together with the reports that put it in front of the governing body. Must include: governance oversight reporting of non-compliance to executive leadership (SCF), management reporting on control exceptions and board reporting on significant deficiencies (SOC 2), quarterly audit recommendation status reports to the board and audit committee (SBP ETGRMF), the material gap register with senior management justification memos and board-signed action plans submitted to the regulator (QCB), vulnerability remediation action plans, and internal audit's independent certification to the board on compliance of cloud outsourcing arrangements with its documented scope, methodology and regulatory compliance matrix (SBP Cloud).

artifacts.name: Business Continuity and Backup Assurance Reporting to the Board
artifacts.description: Evidence that the governing body evaluates resilience testing outcomes: the report submitted to the board summarising the BCP testing programme and its results, and the records showing both senior management and the board evaluated that programme. PISF 2026 additionally requires the documented mechanism for continuous monitoring of backup and restore activity and evidence that backup/restore effectiveness is included in the regular audits reported to senior management.

artifacts.name: Executive Leadership Accountability and Commitment Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that named executives own the programme and that top management demonstrably backs it: appointment letters for the CIO, CTO and CISO with the job descriptions setting out required expertise and the board or CEO approval of those appointments (MAS TRM), board member CVs evidencing cyber expertise (QCB), the signed top-management commitment statement aligning the programme with strategic direction, records of budget and resource allocation provisioned to the programme, the log of leadership communications (town halls, memos) on its importance, records of executive cyber briefings and drills, board approval of the cybersecurity policies (NIS2), and the HITRUST awareness communications and periodic review records evidencing management commitment is maintained over time.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Oversight Records
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are in scope: the approved policies and procedures for human oversight of AI, the human-AI configuration design showing override and appeal mechanisms, context documentation covering intended purposes, deployment settings, users and assumptions (current, version-controlled and dated), and the periodic review records showing the oversight arrangements remain effective over time. Required by NIST AI RMF GOVERN 2.3 and MAP 3.5.

artifacts.name: Privacy Programme Reporting Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy and implementing procedure for privacy protection reporting, the privacy notice or statement published to data subjects with its version history, and the records that demonstrate the privacy programme operates - consent records, opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, retained for the required period and protected from tampering. Required by HITRUST as the privacy counterpart to security oversight reporting.

GOV-01.2.notes: 145 entries from 11 frameworks collapsed to 13 artifacts, all assigned exactly once. No automated collectors exist for this control and none realistically could - it is board and committee governance evidence - so nearly everything is manual; only the audit-findings tracker is hybrid because a GRC or ticketing system holds it. SBP ETGRMF dominates the input (60+ entries) because it enumerates every individual report to every governing forum; those collapse into three report artifacts (cyber status, consolidated IT/operations reports to Audit Committee, and project oversight) plus one minutes artifact.

artifacts.name: Resource Gap Analysis
artifacts.description: The management-produced resource gap report identifying deficiencies across people, process and technology submitted to the governing body, the management resource gap analysis, the register of sanctioned security posts with fill status and justification, and the approved staffing plan showing conversion of positions or new hiring for dedicated security roles.

artifacts.name: Gap Closure Tracking
artifacts.description: The action plan with owners, timelines and budgets for filling the identified gaps; the tracking log showing status and timelines for each gap; the gap status tracking log updated periodically; the improvement tracking; and the enhancement implementation records.

artifacts.name: Resource Investment Records
artifacts.description: The board resolutions approving budgets and resources to close identified gaps, the approved headcount plans and budgets demonstrating allocation against those gaps, the budget allocation records, the board or management-approved annual budget with dedicated line items for security solutions, training and certifications, the register mapping allocated funds to security initiatives with spend tracking, the minutes evidencing budget approval, the annual awareness budget approval, and the appointment or reassignment orders establishing dedicated security roles.

artifacts.name: Programme Charter and Benchmarking
artifacts.description: The information security organisation charter, the programme document referencing recognised industry practice, the awareness programme charter, the security function job description covering the listed responsibilities, the annual performance review of that role, and the programme and budget presentations to executive leadership.

artifacts.name: Framework Improvement Records
artifacts.description: The records of periodic reviews of the audit framework, the log of improvements aligning the framework with evolving standards and threats, and the lessons learned feeding them.

artifacts.name: Technology Watch Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for monitoring technological developments relevant to cyber risk management, the list of subscriptions, feeds and research memberships supporting it, the reports on emerging threats and new cyber risk management processes, and the change log of controls updated in response to those developments.

artifacts.name: Continuous Improvement Records
artifacts.description: The documented continuous improvement specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records.

artifacts.name: Data Governance Records
artifacts.description: The data governance framework and policies, the data classification and metadata management documentation, the data quality management reports and metrics, and the data retention policies with their backup and recovery procedures.

GOV-01.3.notes: 38 asks across 6 frameworks. The gap analysis, the resources committed to close it and the record that the gap actually closed are three proofs; the last is what distinguishes commitment from intent.

artifacts.name: Information Security Policy
artifacts.description: The organization's top-level, currently approved information security policy. Must state purpose, scope (systems, data, personnel, third parties), management commitment, roles and responsibilities, coordination across organizational units, and compliance/enforcement expectations including consequences of violation. Must carry evidence of approval by the board or the most senior accountable body (financial-sector frameworks specify board or BoD approval; ISO/NIST accept senior management), show a version and effective date, and be the version currently in force. Health-sector frameworks additionally require it to reference disciplinary process and applicable government sanctions.

artifacts.name: Topic-Specific Policy Set
artifacts.description: The full set of subordinate policies beneath the top-level policy, one per security domain. Collectively they must cover, at minimum: access control and identity; authentication and passwords; audit and accountability; awareness and training; configuration and secure baselines; change management; cryptography and key management; data protection, classification and privacy; DLP; incident response; business continuity and contingency; physical and environmental security; media handling and disposal; personnel security; risk assessment; acquisition, secure development and SDLC; supply chain and third-party security; network, communications and transmission security; malware protection; vulnerability and threat management; endpoint and mobile devices; logging and monitoring; interoperability and portability; and where applicable AI governance and health-information protection. Each must be individually approved, versioned and attributable to a named owner. Only the policies relevant to the organization's scope are required, but the set must have no gaps against the frameworks in scope.

artifacts.name: Security Standards Library
artifacts.description: The technical standards that sit between policy and procedure and make policy requirements measurable — for example access control standards and matrices, authentication standards, API security design standards, cryptographic standards, and configuration/hardening standards. Must show approval, version control and the policy clause each standard implements. Cited separately from policies by SCF (E-GOV-09) and by frameworks that distinguish policy from standard.

artifacts.name: Operating Procedures & Runbook Library
artifacts.description: Documented procedures, standard operating procedures, work instructions and runbooks that implement each policy — including operations procedures available to the personnel who run the systems, on-call and handover procedures, and domain procedures (access authorization, incident handling, key generation/distribution/storage/destruction, media disposal, physical access, change control, backup/recovery). Must be under version control, current, and demonstrably available to the staff who need them. Several frameworks require the procedure set to be complete against every published policy, and health-sector frameworks require coverage of a defined list of operational management areas.

artifacts.name: Policy Approval Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that each policy, standard and framework document was formally approved by the authority the applicable framework requires: board resolutions or BoD/committee minutes for the financial-sector frameworks, top-management sign-off for ISO 27001/42001 and HITRUST, and documented management authorization for NIST and PCI DSS. Must tie a specific document version to a specific approval date and approver, and cover the version currently in force.

artifacts.name: Policy Dissemination & Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that published documents actually reached the people bound by them and were acknowledged. Must show both the publication channel (intranet, policy portal, LMS, document management system, including access for onsite vendors and contractors where required) and per-person acknowledgement — signed or system-recorded — from personnel and, where the framework requires it, third-party representatives and external stakeholders. Distribution logs, communication emails and awareness announcements support the same ask. PCI DSS requires acknowledgement by all personnel in scope; several health and banking frameworks require stakeholder acknowledgement per policy.

artifacts.name: Policy & Document Register
artifacts.description: A single master register of all security, compliance and resilience documentation: document name and type (policy, standard, procedure), owner, current version, approval date, next review date, classification, retention and status. Must reconcile to the documents actually published — nothing in force that is missing from the register and nothing registered that cannot be produced. ISO 42001 additionally expects an index of documented information for the management system; several frameworks expect an external-origin document register and retention/disposition schedule alongside it.

artifacts.name: Document Control Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure governing how documented information is created, reviewed, approved, versioned, distributed, protected, retained and disposed of — including the document template library, access controls on the document repository, handling of external-origin documents, and the retention and disposition schedule. Must demonstrate that only current, approved versions are available for use and that superseded versions are withdrawn or clearly marked.

artifacts.name: Roles & Responsibilities Matrix
artifacts.description: Documented assignment of security, compliance and resilience responsibilities — an org chart plus a RACI or equivalent matrix covering policy ownership, control ownership, asset ownership, incident management roles, third-party relationship management and, where AI systems are in scope, AI risk management and human-oversight roles. Frameworks require that these roles are stated in or referenced by the policy set and that named individuals are aware of and have accepted them.

artifacts.name: Security Awareness & Training Records
artifacts.description: The awareness and training program that carries the published policies to personnel: the program plan and annual schedule, curriculum and campaign materials, per-person completion records, and effectiveness measurement (including phishing simulation results where used). Must cover all personnel in scope and, where frameworks require, contractors and onsite vendors. Frequency expectations differ — several frameworks require at least annual delivery, others require it on hire and on significant policy change.

artifacts.name: Security Program Charter & Governance Framework
artifacts.description: The document that establishes the program the policies belong to — an information security program plan, security program charter, IT/technology governance framework, or sector-specific security framework (for example an internet banking security framework or a national sector framework). Must define program scope, governance structure and committees, oversight and reporting lines, resourcing, and how the policy, standard and procedure layers relate to each other. Where a governance committee exists, its charter and minutes evidence the same requirement.

artifacts.name: Policy Review & Update Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the published set is kept current: review minutes, review sign-offs, version/update history and the trigger for each update (scheduled cycle or significant change). Most frameworks require review at least annually; some banking frameworks require a documented review register with version history and approval evidence for each annual update. Deeper periodic-review evidence is collected under the program review control — here the ask is proof the published documents are the reviewed, current versions.

artifacts.name: Policy Implementation Evidence Samples
artifacts.description: For a sample of published policies, the operating records that show the document is more than paper — for example key management ceremony and custodian records, incident and violation logs with corrective actions, physical access and visitor records, access provisioning and review records, encryption and MFA deployment evidence, security testing results, and DLP tool deployment records. CSA CCM asks for this explicitly for each policy domain in the cloud environment; other frameworks fold it into their policy requirement. Sample selection should follow the policy domains in scope rather than attempting full coverage.

artifacts.name: Compliance Monitoring & Security Metrics Reporting
artifacts.description: Reporting that shows whether the published policies are being followed: policy compliance monitoring reports, security metrics or KPI dashboards, exception and deviation registers, policy implementation status reports, and the briefing packs through which results reach senior management or the board. NIS2 requires the management body to be briefed on effectiveness; banking frameworks require an integrated governance reporting pack and an exception/deviation register.

artifacts.name: Framework & Regulatory Coverage Mapping
artifacts.description: A mapping showing that the published policy set covers every applicable legal, regulatory and framework obligation — policy-to-requirement matrices, framework-to-policy coverage maps, a legal and regulatory obligations register, regulatory change impact logs, and gap analysis reports with remediation actions for uncovered requirements. Sector schemes additionally require alignment evidence against participation criteria or a sector framework.

GOV-02.notes: 450 entries collapse to 15 artifacts. The bulk (CSA CCM, NIST 800-53 xx-1 family, PCI DSS x.1.1 family, ADHICS, HIPAA, NIS2 21(2)) are the same request repeated per security domain: 'the approved policy and the procedure for domain X'. Those become two artifacts (top-level policy, topic-specific policy set) plus a procedures library, rather than ~40 near-identical items. Implementation evidence pulled in by broad framework clauses (key ceremony records, physical access logs, MFA deployment, pen test reports) is consolidated into one sampled-implementation item, since for THIS control it only proves the published document is real. No automated collectors are mapped to this control, so nothing is marked automated except where an LMS/intranet could export completion data.

artifacts.name: Policy & Procedure Review Schedule
artifacts.description: The documented plan that sets when the program is reviewed: defined review frequency for policies, standards and procedures, the named owner accountable for each document's review, the review calendar for the current cycle, and the defined events that force an out-of-cycle review (significant change to the business, technology, threat landscape, regulation, or a major incident). Most frameworks require at least annual review; some require the defined frequency to be stated explicitly rather than assumed.

artifacts.name: Policy Review Minutes & Sign-off Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that each scheduled review actually happened: review meeting minutes naming attendees and documents covered, the reviewer's conclusion on continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness, and dated sign-off by the approving authority. Must cover the full document set in scope for the period, not only the top-level policy, and must show the outcome for each document — reaffirmed unchanged, updated, or withdrawn. SCF requests this as E-GOV-12.

artifacts.name: Policy Version History & Change Log
artifacts.description: The document-control trail showing what changed and when: version history per document, update history with the substantive change made, the reason or trigger for the change, effective dates, and the change management records covering policy amendments. Must let a reviewer tie any current clause back to when it was introduced and who approved it, and must show that superseded versions are retained but withdrawn from use.

artifacts.name: Policy & Standards Master Register
artifacts.description: The register the review is run against: every policy, standard and procedure with owner, version, approval date, last review date, next review due and status. Must reconcile to the documents actually in force, and is the artifact that demonstrates the review cycle covered the whole program rather than whichever documents came to hand.

artifacts.name: Current Approved Policy & Procedure Set
artifacts.description: The reviewed documents themselves — the top-level information security policy, the topic-specific policies across all in-scope domains (access control, awareness and training, audit and accountability, assessment and authorization, configuration and change management, contingency planning, identification and authentication, incident response, maintenance, media protection, physical and environmental, planning, personnel security, privacy, risk assessment, acquisition and secure development, communications protection, system integrity, supply chain, logging and monitoring, cryptography, malware protection, endpoint, business continuity, and AI where applicable) and their operating procedures. Needed here as the object of the review: each must carry the version and date that the review records refer to.

artifacts.name: Program Effectiveness Assessment Report
artifacts.description: The assessment behind the review conclusion — evidence the program was judged on how it performs, not only on whether documents exist: governance effectiveness review reports, program review records, control implementation and operating evidence sampled during the review, governance KPI dashboards, audit framework review records, log and monitoring review outputs used as inputs, and the resulting improvement log. Must connect observed performance to the decision to keep, change or extend each part of the program.

artifacts.name: Board & Senior Management Review Reporting
artifacts.description: The reporting through which review outcomes reach the accountable body: the annual review report to the board, board or board-IT-committee minutes recording the review and any decisions, senior management oversight records, approval of updated documents by resolution where required, stakeholder communication packs and governance reporting templates. Financial-sector frameworks require board-level approval of the reviewed policy set; others accept senior management.

artifacts.name: Change-Trigger Impact Assessments
artifacts.description: Records of out-of-cycle reviews driven by change: regulatory change impact logs, threat-landscape briefings considered by management, business model and significant organizational change impact assessments, environmental scanning and threat intelligence inputs, and the assessment of whether each change required a policy or procedure amendment. Must show the trigger, the assessment, and the decision taken.

artifacts.name: Policy Gap Analysis & Compliance Coverage Assessment
artifacts.description: The gap view produced by or feeding the review: policy gap analysis reports, the regulatory compliance register with applicable requirements mapped to the documents that satisfy them, compliance assessment reports, coverage maps, and external audit or regulatory examination findings that identified program shortfalls. Must record remediation actions and owners for identified gaps, and management justification where a gap is accepted rather than closed.

artifacts.name: Security Strategy & Program Charter with Review Records
artifacts.description: The strategic layer reviewed alongside the policy set: the approved information security or IT and digital strategy, the technology governance program charter or sector security framework, the implementation roadmap with progress review records, current-versus-target state and gap analysis, resource allocation evidence, and the minutes and change log of the strategic review itself.

artifacts.name: Document Control Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure governing how reviewed documents are versioned, approved, distributed and retired, together with the document template library and the review and approval records it generates. Needed here to show the review outcome is applied consistently — that updated documents are re-issued through a controlled process and superseded versions removed from circulation.

artifacts.name: Post-Review Communication & Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that revised documents were re-published and re-acknowledged after the review: communication records for updated policies, personnel acknowledgement of the current version, and awareness communications informing staff of what changed. Required where a framework treats the review as incomplete until the updated document reaches the people it binds.

artifacts.name: Policy Exception Register
artifacts.description: The record of exceptions granted against the policy set and their status at review: exception, justification, compensating control, approver and expiry. Reviewed as part of the periodic cycle to confirm exceptions remain justified or are closed.

GOV-03.notes: 216 entries collapse to 13. Nearly half the input is the same request in two shapes: 'the policy for domain X' (which is really GOV-02's artifact, needed here only as the reviewed object) and 'the review/approval record for domain X'. Those become one current-approved-set item plus three review-evidence items (schedule, minutes, version history). The distinctive asks specific to this control — effectiveness assessment, change triggers, gap analysis, board reporting — are kept separate because they are what distinguishes a real periodic review from a re-dated document. No collectors are mapped to this control.

artifacts.name: Security & Compliance RACI Matrix
artifacts.description: One responsibility assignment matrix covering the security, privacy and resilience domains in scope - access control, authentication, logging, configuration, anti-malware, network security, data protection, transmission security, physical access, SDLC, security testing, AI governance and continuity - rather than a separate matrix per domain. Must name accountable owners (not just teams), reconcile to the org chart, and evidence segregation of duties between the security function and IT operations.

artifacts.name: Security & Compliance Role Job Descriptions
artifacts.description: Job descriptions for the qualified individuals carrying the programme - CISO or equivalent, and the CIO, CRO, CPO, DPO, COO and security officer roles where they exist - stating the mission, authority, required expertise and reporting line. Several frameworks additionally require the description to evidence independence from IT delivery and to enumerate the specific programme responsibilities the role owns.

artifacts.name: Roles & Responsibilities Documents per Security Domain
artifacts.description: The narrative responsibility documents that accompany the RACI - who performs, reviews and approves each activity within each security domain, and how ICT and continuity responsibilities are allocated. Where the framework requires it, this must exist as an approved standard or work instruction, not just a matrix.

artifacts.name: Organisation Chart with Security Function
artifacts.description: Current organisation chart showing the security, compliance and resilience function, its position in the enterprise, and its reporting lines up to executive management or the board. Must make the separation between the security function and IT operations visible, and cover the continuity organisation where a separate BCMS structure exists.

artifacts.name: Board & Senior Management Oversight Records
artifacts.description: Minutes and reporting packs evidencing that leadership actually oversees the programme: board or committee minutes covering security, ICT and AI risk, the periodic CISO report to senior management and the board, programme and budget presentations, and the senior-management oversight records for the period. Cadence expectations differ - some frameworks accept annual board approval, others expect at least quarterly reporting - so provide the full period.

artifacts.name: Security Policy Set Assigning Responsibilities
artifacts.description: The approved policies and standards that formally allocate information security responsibilities, including the policy sections stating management commitment and the documented procedures or work instructions implementing that allocation, plus evidence the policy library is maintained and implemented.

artifacts.name: Officer Appointment Letters
artifacts.description: Signed appointment or designation letters for the accountable officers - CISO, security officer, privacy/data protection officer, continuity lead and the equivalent function leads - showing the appointing authority, effective date, and the approval of that appointment by the board or CEO where the framework requires it.

artifacts.name: Periodic Review of Roles, Structure & Programme Performance
artifacts.description: Evidence that the assignment is re-examined rather than set once: annual review of the security policy and of the organisational structure with its rationale, benchmarking against peers or standards, CISO objectives and performance review, programme KPIs and maturity assessments, and compliance monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Role Communication & Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that assigned responsibilities were communicated and accepted: the communication announcing role allocation, personnel acknowledgement records for their security responsibilities and the code of conduct, awareness session logs, and any disciplinary records arising from conduct violations.

artifacts.name: Resource, Budget & Skills Allocation Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence the function has the means to deliver: approved budget and its review, headcount and staffing plan against the security organisation, skills inventory or competency matrix for the team, tooling inventory for risk, vulnerability and forensic work, and documented delegation of authority to the accountable officer.

artifacts.name: Security Function & Committee Charters
artifacts.description: Charter or terms of reference for the security function and for the governing committees under it (information security group, incident response programme, physical security), stating mandate, scope, membership and decision rights.

artifacts.name: Asset, Facility & Third-Party Ownership Records
artifacts.description: Records showing accountability extends beyond the core team: asset ownership register, evidence of coverage across facilities including physical access and CCTV records where the framework maps them here, and third-party agreements with security clauses, SLAs and right-to-audit together with the supplier assessment and monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Security Programme Strategy & Roadmap
artifacts.description: The approved enterprise security strategy or cyber security framework document that the assigned function is mandated to deliver, referencing the standard it is built on, together with the implementation roadmap and its review records.

artifacts.name: Risk Tolerance & Risk Governance Records
artifacts.description: Documented risk tolerance or appetite statements approved by leadership - covering ICT and, where in scope, AI risk - the board-level risk policies, the risk assessment reports the function produces, and residual risk acceptance records signed by the accountable owner.

artifacts.name: Independence & Conflict-of-Interest Assessment
artifacts.description: Assessment of the security leader's reporting line for conflicts of interest, with the conclusion on independence from the functions being assured, and the role-dedication policy governing whether the role may be combined with other duties.

GOV-04.notes: 177 entries collapsed to 15 artifacts. The largest duplication is PCI DSS restating the same two artifacts (a RACI matrix and a roles-and-responsibilities document) once per security domain - twelve domains, twenty-four entries, two real documents. Org chart, acknowledgements and headcount evidence are hybrid given the HRIS collector (Rippling).

artifacts.name: Organization Chart & Reporting Structure
artifacts.description: Current organisation chart showing reporting lines for the IT, security, risk and business functions, including the governance structure diagram and the specific structures required by individual frameworks (BCMS, incident response team, cross-departmental security representation). Must show independence of the security function and be recent enough to match the personnel actually in post.

artifacts.name: Roles & Responsibilities / RACI Matrix
artifacts.description: The master accountability matrix assigning responsible, accountable, consulted and informed parties for every cybersecurity, privacy and technology risk activity, with function-specific views where frameworks demand them: AI risk management, business continuity, incident handling, IT operations, procurement, documentation change control and critical information infrastructure. Must cover mapping, measuring and managing asset, application, service and data risk, name the empowered individuals or roles rather than departments only, and be formally approved.

artifacts.name: Governance Body Charters, Terms of Reference & Appointment Records
artifacts.description: Charters and terms of reference for the governing bodies and accountable roles — cyber/security governance committee, risk management forum, operational risk group, legal function, security function — together with the appointment letters or designation records naming individuals to accountable positions.
