artifacts.name: Continuity Resource Requirements
artifacts.description: The resource requirements analysis for continuity, the technology recovery requirements, the alternate site specifications, and the third-party service agreements supporting them.

artifacts.name: Privileged Operator Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The roster of staff authorised for privileged operations with their training records, and the dual-control or four-eyes workflow governing administrative access.

artifacts.name: AI Competence and Team Composition Records
artifacts.description: The AI risk management training records with attendees, the team composition records evidencing demographic, disciplinary and domain diversity, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the AI impact assessment, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, the risk treatment plan, and the demonstration of validity and reliability with limitations documented.

HRS-03.2.notes: 82 asks across 13 frameworks. Competence and training overlap but are distinct here: the competence matrix defines what a role requires, the training records evidence what a person received. Both are kept because an assessor asks for the matrix first and the records against it.

artifacts.name: Background Screening Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining screening scope by role and jurisdiction in line with privacy law, the background check policy and procedures, the matrix specifying required checks per role tier, the background check criteria matrix by role and risk, the documented background verification process, the screening procedures, the personnel security policy alignment, and the documented screening procedure for roles with access to regulated environments within local legal constraints. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented background screening policy requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the screen-individuals-before-access requirement. HITRUST requires the approved screening policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Screening Records
artifacts.description: The completed screening reports covering criminal, credit, reference and qualification checks; the completed background verification records; the background check records; the background verification records per role sensitivity; the records of completed checks for technology personnel; the vetting and background check records; the reference check documentation; the verification reports; the screening records; and the tracker of screening status for all hires with completion dates and sign-offs.

artifacts.name: Re-Screening Records
artifacts.description: The records of periodic re-screening for high-risk roles where legally permitted and the rescreening schedule governing them.

artifacts.name: Screening Provider Agreements
artifacts.description: The agreement with the background check provider including its data protection clauses, the vendor agreements for background verification services, the documentation of jurisdictional legal constraints affecting screening scope, and the government mandate compliance evidence where screening is legally directed.

artifacts.name: Customer and Vendor Due Diligence
artifacts.description: The know-your-customer procedure and the employee and vendor due diligence records applying equivalent scrutiny outside the payroll.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Controls
artifacts.description: The identity verification procedures, the authentication policy and procedures, the authentication mechanism documentation, and the multi-factor authentication implementation evidence establishing that the screened person is the person accessing.

artifacts.name: AI Competence Records
artifacts.description: The competence matrix mapping AI-related roles to required education, training, experience and skill level; the updated job descriptions specifying those requirements; the training records; and the records evaluating the effectiveness of the competence actions taken.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Screening Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit; the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records; and the data classification scheme determining which provider roles require screening.

HRS-04.notes: 46 asks across 12 frameworks. Overlaps HRS-04.1; here the object is screening for all personnel rather than the elevated tier, so the role-tier matrix stays with the policy and re-screening is kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Background Screening Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining screening scope by role and jurisdiction in line with privacy law, the background check policy and procedures, the matrix specifying required checks per role tier, the background check criteria matrix by role and risk, the documented background verification process, the screening procedures, and the documented personnel screening procedure for roles with access to regulated environments within local legal constraints. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented screen-individuals-before-access requirement. HITRUST requires the approved screening policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Screening Records
artifacts.description: The completed screening reports covering criminal, credit, reference and qualification checks; the completed background verification records; the background check records; the background verification records per role sensitivity; the records of completed checks for technology personnel; the reference check documentation; the verification reports; the screening records; and the tracker of screening status for all hires with completion dates and sign-offs.

artifacts.name: Re-Screening Records
artifacts.description: The records of periodic re-screening for high-risk roles where legally permitted and the rescreening schedule governing them.

artifacts.name: Screening Provider Agreements
artifacts.description: The agreement with the background check provider including its data protection clauses, the vendor agreements for background verification services, the documentation of jurisdictional legal constraints affecting screening scope, and the government mandate compliance evidence where screening is legally directed.

artifacts.name: Security Role Appointments
artifacts.description: The letters or electronic appointments formally assigning security roles, the job descriptions for the security function explicitly listing security duties, the organisation chart showing reporting lines for the security function and its independence from technology operations, the matrix mapping security activities to roles marked responsible, accountable, consulted and informed, and the signed acceptance forms showing named risk owners have formally accepted residual risks.

artifacts.name: AI Role Allocation Records
artifacts.description: The charter defining AI roles and responsibilities across risk management, impact assessments and asset and resource management; the responsibility matrix mapping AI activities to accountable roles; and the communications and appointment letters allocating those roles to specific persons.

artifacts.name: AI Competence Records
artifacts.description: The competence matrix mapping AI-related roles to required education, training, experience and skill level; the updated job descriptions specifying those requirements; the training records; and the records evaluating the effectiveness of the competence actions taken.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Records
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures covering AI, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the AI impact assessment, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, and the documented evidence demonstrating the outcome.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Records
artifacts.description: The segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records, the business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, and the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Screening Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit; the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records; and the data classification scheme determining which provider roles require screening.

HRS-04.1.notes: 53 asks across 11 frameworks. Screening for sensitive roles, the formal appointment of security roles and AI-specific competence are three separable obligations; ISO 27001 A.5.2 role appointment arrives through the crosswalk and is kept apart from screening.

artifacts.name: Employment Contract with Security Clauses
artifacts.description: The standard contract template with security, confidentiality and intellectual property clauses baked in; the sample redacted contract showing those clauses in the terms and conditions of employment; the sample redacted signed contracts; the signed employment agreements with information security clauses; the standardised terms and conditions document; the employment contract templates with security clause samples; and the annual legal review record of the clauses. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented employment agreement content and process requirements.

artifacts.name: Confidentiality Agreements
artifacts.description: The employee non-disclosure agreement whether separate from or attached to the employment contract, the signed terms and conditions and non-disclosure agreements, and the retention records for the signed set.

artifacts.name: Contractor and Third-Party Agreements
artifacts.description: The agreement template used for contractors and agency staff carrying equivalent obligations, the third-party and contractor agreements, the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records. HITRUST requires the approved terms and conditions of employment policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy and Enforcement
artifacts.description: The documented acceptable use policy for end-user technologies including the explicit approval requirement and the list of acceptable uses, the rules of behaviour document, the acceptable use guidelines, the distribution and acknowledgment records, the user acknowledgment records, the employee acknowledgement captured at onboarding, and the endpoint or device management configuration enforcing it technically. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented acceptable use and compliance user responsibility requirements.

artifacts.name: Policy Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The policy acknowledgment forms, the acceptable usage policy acknowledgement records, the records of personnel acknowledging their information security responsibilities, and the awareness communications and training records demonstrating personnel awareness of them.

artifacts.name: Role Definition and Onboarding Records
artifacts.description: The sections of the information security policy defining security roles and responsibilities, the sample job descriptions with their information security sections, the performance review templates including information security objectives, the human resources onboarding and role-change checklist, the information security briefing session records, and the induction attendance or checklist signed by new hires confirming a briefing before access.

artifacts.name: Management Commitment Records
artifacts.description: The signed leadership statement committing to enforce security policies and provide resources, the management review meeting minutes with directives to staff, and the guidance issued to line managers on enforcing policy in their teams.

artifacts.name: Code of Conduct and Governance Records
artifacts.description: The code of conduct or ethics policy with the employee acknowledgment records, the board minutes demonstrating oversight, and the disciplinary action records for conduct violations.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the mail encryption configuration; the managed transfer platform log showing encrypted transfers and recipients; the transfer agreement templates; and the courier chain-of-custody receipts for physical media.

artifacts.name: Workstation Use Controls
artifacts.description: The workstation use policy with the placement and screen privacy requirements governing where and how equipment may be used.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, individual contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts including posters, newsletters, e-learning and intranet content; and the attendance and completion records across the workforce.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data on Public Systems
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence controlling regulated data on publicly accessible systems, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating.

HRS-05.notes: 65 asks across 12 frameworks. Overlaps HRS-05.7; what is distinct here is the contract and its clauses rather than the acknowledgement of them. ISO 27001 A.5.14 information transfer arrives here through an odd crosswalk and is kept separate rather than dissolved into employment terms.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy / Rules of Behavior
artifacts.description: The approved, current-version document defining acceptable and unacceptable use of organizational technology, systems, data and networks, and the consequences of violating it. Must state scope and applicability (employees, contractors, third parties), roles and responsibilities, the technologies covered (end-user devices, email, internet, removable media, browser extensions, AI systems), explicit approval requirements for use, the list of company-approved products and technologies, workstation use expectations, and handling rules for sensitive/regulated data (ePHI, CUI, cardholder data). Must carry version history, review frequency, and management or board approval signature. Frameworks differ on packaging: PCI DSS wants a distinct end-user technology AUP naming approved products; HIPAA and DoH ADHIE want workstation-use rules included; NIST 800-53 calls it a rules-of-behavior document; HITRUST wants both an approved policy/standard and a documented procedure implementing it; NIST AI RMF expects it extended to AI use with step-by-step instructions, control points and exception handling.

artifacts.name: Rules of Behavior Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Signed or electronically captured acknowledgements from every employee, contractor and third-party user confirming they have read, understood and agree to abide by the rules of behavior, captured before system access is granted. Must be traceable to a named individual, a date, and a specific policy version, and cover the whole in-scope population rather than a sample. Frameworks add: PCI DSS wants both distribution records and acknowledgement of individual information security responsibilities; SOC 2 wants code-of-conduct acknowledgement; ADHICS and DoH ADHIE want signed records tied to the current approved version; NIST 800-53 requires re-acknowledgement by anyone who signed a superseded version.

artifacts.name: Policy Review and Re-Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the rules of behavior and the employment/agreement clauses that carry them are reviewed and updated on the organization's defined frequency, and that users re-acknowledge after material change. Must show the review date, reviewer and approver, observations, changes made or a no-change decision, corrective actions, and the resulting version. ISO 27001 asks specifically for an annual legal review of security clauses in employment documents; ADHICS, HITRUST and DoH ADHIE ask for periodic review records including compliance review of signed agreements; SL CSF asks for policy review records. Where the defined frequency is other than annual, state and evidence the frequency actually applied.

artifacts.name: Code of Conduct and Management Commitment Evidence
artifacts.description: The organization's code of conduct/ethics policy plus evidence that leadership actively backs and oversees behavioral expectations: a signed management commitment statement undertaking to enforce security policies and provide resources, and minutes of board or management review meetings showing oversight of conduct and ISMS performance and any directives issued to staff. Minutes must be dated, name attendees, and record the decisions or directions given.

artifacts.name: Employment Contracts and Confidentiality Agreements with Security Clauses
artifacts.description: The standard employment contract template and redacted signed examples showing that security, confidentiality, intellectual property and acceptable-use obligations are embedded in the terms and conditions of employment, together with the standalone employee NDA where confidentiality is handled separately. Must show scope, term, confidentiality obligations, the user's security responsibilities, and signatures of both parties. HITRUST additionally wants both an approved terms-and-conditions-of-employment policy and the procedure or work instruction that implements it; DoH ADHIE requires an authorized-user agreement template carrying all six of its mandated clauses (including breach notification and right to audit).

artifacts.name: Contractor and Third-Party Agreements with Equivalent Obligations
artifacts.description: Agreements used for contractors, agency staff and third parties that impose behavioral and security obligations equivalent to those placed on employees, plus the records showing those parties are risk-assessed and monitored on an ongoing basis. Agreements must include security clauses, SLAs, right-to-audit and breach-notification provisions and be signed by both parties; monitoring records must show what was assessed, when, by whom, the findings, management responses and remediation tracking.

artifacts.name: Onboarding Security Briefing and Access Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that individuals receive a security briefing and are bound by the rules of behavior before access is granted: induction attendance records or signed onboarding checklists for new hires, and access provisioning records that link each grant back to the signed policy acknowledgement for that person. Records must show date, performer, approver, and traceability from the access request to the acknowledgement. HITRUST extends this to provisioning, modification and periodic review records for the same population.

artifacts.name: Awareness Training Records and Materials
artifacts.description: The awareness content used to communicate the rules of behavior and the records proving it reached the workforce. Content includes training modules and decks, the topic coverage matrix showing which behavioral requirements each module addresses, awareness communications about the disciplinary consequences of misuse, posters/newsletters/intranet material, and guidance issued to line managers on enforcing the rules in their teams. Records include LMS completion and attendance reports covering employees and contractors, with delivery dates, attendee lists, module references, completion status and, where assessed, effectiveness. ISO 42001 requires the programme to also cover AI policy, each individual's contribution, and the implications of non-conformance; PCI DSS and HITRUST require evidence that personnel were informed of their specific responsibilities.

artifacts.name: Disciplinary Process and Violation Case Records
artifacts.description: The documented disciplinary/sanctions process that defines the consequences of unacceptable behavior, and sanitized case records showing it has actually been applied. The process must give step-by-step handling instructions, responsible roles, control points and exception handling; SL CSF additionally asks for violation-handling procedures. Case records must include detected violations of the acceptable use rules, the action taken, dates, performer and approver, and the linkage from the triggering incident to the disciplinary outcome. Redact personal data before submission.

artifacts.name: Roles, Responsibilities and Segregation of Duties Matrix
artifacts.description: Documentation defining who is responsible for what in relation to acceptable use and information security: the roles-and-responsibilities section of the information security policy covering all personnel, a segregation of duties matrix identifying conflicting duties, and a role-to-permission access control matrix for the in-scope systems. Must identify owners, cover all relevant roles and systems, flag conflicts of interest, and carry a last-updated date.

artifacts.name: Technology Use Enforcement Configuration and Approved Technology Inventory
artifacts.description: Evidence that the rules of behavior are enforced technically, not just written down. Covers MDM/endpoint policy configuration implementing the AUP (removable media controls, application allow-listing), the approved browser extension list with the restriction configuration enforcing it and extension audit reports, DLP policy configuration with supporting monitoring output, access rights enforcement configuration on workstations, the login banner presented to users reminding them of acceptable use obligations, and the asset inventory register showing classification, ownership, location and lifecycle status for the assets covered by the policy. Configuration evidence must be a dated extract, export or screenshot identifying the system and the reviewer; the approved-technology and extension lists are human-maintained and must be current and owned.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Policy and Secure Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The policy and procedures governing how users may move information out of the organization, plus proof they are followed. The policy must define authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approval steps; procedures must cover each specific method in use (SFTP, secure email, encrypted removable media, managed file transfer). Supporting records: the standard data transfer / data sharing agreement template used with third parties, a managed file transfer log export showing encrypted transfers and recipients, the mail gateway TLS/S-MIME/PGP configuration enforcing encryption on external mail, and signed chain-of-custody receipts for physical media moved by approved couriers.

artifacts.name: Clean Desk and Workstation Use Safeguards
artifacts.description: The clean desk policy and its implementing procedures, together with evidence that workstation-level behavioral safeguards are in place: workstation placement and screen privacy requirements, and evidence of the physical safeguards actually applied (privacy screens, positioning, lock-away storage, screen lock expectations). Records must show the requirement, where it applies, and dated evidence of implementation, including in cloud/remote working settings where CSA CCM requires the practice to be demonstrated in the operating environment.

artifacts.name: Public-Facing Content Posting Controls and Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of the rules and operating records controlling what users may post to publicly accessible systems, specifically preventing regulated information (CUI) from being published. Must include the documented restriction and designation of who is authorised to post, plus records showing publicly accessible content is reviewed for regulated information and that anything improperly posted is removed, with dates and the reviewer identified.

artifacts.name: AI System Use and Safety Documentation
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are in scope of the rules of behavior, the documentation supporting a critical-thinking and safety-first posture: an AI impact assessment covering the likelihood and magnitude of beneficial and harmful impacts (scope, criteria, methodology, findings, risk ratings, recommendations, treatment decisions); context documentation stating intended purposes, deployment settings, users and assumptions, version-controlled, dated, approved and traceable to the specific AI system and lifecycle stage; safety evaluation records covering fail-safe behavior, residual risk and real-time monitoring; and dated outcome artifacts naming the owner and the related policy or process.

HRS-05.1.notes: Single control in batch12. 101 manual evidence entries across 16 sources collapse to 15 artifacts. The bulk is one document (an Acceptable Use Policy / Rules of Behavior) requested 17 different ways, plus its acknowledgement, review and enforcement records. Automated list is empty, so nothing is genuinely collected today; items marked hybrid/automated are ones a connector (MDM, browser management, DLP, IAM, LMS/HRIS, mail gateway, MFT) could supply part of.

artifacts.name: Social Media Policy
artifacts.description: The social media policy, the forum usage procedure, and the acceptable use restrictions on organisational mail governing what personnel may publish.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining permitted and prohibited uses of technology resources, mail, internet and data; the acceptable use policy; and the rules of behaviour document. HITRUST requires the approved acceptable use of assets policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Policy Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The signed or electronically acknowledged records from employees and contractors, the employee acknowledgement captured at onboarding, the user acknowledgment records, and the training module completion report.

artifacts.name: Violation Records
artifacts.description: The redacted records of violations detected with the actions taken and the login banner reminding users of their obligations.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data on Public Systems
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence controlling regulated data on publicly accessible systems, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating, and the mail classification tooling supporting it.

artifacts.name: Employment Terms and Agreements
artifacts.description: The standard contract template with security, confidentiality and intellectual property clauses; the sample redacted signed contracts; the sample redacted contract showing the clauses in the terms and conditions of employment; the employee non-disclosure agreement; the agreement template used for contractors and agency staff; and the annual legal review record of those clauses.

artifacts.name: Management Commitment Records
artifacts.description: The signed leadership statement committing to enforce security policies and provide resources, the management review meeting minutes with directives to staff, the guidance issued to line managers on enforcing policy, and the induction attendance or checklist signed by new hires confirming a security briefing before access.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, individual contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts; and the attendance and completion records across the workforce.

artifacts.name: Asset Inventory and Review Records
artifacts.description: The asset inventory register with classification, the awareness communications informing personnel of the acceptable use requirements, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

HRS-05.2.notes: 33 asks across 6 frameworks. Overlaps HRS-05.3; what is distinct here is the social media and public-forum restriction specifically, kept separate from the general acceptable use policy it sits inside.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining permitted and prohibited uses of technology resources, mail, internet and data; the documented acceptable use policy for end-user technologies including the explicit approval requirement and list of acceptable uses; the acceptable usage policy document; the internet services usage policy; the rules of behaviour document; and the acceptable use guidelines. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented acceptable use of technology requirement. HITRUST requires the approved acceptable use of assets policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Policy Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The signed or electronically acknowledged records from employees and contractors, the employee acknowledgement captured at onboarding, the signed user acknowledgements, the acceptable usage policy acknowledgement records, the user acknowledgment records, the records of policy distribution and personnel acknowledgments, and the communication evidence to employees and contractors.

artifacts.name: Technical Enforcement Configuration
artifacts.description: The device management or endpoint policy configuration enforcing the policy technically through removable-media controls and application allow-listing, the address filtering policy, the proxy block list including public web-mail, and the web filtering and cloud access security controls.

artifacts.name: Use Restriction Awareness
artifacts.description: The training module completion report, the acceptable usage awareness material, the awareness course modules covering internet and mail use, the login banner reminding users of their obligations, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the restrictions.

artifacts.name: Violation Records
artifacts.description: The redacted records of violations detected with the actions taken and the violation handling procedures they invoke.

artifacts.name: Policy Review Records
artifacts.description: The policy review records, the periodic review records naming the reviewer, and the asset inventory register with classification the restrictions are scoped against.

artifacts.name: Employment Terms and Agreements
artifacts.description: The standard contract template with security, confidentiality and intellectual property clauses; the sample redacted signed contracts; the sample redacted contract showing the clauses in the terms and conditions of employment; the employee non-disclosure agreement; the agreement template used for contractors and agency staff; and the annual legal review record of those clauses.

artifacts.name: Management Commitment Records
artifacts.description: The signed leadership statement committing to enforce security policies and provide resources, the management review meeting minutes with directives to staff, the guidance issued to line managers on enforcing policy in their teams, and the induction attendance or checklist signed by new hires confirming a security briefing before access.

artifacts.name: Workstation Use Controls
artifacts.description: The workstation use policy with its placement and screen privacy requirements governing where and how equipment may be used.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, individual contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts; and the attendance and completion records across the workforce.

HRS-05.3.notes: 51 asks across 11 frameworks. Overlaps HRS-05 and HRS-05.7; what is distinct here is the technical enforcement of the use restrictions rather than the policy or its acknowledgement, so the endpoint and filtering artifacts are kept separate from the policy set.

artifacts.name: Policy Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The signed acknowledgements confirming personnel have read and understood the policies that apply to them, the employee acknowledgement records, the user acknowledgment records, and the signed statements retained against each person. DoH ADHIE requires the statement template to reference the policy and participant agreement, with records retained.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy and Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: The acceptable usage policy document, the signed acknowledgements, the communication evidence to employees and contractors, the periodic review records, and the access provisioning records linked to the signed policy so access is not granted before acknowledgement.

artifacts.name: Employment Terms Acknowledgement
artifacts.description: The standardised terms and conditions of employment document, the signed employment agreements with information security clauses, the third-party and contractor agreements, and the retention records for the signed terms.

artifacts.name: Policy Repository and Communication
artifacts.description: The policy repository or intranet where the current versions are published, the communications and notifications to employees regarding policy changes with their acknowledgements, and the policy review records evidencing the published set is current.

artifacts.name: Security Briefing Records
artifacts.description: The information security briefing session records, the role orientation documentation, the manager sign-off records, the access request forms, and the security briefing records captured at onboarding and role change.

artifacts.name: Awareness Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The approved awareness training curriculum, the learning management system completion records evidencing training on hire and at least annually, the attendance and acknowledgement records, the post-training assessments, and the phishing simulation results with remediation activity.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Training Records
artifacts.description: The approved training plan and curriculum for the roles in scope covering security risks and controls, the matrix mapping roles to mandatory modules and refresher cadence, the completion records within the required timeframes, and the effectiveness assessment.

artifacts.name: Access Training Certification Records
artifacts.description: The training programme curriculum covering the required access topics, the trainee acknowledgement records of topic coverage, the signed training certifications, the course materials, and the certification storage and retention evidence.

artifacts.name: Domain Policy Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: The approved physical and environmental security policy and the clear desk and clear screen policy with their top management approval, roles and responsibilities matrices, review records, audit records and signed acknowledgements — the domain-specific policies personnel must separately confirm.

artifacts.name: Privacy Complaint and Officer Records
artifacts.description: The privacy officer designation documentation with the job description, the complaint handling procedures, and the designation of the contact person for complaints that personnel are made aware of.

artifacts.name: Knowledge and Background Verification
artifacts.description: The records of verifying appropriate knowledge and background through assessment or pre-hire screening, confirming familiarity is established before responsibilities are assigned.

artifacts.name: Violation Handling Procedures
artifacts.description: The violation handling procedures that the acknowledged policies invoke, establishing what follows a breach of the terms personnel have accepted.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, individual contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts; and the attendance and completion records.

artifacts.name: Management Responsibility Records
artifacts.description: The approved standard on management responsibilities with its implementing procedure, the awareness communications, and the third-party agreements and risk assessment records extending the acknowledgement obligation to provider personnel.

HRS-05.7.notes: 68 asks across 9 frameworks. The demand is narrow — that each person has read and acknowledged the policies that bind them — so the artifacts are grouped by which policy set is acknowledged rather than by framework.

artifacts.name: Access Agreement Templates
artifacts.description: The access agreement templates, the access rights statement template, the non-disclosure agreement documentation, and the standard employment contract templates and security clause samples carrying equivalent access obligations.

artifacts.name: Signed Access Agreements
artifacts.description: The signed access agreements, the signed terms and conditions and non-disclosure agreements, the signed employment agreements with information security clauses, the signed employment agreements, the policy acknowledgment forms, the retention records for the signed terms, and the agreement review records confirming they are re-signed when required. HITRUST requires the approved terms and conditions of employment policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Authorised User Agreement Records
artifacts.description: The authorised user agreement template containing all six required clauses, the signed authorised user agreements, the signed agreement records, the acknowledgement records, the issuance records to authorised users, the acknowledgement of receipt records, and the periodic agreement compliance review records.

artifacts.name: Authorised User Obligations Statements
artifacts.description: The statement template referencing the governing policy and participant agreement, the signed obligations statements from authorised users, the records retention for the signed statements, the signed training certifications, and the certification storage and retention evidence.

artifacts.name: Agreement Register
artifacts.description: The agreement register with renewal dates and the agreement compliance acknowledgements recorded against each entry.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy and Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: The policy defining permitted and prohibited uses of technology resources, mail, internet and data; the signed or electronically acknowledged records from employees and contractors; the training module completion report; the login banner reminding users of their acceptable use obligations; and the redacted records of violations detected with the actions taken.

artifacts.name: Onboarding and Briefing Records
artifacts.description: The human resources onboarding and role-change checklist, the information security briefing session records, and the standardised terms and conditions of employment document presented at that point.

artifacts.name: Authentication and Access Control Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering user authentication, access provisioning, multi-factor authentication and acceptable use acknowledgement; the configuration evidence for authentication commensurate with information classification; and the register showing security-management staff duties do not create conflicts of interest.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Access Agreements
artifacts.description: The third-party and contractor agreements, the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records. HITRUST requires the approved policy and standard on addressing security when dealing with external parties with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Accountability Framework Records
artifacts.description: The accountability framework documentation, the performance evaluation criteria including security responsibilities, the incentive and reward programme documentation tied to control objectives, and the security performance dashboards and reports.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the mail encryption configuration; the managed transfer platform log; the transfer agreement templates; and the courier chain-of-custody receipts.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, individual contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts; and the attendance and completion records across the workforce.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the access agreement requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

HRS-06.notes: 63 asks across 10 frameworks. Distinct from HRS-05 and HRS-05.7 in that the object is the access agreement signed as a condition of being granted access, not the employment contract. DoH ADHIE contributes a prescriptive six-clause authorised-user agreement kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Non-Disclosure Agreement Templates
artifacts.description: The standard template covering duration, scope and breach consequences, the variant library for mutual, one-way and project-specific contexts, the access agreement templates, and the annual legal review confirming the templates remain enforceable. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Signed Employee Confidentiality Agreements
artifacts.description: The repository of signed agreements from all personnel, the signed terms and conditions captured at onboarding or role change, the policy acknowledgement records, and the onboarding and role-change checklist evidencing the agreement is obtained before access is granted.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Confidentiality Agreements
artifacts.description: The register of agreements signed with contractors, consultants, vendors and business partners; the signed information exchange agreements; the templates used; and the register with renewal dates. ADHICS requires right-to-audit clauses in the same agreements.

artifacts.name: Agreement Renewal and Review Records
artifacts.description: The renewal and reissue log showing agreements refreshed as scopes or terms change, the agreement review records, the compliance acknowledgements, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Contract Clause Coverage Checklist
artifacts.description: The checklist confirming the required provisions are present in each agreement, sample vendor contracts containing them, and the supplier agreements carrying the security, data-protection, audit-rights and notification clauses.

artifacts.name: Right-to-Audit Clauses and Exercise Records
artifacts.description: Sample executed provider contracts containing the organisation's and the regulator's contractual right to audit the provider's security controls, the legal function sign-off confirming every contract carries compliant confidentiality and audit provisions, and the records of audit rights actually exercised with engagement letters, reports and findings.

artifacts.name: Audit Confidentiality Controls
artifacts.description: The procedures protecting sensitive information during audits, the non-disclosure agreements executed with auditors, and the evidence of least-privilege access and data masking or watermarking applied to audit data.

artifacts.name: Human Resources Security Policy
artifacts.description: The approved human resources security policy with its review and approval records, the background verification process documentation, the roles and responsibilities matrix, the job descriptions carrying security duties, and the disciplinary process the confidentiality obligation is enforced through.

artifacts.name: Health Information Protection Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy with its access criteria, ownership and sharing requirements; the documented non-disclosure obligations specific to health information; and the references to the disciplinary process and applicable government sanctions.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the email encryption configuration; the managed transfer platform log; the data transfer agreement templates; and the courier chain-of-custody receipts.

artifacts.name: Data Exchange Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The data-exchange risk assessments performed before an exchange arrangement is entered, and the outsourcing agreements carrying the data security clauses that follow from them.

artifacts.name: Vendor Compliance Monitoring
artifacts.description: The vendor audits and compliance monitoring reports evidencing the confidentiality obligations in the agreements are actually being met.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, each person's contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts used; and the attendance and completion records across the workforce.

artifacts.name: Accountability and Performance Records
artifacts.description: The accountability framework, the performance evaluation criteria including security responsibilities, the incentive documentation tied to control objectives, the responsibility assignment records, and the security KPI dashboards reported against them.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the confidentiality requirements and the obligations their signed agreement places on them.

HRS-06.1.notes: 76 asks across 12 frameworks. Employee non-disclosure agreements and third-party confidentiality clauses are separated because they are held by different functions, renewed on different cycles and tested separately.

artifacts.name: Disciplinary Policy
artifacts.description: The formal disciplinary policy covering security violations with fair process and graduated sanctions, the written sanction policy, the progressive discipline procedures, the penalty guidelines, and the process flowchart showing the stages from investigation to hearing to outcome. HITRUST requires the approved disciplinary process standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Disciplinary Case Records
artifacts.description: The redacted case records showing the process applied to security breaches, the disciplinary action records, the records of sanctions applied, the case handling records, the enforcement case records, and the sanction outcomes with their tracking.

artifacts.name: Violation Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The violation investigation procedures, the investigation and remediation evidence, the staff accountability records, the incident-to-action linkage records connecting a security event to the personnel consequence, and the evidence collection standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: HR and Security Coordination Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure describing how security investigations feed into disciplinary action, establishing the handoff between the function that detects a violation and the function that sanctions it.

artifacts.name: Workforce Acknowledgement of Sanctions
artifacts.description: The workforce acknowledgement of the sanction policy, the employee handbook extract covering the disciplinary process with its acknowledgement records, the policy acknowledgement records from employees and third parties, and the communication explaining the disciplinary consequences of security breaches.

artifacts.name: Human Resources Security Policy
artifacts.description: The approved human resources security policy with its review and approval records, the background verification process documentation, the roles and responsibilities matrix, and the signed non-disclosure agreements the sanctions enforce.

artifacts.name: Health Information Protection Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy with its access criteria, ownership and sharing requirements; the documented non-disclosure obligations; and the references to the disciplinary process and applicable government sanctions.

artifacts.name: Policy Inventory and Compliance Monitoring
artifacts.description: The IT policy inventory with its approval records, the annual policy review documentation, the policy communication and acknowledgment evidence, and the policy compliance monitoring results that surface the violations sanctions respond to.

artifacts.name: Incident Response and Register
artifacts.description: The incident response plan with classification, escalation and notification timelines, and the incident register with its case records, providing the source from which disciplinary matters arise.

artifacts.name: Incident Root Cause and Responsibility Fixing
artifacts.description: The root cause analysis reports for reported incidents including findings, corrective actions, preventive actions and responsibility determination; the records demonstrating responsibility-fixing outcomes where applicable; the recurrence prevention tracker with owners and status; the regulator incident reporting procedure; and sample notifications demonstrating timely and complete submission.

artifacts.name: Access Misuse Prevention Records
artifacts.description: The approved standard for preventing misuse of information assets with its implementing procedure, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Accountability and Performance Records
artifacts.description: The accountability framework, the performance evaluation criteria including security responsibilities, the incentive documentation tied to control objectives, and the security KPI dashboards reported against them.

artifacts.name: AI Awareness Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI awareness programme covering the AI policy, individual contribution and the implications of non-conformance; the communication artifacts; and the attendance and completion records.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the disciplinary process and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

HRS-07.notes: 70 asks across 11 frameworks. The disciplinary policy and the record of it being applied are separated because an assessor accepts a policy as design evidence but requires case records as operating evidence, and most organisations have the first without the second.

artifacts.name: Transfer Procedure
artifacts.description: The internal transfer and role change procedure, the transfer access review procedures, the transfer authorisation documentation, the human resources transfer notification process, the joiner-mover-leaver workflow, and the communication protocol for employment exit and role change. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-regulated-data-during-personnel-actions requirement; CSA CCM likewise for the user access changes and revocation requirement. HITRUST requires the approved termination or change of responsibilities policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Transfer Access Records
artifacts.description: The access reassignment records, the authorisation records for the new role's privileges, the access modification records, the access modification request forms with their manager approval documentation, the before-and-after access comparison, the access removal logs, the account audit reports, the joiner-mover-leaver synchronisation evidence, and the records showing access rights reviewed and adjusted when staff change roles internally.

artifacts.name: Revocation Timeliness Records
artifacts.description: The timestamped log confirming access removed from each system, the access termination workflow records with timing metrics against the agreed service level, the access revocation records, and the account deactivation logs.

artifacts.name: Handover and Knowledge Transfer
artifacts.description: The handover documentation templates, the knowledge transfer checklists and records, and the role change notifications to stakeholders.

artifacts.name: Offboarding Checklist and Asset Return
artifacts.description: The comprehensive leaver checklist covering access revocation, asset return and exit briefing; the exit checklist; the asset return checklist; the equipment return documentation; the termination checklist and procedures; the termination procedure; the termination and exit procedure documentation; and the termination responsibility assignments.

artifacts.name: Exit Interview Records
artifacts.description: The exit interview forms covering reminders of continuing obligations, the exit interview records, the standard letter sent to leavers reminding them of ongoing obligations, and the contract clauses surviving termination.

artifacts.name: Accountability Framework Records
artifacts.description: The accountability framework documentation, the performance evaluation criteria including security responsibilities, the incentive and reward programme documentation tied to control objectives, and the security performance dashboards and reports.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of their responsibilities on transfer and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

HRS-08.notes: 47 asks across 11 frameworks. Overlaps HRS-09 and IAC-07.1; what is distinct here is the transfer itself — the reassignment record showing old access removed as new access is granted, which neither a joiner nor a leaver record captures.

artifacts.name: Termination Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented termination and exit procedure, the offboarding procedures, the access termination procedure document, the termination checklist and procedures, the joiner-mover-leaver workflow, the documented procedure for immediate access revocation upon termination with human resources and technology integration, the termination responsibility assignments, and the notification process from human resources to technology. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented employment termination requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the protect-regulated-data-during-personnel-actions requirement.

artifacts.name: Access Revocation Records
artifacts.description: The timestamped log confirming access removed from each system on termination, the access revocation logs for terminated personnel, the access removal logs, the account deactivation logs, the audit trail of disabled accounts, the audit logs evidencing termination-driven account disablement, the sample termination tickets with timestamps showing immediate revocation, the sample of terminated users verified as disabled, and the termination workflow records.

artifacts.name: Revocation Timeliness Metrics
artifacts.description: The time-to-revoke metrics with their supporting audit logs, the access termination workflow records with timing metrics against the agreed service level, the timeliness comparison of termination date against account disable date, and the timeliness verification records.

artifacts.name: Offboarding Checklist
artifacts.description: The comprehensive leaver checklist covering access revocation, asset return and exit briefing; the exit checklist; the termination access revocation checklist; and the asset return checklist.

artifacts.name: Asset Return Records
artifacts.description: The equipment return documentation and the property return records evidencing organisational assets were recovered at exit.

artifacts.name: Exit Interview Records
artifacts.description: The exit interview forms covering reminders of continuing obligations, the exit interview documentation, the exit interview records, the standard letter sent to leavers reminding them of ongoing obligations, and the contract clauses surviving termination covering confidentiality and, where lawful, restraint.

artifacts.name: Handover and Knowledge Transfer
artifacts.description: The handover documentation templates, the knowledge transfer checklists and records, and the communication protocol for employment exit notifying the parties who need to know.

artifacts.name: Role Change Offboarding Records
artifacts.description: The records showing access rights reviewed and adjusted when staff change roles internally, applying the same discipline to movers as to leavers.

artifacts.name: Regulator Notification Records
artifacts.description: The communication records with the health sector regulator covering personnel departures the regulator must be told about.

artifacts.name: Accountability Framework Records
artifacts.description: The accountability framework documentation, the performance evaluation criteria including security responsibilities, the incentive and reward programme documentation tied to control objectives, and the security performance dashboards and reports.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of their termination responsibilities and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved termination or change of responsibilities policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

HRS-09.notes: 55 asks across 14 frameworks. Access revocation, asset return and the exit briefing are three separate proofs; the timeliness metric is kept separate from the revocation records because it is the measure an assessor samples against and is frequently absent.

artifacts.name: Separation of Duties Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved policy and its implementing procedure establishing that incompatible duties are identified and separated. Must define the principle, name the accountable owner, state how conflicts are identified and resolved, and set the review cadence. Financial-sector frameworks additionally require it to address fraud prevention (QCB) and to cover authentication and access provisioning in the same instrument (SBP ETGRMF); SOX expects a named SoD framework; PCI DSS expects a role separation standard covering production versus pre-production. NIST 800-171 and CSA CCM accept either the documented policy or configuration evidence in its place.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix of incompatible activity pairs (request vs approve, develop vs deploy, prepare vs post) mapped to roles and to the systems where each pair is enforced. Must identify the conflicting roles explicitly rather than list roles generically. MAS TRM requires the CI/CD pipeline to be covered; HITRUST and MAS TRM also expect the underlying role-to-permission or RBAC mapping; SOC 2 CC5.1 expects the matrix to tie back to the risks the control activities address; SBP ETGRMF requires a register showing security-management staff carry no conflicting duties.

artifacts.name: SoD Enforcement Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration proving the matrix is enforced by the systems rather than only documented: ERP/IAM SoD ruleset exports (SAP GRC, SailPoint), workflow definitions showing dual-control or four-eyes approval on sensitive processes, CI/CD pipeline configuration allowing only reviewed and approved changes into production, and reconciliation and journal-entry application settings enforcing preparer/approver segregation. QCB also requires evidence that change implementers are competent for the change they perform.

artifacts.name: SoD Conflict and Violation Report
artifacts.description: The periodic report of detected conflicts: each violation, its owner, the mitigation status and management sign-off. Typically GRC-tool output. SOX additionally expects trend analysis across periods and evidence that identified conflicts are tracked through to remediation; PCI DSS expects a periodic audit confirming production and pre-production role separation; ISO 27001 and SL CSF expect the completed access recertification that surfaces the conflicts.

artifacts.name: Compensating Controls and SoD Exception Register
artifacts.description: Where full separation is not feasible, the documented compensating control (for example independent review of sensitive transactions) together with the approved exception, its owner, expiry date and the reason separation cannot be achieved. Frameworks are consistent that an accepted conflict without a recorded compensating control is a finding, not an exception.

artifacts.name: Production Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that developers hold no direct production access, or that a compensating control operates where they do: production access control lists, developer versus migrator privilege reports, and review of migration logs confirming the person who built a change did not move it to production.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning, Modification and Removal Records
artifacts.description: The operational record that access follows the approved matrix: provisioning requests with approvals, role-change records for movers, removal records for leavers against the target SLA, and authorization records for system access. ADHICS requires provisioning to be linked to the signed policy acknowledgement; NIST 800-171, NIST 800-53 and CSA CCM accept these records as demonstrating that duty separation is implemented and operating, with CSA CCM scoping it to the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access and Activity Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: Records covering privileged use rather than privileged assignment: just-in-time privileged access requests and approvals from the PAM platform, monitoring logs and alerts for administrator activity, the SIEM use-case library for detecting unusual or unauthorised activity, transaction and journal-entry audit trails, and the MFA/strong-authentication configuration commensurate with information classification.

artifacts.name: Security Function Independence Evidence
artifacts.description: Organisational proof that the security function is separated from the function it oversees: the charter or terms of reference establishing its mandate, the order or notification establishing it as distinct from IT/ICT, the organisation chart showing the reporting line, the appointment order and job description for the function lead, and a documented assessment confirming no conflict of interest with IT/ICT. SBP ETGRMF requires this at board-resolution level for CISO independence; PISF 2026 requires steering-committee approval of the role assignments and the approval minutes.

artifacts.name: Acceptable Use Policy and Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: The current Acceptable Use Policy governing use of internal systems, together with signed user acknowledgements captured at first login or on annual re-acknowledgement, and the records of the security briefing at which it was communicated.

artifacts.name: Independent Procurement Function Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that procurement is separated from the functions that request and approve spend: the charter establishing an independent procurement unit, its organisation chart, the procedure governing procurement by scope, level and size, and the IT steering committee minutes evidencing that governance in operation.

artifacts.name: End-User Computing Control Evidence
artifacts.description: For spreadsheets and other end-user computing tools in the financial reporting path: the formula validation and review checklist, sign-off by a reviewer independent of the preparer, records of errors identified and corrected, and the periodic re-validation schedule with evidence it was followed.

artifacts.name: Software Release Authorization Records
artifacts.description: Records showing releases are authorised by someone other than the person who developed them, covering the documented release process, the authorization record per release, and the DevSecOps controls applied within the pipeline.

artifacts.name: Network Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: Kept separate from the duty-separation artifacts because HITRUST 09.c addresses segregation in networks rather than of duties: the network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones, plus network device configuration baselines and the records of ruleset review.

HRS-11.notes: 123 asks across 14 frameworks merged into 14 artifacts. The frameworks split into four distinct demands that look alike in a raw list: the SoD ruleset itself, its technical enforcement, the periodic detection of violations, and organisational independence of the security and procurement functions. HITRUST 09.c also pulls in network segregation, which is a genuinely different artifact and is kept separate rather than folded into the SoD matrix.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix of conflicting activities with the enforcement approach per system, the segregation of duties matrix, the conflict matrix documentation, the identified conflicting roles documentation, the role conflict analysis, the segregation of duties policy and framework, and the segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records.

artifacts.name: Technical Enforcement Records
artifacts.description: The export from the resource planning or identity platform showing configured conflict rules and violations, the technical enforcement configuration evidence, the access control configuration, and the access review records confirming the configured rules hold.

artifacts.name: Conflict Detection and Remediation
artifacts.description: The periodic report listing detected conflicts with owners, mitigation status and sign-off; the internal audit report confirming compliance; and the access review records covering the conflicted populations.

artifacts.name: Compensating Controls Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented compensating controls where full segregation is not feasible, the compensating control documentation where applicable, the compensating controls for detected violations, the exception and compensating control documentation, and the evidence of dual-control or four-eyes approval for high-risk operational changes.

artifacts.name: Development and Production Separation
artifacts.description: The segregation policy prohibiting developer access to production, the access review records showing no developer holds production access, the production access restriction evidence, the developer against migrator access privilege reports, the migration log review for compliance, the access privilege reports per environment, the environment architecture diagram showing segregation, the environment configuration management documentation, and the data masking procedures for non-production use.

artifacts.name: Key Management Role Separation
artifacts.description: The cryptographic key management roles and responsibilities. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, and the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation.

HRS-12.notes: 34 asks across 7 frameworks. The conflict matrix, its technical enforcement and the compensating controls where enforcement is impossible are three proofs; developer access to production is a named conflict and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Skills Inventory and Gap Matrix
artifacts.description: The skills inventory mapping required competencies for governance, service delivery, security and risk management against current staff; the matrix of required skills by role mapped against competency levels; the headcount and skills matrix; the staffing plans and skills inventory; the prioritised asset list of required competencies; the skill and competency gap assessment reports; and the current job descriptions specifying the required expertise for each role.

artifacts.name: Certification Register
artifacts.description: The register of professional certifications held by staff with their renewal dates, the certification records for security personnel, the budget allocations and records of certifications obtained, the copies of relevant certifications and curricula vitae for post-holders, and the register of function-lead and critical roles with full-time status, qualifications and experience.

artifacts.name: Gap Remediation Plans
artifacts.description: The individual development plans addressing identified skills gaps, the individual development plans, the annual capacity building plan with skills targets linked to service delivery, the annual training plan, the internal skills development plan covering outsourced functions, the training and development programmes with their completion records, and the training programme records for skill development.

artifacts.name: Competence Evaluation Records
artifacts.description: The performance appraisal records, the performance evaluation records with their competency assessments, the service delivery performance trends, and the training completion records evidencing the plan was executed.

artifacts.name: Board Skills Oversight
artifacts.description: The report tabled at the board on the adequacy and currency of technology skills across the organisation and the employment or deployment orders confirming full-time deployment to security roles.

artifacts.name: Succession and Workforce Planning
artifacts.description: The documented succession plan for key positions, the succession planning documentation, the workforce plan, the capacity plan integrated with the annual budgeting process, and the reconciliation showing capacity requirements reflected in the budgets.

artifacts.name: Governance Structure Records
artifacts.description: The technology management framework documentation and policies, the organisational structure charts with technology roles and responsibilities, the responsibility matrices for technology processes, and the capability maturity assessments with their improvement plans.

artifacts.name: Tooling Inventory
artifacts.description: The tooling inventory covering the risk, vulnerability assessment and forensic capabilities the skills are meant to operate.

artifacts.name: Specialist Team Records
artifacts.description: The documented data science team specification with its compliance evidence, the implementation evidence demonstrating the outcome, the business intelligence dashboards and analytics use-case register, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

HRS-13.notes: 40 asks across 6 frameworks. The skills inventory, the gap it exposes and the plan that closes the gap are three proofs; the certification register is kept separate because it is the objective evidence behind a self-assessed inventory.

artifacts.name: Reporting Channel Documentation
artifacts.description: The formal incident reporting channel documentation, the incident reporting procedures, the reporting channels documentation, the reporting mechanism documentation, the security weakness reporting channel documentation, the designated point of contact records, and the escalation matrix routing what is reported. HITRUST requires the approved reporting information security events policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Weakness Reporting Records
artifacts.description: The weakness reporting procedure, the weakness reports received, the weakness reports register, and the code of conduct prohibiting exploitation of a discovered weakness. HITRUST requires the approved reporting security weaknesses policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Reporting Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness materials on reporting, the awareness records on incident reporting requirements, the awareness training records on weakness reporting, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the obligation.

artifacts.name: Whistleblower Channel
artifacts.description: The whistleblower policy and channel and the dispute and exception escalation logs providing a route outside the reporting line.

artifacts.name: Fraud Reporting Channels
artifacts.description: The fraud reporting channels, the investigation reports arising, and the mystery shopping or seeding records testing whether the channel works.

artifacts.name: Incident Register and Reports
artifacts.description: The incident register with its case records, the incident reports, the incident response plan with its classification, escalation and notification timelines, and the stakeholder and authority communication protocols.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Reporting Obligations
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records extending the reporting obligation to provider personnel.

HRS-15.notes: 33 asks across 4 frameworks. Overlaps IRO-11; what is distinct here is the personnel-side obligation to report — the channel they use, the awareness that tells them to, and the prohibition on exploiting a weakness instead.

artifacts.name: IAM & Access Control Policy with Approval and Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The approved, current-version access control and identity management policy - the single document nearly every framework restates. Must carry formal management or board approval with approver name, role and date, define scope and applicability, assign roles and responsibilities, state the access control model and the default-deny standard, and include version history. Additional content named by individual frameworks: information access management, workforce security across the employment lifecycle, least privilege requirements, and technical access control for systems holding regulated data. Review and update records with reviewer, date and changes captured are required, annually by several frameworks, and the policy must be demonstrably communicated - stakeholder acknowledgement records, user communication records and awareness communications with attendee lists and delivery dates.

artifacts.name: Access Control Procedures & Logical Access Standards
artifacts.description: The documented procedures and technical standards implementing the policy: how identification, authentication and authorisation are performed, the logical access rules (authentication, authorisation and session parameters) defined per system type, access authorisation procedures, and access rights management procedures covering the full lifecycle. Must include step-by-step instructions, the roles responsible at each step, control points and exception handling. Business process control documentation showing where access controls sit within operational processes is additionally required.

artifacts.name: Role Definitions & Access Control Matrix
artifacts.description: The access control matrix mapping each role or job classification to the specific system and application permissions it carries, with role-based access criteria documented and role owners identified. Must cover all relevant systems in scope. One framework requires the segregation of duties matrix and the associated access privilege records to be maintained alongside it so conflicting role combinations are visible.

artifacts.name: IAM System, Directory & Identity Inventory
artifacts.description: Evidence of the IAM function and the systems it operates: the inventory of access control, authentication and authorisation systems (directory services, IAM platforms, native OS controls, application IAM, AAA solutions), the directory service configuration, and the coverage mapping showing every in-scope system component is governed by at least one of them, including integration coverage reports for systems federated to the central identity provider. Must be accompanied by the identity inventory itself - user, service and system identities under governance - the list of authorised system authenticator types, and the IT asset inventory with classification identifying what those identities reach. Periodic review records confirming the inventory remains complete are required.

artifacts.name: Service, System, Default & Third-Party Account Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented account management practices plus the records proving they operate for non-human and externally held accounts. Must cover: the inventory of system and service accounts with owner and purpose, the monitoring and periodic review of those accounts, the inventory of accounts capable of interactive login with the configuration preventing such login where possible and monitoring or alerting where it is permitted, the default account management procedure with audit results showing vendor default accounts were removed, disabled or had their credentials changed, and the access control procedures and monitoring records covering service provider access to the environment.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning, Modification & Revocation Records
artifacts.description: Lifecycle records for identity changes: access request and approval forms with the business justification, the minimum-necessary determination behind each grant, the request-approve-provision workflow evidence, the audit log of role changes processed for movers with their approvals, privileged access request and approval records from the PAM platform, and metrics showing access was removed within the target SLA after termination.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review, Recertification & Compliance Verification Records
artifacts.description: Completed access recertification campaigns with the entitlements reviewed, the reviewer, the date and the resulting revocations, signed off by the responsible managers or system owners; quarterly and bi-annual cadences are both specified across the frameworks, so collect at the shortest applicable cycle. Must also cover periodic review of the access control system configuration itself, implementation verification records proving the documented controls are actually in place, and where a national authority conducts its own assessment, that authority's compliance records for identity and access management.

artifacts.name: Least-Privilege, Default-Deny & Need-to-Know Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration exports from every access control system showing no access is granted unless explicitly authorised, that granted permissions match the documented role definitions, and that need-to-know restrictions are enforced on the data behind them.
