Must include test evidence proving the default-deny behaviour (a newly created account with no role, or failed access attempt logs) and cover the full in-scope estate rather than a sample. The identity and access management system configuration and the records demonstrating the policy is operating in practice are required by several frameworks.

artifacts.name: Authentication & Password Management Policy and Procedures
artifacts.description: The approved authentication policy and password management policy, covering selection of strong authentication factors, how users must protect them, the password composition, rotation and reuse rules, and the procedures implementing them. Must include the identity verification procedure applied before any authentication factor is modified - requiring the current factor, a recovery factor or helpdesk verification - so that a reset cannot itself become the attack path.

artifacts.name: Authentication & MFA Implementation Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence that the authentication policy is enforced: the MFA system architecture and configuration export demonstrating it resists replay, cannot be bypassed by users including administrators, uses genuinely distinct factors and requires all factors to succeed before access is granted; the MFA coverage assessment showing which critical systems and which external access paths are protected and which are not; the self-service password reset configuration showing the identity verification step; and the password policy configuration in the identity provider. Helpdesk records sampling identity verification before factor changes evidence the manual path.

artifacts.name: Access Exception & Bypass Approval Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved deviations from the access baseline, each with its business justification, named approver, expiry date and compensating controls: MFA bypass authorisations, approvals permitting interactive use of accounts that would otherwise be blocked, and documented exceptions where a vendor default account cannot be removed or disabled.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control Rules & Records
artifacts.description: The documented rules and zoning for physical areas (offices, data centre, restricted labs) and the role-based physical access matrix showing who may enter which zone, plus the access validation procedures confirming a person's entitlement before entry is granted. Supporting records: badge or key card access logs and the visitor sign-in register for the controlled areas, retained for the required period.

artifacts.name: Access & Identity Activity Logs and Log Review Records
artifacts.description: Logging configuration for the identity and access systems, the log retention policy setting the required period, evidence the logs are forwarded to and correlated in the SIEM, and the records of periodic log review showing anomalies were identified and followed up. Must include error and exception handling logs with the corrective action documented, and processing validation and integrity check records where the framework requires them.

artifacts.name: Security & Privacy Awareness Training Records
artifacts.description: The training programme content and curriculum covering access, identity and privacy obligations, with completion records for all workforce members, awareness campaign materials, and assessments measuring whether the training was effective. Must evidence that new hires are trained within the required timeline after joining and that refresher training runs on a defined schedule, with the records to prove both.

artifacts.name: Network & Secure Communications Configuration
artifacts.description: Boundary and communications controls supporting the access management programme: firewall and network security control configurations, IDS/IPS configuration, network architecture and segmentation diagrams, and VPN and remote access security configuration. One framework additionally requires documentation of the secured communications solution used for sensitive internal communication and testing records for the emergency communication system. Cross-mapped into this control; the substantive evidence is normally owned by the network security and segmentation controls.

IAC-01.notes: 135 entries across 19 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts. This control is the IAM programme umbrella, so 29 of the 135 entries are restatements of the same approved access control policy - the single largest de-duplication in the batch. 59 SaaS evidence collectors are configured, which makes identity inventory, MFA status and least-privilege configuration genuinely automatable across the connected estate.

artifacts.name: Access Control Policy
artifacts.description: The topic-specific policy defining least privilege and need-to-know with the logical access rules standard for each system type, the authentication standards, and the acceptable use policy with its acknowledgement records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented procedure.

artifacts.name: Unique User Identification Evidence
artifacts.description: The unique user ID assignment policy with the assignment records, the account naming convention documentation, the prohibition of shared accounts, the credential issuance log, and the user activity logs linked to unique identifiers so an action can be attributed to a named person. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Authentication Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: The authentication mechanism documentation with the configuration enforcing it on every system, the multi-factor configuration commensurate with information classification, the enrolment evidence for sensitive systems, and the deployment records.

artifacts.name: Access Control Model Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented access control model covering how access is granted by business and job need, with the least-privilege implementation evidence across in-scope systems, the permission matrix, the role-based configuration export showing permissions per job classification, and the records of periodic review of the model itself.

artifacts.name: Default-Deny Posture Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented standard requiring a default-deny posture in all access control systems, the configuration export from each system showing no access unless explicitly granted, and test evidence such as a new-user creation with no role or failed access attempt logs confirming the posture is actually enforced.

artifacts.name: Access Control System Coverage Mapping
artifacts.description: The inventory of access control systems covering directory services, identity platforms, native operating system and application controls, and the mapping showing every in-scope system component is governed by at least one of them, with the periodic configuration review evidence.

artifacts.name: Centralised Identity Management Evidence
artifacts.description: The centralised identity management documentation, the directory service configuration, the single sign-on integration records, the integration and access control coverage reports, and the authentication, authorisation and accounting server configuration with its log review records and network device integration.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Access Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping roles to permitted functions in key business applications, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the segregation of duties register showing no role combination creates a conflict.

artifacts.name: Account Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The user ID management procedure with the account lifecycle records, the provisioning, modification and review records, and the account provisioning records evidencing each account traces to an approved request.

artifacts.name: Service Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of service accounts with documented ownership and the periodic review records, kept separate from user accounts because they are provisioned, owned and reviewed differently.

artifacts.name: Access Review Evidence
artifacts.description: The completed access review results signed off by data or system owners, with the cadence defined in the policy.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Before Credential Change
artifacts.description: The procedure for verifying user identity before any authentication factor is modified, the self-service reset configuration showing that verification step, and sample helpdesk records of verification performed.

artifacts.name: Single-Factor Account Handling Evidence
artifacts.description: For accounts using a single factor: the configuration showing passwords changed at least every 90 days or dynamic posture analysis governing the access decision, with the expiry schedule and the posture engine configuration where used.

artifacts.name: Secure Logon Configuration
artifacts.description: The secure log-on procedure documentation, the logon banner evidence, and the auto-lock and session timeout configuration limiting exposure on an unattended session.

artifacts.name: Identity System Documentation
artifacts.description: The user identity management system documentation with the username and credential assignment records showing how identities are created and bound to people.

artifacts.name: Information Asset and Network Context
artifacts.description: The information asset inventory with classification and the network architecture and segmentation diagrams, establishing what the access controls are protecting and where the boundaries sit.

artifacts.name: Identity Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented identity management artifacts held under the national regulator's regime, the evidence of compliance, and the regulator's own assessment records.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the identification and authentication requirements and their obligations under them.

IAC-02.notes: 86 asks across 16 frameworks. PCI DSS 7.2/7.3 contributes a distinct block on the access control model and default-deny posture that is separate from the identification and authentication demands the other frameworks make, so it is kept apart.

artifacts.name: Device Authentication Configuration
artifacts.description: The device authentication configuration, the certificate-based authentication documentation, the device identity management procedures, the network access control solution configuration, the network access control deployment configuration, the device posture policy, the authentication, authorisation and accounting server configuration, and the network device integration with that server. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented identify-users-processes-and-devices and authenticate-identities-before-access requirements; CSA CCM likewise for the uniquely identifiable users requirement. HITRUST requires the approved equipment identification in networks policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Network Device Inventory
artifacts.description: The network asset inventory, the asset discovery tool reports, and the information asset inventory and classification recording which devices are entitled to an identity.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Device Detection
artifacts.description: The unauthorised device detection logs and the authentication, authorisation and accounting log review records evidencing devices without a valid identity are found and acted on.

artifacts.name: Identity Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for joiner, mover and leaver handling of identities end to end; the identity provider configuration showing the unique identifier policy and lifecycle rules; the sample provisioning tickets showing approval, provisioning and closure; the log showing timely disablement after termination; the periodic dormant account report with the remediation taken; and the register of approved shared and service accounts with justification and owner.

artifacts.name: Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the identity and access management system configuration, and the network architecture and segmentation diagrams determining what an authenticated device may reach.

artifacts.name: Network Boundary Records
artifacts.description: The network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones; the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records; and the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register covering where devices physically connect.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The secure area authorisation records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: National Authority Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented identity specification with its evidence of compliance and the assessment or compliance records held by the national authority.

IAC-04.notes: 39 asks across 10 frameworks. The device identity mechanism, the network access control that enforces it and the detection of devices that hold no identity are three proofs; the last is what proves the control is not merely configured.

artifacts.name: Authentication Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy specifying strong passwords, multi-factor authentication and adaptive or risk-based authentication by sensitivity, with the implementing procedure. PISF 2026 requires adaptive authentication scaled to sensitivity and risk; QCB requires documented authentication standards and a reset procedure; CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the document.

artifacts.name: MFA Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration export from the identity or MFA platform showing enforcement, scope and enrolled population, with sample authentication logs demonstrating the challenge occurred. PCI DSS requires coverage of all non-console access into the cardholder data environment, not administrators only; SBP Cloud requires enforcement for all users accessing the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: MFA Coverage Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment or report showing which systems and user populations are covered by multi-factor authentication and which are not, with the gap treated as a tracked exposure. MAS TRM scopes this to sensitive systems, NIS2 to critical systems, QCB to remote access for critical systems and sensitive-system enrolment.

artifacts.name: MFA Enrolment and Token Inventory
artifacts.description: Enrolment records for the enrolled population, the inventory of issued tokens or devices, and the deployment records showing rollout progress against the target population.

artifacts.name: MFA Bypass and Exception Records
artifacts.description: Documented bypass authorisations, time-limited and manager-approved, with the compensating controls applied while the bypass is in force. PCI DSS treats an undocumented bypass path as a control failure, so the absence of exceptions must itself be evidenced.

artifacts.name: MFA System Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The architecture document showing the authentication system is not susceptible to replay, cannot be bypassed by users including administrators unless specifically authorised, requires distinct factor types and requires all factors to succeed before access is granted, with the configuration export evidencing each property.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Authentication Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration of remote access gateways (VPN, ZTNA, RDP or jump host) enforcing multi-factor authentication for access originating outside the network, the encryption standard applied to those channels with prohibited protocols named, and test evidence such as a simulated remote login confirming the challenge fires.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Policy and Approval Records
artifacts.description: The remote access policy covering approvals, authentication, encryption, device protection, logging and monitoring, with the workflow records of remote access requests and the written management approvals for access to high-risk assets.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Session Logs and Audit Reports
artifacts.description: Logs from the VPN, ZTNA or privileged access gateway covering remote sessions, with the regular audit reports over them covering frequency, users, sessions and anomalies.

artifacts.name: Password and Account Lockout Configuration
artifacts.description: The password policy with its complexity, history and reset rules, the account lockout policy settings, and the system security parameter settings evidencing both as configured rather than only as written.

artifacts.name: Cloud Privileged Access Controls
artifacts.description: Evidence that the provider cannot reach the institution's data and that master credentials are controlled: the contractual clause prohibiting provider access, monitoring logs and alerts for any provider access attempt, the master account use log with justification and approver, immediate alerting rules on master account use, IP source restrictions where technically possible, key custody evidence showing sole retention of encryption keys, and access controls on backup and log stores including immutability.

artifacts.name: Customer Two-Factor Authentication Evidence
artifacts.description: For the customer-facing channel rather than the workforce: the approved policy mandating two-factor authentication for all customer logins and transaction approvals, the inventory of approved second factors, the configuration export showing enforcement, workflow screenshots of the login and transaction-approval prompts, the coverage audit confirming no bypass route exists, and the authentication architecture covering the identity provider, MFA broker and risk-based logic.

artifacts.name: Per-Customer Service Provider Credentials
artifacts.description: For service providers with remote access into multiple customer environments: the register of customer-specific credentials or keys, the configuration evidence showing unique authentication factors per customer environment, and sample audit logs demonstrating credentials are not shared across customers.

artifacts.name: Email Security Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration of email threat protection with multi-factor authentication for administrative, remote and webmail access, the DNS records or configuration for SPF, DKIM and DMARC, and evidence of email archiving, backup and restoration capability.

artifacts.name: Layered Security Architecture Evidence
artifacts.description: The multi-layer security architecture diagram showing firewalls, secure sign-on, dual authentication with triangulation of access and real-time event monitoring, the matrix showing layer coverage across assets, the firewall rulebase with periodic review evidence, and the real-time monitoring dashboards.

artifacts.name: Unique User Identification Evidence
artifacts.description: The user identification procedures and the records or configuration demonstrating every user is uniquely identifiable, so that an authentication event can be attributed to a named individual rather than a shared account.

artifacts.name: Secured Communications Solution Evidence
artifacts.description: Documentation of the secured voice, video and text communications solution and the records of emergency communication system testing.

artifacts.name: Access Matrix and Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix mapping roles to permissions for the systems in scope, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the network architecture and device baselines that the authentication controls sit within.

IAC-06.notes: 104 asks across 18 frameworks. Workforce MFA and customer-facing two-factor authentication are separated: SBP Internet Banking 2.2.1(b) governs customer logins and transaction approval, which is a different population, a different threat model and different evidence from workforce or administrator MFA.

artifacts.name: Administrative Multi-Factor Configuration
artifacts.description: The multi-factor configuration evidence for non-console administrative access into the protected environment, the administrative multi-factor configuration documentation, the multi-factor configuration for administrative access, the multi-factor authentication configuration, the multi-factor deployment records, the multi-factor implementation, the privileged access multi-factor enforcement records, and the administrative multi-factor compliance reports. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented use-multifactor-authentication requirement.

artifacts.name: Protected Environment Access Coverage
artifacts.description: The multi-factor configuration evidence for all non-console access into the protected environment beyond administrators, the audit confirming coverage of all administrative non-console access paths, and the documentation of any approved bypass exceptions with their compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Multi-Factor Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration of remote access gateways enforcing multi-factor for all access originating outside the network, the sample remote access authentication logs showing that enforcement, and the test evidence confirming the challenge is presented.

artifacts.name: Authentication Logs
artifacts.description: The sample authentication logs showing multi-factor prompts for administrative access, the privileged access logs and audit reports, and the authentication mechanism documentation behind them.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Separation
artifacts.description: The privileged account inventory, the evidence separating normal from privileged accounts, the service account inventory with its controls, and the user identification procedures. HITRUST requires the approved user identification and authentication policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Authentication Parameter Configuration
artifacts.description: The password policy, the password policy configuration screenshots, the authentication configuration, the account lockout policy settings, and the system security parameter settings.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the authentication requirements.

IAC-06.1.notes: 37 asks across 9 frameworks. PCI DSS separates administrative non-console access, all non-console access into the protected environment, and remote access originating outside the network; those three coverage scopes are preserved.

artifacts.name: Access Management Policy, Procedure and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Approved, current policy governing user registration, de-registration and the assignment of access rights, with the procedures implementing it, management sign-off and version history. Must define scope, roles and responsibilities, the criteria and prerequisites for creating, enabling, modifying, disabling and removing accounts, and how exceptions are handled. Several frameworks require domain-specific extensions of the same policy: cloud workload access including the four-eye principle (SBP Cloud), database and document/content access approval with the supporting data management strategy (NDMO), and secured workstation and transaction-level access (DoH ADHIE). HITRUST additionally requires awareness communications evidencing personnel were informed, and CSA CCM requires records that provisioning and revocation operate in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Joiner-Mover-Leaver Procedure and Checklists
artifacts.description: The end-to-end identity lifecycle procedure with the onboarding, role-change and offboarding checklists it drives. Must cover addition, modification and deletion of user IDs and authentication factors with required approvals and traceability, the trigger events and timing for each step, and the handoffs between HR, the manager and IT. Applies to user, service and system accounts (PISF 2026) and must include the termination checklist covering revocation of all access on exit (HIPAA).

artifacts.name: Access Request and Approval Records
artifacts.description: Completed access request records for the period showing, per request, the requester, the access sought, the business justification, the named approver, the approval date and the provisioning confirmation. Approval must come from personnel authorised to grant that access, and the record must be traceable through to the account actually created or modified. Sample across onboarding, role change and privileged access requests, and include the documented approval for document, content and database access where that is separately controlled.

artifacts.name: Authorised Approver Register and Approval Workflow Configuration
artifacts.description: The register of personnel authorised to approve access requests with the scope of each person's approval authority, plus the configuration of the IAM or ITSM workflow enforcing that approval is obtained before access is provisioned. SBP Cloud additionally requires the workflow to enforce a four-eye (maker-checker) separation, evidenced in the tool configuration.

artifacts.name: Deprovisioning and Revocation Records with Timeliness Metrics
artifacts.description: Evidence that access is removed promptly and completely when employment ends or a role changes: the account disablement and deletion records with timestamps, the audit log of deactivation, the equipment and asset return record, and the metrics showing removal occurred within the target service level. Frameworks differ on the trigger threshold: QCB requires suspension after 60 days of inactivity followed by deletion; ISO 27001 and PISF 2026 require disablement within the organisation's own defined SLA on exit or role change; HIPAA requires termination of access as part of the workforce termination procedure.

artifacts.name: Account Inventory and Reconciliation Report
artifacts.description: Current inventory of all accounts with the user or owner, system, status, entitlement level, creation date and last review date, reconciled periodically against the authoritative list of authorised users (typically the HR joiner-leaver feed). Must surface dormant, orphaned and inactive accounts with the remediation taken. The register of access rights with documented changes serves the same purpose for DoH ADHIE.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review and Recertification Records
artifacts.description: Completed access recertification campaigns showing the population reviewed, the reviewer, the date, the decisions (retain, modify, revoke) and evidence that revocations were actioned. Reviews must be signed off by the business or system owner and, for cloud access rights changes, performed independently of the person who made the change (SBP Cloud). Frequency expectations differ: SOC 2 expects at least quarterly, ISO 27001 accepts quarterly or bi-annual, and others state a defined periodic cadence. Include the periodic review of whether assigned roles still reflect business need.

artifacts.name: Role-to-Access Mapping and Segregation of Duties Matrix
artifacts.description: The definitive mapping of roles to access levels and entitlements per system, used as the basis for what a given user should receive on provisioning. Must identify owners and responsibilities, cover all in-scope systems, be dated with a last-update, and flag conflicting combinations. Includes the segregation of duties matrix confirming administrators hold no transactional authority (SBP ETGRMF), the role mandates, RACI and job descriptions supporting it, and the data classification scheme that determines which access levels apply to which data (NDMO).

artifacts.name: Privileged and Administrative Account Controls Evidence
artifacts.description: The additional controls applied when the account being provisioned is privileged: the privileged access management procedure, records of just-in-time privileged access requests and approvals, evidence that administrators hold separate accounts for routine versus privileged work, multi-factor authentication enforced on service, generic and administrative accounts, the enhanced password length, complexity and age settings for admin accounts, and the policy plus technical enforcement restricting privileged account use to dedicated administrative machines. Includes the formal security administration procedures for allocating rights on a least-privilege basis.

artifacts.name: Service, Shared and Third-Party Account Register
artifacts.description: Register of approved non-personal accounts, covering service, generic, shared, temporary and third-party or contractor accounts, with the named human owner, business justification, the systems accessed, the compensating controls applied and the expiry or review date, plus the procedure governing how temporary and third-party accounts are requested, time-boxed and removed.

artifacts.name: IAM Platform Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration of the identity platform enforcing the registration rules: unique identifier policy, account lifecycle rules and their triggers, password policy settings, and the requirement that an initial or reset credential is unique per user and must be changed at first use. Include the documented password set and reset procedure with sample reset records showing a unique value was assigned and immediate change enforced, and the workstation access control configuration where access is restricted by endpoint.

artifacts.name: Account Change Audit Logs and Privileged Activity Monitoring
artifacts.description: System-generated audit logs of account additions, modifications and deletions and of entitlement changes, each showing actor, subject account, change made, timestamp and outcome, so that every provisioning and de-provisioning action in the records above can be independently corroborated. Include the modification audit trail for access rights, provisioning logs, transaction-level access records, and the monitoring logs and detection use cases covering privileged and administrator activity for unusual or unauthorised behaviour.

artifacts.name: Access Rights Statement and User Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The template statement of access rights issued to each authorised user on appointment, the issuance records showing it was provided, and the signed acknowledgements of receipt, together with the formal appointment records designating individuals as authorised users. Required by DoH ADHIE as the user-facing half of the registration process.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Evidence at Enrollment
artifacts.description: For customer-facing channels, evidence that identity is verified before access is granted: the documented enrollment procedure specifying the verification steps, workflow evidence showing the verification methods executed (identity document, biometric or national registry check, one-time passcode, branch confirmation), sample enrollment audit logs recording the method used, timestamp, agent and outcome, and system configuration evidence that products and services remain on pre-activation hold until verification succeeds.

artifacts.name: Access Exception Register
artifacts.description: Register of approved departures from the standard entitlement model, with the access granted, the justification, the compensating controls, the approver and the expiry date, reviewed so that exceptions do not become permanent.

IAC-07.notes: 105 manual entries across 17 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts. Twenty-one evidence collectors are already wired (Okta, OneLogin, Clerk, Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Rippling and the SaaS estate), plus an automated IAM password-length check, so user lists, account inventories, deprovisioning logs, account change logs and IAM platform configuration are automated or hybrid; approvals, reviews and procedures remain manual. SBP Cloud contributes the strictest privileged-account requirements (four-eye, dedicated admin machines, separate admin accounts); SBP Internet Banking contributes a customer-enrollment identity verification strand kept separate because it only applies to retail banking channels.

artifacts.name: Role Change Procedure
artifacts.description: The internal transfer and role change procedure, the human resources transfer notification process, the coordination records between human resources and technology, the role change notifications to stakeholders, and the workforce clearance and access authorisation procedures applied at the change.

artifacts.name: Role Change Access Records
artifacts.description: The access reassignment records, the authorisation records for the new role's privileges, the access modification request forms with their manager approval documentation, the before-and-after access comparison, the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals, the sample access change authorisation records with approver sign-off, and the log of access modifications and revocations on role change, transfer or termination.

artifacts.name: Termination Access Revocation
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for immediate access revocation upon termination with human resources and technology integration, the access revocation procedure, the offboarding and termination procedures, the sample termination tickets with timestamps showing immediate revocation, the access revocation and removal records, the audit logs evidencing termination-driven account disablement, the de-provisioning procedures and evidence, the timeliness verification, and the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers.

artifacts.name: Identifier Lifecycle Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for addition, deletion and modification of user identifiers and authentication factors with appropriate approval; the sample lifecycle change records with approver and timestamps; the audit logs of account additions, deletions and modifications; the access provisioning workflow screenshots showing request, approve and provision steps; and the user access provisioning procedures with their approval records.

artifacts.name: Access Approval Controls
artifacts.description: The workflow configuration requiring approval by authorised personnel before access is provisioned, the register of personnel authorised to approve access requests with their scope of authority, the sample completed access request records showing approver identity and approval date, and the supervisor approval records.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers, the records of regular user access-rights reviews with sign-off, the periodic user access reviews at the required cadence, the schedule showing review cadence for high, medium and low risk systems aligned with the risk classification, and the quarterly privileged access review with sign-off.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Access Matrix
artifacts.description: The role-based access matrix mapping job functions to access rights with approver designations, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the approved access rights policy implementing least privilege, and the segregation-of-duties conflict analysis report with its mitigation actions.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Records
artifacts.description: The privileged access management procedures and the platform records showing just-in-time privileged access requests and approvals, covering the elevated rights a role change most often leaves behind.

artifacts.name: Access Exception Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved access exceptions with expiry dates and compensating controls, recording the departures from the role model that survive a review.

artifacts.name: Access Activity Logs
artifacts.description: The system access logs evidencing what the reassigned identity actually reached after the change. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented user access changes and revocation requirement.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation, and the segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Access Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit; the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records; and the user access provisioning, modification and review records covering provider personnel. HITRUST requires the approved removal of access rights policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

IAC-07.1.notes: 60 asks across 14 frameworks. Movers and leavers arrive together through most crosswalks; the transfer records are separated from the termination records because a mover's stale access is the failure this control exists to catch and it is invisible in termination evidence.

artifacts.name: Termination Access Revocation Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for immediate access revocation on termination with the human-resources-to-IT integration that triggers it, the access termination procedure, the offboarding procedures, the termination checklist, and the user registration and de-registration procedure. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Access Revocation Records
artifacts.description: The revocation and account disablement records for terminated personnel, the sample termination tickets with timestamps, the account deactivation logs, the audit trail of disabled accounts, and the audit logs from the identity platform evidencing termination-driven disablement.

artifacts.name: Revocation Timeliness Metrics
artifacts.description: The comparison of termination date against account disable date, the time-to-revoke metrics with their supporting audit logs, the access removal service level report, the workflow records with timing metrics against the target, and the timeliness verification evidence. This is the artifact that distinguishes a revocation process from a prompt one.

artifacts.name: HR Notification Records
artifacts.description: The human resources termination notification to IT, the coordination records between the two functions, the user change notification procedure with its notification records and timestamps, the add and remove tracking log, and the communications with the sector regulator where notification is required.

artifacts.name: Account Lifecycle Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented joiner, mover and leaver processes covering user, service and system accounts; the identifier lifecycle procedure for addition, deletion and modification with the required approvals; the account management procedures; and the temporary and third-party account procedure.

artifacts.name: Account Reconciliation Records
artifacts.description: The periodic reconciliation of active accounts against authorised users, the account inventory by user, the terminated user account records, and the sample of terminated users verified as disabled.

artifacts.name: Access Change and Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The log of access modifications and revocations on role change or transfer, the access modification log for movers with their approvals, the provisioning workflow evidence, the lifecycle change records with approver and timestamps, and the account change audit logs.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The completed access recertification signed by managers, the regular access-rights review records with sign-off, the account review documentation, and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Equipment Return Records
artifacts.description: The equipment return documentation completed at termination, closing the physical side of offboarding alongside the logical.

artifacts.name: Financial Reporting System Access Records
artifacts.description: The access provisioning approvals for financial reporting systems, the consolidation system access reports, the reporting database privilege listings, and the periodic access review documentation for those tools.

artifacts.name: Access Control Matrix and Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the user authorisation records, and the account creation request and approval forms.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Termination Records
artifacts.description: The privileged access management platform records showing just-in-time requests and approvals, evidencing privileged entitlements are removed alongside standard ones at termination.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Access Termination Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses and right-to-audit and the third-party risk assessment and monitoring records, covering revocation for provider personnel who leave.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the termination and role-change obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

IAC-07.2.notes: 71 asks across 13 frameworks. The recurring demand is timeliness, not just revocation — SOX, DoH ADHIE, HITRUST and ISO 27001 each require the interval between termination and disablement to be measured. That measurement is its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Access Control Policy & Standards
artifacts.description: The approved access control policy and supporting logical/physical access rules standard, setting out least privilege, need-to-know, default-deny, role assignment and authorization rules, with management sign-off and evidence of periodic (HITRUST: annual) review. Include the access rights management and account management procedures and the formal approval/socialisation records NDMO requires.

artifacts.name: Role Definitions & Access Control Matrix
artifacts.description: The RBAC/ABAC model itself: defined roles with their business purpose, the role-to-permission mapping, and the per-system access control matrix approved by the system or data owner, including privileged roles, application and system accounts, database roles and specialised roles (e.g. medical device roles with their qualification requirements). Must show each role reflects a legitimate business need and that the matrix is reviewed and owner-approved, not merely drafted.

artifacts.name: RBAC Configuration Export & System Access Settings
artifacts.description: Exports from the actual systems showing the role model as implemented: role and group definitions, user-to-role/group membership, entitlement reports, permission matrices, authorization mechanism configuration, database and VM/hypervisor role settings, and the identity provider configuration. This is what the connectors already collect across the IdP, SaaS, code and cloud estate; export dates must fall within the audit period.

artifacts.name: Access Request, Authorization & Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: Per-user records showing access was requested, justified by assigned duties, approved by the appropriate manager or data owner, and provisioned as approved — including the business-need justification, supervisor/workforce clearance approval, authorized-user appointment records, and modification requests with their approvals. Sample must span the review period, not just current state.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review & Recertification Records
artifacts.description: Completed access reviews for users, roles and privileged accounts: the population reviewed, the reviewer, the decision per entitlement, the date, and evidence that revocations identified were actually actioned. Frequency varies — PCI DSS requires at least every six months for accounts and periodic review of the access model, HIPAA and SOC 2 expect a defined periodic recertification, HITRUST expects annual policy and review records.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Inventory & Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: Inventory of privileged and administrative accounts with the role each is tied to, evidence that privileged roles are segregated and managed under stricter approval, and the monitoring records showing privileged role/attribute assignments and changes to them are watched, with revocation when the assignment is no longer appropriate.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Matrix & Dual-Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The segregation of duties matrix identifying conflicting role combinations and how they are prevented or compensated, plus evidence of four-eyes/dual-authorisation enforcement in critical systems.

artifacts.name: Least Privilege & Default-Deny Enforcement Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that the model denies by default and grants the minimum required: default-deny configuration exports and test results proving unauthorised access is refused, least-privilege assessments or attestations for high-privilege roles, restrictions on transactions and functions available to each role, and controls on flow of regulated data between roles.

artifacts.name: Access Revocation Records on Termination or Role Change
artifacts.description: Records showing access was removed when a user left or changed role, with the timeliness evidence MAS TRM requires (date of termination versus date of revocation), the terminated-account listing, and the access modification change log tying each change to an approved trigger.

artifacts.name: Data Classification & Need-to-Know Scope Records
artifacts.description: The data classification scheme and labelled dataset/asset register that determine which roles may access which data, the data ACL configuration and need-to-know justifications for restricted datasets, database data classification, restricted access lists for support staff, and retention/archival rules constraining access to regulated records.

artifacts.name: De-identification Method & Re-identification Risk Records
artifacts.description: Where access is granted to de-identified data instead of the regulated original: the de-identification policy and procedure, the expert determination or safe harbour documentation supporting the method, verification records for each de-identified dataset, and the re-identification risk assessment.

artifacts.name: Access Control Training & Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that people holding roles were trained on the access and privacy rules attached to them: curriculum, new-hire training within the required timeline, refresher schedule and completion records, and the awareness communications HITRUST requires showing personnel were informed of the access control policy.

artifacts.name: Access Decision & Privileged Activity Logs
artifacts.description: Logs evidencing the model operating: access decision/authorisation audit logs, privileged and administrative activity logs, access control list changes, and device or application access logs, retained for the required period and monitored for anomalies.

artifacts.name: Network Segmentation & Platform Hardening Evidence
artifacts.description: Architecture and segmentation diagrams showing the boundaries the role model relies on, plus VM/hypervisor hardening checklists, resource limits and per-host firewall configuration where roles are enforced at platform level.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan & Escalation Procedures
artifacts.description: Incident response plan with the escalation path and communication templates for access-related incidents, plus tabletop exercise records — required by SWIFT CSCF alongside the access controls it maps to.

IAC-08.notes: 156 entries reduce to 15. This control has 55 live collectors (Okta, Entra/M365, Google Workspace, GitHub/GitLab, AWS IAM, JumpCloud, Auth0 etc.), so the configuration, entitlement and log clusters are genuinely automated; the role model, approvals and review sign-off remain human. Segregation-of-duties and network-hardening clusters are small but kept separate because they are distinct artifacts a team collects from different owners.

artifacts.name: Identifier Management Procedure
artifacts.description: The identifier management procedures, the user identifier management procedure, the procedure ensuring every user is assigned a unique identifier before access to system components or regulated data, the unique user identifier assignment policy, the account naming convention documentation, the unique identifier scheme documentation, and the identity lifecycle procedure for joiner, mover and leaver handling end to end. HITRUST requires the approved user identification and authentication policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Identifier Assignment Records
artifacts.description: The user identifier assignment records, the unique user identifier assignment records, the user account provisioning records, the credential issuance log, the username and password assignment records, the joiner process evidence, the user account listing, the sample tickets showing approval, provisioning and closure for recent onboardings, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Identifier Reuse Prevention
artifacts.description: The controls preventing reuse of an identifier once retired, with the records demonstrating they operate. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented prevent-identifier-reuse requirement.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Controls
artifacts.description: The prohibition of shared accounts documentation and the register of approved shared and service accounts with their justification and owner, recording the exceptions to the unique-identifier rule.

artifacts.name: Inactive Identifier Review
artifacts.description: The inactive identifier review records, the periodic report identifying dormant accounts with the remediation taken, the log showing timely disablement of accounts within the service level after termination, and the account lifecycle records.

artifacts.name: Identity Platform Configuration
artifacts.description: The identity provider configuration showing the unique identifier policy and lifecycle rules, the identity and access management system configuration, the centralised identity management documentation, the directory service configuration, the integration coverage reports, the identity system configuration evidence, and the identity management system documentation.

artifacts.name: Identifier to Activity Linkage
artifacts.description: The audit log linkage to user identifiers and the user activity logs linked to unique identifiers, evidencing that actions can be attributed to an individual.

artifacts.name: Authentication Standards
artifacts.description: The authentication standards and configuration documentation, the password policy with each required minimum standard configured, and the password policy compliance audit reports.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The controls safeguarding log integrity so that identifier-attributed activity cannot be altered. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented safeguard logs integrity requirement.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Asset Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the information asset inventory and classification, the network architecture and segmentation diagrams, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the identification requirements.

IAC-09.notes: 47 asks across 12 frameworks. Unique identifier assignment, the prohibition on shared accounts and identifier reuse prevention are three proofs; the last is kept separate because reuse is invisible in a current account listing.

artifacts.name: Authenticator and Credential Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering the full credential lifecycle from generation to disposal, the authenticator distribution procedures, the credential management system documentation, and the accepted authentication factor standard. CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the documented policy.

artifacts.name: Credential Configuration Export
artifacts.description: The directory or identity provider configuration export showing enforced complexity, length, history and lockout, with the compliance reports confirming it across the estate.

artifacts.name: Identity Lifecycle Change Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for addition, deletion and modification of user identifiers and authentication factors with the required approvals, the sample joiner, mover and leaver records with approver and timestamps, the account change audit logs, the provisioning workflow evidence, the modification log, and the removal SLA report.

artifacts.name: Initial and Temporary Credential Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for setting and resetting credentials requiring a unique value per user, the configuration enforcing a change at first use, the log of temporary or initial credentials issued and delivered securely, sample reset records, and the documented requirement or configuration evidence permitting a temporary password only with forced change.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Before Credential Change
artifacts.description: The procedure for verifying identity before any authentication factor is modified, the helpdesk password reset procedure with its verification steps, the user identification procedure applied prior to reset, the self-service reset configuration showing the verification step, and sample helpdesk records of verification performed.

artifacts.name: Credential Rotation and Revocation Records
artifacts.description: The logs of credential rotation and revocation events, the rotation records from the vault, and the compromise handling procedure defining what happens when a credential is suspected exposed.

artifacts.name: Secrets and Password Vault Configuration
artifacts.description: The password manager or privileged access vault configuration with its access controls, the secrets vault configuration with rotation, the procedure protecting application and system account credentials through periodic change, and the targeted risk analysis defining that frequency.

artifacts.name: Token and Certificate Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedure assigning tokens, smart cards or certificates to named individuals with no sharing permitted, the assignment records, the revocation and replacement records following loss, theft or malfunction, and sample audit logs of authentication using them.

artifacts.name: Credential Reuse Prevention Evidence
artifacts.description: The password history configuration, the documented prohibition on reuse, and the test evidence confirming a recent credential is actually rejected on reuse.

artifacts.name: Default Credential Change Evidence
artifacts.description: The checklist and sign-off confirming vendor default credentials are changed before a system enters service, with the change records.

artifacts.name: Credential Storage Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The hashing and encryption configuration evidencing credentials are not stored recoverably, and the credential communication procedures governing how they reach the user.

artifacts.name: Unique Credential Assignment Records
artifacts.description: The unique credential assignment procedure, the credential management system records, and the acknowledgements from users that credentials are not to be shared.

artifacts.name: Multi-Factor Enrolment Evidence
artifacts.description: The multi-factor implementation with the enrolment coverage report across users including privileged accounts, and the strong authentication requirement with its supporting records.

artifacts.name: Single-Factor Account Handling Evidence
artifacts.description: For accounts using a single factor: the configuration showing credentials changed at least every 90 days or dynamic posture analysis governing the access decision, with the expiry schedule and the posture engine configuration where used.

artifacts.name: Access Review and Exception Records
artifacts.description: The completed access recertification signed by managers, the privileged access request records, and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Access Control Context Documentation
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the identity and access management system configuration, the information asset inventory with classification, and the network architecture and segmentation diagrams establishing what the credentials protect.

artifacts.name: Credential Awareness Training Records
artifacts.description: The training records on credential handling and the awareness communications informing personnel of their obligations.

IAC-10.notes: 82 asks across 14 frameworks. Distinct from IAC-10.1 (password rules) in that this control covers the authenticator lifecycle — issue, distribute, rotate, revoke, replace — across all factor types, not just passwords. Token and certificate handling is kept separate from password handling for that reason.

artifacts.name: Password and Authentication Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy specifying complexity, minimum length, history, rotation, lockout, storage and reset rules, with the accepted authentication factor standard behind it. PCI DSS requires a minimum length of 12 characters (or 8 with documented system limitation and risk acceptance) and history of at least 4; DoH ADHIE requires all eight of its minimum standards to be configured; CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the document.

artifacts.name: Password Configuration Export
artifacts.description: The directory or identity provider configuration export showing the enforced settings — minimum length, complexity, history, expiry, lockout threshold and duration — evidencing the policy is applied rather than only written, together with the compliance scan output confirming it across the estate.

artifacts.name: Account Lockout and Session Configuration
artifacts.description: The lockout policy and its configuration enforcing lockout after consecutive failed attempts, the session timeout configuration covering idle and absolute limits, sample logs showing lockout events and session expiries, and the documented criteria for re-authenticating after sensitive actions, elapsed time or device change.

artifacts.name: Initial and Reset Credential Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for setting and resetting passwords requiring a unique value per user and an immediate change at first use, the system configuration enforcing that first-use change, sample reset records showing unique value assignment, the log of temporary credentials issued and delivered securely, and the user credential communication procedures.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Before Credential Change
artifacts.description: The procedure requiring verification of user identity before any authentication factor is modified — current factor required, or a recovery factor — the self-service reset configuration showing that verification step, and sample helpdesk records of verification performed before a change.

artifacts.name: Password Reuse Prevention Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration export showing password history enforced, and test evidence confirming reuse of a recent password is actually rejected rather than only configured to be.

artifacts.name: Single-Factor Account Handling Evidence
artifacts.description: For accounts using a single factor: the configuration evidence showing passwords are changed at least every 90 days or that dynamic posture analysis governs the access decision, the password expiry schedule, and the configuration of the access decision engine where posture analysis is used.

artifacts.name: Application and System Account Credential Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure protecting application and system account passwords through periodic change with the targeted risk analysis defining that frequency and complexity, the password vault or privileged access management configuration with its access controls, and the rotation records from the vault.

artifacts.name: Default Credential Change Evidence
artifacts.description: The checklist and sign-off confirming vendor default credentials are changed before a system enters service, the default password change records, and the default-account hardening evidence.

artifacts.name: Credential Storage Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The password hashing and encryption configuration evidencing credentials are not stored recoverably, and the credential management system documentation and authenticator distribution procedures behind it.

artifacts.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Evidence
artifacts.description: The multi-factor configuration evidence with the enrolment coverage report across users including privileged accounts, and the implementation plan where rollout is still in progress.

artifacts.name: Password Compliance Audit Records
artifacts.description: The periodic compliance audit reports over password configuration and practice, the password change logs, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Unique User Identification Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence that every user is uniquely identifiable and the strong authentication requirement applied, with the records demonstrating each is implemented in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Authentication Flow Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented authentication flow for each system class showing which factors are required at which step, and the configuration evidence from in-scope systems confirming at least one factor is enforced at every entry point.

artifacts.name: Password Awareness Training Records
artifacts.description: The training content on password practice with attendance records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the requirements.

artifacts.name: Identity System Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: The identity system configuration evidence supporting the password controls, showing where the policy is enforced and for which populations.

IAC-10.1.notes: 93 asks across 16 frameworks. PCI DSS 8.3 contributes eight separately testable password requirements (factor standard, first-use change, identity verification before change, complexity, history, expiry, single-factor handling, system-account rotation); those are grouped by what an assessor asks for in one go rather than one artifact per sub-requirement.

artifacts.name: Authenticator Storage Protection
artifacts.description: The password hashing or encryption configuration evidence, the password storage with hashing or encryption, and the documented protection of stored and transmitted credentials with the records demonstrating it operates. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Authenticator Distribution Records
artifacts.description: The authenticator distribution procedures, the user credential communication procedures, the log of temporary or initial credentials issued, delivered securely and forced-changed on first use, the checklist and sign-off confirming vendor defaults changed on new systems, and the default password change records.

artifacts.name: Credential Lifecycle Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure covering the full credential lifecycle from generation to disposal, the credential management system documentation, and the logs of credential rotation and revocation events.

artifacts.name: Secrets Vault Configuration
artifacts.description: The password manager or privileged access vault configuration with its access controls, the configuration of secure credential and secret storage with rotation, and the privileged password vault with its offsite backup.

artifacts.name: Password Policy and Configuration
artifacts.description: The authentication and password policy specifying complexity, length, rotation, multi-factor scope and storage rules; the password policy with its complexity, history and recycling requirements; the password and authenticator policy; the password complexity configuration; the password configuration export demonstrating enforced complexity and lockout settings; and the multi-factor enrolment coverage report across users including privileged accounts. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented passwords management requirement. HITRUST requires the approved password use and password management system policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Physical Authenticator Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure assigning tokens, smart cards or certificates to individuals with no sharing and covering revocation and replacement on loss; the records of those assignments; the revocation and replacement records following loss, theft or malfunction; and the sample audit logs of authentication using them.

artifacts.name: Authentication Protocol Hardening
artifacts.description: The authentication protocol hardening evidence and the transport, anti-replay and anti-hijack configurations protecting the authenticator in transit.

artifacts.name: Credential Awareness and Access Records
artifacts.description: The password awareness training records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the credential handling requirements, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the physical access logs with the visitor register, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

IAC-10.5.notes: 41 asks across 9 frameworks. Storage protection, distribution protection and the vault that holds shared secrets are three proofs; PCI DSS 8.3.11's physical token handling is kept separate because it protects a different kind of authenticator.

artifacts.name: Vendor Default Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of vendor default accounts on all in-scope system components with status showing changed, disabled or removed; the documented procedure for discovering and remediating vendor default accounts on new deployments; the default account management procedures; the default account audit results; and the exception documentation for defaults that cannot be changed.

artifacts.name: Default Credential Change Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration export or password vault entries confirming default passwords have been changed, the checklist and sign-off confirming vendor defaults changed on new systems, the default password change records, the documentation of renames and password changes, the default-account hardening evidence, and the configuration evidence showing unused default accounts removed or disabled.

artifacts.name: Wireless Default Change Records
artifacts.description: The documented wireless hardening standard listing each default to be changed, the wireless controller and access point configuration export showing secure settings and absence of vendor defaults, and the records evidencing all wireless vendor defaults including default keys, community strings, administrative passwords and network identifiers have been changed.

artifacts.name: Password Policy and Configuration
artifacts.description: The authentication and password policy specifying complexity, length, rotation, multi-factor scope and storage rules; the password policy with its complexity, history and recycling requirements; the password configuration export demonstrating enforced complexity and lockout settings; the password complexity configuration; the password rotation configuration; the password hashing or encryption configuration evidence; the password management policy compliance evidence; and the compliance scans confirming it. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented passwords management requirement. HITRUST requires the approved user password management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Initial Credential Issuance Records
artifacts.description: The log of temporary or initial credentials issued, delivered securely and forced-changed on first use; the authenticator distribution procedures; the user credential communication procedures; the forced change at first or expired logon configuration; and the credential management system documentation.

artifacts.name: Credential Vault and Multi-Factor Records
artifacts.description: The password manager or privileged access vault configuration with its access controls and the multi-factor enrolment coverage report across users including privileged accounts.

artifacts.name: Significant Change Assessment
artifacts.description: The documented definition of a significant change applicable to the environment, the records confirming all applicable requirements are in place on new or changed systems and networks following such a change, the updated network and data-flow diagrams, scope documentation and inventories, and a sample completed significant-change assessment for a recent change.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Asset Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the identity and access management system configuration, the information asset inventory and classification, and the network architecture and segmentation diagrams scoping where defaults may exist.

artifacts.name: Network Control Records
artifacts.description: The network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones; the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records; the awareness communications informing personnel of the credential requirements; and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved network controls policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Password Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The password awareness training records covering how credentials are to be chosen, stored and changed.

IAC-10.8.notes: 52 asks across 9 frameworks. The vendor-default inventory, the evidence each default was changed, and the wireless defaults are kept apart because wireless defaults extend beyond passwords to keys, community strings and network identifiers.

artifacts.name: Access Control Policy
artifacts.description: The topic-specific policy defining principles of least privilege and need-to-know with its scope, the access control policy and procedures, the standard defining authentication, authorisation and session rules for each system type, the access matrices by user type and method, the system access standard operating procedures, and the authentication standards and configuration documentation. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limit-access-to-authorised-transactions requirement.

artifacts.name: Identity Lifecycle Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for joiner, mover and leaver handling of identities end to end; the documented lifecycle processes for user, service and system accounts; the account management procedures; the user identifier management procedure; the user registration procedure; and the procedure for addition, deletion and modification of user identifiers and authentication factors with appropriate approval. HITRUST requires the approved user registration policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: The sample tickets showing approval, provisioning and closure for recent onboardings; the access request forms with their approval workflow records; the access provisioning logs; the access provisioning workflow screenshots; the sample lifecycle change records with approver and timestamps; the user access authorisation records; and the audit logs of account additions, deletions and modifications.

artifacts.name: De-provisioning Records
artifacts.description: The log showing timely disablement of accounts within the service level after termination, the records and logs evidencing timely de-provisioning on exit or role change, the terminated user account records, the metrics showing access removed within the target service level, and the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals.

artifacts.name: Account Reconciliation and Dormancy
artifacts.description: The periodic reconciliation of active accounts against authorised users, the periodic report identifying inactive accounts with the remediation taken, the account review documentation, and the account lifecycle records supporting them.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The quarterly access review results signed off by data and system owners, the evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Identity Platform Configuration
artifacts.description: The identity provider configuration showing the unique identifier policy and lifecycle rules, the identity and access management system configuration, and the role-based access matrix mapping roles to permitted functions in key business applications.

artifacts.name: Shared and Service Account Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved shared and service accounts with justification and owner, the inventory of system and application accounts that can be used for interactive login, the configuration preventing interactive use where possible, the approval records for accounts where interactive use is permitted with documented business need and time limit, and the monitoring and alerting on interactive use of those accounts.

artifacts.name: Emergency Access Procedure
artifacts.description: The emergency access procedure document, the break-glass account procedures, the emergency access audit logs, and the post-emergency access review records.

artifacts.name: Privileged and Exception Records
artifacts.description: The platform records showing just-in-time privileged access requests and approvals and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Service Provider Access Controls
artifacts.description: The service provider access control procedures and the service provider access monitoring records covering accounts held by third parties.

artifacts.name: Customer Credential Guidance
artifacts.description: The guidance issued to customer users covering periodic change of credentials and how to recognise when credentials may be compromised, with the evidence of its distribution through portal publication or onboarding communications.

artifacts.name: Asset Inventory and Segmentation
artifacts.description: The information asset inventory and classification and the network architecture and segmentation diagrams that determine what each account population may reach.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Rules
artifacts.description: The rules and zoning document for physical areas covering offices, data centres and restricted labs, applying the same account model to physical entry.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the account management requirements that bind them.

IAC-15.notes: 59 asks across 11 frameworks. The account lifecycle, the non-human accounts and the emergency accounts are three separate populations with different controls; PCI DSS 8.6.1's interactive-use restriction on system accounts is kept whole rather than dispersed.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved shared and service accounts with justification and owner, the inventory of group, shared and generic accounts with justification, approver and individual accountability mechanism, the shared account register, the service account inventory with owners, and the sample management approval records for current exceptions.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Exception Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure governing exceptional use of group, shared or generic identifiers requiring management approval and individual accountability, the compensating controls documentation for shared accounts, the compensating controls recorded against each entry, and the service-account usage policy.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Attribution
artifacts.description: The monitoring and audit logs ensuring traceability of actions performed via shared accounts, the shared identifier usage tracker, the correlation evidence tying a shared-account action to a time and location, and the evidence of individual operating-system accounts for database administrators.

artifacts.name: Service Account Controls
artifacts.description: The interactive login restriction evidence and the password management procedures for service accounts.

artifacts.name: Identity Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for joiner, mover and leaver handling of identities end to end; the identity provider configuration showing the unique identifier policy and lifecycle rules; the sample provisioning tickets showing approval, provisioning and closure; the log showing timely disablement after termination; the periodic dormant account report with the remediation taken; the account management procedures; the account review documentation; the user access authorisation records; and the terminated user account records.

artifacts.name: Password Policy Records
artifacts.description: The password policy with each required minimum standard configured, the identity system configuration evidence, and the password policy compliance audit reports.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the identification requirements. HITRUST requires the approved user identification and authentication policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

IAC-15.5.notes: 32 asks across 7 frameworks. Overlaps IAC-19; what is distinct here is the restriction on group accounts specifically, with the correlation evidence that attributes a shared-account action to an individual.

artifacts.name: Emergency Access Procedure
