artifacts.description: The emergency access policy and procedure, the emergency access procedure document, the break-glass account procedures, the procedure for enhanced-authorisation, time-limited emergency and third-party privileged access, and the authorised role list for emergency access.

artifacts.name: Qualifying Condition Records
artifacts.description: The qualified condition definition documentation, the qualified condition assessment procedure, the immediate medical attention justification records, the reasonable judgment determination records, and the treatment material assessment evidence establishing that the emergency was genuine.

artifacts.name: Emergency Access Event Records
artifacts.description: The break-the-seal incident logs, the authorised user event records, the justification documentation per event, the direction attribution log, the healthcare professional name capture in audit logs, the platform access record verification, the emergency access audit logs, the auditable log of break-glass and third-party privileged access with justification and duration, and the tracking register.

artifacts.name: Post-Emergency Review Records
artifacts.description: The break-the-seal attestation procedure, the attestation records per event, the condition compliance verification records, the periodic review of break-the-seal events, the post-emergency access review records, and the evidence that privileged activities are logged and monitored.

artifacts.name: Cloud Master Account Controls
artifacts.description: The log documenting each use of the master account with justification, approver and timestamp; the alerting rules configured to notify the security team immediately on any master account use; the configuration evidence showing enforced multi-factor for all users accessing the cloud environment; and the address source restrictions or allow-lists for cloud access.

artifacts.name: Provider Access Prohibition
artifacts.description: The service level clause prohibiting the provider from accessing the organisation's systems, software and data; the monitoring logs and alerts for any provider access attempts; the evidence that the organisation retains sole custody of encryption keys preventing provider data access; and the access control configuration on cloud backup stores and log data covering immutability, vault lock and access lists.

IAC-15.9.notes: 33 asks across 4 frameworks. The health-sector break-the-seal regime and the cloud master-account regime are different emergency-access populations with different justification tests, and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining what constitutes privileged access, how it is provisioned and how it is overseen, with the access control policy and logical access rules standard behind it. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented least-privilege requirement; CSA CCM requires the management and segregation of privileged access roles to be documented separately.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of privileged accounts with owner, purpose and review date, the register classifying them by business impact, the administrator account inventory, and the account inventory database covering the full population. ADHICS requires evidence that normal and privileged accounts are separated for the same individual.

artifacts.name: PAM Platform Configuration
artifacts.description: The privileged access management tool configuration showing vaults, safes, policies and approvers, just-in-time elevation, non-shared access and the approval workflow, with the multi-factor configuration for administrative access.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Request and Approval Records
artifacts.description: The just-in-time approval log for privileged session requests with approvers and durations, the access request records, the workflow configuration requiring approval before provisioning, the register of personnel authorised to approve with their scope, and sample completed requests showing approver identity and date.

artifacts.name: Privileged Session Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The privileged activity monitoring logs, the session recordings enabled on privileged sessions with samples, the continuously monitored session logs, the administrator account usage audit logs, and the access monitoring logs from the platform.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic reviews of privileged accounts with sign-off by system owners, the account review records, the audit reports on privileged access with findings and closures, and the recertification evidence. Cadence differs: SOX and ISO 27001 quarterly, SWIFT CSCF and MAS TRM periodic against a documented schedule.

artifacts.name: Application and System Account Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of application and system accounts with purpose, privileges and owner, the procedure for assigning and managing them including periodic review, the configuration evidence showing least privilege for each, the review records, and the service account documentation and controls.

artifacts.name: Break-Glass Account Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented emergency access procedure with usage monitoring, showing how emergency credentials are issued, used under supervision and revoked afterwards.

artifacts.name: Least Privilege and Role Matrix
artifacts.description: The role-based access matrix mapping roles to permitted functions, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the segregation of privileged access roles, and the least-privilege configuration evidence across in-scope systems.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning and Removal Records
artifacts.description: The provisioning workflow evidence, the modification log for role changes, the removal SLA report for leavers, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Operating System Hardening Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented hardening standard for the servers carrying privileged accounts, the configuration compliance report from the hardening assessment tool, and the physical access controls protecting consoles in the data centre.

artifacts.name: Script and Automation Authorisation
artifacts.description: The script execution policy configuration, the inventory of authorised scripts, and the digital signature verification records confirming only approved automation runs with elevated rights.

artifacts.name: Control Implementation and Testing Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of implemented access, privileged, authentication, encryption and network controls organised by asset criticality, with the reports of regular testing of those controls.

artifacts.name: Access Control Context Documentation
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the identity and access management system configuration, the information asset inventory with classification, the network architecture and segmentation diagrams, and the physical access rules for the areas the privileged accounts administer.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel holding privileged access of their obligations and the monitoring applied to their sessions.

IAC-16.notes: 83 asks across 15 frameworks. Privileged accounts held by people, application and system accounts, and emergency break-glass accounts are separated because each is provisioned, monitored and reviewed differently, and PCI DSS 7.2.5 tests the second on its own.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of all privileged accounts with owner, purpose and review date; the privileged account inventory; the register classifying privileged accounts by business impact; the master privileged user list maintained by the security function; the account inventory database; and the account review records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented identity inventory, management of privileged access roles, and customer approval for agreed privileged access role requirements.

artifacts.name: Service Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The service account inventory with its ownership documentation, the service account documentation, and the service account review records covering the accounts no person logs into.

artifacts.name: Break-Glass Account Register
artifacts.description: The documented emergency access procedure with its usage monitoring, recording the accounts held outside the normal privileged model.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining privileged access definitions, provisioning and oversight; the approval documentation for privileged access; and the privileged access management controls implementing it. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented employ-least-privilege requirement.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Vault Configuration
artifacts.description: The privileged access vault configuration showing safes, policies and approvers; the platform configuration for vaulting, just-in-time elevation, non-shared access and approval workflows; the platform documentation; and the just-in-time approval log for privileged session requests with approvers and durations.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The quarterly reviews of privileged accounts with sign-off by system owners, the quarterly privileged access review with sign-off, the procedure governing periodic access reviews at least every six months including third-party and vendor accounts, the access review reports, the tracker of reviews including in-scope users, third parties and remediation status, the evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers, and the records of access removed or modified following review with timestamps.

artifacts.name: Privileged Session Monitoring
artifacts.description: The logs of continuously monitored privileged sessions, the evidence of session recording enabled on privileged sessions, the privileged activity monitoring logs, the access monitoring logs, and the activity logs from the privileged estate.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning and Removal Records
artifacts.description: The access provisioning workflow screenshots showing request, approve and provision steps; the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals; the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers; and the just-in-time privileged access requests and approvals from the management platform.

artifacts.name: Access Exception Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved access exceptions with expiry dates and compensating controls, recording the privileged grants that sit outside the role model.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones, and the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records. HITRUST requires the approved segregation of duties policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

IAC-16.1.notes: 51 asks across 11 frameworks. The privileged inventory, the service-account inventory and the break-glass register are three distinct populations; service accounts are separated because they have owners rather than users and are the population reviews most often skip.

artifacts.name: Access Control Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved access control policy defining least privilege and need-to-know, with the implementing procedure covering provisioning, modification, review and revocation, and the logical access rules standard for each system type. SBP Cloud scopes this to the full cloud workload access lifecycle including a four-eye requirement; SBP Internet Banking requires the least-privilege principle to be explicit for IB systems; CSA CCM and NIST 800-53 accept configuration evidence in place of the document.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Access Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping roles to permitted functions and permissions across key business applications, with the access inventory it is reconciled against. PISF 2026 requires it to enforce least privilege for data specifically; SOC 2 requires role-based configurations for confidential systems; ADHICS requires an access inventory or matrix maintained alongside it.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review Records
artifacts.description: Completed access recertification listings signed off by data or system owners, with the review procedure and schedule behind them. Cadence differs by framework and the evidence must satisfy the shortest applicable: SOC 2 at least quarterly, PCI DSS and QCB at least every six months, ADHICS and SOX annually with a documented schedule. PCI DSS requires third-party and vendor accounts to be in scope; SBP Internet Banking requires the cadence to be risk-ranked against system classification; SBP Cloud requires the review to be independent of the person who granted the access.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Inventory and PAM Configuration
artifacts.description: The inventory of privileged accounts with owner, purpose and review date, the PAM vault configuration showing safes, policies and approvers, the register of service, generic and administrative accounts with justification, and the mapping showing administrators hold separate accounts for routine versus privileged work.

artifacts.name: Access Change, Revocation and Joiner-Mover-Leaver Records
artifacts.description: Authorisation records for every access change with approver sign-off, the modification audit trail, removal records against the target SLA for leavers, inactivity-based revocation configuration, and the evidence that joiner-mover-leaver events synchronise into the access systems.

artifacts.name: Review Exception and Remediation Records
artifacts.description: Records of access removed or modified following a review with timestamps, the tracker showing in-scope users and remediation status, evidence of remediation for exceptions raised, the reviewer's acknowledgment of responsibility, and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Privileged Activity Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: Access and privileged activity monitoring logs, privileged session recordings where enabled, just-in-time privileged access request and approval logs with durations, and the account audit reports derived from them.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Conflict Analysis
artifacts.description: The segregation-of-duties conflict analysis over access rights with mitigation actions, conflict identification and remediation tracking, periodic SoD review reports with management sign-off, and trend analysis of conflicts over time.

artifacts.name: Privileged Authentication Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence that MFA is enforced on service, generic and administrative accounts, the password policy configuration, the four-eye (maker-checker) workflow enforced in the access-management tool, and the policy and technical enforcement restricting privileged account use to dedicated administrative machines.

artifacts.name: Workforce Clearance and Authorization Criteria
artifacts.description: The documented criteria by which access levels are determined for each workforce role, the workforce clearance procedures applied before access is granted, and the background check records supporting them.

artifacts.name: Health Information Exchange Access Records
artifacts.description: Authorisation records for access to the health information exchange, the periodic reviews of that access, the exchange audit reports, and the incident reports made to the exchange operator and the regulator. Kept separate because the access being reviewed sits on a platform the assessed facility does not administer.

artifacts.name: Emergency and Break-Glass Access Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented emergency access procedure with its usage monitoring, showing how break-glass credentials are issued, used under supervision and revoked afterwards.

artifacts.name: Financial Reporting System Access Evidence
artifacts.description: Access provisioning approvals and privilege listings for financial reporting systems, consolidation and reporting database access reports, periodic access review documentation for reporting tools, and the reconciliation system access privilege reports and workflow enforcement configuration.

artifacts.name: Confidential Data Access Records
artifacts.description: Access control lists for confidential data repositories, the request and approval records for access to confidential information, and the periodic review results covering it.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Authorization Records
artifacts.description: The remote access policy, the approved user list for VPN or equivalent remote access, and the monthly reconciliation reports confirming the live entitlement set matches the approved list.

IAC-17.notes: 122 asks across 16 frameworks. The frameworks agree on the review but differ on cadence (PCI DSS six-monthly, SOC 2 quarterly, QCB semi-annual, ADHICS annual) and on scope (SBP Cloud four-eye enforcement, HIPAA workforce clearance, DoH ADHIE exchange access). Cadence differences are stated in the review artifact rather than split across artifacts.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Prohibition
artifacts.description: The no-sharing account policy, the unique credential assignment procedure, the no-sharing acknowledgement records, the user registration and de-registration procedure, the account inventory by user, the user account creation request and approval forms, and the account revocation records for exits.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Register
artifacts.description: The inventory of group, shared and generic accounts with justification, approver and individual accountability mechanism; the shared account register; the service account inventory with owners; the temporary and third-party account procedure; and the sample management approval records for current exceptions.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Exception Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure governing exceptional use of group, shared or generic identifiers requiring management approval and individual accountability, the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls, the compensating controls documentation for shared accounts, and the compensating controls recorded against each entry.

artifacts.name: Shared Account Traceability
artifacts.description: The monitoring and audit logs ensuring traceability of actions performed via shared accounts and the access control lists preventing privileged users from reaching the log server that records them.

artifacts.name: Service Account Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of system and application accounts that can be used for interactive login, the configuration preventing interactive use where possible, the interactive login restriction evidence, the approval records for accounts where interactive use is permitted with documented business need and time limit, the monitoring and alerting on interactive use, and the password management procedures for service accounts.

artifacts.name: Credential Management Records
artifacts.description: The credential management system records, the identity system configuration evidence, the password policy with each required minimum standard configured, the password configuration export demonstrating enforced complexity, and the password policy compliance audit reports. HITRUST requires the approved password use policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Authorised User Agreements
artifacts.description: The authorised user agreement template containing all required clauses, the signed agreement records, and the periodic agreement compliance review records binding individuals to the no-sharing obligation.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning and Review Records
artifacts.description: The provisioning workflow screenshots showing request, approve and provision steps; the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals; the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers; the evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers; the privileged access requests and approvals from the management platform; the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping; and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register covering the same no-sharing expectation for physical credentials.

IAC-19.notes: 42 asks across 7 frameworks. The prohibition, the register of approved exceptions and the traceability mechanism that makes a shared account auditable are three proofs; the last is what an assessor tests.

artifacts.name: Access Control Policy and Least-Privilege Standard
artifacts.description: Management-approved policy and supporting procedures governing logical access: default-deny posture, least privilege and need-to-know, role definition, approval authority, provisioning/modification/removal steps, handling of application and system (non-human) accounts, and exception handling. Must carry scope, roles and responsibilities, version history and the approver's name, role and date. Several frameworks require evidence of periodic review - at minimum annual (HITRUST 01.i explicitly requires annual review records with reviewer, date and changes) - plus records that the policy was disseminated to and acknowledged by affected personnel.

artifacts.name: Role and Entitlement Matrix
artifacts.description: The documented access control model: every defined role or user group mapped to the permissions it carries, per in-scope system, classified by job function. Must cover all in-scope systems, name the system/data owner who approved each mapping, state the business rules behind the entitlements, and show a last-updated date. QCB and HITRUST require owner approval of the matrix itself, not just its existence; PCI DSS requires the mapping be traceable to job classification and business need.

artifacts.name: IAM Configuration and Entitlement Export
artifacts.description: Live configuration evidence from identity providers, directories, cloud IAM, applications and network devices showing the model is actually enforced: default-deny by default, RBAC/ABAC role assignments, current user-to-role and user-to-permission listings, need-to-know restrictions, and the multi-tier controls (IAM, network ACL, WAF) protecting the environment. Each export or screenshot must be dated and identify the system and the person who produced it. Entitlement reports listing each group with its members and privileges are the same artifact viewed per-user rather than per-role.

artifacts.name: Access Review and Recertification Records
artifacts.description: Completed periodic reviews confirming that granted access still matches business need, signed by the system or data owner / line manager. Must cover end-user access, privileged access, application and system (service) accounts, and access to confidential or regulated data repositories. Review cadence varies by framework - ISO 27001 accepts quarterly or bi-annual, PCI DSS requires application/system account review at defined intervals, and several regulators expect at least annual - so state the cadence applied and evidence it was met. Include the resulting revocations/changes and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry dates and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Access Request, Approval and Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: Ticket-level evidence for a sample of joiners, movers and leavers: the request, the documented business-need justification, the approver's identity and date, and the provisioning/modification/revocation action taken. Must include workflow evidence from the request tool, role-change records for movers, and revocation timeliness against the defined SLA for leavers. Network- and zone-level access authorisations and access to health information exchanges are covered by the same artifact where those systems are in scope.

artifacts.name: Privileged and Service Account Inventory
artifacts.description: Inventory of all privileged, administrative, application and system/service accounts with purpose, owner, the privileges held and justification for them, plus the restricted list of support/third-party staff holding elevated rights. Where just-in-time privilege elevation is used, include the PAM records showing each elevation request, its approval and its expiry.

artifacts.name: Data Repository Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that access to regulated data stores (cardholder data repositories in PCI DSS scope) is mediated: a documented standard requiring user access through programmatic methods such as stored procedures or parameterised queries under authorised application accounts, database configuration showing direct or ad-hoc query access is limited to named administrators with documented business need, and the permission mapping showing which application/service accounts hold query rights.

artifacts.name: Access and Security Event Logs
artifacts.description: Log extracts evidencing that access enforcement is monitored: database audit logs of queries against regulated repositories, transaction-level access records, and security event monitoring output with the detection/triage results. Logs must be timestamped, attribute the actor and the action, show the outcome, and be retained and protected against tampering for the required period.

artifacts.name: Access Control Testing and Audit Reports
artifacts.description: Independent or internal test results confirming access enforcement works as designed - access enforcement test results, audit reports on protection of critical information assets, and audit reports covering interconnected/exchange systems. Each report must state scope and methodology, findings with risk ratings, evidence references, recommendations, and management responses with remediation timelines.

artifacts.name: Information Asset and Network Service Inventory
artifacts.description: Inventory of the information assets and network services in scope, with classification, owner, custodian, status and date of last review, traceable to the source systems it was drawn from. This is what makes 'all in-scope systems' in the other artifacts a checkable claim.

artifacts.name: Network Segmentation Architecture and Access Matrix
artifacts.description: Current, version-controlled network architecture and segmentation diagrams showing trust zones, firewalls, interconnections and data flows, together with the matrix defining which users, roles and systems may cross between shared and isolated zones. Must be dated and approved, and reflect the environment as it is now rather than as designed.

artifacts.name: System and Network Hardening Baselines
artifacts.description: Documented configuration baselines and hardening checklists for applications, network devices and endpoints - including which optional features and services are enabled and the review that confirmed only required functionality is on - plus network device ruleset review records and evidence that anti-malware protection is deployed and current.

artifacts.name: Access Violation Incident Response and Escalation Records
artifacts.description: The incident response plan covering unauthorised-access and access-violation scenarios, with defined escalation paths and notification obligations to external operators and regulators (SWIFT escalation procedures, reports to the HIE operator and Department of Health where applicable), the prepared communication templates, and records of tabletop exercises testing the plan.

artifacts.name: Data Integrity and Loss Prevention Control Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence of the technical controls protecting data from unauthorised modification or disclosure once access is granted: the documented integrity controls standard (hashing, checksums, signed messages) covering databases, application services and message queues, file integrity monitoring configuration and a sample period of its alerts with triage outcomes, database tamper-proofing such as audit logging, row-level hashes or write-once journaling, and DLP/encryption deployment evidence on critical assets.

artifacts.name: Workstation and Physical Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The workstation use and acceptable-use documentation defining permitted functions and the environment workstations may operate in, workstation access control configuration, and the physical safeguards backing logical restriction: badge/biometric access logs, the visitor register, and CCTV deployment and footage retention records. Physical logs must be tamper-protected and retained for the required period with timestamp, actor, action and outcome.

IAC-20.notes: 117 manual entries collapse to 15 artifacts. Roughly a third of the input is the same four things restated: the access control policy, the role/entitlement matrix, the live IAM configuration, and the recertification records. Several framework refs pull in adjacent-but-real asks (SWIFT 5.1 incident response, HITRUST 01.v physical/CCTV, DoH workstation use, SBP Internet Banking integrity controls) - kept as their own artifacts rather than forced into the least-privilege clusters. The 54 SOC 2 collectors already produce user/role/MFA state for connected SaaS, so entitlement exports and log pulls are automated; anything requiring approval, justification or sign-off stays manual or hybrid.

artifacts.name: Access Control Model
artifacts.description: The documented access control model covering appropriate access depending on business and access need and access restriction by default; the configuration evidence showing a default-deny posture across identity systems; the evidence of least-privilege implementation across in-scope systems; the records of periodic review of the model; the need-to-know enforcement evidence; and the access justification records behind each grant. HITRUST requires the approved information access restriction policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Role Definitions and Access Matrix
artifacts.description: The documented role definitions with associated privileges classified by job function, the access control matrix, the role-based access control configuration export, the role-based access matrix enforcing least privilege for data, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the sample access provisioning records demonstrating job-classification-based least privilege.

artifacts.name: Application and System Account Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of all application and system accounts with purpose, privileges and owner; the procedure for assigning and managing them including periodic review; the configuration evidence showing they hold only the least privilege necessary; and the records of their periodic review.

artifacts.name: Programmatic Access Restriction
artifacts.description: The documented standard requiring all user access to regulated data repositories via programmatic methods, the database configuration evidence showing direct and ad-hoc user query access is limited to administrators, the permission mapping showing only authorised application and service accounts hold query rights, and the sample database audit logs of repository queries.

artifacts.name: Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers, the records of regular data-access reviews and monitoring, the access review documentation for end-user computing repositories, the periodic access review documentation for reporting tools, the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals, the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning Workflow
artifacts.description: The provisioning workflow screenshots showing request, approve and provision steps; the information access request and approval workflow; the access provisioning approvals for reporting systems; the restricted access list for support staff; and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Authentication and Segregation Controls
artifacts.description: The policy covering user authentication, access provisioning, multi-factor authentication and acceptable use acknowledgement; the configuration evidence for authentication commensurate with information classification; the acceptable use policy with its acknowledgement records on first login or annual re-acknowledgement; the register showing security-management staff duties do not create conflicts of interest; and the privileged access requests and approvals from the management platform.

artifacts.name: End-User Computing Controls
artifacts.description: The end-user computing file access permission settings, the cell and workbook protection configuration, the version history or change tracking evidence, the consolidation system access reports, and the reporting database access privilege listings.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Access Restrictions
artifacts.description: The access control policy preventing foreign intermediary access to in-country technology systems.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Data Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The sensitive data transfer controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented sensitive data transfer requirement.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register and the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records covering the areas where the regulated data is reachable.

IAC-20.1.notes: 51 asks across 9 frameworks. The access control model, the role definitions it produces and the review that confirms it holds are three proofs; PCI DSS 7.2.6's programmatic-only access to regulated repositories is a distinct technical restriction and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Privileged Utility Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of utilities capable of bypassing controls with their approval status, the system utilities inventory, the authorised utility list, and the evidence that unnecessary utilities have been removed from production systems.

artifacts.name: Utility Access Restriction
artifacts.description: The configuration restricting access to utilities to authorised administrators, the utility access control configuration, the access restriction configuration, the utility access policy, the application allow-list configuration restricting utility execution, the workflow requiring approval before sensitive utility use, and the authorisation records for utility access. HITRUST requires the approved use of system utilities policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Utility Usage Logs
artifacts.description: The log of utility program executions with user, host, command and timestamp; the utility usage monitoring logs; and the utility usage logs.

artifacts.name: Direct Data Access Controls
artifacts.description: The evidence segregating application access from direct data access, the database access privilege reports, the database administrator access review documentation, and the direct data change approval and logging evidence.

artifacts.name: Interactive Account Restrictions
artifacts.description: The inventory of system and application accounts that can be used for interactive login, the configuration preventing interactive use where possible, the approval records for accounts where interactive use is permitted with documented business need and time limit, and the monitoring and alerting on interactive use of those accounts.

artifacts.name: Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The provisioning workflow screenshots showing request, approve and provision steps; the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals; the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers; the evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers; the privileged access requests and approvals from the management platform; the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls; and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the restrictions on system utility use.

IAC-20.3.notes: 32 asks across 6 frameworks. The utility inventory, the restriction on who may run them and the log of each execution are three proofs; direct database access bypassing the application is a named case and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Access Control & Least Privilege Policy
artifacts.description: The approved, current-version policy (or policy set) establishing least privilege and need-to-know as the governing access principles. Must carry formal management/board approval with approver name, role and date, define scope and applicability, assign roles and responsibilities, state the default-deny posture required of all access control systems, and include version history. Several frameworks add specific content: separate coverage for privilege management and information access restriction, a requirement that dedicated administrative accounts be used for administrative work only, and an explicit statement of the access control model (RBAC and/or ABAC). Review cadence differs by framework - annual review with reviewer, date and changes captured is the common floor, and evidence that personnel were informed of the policy (communication records, attendee lists, delivery dates) is also required.

artifacts.name: Access Control & Privilege Management Procedures
artifacts.description: Documented step-by-step procedures or work instructions that operationalise the policy: how access is requested, authorised, granted, modified and revoked; who approves at each step; control points and exception handling. Must cover privilege management and information access restriction specifically, and include timely revocation on termination or role change. Security administration procedures covering allocation of access rights, monitoring of system use and detection of unusual activity are required by the banking frameworks.

artifacts.name: Role Definitions & Access Control Matrix (RBAC/ABAC)
artifacts.description: A role catalogue and access control matrix mapping every defined role or job classification to the specific system, application and data permissions it carries, with the business need for each. Must cover all in-scope systems and identify role owners. Frameworks differ on depth: some require the matrix to cover physical as well as logical authorisations, some require database-level role/permission mapping, some require role definitions to be explicitly tied to a documented business purpose, and one requires roles supporting transaction validation and dual control to be shown separately.

artifacts.name: Least-Privilege & Default-Deny Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration exports from the IAM platforms, directories, operating systems, applications and cloud IAM services showing that access is denied unless explicitly granted, that granted permissions match the documented role definitions, and that need-to-know restrictions are enforced. Should include ABAC/attribute policy configuration where used, evidence that each identity is uniquely identifiable (no shared accounts), and test evidence proving the default-deny behaviour (for example a newly created account with no role, or failed access attempt logs). Coverage must extend to every in-scope system component, not a sample of convenience.

artifacts.name: Access Control System & Governed Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: An inventory of the access control systems in use (directory services, IAM platforms, native OS controls, application-level IAM, AAA solutions) together with a mapping showing that every in-scope system component and information asset is governed by at least one of them. Must identify the IAM function or team accountable for operating these systems, and include the classification of the assets whose access is being governed so that gaps in coverage are visible.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning, Modification & Revocation Records
artifacts.description: Ticket-level records for the joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle: access requests with the documented business justification, the approver's sign-off, the resulting grant, role changes processed for movers, and removals on termination. Must show provisioning decisions were tied to job function and business need, not convenience. Frameworks add: evidence of the request-approve-provision workflow itself (screenshots or workflow configuration), metrics proving revocation happened within the target SLA after termination, and change tickets for access modifications in the internet banking scope.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review & Least-Privilege Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Completed access recertification campaigns with the entitlement report reviewed, the reviewer, the date, the decisions taken and the revocations actually executed, signed off by data, system or business owners. Must also cover periodic review of the access control model and of the access control system configuration itself. Cadence varies: quarterly and bi-annual reviews are both specified, one framework requires the review schedule to be risk-ranked so high-risk systems are reviewed more often, and one requires an assessment that specifically identifies over-privileged accounts with remediation actions tracked to closure. Control effectiveness test reports covering the implemented access controls are also requested.

artifacts.name: Privileged, Administrative & Service Account Inventory and Monitoring
artifacts.description: A current inventory of every privileged, administrative, system and service account, showing owner, purpose and the privileges held, plus the monitoring applied to their use. Must include: dedicated admin accounts used only for administrative work, service and application accounts capable of interactive login with the configuration that prevents such login where possible, just-in-time or PAM-brokered elevation records showing request and approval, and audit or alert logs of privileged and administrator activity. Where interactive use of a system account is permitted, the time-limited approval must be evidenced.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Matrix & Conflict Analysis
artifacts.description: A segregation-of-duties matrix for the in-scope roles, plus the conflict analysis run against actual entitlements with the mitigating actions taken for each conflict found. Must confirm administrators hold no transactional authority, and evidence dual control on sensitive processes through the approval workflow that enforces it.

artifacts.name: Access Exception & Authorization Register
artifacts.description: A register of approved deviations from the least-privilege baseline: each exception with its business justification, the named approver, an expiry date and the compensating controls applied. Must cover exceptions to restricted-session controls (personnel explicitly authorised to copy, transfer or capture sensitive data) and exceptions permitting interactive use of accounts that would otherwise be blocked.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Data Repository Access Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that access to repositories holding sensitive or regulated data is restricted beyond ordinary system access: the documented standard requiring user access through programmatic methods (stored procedures, parameterised queries) controlled by authorised applications; database configuration showing direct or ad-hoc query access is limited to named administrators with documented business need; the permission mapping showing which application or service accounts hold query rights; row- and column-level security configuration; and the data classification the restrictions are based on. Sample database audit logs of repository queries are required to show the restriction operating.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention & Remote Session Exfiltration Controls
artifacts.description: The DLP policy plus the deployed ruleset covering email, endpoint, web and cloud channels, with dashboard evidence of coverage and the alert log showing alerts triaged and investigated to closure. Must include endpoint control over removable media and DLP configuration for cloud storage, and the response playbook for a confirmed leakage event. Also covers restriction of remote-access sessions (Citrix, RDP, VDI, jump hosts) so that copy/paste, file transfer and screen capture of sensitive data are prevented, with the DLP configuration blocking exfiltration through those channels.

artifacts.name: Security Architecture, Hardening Baselines & Environment Isolation Documentation
artifacts.description: The security architecture and secure design documentation demonstrating that least privilege is applied as a design principle, together with the hardening standards and configuration baselines for in-scope systems, the verification reports showing systems match those baselines, and the record of services and features removed or disabled. Must also evidence isolation between production and non-production environments and the approvals governing access to non-production. Security engineering review records evidencing the design principles were applied are required.

artifacts.name: Access Activity Logs & Detection Use-Cases
artifacts.description: Audit logs from the access management systems showing granted and denied access decisions, sample remote-session audit logs or session recordings demonstrating the restrictions were enforced, and the SIEM detection use-case library covering unusual or unauthorised access activity. Logs must carry timestamps, actor identity and be retained for the applicable period.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control Rules & Records
artifacts.description: The documented rules and zoning for physical areas (offices, data centre, restricted labs) defining who may enter which zone, together with the badge or biometric access logs and visitor register for those zones, retained for the required period and protected from tampering. CCTV deployment evidence and footage retention records are additionally required by one framework.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan & Escalation Procedures
artifacts.description: The documented incident response plan with the escalation path and notification procedures for the in-scope platform, the communication templates used during an incident, and records of tabletop exercises that tested the plan. Requested here through the payment-messaging framework's cross-mapping to this control; the substantive evidence is normally owned by the incident response control.

IAC-21.notes: 141 manual evidence entries across 18 frameworks collapsed to 16 artifacts. Several buckets (hardening baselines, incident response plan, physical access, DLP) come from framework requirements cross-mapped to this control rather than from least privilege itself; they are retained because every entry traces to the input, but a compliance team can usually satisfy them from the owning control instead of re-collecting here.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Approval Workflow
artifacts.description: The workflow configuration requiring approval by authorised personnel before privileged access is provisioned, the register of personnel authorised to approve access requests with their scope of authority, the sample completed access request records showing approver identity and approval date, the approval documentation for privileged access, the access request records, the privileged account change requests carrying the required director and security officer approvals, and the provisioning workflow screenshots showing request, approve and provision steps.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining privileged access definitions, provisioning and oversight; the least privilege access policy; and the just-in-time access records evidencing elevation is granted for a bounded period. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented employ-least-privilege requirement. HITRUST requires the approved privilege management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of all privileged accounts with owner, purpose and review date and the privileged account inventory held per framework.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The quarterly reviews of privileged accounts with sign-off by system owners, the quarterly privileged access review with sign-off, the periodic privilege reviews, the periodic access review documentation, and the evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Platform Records
artifacts.description: The privileged access vault configuration showing safes, policies and approvers; the just-in-time approval log for privileged session requests with approvers and durations; the platform records showing those requests and approvals; the privileged access management logs; the evidence of session recording enabled on privileged sessions; and the privileged activity monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Break-Glass Account Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented emergency access procedure with its usage monitoring, covering privileged access granted outside the normal approval path.

artifacts.name: Access Exception Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved access exceptions with expiry dates and compensating controls, the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals, and the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Privileged Roles
artifacts.description: The segregation of privileged access roles. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the privilege management requirements.

IAC-21.3.notes: 38 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps IAC-16.1; what is distinct here is the approval gate before a privileged grant — the authorised approver register and the sample approvals — rather than the inventory of what was granted.

artifacts.name: Privileged Function Restriction
artifacts.description: The documented prevention of non-privileged users running privileged functions with the records demonstrating it operates, the least privilege access policy, the just-in-time access records, the evidence separating normal from privileged accounts, the service account inventory with its controls, and the privileged access management platform configuration with vaulting. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement; CSA CCM likewise for the segregation of privileged access roles requirement.

artifacts.name: Privileged Function Audit Records
artifacts.description: The privileged access logs and audit reports, the administrator audit trail capture, the activity logs, the sample privileged session recordings from the management platform, the periodic audit report on privileged access with its findings and closures, the periodic privilege reviews, the review records triggered by alerts and incidents, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved administrator and operator logs policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Inventory
artifacts.description: The privileged account inventory and the multi-factor configuration for administrative access protecting it.

artifacts.name: Emergency Elevation Records
artifacts.description: The break-the-seal tracking register, the condition compliance verification records, and the periodic review of break-the-seal events.

artifacts.name: System Utility Controls
artifacts.description: The system utilities inventory, the utility access control configuration, the authorisation records for utility access, and the utility usage monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Operating System Hardening Records
artifacts.description: The documented hardening standard for the systems in scope, the configuration compliance report from the hardening tool, and the physical access controls protecting the consoles in the data centre.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the restrictions on privileged function use.

IAC-21.4.notes: 35 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps MON-03.3 and MON-01.15; what is distinct here is the prevention of privileged function use by non-privileged users, with the audit as the check on it.

artifacts.name: Lockout Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration showing the account locked after the permitted number of invalid attempts with the required lockout duration, the account lockout policy configuration, the approved policy and application configuration enforcing lockout on consecutive failed logins, the lockout policy documentation, the lockout threshold and duration configuration, the device lockout policy configuration, the device management lockout settings, and the system security parameter settings. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limit-unsuccessful-logon-attempts requirement. HITRUST requires the approved secure log-on procedures policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Lockout Test and Compliance Evidence
artifacts.description: The test evidence demonstrating lockout enforcement, the lockout policy compliance reports, and the configuration compliance verification across the estate.

artifacts.name: Lockout Event Logs
artifacts.description: The account lockout event records, the failed logon attempt logs, the sample audit logs evidencing lockout events, and the sample logs showing lockout events, session expiries and re-authentication challenges enforced.

artifacts.name: Access Re-establishment Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for re-establishing access after lockout and the single sign-on delegation records where the unlock path runs through a federated identity provider.

artifacts.name: Session and Re-Authentication Controls
artifacts.description: The session timeout configuration covering idle and absolute limits, the documented predefined criteria for re-authenticating users on sensitive actions, elapsed time or device change, the mandatory password change frequency and history configuration, and the session timeout, idle lockout and re-authentication configuration evidence.

artifacts.name: Authentication Architecture
artifacts.description: The documented architecture of customer authentication including the identity provider, authentication broker and risk-based engine; the approved authentication policy covering enrolment, second-factor authentication, layered security, account lockout and session handling; the matrix listing each authentication control with implementation status, owner and last review date; the multi-factor configuration evidence; and the password policy configuration screenshots.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Security Records
artifacts.description: The endpoint security policy covering configuration, encryption, malware protection and remote wipe; the hardening baseline applied; the detection and response platform coverage evidence; the disk encryption coverage report; the device management enrolment report; the mobile device compliance policies; and the log of remote wipe actions on lost or stolen devices.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the lockout behaviour and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

IAC-22.notes: 40 asks across 10 frameworks. The threshold configuration, the test that proves lockout fires and the re-establishment procedure are three proofs; the last is kept separate because a lockout with no unlock path is a denial of service.

artifacts.name: Session Lock Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export enforcing an idle session timeout requiring re-authentication, the group policy or device management lockscreen configuration, the auto-lock and session timeout configuration, the auto-lock and screen-saver configuration evidence, the screen lock configuration evidence, the screen lock policy settings, the session timeout configuration, the session timeout, idle lockout and re-authentication configuration evidence, the session timeout and monitoring configuration, the timeout configuration records, and the session lock configuration documentation. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented use-session-lock requirement; CSA CCM likewise for the automatic lock screen requirement.

artifacts.name: Session Lock Verification
artifacts.description: The test evidence confirming timeout enforcement on in-scope systems, the screenshot demonstrating the session lock or re-authentication prompt after the required idle period, the configuration compliance scan results, and the workstation locking enforcement records. HITRUST requires the approved session time-out policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Clear Desk and Screen Policy
artifacts.description: The clear desk and clear screen policy document, the clear desk policy, the clear screen policy, the signed policy acknowledgements, the awareness training materials, the clear desk audit records, and the compliance audit records showing walkthrough results.

artifacts.name: Unattended Equipment Responsibilities
artifacts.description: The documented user responsibilities for unattended equipment, the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, and the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records covering the areas where equipment is left. HITRUST requires the approved unattended user equipment policy and standard with its implementing procedure, its awareness communications and its periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Secure Logon Controls
artifacts.description: The secure log-on procedure documentation, the logon banner screenshots, the authentication enforcement evidence across all systems, the authentication policy specifying strong passwords, multi-factor and adaptive authentication by sensitivity, the multi-factor enforcement configuration, and the session management logs from the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Account Management Records
artifacts.description: The account management procedures, the account review documentation, the user access authorisation records, and the terminated user account records for the sessions the lock applies to.

artifacts.name: System Configuration Documentation
artifacts.description: The system configuration documentation for the platforms carrying the lock settings.

IAC-24.notes: 51 asks across 10 frameworks. The lock configuration, the test that proves it fires and the clear-screen policy behind it are three proofs; NIST 800-53's account management asks arrive through an adjacent crosswalk and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Session Timeout Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export enforcing an idle session timeout requiring re-authentication, the session timeout policy and configuration, the auto-lock and session timeout configuration, the session timeout configuration evidence, the timeout configuration records, the group policy or device management configuration evidence, the system configuration screenshots showing the timeout settings, and the session timeout, idle lockout and re-authentication configuration evidence. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented terminate-user-sessions requirement. HITRUST requires the approved session time-out policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Session Termination Evidence
artifacts.description: The test evidence confirming timeout enforcement on in-scope systems, the screenshot demonstrating the session lock or re-authentication prompt after the required idle period, the session log records showing timeout enforcement, the session management logs, and the sample logs showing lockout events, session expiries and re-authentication challenges enforced.

artifacts.name: Re-Authentication Criteria
artifacts.description: The re-authentication procedure documentation and the documented predefined criteria for re-authenticating users on sensitive actions, elapsed time or device change.

artifacts.name: Remote Session Timeout
artifacts.description: The virtual private network idle timeout configuration and the site-to-site tunnel timer configuration terminating remote sessions.

artifacts.name: Secure Logon Controls
artifacts.description: The secure log-on procedure documentation, the logon banner screenshots, the authentication enforcement evidence across all systems, the approved lockout policy and application configuration enforcing lockout on consecutive failed logins, and the mandatory password change frequency and history configuration.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Protection Records
artifacts.description: The anti-malware deployment and update records, the removable media restriction policy with its data loss prevention and encryption configuration, and the system configuration documentation covering the endpoints the sessions run on.

artifacts.name: Unattended Equipment Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the unattended equipment expectations, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved unattended user equipment policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

IAC-25.notes: 40 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps IAC-24; a session lock leaves the session alive while termination ends it, so the timeout configuration and the re-authentication criteria are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Identity Proofing Procedure
artifacts.description: The identity-proofing procedure document, the documented procedure for customer registration and enrolment specifying the verification steps performed before activation, the identity verification procedures, the national identity document verification procedure, the channel verification procedures, the know-your-customer procedure, and the customer authentication policy covering enrolment.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Records
artifacts.description: The records of identity verification for each authorised user, the identity verification log, the on-file identity document copies, the identification material register, the workflow and screenshots showing identity verification executed at enrolment, the sample audit log of enrolments showing verification method, timestamp, agent and outcome, and the evidence that products and services are activated only after successful verification.

artifacts.name: Help Desk Verification Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure for verifying user identity before modifying any authentication factor, the sample help desk records of identity verification before factor modification, the help desk password reset standard operating procedure with its verification steps, the user identification procedure prior to reset, the self-service password reset configuration showing the identity verification step, and the password compromise handling standard operating procedure.

artifacts.name: Authentication Architecture
artifacts.description: The documented architecture of customer authentication including the identity provider, authentication broker and risk-based engine; the matrix listing each authentication control with implementation status, owner and last review date; the authentication mechanism documentation; the authentication policy and procedures; and the multi-factor authentication implementation evidence.

artifacts.name: Access Grant Records
artifacts.description: The access grant workflow with its approval logs, the privilege management procedure documentation, and the records relying on the originating facility's own authentication of the individual.

artifacts.name: Instrument Activation Controls
artifacts.description: The card activation workflow requiring explicit customer instruction, the card authentication protocol implementation, the cardholder enrolment and communication evidence, and the know-your-customer procedures applied to instrument operations.

artifacts.name: Channel Fraud Assessment
artifacts.description: The per-channel fraud vulnerability assessments and the employee and vendor due diligence records supporting the proofing decisions.

artifacts.name: Password Management Records
artifacts.description: The password configuration export demonstrating enforced complexity, the awareness communications informing personnel of the credential handling requirements, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved user password management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

IAC-28.notes: 39 asks across 6 frameworks. Enrolment proofing, help-desk verification before a credential change, and per-channel fraud assessment are three proofs; help-desk verification is kept separate because it is the most exploited path.

artifacts.name: Access Approval Matrix
artifacts.description: The approver matrix, the access provisioning policy, the access request and approval workflow, the user provisioning workflow documentation, the access authorisation procedures, and the workforce clearance procedures. HITRUST requires the approved user registration policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Access Request and Approval Records
artifacts.description: The access request forms with their approvals, the formal approvals tying access grants to documented business need, the sample access change authorisation records with approver sign-off, the access modification request forms, the manager approval documentation, the supervisor approval records, the sample of provisioned accounts with matching approvals, the before-and-after access comparison, the access provisioning approvals for reporting systems, the information access request and approval workflow, the exception approvals, and the privileged account change requests carrying the required senior approvals.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Access Model
artifacts.description: The documented access-control model enforcing least privilege, the role-based access matrix mapping job functions to access rights with approver designations, the role-based access matrix, the approved access rights policy implementing least privilege, the entitlement report demonstrating least-privilege alignment, and the segregation-of-duties conflict analysis with its mitigation actions.

artifacts.name: Periodic Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic user access review reports prioritised by risk ranking, the schedule showing review cadence for high, medium and low risk systems, the periodic access review documentation for reporting tools, the reporting database access privilege listings, the consolidation system access reports, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Transfer Notification Records
artifacts.description: The human resources transfer notification process feeding the access change requests raised for movers.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Approval Records
artifacts.description: The remote access request and approval workflow with the risk assessment performed per request.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the account approval requirements.

IAC-28.1.notes: 36 asks across 6 frameworks. The approver matrix, the request record carrying the approval and the periodic review confirming the grant is still warranted are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Security Assessment Policy
artifacts.description: The security assessment policy, the authorisation procedures, the authorisation process documentation, the risk-based decision documentation, the authorisation tracking records, and the policy review records.

artifacts.name: Assurance Programme Records
artifacts.description: The assurance initiative plans with their scope and objectives, the assurance review reports with findings and recommendations, the management action plans responding to those findings, the follow-up tracking of recommendation implementation, the internal audit plan and schedule, and the continuous monitoring programme documentation.

artifacts.name: Control Effectiveness Testing
artifacts.description: The control testing results and documentation, the technology control effectiveness assessment reports, the security control testing results and reports, and the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports.

artifacts.name: Application Security Testing
artifacts.description: The application security testing strategy and procedures, the static, dynamic and interactive testing tool deployment with their scan reports, the interface security testing reports, the interface access session logs, the security defect tracking records, and the pre-deployment remediation verification reports.

artifacts.name: System Test Records
artifacts.description: The system testing methodology documentation, the test plans covering security and performance, the requirements traceability matrix, and the change endorsement records for deviations from the requirements.

artifacts.name: End User Application Controls
artifacts.description: The end user application risk assessment procedures and the end user application approval records covering the software business functions build for themselves.

artifacts.name: AI Deployment Assurance
artifacts.description: The deployment plan covering development and deployment environments, component-level deployment and release criteria, and the approval records confirming pre-deployment requirements are met and impacts to interested parties considered.

artifacts.name: AI Test and Evaluation Records
artifacts.description: The test, evaluation, verification and validation plans; the incident response plan with the AI incident or error register; the context documentation covering intended purposes; the documented evidence demonstrating each governance and management outcome; the implementation records and artifacts evidencing them within the AI estate; and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The policy addressing risks from hardware, software and cloud vendors across the supply chain; the risk register tracking supply chain risks; the completed vendor due diligence reports; the audit or assurance reports from technology suppliers; the software bills of materials with their component analysis; and the plans for replacing or mitigating loss of critical suppliers.

IAO-01.notes: 44 asks across 7 frameworks. The assurance programme, its testing, and the authorisation decision it feeds are three proofs; MAS TRM's application security testing arrives here and is kept separate from the assurance governance.

artifacts.name: Security Assessment Plan
artifacts.description: The security assessment plan with its scope, the assessment schedule across systems and processes, the annual security testing calendar, and the security testing policy defining the test types, frequency and ownership.

artifacts.name: Assessment Results Report
artifacts.description: The assessment results report, the plan of action and milestones arising from it, the periodic evaluation reports covering both technical and non-technical findings, and the remediation plans. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented periodic assessment.

artifacts.name: Internal Control Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The documented methodology for evaluating control effectiveness, the reports from periodic internal control assessments, the control testing programme with its results, the effectiveness review reports, and the action plans addressing gaps identified.

artifacts.name: Penetration Test Reports
artifacts.description: The penetration test reports with findings and severity, the bug bounty programme reports with valid findings, the retest and closure evidence after remediation, and the documentation of the isolated test environments used.

artifacts.name: Security Testing Strategy and Plans
artifacts.description: The strategy defining testing types and coverage across the release cycle, the test plans per release including security test cases, the security acceptance test results before go-live, and the application security testing strategy and procedures.

artifacts.name: Application Security Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The static, dynamic and interactive application security testing tool deployment with their scan reports, evidencing the code and running application were both assessed.

artifacts.name: Control Effectiveness Evaluation Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix evaluating each existing control against each identified threat and vulnerability, the gap analysis report identifying deficiencies and recommended enhancements, the control testing results from adversary-simulation exercises, and the residual risk register.

artifacts.name: Comprehensive Testing Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented testing programme covering internal and external stakeholder participation, the log showing participation of business line management and response teams, and the test execution reports with results and improvement actions.

artifacts.name: Test Data Masking Evidence
artifacts.description: The standard operating procedure for masking production data in test environments where external parties are involved, and the verification evidence confirming masking was validated before external testing began.

artifacts.name: Testing Finding Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker carrying security testing findings through to closure, the remediation records, the gap analysis with its roadmap, and the re-testing performed after environmental change.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Posture Assessment
artifacts.description: The cloud security policy covering acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit; the provider risk assessment including data residency and certifications; the configuration baseline applied; the posture management scan results with remediation status; the tenant admin access review; the shared responsibility matrix; and the documented exit strategy.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The supply chain risk management policy, the risk register tracking fourth-party and concentration exposure, the vendor due diligence reports, the supplier security audit and assurance reports, the software bill of materials with its component analysis, and the critical vendor contingency plan.

artifacts.name: Audit Coverage and Findings
artifacts.description: The coverage matrix confirming audit scope across all required control domains, the annual coverage dashboard, the general controls audit reports, the remediation records, the audit workpapers and test results, and the findings and deficiency reports.

artifacts.name: Independent Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The assurance initiative plans with scope and objectives, the assurance review reports with findings and recommendations, the management action plans responding to them, the follow-up tracking of recommendation implementation, and the continuous monitoring programme documentation.

artifacts.name: Pre-Deployment Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The deployment plan covering development versus deployment environments, component-level deployment and release criteria, with the approval records confirming pre-deployment requirements are met and impacts to interested parties considered.

artifacts.name: Development Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The development standards and quality assurance test plans, the solution design documents, the procurement and build approval documentation, the test results with defect tracking, the requirements traceability matrix, and the change endorsement records for deviations.

IAO-02.notes: 81 asks across 12 frameworks. Security testing (technical) and control assessment (procedural) both land here and are kept separate: an assessor asks for the penetration test report and the internal control assessment report as distinct evidence.

artifacts.name: Application Security Testing Records
artifacts.description: The application security testing strategy and procedures, the static, dynamic and interactive testing tool deployment with their scan reports, the security test plans per release, the security acceptance test results before go-live, the retest and closure evidence, and the documentation of isolated test environments. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented automated testing requirement.

artifacts.name: Application System Review Reports
artifacts.description: The review reports identifying, documenting, testing and evaluating application controls for confidentiality, integrity and availability; the review schedule; the test evidence supporting the conclusions; and the records of control deficiency remediation arising from them.

artifacts.name: Developer Security Testing Records
artifacts.description: The developer security testing plan, the testing results and reports, and the flaw remediation documentation showing findings from developer-side testing were closed.

artifacts.name: Expert Design Review Records
artifacts.description: The security design review reports produced by specialists, the expert engagement records for those reviews, and the acquired-software security risk assessment reports with the compensating controls documented where a commercial product cannot meet the requirement.

artifacts.name: Penetration Test and Bug Bounty Reports
