artifacts.description: The penetration test reports with findings and severity, the bug bounty programme reports with valid findings, and the security testing strategy defining types and coverage across the release cycle.

artifacts.name: API Security Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The API security testing reports and the API access session logs supporting them, covering an interface class that general application testing routinely misses.

artifacts.name: Performance Test Records
artifacts.description: The performance test plans and results demonstrating smooth operation before production deployment, the output from the performance testing tooling, and the go-live sign-off confirming testing completed before deployment.

artifacts.name: Independent Data Centre Assessment
artifacts.description: The independent threat and vulnerability assessment covering the provider data centres holding material workloads, the assessor engagement letter confirming independence and scope, the mapping of each material workload to its data centre, the coverage list, the country risk report per location, the supplementary assurance reports, the findings remediation tracker with both parties' actions, and the internal audit and information security review of the results.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Posture Assessment
artifacts.description: The cloud security policy covering acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit; the provider risk assessment including data residency and certifications; the configuration baseline applied; the posture management scan results with remediation status; the tenant admin access review; the shared responsibility matrix; and the documented exit strategy.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The supply chain risk management policy, the risk register tracking fourth-party and concentration exposure, the vendor due diligence reports, the supplier security audit and assurance reports, the software bill of materials with its component analysis, and the critical vendor contingency plan.

artifacts.name: Security Assessment Plan and Results
artifacts.description: The security assessment plan, the assessment results report, the plan of action and milestones, the continuous monitoring programme documentation, and the internal audit plan and schedule.

artifacts.name: AI System Deployment Assessment
artifacts.description: The deployment plan covering development versus deployment environments, component-level deployment and release criteria, with the approval records confirming pre-deployment requirements are met and impacts to interested parties considered.

artifacts.name: AI Measurement and Evaluation Records
artifacts.description: The defined AI risk metrics with measurement methodology, the test and evaluation plans, the demonstration of validity and reliability with generalizability limitations documented, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the ongoing monitoring and periodic review records, and the implementation records evidencing the outcome within the AI lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Data Integrity Test Records
artifacts.description: The data integrity test results and the application controls audit workpapers supporting them, evidencing the processing itself was assessed rather than only its security posture.

IAO-02.2.notes: 75 asks across 10 frameworks. Distinct from IAO-02 in that these are assessments requiring specialist skill or independence — application system review, developer testing, expert design review, independent data-centre assessment — rather than the organisation's own control testing.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Standard
artifacts.description: The approved secure software development lifecycle standard incorporating industry standards and best practices, the policy embedding security activities throughout the lifecycle, the documentation of each phase with its security gates and deliverables, the evidence of security gates in each stage from requirements through retirement, and the records of security gate approvals before release.

artifacts.name: Threat Model Artifacts
artifacts.description: The threat models created during the design phase for sample projects, the sample secure design review records for in-flight projects, and the template used to capture security requirements in user stories and specifications.

artifacts.name: Secure Coding Standards
artifacts.description: The documented secure coding standards aligned to a recognised application security verification standard with language-specific guides, the documented engineering techniques addressing each common attack category including injections and data and structure attacks, and the sample code or library evidence of the mitigations implemented.

artifacts.name: Developer Security Training Records
artifacts.description: The approved secure coding training curriculum covering software security relevant to the technologies in use, the learning management records of completion at least once every twelve months for all developers of bespoke and custom software, and the sample completion certificates and acknowledgments.

artifacts.name: Code Review Records
artifacts.description: The procedure mandating pre-release reviews by knowledgeable individuals other than the originating developer, the code review checklist, the sample pull-request approvals from the source control platform showing reviewer sign-off, and the evidence of identified vulnerabilities corrected prior to release with re-review confirmation.

artifacts.name: Automated Security Testing Evidence
artifacts.description: The static application security testing reports demonstrating automated scanning or manual review, the continuous integration pipeline configuration with embedded static, dynamic and composition scans, the mapping of scanner rule sets to each attack category demonstrating coverage, the developer security testing plan, and the testing results and reports.

artifacts.name: Penetration Testing Programme
artifacts.description: The documented penetration testing methodology covering industry-accepted approaches, perimeter and critical system coverage; the review and update records for the methodology; the documentation of internal or external tester qualifications and organisational independence; the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports; the finding tracker with risk ranking, owner and remediation status; the documented risk-based remediation plan with timelines per severity; and the retest or rescan records demonstrating remediation.

artifacts.name: Public Web Application Protection
artifacts.description: The annual security assessment report covering each public-facing web application using manual or automated methods, the post-change reassessment records, the tracker of identified vulnerabilities with correction status and reassessment confirmation, the configuration export of the web application firewall or runtime protection showing it deployed in front of those applications, the evidence it operates in blocking mode or that its alerts are promptly investigated, the rule-set currency records, and the sample audit logs showing detection and blocking.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Intelligence and Ranking
artifacts.description: The inventory of vulnerability intelligence sources subscribed to, the documented risk ranking methodology aligned with industry sources for newly discovered vulnerabilities, the vulnerability management procedure covering identification and ranking, the tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status, the flaw remediation documentation, the defect tracking system records, and the software composition analysis reports for third-party components.

artifacts.name: Nonconformity and Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining handling of nonconformities including reaction, root-cause analysis, corrective action and effectiveness review; the log of nonconformities with cause analysis, similar-nonconformity checks and actions taken; the root cause analyses performed for material nonconformities; the control deficiency tracking and remediation log; the corrective action plans with timelines and status; the management reporting on control exceptions; the board reporting on significant deficiencies; the major issue escalation reports; and the records reviewing effectiveness of the corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Internal Assessment Programme
artifacts.description: The internal audit plan and schedule, the continuous monitoring programme documentation, and the security control testing results and reports.

artifacts.name: Standards Alignment Records
artifacts.description: The standards mapping and alignment documentation, the gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation, and the segregation of duties matrix with the access privilege records supporting it.

IAO-04.notes: 65 asks across 8 frameworks. Threat modelling, code review, testing and remediation are separate stages of the same pipeline and are kept apart; the web application protection artifacts (assessment, correction, web firewall) sit together because PCI DSS 6.4 treats them as alternatives to one another.

artifacts.name: Audit Findings Register
artifacts.description: The register of audit findings with control weaknesses, recommendations, owner, due date and ageing analysis. SBP ETGRMF requires a recommendation register with status tracking and an open findings register with ageing; COBIT expects assurance review reports with findings and recommendations behind it.

artifacts.name: Management Response and Remediation Plans
artifacts.description: Management's documented response to each finding: the remediation plan with timelines and owner, the corrective action plan with status, and the action item tracking through to closure.

artifacts.name: Finding Follow-up and Closure Validation
artifacts.description: The documented follow-up process for significant findings, the records of the audit function monitoring management's implementation, the independent closure validation, the escalation log for overdue findings, and the evidence that findings are integrated back into risk management practice.

artifacts.name: Plan of Action and Milestones
artifacts.description: The POA&M or equivalent plan of action recording each identified control deficiency, the milestones and resources for correcting it, and the review and update records showing it is maintained rather than written once.

artifacts.name: Control Deficiency Tracking Log
artifacts.description: The log of identified control deficiencies with remediation status, the management reporting on control exceptions, and the board reporting on significant deficiencies.

artifacts.name: Nonconformity and Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining how nonconformities are handled including reaction, root-cause analysis, corrective action and effectiveness review; the log of all nonconformities with cause analysis and checks for similar occurrences; the root cause analyses performed for material nonconformities; and the records reviewing the effectiveness of the corrective actions taken.

artifacts.name: Gap Assessment Against Standards
artifacts.description: The gap analysis against the applicable standards or target state with the roadmap addressing each gap. NIS2 expects mapping and alignment documentation against relevant international standards with the compliance assessment reports and any certification scheme participation records; QCB expects an annual gap analysis report with a remediation roadmap.

artifacts.name: Audit Plan, Workpapers and Reports
artifacts.description: The audit plan and scope, the workpapers and test results supporting the findings, the assurance initiative plans with scope and objectives, and the resulting reports.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Compliance Register
artifacts.description: The register of applicable laws, regulations and contractual requirements with the compliance assessment reports and gap analyses against them, evidence of compliance, and the external audit reports and regulatory examination findings that test it.

artifacts.name: Risk Register and Treatment Plans
artifacts.description: The risk management policy and framework, the risk register with assessments and treatment plans, risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact, and the risk response actions and monitoring reports that show deficiencies being carried as risk where they are not yet closed.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Treatment and Residual Risk Records
artifacts.description: The AI risk treatment plan with prioritisation, the residual risk register, AI impact assessments, the incident and error register, third-party AI and data risk assessments, the defined AI risk metrics with measurement methodology, and the demonstration of validity and reliability with generalizability limitations documented.

artifacts.name: Data Management Issue Tracking Register
artifacts.description: The documented data management issue tracking register and data quality support specification with their implementing procedures, the data quality profiling reports, the future-state gap assessment, the data architecture artifacts, the register or inventory evidencing each with a named owner, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Governance Committee Oversight Records
artifacts.description: The IT governance committee charter, meeting minutes and attendance records, the IT risk dashboard and metrics reviewed at those meetings, and the senior management reporting on outstanding remediation.

artifacts.name: Post-Implementation Verification Records
artifacts.description: Verification that a remediation actually corrected the deficiency: the post-implementation review report, control effectiveness verification, requirements fulfilment validation, and the lessons learned documentation.

IAO-05.notes: 104 asks across 13 frameworks. Three distinct trackers are conflated in the raw list: audit findings (SBP ETGRMF, PISF 2026, SOX, CSA CCM), management-system nonconformities (ISO 42001), and plans of action for control deficiencies (NIST 800-53 POA&M, NIST 800-171). They are kept apart because each has its own owner and closure authority.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Policy
artifacts.description: The approved, management-signed policy establishing the incident response capability - scope, applicability, roles and responsibilities, control objectives, review frequency, version history and approval evidence. Must be accompanied by its review records showing it is kept current, and by acknowledgement records where personnel are required to attest to it. NIST AI RMF adds an approved procedure for responding to previously unknown risks; HIPAA cross-maps the security program charter and security policy manual here.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan and Scenario Playbooks
artifacts.description: The operational IRP/runbook plus the scenario playbooks that make it usable: defined roles and escalation paths, and coverage of the full lifecycle - preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, reporting, remediation and lessons learned (PISF wants a checklist mapping the plan to each lifecycle stage). Playbooks must exist for the common scenarios (ransomware, phishing, data exfiltration, DDoS) and, where cross-mapped, be underpinned by a threat scenario register. Include the linked contingency, emergency response and disaster recovery procedures that the IRP coordinates with, since several sources require incident handling and contingency planning to be joined up.

artifacts.name: Incident Classification and Severity Criteria
artifacts.description: The taxonomy used to triage: incident categories, severity levels, the criteria for assigning each, and the resulting prioritisation and escalation thresholds. Must include the criteria that make an incident 'significant' and therefore externally reportable under NIS2, so that classification and notification decisions are traceable to a documented rule rather than judgement.

artifacts.name: IR Team Charter, Roster and Contact Lists
artifacts.description: Who responds and how they are reached: the IR team charter (with programme owner appointment and budget where required), the cross-functional team roster and on-call rota, the RACI or roles-and-responsibilities matrix, current internal contact details, and executed agreements with external incident response providers or retainers. Contacts must be current, not a stale appendix.

artifacts.name: Incident Register and Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The incident log or ticketing system extract for the review period, showing each incident with classification, priority, timestamps, assignee, actions taken and resolution, plus the investigation and analysis write-ups for significant cases. Must include security violation and error records, and be retained tamper-protected with timestamp, actor, action and outcome. Several sources want the monitoring and follow-up procedure that governs how open incidents are chased.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review, Root Cause and Lessons-Learned Records
artifacts.description: Completed post-incident reviews with root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, the owner and due date for each, and evidence those actions were tracked to closure and fed back into procedures, playbooks, training and testing. Include the documented RCA procedure and the preventive measures adopted as a result.

artifacts.name: External Notification Procedures, Templates and Reporting Records
artifacts.description: How incidents leave the building: the notification workflow and decision points, the escalation matrix and communication procedures, current contact details and channels for the CSIRT or competent authority, pre-approved communication templates for internal, customer, regulator and media audiences, and the completed notification records and submitted report forms for incidents that met the reporting threshold.

artifacts.name: IR Exercise and Plan Testing Records
artifacts.description: Reports from tabletop or simulation exercises - date, participants, scenario, observations, gaps identified - together with the resulting plan updates, evidencing that the plan is tested and revised rather than merely written. NIS2 additionally expects the plan's testing and update history to be shown.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Training and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Security awareness and incident-specific training: programme content, delivery and attendance records, evidence that senior management were included, effectiveness assessments, and policy acknowledgement records confirming staff know their reporting obligations.

artifacts.name: Detection and Alerting Configuration
artifacts.description: The technical detection layer feeding the process: IDS/IPS and threat-detection service configuration, defined early-warning indicators and alert thresholds, health-check/heartbeat configuration on critical security control systems, audit logging configuration, integrity monitoring and change detection tooling, and network and credential monitoring logs. Must show what triggers an alert and where that alert lands.

artifacts.name: Critical Security Control Failure Detection and Response Records
artifacts.description: The PCI DSS 10.7 set: the documented procedure for detecting and responding to failures of critical security control systems (network security controls, IDS/IPS, file integrity monitoring, anti-malware, physical and logical access control, audit logging, segmentation controls), sample failure alerts with triage, and the response records showing for each failure that security functions were restored, the cause and duration documented, security issues arising during the outage addressed, a risk assessment performed, preventive controls implemented and monitoring resumed.

artifacts.name: Forensic Readiness Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for preserving and handling evidence during an incident - collection methods, chain of custody, storage, and the forensic tooling and external support available.

artifacts.name: Incident Metrics, Trend Analysis and Programme Assessment Reporting
artifacts.description: Management reporting over the incident population: trend analysis and dashboards, SLA and service-request fulfilment compliance, mean-time-to-restore metrics for control failures, and independent or regulator-led assessment and compliance records for the incident management programme with findings and remediation tracking.

artifacts.name: AI System Incident, Third-Party and Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The AI-specific set cross-mapped from NIST AI RMF: third-party AI and data risk assessments with contractual IP clauses and ongoing monitoring records, evidence of third-party contingency arrangements, the documented procedure and executed records for superseding, disengaging or safely deactivating an AI system, and validity/reliability demonstrations documenting generalizability limitations. Supply only where AI systems are in scope.

artifacts.name: SWIFT Environment Connectivity and Credential Custody Evidence
artifacts.description: The SWIFT CSCF set cross-mapped here: connectivity architecture documentation with the approved connection method and VPN configuration, hardware token inventory with custody and destruction records, key lifecycle documentation, credential protection measures including password vault usage, and database access controls for the messaging environment. Supply only where a SWIFT-connected environment is in scope; otherwise mark not applicable.

IRO-01.notes: 120 manual entries across 19 sources collapsed to 15 artifacts. Six collectors are live (GuardDuty detector check, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, ServiceNow, Better Stack, Qovery), so alerting configuration, on-call rosters and incident tickets are partly collected already. The SWIFT CSCF 6.x/7.1 entries and the NIST AI RMF GOVERN 6.2 / MANAGE 2.x entries are loose cross-maps; they are kept as two clearly-labelled artifacts rather than mixed into the core IR set.

artifacts.name: Incident Management Policy & Procedure
artifacts.description: Approved policy and the detailed handling procedure beneath it, covering the full lifecycle - preparation, intake and detection, analysis, containment, eradication and recovery - with management approval and periodic review evidence. Must include the cloud and privacy-incident variants where those environments are in scope, and the review record must name the reviewer and date.

artifacts.name: Incident Ticket & Case Handling Records
artifacts.description: The incident record population itself: tickets or register entries showing intake, classification, assignment, containment, eradication, recovery and closure with timestamps, plus mitigation actions taken. Must reconcile to the alerting/ticketing system and be complete for the period, since this is the sample source for testing that the documented lifecycle was actually followed.

artifacts.name: Event Detection, Alerting & Triage Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence of the automated detection side of intake: inventory of alert sources, SIEM/IDS-IPS use cases and alert configuration, the event triage procedure and triage logs, and at least one worked sample showing an alert escalated into an incident ticket. Include detection effectiveness metrics and event correlation output where the framework asks for them.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Team Charter, Roster & RACI
artifacts.description: Charter establishing the response team with its authority, the current roster with named handlers and cross-functional representation, on-call schedule, and the RACI or role assignments across the lifecycle stages. Where a cloud provider shares the response, the shared RACI must show which party owns each step.

artifacts.name: Incident Classification & Severity Criteria
artifacts.description: The taxonomy and thresholds that drive handling: incident categories, severity levels with their impact assessment method, prioritisation rules, the significant-incident test, and the escalation thresholds tied to each level. Evidence should include the periodic review of those thresholds where required.

artifacts.name: Payment/Messaging Environment Monitoring & Credential Control Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration and monitoring evidence for the secure payment-messaging environment that feeds incident detection: audit logging configuration, network and integrity monitoring output, credential protection and password vault usage, VPN and connection-method approval, token inventory, custody and destruction records, key lifecycle documentation, phishing protection, and unauthorised software removal records.

artifacts.name: Incident Reporting Channels & Awareness Material
artifacts.description: Evidence that staff and users can raise an incident and know to do so: documented intake channels with screenshots or configuration, the anonymous/whistleblower route, any AI-concern or fraud reporting route, and the awareness material and training records covering the duty to report.

artifacts.name: Escalation Matrix & Incident Contact Directory
artifacts.description: Escalation matrix with criteria and timeframes per severity level, the internal and external contact directory including CSIRT/competent authority, and the backup communication mechanisms with evidence that those channels have been tested.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Playbooks & Containment Runbooks
artifacts.description: Scenario playbooks and SOC runbooks covering the common incident types in scope, each carrying the containment, eradication and recovery steps - including isolation/quarantine actions and, where relevant, decommissioning or deactivation procedures.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review, RCA & Problem Records
artifacts.description: Post-incident reports with root cause analysis and lessons learned, the resulting improvement actions tracked to closure, and the problem-management records - known-error entries, workarounds and trend analysis - where the framework expects incidents to feed problem management.

artifacts.name: Investigation Case Files & Evidence Preservation Records
artifacts.description: Forensic readiness procedure and chain-of-custody/evidence preservation records, with completed investigation case files and their outcomes, including war-room or decision logs for major incidents.

artifacts.name: Third-Party & Cloud Provider Incident Handling Agreements
artifacts.description: Contractual and operational arrangements with providers who participate in response: cloud provider incident-handling MoU or clauses granting incident and RCA access and investigation cooperation, retainer agreements with external IR services, the shared RACI, and the RCA reports actually received from providers.

artifacts.name: Incident Notification Templates & Records
artifacts.description: Communication templates used during handling and the notifications actually sent to regulators and customers for incidents in the period, together with the breach-notification procedure that governs when each is used. Detailed reporting-timeliness evidence belongs to the stakeholder reporting control.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The approved incident response plan itself - the document the procedures and playbooks hang off - covering all six lifecycle stages with roles, escalation and notification timelines, and evidence that it is implemented in each environment in scope, including cloud.

artifacts.name: IR Tabletop Exercise & Plan Test Records
artifacts.description: Reports from tabletop or simulation exercises testing the handling capability, with participants, scenario, findings and the plan updates that followed, plus records of communication-channel testing and any live seeding or mystery-shopping tests of the intake path.

IRO-02.notes: 200 entries collapsed to 15 artifacts spanning the six lifecycle stages. Ticketing, detection and contact/on-call evidence are hybrid because this control has live collectors (GuardDuty, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, ServiceNow, Better Stack, Qovery). The SWIFT CSCF entries describe a distinct payment-environment control set and are kept as one artifact rather than forced into the generic clusters.

artifacts.name: Incident Classification Scheme
artifacts.description: The severity and impact classification scheme for incidents, the severity classification matrix, the classification scheme aligned with the regulator's recommendations, the incident records showing the applied classification, and the evidence of periodic classification review for accuracy.

artifacts.name: Escalation Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented escalation procedure between tiers with its triggers and service levels, the escalation matrix and communication procedures, the escalation procedure, the incident handling workflows by severity and classification, and the escalation procedures for the payment network.

artifacts.name: Tiered Support Model
artifacts.description: The documentation of the tiered support structure with roles and escalation paths, the job descriptions and role boundaries for each support tier, the training records evidencing team understanding of tier responsibilities, and the problem management roles with their service levels.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The incident response plan documentation with classification, escalation and notification timelines; the incident management policy and procedures; the incident management procedures; the incident playbooks covering each listed step; the response team composition and contact details; the incident response team charter; the plan testing and update records; and the tabletop exercise records.

artifacts.name: Incident Records
artifacts.description: The incident tracking system records, the incident response records, the incident tickets with their classification and resolution, the incident service levels and resolution time tracking, the incident dashboard, and the post-incident review reports.

artifacts.name: Incident Trend Reporting
artifacts.description: The incident trend reports to management, the trend analyses of classified problems and errors, and the root cause analysis reports for significant incidents.

artifacts.name: Notification Procedures
artifacts.description: The notification procedures and templates, the communication templates, and the contact information for the parties to be notified at each severity.

artifacts.name: Problem Management Records
artifacts.description: The problem management procedures with their classification criteria, the classification scheme for problems and errors, the problem records with their root cause analysis documentation, the known error database with workaround documentation, the proactive problem management trend analysis reports, the problem queue dashboards, and the service management tool records showing regular classification of problems and errors.

artifacts.name: Detection Alert Configuration
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention alert configuration feeding the classification decision.

artifacts.name: AI Incident Governance Records
artifacts.description: The incident response plan with the AI incident or error register, the third-party AI and data risk assessments, the documented evidence demonstrating the governance outcome, and the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate.

IRO-02.4.notes: 49 asks across 11 frameworks. Incident classification and problem classification arrive together through COBIT and SBP ETGRMF but are different objects, so the problem-management artifacts are kept separate from incident severity.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The current, approved Incident Response Plan (or cyber crisis management plan / breach response policy) covering the full lifecycle: preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, reporting, remediation and lessons learned. It must define reportable incidents, the structure and authority of the response team, activation criteria, escalation and notification timelines, metrics for measuring the capability, resources and management support, and how incident information is shared. Several frameworks additionally require it to be explicitly aligned to business continuity/crisis objectives (PISF), to cover payment-brand and acquirer obligations (PCI DSS), and to be tailored to the organisation's own regulatory context. Provide the approved current version with version history and owner.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Playbooks and Runbooks
artifacts.description: Scenario-level playbooks that operationalise the plan, with step-by-step containment, eradication and recovery actions per incident type. Collectively the frameworks expect coverage of ransomware, phishing, data exfiltration, DDoS (with a dedicated DDoS playbook), intrusion/counter-intrusion, quarantine procedures, breach-type taxonomy, unexpected discovery of cardholder data outside the CDE (identify how it got there, remediate, prevent recurrence), and identity-theft/fraud response for customer-facing banking channels including protected-data identification. Provide the current playbook set with owners and last-review dates.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Team Charter, Roster and Contact Lists
artifacts.description: The IR team charter/RACI showing named handlers, designated responsibilities, authority and dependency levels, the cross-functional roster (security, legal, comms, business, executive) and the current on-call rota. Include the escalation contact tree and external contact lists — for PCI DSS specifically the payment brand and acquirer contacts, and for banking frameworks law-enforcement/regulator contacts. Roster and on-call data can be exported from the paging platform; charter, RACI and appointment approvals are manual.

artifacts.name: Incident Classification and Escalation Criteria
artifacts.description: The severity/category matrix used to triage incidents, together with the quantitative thresholds that trigger escalation, the indicator-of-compromise to severity mapping, early-warning indicator definitions, and the criteria that make an incident externally reportable. Frameworks also expect evidence that thresholds are reviewed and updated periodically, and (for banking) a catalogue of identity-theft and fraud threat types feeding classification.

artifacts.name: Incident Communications Plan and Notification Templates
artifacts.description: The communications plan covering who communicates with whom during an incident, plus pre-approved templates for internal, customer, regulator, law-enforcement and media messaging. Must include out-of-band/backup communication mechanisms for when primary channels are unavailable, the breach-notification process with defined timelines, and stakeholder responsibilities and escalation paths.

artifacts.name: Incident Register and Case Records
artifacts.description: The incident register plus a sample of complete case records showing the lifecycle end to end: detection source, classification, timestamps against SLA, actions taken, decision/war-room records for major incidents, recovery and closure. Frameworks variously require the register to evidence that all incidents are reported and managed per the plan, to be tamper-protected and retained, to include AI system errors and incidents, and (PCI DSS) to include records of unexpected PAN discovery and its secure deletion. Ticket data exports from the ITSM/paging platforms; war-room minutes and narrative case files are manual.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Reviews and Root Cause Analyses
artifacts.description: Formal post-incident reports for significant incidents covering timeline, impact, root cause, corrective and preventive actions with owners and due dates, plus the documented RCA methodology/template used. Also covers periodic incident trend analysis and reporting used to drive preventive measures.

artifacts.name: Breach Notification Records and Regulatory Reporting Map
artifacts.description: The mapping of legal, regulatory and contractual reporting obligations applicable to a compromise (who must be told, by when, in what form), together with evidence of actual notifications sent to regulators, customers, payment brands or supervisory authorities, timestamped against the applicable deadline.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Exercise and Test Reports
artifacts.description: Reports from incident response testing: tabletop exercises with participants, scenario, observations and lessons; response-plan testing/drills including DDoS drills where required; and tests of the backup communication channels. Frameworks expect at least annual exercising, with banking and payment regulators expecting scenario-specific drills in addition.

artifacts.name: Detection-to-Response Integration Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that monitoring output actually reaches the response process: the documented procedure linking alerts to incident response, an inventory of integrated alert sources (IDS/IPS, FIM, anti-malware, change-detection on payment pages, threat detection services), alert/detection rule configuration, and sample records of alerts triaged into incidents with disposition. Also includes the supporting monitoring configuration evidence cited by SWIFT (audit logging, integrity monitoring, change detection on the messaging environment) and data-discovery tooling configuration used to detect unexpected data. Threat-detection and alerting configuration is collector-supplied; the integration procedure and triage sampling are manual.

artifacts.name: Forensic Readiness and Evidence Preservation Records
artifacts.description: The forensic readiness procedure covering evidence identification, acquisition, chain of custody and tooling, plus completed chain-of-custody forms and forensic imaging records from recent incidents demonstrating the procedure is followed.

artifacts.name: IRP Approval, Review, Distribution and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the plan is current and available to all stakeholders: management/board approval of the plan and its revisions, the review and update log showing the plan is maintained at the defined cadence (annually at minimum, and after significant incidents or organisational change), the distribution list of who holds the plan, and awareness communications confirming personnel know their incident reporting and response responsibilities. Periodic review records should name the reviewer, date, observations and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Incident Coordination and Threat Information-Sharing Arrangements
artifacts.description: Documentation of incident dependencies on third parties and external bodies: contingency arrangements and risk assessments for third-party/AI suppliers whose failure would affect response, contractual incident-notification and cooperation terms, and formal threat-intelligence or incident information-sharing arrangements with sector bodies, regulators or CERTs. Include records showing these arrangements have been exercised or used.

artifacts.name: Board-Approved Cyber Security Action Plan and Standards Alignment
artifacts.description: For the banking and national-regulator frameworks: the board-approved cyber security action plan setting out how the institution anticipates, withstands, detects and responds to attacks, mapped to the international standard(s) adopted (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls), with the implementation tracker/dashboard, board resolution or minutes evidencing approval, periodic board progress reports, and the corresponding national-regulator compliance and assessment records for incident management.

IRO-04.notes: 133 framework-worded requests collapse to 14 artifacts. The bulk (26 entries) are restatements of the incident response plan itself; playbooks, roster/contacts, classification criteria and the incident register are the next largest duplicate groups. Detection tooling and ticketing (GuardDuty, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Better Stack, ServiceNow, Qovery collectors) already cover parts of the register and alert-integration artifacts, so those are hybrid.

artifacts.name: Breach Notification Policy
artifacts.description: The breach notification policy and procedures, the breach notification policy with regulatory timelines, the approved breach response policy and procedures, the notification process documentation, and the privacy incident handling procedures with their reporting workflows.

artifacts.name: Breach Register
artifacts.description: The breach register, the breach log and tracking system, the notification timing log against the legal requirements, and the breach notification tracking and compliance records.

artifacts.name: Breach Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The breach risk assessment methodology, the breach type taxonomy with its response playbooks, and the root cause analysis template and methodology applied to each assessed breach.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Notification Records
artifacts.description: The regulatory notification records, the supervisory authority breach reporting records, and the notification templates used for the regulator.

artifacts.name: Individual Notification Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for notifying affected individuals with the risks and protective measures, the notification template for affected individuals, the patient notification procedure and templates, the breach notification templates, and the incident communication templates for data subjects and regulators.

artifacts.name: Breach Containment Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining immediate containment actions on breach detection, the records of containment actions taken for past incidents and exercises, the cyber-breach response plan, and the counter-intrusion playbooks supporting it.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The incident response plan document with its procedures, the plan review and approval records, the distribution list for the plan, the security incident classification and prioritisation criteria, and the incident investigation and analysis reports produced under it.

artifacts.name: Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The investigation procedures, the investigation reports, the root cause analysis, and the post-incident review and lessons learned documentation.

artifacts.name: Event Triage Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedure for triaging raw events into categorised incidents, the catalogue of detection use cases with severity mapping, the runbook extract covering triage decision trees, the log export showing events assessed, closed as non-incidents or escalated, the sample ticket records showing event-to-incident decisions with justification, and the report showing correlation of related events into single incidents.

artifacts.name: Points of Contact Records
artifacts.description: The maintained points of contact for breach notification. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented points of contact maintenance requirement.

artifacts.name: Legal Disclosure Records
artifacts.description: The legal disclosure request evaluation procedures, the government and legal request tracking register, the legal counsel review documentation for disclosure requests, the records of information disclosed in response to legal requests, and the third-party breach notification clauses in contracts.

artifacts.name: Data Breach Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented data breach notification and data breach management process specifications with their compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing them, the data security control evidence including access controls, the privacy artifacts, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the compliance audit reports and assessment records.

IRO-04.1.notes: 60 asks across 11 frameworks. Notification to the regulator and notification to affected individuals are separate obligations with different clocks and different templates, so they stay apart; ISO 27001 A.5.25 event triage arrives upstream of breach handling and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The maintained incident response plan with its procedures, roles, escalation paths and recovery steps; the documented plan for cloud-hosted workloads with its cybersecurity considerations; the incident response policy and procedures documentation; and the plan with its classification, escalation and notification timelines. HITRUST requires the approved learning policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Plan Review Records
artifacts.description: The annual review records evidencing review of the plan at least every twelve months, the records of annual evaluation of the recovery plan and incident response procedures, the sign-off records for annual review completion, the plan review records, and the log evidencing plan maintenance.

artifacts.name: Lessons-Learned Update History
artifacts.description: The update history documenting changes to the plan based on lessons learned and exercise outcomes, the update history showing modifications driven by lessons learned, the post-incident review records feeding those updates, the lessons learned documentation and reports, the improvement actions, and the process improvement updates.

artifacts.name: Industry-Driven Update Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of industry source subscriptions informing the plan's evolution and the update history showing modifications driven by industry developments rather than only by internal events.

artifacts.name: Change-Triggered Update Records
artifacts.description: The log of plan updates triggered by specific changes and the records of updates made in response to business, system and network changes.

artifacts.name: Plan Test Records
artifacts.description: The annual test reports covering tabletop exercises, simulations and drills; the annual test report; and the tracker of deficiencies identified in testing with their closure status.

artifacts.name: Provider Incident Review Records
artifacts.description: The service level clause requiring the provider to conduct and share post-incident reviews for material incidents, the reviews received with the organisation's review notes, the periodic incident pack submitted to the governing committee with trends, significant events and actions, and the committee minutes evidencing that review.

artifacts.name: Incident Repository Records
artifacts.description: The incident documentation repository, the incident register with its case records, the audit logging configuration evidence, and the log review records with their follow-up case documentation.

artifacts.name: Problem Management Records
artifacts.description: The problem management procedures with their classification criteria, the problem records with their root cause analysis documentation, the known error database with workaround documentation, and the proactive problem management trend analysis reports.

IRO-04.2.notes: 38 asks across 9 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is that the plan changes in response to what is learned; the update history driven by lessons and by industry developments are two separate triggers and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Lessons-Learned Records
artifacts.description: The lessons learned documentation, the post-incident lessons-learned documentation per incident, the lessons learned documentation per incident, the register capturing lessons from internal and external events, the post-incident review reports and records, and the lessons learned recorded for each test.

artifacts.name: Improvement Action Tracking
artifacts.description: The tracker of corrective actions with defined timelines and closure, the corrective and preventive action records, the improvement actions, the improvement action plans implementing lessons to improve resilience and prevention, the post-incident improvement recommendations, the control enhancement records based on incident lessons, and the log of continuous improvements to problem and error controls.

artifacts.name: Incident Knowledge Base
artifacts.description: The knowledge database for incident diagnosis and response, the maintained known-error database with workarounds and permanent-fix status, the known error database with its workaround documentation, and the lessons learned sharing records with stakeholders.

artifacts.name: External Event Analysis
artifacts.description: The briefs analysing significant external cyber events and the lessons applicable to the organisation.

artifacts.name: Incident Trend Analysis
artifacts.description: The incident trend analysis reports and the proactive problem management trend analysis reports.

artifacts.name: Problem Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented problem and error control procedures, the problem management procedures with their classification criteria, the database of problem records with their root cause analyses, and the problem records with their root cause analysis documentation.

artifacts.name: Exercise and Test Records
artifacts.description: The incident response test procedures, the test plans and results, the tabletop exercise reports and records, the annual tabletop and simulation reports, the gap analysis reports from those tests, and the updated procedures issued after test gaps.

IRO-04.3.notes: 33 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps IRO-04.2; what is distinct here is the improvement mechanism itself — the knowledge base, the known-error database and the analysis of external events — rather than the plan update it produces.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Test Plan
artifacts.description: The incident response test procedures, the exercise planning documentation, the test plans covering broad scenarios including simulation of extreme but plausible attacks, the cyber exercise plans and scenarios, the threat-actor tactic-based scenario documentation with the threat actor analysis reports behind it, and the denial-of-service response playbook exercised against it. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented incident response testing requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the test-incident-response-capability requirement.

artifacts.name: Exercise Execution Records
artifacts.description: The annual test reports covering tabletop exercises, simulations and red-team-driven drills; the tabletop exercise reports and records; the tabletop exercise and test records; the annual tabletop and simulation reports; the reports of regular mock drills; the exercise results and observations; the governance and communication plan test records; the staff exercise participation records for unfamiliar scenarios; the exercise participant lists; the stakeholder debriefing records; and the denial-of-service drill reports.

artifacts.name: Test Findings and Improvement Records
artifacts.description: The gap analysis reports from the tests, the tracker of deficiencies identified with closure status, the tracker of loopholes identified in drills with the improvements made, the after-action improvement plans, the lessons learned documentation, the lessons learned recorded for each test, the register of findings and improvements from scenario testing, the exercise results with their improvement actions, and the updated procedures issued after test gaps.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan and Review
artifacts.description: The incident response plan documentation with classification, escalation and notification timelines; the documented plan for cloud-hosted workloads with its cybersecurity considerations; the annual review records evidencing review at least every twelve months; the update history documenting changes made from lessons learned and exercise outcomes; the communication templates and escalation procedures; and the incident register with its case records. HITRUST requires the approved incident responsibilities and procedures policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Provider Incident Review Records
artifacts.description: The service level agreement clause requiring the provider to conduct and share post-incident reviews for material incidents, the reviews actually received with the organisation's review notes, the periodic incident pack submitted to the governing committee with trends, significant events and actions, and the committee minutes evidencing review and discussion of those incidents.

artifacts.name: ICT Continuity Plan and Testing
artifacts.description: The plan for restoring services within the recovery objectives, the register of critical services with agreed objectives and dependencies, the inventory of critical systems with owners and recovery tiers, the technical failover runbooks for each critical system, the architecture diagram showing redundancy and failover paths, and the most recent test report showing achievement of the objectives.

artifacts.name: Detection Capability Evidence
artifacts.description: The system monitoring strategy, the security information platform deployment documentation, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, and the monitoring alert review records evidencing the capability the exercises assume exists.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of their incident response responsibilities and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

IRO-06.notes: 61 asks across 14 frameworks. Exercise scenarios, exercise records and the improvements they produce are kept separate because the third is what an assessor actually looks for and the first two are frequently produced without it.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The approved incident response plan or framework covering the full lifecycle — detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, closure and lessons learned — with defined roles, activation criteria, classification, escalation paths and notification timelines, and a named owner accountable for it. Cloud environments require the handling procedure to be mutually agreed with the cloud provider; internet banking requires a specific security breach response procedure; PISF 2026 expects a structured, stakeholder-wide incident management approach.

artifacts.name: ISIRT / CSIRT Charter
artifacts.description: The charter formally establishing the integrated response team, stating its mission, authority, membership drawn from cybersecurity, IT and business functions, activation and deployment expectations, and the organisation chart it sits within. Include the budget or resourcing allocation records demonstrating the team is actually resourced. Where an on-demand rapid response team exists (internet banking) or a dedicated SIRT covers cloud services, their charters count here.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Team Roster & On-Call Schedule
artifacts.description: The current roster of designated responders with primary and alternate assignments, the on-call rotation, and evidence the team can be deployed within the organisation's defined timeframe. PCI DSS requires 24/7 availability of designated personnel; ISO 22301 requires the incident management team structure with contact details; QCB requires site-level team rosters; SBP requires the SIRT and rapid response rosters with contact details. Formal designation or nomination records for each member should accompany the roster.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Roles, Responsibilities & RACI Matrix
artifacts.description: Documented allocation of responsibility across the integrated team: the RACI or responsibility matrix for incident handling showing authority and dependency levels, role descriptions and job boundaries for each function and support tier (L1/L2/L3), member nomination records, and — for outsourced or cloud services — the RACI formalising the split of responsibilities between the organisation and the provider.

artifacts.name: Contact Directory & Escalation Procedures
artifacts.description: Current contact information for responders and stakeholders together with the escalation procedure that says who is contacted at each severity and within what timeframe, including the paging and alerting configuration that implements it and the route for escalating major incidents to senior management and business continuity leadership.

artifacts.name: Incident Classification & Escalation Criteria
artifacts.description: The severity classification matrix and the thresholds that determine when an event becomes an incident, when the team is activated and when escalation occurs, including required response times and performance expectations per severity level, the activation threshold criteria for major disruption, the detection use cases mapped to severity, and records showing the thresholds are periodically reviewed.

artifacts.name: Incident Triage Runbooks & Playbooks
artifacts.description: The operational playbooks and runbooks the team actually works from: the triage procedure for turning raw events into categorised incidents with its decision trees, per-scenario response playbooks, and the monitoring and alert-handling procedures (including detection tuning and escalation) that feed them.

artifacts.name: Incident Records & Register
artifacts.description: The incident register and the underlying case records showing the team operated: tickets with full lifecycle timestamps, event assessment logs showing what was closed as a non-incident versus escalated, the classification decision and its justification, correlation of related events into single incidents, alert triage and disposition logs, and chain-of-custody or forensic imaging records where evidence was preserved. Should include a sample of recent major incidents with response times measured against the defined deployment and reporting timeframes.

artifacts.name: Incident Communication Plan & Notification Records
artifacts.description: The communication plan covering internal and external stakeholders, including the backup communication mechanisms used if primary channels are unavailable and records of those channels being tested, the designated spokesperson and subject matter experts, and the notification templates. Evidence must include actual notifications sent — senior management notification for major incidents, regulator and customer breach notifications with timestamps against the applicable SLA, and reports and coordination records for severe incidents submitted to the sector regulator (DOH under ADHICS).

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review Reports
artifacts.description: Formal post-incident reviews covering root cause, impact, timeline and remediation actions with owners, together with the war-room or coordination call minutes for major incidents, root cause analyses obtained from service providers for incidents on their side, and the periodic review records confirming the response capability itself is reassessed and corrected.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Exercise & Drill Records
artifacts.description: Records of tabletop exercises and mock drills testing the integrated team: scenario used, date, participants across cybersecurity, IT and business functions, observations, and the tracker of gaps identified and improvements made as a result.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Training & Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Training evidence for the responders and the wider workforce: programme content, attendance and completion records, evidence that senior management received training, training on tier-specific responsibilities for support staff, CSIRT-specific training records, awareness communications informing personnel how and when to report suspected incidents, and the assessments used to gauge training effectiveness.

artifacts.name: Provider Incident Cooperation Agreements
artifacts.description: The contractual instruments that pull external providers into the integrated response: the joint incident handling MoU or agreed document with the cloud/service provider, the SLA clause granting access to the provider's incident and root cause analysis reports, and the clause requiring the provider to cooperate and supply information for investigations led by the organisation.

IRO-07.notes: 102 framework evidence asks collapse to 13 artifacts. PagerDuty, Opsgenie and Better Stack collectors are already attached to this control, so on-call rosters/schedules, paging configuration and incident ticket records are marked hybrid — the tooling supplies the current state, a human must supply the charter, RACI and narrative records.

artifacts.name: Evidence Collection Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure covering identification, acquisition, preservation and handling of digital evidence; the incident evidence collection procedure; the evidence collection procedure; the evidence preservation guidelines; the forensic procedure; and the phishing evidence preservation procedure. HITRUST requires the approved collection of evidence policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Chain of Custody Records
artifacts.description: The standard form for recording custody transfers with timestamps and signatures, the chain-of-custody templates, the example completed forms from prior incidents, the chain of custody documentation, and the chain of custody records.

artifacts.name: Forensic Image Integrity Records
artifacts.description: The register of forensic images taken with their cryptographic hashes for integrity, the forensic capture records, the evidence preservation records aligned with the retention policy, and the evidence repository holding them.

artifacts.name: Forensic Capability Records
artifacts.description: The certifications of forensic staff or the retainer agreement with a forensic firm, the inventory of forensic tools in use with their licence status, the forensic tooling inventory, and the forensic accounting capability.

artifacts.name: Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The investigation procedures, the investigation reports, the root cause analysis, the exploit and vulnerability identification per incident, and the legal liaison procedures governing when an investigation becomes a legal matter.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Records
artifacts.description: The detailed step-by-step procedures for containment, eradication, recovery and closure; the incident handling procedures; the incident response records; the incident tracking system records; the incident record register; the incident register with its case records; the redacted recent incident tickets showing the full response lifecycle with timestamps; the incident coordination call minutes for major incidents; and the incident response plan with its classification, escalation and notification timelines.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Reports
artifacts.description: The formal post-incident report covering root cause, impact, timeline and remediation; the post-incident review reports; and the sent notifications to regulators and customers for breaches with timestamps measured against the applicable service level.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the evidence collection requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

IRO-08.notes: 42 asks across 7 frameworks. The evidence collection procedure, the custody form and the forensic capability behind them are three proofs; analyst qualifications and toolkit are kept separate because a procedure without capability is unexecutable.

artifacts.name: Incident Register
artifacts.description: The incident tracking system with its log reports, the incident log, the incident records, the incident ticket logs with classification, prioritisation and resolution details, the security incident tracking records, the breach register, the closure tracker, and the incident documentation and report templates behind the entries.

artifacts.name: Incident Trend Analysis
artifacts.description: The incident trend analysis reports, the incident trend analysis and reporting dashboards, and the service request fulfilment records with their service level compliance reports read alongside them.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The documented incident response procedure covering identification, classification, escalation, reporting and closure; the incident response plan with defined roles and escalation procedures; the incident and service request management procedures; and the incident response tabletop exercise records testing them.

artifacts.name: Incident Notification Contact List
artifacts.description: The incident notification contact list, the regulatory reporting contacts, the contact list review records, and the incident response team roster with its contact information.

artifacts.name: Incident Communication Plan
artifacts.description: The incident response communication plan, the backup communication mechanisms, the communication channel testing records, the security incident communication templates with their notification records, the breach notification procedures with their templates, and the investigation report sharing logs.

artifacts.name: Incident Escalation Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix defining which incidents are significant enough to require governing committee review, the records of significant incident submissions to that committee, and the report submission records evidencing escalation occurred.

artifacts.name: Management Incident Reporting
artifacts.description: The periodic incident management information submitted to senior management and the governing committee, the management information reports on incidents, logs and breaches reviewed periodically, the minutes of senior management meetings evidencing that review, and the template aligned with the regulator's reporting format used for time-bound regulatory reports.

artifacts.name: Board Cyber Briefing Records
artifacts.description: The periodic briefing pack submitted to the board covering cyber security action plan developments and implementation status, the board minutes evidencing receipt, discussion and direction on those updates, the summary report on major threats and attacks faced with estimated operational impact, and the calendar of periodic cyber security reporting to the board.

artifacts.name: Event Triage Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedure for triaging raw events into categorised incidents, the catalogue of detection use cases with severity mapping, the runbook extract covering triage decision trees, the log export showing events assessed, closed as non-incidents or escalated, the sample ticket records showing event-to-incident decisions with justification, and the report showing correlation of related events into single incidents.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The audit log review procedures and schedule, the sample audit log review reports, and the access report review documentation supplying the situational picture the incident register is drawn from.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review Records
artifacts.description: The post-incident reviews and the corrective action tracking arising from them.

artifacts.name: External Information Sharing Records
artifacts.description: The coordination records with the sector regulator for cybersecurity information, the information sharing community memberships, the threat intelligence subscriptions and feeds, and the priority information identification process determining what is shared.

IRO-09.notes: 54 asks across 12 frameworks. The incident register, the contact list and the reporting up to management are three distinct proofs; SBP ETGRMF's board-level cyber briefing pack is kept separate from operational incident reporting because they answer to different audiences.

artifacts.name: Incident Repository
artifacts.description: The incident documentation repository, the incident record register, the incident records, the incident tickets with their classification and resolution, the incident documentation and report templates, the incident dashboard, and the incident service levels with their resolution time tracking.

artifacts.name: Root Cause and Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: The root cause analysis reports for significant incidents, the corrective and preventive action tracker, the corrective action tracking, the closure tracker, the impact assessment, and the post-incident reviews.

artifacts.name: Trend and Improvement Records
artifacts.description: The incident trend reports to management, the trend analysis reports, the incident metrics, the lessons learned documentation and reports, the improvement recommendations, and the process improvement updates arising from the repository.

artifacts.name: Evidence Preservation Records
artifacts.description: The incident evidence collection procedure, the chain of custody documentation, the evidence preservation records aligned with the retention policy, and the investigation report sharing logs.

artifacts.name: Breach Reporting Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for identifying established security breaches and reporting them to the payment systems regulator, the documented criteria distinguishing established breaches from suspected or unconfirmed events, and the incident management procedures behind them.

artifacts.name: Quarterly Regulatory Submissions
artifacts.description: The standard submission template containing all prescribed header fields, the mapping documentation explaining how breach data is captured against the prescribed columns, the quarterly reports submitted to the regulator covering the last four quarters, the internal review and approval workflow records for each submission, the regulator acknowledgments confirming receipt, and the tracker of all submissions with quarter-end date, submission date, submitter and acknowledgement.

artifacts.name: Breach Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The detailed impact analysis reports covering effects on the institution's business, systems, applications and customers.

IRO-09.3.notes: 40 asks across 7 frameworks. Overlaps IRO-09; what is distinct here is the repository as a durable record and the quarterly regulatory submission drawn from it, which is kept as its own artifact set.

artifacts.name: Incident & Breach Reporting Procedure
artifacts.description: Approved procedure defining who reports which incidents to whom and by when, covering all three audiences: internal stakeholders, affected clients/third parties, and regulators. Must state the event that starts the clock (detection vs. awareness) and every applicable deadline - 1 hour for critical incidents, 24-hour early warning, 48-hour and 72-hour breach reports, and periodic/quarterly submissions - plus internal approval before submission and a regulatory reporting map showing which authority, form and channel applies to each incident and breach type across the jurisdictions in scope.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: Approved incident response plan showing that stakeholder and regulatory reporting is built into the response lifecycle, not bolted on: defined roles and escalation path, notification decision points and timelines, alignment with the business continuity plan, and evidence the plan is reviewed, tested and updated. Some frameworks additionally require documented management approval of the plan.

artifacts.name: Incident Severity & Breach Determination Criteria
artifacts.description: Documented criteria used to decide whether and how fast to report: severity/impact levels, the significant-incident test, the breach-determination and risk-of-harm assessment method, cross-border impact criteria, and configured notification thresholds. Must be specific enough that two responders classify the same incident the same way, and must map each classification to the reporting obligation it triggers.

artifacts.name: Regulatory & Stakeholder Contact Directory
artifacts.description: Current, maintained contact list for incident notification: competent authority/CSIRT, sector regulator and law-enforcement hotline, payment brands and acquirers, key clients, and the internal response team with on-call coverage. Evidence must show the list is reviewed periodically and kept current, including designated points of contact and any media spokesperson.

artifacts.name: Incident Notification Templates
artifacts.description: The template set used for reporting: early-warning/initial, intermediate and final report forms for regulators (including prescribed submission forms), plus notification letters for clients, data subjects and patients, and press/holding statements. Templates must carry the mandatory fields each regulator expects - incident description, timeline, impact, affected parties, measures taken and root cause in the final report.

artifacts.name: Regulatory & Authority Notification Records
artifacts.description: The notifications actually filed during the audit period, with the submission timestamp and the authority's acknowledgement or receipt for each - covering every regulator in scope and both incident and breach filings, plus periodic/quarterly returns where required. Include the small number of nil returns or the statement that no reportable incidents occurred, so the population is complete.

artifacts.name: Affected Client & Data Subject Notification Records
artifacts.description: Procedures and executed notices for affected clients, service recipients, patients and data subjects, including the remedial guidance given to them and any customer-facing advisories (for example phishing warnings). Records must show who was notified, when relative to the deadline, and through which channel.

artifacts.name: Incident & Breach Register with Reporting Timeliness Log
artifacts.description: Single register of incidents and breaches with, for each entry, detection date, awareness date, classification, notification deadline, actual notification date to each recipient, and whether the deadline was met. This is the artifact auditors sample from, so it must reconcile to the ticketing/alerting system and to the filed notifications.

artifacts.name: Internal Escalation & Management Reporting Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that internal stakeholders were informed: senior management and board incident notifications, management information packs and governance reporting on incidents, internal approval of outbound notifications, and any internal audit or compliance review of notification timeliness.

artifacts.name: Incident Reporting Channels Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that reporting channels exist and work: the formal intake channel (hotline, mailbox, portal or form) with screenshots or configuration, the anonymous/whistleblower route, and the internal-and-external communication plan that governs their use during an incident, including any external channel for reporting adverse impacts.

artifacts.name: Incident Reporting Awareness, Training & Drill Records
artifacts.description: Awareness material and training on the duty to report suspected incidents and the timeframe for doing so, with attendance records and, where required, effectiveness assessment and separate senior-management training. Include communication drills and tabletop exercises that specifically exercised stakeholder and regulator notification.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Report & Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: Final incident reports with root cause analysis and the corrective/recurrence-prevention actions tracked to closure, including the RCA methodology or template used and, where the framework requires it, accountability or disciplinary outcomes.

artifacts.name: Threat & Incident Information-Sharing Arrangements
artifacts.description: Agreements and membership records for sharing incident and threat information with authorities and peer/sector groups, plus the sharing protocol, records of voluntary reports and indicator sharing, advisories received or issued, and membership change or withdrawal notifications.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Breach Notification Clauses & Oversight Records
artifacts.description: Contract clauses that oblige suppliers, service providers and acquiring partners to notify the organisation of incidents within a defined time, together with the SLA and right-to-audit terms and the ongoing third-party assessment or monitoring records, plus any incident/fraud reports received from those parties.

artifacts.name: Incident Reporting Roles & Accountability Evidence
artifacts.description: Documentation of who owns incident reporting: appointment letter and job description for the accountable officer (CISO or equivalent), the organisation chart placing the function, and the roles-and-responsibilities section of the response plan showing named escalation and notification owners.

IRO-10.notes: 208 entries collapsed to 15 artifacts. Clustered by real-world document: the procedure, the plan, the criteria, the contact list, the templates, the submissions, the register, and the supporting records. Framework-specific report forms (BPRD, Annexure-I, HHS, DOH/ADHIE, QCB/MOI, US-CERT, NIS2 24h/72h, DORA initial/intermediate/final) are the same two artifacts - a template set and a submission record set - and are consolidated as such, with the differing clocks named in the descriptions.

artifacts.name: Breach Reporting Procedure
artifacts.description: The breach notification policy and procedures, the procedure specifying the critical and non-critical reporting timelines to the regulator and national response team, the procedure for reporting incidents to the banking regulator within the prescribed window with its defined triggers, the breach notification procedure to the health information exchange and its regulator, the breach reporting procedure, the privacy incident handling procedures with their reporting workflows, and the notification procedures.

artifacts.name: Notification Templates
artifacts.description: The notification templates, the breach notification templates, the reporting template aligned with the regulator's prescribed format, and the patient notification procedure and templates.

artifacts.name: Submitted Notification Records
