artifacts.description: The records of breach notifications submitted with timestamps, the copies of actual incident reports submitted using the prescribed template, the acknowledgement emails confirming receipt, the breach report records to the regulator and operator, the notification records with timestamps, the regulatory notification records, and the supervisory authority breach reporting records.

artifacts.name: Reporting Timeliness Log
artifacts.description: The log demonstrating adherence to the reporting timelines, the reporting timing logs, the notification timing log against the legal requirements, and the compliance audit of notification timing.

artifacts.name: Breach Register
artifacts.description: The breach register, the breach log and tracking system, the log of reportable incidents with triage, reporting decision and submission timestamps, and the breach risk assessment methodology determining which incidents are reportable.

artifacts.name: Reporting Contact List
artifacts.description: The incident notification contact list, the regulatory reporting contacts, the external contacts held for notification, the contact list review records, and the incident response team roster with its contact information.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan
artifacts.description: The incident response plan with its defined roles and escalation procedures, the security incident communication templates with their notification records, and the incident response tabletop exercise records testing whether the reporting works under pressure.

artifacts.name: Breach Notification Accountability
artifacts.description: The documented data breach notification specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the data security control evidence including access controls, the privacy artifacts, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability.

IRO-10.2.notes: 42 asks across 10 frameworks. Each regulator sets a different clock and a different template; the reporting-timeliness log is kept as its own artifact because it is the only evidence the clocks were met.

artifacts.name: Serious Incident Criteria
artifacts.description: The documented criteria distinguishing established breaches from suspected or unconfirmed events for reporting purposes and the critical incident reporting procedure with its immediate reporting service level.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Reporting Procedures
artifacts.description: The procedure for reporting incidents to the banking regulator within the prescribed window with its defined triggers, the procedure specifying the critical and non-critical reporting timelines to the regulator and national response team, the procedure mandating breach reporting to the relevant sectoral response team, the breach notification procedure to the health information exchange and its regulator, the procedure referencing the framework requirements and subsequent regulatory directives, the documented procedure for identifying established security breaches and reporting them to the payment systems regulator, the hotline reporting procedure, and the reporting template aligned with the regulator's prescribed format.

artifacts.name: Submitted Notification Records
artifacts.description: The records of breach notifications submitted with timestamps, the copies of actual incident reports submitted using the prescribed template, the acknowledgement emails confirming receipt, the sample redacted incident notification communications demonstrating timely submission and completeness, the regulator notification records, the authority notification log, the notification records with timestamps, the records of incident notifications to sectoral regulators and response teams, the quarterly breach reports submitted with their acknowledgments, and the tracker of those quarterly submissions.

artifacts.name: Reporting Timeliness Log
artifacts.description: The log demonstrating adherence to the reporting timelines, the log of reportable incidents with triage, reporting decision and submission timestamps, and the compliance audit of notification timing.

artifacts.name: Root Cause and Recurrence Prevention
artifacts.description: The root cause analysis reports for reported incidents including findings, corrective actions, preventive actions and responsibility fixing; the tracker of actions from incident reviews to prevent recurrence with owners and status; and the records demonstrating responsibility-fixing outcomes where applicable.

artifacts.name: Breach Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The detailed impact analysis reports covering effects on the institution's business, systems, applications and customers.

IRO-10.5.notes: 32 asks across 6 frameworks. Overlaps IRO-10.2; what is distinct here is the seriousness threshold and the responsibility-fixing that follows a serious incident, with each regulator's clock preserved.

artifacts.name: Internal Reporting Channel
artifacts.description: The formal incident reporting channel documentation, the incident reporting procedures, the reporting channels documentation, the reporting mechanism documentation, the designated point of contact records, and the escalation matrix routing what is reported. HITRUST requires the approved reporting information security events policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Weakness Reporting Records
artifacts.description: The weakness reporting procedure, the weakness reports received, and the awareness materials on reporting encouraging staff to raise them. HITRUST requires the approved reporting security weaknesses policy and standard with its implementing procedure and its awareness communications.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Help Desk
artifacts.description: The incident response help desk or hotline documentation, the support resource availability records, the user communication templates, the helpdesk operating model, and the tiered escalation procedure behind it.

artifacts.name: Customer Help Desk Records
artifacts.description: The published help desk contact details covering a round-the-clock hotline, mail address and in-application channel addressing lost credentials, fraud and identity theft; the standard operating procedure for handling those case types; the sample help desk logs demonstrating that handling; and the screenshots showing the contact details on the website, mobile application and customer portal.

artifacts.name: Fraud Reporting Channels
artifacts.description: The fraud reporting channel documentation, the dedicated fraud reporting mail address and telephone line, the customer advisory on fraud detection, the investigation reports arising, and the mystery shopping or seeding records testing whether the channel works.

artifacts.name: Client Notification Procedures
artifacts.description: The client notification procedures, the notification templates, the protection measure advisories issued to clients, and the client communication records evidencing they were sent.

artifacts.name: Authority Communication Protocols
artifacts.description: The stakeholder and authority communication protocols governing who contacts the regulator and when.

artifacts.name: Reporting Awareness Training
artifacts.description: The security awareness programme content covering how and when to report, the topic coverage matrix, the training material decks and learning modules, the training attendance records, the training effectiveness assessments, the senior management training evidence, the awareness records on incident reporting requirements, and the training records for the front-line staff who receive reports.

artifacts.name: Incident Register and Reports
artifacts.description: The incident register with its case records, the incident reports, the incident response plan with its classification, escalation and notification timelines, and the third-party agreements and risk assessment records extending the reporting obligation to providers.

IRO-11.notes: 50 asks across 8 frameworks. The internal reporting channel for staff, the customer-facing help desk and the regulator or client notification are three distinct audiences and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Incident Response & Problem Management Policy and Procedures
artifacts.description: The approved policy and supporting procedures governing incident handling, breach response and problem management, including the criteria for classifying a problem, the requirement to perform root cause analysis, and the assignment of an owner for the policy. Must name the personnel/roles the policy is distributed to, define the review frequency and the events that force an off-cycle review, and cover the full incident lifecycle end to end. Healthcare and banking sources additionally require a dedicated breach response procedure and evidence of top-management approval.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Plan, Playbooks & Team Charter
artifacts.description: The operational IRP with the incident response team charter, current roster and contact details, the incident classification taxonomy, the escalation matrix, notification timelines, communication templates, per-scenario playbooks (including breach types) and the forensic readiness procedure. Cloud-hosted scope requires a cloud-specific IRP variant. Must be current, version-controlled, and show the integrated team of security, IT and business representatives that conducts after-action reviews.

artifacts.name: Root Cause Analysis Reports
artifacts.description: Completed RCA records for escalated incidents, problems and significant test failures, produced against a documented RCA methodology or template. Each must identify the underlying cause (not just the symptom), the exploited weakness or vulnerability where applicable, the contributing factors, and the fixes required to prevent recurrence. Banking sources also expect the breach source, nature and reasons to be mapped, and remediation findings recorded alongside the investigation output.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Review / Lessons Learned Reports
artifacts.description: After-action review records for incidents that met the escalation threshold, and for IRP tests and training exercises. Each report must capture what happened, what worked and failed in the response, the lessons drawn, and the specific changes to be made to controls, documentation and training. A standard template plus completed instances covering the reporting period are both requested; PCI requires review after each significant incident, and several sources expect a maintained lessons-learned register rather than loose documents.

artifacts.name: Corrective & Preventive Action Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker showing every improvement action raised from incidents, RCAs, post-incident reviews and external event analysis, with owner, priority, target date, current status and evidence of closure. Must demonstrate that RCA outputs convert into permanent fixes rather than workarounds, and that recurrence-prevention actions are followed through. Banking sources additionally require records where accountability was fixed on individuals or functions.

artifacts.name: Incident Register & Case Records
artifacts.description: The central incident and problem register (or ticketing system export) with individual case records for the period, showing classification, timeline, actions taken, linkage to the RCA and lessons-learned output, and closure. Must include environmental/facility incidents where those are in scope, and be complete enough to evidence that every escalated incident received an after-action review.

artifacts.name: Known Error Database / Incident Knowledge Base
artifacts.description: The maintained knowledge base of known errors, diagnoses and workarounds built from resolved incidents and problems, showing it is used by responders to speed diagnosis and response. Evidence should show entries created from recent RCAs and that the base is accessible to the incident response and service teams.

artifacts.name: Incident Metrics & Trend Analysis Reports
artifacts.description: Periodic reporting on incident volumes, categories, response times, recurrence rates and emerging trends, used proactively to identify problems before they cause incidents. Must show the analysis feeding improvement recommendations, and demonstrate whether recurrence of previously analysed incidents is falling.

artifacts.name: Regulatory & External Incident Notification Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for reporting incidents to regulators, CERTs and other external parties, plus the notifications actually submitted in the period, the internal approval workflow behind them, acknowledgements received, and a submission tracker. Where a prescribed template applies (e.g. an annexure form mandated by the banking regulator), both the blank template and completed submissions are required, with breach cause detail included.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Test & Tabletop Exercise Reports
artifacts.description: Reports from IRP tests, tabletop exercises and simulations, including scope, participants, scenario, observed gaps and the deficiency tracker showing gaps through to closure. Cloud and banking sources require testing at least annually; results must be shown feeding back into plan updates and training content.

artifacts.name: Incident Documentation Review & Update History
artifacts.description: Records showing the incident response policy, plan and procedures are reviewed at the defined frequency and after triggering events, with a version/change history that ties specific updates back to lessons learned from real incidents and tests. Must identify the reviewer and the approval date for each revision.

artifacts.name: Awareness & Training Updates Driven by Lessons Learned
artifacts.description: Evidence that lessons learned are disseminated and change what people are taught: updated awareness or training content traceable to specific incidents, records of lessons shared with affected stakeholders, and briefs analysing externally reported events at peer organisations. PCI additionally expects proof of subscription to industry threat and incident information sources.

artifacts.name: Risk Register & Impact Assessment Updates from Incidents
artifacts.description: Impact assessments performed for significant incidents and the resulting updates to the risk register or risk assessment, showing that realised incidents adjust the organisation's assessed likelihood and impact and drive control changes.

artifacts.name: Third-Party / Cloud Provider Post-Incident Reports & Governance Minutes
artifacts.description: For outsourced and cloud-hosted services: the contractual or SLA clause obliging the provider to deliver a post-incident review, the PIR reports actually received from providers, and the incident packs escalated to the governing committee together with the minutes recording their review and decisions.

artifacts.name: Security Log Review & Follow-Up Records
artifacts.description: Audit logging configuration for the systems in scope plus records of the periodic log reviews, showing that detected anomalies were opened as cases and followed through to resolution — the detection path that feeds incidents into the lessons-learned process.

IRO-13.notes: 113 framework asks collapse to 15 artifacts. No connectors are attached to this control, so nothing is fully automated; the register, CAPA tracker, metrics and log-review items are marked hybrid because they are exports from an existing ITSM/SIEM system of record that still need human curation and sign-off. The dominant duplication was 'RCA report' vs 'post-incident review' vs 'lessons learned' — kept as two artifacts (the causal analysis, and the improvement review) because several frameworks demand both distinctly.

artifacts.name: Authority Contact Directory
artifacts.description: The contact list of authorities, the contact directory for the regulator and law enforcement, the documented points of contact for response team coordination, and the authority contact procedures governing their use.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Reporting Procedure
artifacts.description: The incident reporting procedures, the procedure specifying the critical and non-critical reporting timelines to the regulator and national response team, the breach reporting procedure with its equivalent timelines, the hotline reporting procedure, and the external reporting documentation.

artifacts.name: Notification Records
artifacts.description: The records of incident notifications to sectoral regulators, response teams and the national response team with timestamps; the records of breach notifications submitted with timestamps; the authority notification log; the regulator notification records; the incident reporting records to authorities; the reports to the sector regulator for severe incidents; the incident report examples; and the fraud reports submitted to the regulator.

artifacts.name: Reporting Timeliness Log
artifacts.description: The log demonstrating adherence to the reporting timelines, measuring notifications against the statutory clocks rather than merely recording that they were sent.

artifacts.name: Response Team Charter
artifacts.description: The response team organisation chart and charter, the member nomination records, the communication and response protocols, the training records, the budget allocation records, the incident response team roster with its contact information, and the records of liaison with organisational, sectoral and national response teams.

artifacts.name: Communication Plan
artifacts.description: The internal and external communication plan, the communication logs, the public relations and communications inclusion in the incident response playbooks, the security incident communication templates with their notification records, and the incident response plan with its defined roles and escalation procedures.

artifacts.name: Information Sharing Records
artifacts.description: The threat information sharing protocol and the sharing records with the regulator and law enforcement, and the coordination records with the sector regulator for severe incidents.

artifacts.name: External Communication Records
artifacts.description: The customer communication procedures for security incidents, the external audit communication protocols, the public-facing security and privacy disclosures, and the service level agreements with security provisions governing outward communication.

artifacts.name: Exercise Records
artifacts.description: The incident response tabletop exercise records testing whether the contacts and clocks work under pressure.

artifacts.name: Breach Notification Accountability
artifacts.description: The documented data breach notification specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the data security control evidence including access controls, the privacy artifacts, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability.

IRO-14.notes: 44 asks across 7 frameworks. The contact directory, the reporting procedure with its statutory clocks, and the record that a notification was actually made within them are three proofs; the timeliness log is what an assessor samples.

artifacts.name: Device Management Enrolment
artifacts.description: The device management platform records, the device management deployment, the device management configuration evidence, the report from the platform showing enrolled devices against workforce count, the device enrolment register, and the teleworking and mobile asset inventory. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented control-mobile-device-connection requirement. HITRUST requires the approved mobile computing and communications policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Device Compliance Policy Configuration
artifacts.description: The device management compliance policies covering passcode, jailbreak detection and application restrictions, the device password enforcement configuration, the endpoint hardening baseline applied, the container policy separating corporate data, the media encryption configuration, the disk encryption coverage report, the portable device access authentication evidence, and the device management policy and configuration.

artifacts.name: Remote Wipe and Locate
artifacts.description: The remote wipe configuration, the remote wipe capability documentation, the log of remote wipe actions performed on lost or stolen devices, and the remote wipe action logs. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remote locate requirement.

artifacts.name: Personally-Owned Device Controls
artifacts.description: The personally-owned device policy and usage agreements, the authorisation records, the risk assessment covering that population, and the signed acknowledgements from the users concerned.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Protection Records
artifacts.description: The endpoint security policy covering configuration, encryption, malware protection and remote wipe, and the detection and response platform coverage and policy screenshots.

artifacts.name: Data Protection on Mobile
artifacts.description: The data loss prevention tool configuration with its reports, the transport encryption configurations, and the removable media policy with its encryption controls covering data leaving a managed device.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the mobile computing requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

MDM-01.notes: 34 asks across 8 frameworks. Enrolment, the policies pushed to enrolled devices, and remote wipe are three proofs; personally-owned device controls are kept separate because they carry a consent dimension corporate devices do not.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Policy
artifacts.description: The maintenance policy, the maintenance procedures documentation, the preventive maintenance policy document, the policy review records, the commissioning, maintenance and decommissioning procedures, and the device and media control policy. HITRUST requires the approved equipment maintenance policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Programme Goals
artifacts.description: The documented preventive maintenance plan goals linked to system objectives, the management approval memo for those goals, and the mapping of goals to specific asset groups.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Schedule and Records
artifacts.description: The planned maintenance schedule covering all critical equipment with intervals, the maintenance schedule and calendar, the history of work orders showing preventive and corrective maintenance performed, the maintenance activity records and logs, the facility maintenance logs, the security-related repair records, and the modification documentation with its approvals.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Personnel Controls
artifacts.description: The list of approved internal and vendor engineers permitted to maintain equipment, the records showing vendor engineers supervised while on site, the hardware and media tracking procedures, and the movement authorisation records for equipment leaving for repair.

artifacts.name: Pre-Maintenance Data Protection
artifacts.description: The records showing sensitive data removed or protected before equipment leaves for repair.

artifacts.name: Environmental Maintenance Procedures
artifacts.description: The documented environmental control procedures with their preventive maintenance schedules, escalation paths and incident response actions, and the facility management responsibility matrix.

artifacts.name: Support Contracts
artifacts.description: The active support agreements with original equipment manufacturers for critical equipment and the supplier maintenance documentation library.

artifacts.name: Secure Development and Procurement Records
artifacts.description: The secure development lifecycle documentation and procedures, the secure procurement policy with security requirements written into tender documents, the security testing results for systems before deployment, and the vulnerability handling and disclosure policy.

artifacts.name: Facility Access and Review Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the maintenance requirements, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

MNT-01.notes: 35 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps MNT-02; what is distinct here is the maintenance policy and programme goals rather than the individual controlled maintenance event.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Schedule
artifacts.description: The planned maintenance schedule covering all critical equipment with intervals, the preventive maintenance schedule with dates, activities and responsible teams for prioritised assets, the maintenance schedule and calendar, the maintenance schedules, and the maintenance schedule and records held per framework. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented perform-system-maintenance requirement. HITRUST requires the approved equipment maintenance policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Work Orders
artifacts.description: The history of work orders showing preventive and corrective maintenance performed, the maintenance work orders, the work-order records, the maintenance activity records and logs, the execution log of completed preventive maintenance activities, the equipment service reports, the maintenance records, the facility maintenance logs, and the security-related repair records.

artifacts.name: Authorised Maintenance Personnel
artifacts.description: The list of approved internal and vendor engineers permitted to maintain equipment, the authorised maintenance personnel list, and the records showing vendor engineers supervised while on site.

artifacts.name: Pre-Maintenance Data Protection
artifacts.description: The records showing sensitive data removed or protected before equipment leaves for repair.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Review Records
artifacts.description: The maintenance review documentation, the minutes of management reviews of preventive maintenance results, the performance report on maintenance effectiveness covering equipment downtime and mean time between failures, the modification documentation with its approvals, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Support Contracts
artifacts.description: The active support agreements with original equipment manufacturers for critical equipment, the maintenance agreements, and the supplier maintenance documentation library.

artifacts.name: Equipment Lifecycle Procedures
artifacts.description: The commissioning, maintenance and decommissioning procedures governing equipment from installation to disposal.

artifacts.name: Fault Logging Records
artifacts.description: The fault logging records with the awareness communications informing personnel how to raise them. HITRUST requires the approved fault logging policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Facility Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register and the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records covering maintenance visits.

MNT-02.notes: 38 asks across 9 frameworks. The maintenance schedule, the work order record and the controls over the engineer performing it are three proofs; data sanitisation before equipment leaves is kept separate because it is the security-specific step.

artifacts.name: Logging and Monitoring Policy
artifacts.description: The approved audit and accountability policy defining what is logged, retention, protection and review requirements, with its approval records and the implementing procedures. CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the document; PISF 2026 requires the requirements to be defined and approved before implementation evidence is assessed.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Detection Configuration
artifacts.description: Alert configuration covering failure of every critical security control system — network security controls, IDS/IPS, file integrity monitoring, anti-malware, physical access controls, logging mechanisms and segmentation controls — with the health-check or heartbeat configuration behind it and sample failure alerts. PCI DSS requires this for service providers and, separately, for all entities.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Response Records
artifacts.description: The documented response procedure covering restoration of the security function, identification and documentation of cause and duration, identification and remediation of the root cause, assessment of whether further action is needed during the outage, and resumption of monitoring; with sample incident response records for past failures, mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Centralised Log Collection Configuration
artifacts.description: The centralised logging architecture documentation, log collection configuration and coverage reports, the log source inventory with frequency and retention per source, and the SIEM ingestion dashboard showing collection health.

artifacts.name: Log Protection and Retention Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration showing log tamper protection, append-only writes and access controls, the retention rules configured in the archive, alerting on log gaps or logging service disruption, and the retention policy with evidence that it is being met.

artifacts.name: Detection Tooling Deployment Evidence
artifacts.description: Deployment documentation and configuration for the detection estate: IDS/IPS, endpoint and network detection and response, server monitoring, and anti-malware, with the SIEM deployment documentation and the system monitoring strategy behind them.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Alert Review and Response Records
artifacts.description: Records of alerts triggered by monitoring with the review, triage and response actions taken, the alert triage and escalation procedures, and the incident response records arising from them.

artifacts.name: Anomaly Investigation and Tracking Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for addressing exceptions and anomalies identified during log review including escalation and investigation, sample investigation records, and the tracker of anomalies with resolution status and closure evidence.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Scope, Roles and Coverage
artifacts.description: The documented monitoring scope and coverage report across environments and assets, the monitoring roles and responsibilities matrix, the standard operating procedures with responsibility assignments, the in-scope asset and process register, the monitoring tool inventory, and the alerting and escalation criteria.

artifacts.name: Network Flow Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: Network flow logging configuration, the flow analysis tool documentation, and the flow log review procedures and records.

artifacts.name: API and Service Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The API monitoring dashboard and alert configuration, with the investigation records for suspicious API activity.

artifacts.name: Security Posture Reporting
artifacts.description: The continuous monitoring procedure defining proactive monitoring of information assets and security controls, the monitoring tooling configuration evidence, and the posture and risk-profile dashboard reported to management.

artifacts.name: Privileged Activity Log Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of periodic review of administrator and privileged activity logs, and the access control lists and user access review documentation that identify whose activity is privileged.

artifacts.name: IT Operations Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: Operations monitoring logs and infrastructure event records, facilities and environmental management records, standard operating procedures for IT operations, outsourced service management reports, and the performance monitoring framework with its dashboards, conformance reports and corrective action tracking.

artifacts.name: Health Information Audit Review Records
artifacts.description: The audit log review procedures and schedule for systems holding electronic protected health information, sample review reports, access report review documentation, the security incident tracking records arising from them, and the security programme charter and violation log they sit under.

artifacts.name: Data Operations Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented information security operations management artifacts held under the national regulator's regime, the evidence of compliance, and the regulator's own assessment records.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Centre Documentation
artifacts.description: The security operations centre or managed provider operational documentation, its roles and responsibilities, the runbooks and playbooks for specific alert types, shift handover records evidencing continuous coverage, and the threat hunting reports produced.

MON-01.notes: 107 asks across 15 frameworks. Overlaps MON-01.8 heavily; the distinguishing demands kept here are PCI DSS 10.7 critical-control failure detection and response, which is about the monitoring apparatus failing rather than about what it detects, and COBIT's operations-monitoring scope.

artifacts.name: Detection Sensor Deployment
artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing sensors deployed at boundaries between security domains aligned to risk classification, the deployment topology for internal and external sensors, the deployment documentation, the deployment architecture, and the validation report confirming all required boundaries have coverage.

artifacts.name: Detection Rule Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export of sensors with their active signature sets and tuning, the detection and prevention configuration, the alert configuration, the catalogue of detection use cases mapped to a recognised adversary technique framework, the log of detection rule changes and tuning actions over time, the detection rule tuning records, the tuning and alert records, and the configuration of continuous monitoring across systems and networks for breach detection.

artifacts.name: Signature Currency Records
artifacts.description: The signature and engine update records evidencing currency of detection capabilities and the signature update logs from the deployed sensors.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage Records
artifacts.description: The sample alerts with personnel response and triage records, the alert triage and disposition logs, the sample breach and anomaly alerts with their triage, the monitoring alert review records, the alert triage and escalation procedures, the sample alerts from the deployed sensors, and the shift handover documentation showing continuous monitoring.

artifacts.name: Alert Response Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented response procedure for detection alerts with its on-call rotation, the detailed procedure for proactive monitoring including monitoring frequency, alert tuning and escalation, the playbooks for responding to specific alert types, the incident management policy and procedures, the incident playbooks covering each listed step, and the incident response records arising.

artifacts.name: Rapid Response Team Records
artifacts.description: The charter of the nominated rapid response team with its mission, authorities and immediate-response responsibilities; the roster of members with on-call rotation and contact details; the detailed security breach response procedure covering detection, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned; and the sample records of breach response activations demonstrating immediate response.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Strategy and Coverage
artifacts.description: The strategy document defining operations centre scope, coverage and detection goals; the system monitoring strategy; the report showing monitoring coverage across environments and assets; the security information platform deployment documentation; the log monitoring and alerting evidence; the anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records; the operations centre procedures; the detection effectiveness metrics; and the preventive and detective control catalogue.

artifacts.name: Threat Hunting Reports
artifacts.description: The proactive threat hunting engagement reports with their findings, evidencing detection beyond what the deployed rules already catch.

artifacts.name: Anti-Spoofing Controls
artifacts.description: The documented standard listing the source address ranges blocked at ingress, the configuration evidence of anti-spoofing controls, and the sample log entries showing spoofed source addresses dropped at the perimeter.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configurations, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, the malware protection deployment and update records, and the access control lists with the user access review documentation covering the monitoring platform.

MON-01.1.notes: 52 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps NET-08 on deployment; what is distinct here is the monitoring and response wrapped around the sensors, so the rapid-response team and breach response procedure are kept as their own artifacts.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Management Configuration
artifacts.description: The privileged access platform configuration for vaulting, just-in-time elevation, non-shared access and approval workflows; the platform configuration for privileged operating-system accounts with vaulting; the platform documentation; and the privileged access management controls it enforces. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented management of privileged access roles, segregation of privileged access roles, and customer approval for agreed privileged access role requirements.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Register
artifacts.description: The register classifying privileged accounts by business impact, the privileged account inventory, the separate system administrator accounts evidencing privileged identities are distinct from daily ones, and the records of user access rights grants showing least-privilege application.

artifacts.name: Privileged Session Records
artifacts.description: The logs of continuously monitored privileged sessions, the sample privileged session recordings from the management platform, the session recordings, the administrator session monitoring logs, the account activity logs, the activity logs, and the evidence that privileged activities are logged and monitored.

artifacts.name: Privileged Activity Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: The privileged activity logging configuration, the administrator audit trail capture, the sample logs covering each listed privileged activity, the sensitive data access logging configuration, and the monitoring logs and alerts for privileged and administrator activities.

artifacts.name: Privileged Activity Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic activity review reports, the periodic audit report on privileged access with its findings and closures, the review records triggered by alerts and incidents, the access log review records, the anomalous access investigation reports, the monitoring alert review records, the review evidence, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved administrator and operator logs policy and standard with its implementing procedure and its awareness communications.

artifacts.name: Break-Glass Access Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for enhanced-authorisation, time-limited emergency and third-party privileged access and the auditable log of break-glass and third-party privileged access with justification and duration.

artifacts.name: Administrator Segregation of Duties
artifacts.description: The segregation of duties matrix confirming administrators have no transactional authority and the formal security administration procedures for allocating access rights, monitoring system use and detecting unusual activities.

artifacts.name: Detection Use-Case Library
artifacts.description: The detection use cases for identifying unusual or unauthorised activity, the security information platform deployment documentation, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, and the system monitoring strategy behind them.

artifacts.name: Operating System Hardening Records
artifacts.description: The documented operating system hardening standard for the systems in scope, the configuration compliance report from the hardening tool, and the physical access controls protecting the consoles in the data centre.

artifacts.name: Integrity Verification Records
artifacts.description: The data integrity verification mechanism documentation, the hash or checksum implementation evidence, the integrity monitoring tool configuration, the software code integrity verification records, and the release traceability documentation.

MON-01.15.notes: 52 asks across 11 frameworks. Overlaps MON-03.3 on privileged logging; what is distinct here is the oversight wrapped around it — the privileged access management platform, break-glass handling and the segregation matrix that limits what an administrator may do.

artifacts.name: Security Monitoring Strategy
artifacts.description: The strategy document defining operations centre scope, coverage and detection goals; the system monitoring strategy; the report showing monitoring coverage across environments and assets; the architecture diagram showing monitoring coverage across attack types; the inventory of automated cyber monitoring solutions; and the operations centre performance dashboard.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Platform Deployment
artifacts.description: The security information platform deployment documentation and evidence, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, the inventory of provider log sources integrated with the platform, the gateway log forwarding configuration, the system event monitoring configuration, and the log management policy and procedures with the retention and protection configuration records.

artifacts.name: Detection Use-Case Library
artifacts.description: The catalogue of detection use cases mapped to a recognised adversary technique framework, the use-case and correlation rule list, the export of correlation rules targeting cloud-specific threats, the real-time monitoring use cases, and the log of detection rule changes and tuning actions over time. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented security monitoring and alerting requirement.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage Records
artifacts.description: The alert triage and escalation procedures, the alert threshold settings with their escalation procedures, the alert volume and triage metrics, the monitoring alert review records, the records of alerts from cloud-specific rules with their triage and closure for a sample period, the reports from automated tools showing tracked cyber attack categories, the operations centre procedures, the playbooks for responding to specific alert types, and the shift handover documentation showing continuous monitoring.

artifacts.name: Daily Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented daily log review procedure listing the required categories, the sample daily review records with reviewer name, date, scope and findings, the reviewer sign-off log, and the dashboard or saved-search exports analysts use for those reviews.

artifacts.name: Anomaly Detection Configuration
artifacts.description: The anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records, the evidence of machine-learning detection tooling with model performance metrics, and the real-time monitoring dashboard screenshots.

artifacts.name: Threat Hunting Reports
artifacts.description: The proactive threat hunting engagement reports with their findings, evidencing detection beyond what the alert rules already catch.

artifacts.name: Multi-Layer Monitoring Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing firewalls, secure sign-on, dual authentication with triangulation and real-time event monitoring; the matrix showing multi-layer control coverage across assets; the firewall rulebase with its periodic review evidence; and the dual authentication configuration with triangulation of access.

artifacts.name: Transaction Monitoring Deployment
artifacts.description: The real-time fraud monitoring deployment and the transaction monitoring across the online, teller-machine and point-of-sale channels.

artifacts.name: Forensic Capability Records
artifacts.description: The forensic tooling inventory and the forensic accounting capability available when monitoring output requires investigation.

artifacts.name: Interface Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The interface monitoring dashboard with its alert configurations and the suspicious interface activity investigation records.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Policy and Review Records
artifacts.description: The audit logging configuration evidence, the log review records with their follow-up case documentation, the awareness communications informing personnel that system use is monitored, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved monitoring system use policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

MON-01.2.notes: 54 asks across 10 frameworks. The tooling, the detection content it runs and the human review of what it produces are three proofs. PCI DSS 10.4.1's daily review is kept separate from continuous alerting because it is a distinct, sampled obligation.

artifacts.name: Control Failure Detection
artifacts.description: The procedure for detecting and addressing failures of each listed critical security control system, the service-provider variant of that procedure, the alert configuration covering network security controls, intrusion detection, integrity monitoring, anti-malware and physical access controls, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, the sample failure alert logs, and the sample failure alerts with their triage and resolution records.

artifacts.name: Control Failure Response
artifacts.description: The documented response procedure covering restoring security functions, identifying and documenting cause and duration, and resuming monitoring; the response records demonstrating prompt addressing of critical control failures; the sample incident response records for past failures with all required response steps documented; the mean-time-to-restore metrics; and the lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Log Anomaly Alerting
artifacts.description: The configuration of alerts on log gaps or logging service disruption and the ingestion dashboard showing log ingestion health.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage Records
artifacts.description: The alert triage and escalation procedures, the anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records, the monitoring alert review records, the operations centre procedures, and the log monitoring and alerting evidence. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented security monitoring and alerting requirement.

artifacts.name: Anomaly Handling Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for addressing exceptions and anomalies identified during log review including escalation and investigation, the sample investigation records for anomalies identified in review, and the tracker of anomalies and exceptions with resolution status and closure evidence.

artifacts.name: Daily Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented daily log review procedure listing the required categories, the sample daily review records with reviewer name, date, scope and findings, the reviewer sign-off log, and the dashboard or saved-search exports used for those reviews.

artifacts.name: Logging Policy and Coverage
artifacts.description: The policy defining what to log, retention, protection and review requirements; the inventory of log sources covered with frequency and retention per source; the centralised logging architecture documentation; the log collection configuration with its coverage reports; the retention rules configured in the log archive; the configuration showing log tamper protection, append-only storage and access controls; and the evidence of periodic review of administrator and privileged activity logs.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The audit logging configuration documentation, the audit log samples from the systems holding regulated data, the audit log review procedures and reports, and the log retention policy with its supporting evidence.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Platform Deployment
artifacts.description: The security information platform deployment documentation, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, and the system monitoring strategy behind the alerting.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation, and the segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records.

MON-01.4.notes: 47 asks across 8 frameworks. PCI DSS 10.7 — detecting failure of a security control itself — is the distinguishing demand here and is kept entirely separate from ordinary alerting, because a silent monitoring failure is invisible in alert volume.

artifacts.name: Integrity Monitoring Configuration
artifacts.description: The integrity monitoring tool configuration applied to critical system, configuration and content files with its comparison cadence; the file integrity monitoring deployment; the file integrity monitoring configuration with its alerts; the integrity monitoring tools; the hash or checksum implementation evidence; the data integrity verification mechanism documentation; and the hash and signature verification records.

artifacts.name: Monitored File Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of monitored critical files with the rationale for including each, scoping what the tool watches.

artifacts.name: Comparison Frequency Records
artifacts.description: The records demonstrating the evaluation cadence meets the required interval and the targeted risk analysis defining the comparison frequency where the default interval is not used.

artifacts.name: Integrity Alerts and Response
artifacts.description: The sample alerts for unauthorised modifications, additions or deletions with their response records; the sample alert logs; the triage records demonstrating alerts are investigated and addressed; the monitoring alert review records; and the sample alerts and response records for detected payment-page modifications.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Integrity Monitoring
artifacts.description: The integrity monitoring configuration applied to audit log files and the central log store and the alert rule configuration generating alerts on log modification attempts. HITRUST requires the approved protection of log information policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Payment Page Tamper Detection
artifacts.description: The configuration of the change and tamper-detection mechanism alerting personnel to unauthorised modification of payment pages.

artifacts.name: Change Control Reconciliation
artifacts.description: The change control documentation and the software integrity verification records against which detected changes are reconciled, distinguishing an approved change from an unauthorised one.

artifacts.name: Source Repository Integrity
artifacts.description: The version control repository access reports, the repository access control configuration, the commit history samples with ticket references, and the release baseline tagging evidence.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Platform Records
artifacts.description: The security information platform architecture covering host and network data sources, the inventory of integrated log sources feeding it, the platform configuration, the active correlation rule set export, the sample logs of configuration changes detected and forwarded to it, the sample access logs from critical applications, the sample logs of privileged access collected by it, the system monitoring strategy, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, the infrastructure monitoring tool configurations with their alert rules, the configuration monitoring and baseline comparison reports, and the vulnerability scanning schedules, tools and reports.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Protection Records
artifacts.description: The anti-malware and endpoint protection deployment evidence, the application allow-listing documentation, and the software installation restriction policies and controls covering the files under monitoring.

artifacts.name: Backup Integrity Procedures
artifacts.description: The backup integrity procedures confirming the copies used to restore a modified file are themselves unaltered.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records for the monitoring platform, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the log protection requirements.

MON-01.7.notes: 48 asks across 9 frameworks. The monitored-file scope, the alert configuration and the triage of what fires are three proofs; PCI DSS separates integrity monitoring of audit logs from integrity monitoring of critical files and that distinction is preserved.

artifacts.name: Logging and Monitoring Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy defining which security events are captured, on which systems, with what retention and what integrity protection, and the procedure implementing it. CIS CSC expects an audit log management process document with a logging requirements specification; SOC 2 expects the defined security events to be enumerated; SBP ETGRMF requires log-integrity protections to be named in the policy.

artifacts.name: Audit Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration evidence showing which events are logged on each system class, the auditable events list with the rationale for its selection, and sample logs demonstrating capture. HIPAA scopes this to systems holding electronic protected health information; SBP Cloud to cloud activity logging with retention settings; SOX to the systems in the financial reporting scope.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The review procedure with assigned reviewers and the completed review records naming reviewer, date, scope and findings. Cadence differs and the evidence must satisfy the shortest applicable: PCI DSS requires daily review of security events and logs of security-critical components with a separate risk-based periodic review of everything else, supported by a targeted risk analysis defining that frequency; HIPAA, HITRUST and SBP Internet Banking require a regular predefined cadence with assigned reviewers; QCB requires daily log monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Anomaly Investigation and Escalation Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for handling exceptions and anomalies identified during review including escalation and investigation, sample investigation records, the tracker of anomalies with resolution status and closure evidence, and the escalation records for suspicious activity.

artifacts.name: SIEM Architecture and Ingestion Evidence
artifacts.description: The architecture of the logging and SIEM infrastructure showing collection, transport and storage, the ingestion health dashboard, the log source inventory with frequency and retention per source, and the monitoring coverage report showing which environments and assets are in scope and which are not.

artifacts.name: Detection Use Cases and Tuning Records
artifacts.description: The catalogue of detection use cases mapped to an adversary framework, the alert configuration derived from them, the log of detection rule changes and tuning actions over time, and the anomaly detection tool configuration and tuning records.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity and Retention Configuration
artifacts.description: The retention configuration and the integrity controls protecting logs from alteration: write-once or immutable storage, hashing, vault lock, segregated log-server access and checksums, with the compliance evidence that retention is actually being met. SBP Internet Banking requires ten-year retention for internet-banking security logs with a compliance report verifying the age of the oldest retained log and tamper-evident storage across that period.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Runbooks and Coverage
artifacts.description: The security monitoring strategy defining scope, coverage and detection goals, the playbooks for responding to specific alert types, the shift handover records evidencing continuous coverage, and the security operations centre procedures.

artifacts.name: Cloud Monitoring Operating Model
artifacts.description: The security operations operating model and 24x7 roster (internal or outsourced) demonstrating continuous coverage of the cloud estate, the executed provider contract or SLA where outsourced covering scope, response times and reporting, cloud-specific incident runbooks, shift handover logs for a sample period, and the monthly KPI and KRI reports including mean time to detect and respond.

artifacts.name: Authentication Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for monitoring and reporting authentication controls with senior management approval, the operational dashboards covering login success and failure, MFA failures, lockouts and anomalies, sample authentication anomaly alert logs with triage records, and the periodic monitoring reports issued under the approved mechanism.

artifacts.name: Data Activity Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration for continuous logging of data access, processing and security events, the alerting rules and sample alerts for unauthorised data activity, and the anomalous access alerting rules covering cloud data and workload access patterns.

artifacts.name: Privileged and Highly-Classified Account Review Records
artifacts.description: The login audit trail configuration and the review evidence for highly classified accounts, together with the periodic access review reports covering the accounts whose activity is being monitored.

artifacts.name: Threat Hunting and Indicator Search Records
artifacts.description: Proactive threat hunting engagement reports with findings, and the indicator-of-compromise hunting evidence showing the estate was searched against current intelligence rather than only alerted on.

artifacts.name: Security Alert Advisory Monitoring
artifacts.description: The records demonstrating that security alerts and advisories from vendors and authorities are monitored and acted upon, and that the set of logged events is periodically reviewed and updated in response.

artifacts.name: Quarterly Compliance Review Records
artifacts.description: The service-provider procedure for quarterly compliance reviews including scope, methodology and reviewer independence, the latest four quarters of reports, evidence the reviews were performed by personnel other than those responsible for the task reviewed, management sign-off, and the remediation tracker.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Scope and Tooling Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented monitoring scope, the monitoring tool documentation and inventory, the monitoring reports produced, and the monitoring procedures with alerting and escalation criteria.

MON-01.8.notes: 104 asks across 19 frameworks. Log review cadence is the main point of divergence and is stated inside the review artifact rather than split across artifacts: PCI DSS daily for security-critical components and risk-based for the rest, HIPAA and SBP Internet Banking periodic with assigned reviewers, SBP Internet Banking ten-year retention against everyone else's shorter horizon.

artifacts.name: Logging and Audit Log Management Policy
artifacts.description: The approved logging policy and standard defining what must be logged, the event types selected and the rationale for why they are adequate for after-the-fact incident investigation, log content requirements, retention periods, protection requirements, review frequency, and the process for periodically reviewing and updating the list of logged events. Must include the auditable-events list itself and the overall system monitoring strategy. NIST 800-171 requires separate documented policy or procedure evidence for each capability (create and retain, review and update logged events, correlate review and reporting, audit reduction and report generation, protect audit information, and restrict audit management to privileged users).

artifacts.name: SIEM and Centralised Log Management Architecture
artifacts.description: Architecture documentation and deployment evidence for the centralised log platform (Splunk, Sentinel, Elastic, or equivalent), showing how logs are forwarded promptly from every source into a central repository, the platform inventory, and the collection topology. PCI DSS requires the architecture to explicitly show prompt backup or forwarding from external-facing technologies; SBP Internet Banking requires the architecture to cover both host and network data sources; ADHICS requires the deployment evidence to be tamper-protected and retained; PISF 2026 requires coverage of critical assets, remote access and privileged accounts.

artifacts.name: Log Source Inventory and Ingestion Coverage Report
artifacts.description: The inventory of log sources integrated with the SIEM - per source, the log types, collection frequency and retention - reconciled against the asset inventory to show coverage gaps. Must include ingestion health evidence (forwarder status, backup execution records) and explicit coverage for the categories each framework names: external-facing technologies such as web servers, firewalls and IDS/IPS (PCI DSS); cloud provider and service provider logs including CloudTrail, VPC Flow, GuardDuty, Azure Activity, Defender and GCP Audit Logs (SBP Cloud, CIS CSC); sensitive assets (CIS CSC); VPN and virtual machine logs (QCB); and host, network, security appliance and application sources for internet banking (SBP Internet Banking).

artifacts.name: Endpoint, Network and Application Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration exports proving the required detail is actually being logged at source, not just that a collector exists. Covers: detailed audit logging configuration with log-content verification, DNS query logging, URL and web proxy logging, command-line and PowerShell/Bash logging, sensitive-data access logging, audit trail configuration on critical devices, virtual machine logging, and cloud activity logging with retention settings. CIS CSC also requires the analysis procedures that accompany the DNS, URL and command-line log types.

artifacts.name: Log Retention and Storage Capacity Evidence
artifacts.description: Retention configuration per log type in the active platform and the archive (cold storage, immutable or WORM tier), with verification that retention is enforced centrally. Must include storage capacity planning, ongoing storage utilisation monitoring and the documented procedure for expanding capacity before logs are lost, plus the enterprise log server archive itself. ADHICS requires retention to be configured and evidenced per log type.

artifacts.name: Time Synchronisation (NTP) Configuration
artifacts.description: Evidence that all log-producing systems synchronise to an authoritative, controlled time source so events can be correlated across repositories: the NTP or time-source configuration, the approved upstream time hierarchy, and monitoring or alerting that detects drift and synchronisation failure.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity Protection and SIEM Access Control Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration and records showing audit information and audit tooling are protected from tampering and restricted to authorised staff: append-only or immutability/WORM settings on active and archived logs, access control lists on the SIEM and log stores, and evidence that audit-log management functions are limited to privileged users. ADHICS additionally requires records showing SIEM operator independence from the teams whose activity is being logged; NIST 800-171 requires operating records, not just configuration, for both protection and privileged-user restriction.

artifacts.name: Correlation Rules and Detection Use Case Catalogue
artifacts.description: Export of the active SIEM correlation rules, detection use cases and alert configurations, mapped to the event categories the frameworks require. Must cover cloud-specific threats such as IAM abuse, root console use and impossible travel (SBP Cloud), anomalous data and workload access patterns, gaps or disruption in the logging service itself (ISO 27001), and the security event set specified for internet banking (SBP Internet Banking). Include IDS/IPS configuration, any UEBA or ML anomaly-detection tooling with its model performance metrics, and the tuning records for anomaly detection thresholds.

artifacts.name: Log Review and Analysis Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that logs are actually reviewed at the defined frequency, with results reported to the defined roles. Must include the documented review procedure and the completed review records naming reviewer, date, scope and findings. PCI DSS requires this daily, listing the categories reviewed (security events, CDE component logs, logs of all critical system components) with a reviewer sign-off log showing consistent daily completion; ISO 27001 requires periodic review of privileged and admin activity logs; SBP Cloud requires periodic access review reports derived from cloud activity logs with anomalies investigated; NIST 800-171 requires operating records for review, correlation across repositories, and audit reduction and report generation. Include the dashboards and saved searches analysts work from.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage, Investigation and Escalation Records
artifacts.description: The SOC operating procedures - alert triage, severity classification and escalation criteria, and the incident response plan they feed into - together with a sample of alerts worked end to end: investigation notes for anomalous access or unusual activity, incident tickets from the tracking system, closure records, and post-incident review reports with lessons learned. Include alert volume and triage metrics (QCB) and tuning/closure records for cloud-specific rules over a defined sample period (SBP Cloud).

artifacts.name: Sample Log Extracts from In-Scope Systems
artifacts.description: Actual log samples proving the configured collection is producing usable records, drawn from the systems each framework names: account activity logs, privileged access and PAM session records for sensitive operating systems, VPN session logs, database activity monitoring output, cloud activity logs capturing access to cloud data and workloads, configuration-change events forwarded to the SIEM, critical application access logs, and network monitoring logs. Samples must be timestamped, attributable to an actor, and cover a representative period.

artifacts.name: SWIFT Connectivity and Operator Credential Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: SWIFT-specific artifacts required alongside centralised logging: documentation of the SWIFT connectivity architecture and approved connection method with its approval record, VPN configuration for the secure zone, the hardware token inventory with custody procedures, key lifecycle documentation and token destruction records, and evidence of operator credential protection - password vault usage, credential monitoring, and anti-phishing measures. Collect these only where SWIFT CSCF is in scope.

artifacts.name: SOC/SIEM Establishment Business Case and Approval
artifacts.description: For organisations standing up or expanding monitoring capability: the documented requirement analysis and feasibility assessment for establishing or acquiring a SOC/SIEM capability, and the approved management decision record resulting from it. Required by PISF 2026 as the governance trail behind the monitoring capability.

MON-02.notes: 146 entries from 14 frameworks collapsed to 13 artifacts, all input entries assigned exactly once. This control has heavy connector coverage (20 collectors listed, including CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, SentinelOne), so most technical artifacts are marked automated. The 11 SWIFT CSCF entries are kept as one separate artifact - they describe SWIFT secure-zone connectivity and operator credential protection rather than centralised log collection, and folding them into a logging artifact would misdescribe what a team has to collect.

artifacts.name: Log Source Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of log sources covered with frequency and retention per source, the inventory of provider log sources integrated with the aggregation platform, the inventory of integrated alert sources feeding incident response, the cloud provider log integration, the service provider log collection configuration, the network flow logging configuration, the sensitive data access logging configuration, and the ingestion dashboard showing log ingestion health.

artifacts.name: Correlation Rule Configuration
artifacts.description: The event correlation rules documentation, the use-case and correlation rule list, the export of correlation rules targeting cloud-specific threats, the advanced threat management solution evidence, the address reputation and threat intelligence integration, the behavioural scoring and fraud analytics deployment, and the machine-learning detection tooling evidence with its model performance metrics. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented correlate-audit-review-and-reporting requirement.

artifacts.name: Correlated Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The correlated event investigation reports, the anomaly investigation records, the audit analysis reports, the audit review procedures, the anomalous access investigation reports, the access log review records, the flow log review procedures with the flow analysis tool documentation, the service provider log review procedures, and the privileged activity log review records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented identify-unauthorised-system-use requirement.

artifacts.name: Alert to Incident Escalation
artifacts.description: The procedure within the incident response plan covering monitoring and response to alerts from intrusion detection, file integrity monitoring, anti-malware and change detection; the sample records of monitoring alerts escalated to incident response with their disposition; the alert triage and escalation procedures; and the alert volume and triage metrics.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Platform Deployment
artifacts.description: The security information platform deployment documentation and evidence, the platform dashboard screenshots, the log monitoring and alerting evidence, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, the system monitoring strategy, the anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records, and the operations centre procedures running them.

artifacts.name: Logging Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The policy defining what to log, retention, protection and review requirements; the retention rules configured in the log archive; the configuration showing log tamper protection, append-only storage and access controls; and the alerting configuration covering log gaps or logging service disruption.

artifacts.name: Incident Handling Records
artifacts.description: The incident response plan and procedures, the incident handling procedures, the incident response records, the incident tracking system records, the incident investigation and analysis reports, the security incident classification and prioritisation criteria, and the post-incident review and lessons learned documentation closing out what the correlation surfaced.

MON-02.1.notes: 55 asks across 9 frameworks. Distinct from MON-01.2 in that the demand is correlation across sources rather than the monitoring capability itself; the source-coverage artifacts are separated from the correlation rules because correlation is worthless over an incomplete source set.

artifacts.name: Centralised Log Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture document showing prompt backup and forwarding of audit logs from all sources including external-facing technologies, the log forwarding agent or syslog configuration demonstrating prompt forwarding to the central server, the coverage evidence specifically for external-facing technologies, the sample backup execution records with forwarder health logs, the platform integration evidence, and the ingestion dashboard showing log ingestion health.

artifacts.name: Log Source Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of log sources covered with frequency and retention per source and the audit logging and logging configuration across those sources.

artifacts.name: Daily Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented daily log review procedure listing the required categories, the sample daily review records with reviewer name, date, scope and findings, the reviewer sign-off log, the dashboard or saved-search exports used for those reviews, the log review procedures, and the log review records with their findings.

artifacts.name: Log Analysis Records
artifacts.description: The audit review procedures, the audit analysis reports, the anomaly investigation records, the anomaly detection reports, the platform dashboard screenshots, and the evidence of periodic review of administrator and privileged activity logs.

artifacts.name: Log Protection and Retention
artifacts.description: The policy defining what to log, retention, protection and review requirements; the log retention policy; the retention rules configured in the log archive; the configuration showing log tamper protection, append-only storage and access controls; the database access controls over the log store; and the alerting configuration covering log gaps or logging service disruption.

artifacts.name: Detection Content and Coverage
artifacts.description: The strategy document defining operations centre scope, coverage and detection goals; the report showing monitoring coverage across environments and assets; the catalogue of detection use cases mapped to a recognised adversary technique framework; the log of detection rule changes and tuning actions over time; the playbooks for responding to specific alert types; the shift handover documentation showing continuous monitoring; and the proactive threat hunting engagement reports.

artifacts.name: Integrity Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The file integrity monitoring configuration, the integrity monitoring tools, the change detection records, the hash and signature verification, the software integrity verification records, and the change control documentation the detected changes are reconciled against.

artifacts.name: Anti-Malware Records
artifacts.description: The anti-malware deployment evidence, the definition update logs, the scan reports, and the malware incident records feeding the central review.

artifacts.name: Staff Event Reporting Channel
artifacts.description: The procedure telling staff what, how, when and to whom to report security events; the documentation of the reporting channels; the screenshot of the internal reporting tool; the anonymous reporting channel configuration with its usage metrics; the log of events reported by staff with triage outcomes and volume metrics; and the posters, articles and training content encouraging reporting.

MON-02.2.notes: 51 asks across 5 frameworks. Central collection, the daily review of what arrives and the protection of the log store are three proofs; ISO 27001 A.6.8 event reporting by staff is a human channel into the same central review and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Logging and Monitoring Policy
artifacts.description: Approved, current policy defining which event types must be logged and why, the systems in scope, the minimum content of a log record, retention, protection, access and review requirements, and the roles accountable. Must include the rationale for why the selected event types are adequate to support after-the-fact investigation of incidents, and state the frequency at which the selected event types are reviewed and updated. HITRUST and several regional frameworks expect a separate step-by-step procedure beneath the policy; NIS2 expects retention and integrity requirements stated in the policy itself.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Content Standard
artifacts.description: The documented standard listing the fields every audit record must contain, mapped to the six minimum elements: the type of event, the date and time it occurred, where it occurred (system, component or resource), the source or origination of the event, the outcome as success or failure, and the identity of the user or subject associated with it. PCI DSS additionally requires the identity or name of the affected data, system component, resource or service. This standard is the yardstick the sample records in the next item are tested against.

artifacts.name: Log Source Inventory and Coverage Map
artifacts.description: Register of every in-scope technology asset, application and service, showing which produce audit logs, which are integrated into the central platform, the retention applied per source, and any gaps with remediation plans. Must demonstrate coverage of all in-scope components, with particular confirmation of coverage for assets holding or processing sensitive data. Traceable to the wider IT asset management inventory so that coverage can be proven complete rather than asserted.

artifacts.name: Logging Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Live configuration exports or screenshots per system class showing audit logging is enabled and set to capture the required content: the event types selected, the fields recorded, and detailed logging where the baseline demands it. Must cover general system and application logging, logon and authentication audit trails, privileged and administrative activity logging, access to sensitive or highly classified data, and logging enabled during data migration activities.
