Each export must carry the date, system identifier and reviewer, and NIST 800-171 additionally requires evidence that actions can be traced to an individual user.

artifacts.name: Sample Log Records Demonstrating Required Content
artifacts.description: Representative live log extracts drawn from each class of in-scope system, showing every required field actually populated: event type, timestamp, location, source, success or failure outcome, and user or subject identity. Samples must span general system activity, user activity, privileged and administrative activity, and migration activity, and must be verifiable against the audit log content standard. This is the direct proof of the control and should not be substituted with configuration evidence alone.

artifacts.name: Centralised Log Management and SIEM Architecture
artifacts.description: Architecture documentation for the central logging capability showing how logs are collected from each source, transported, normalised, stored and retained, and the platform dashboard evidencing current ingestion health and source coverage. Must make clear which sources feed the platform and how collection failures become visible.

artifacts.name: Log Retention Configuration and Records
artifacts.description: The retention rules as configured in the log platform and archive, together with the policy stating the retention period per log type and the legal, regulatory or contractual basis for it. QCB requires a minimum of 180 days; HIPAA, ADHICS and others require retention consistent with the organisation's stated obligation without a fixed figure, so state the period applied per source. Include archival and immutable or cold-storage configuration, and where outputs and reports are retained, the archival and retention procedures covering them.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity and Tamper Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: Configuration and operating evidence that recorded log content cannot be altered or deleted: write-once or WORM storage, hashing or checksums, append-only settings, segregated log server storage, and the monitoring that detects tampering or gaps. CSA CCM expects records that log protection is operating in the cloud environment, not just documented.

artifacts.name: Log Access Control and Audit Tool Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that access to logs and to the audit tooling is restricted and authorised: the access control matrix mapping roles to permissions on the logging platform and log stores, the inventory of audit tools with their access restrictions and authorisation records, and the provisioning, modification and review records for the individuals holding that access.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that logs are actually examined: the review schedule, and completed review records showing reviewer, date, scope of logs reviewed, observations and any follow-up case raised. Must cover periodic review of privileged and administrative activity, review of access to sensitive data with investigation of anomalies, review of high-interest log categories, review of highly classified account logins, and review of migration logs. HIPAA and ADHICS additionally require the documented review procedure alongside the records.

artifacts.name: Alert Rules and Monitoring Response Records
artifacts.description: The configured detection and alerting rules built on log content, including alerts on logging gaps or logging service disruption, together with records of alerts triggered in the period, the triage performed and the response actions taken. Includes investigation reports for anomalous access identified through log review.

artifacts.name: Web Application Firewall Attack Logging Evidence
artifacts.description: For public-facing web applications, the configuration export showing the WAF or RASP solution is deployed in front of the application, running, and current; sample generated logs showing detection and blocking of web-based attacks with the required event content; evidence of the operating mode (blocking, or alerting with prompt investigation and resolution); and the rule-set currency records.

artifacts.name: Logging Obligations and Compliance Audit Records
artifacts.description: The register of statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations that drive logging content and retention, mapped to the systems affected, plus the assurance records over the logging control itself: information systems audit scope, methodology, sample and findings with management responses and remediation tracking; the risk register entries and risk assessment methodology covering logging; awareness communications informing personnel of the requirement; and, for data platforms, the metadata and catalogue audit trail with its register, compliance audit reports and KPI dashboard.

artifacts.name: Processing and Output Integrity Records
artifacts.description: Records evidencing that business process activity is logged completely and accurately end to end: the process control documentation, the segregation of duties matrix and access privilege records governing who can act, information processing validation and integrity check records, error and exception logs with the corrective action taken, and for generated outputs the delivery verification and acknowledgement logs, distribution access controls, and report completeness and accuracy validation.

MON-03.notes: 106 manual entries across 18 frameworks collapsed to 14 artifacts. No collectors are wired to this control, but logging configuration, retention settings, SIEM ingestion health and sample records are all connector-collectable, so those are hybrid. The control is narrowly about log CONTENT, so the required-fields standard and the sample records proving the fields are populated are the two load-bearing artifacts; the surrounding policy, retention, integrity, review and access items come from the wider logging control families the crosswalk pulled in. QCB is the only source stating a numeric retention floor (180 days). COBIT DSS06 and SOC 2 PI1.4 contribute a processing-integrity strand kept as one clearly-scoped item.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Field Standard
artifacts.description: The documented standard listing the required fields per audit log entry including user identification, event type and date and time; the approved audit trail policy specifying events captured, fields recorded, retention period and tamper-evident storage; the logging configuration export demonstrating capture of all required fields; the sample log entries from in-scope systems showing every required field populated; the audit logging configuration documentation; and the standard specifying mandatory fields, retention and tamper-evident storage.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Coverage
artifacts.description: The configuration export evidencing audit log enablement on all in-scope system components, the coverage map showing every component is producing audit logs, the inventory of integrated log sources feeding the aggregation platform, the sample live audit logs, and the audit log samples from the systems holding regulated data.

artifacts.name: End-to-End Transaction Traceability
artifacts.description: The standard operating procedure for end-to-end traceability of every transaction from origin through each tier, the sample redacted end-to-end audit trail for a single transaction, the sample end-to-end transaction audit trail demonstrating traceability across customer device, application and core systems, and the mapping of the relevant statutory sections to the traceability controls and audit trail capabilities.

artifacts.name: Log Retention and Tamper Evidence
artifacts.description: The audit trail retention configuration meeting the statutory requirement, the evidence of tamper-evident storage through write-once media or hash-chained logs, and the log retention policy with its supporting evidence.

artifacts.name: Non-Repudiation Controls
artifacts.description: The documentation of non-repudiation controls including digital signatures on transactions and signed one-time-passcode verifications supporting the audit trail.

artifacts.name: Identifier Attribution Records
artifacts.description: The account naming convention documentation, the unique identifier policy, the unique identifier scheme documentation, the unique user identifier assignment records, the user identifier assignment records, the audit log linkage to user identifiers, the user activity logs linked to unique identifiers, and the identity governance reports.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The audit log review procedures and reports evidencing the trail is examined rather than merely retained.

artifacts.name: Journal Entry Audit Records
artifacts.description: The journal entry application security configuration, the journal entry audit trail reports, the exception reporting configuration for unusual entries, and the preparer and approver segregation evidence.

artifacts.name: Catalog Audit Trail Records
artifacts.description: The documented metadata and catalog audit trail specification with its compliance evidence, the metadata repository or data catalog export, the register or inventory evidencing the audit trail with a named owner, the performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records, and the compliance audit reports and assessment records.

MON-03.2.notes: 38 asks across 8 frameworks. The log field standard, its enablement across components and the end-to-end traceability of a single transaction are three proofs; the last is the demanding one and is kept apart.

artifacts.name: Privileged Activity Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: The privileged activity logging configuration, the administrator audit trail capture, the command-line and shell logging configuration, the audit logging configuration per system and application, the log content standards documentation, and the sample logs covering each of the listed privileged activities.

artifacts.name: Privileged Session Records
artifacts.description: The privileged access management session recordings, the administrator session monitoring logs, the sample logs of privileged access to sensitive operating systems collected by the monitoring platform, the account activity logs, the access monitoring logs, and the privileged activity monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Privileged Activity Review Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of periodic review of administrator and privileged activity logs, the periodic activity review reports, the command-line log review procedures, the review records triggered by alerts and incidents, the log review schedules and records, the log review records with their follow-up case documentation, the audit review procedures, the audit analysis reports, and the anomaly investigation records. HITRUST requires the approved administrator and operator logs policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Privileged Account Inventory and Approval
artifacts.description: The privileged account inventory, the approval documentation for privileged access, the quarterly privileged access review with sign-off, the separate system administrator user accounts evidencing privileged identities are distinct from daily ones, the privileged access management controls, and the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented management of privileged access roles, segregation of privileged access roles, and customer approval for agreed privileged access role requirements.

artifacts.name: Logging Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The policy defining what to log, retention, protection and review requirements; the log retention policy and configuration; the retention rules configured in the log archive; and the inventory of log sources with frequency and retention per source. HITRUST requires the approved audit logging policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity Protection
artifacts.description: The configuration showing log tamper protection, append-only storage and access controls; the log tamper protection evidence; and the alerting configuration covering log gaps or logging service disruption.

artifacts.name: Log Aggregation Platform Evidence
artifacts.description: The security information platform architecture covering host and network data sources, the inventory of integrated log sources feeding it, the ingestion health dashboard, the platform dashboard screenshots, the active correlation rule set export, the sample access logs from critical applications ingested by it, and the sample logs of configuration changes detected and forwarded to it.

artifacts.name: Audit Tool Access Controls
artifacts.description: The audit tool inventory with its access restrictions and authorisation records, protecting the tools that hold the privileged activity record from the privileged users they monitor. HITRUST requires the approved information systems audit controls policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The risk assessment methodology documentation with its approval records and the risk register with entries, owners, ratings and treatment plans that determine which privileged functions warrant logging.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel that privileged actions are logged and the user access provisioning, modification and review records for the accounts under that logging.

MON-03.3.notes: 64 asks across 10 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is that privileged actions specifically are captured and reviewed; the general logging platform artifacts are kept separate from the privileged-activity ones so the control is not satisfied by a log source inventory alone.

artifacts.name: Audit Report Generation Capability
artifacts.description: The log analysis tool documentation, the report generation capability demonstration, the sample audit reports, the audit configuration across system components, and the audit generation verification results. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented audit-reduction-and-report-generation requirement.

artifacts.name: Centralised Log Platform
artifacts.description: The centralised log management deployment evidence, the centralised logging architecture documentation, the platform use cases and dashboards, the ingestion dashboard showing log ingestion health, the log monitoring and alerting evidence, and the log retention configuration per type.

artifacts.name: Platform Access Independence
artifacts.description: The platform access control records and the operator independence evidence showing whoever runs the monitoring is not the subject of it.

artifacts.name: Domain Monitoring Reports
artifacts.description: The formally documented monitoring and reporting procedure for the domain in scope with its senior management approval, the operational dashboards monitoring the events covered, the periodic reports issued under the approved mechanism, and the sample anomaly alert logs with their triage records.

artifacts.name: Logging Policy and Standards
artifacts.description: The policy defining what to log, retention, protection and review requirements; the inventory of log sources covered with frequency and retention per source; the retention rules configured in the log archive; the configuration showing log tamper protection, append-only storage and access controls; the alerting configuration covering log gaps or logging service disruption; and the evidence of periodic review of administrator and privileged activity logs.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage and Response
artifacts.description: The alert triage and escalation procedures, the anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records, the operations centre procedures, the incident response plan and procedures, the security incident classification and prioritisation criteria, the incident investigation and analysis reports, and the post-incident review and lessons learned documentation.

artifacts.name: Staff Event Reporting Channel
artifacts.description: The procedure telling staff what, how, when and to whom to report security events; the documentation of the reporting channels; the screenshot of the internal reporting tool; the anonymous reporting channel configuration with its usage metrics; the log of events reported by staff with triage outcomes and volume metrics; and the posters, articles and training content encouraging reporting.

MON-06.notes: 39 asks across 6 frameworks. The reporting capability, the reports it produces and the independence of whoever runs it are three proofs; ISO 27001 A.6.8 staff event reporting is a separate inbound channel and is kept apart.

artifacts.name: Log Protection Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy defining what is logged, how it is protected and who may read it, with the implementing procedure. NIS2 requires retention and integrity requirements to be stated in the policy; NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement to protect audit information and tools.

artifacts.name: Log Read Access Controls
artifacts.description: The access control configuration on log files, the security information platform and the log store limiting read access to personnel with a job-related need, the register of authorised personnel with that documented need, the access control lists over the log stores, and the periodic review records of log read access.

artifacts.name: Log Modification Prevention Evidence
artifacts.description: The access control evidence preventing user-level modification of log files, the write-once, append-only or immutable storage configuration protecting them, and the test evidence demonstrating modification attempts are actually prevented or detected rather than only configured against.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity Verification Mechanisms
artifacts.description: The integrity control evidence covering write-once media, hashing, immutable storage and segregated log server access, the integrity verification mechanisms, and the integrity monitoring configuration.

artifacts.name: Privileged Operator Separation Evidence
artifacts.description: The log server access controls preventing a privileged user from reaching the logs that record their own actions, the no-sharing policy for privileged accounts, the documentation of privileged access to audit tools, and the operator independence evidence.

artifacts.name: Logging Configuration Baselines
artifacts.description: The logging configuration baselines per system class, the log source inventory with frequency and retention per source, the log classification scheme, and the configuration for the in-scope systems.

artifacts.name: Log Availability Monitoring
artifacts.description: The alerting configuration on log gaps or logging service disruption, the ingestion health dashboard, the log backup evidence, and the monitoring rules and alert configuration records — detecting when logging stops is part of protecting it.

artifacts.name: Centralised Log Management Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture of the logging infrastructure showing collection, transport and storage, the centralised aggregation configuration covering critical assets, remote access and privileged activity, the platform documentation, and the integration evidence.

artifacts.name: Log Retention Configuration
artifacts.description: The retention rules configured in the archive, the retention and protection configuration records, and the compliance evidence that the configured period is actually being met.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The review procedures with the completed review records, the privileged activity log review evidence, the alert response records, and the follow-up case documentation arising from them.

artifacts.name: Time Synchronisation Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of time synchronisation across systems, without which protected logs cannot be correlated into a defensible sequence.

artifacts.name: Encryption Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The documented encryption monitoring and reporting with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered, evidencing the protection applied to logs in transit and at rest is itself monitored.

artifacts.name: Storage and Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The data storage integrity controls and checksums, the database integrity monitoring configuration, the storage access control configuration, and the archival and retention procedures protecting the stored records.

artifacts.name: Output Integrity and Distribution Controls
artifacts.description: The output distribution access controls, the delivery verification and acknowledgement logs, the report generation completeness and accuracy validation, and the output archival and retention procedures.

artifacts.name: Security Alert Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The security alert investigation and resolution records drawn from the protected logs, evidencing the protection preserves evidence that is actually used.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the log protection requirements, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping over the log platform, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

MON-08.notes: 78 asks across 16 frameworks. Distinct from MON-10 (retention) in that this control is about protecting the log from the people it records: read restriction, modification prevention and privileged-operator separation are the three demands, and PCI DSS 10.3 tests each separately.

artifacts.name: Log Retention Policy
artifacts.description: The approved retention policy defining how long each log type is held and where. Durations differ materially and the policy must satisfy the longest applicable: PCI DSS requires twelve months with the most recent three immediately available; PISF 2026 twelve months for critical assets and three for others; QCB at least 180 days with a separate archival policy for regulated records; SBP Internet Banking ten years for internet-banking security logs and audit trails.

artifacts.name: Log Retention Configuration
artifacts.description: The storage configuration enforcing the retention period — lifecycle policy, archive tier, repository capacity — with the log archival procedures and the archive storage documentation behind it.

artifacts.name: Retention Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The audit or report verifying the age of the oldest retained logs actually meets the required period, and where a tiered requirement applies, that the immediately available window is also met. This is the evidence that distinguishes a configured policy from a met one.

artifacts.name: Archive Restoration Test Records
artifacts.description: The test record demonstrating archived logs can actually be restored from cold storage within a reasonable time, proving the archive is usable rather than merely retained.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The immutability or write-once configuration and access controls protecting both active and archived logs, the tamper protection evidence, the tamper-evident storage evidence covering the full retention period, and the documented access and accountability controls over the audit logs themselves.

artifacts.name: Audit Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: The logging configuration per system and application, the log content standards defining the required fields, a sample log entry demonstrating them, and the critical device audit trail configuration.

artifacts.name: Centralised Log Management Evidence
artifacts.description: The centralised aggregation and correlation configuration covering critical assets, remote access and privileged activity; the log management platform inventory; the enterprise log server archive; the integration evidence; and the use cases and dashboards built on it.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The review schedules and completed review records with the reviewer named, the manual review records for high-interest logs, the review records triggered by alerts, and the follow-up case documentation arising from them.

artifacts.name: Log Platform Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The access control records for the log platform, the operator independence evidence showing those who administer systems do not control the logs that record their actions, and the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping over the platform.

artifacts.name: Time Synchronisation Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of time synchronisation across systems, without which retained logs cannot be correlated into a reliable sequence.

artifacts.name: Data Retention and Disposal Schedule
artifacts.description: The retention and disposal schedule covering the data the logs describe, the disposal verification and audit trail, the media sanitisation records, and the secure destruction procedures with their certificates.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Mapping for Logging
artifacts.description: The mapping of logging and retention practice to the applicable regulations and the legal review of the monitoring and logging activities, establishing the basis for the retention periods chosen.

artifacts.name: Security Alert Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The security alert investigation and resolution records drawn from the retained logs, evidencing the retention serves an operational purpose rather than only a compliance one.

artifacts.name: Virtualised and Database Logging Evidence
artifacts.description: The virtual machine logging configuration with those logs forwarded to the central platform, and the database activity monitoring logs, covering the layers that are easily omitted from an estate-wide logging standard.

artifacts.name: Core Platform Records Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The archival policy with the applicable jurisdictional retention, the database integrity and versioning controls, the layered encryption and role-based access over sensitive core data, and the continuity mechanisms protecting those records.

artifacts.name: Metadata Audit Trail Records
artifacts.description: The documented metadata and catalog audit trail specification with its compliance evidence, the metadata repository export, the register with a named owner, the performance metrics dashboard, and the compliance audit reports.

MON-10.notes: 85 asks across 17 frameworks. Retention duration is the point of maximum divergence and is stated inside the retention artifact: PCI DSS twelve months with three immediately available, PISF 2026 twelve for critical and three for others, QCB 180 days, SBP Internet Banking ten years. The evidence must satisfy the longest applicable.

artifacts.name: Anomaly Detection Configuration
artifacts.description: The anomaly detection system documentation, the anomaly detection rules, the anomaly detection tool configurations with their tuning records, the anomaly alerting configuration, the alert configuration, the monitoring tool documentation, and the configuration of continuous monitoring across systems and networks for breach detection. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented identify-unauthorised-system-use requirement.

artifacts.name: Baseline Profile Documentation
artifacts.description: The system baseline profile documentation and the baseline deviation analysis reports establishing what normal looks like before an anomaly can be recognised.

artifacts.name: User Behaviour Analytics Records
artifacts.description: The user behaviour analytics tool documentation, the analytics alert and investigation records, and the data loss prevention and behaviour analytics detection rules.

artifacts.name: Detection Alert Review Records
artifacts.description: The sample breach and anomaly alerts with their triage, the alert triage and escalation procedures, the monitoring alert review records, the monitoring reports, the monitoring procedures, and the security operations centre procedures governing them.

artifacts.name: Security Monitoring Platform
artifacts.description: The system monitoring strategy, the security information platform deployment documentation, the platform configuration and alert rules, the log monitoring and alerting evidence, the intrusion detection and prevention configuration, and the single point of failure analysis over the monitoring estate itself.

artifacts.name: Detection Mechanism Testing
artifacts.description: The detection mechanism testing records evidencing the anomaly detection actually fires on the conditions it claims to cover.

artifacts.name: Fraud Monitoring Framework
artifacts.description: The approved fraud risk management framework for the channel covering detection, prevention and response; the fraud monitoring system documentation; the inventory of fraud detection tools deployed; the active fraud detection and transaction monitoring rule set with thresholds, scoring and triggers; and the fraud detection rule configuration records.

artifacts.name: Fraud Alert and Case Records
artifacts.description: The sample alerts generated by fraud monitoring and unauthorised-access detection with their triage and disposition records, and the sample fraud case investigation records demonstrating proactive identification, escalation and customer protection.

artifacts.name: Transaction Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The payment limit configurations, the dual authorisation evidence, and the transaction verification procedures constraining what an anomalous session can do before it is caught.

artifacts.name: Audit Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The audit logging configuration documentation, the audit log samples from the systems holding regulated data, the audit log review procedures and reports, and the log retention policy with its supporting evidence.

artifacts.name: Data Integrity Monitoring
artifacts.description: The data integrity verification mechanism documentation, the hash or checksum implementation evidence, and the integrity monitoring tool configuration.

artifacts.name: Account Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The account management procedures, the account review documentation, the user access authorisation records, and the terminated user account records that anomalous-account detection is measured against.

artifacts.name: Incident Handling Records
artifacts.description: The incident handling procedures, the incident response records, the incident tracking system records, and the post-incident review reports closing out the anomalies that proved real.

artifacts.name: Network Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The network security policy defining controls proportionate to network complexity, the current network architecture diagram showing security zones, firewalls, detection sensors and monitoring points, the logs from network monitoring detecting policy violations and atypical activities, and the assessment report on the adequacy of those controls.

artifacts.name: Connected Device Monitoring
artifacts.description: The connected-device monitoring procedures and the anomaly detection and response records for those devices, covering the estate that conventional endpoint monitoring does not reach.

MON-16.notes: 58 asks across 12 frameworks. Behavioural anomaly detection, fraud transaction monitoring and file integrity monitoring answer different questions from different tools and are kept apart; a single 'monitoring' artifact would let one substitute for the others.

artifacts.name: Log Retention Configuration
artifacts.description: The approved log retention policy, the log retention policy and configuration, the log retention configuration per type, the log retention procedures, the log retention settings, and the storage configuration evidence implementing the required period. Retention obligations diverge across frameworks — from a minimum of 180 days up to ten years for payment security logs — and the longest applicable period governs; the compliance report verifying the age of the oldest retained log evidences it.

artifacts.name: Log Integrity Protection
artifacts.description: The evidence of tamper-evident or write-once log storage protecting integrity over the retention period, the log tamper protection evidence, the log access control lists, and the log backup evidence.

artifacts.name: Audit Logging Configuration
artifacts.description: The audit logging configuration per system and application, the audit logging configuration evidence, the audit logging policy, the log content standards documentation, the logging configuration, the critical device audit trail configuration, the login audit trail configuration, and the sample log entry with its required fields. HITRUST requires the approved monitoring system use policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for monitoring logs and audit trails on a regular and predefined periodic basis with assigned reviewers, the log review schedules and records, the log review records with their follow-up case documentation, the log review records, the manual review records of high-interest logs, the review evidence for highly classified accounts, the review records triggered by alerts, the sample log review records, the log samples, and the monitoring procedures.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage Workflow
artifacts.description: The alert-to-ticket workflows, the exception action records, the anomaly monitoring configuration, and the action plan workflow for issue closure.

artifacts.name: Investigation Records
artifacts.description: The suspicious transaction investigation procedures and the investigation case records with their outcomes.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel that system use is monitored.

MON-17.notes: 39 asks across 7 frameworks. Retention periods diverge sharply here — 180 days in one framework, ten years in another — so the retention artifact states both and the strictest governs; review and triage are kept separate from retention.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy & Procedures
artifacts.description: The approved network / system-and-communications-protection policy and its supporting procedures, covering boundary protection, transmission security, secure network management and the access control rules applied to network resources. Must identify the official responsible for the policy, the roles it is disseminated to, the review frequency and the events forcing an off-cycle review, and be evidenced with policy review, distribution and awareness communication records. Regulated entities additionally require a stated set of approved network security requirements and an in-house controls policy.

artifacts.name: Network Architecture & Segmentation Diagrams
artifacts.description: Current network architecture and segmentation diagrams showing trust zones, boundary devices, DMZs and the isolation of sensitive environments — cardholder data environment, payment/core banking systems, SWIFT secure zone, and any physically or logically separated browsing stations. Must be up to date, show the defence-in-depth layering, and be accompanied by records of architecture review; resilience and high-availability design is required for core banking scope.

artifacts.name: Firewall Rule Base & Access Control List Review Records
artifacts.description: Exports of the live firewall rule bases and network ACLs (including proxy rules restricting general internet access from protected zones) together with the records of their periodic review — who reviewed, when, which rules were challenged, and what was removed. Must show rules are justified, documented and reviewed rather than accumulated, and cover the trust boundaries drawn on the architecture diagrams.

artifacts.name: Network Device Inventory, Hardening Baselines & Management Configuration
artifacts.description: The inventory of network components and information assets with classification, the hardening standards and configuration baselines applied to network devices, and evidence of centralised and out-of-band network management. Payment card systems require documented hardening specific to that scope. Must show devices in the inventory are the ones actually covered by the baselines.

artifacts.name: Network Device Patch & Firmware Currency Records
artifacts.description: Firmware and software version inventory for network devices, the patch and update records applied during the period, and a version compliance report showing devices running supported, current firmware against the standard.

artifacts.name: Network Monitoring, IDS/IPS & Protective Control Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration of the intrusion detection/prevention and network monitoring stack together with the alert and event logs it produced, security operations monitoring procedures, malware protection deployment and update records, and reports on the effectiveness of network controls. Must show alerts are generated, reviewed and acted on, not merely that sensors are deployed.

artifacts.name: Remote Access, VPN & Authentication Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration evidence for remote and privileged network access: VPN and circuit encryption, RDP/SSH hardening and session encryption settings, jump server configuration, multi-factor authentication enforced for external access, and the identity and access management configuration governing who can reach network resources.

artifacts.name: Encryption-in-Transit & Secure Protocol Configuration
artifacts.description: Evidence that data in transit is protected: TLS and network encryption configuration with integrity verification, message authentication implementation, email encryption settings, documentation of approved secure protocols, and remediation records for insecure or deprecated protocols found in use.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Policy & Data Exchange Agreements
artifacts.description: The information transfer policy and secure transfer procedures, the data transfer / information exchange agreement templates and executed agreements with counterparties, managed file transfer logs, and chain-of-custody receipts for physical media movement — the governance layer over data crossing the network boundary.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Configuration & Alert Records
artifacts.description: The DLP policy plus the deployed ruleset export covering endpoint, email, cloud and removable media channels, the alert and investigation log with dispositions, dashboard evidence of coverage, and the playbook followed when DLP fires. Must show rules map to the classified data they are meant to protect.

artifacts.name: Wireless Security Configuration & Rogue Access Point Scan Reports
artifacts.description: Wireless network security configuration (authentication, encryption, segregation from sensitive zones), the documented procedure for detecting unauthorised access points, the wireless detection system configuration, and the scan results — required at least quarterly under PCI DSS — together with the response records for any rogue device found.

artifacts.name: Network Change Management Records
artifacts.description: Change records for network configuration and firewall rule modifications, and the change log for network services, showing each change was requested, reviewed for security impact, approved and implemented as approved.

artifacts.name: Network Security Assessment & Control Test Reports
artifacts.description: Independent or internal assessment output demonstrating the controls actually work: network security assessment reports, threat and vulnerability assessments of the network, protocol compliance audit results, security testing performed before systems are deployed, control test reports and the coverage matrix mapping implemented controls to required ones. Must evidence both implementation and operating effectiveness of the boundary protection controls.

artifacts.name: Network Service Provider Agreements & Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: Agreements with network service providers together with the security specifications attached to those services, the service monitoring reports received, and provider audit or assurance reports — evidencing that security levels of externally supplied network services are defined and verified.

artifacts.name: Secure Acquisition, Development & Vulnerability Disclosure Documentation
artifacts.description: Security requirements embedded in procurement of network systems and services, the secure development lifecycle documentation for systems placed on the network, and the vulnerability handling and coordinated disclosure policy — the NIS2 supply-chain and product-security layer supporting the network controls.

NET-01.notes: 111 asks collapse to 15 artifacts. 59 collectors are attached but they cover SaaS tenant configuration and three AWS checks, not on-premise firewalls, switches or wireless — so configuration items are hybrid rather than automated: the connector output covers the cloud/SaaS estate and the network team must supply device exports for the rest. 'Firewall rules', 'ACLs' and 'network access controls' were the biggest restatement cluster and collapse to one rule-base-and-review artifact.

artifacts.name: Defence-in-Depth Architecture
artifacts.description: The network architecture aligned to defence in depth and the risk management strategy, the defence-in-depth network security architecture document covering perimeter, demilitarised zone, internal segmentation and micro-segmentation, the multi-layer security architecture diagram, the current network architecture diagram including security zones and controls, the current-state topology diagram showing the layers, the network architecture documentation, the network segmentation diagrams, the up-to-date network diagrams, the network diagrams showing zone segregation, and the architecture review records.

artifacts.name: Layer Coverage Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix showing multi-layer control coverage across assets and the inventory of network controls with ownership and coverage, evidencing that each asset sits behind more than one independent control.

artifacts.name: Perimeter Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing network security control deployment at every boundary between trusted and untrusted networks, the configuration export of those perimeter controls, the register classifying every network as trusted or untrusted with its enforcement point, the firewall rule base export, the firewall rules documentation, the access control lists, the jump server configuration, and the firewall and network security control configurations.

artifacts.name: Ruleset Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic firewall ruleset review records with justification and cleanup actions and the firewall rulebase with its periodic review evidence.

artifacts.name: Segmentation Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration evidence of network segmentation between zones restricting lateral movement and the periodic validation report through segmentation testing or attack simulation confirming the layered controls function as designed.

artifacts.name: Detection Layer Configuration
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention rule configuration with sample alerts investigated, the intrusion detection and prevention system configurations, the real-time security event monitoring dashboard screenshots, and the network control effectiveness monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Authentication Layer Configuration
artifacts.description: The multi-factor authentication implementation for external access, the dual authentication configuration with triangulation of access, the virtual private network and remote access security configurations, and the network access trust controls.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy and Requirements
artifacts.description: The policy covering network security architecture, controls and operations; the documented and formally approved network security requirements; the evidence that the approved controls are implemented and maintained; the hardening standards applied to routers, switches, firewalls and access points; the centralised network management evidence; and the network component inventory.

artifacts.name: Wireless Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The wireless security configuration covering enterprise-grade encryption, rogue access point detection and guest network isolation.

artifacts.name: Network Threat Assessment
artifacts.description: The network threat and vulnerability assessment informing where the layers are placed.

NET-02.notes: 40 asks across 9 frameworks. The layer-coverage matrix is the distinguishing artifact — it is what proves defence in depth rather than a collection of individually configured controls — and is kept apart from the per-control configuration.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy and Architecture
artifacts.description: The network security policy covering architecture, controls and operations, with the current network architecture diagram showing security zones, segmentation and trust boundaries, and the network routing configuration documentation. HITRUST requires the segregation policy and its implementing procedure with awareness communications; MAS TRM requires the security architecture to be documented separately from the diagram.

artifacts.name: Firewall Configuration and Rule Base
artifacts.description: The firewall rule base export with source, destination, port, service and justification per rule, and the deployment records showing a control at every boundary between distinct security domains. SBP Internet Banking requires a firewall selection and deployment policy referencing traffic volume and asset risk classification, plus capacity and performance reports showing sizing matches traffic.

artifacts.name: Firewall Rule Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic ruleset review records identifying redundant, shadowed or overly permissive rules, with the justification and cleanup actions taken. HITRUST requires device configuration baselines to be reviewed alongside the ruleset.

artifacts.name: Trusted and Untrusted Network Register
artifacts.description: The register classifying every network as trusted or untrusted with the enforcement point that separates them, the architecture diagram showing a network security control deployed at every such boundary, and the configuration export of those perimeter controls.

artifacts.name: Inbound Traffic Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The register of allowed inbound flows with port, protocol, destination component and business justification, the firewall ruleset export restricting inbound traffic from untrusted networks to only what is authorised, and the evidence of default-deny rules blocking everything else.

artifacts.name: Wireless Network Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: The inventory of all wireless networks (corporate, guest, scanner) with their enforcement points, the architecture showing a network security control between every wireless network and the protected environment, the ruleset export from those controls, and the wireless security configuration covering WPA3 or enterprise authentication, rogue AP detection and guest isolation. QCB requires a firewall between wireless and wired networks and a MAC filtering policy.

artifacts.name: IDS/IPS Configuration and Alert Response
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection or prevention architecture, configuration export showing active signature sets and tuning, signature and engine update records evidencing currency, sample alerts with triage and personnel response records, and the documented response procedure with on-call rotation.

artifacts.name: Network Segmentation Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export evidencing segregation between environments and zones — VLAN or VPC definitions, DMZ architecture, and the boundary enforcement between them — with the covert channel scan reports and external traffic monitoring records where required.

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Monitoring Logs
artifacts.description: The monitoring logs from boundary protection devices with the records demonstrating that boundaries are monitored and protected in operation rather than only configured, and the routing protocol authentication evidence.

artifacts.name: Network Device Hardening Standards
artifacts.description: The hardening standards applied to routers, switches, firewalls and wireless access points, the server hardening baselines with unused ports and services disabled, and the configuration baselines against which devices are assessed.

artifacts.name: Network Access Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The network access control policy and solution configuration, the remote device compliance checks it enforces, and the network access control records showing which devices are admitted to which segments.

artifacts.name: Email Gateway Filtering Configuration
artifacts.description: The email gateway file type blocking configuration with the blocked file type list, and the filtering reports showing what was blocked over the period.

artifacts.name: Network Service Provider Agreements
artifacts.description: Contracts with connectivity and interconnect providers carrying security terms, the documented security features required of each network service (DDoS protection, link encryption), the change log for network services with security impact assessments, the assurance reports received from providers, the service monitoring reports showing adherence to agreed levels, and the evidence of encryption on inter-site circuits and VPNs.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Configuration
artifacts.description: The VPN configuration with monitoring, auditing and multi-factor authentication for remote connectivity, and the remote access security configurations evidencing encrypted transport.

artifacts.name: Cloud Perimeter Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration export for cloud perimeter firewalls, intrusion detection, web application firewall and DDoS protection services, the cloud-specific threat model mapping threats such as hypervisor escape, weak APIs and side channels to the controls implemented, the service status dashboard showing health and alert counts, and the evidence from simulated attacks or red-team exercises demonstrating detection and mitigation.

artifacts.name: Endpoint and Malware Protection at the Boundary
artifacts.description: The anti-malware controls inventory and endpoint protection deployment records, pre-transmission scanning configuration, periodic malware scanning reports, file integrity monitoring configuration and alerts, application allow-listing documentation, and the software installation restriction controls.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the identity and access management system configuration, the information asset inventory with classification, and the multi-factor authentication implementation for external access — the identity side of the boundary the network controls enforce.

artifacts.name: Backup and Logging Assurance Evidence
artifacts.description: Encrypted, access-controlled backups with periodic restoration testing and geographically separate storage, and the evidence of continuous monitoring and incident response tooling with at least twelve months of secure log retention.

NET-03.notes: 98 asks across 17 frameworks. PCI DSS drives the most specific demands here — a trusted/untrusted register, default-deny evidence and wireless-to-CDE enforcement — and those are kept as their own artifacts because they are tested as discrete requirements rather than as attributes of the firewall configuration.

artifacts.name: Permitted Connection Register
artifacts.description: The register of allowed inbound flows with port, protocol, destination component and justification; the firewall ruleset export restricting inbound traffic from untrusted networks to the permitted components; the evidence of default-deny rules blocking all other inbound traffic; the network service inventory; and the shared and isolated network access matrix.

artifacts.name: Network Access Authorisation
artifacts.description: The authorisation-based access configuration, the network access authorisation records, and the access provisioning records per network zone. HITRUST requires the approved network connection control policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Configuration
artifacts.description: The network boundary protection documentation, the demilitarised-zone architecture documentation, the firewall and proxy configurations, the firewall and network security control configurations, the boundary protection monitoring logs, the network segmentation documentation, and the network architecture and segmentation diagrams.

artifacts.name: Detection and Monitoring Configuration
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention configuration, the security information platform deployment documentation, the system monitoring strategy, and the monitoring alert review records covering the permitted connections.

artifacts.name: Remote and External Access Controls
artifacts.description: The multi-factor authentication implementation for external access and the virtual private network and remote access security configurations governing connections originating outside the network.

artifacts.name: Wireless Connection Detection
artifacts.description: The procedure for detection of authorised and unauthorised wireless access points at the required interval, the latest four quarters of wireless scan reports, the wireless intrusion detection configuration evidencing automated continuous detection, and the sample response records for unauthorised detections.

artifacts.name: Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy and procedures, the identity and access management system configuration, the information asset inventory and classification, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

NET-03.1.notes: 35 asks across 5 frameworks. The permitted-connection register and the default-deny that backs it are the distinguishing artifacts; PCI DSS 11.2.1 wireless scanning arrives through an adjacent crosswalk and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Information Flow Control Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining permitted information flows and the enforcement points that implement them, the network connection and routing control policies with their implementing procedures, and the filtering policy documentation. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented flow-control procedure.

artifacts.name: Access Control List Configuration
artifacts.description: The access control list configuration on network devices, the network segmentation filtering rules, the firewall rule base export with source, destination, port, service and justification, and the periodic ruleset review records with cleanup actions.

artifacts.name: Inbound Traffic Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The network diagram marking the protected perimeter and the controls enforcing inbound restriction, the firewall or security-group ruleset export showing inbound traffic restricted to what is necessary, the register of allowed inbound flows with justification, the ruleset restricting traffic from untrusted networks, and the explicit default-deny rule terminating the inbound chain.

artifacts.name: Outbound Traffic Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The register of approved outbound destinations with business justification, the ruleset export showing outbound traffic restricted to what is necessary, and the default-deny rule terminating the outbound chain.

artifacts.name: Anti-Spoofing Configuration
artifacts.description: The documented standard listing the source address ranges blocked at ingress, the configuration evidence for anti-spoofing controls such as reverse-path forwarding and bogon filtering, and sample log entries showing spoofed sources being dropped at the perimeter.

artifacts.name: Network Segmentation Evidence
artifacts.description: The network architecture and segmentation diagrams showing zones and trust boundaries, the segmentation configuration, the documented analysis of security domains with criticality, protocols and trust considerations, the domain-specific control design, and the test report validating segmentation is actually enforced.

artifacts.name: Application and Data Access Control Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix of permissions per role in each business application, the row or column-level security configuration in databases and data platforms, the attribute-based access control policy configuration, the access decision audit log showing granted and denied decisions, and the periodic least-privilege assessment identifying over-privileged accounts with remediation.

artifacts.name: Access Review and Need-to-Know Justification
artifacts.description: The access control review records, the documented need-to-know justification for each grant, the application access review outputs signed off by business owners, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method such as secure file transfer, secure email and encrypted removable media; the managed file transfer platform logs showing encrypted transfers and recipients; the email encryption configuration enforcing protected external mail; the data transfer agreement templates used with third parties; and the courier chain-of-custody receipts for physical media.

artifacts.name: Secure Protocol Enforcement Evidence
artifacts.description: The secure protocol implementation documentation, the protocol compliance audit results, and the insecure protocol remediation records showing legacy protocols removed from the estate.

artifacts.name: Network Device Configuration Management
artifacts.description: The network device hardening standards, the configuration baselines and ruleset review records, the secure management procedures, the version control system documentation for device configuration, and the change management records covering rule changes.

artifacts.name: Boundary Monitoring and Detection Evidence
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention configuration with sample alerts investigated, the external traffic monitoring records, the covert channel scan reports, and the routing protocol authentication evidence.

artifacts.name: Network Service and Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: The network service inventory, the network access authorisation records, the information asset inventory with classification, and the identity and access management system configuration that governs who may reach each service.

artifacts.name: Segregated Zone Access Evidence
artifacts.description: The jump server configuration and the network diagrams showing the segregated zone, evidencing that access into the protected zone is brokered rather than direct.

artifacts.name: Remote and Wireless Access Configuration
artifacts.description: The VPN and remote access security configurations, the multi-factor authentication implementation for external access, and the wireless network security configuration with rogue access point detection and guest isolation.

NET-04.notes: 89 asks across 11 frameworks. PCI DSS drives four separately testable flow-control requirements (inbound CDE restriction, outbound restriction, untrusted-network inbound, anti-spoofing) and each is kept as its own artifact because each has its own default-deny evidence.

artifacts.name: Default-Deny Rule Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of an explicit default-deny or implicit deny rule terminating both the inbound and outbound rule chains, the ruleset with explicit deny, and the documented requirement or configuration evidence that network traffic is denied by default with the records demonstrating it operates.

artifacts.name: Allowed Traffic Register
artifacts.description: The register of allowed inbound flows with port, protocol, destination component and business justification, and the register of approved outbound destinations with their justification — the exception list that the default deny admits.

artifacts.name: Firewall Rule Base Export
artifacts.description: The firewall or security group ruleset export with source, destination, port, service and description per rule; the inbound and outbound rulesets restricted to what is necessary; the access control list configuration; and the network segmentation filtering rules.

artifacts.name: Firewall Rule Review Records
artifacts.description: The review procedure defining frequency, post-change triggers, reviewers and sign-off; the completed review records with rule-by-rule justification and stale-rule removal evidence; the periodic ruleset review records with cleanup actions; and the rule analysis tool reports identifying redundant, shadowed or overly permissive rules.

artifacts.name: Firewall Deployment Architecture
artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing controls deployed between every pair of distinct security domains, the boundary network diagram marking the protected perimeter, the network architecture diagram with security zones, and the boundary protection documentation.

artifacts.name: Firewall Selection and Sizing Records
artifacts.description: The approved firewall selection and deployment policy referencing network traffic volume and asset risk classification, and the capacity and performance reports demonstrating the deployed devices are sized for the traffic they carry.

artifacts.name: Cloud-to-On-Premise Rule Controls
artifacts.description: The site-to-site connection or direct-link configuration, the address management register identifying dedicated source and destination endpoints, and the rule export showing traffic permitted only between those endpoints and ports.

artifacts.name: Gateway Hardening Evidence
artifacts.description: The internet gateway hardening evidence, the hardening checklist covering each required element, the pre-production hardening sign-off, and the network device hardening standards applied to routers, switches and firewalls.

artifacts.name: Wireless Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: The inventory of wireless networks with their enforcement points, the architecture showing a control between every wireless network and the protected environment, the ruleset export from those controls, the firewall between wireless and wired networks, the address filtering policy, and the wireless security configuration with rogue access point detection and guest isolation.

artifacts.name: Boundary Detection and Monitoring
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention configuration with sample alerts investigated, the boundary protection monitoring logs, the demilitarised zone architecture documentation, and the jump server configuration brokering access into protected zones.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the email encryption configuration; the managed transfer platform log; the transfer agreement templates; and the courier chain-of-custody receipts for the paths that bypass the network entirely.

artifacts.name: Network Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, the device configuration baselines with ruleset review records, and the multi-factor implementation for external access.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering network security architecture, controls and operations, the filtering policy documentation, and the approved network connection control standard with its implementing procedure.

NET-04.1.notes: 68 asks across 12 frameworks. The single demand is that the ruleset ends in an explicit deny and every allow is justified; the artifacts separate the rule configuration, the justification register and the review that removes what is no longer justified.

artifacts.name: Interconnection Security Agreements
artifacts.description: The interconnection security agreements, the memoranda of understanding, the system interconnection documentation, the network service contracts with their service level agreements, the network service requirements and security feature documentation, the third-party information exchange security requirements, the security requirements per sharing platform, and the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit. HITRUST requires the approved interconnected business information systems and security of network services policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Interconnection Inventory
artifacts.description: The business information system integration inventory, the information sharing platform inventory, the inter-system data flow security measures, and the interconnection security architecture documentation.

artifacts.name: Interface Design and Conformance
artifacts.description: The platform interface standards compliance documentation, the electronic interface design and architecture diagrams, the interface conformance test results, the interface maintenance log, the application integration security documentation, the information sharing security practices documentation, and the interoperability standards used.

artifacts.name: Connection Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The secure connection configuration documentation covering the tunnelling and transport protection in use, the secure connectivity configuration for the sharing platforms, the access control documentation for those platforms, and the pre-data-exchange validation records.

artifacts.name: Connection Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The connection monitoring logs, the boundary protection monitoring logs, and the connection termination evidence where the connection was withdrawn.

artifacts.name: Connection Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The per-application network access risk assessments, the risk assessment for trusted network connectivity, the cascading-risk evaluation, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Documentation
artifacts.description: The network boundary protection documentation, the demilitarised-zone architecture documentation, the firewall and proxy configurations, the network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones, and the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the interconnection requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

NET-05.notes: 43 asks across 6 frameworks. The agreement, the technical interface it governs and the monitoring of the live connection are three proofs; the interface conformance test is kept separate because it is what proves the agreement was implemented.

artifacts.name: Network Security & Segmentation Policy
artifacts.description: The approved network security policy and the segmentation standard beneath it, defining the security zones the organisation recognises, the trust levels assigned to each, the information flow control rules between them, and the requirement that publicly accessible components be isolated from internal networks. Must include the network security control ruleset configuration standard: baseline rule sets, default settings, naming conventions, documentation requirements and the mandated review cadence. Frameworks add a firewall selection and deployment policy tied to traffic volume and asset risk classification, the documented procedure or work instruction implementing network segregation, and evidence that personnel were informed of the requirement.

artifacts.name: Network Segmentation Design & Security Domain Analysis
artifacts.description: The segmentation design document defining the VLANs, subnets, zones and trust levels, the criteria and strategy by which the network was segregated, and the security requirements applying to each zone. Must show the analysis behind the design: the security domains identified with their criticality, protocols, performance and trust considerations, and the controls tailored to each. Framework-specific coverage: segmentation by workload type (production, pre-production, QA, development) and by purpose (end users, critical servers, middleware, management), defence-in-depth network design, segmentation between operational technology and corporate networks where applicable, and a single-point-of-failure review of the design.

artifacts.name: Current Network & Security Zone Diagrams
artifacts.description: Current-state, version-controlled network and topology diagrams showing every security zone, the components in each, all interconnections, and the network security controls enforcing the boundaries between them. Must show every connection between the regulated environment and other networks including corporate, partner and internet, mark the perimeter and the controls enforcing it, and include the management network. Diagrams must be demonstrably current: the update log evidencing refresh after every significant environment change is explicitly required.

artifacts.name: Data Flow Diagrams & Transmission/Storage Inventory
artifacts.description: Current data-flow diagrams showing every ingress point, processing point, storage location and transmission path for the regulated data, supported by an inventory of the transmission channels and storage locations the diagrams reference. Must be updated whenever data flows or the environment change, with records evidencing those updates.

artifacts.name: Network Zone, VLAN & Trust-Boundary Register
artifacts.description: The register classifying every network as trusted or untrusted with the control enforcing each boundary, the VLAN and subnet register listing purpose, owner and permitted traffic per segment, and the zone classification records. Must be accompanied by the inventory of the segmentation and network controls themselves (firewall, IDS/IPS, WAF, NAC, NDR, DDoS, secure DNS, proxy) with ownership and coverage, the shared versus isolated network access matrix, and the provisioning records showing who was granted access to each zone. Classification of the assets residing in each zone is required so the zoning can be justified.

artifacts.name: Firewall / Network Security Control Ruleset Export
artifacts.description: Rule base exports from every network security control enforcing a segment boundary - perimeter firewalls, internal and inter-zone firewalls, cloud security groups and access control lists - showing source, destination, port, service and the justification for each rule. Must demonstrate: inbound traffic to the protected environment restricted to what is necessary, outbound traffic likewise restricted, traffic from untrusted networks permitted only to explicitly authorised components, and an explicit default-deny rule terminating each chain. Controls must be deployed at every boundary between trusted and untrusted networks and between every pair of distinct security domains, and the mitigating configuration for any insecure service permitted must be shown.

artifacts.name: Segmentation Enforcement Configuration
artifacts.description: Technical configuration proving the designed segmentation is actually enforced: cloud network configuration (VPC/VNet, subnets, route tables, network ACLs and security groups), microsegmentation policy configuration where deployed, and the routing and filtering evidence showing internet egress passes through the dedicated security segment with no direct egress from workload subnets. Must include the controls isolating publicly accessible components from internal networks, proxy or firewall configuration blocking direct internet access from the protected zone, jump-server or bastion configuration governing entry into it, and evidence of separate browsing stations where the framework requires them.

artifacts.name: Wireless Network Inventory & Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: An inventory of every wireless network and access point - corporate, guest and purpose-built - with its placement, SSID, encryption configuration and whether it connects to the protected environment, plus the access point registration list. Must evidence that network security controls sit between every wireless network and the protected environment regardless of how the wireless network is classified, that guest and corporate wireless are segregated from each other and from critical systems, and that the wireless security configuration (WPA3/Enterprise, rogue AP detection) is in place. A wireless risk assessment is required by one framework.

artifacts.name: Approved Services, Ports & Protocols Register
artifacts.description: The register of every service, protocol and port permitted across the segment boundaries, each with a documented business justification and a named approver, supported by the sample approval records. Must separately identify insecure services, protocols or ports still in use with the specific compensating security features applied to each and the documented risk acceptance for retaining them. Registers of approved inbound flows and approved outbound destinations, each with port, protocol, endpoint and justification, are required.

artifacts.name: Firewall Ruleset & Segregation Review Records
artifacts.description: Records of the periodic review of network security control configurations and rule sets, showing the reviewer, the scope covered, the findings, the reviewer or approver sign-off, and a tracker of follow-up actions through to closure. Reviews must identify redundant, shadowed and overly permissive rules. Cadence differs materially by framework: six-monthly review of network security control configurations, quarterly configuration review, and periodic reviews of segregation adequacy without a fixed interval - collect at the shortest applicable cycle. Maintenance and version history of the configuration standard itself, and firewall capacity and performance reports demonstrating sizing matches traffic volume, are also requested.

artifacts.name: Segmentation Penetration Test & Validation Reports
artifacts.description: Independent testing that the segmentation actually isolates what it claims to: the segmentation penetration test report confirming out-of-scope networks cannot reach the protected environment, the inventory of segmentation controls covered by the test, coverage evidence showing all isolation mechanisms were exercised, and remediation records for every deficiency found. Frequency differs: at least every twelve months and after any change to segmentation controls for most entities, at least every six months for service providers, with the test schedule and history to prove the cadence. Also covers connectivity test results proving the management segment is unreachable from workload segments, and the periodic network security validation report or attack simulation confirming the layered controls function as designed.

artifacts.name: Environment Scope Definition & Validation Records
artifacts.description: The annually confirmed scope document defining the protected environment: all data flows, all locations where regulated data is stored, processed or transmitted, and identification of every system component in and connected to that environment. Must be supported by the documented scoping validation methodology, the results of the validation activities performed (data discovery scans, network analysis, personnel interviews) and records of scope reviews triggered by significant changes to the environment.

artifacts.name: Network Device Hardening Standards & Configuration File Management
artifacts.description: The hardening standards applied to routers, switches, firewalls and wireless access points, plus the procedure governing where network security control configuration files (running and start-up) are stored and how they are protected. Must include the access control configuration on the configuration repository or backup store holding those files, and records confirming start-up configurations are kept synchronised with running configurations so a device reboot does not silently drop enforcement.

artifacts.name: IDS/IPS, NAC & Network Monitoring Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration of the detection and admission controls layered on the segmented network: IDS/IPS rule configuration with sample alerts investigated, deployment evidence showing coverage across the zones, network access control and 802.1X configuration, and port security or MAC filtering configuration on access switches. Must include network activity logs and the change and configuration management records for network changes, and the staffing arrangement for continuous monitoring where the framework requires a round-the-clock security operations capability.

artifacts.name: Secure Management, Remote & Zone Access Configuration
artifacts.description: Configuration governing administrative and remote entry into the segmented network: the jump server or bastion configuration through which management access is brokered, encrypted management protocols (SSH, IPSec) with multi-factor authentication enforced, the AAA server deployment authenticating those sessions, VPN and remote access configuration with monitoring, auditing and MFA, and the identity and access management system configuration backing the authorisation decisions.

NET-06.notes: 135 entries across 18 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts. The listed automated collectors are SaaS identity connectors rather than network device collectors, so cloud-native network configuration (VPC/subnet/security group) is partly collectible while on-premise firewall, wireless and NAC evidence remains manual. PCI DSS contributes 47 of the 135 entries and drives the scope-definition and approved-services buckets.

artifacts.name: Intrusion Detection Deployment Architecture
