artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing sensors deployed at boundaries between security domains aligned to risk classification, the deployment topology for internal and external sensors, the deployment documentation, the approved network architecture diagram showing perimeter security, intrusion detection, web application firewall and denial-of-service protection placement, the network architecture and firewall rules surrounding them, and the validation report confirming all required boundaries have coverage.

artifacts.name: Detection Rule Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export of sensors with their active signature sets and tuning, the detection and prevention rule configuration, the prevention action logs, the alert configuration, the alert threshold configurations, the automated alert mechanism documentation, the multi-layer detection architecture documentation, and the perimeter, web application firewall and denial-of-service protection configuration export for cloud-hosted environments. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented attack monitoring requirement.

artifacts.name: Signature Currency Records
artifacts.description: The signature and engine update records evidencing currency of detection capabilities, the signature update logs, and the detection rule tuning records with the tuning and alert records supporting them.

artifacts.name: Alert Triage and Response Records
artifacts.description: The sample alerts with the personnel response and triage records, the documented response procedure with its on-call rotation, the alert review records, the alert and blocking reports, the incident response records, the incident response trigger criteria, and the sample alerts from the deployed sensors.

artifacts.name: Detection Effectiveness Testing
artifacts.description: The evidence from simulated attacks or red-team exercises showing detection and mitigation, the network security assessment results, the gap analysis documentation, the scenario-based test results, the annual testing plan for critical systems with the critical system identification behind it, the test execution records, and the testing coverage reports.

artifacts.name: Anti-Spoofing Controls
artifacts.description: The documented standard listing the source address ranges blocked at ingress, the configuration evidence of anti-spoofing controls including reverse path forwarding and private and bogon address filtering, and the sample log entries showing spoofed source addresses dropped at the perimeter.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy and Assessment
artifacts.description: The policy defining network security controls proportionate to network complexity, the assessment report on the adequacy of those controls, the logs from network monitoring detecting policy violations and atypical activities, and the virtual private network concentrator deployment in the demilitarised zone.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Capability
artifacts.description: The inventory of automated cyber monitoring solutions, the operations centre architecture showing monitoring coverage across attack types, the reports showing tracked cyber attack categories, the performance dashboard for the operations centre, and the dashboard export showing health and alert counts for the deployed security services.

artifacts.name: Cloud Threat Model
artifacts.description: The threat model mapping cloud-specific threats including hypervisor escape, weak interfaces, token wrapping and side channels to the implemented detection controls.

artifacts.name: Network Service Provider Controls
artifacts.description: The documented security features required of each network service, the contracts with connectivity and interconnect providers carrying security terms, the log of changes to network services with their security impact assessments, the monitoring reports showing adherence to agreed service levels, the assurance reports received from providers, and the evidence of encryption on inter-site circuits and virtual private networks.

artifacts.name: Endpoint and Host Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The anti-malware and endpoint protection deployment evidence, the file integrity monitoring configuration with its alerts, the application allow-listing documentation, and the software installation restriction policies and controls covering the hosts behind the network sensors.

artifacts.name: Mail Gateway Filtering Evidence
artifacts.description: The mail gateway file type blocking configuration with the blocked file type list and the gateway filtering reports.

NET-08.notes: 65 asks across 13 frameworks. The intrusion detection deployment, its tuning and its alert handling are three distinct proofs. PCI DSS 1.4.3 anti-spoofing and ISO 27001 A.8.21 network services arrive through adjacent crosswalks and are kept separate rather than absorbed.

artifacts.name: Network Security Control Configuration Standard
artifacts.description: The approved configuration standard defining ruleset baselines, defaults, naming, documentation requirements and review cadence, with the version history and maintenance records naming reviewer and approver, and sample production configurations demonstrating the standard is implemented.

artifacts.name: Network Architecture and Zone Diagram
artifacts.description: The current network architecture diagram showing security zones, the DMZ topology identifying which servers sit in it, the diagram marking the protected environment perimeter and the controls enforcing it, the perimeter deployment architecture at every trusted/untrusted boundary, and the update log evidencing refresh after every significant change.

artifacts.name: Data Flow Diagram and Transmission Inventory
artifacts.description: The current data-flow diagram showing every ingress, processing point, storage location and transmission path, the inventory of transmission channels and storage locations it references, and the records evidencing the diagrams are updated after changes to data flows or environment.

artifacts.name: Trusted and Untrusted Network Register
artifacts.description: The register classifying every network as trusted or untrusted with the enforcement point separating them, and the configuration export of the perimeter controls at those boundaries.

artifacts.name: Inbound and Outbound Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The register of allowed inbound flows and approved outbound destinations with business justification, the ruleset exports showing traffic restricted to what is necessary in each direction, and the explicit default-deny rules terminating both chains.

artifacts.name: Approved Services and Ports Register
artifacts.description: The register listing every allowed service, protocol and port with its documented business justification and approver, the sample approval records, and the configuration export demonstrating only those are permitted.

artifacts.name: Insecure Service Mitigation Records
artifacts.description: The register of insecure services, protocols or ports still in use with the specific compensating security features applied to each, the configuration evidence of those mitigations, and the documented business justification and risk acceptance for retaining them.

artifacts.name: Ruleset Review Records
artifacts.description: The last two cycles of six-monthly configuration review reports with reviewer, scope and conclusions; the reviewer sign-off records; the periodic ruleset review records with justification and cleanup actions; and the tracker of follow-up actions with closure status.

artifacts.name: Configuration File Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The procedure governing where running and start-up configuration files are stored and how they are protected, the access control configuration on the repository or backup store holding them, and the records confirming start-up configurations remain synchronised with running configurations.

artifacts.name: Segmentation Penetration Test Records
artifacts.description: The inventory of segmentation controls in scope of testing, the latest segmentation penetration test report, the test evidence confirming out-of-scope networks remain isolated, and the coverage evidence across all isolation mechanisms. Cadence differs: at least annually and after segmentation changes for all entities, at least six-monthly for service providers with the test schedule and history.

artifacts.name: Scope Validation Records
artifacts.description: The annually confirmed scope document including all data flows, storage locations and connected systems; the documented scoping validation methodology; the validation results from data discovery scans, network analysis and interviews; and the scope reviews performed after significant changes.

artifacts.name: Wireless Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: The inventory of all wireless networks with their enforcement points, the architecture showing a control between every wireless network and the protected environment, the ruleset export from those controls, the wireless documentation with placement, identifiers and encryption, and the wireless security configuration with rogue access point detection and guest isolation.

artifacts.name: Boundary Monitoring and Detection Evidence
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention configuration with sample alerts investigated, the adjacent firewall and intrusion prevention configuration for the exposed segment, the external traffic monitoring records, the covert channel scan reports, the routing protocol authentication evidence, and the concentrator deployment in the exposed zone.

artifacts.name: Network Security Policy and Hardening
artifacts.description: The network security policy covering architecture, controls and operations, the device hardening standards, the configuration baselines, the segregation policy with its implementing procedure, and the awareness communications informing personnel of it.

artifacts.name: Remote and External Access Configuration
artifacts.description: The VPN and remote access security configurations, the multi-factor implementation for external access, and the firewall and network security control configurations governing them.

NET-08.1.notes: 73 asks across 6 frameworks but dominated by PCI DSS, which contributes eight separately testable network-security-control requirements. They are grouped by what an assessor asks for in one go — the ruleset standard, the boundary evidence, the review cycle, the segmentation test — rather than one artifact per sub-requirement.

artifacts.name: Cryptographic Standard for Transmission
artifacts.description: The approved standard listing permitted protocols, cipher suites, key lengths and key exchange algorithms for data in transit, the cipher policy, and the encryption practices inventory covering each transport method in use.

artifacts.name: Transmission Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: The transport layer configuration export for applications and network devices, the encryption configuration for data in transit including sensitive categories, the secure file transfer configuration, the dynamic key exchange evidence, the hardware security module usage records, and the transfer encryption configuration.

artifacts.name: Certificate Inventory and Validation
artifacts.description: The inventory of certificates used to protect data in transit with issuer, expiry, key length and subject alternative names; the procedure governing certificate trust validation including chain and revocation checking; and the certificate management records.

artifacts.name: External Transport Security Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The external scan reports confirming only current protocol versions are accepted and only strong cipher suites are offered, providing independent proof that the configured standard is what the network actually presents.

artifacts.name: Cloud-to-On-Premise Connectivity Controls
artifacts.description: The site-to-site connection or direct-link configuration, the address management register identifying dedicated source and destination endpoints, the access rule export showing traffic permitted only between those endpoints and ports, the rule review procedure defining frequency and reviewers, the completed review records with rule-by-rule justification and stale-rule removal, and the rule analysis tool reports identifying redundant, shadowed or overly permissive rules.

artifacts.name: Electronic Commerce Service Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of electronic commerce services, the documented security measures for each, the partner service agreements, the service provider details, and the approved standard for electronic commerce services with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Public Information Controls
artifacts.description: The public information policy with the information disclosure guidelines, the content approval workflow, and the website content review records governing what is placed on open networks deliberately.

artifacts.name: Network Access Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The access control list configuration, the role-based access control documentation, the access enforcement testing results, the account management procedures with review documentation, the user authorisation records, and the separation of duties matrix with incompatible duties identified.

artifacts.name: Boundary Detection and Monitoring
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention configuration, the system monitoring strategy, the security information platform deployment documentation, the monitoring alert review records, and the firewall and network security control configurations.

artifacts.name: Malware Protection over Open Networks
artifacts.description: The anti-malware solution documentation, the definition update records, the scan reports and the malware incident records covering the paths where data crosses untrusted networks.

artifacts.name: Input Validation Controls
artifacts.description: The input validation procedures and configuration documentation with the application input validation testing results, protecting the receiving end of an open-network transmission.

artifacts.name: Integrity Verification Records
artifacts.description: The file integrity monitoring configuration, the integrity verification tool reports, and the unauthorised change detection records covering the systems that terminate open-network connections.

artifacts.name: Security Advisory Response Records
artifacts.description: The security alert subscription records, the internal security advisory procedures, and the advisory review and response records covering protocol and cipher weaknesses as they are disclosed.

artifacts.name: Network Availability Protections
artifacts.description: The network availability protections and the secure file transfer policy and configuration, and the virtual private network configuration over wireless where that path is used.

artifacts.name: Transmission Security Architecture
artifacts.description: The network security architecture documentation, the transmission security controls inventory, the network architecture diagram showing segmentation and trust zones, and the device configuration baselines with ruleset review records.

NET-12.notes: 71 asks across 10 frameworks. PCI DSS 4.2.1 drives the most specific demands — certificate inventory, cipher standard, external scan proof — and those are kept apart from the general transmission-encryption evidence because they are tested with named artifacts.

artifacts.name: Electronic Messaging Policy
artifacts.description: The mail security policy, the internet usage policy, the control requirements per messaging type, the defined and approved security requirements ensuring confidentiality, integrity and availability of mail and hosting services, and the evidence those requirements are implemented for hosted services. HITRUST requires the approved electronic messaging policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Messaging Inventory
artifacts.description: The electronic messaging inventory by category and the distribution list governance policy scoping which channels the controls must cover.

artifacts.name: Message Transport Encryption
artifacts.description: The mail encryption configuration enforcing encrypted external mail flows, the encrypted messaging configuration, the encryption configuration for data in transit, the transport encryption configurations, the certificate documentation, the transmission integrity verification, and the virtual private network encryption standards.

artifacts.name: Message Content Controls
artifacts.description: The content filtering configuration, the mail security controls, the data loss prevention tool configuration with its reports, the auto-response restriction configuration, the signature and disclaimer configuration, and the legal disclaimer applied to outgoing mail.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the managed transfer platform log showing encrypted transfers and recipients; the secure file transfer policy and configuration; the transfer agreement templates; the courier chain-of-custody receipts; and the information exchange agreements with their secure transfer mechanism configuration.

artifacts.name: Voice Messaging Controls
artifacts.description: The documented controls over voice-over-address services with the records demonstrating they operate. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Network Protection Records
artifacts.description: The firewall and network security control configurations, the intrusion detection and prevention system configurations, the multi-factor authentication implementation for external access, the virtual private network and remote access security configurations, and the network availability protections covering the messaging infrastructure.

artifacts.name: Endpoint Messaging Controls
artifacts.description: The device management policy and configuration and the removable media policy with its encryption controls governing messaging from managed devices.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the electronic messaging requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

NET-13.notes: 40 asks across 9 frameworks. Mail transport protection, mail content controls and the messaging inventory that scopes both are three proofs; NIST 800-171's voice-over-address control arrives here and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering approvals, authentication, encryption, device protection, logging and monitoring of remote connections, with the remote working policy defining conditions and approvals and the risk assessment covering threats, controls and residual risk. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement to monitor and control remote access.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Gateway Configuration
artifacts.description: The VPN or zero-trust gateway configuration with its documentation, the multi-factor enforcement on remote endpoints, the encryption standard for remote sessions with prohibited protocols named, the integration with the central authentication service, and the secure channel configuration.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Approval Records
artifacts.description: The workflow records of remote access requests and their approvals, the written management approvals for access to high-risk assets, the risk assessment performed per request, the approved user list, and the monthly reconciliation confirming the live entitlement set matches it.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Session Logs
artifacts.description: The logs from the remote access gateway covering all sessions with source addresses, durations and anomaly alerts; the connection logs; the session monitoring logs; and the regular audit reports over them covering frequency, users, sessions and anomalies.

artifacts.name: Remote Device Security Standards
artifacts.description: The hardening baseline applied to devices used remotely covering encryption and endpoint protection, the remote device security standards, the device compliance verification records, and the home office security guidelines issued to staff.

artifacts.name: Remote Working Agreements
artifacts.description: The signed agreements between employee and organisation covering the terms under which remote working is permitted.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Remote Access Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of third-party remote access accounts with vendor, purpose and access window; the just-in-time procedure enabling accounts only during the period needed and disabling them otherwise; the enable and disable records aligned to those windows; and the monitoring or recording logs of third-party sessions.

artifacts.name: Per-Customer Provider Credentials
artifacts.description: For providers with remote access into multiple customer environments: the register of customer-specific credentials or keys, the configuration evidence showing unique authentication factors per environment, and sample audit logs demonstrating credentials are not shared across customers.

artifacts.name: Remote Session Data Exfiltration Controls
artifacts.description: The configuration of remote access tooling preventing copy and paste, file transfer and screen capture; the data-loss prevention configuration covering remote channels; the documented authorisation records for personnel granted an explicit exception with a defined business need; and sample session audit logs or recordings demonstrating enforcement.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Service Provider Register
artifacts.description: The list of providers with which regulated data is shared or that could affect its security, with the description of what each receives and through which channel, and the records evidencing the list is maintained as new providers are engaged.

artifacts.name: Application and System Account Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of application and system accounts with purpose, privileges and owner, the procedure for assigning and managing them including periodic review, the least-privilege configuration evidence, and the review records.

artifacts.name: Network Segregation for Remote Access
artifacts.description: The network segmentation and perimeter configuration export evidencing separation, the evidence that wireless and internet-facing systems are isolated from critical systems, the network activity logs and change management records for network changes, and the network architecture diagram showing the trust zones remote access terminates in.

artifacts.name: Access Matrix and Provisioning Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix mapping roles to permissions by user type and access method, the system access standard operating procedures, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

NET-14.notes: 76 asks across 14 frameworks. Workforce remote access, third-party remote access and service-provider access into customer environments are three different populations with different controls; PCI DSS tests the second and third separately from the first.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering approvals, authentication, encryption, device protection, logging and monitoring of remote access; the remote access policy; and the standard specifying encryption for remote access channels. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented encrypt-remote-access-sessions requirement. HITRUST requires the approved user authentication policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Remote Session Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration evidence of encrypted remote access protocols with prohibited versions disabled, the end-to-end encrypted remote access protocols, the virtual private network configuration documentation, the secure channel configuration for remote access, the encrypted remote access for vendors, the secure tunnelling evidence, the cryptographic standard document for the tunnel, the session integrity evidence, and the configuration audits verifying them.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Authentication
artifacts.description: The configuration evidence of multi-factor authentication enforced for remote access across the tunnel, zero-trust broker and jump host; the multi-factor configuration evidence for remote access endpoints; the multi-factor configuration for remote users; the multi-factor implementation; and the integration of the remote access gateway with the central authentication service.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Approval Records
artifacts.description: The sample written management approvals for remote access to high-risk assets, the workflow records of remote access requests and approvals, and the remote access authorisation records.

artifacts.name: Remote Session Logs
artifacts.description: The sample logs from the tunnel, zero-trust broker or privileged access platform showing remote sessions to high-risk assets, the logs from remote access gateways covering all communications, the remote access connection logs, the remote access logs, and the remote session monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Audit Reports
artifacts.description: The regular audit reports on remote access to high-risk assets covering frequency, users, sessions and anomalies.

artifacts.name: Network Boundary Records
artifacts.description: The network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones; the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records; the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping; and the user access provisioning, modification and review records covering remote users.

NET-14.2.notes: 38 asks across 9 frameworks. The remote access policy, the encryption and authentication configuration enforcing it, and the session logs proving it are three proofs; the approval records are kept separate because access is granted per request rather than standing.

artifacts.name: Remote Working Policy
artifacts.description: The policy defining remote working conditions, approvals and security requirements; the teleworking policy; the home working policy for critical functions; the guidance issued to staff on securing home work environments; and the risk assessment covering threats, controls and residual risks for remote working. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remote and home working policy requirement. HITRUST requires the approved teleworking policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Remote Working Agreements
artifacts.description: The signed agreements between employee and organisation covering remote working terms and the approval records for privileged users working remotely.

artifacts.name: Remote Device Baseline
artifacts.description: The hardening baseline applied to devices used remotely covering encryption and endpoint protection, the device management policy with its enrolment register, and the teleworking access authentication evidence.

artifacts.name: Remote Access Configuration and Logs
artifacts.description: The secure remote access configuration with its multi-factor and encryption evidence and the log of remote access sessions with source addresses, durations and anomaly alerts. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented monitor-and-control-remote-access requirement.

artifacts.name: Off-Premises Asset Controls
artifacts.description: The policy governing use of assets outside organisational premises, the log of assets checked out for off-site use with expected return, the management authorisation records for off-site equipment use, the travel security guidance including country-specific advice, the off-site equipment insurance, and the log of off-site asset loss or theft incidents with the response actions taken.

artifacts.name: Alternate Site Data Safeguards
artifacts.description: The documented safeguarding of regulated data at alternate work sites with the records demonstrating it operates, the random audit reports of teleworking sites, and the sector-specific protection controls applied to regulated data handled remotely. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Facility Access Records
artifacts.description: The physical access control records, the data centre access logs, the visitor management logs, and the security camera evidence covering the premises staff return to.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the teleworking requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

NET-14.5.notes: 35 asks across 7 frameworks. The remote working policy and agreement, the device baseline and the off-premises asset controls are three proofs; ISO 27001 A.7.9 off-premises equipment is kept separate from A.6.7 remote working because one covers assets and the other the working arrangement.

artifacts.name: Authorised Access Point Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of authorised wireless access points with location, network identifier, hardware address and business justification; the wireless access point inventory; the access point registration list; the records evidencing inventory maintenance and updates; the wireless authorisation records; and the wireless site survey reports. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented authorise-wireless-access requirement.

artifacts.name: Rogue Access Point Detection
artifacts.description: The procedure for detection of authorised and unauthorised wireless access points at the required interval, the latest four quarters of wireless scan reports, the wireless intrusion detection configuration evidencing automated continuous detection, and the sample response records for unauthorised detections with their investigation and remediation.

artifacts.name: Wireless Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The wireless network configuration standards, the enterprise-grade encryption configuration, the enterprise authentication configuration, the network identifier broadcasting settings, the wireless administrative restriction evidence, the trusted device wireless access evidence, and the wireless security assessment results.

artifacts.name: Wireless Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: The guest network isolation architecture, the guest network segregation configuration, the network design showing isolation, the evidence of isolated wireless and internet-facing systems segregated from critical systems, the network segmentation and perimeter configuration export, the specialised device wireless restrictions, and the guest wireless access monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Wireless Usage Policy
artifacts.description: The wireless access policy, the wireless usage policy, and the wireless network risk assessment scoping where wireless is permitted.

artifacts.name: Network Service Provider Controls
artifacts.description: The documented security features required of each network service, the contracts with connectivity and interconnect providers carrying security terms, the log of changes to network services with their security impact assessments, the monitoring reports showing adherence to agreed service levels, the assurance reports received from providers, and the evidence of encryption on inter-site circuits and virtual private networks.

artifacts.name: Network Change and Logging Records
artifacts.description: The network activity logs with the change and configuration management records for network changes and the remote access configuration with its monitoring, auditing and multi-factor authentication.

NET-15.notes: 37 asks across 7 frameworks. The authorised access point inventory, the periodic scan for unauthorised ones, and the encryption and segregation of the authorised estate are three proofs; the rogue detection is what proves the inventory is complete.

artifacts.name: Wireless Encryption Configuration
artifacts.description: The wireless encryption configuration using enterprise-grade protection, the encryption configuration, the authentication method configuration, and the wireless network configuration standards. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-wireless-access requirement.

artifacts.name: Wireless Hardening Records
artifacts.description: The documented wireless hardening standard listing each default to be changed, the wireless controller and access point configuration export showing secure settings and absence of vendor defaults, the records evidencing all vendor defaults have been changed, the access point hardening configuration, the network identifier broadcasting settings, the hidden identifier setting, and the wireless administrative restriction evidence.

artifacts.name: Wireless Segregation Evidence

artifacts.description: The wireless access policy, the wireless usage policy, the wireless authorisation records, the access point registration list, the wireless access point inventory, the wireless network risk assessment, and the wireless security assessment results.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Policy

artifacts.name: Leakage Alerts and Incidents

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Records

NET-17.notes: 43 asks across 8 frameworks. The policy, the rule set and the alerts it produces are three proofs; SBP Cloud 12.2 arrives carrying a full cloud data-protection stack whose backup and residency parts are kept out of the leakage-prevention artifacts.

artifacts.name: Web Filtering Policy

artifacts.name: Web Filtering Configuration
