artifacts.description: The proxy log showing allowed and blocked requests for sample periods, the address filtering reports, the records of investigations into blocked-site hits suggesting malicious activity, and the gateway threat detection reports.

artifacts.name: Name Resolution Filtering
artifacts.description: The name-resolution filtering configuration, the filtering service configuration, the blocked domain lists, the filtering reports, the resolution-layer firewall deployment, and the resolution-layer threat intelligence subscription feeding it.

artifacts.name: Name Resolution Architecture
artifacts.description: The name-resolution architecture diagram distinguishing internal, external and demilitarised-zone resolvers, the resolution service hardening baseline, and the next-generation firewall configuration in front of it.

artifacts.name: Application Layer Filtering
artifacts.description: The application layer filtering configuration with its filtering reports, the web application firewall and proxy configuration, the deep packet inspection enablement evidence, the application control and allow-list, and the endpoint hardening supporting it.

artifacts.name: Mail Gateway Filtering
artifacts.description: The mail gateway anti-malware configuration, the mail security controls, and the mail security policy governing them.

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Documentation
artifacts.description: The network boundary protection documentation, the demilitarised-zone architecture documentation, the firewall and proxy configurations, and the boundary protection monitoring logs. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented regulated-data flow control requirement.

artifacts.name: Isolated Browsing Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of separate browsing stations, the network architecture documentation showing their isolation, and the proxy or firewall configuration blocking internet access from the protected zone.

artifacts.name: Denial of Service Protection
artifacts.description: The protection solution documentation and the mitigation service agreements covering the perimeter through which filtered traffic passes.

artifacts.name: Network Routing Controls
artifacts.description: The network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones; the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records; the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping; and the user access provisioning, modification and review records. HITRUST requires the approved network routing control policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Safe Browsing Awareness Material
artifacts.description: The training content teaching staff safe browsing practices, communicating what the filter blocks and why.

artifacts.name: Information Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining authorised transfer methods, encryption requirements and approvals; the procedures for each specific method; the mail encryption configuration; the managed transfer platform log; the transfer agreement templates; and the courier chain-of-custody receipts.

NET-18.notes: 61 asks across 10 frameworks. Name-resolution filtering and web-category filtering are kept apart because they sit at different layers and are evidenced from different consoles; ISO 27001 A.5.14 information transfer arrives through an adjacent crosswalk and is not folded in.

artifacts.name: Operations Security Policy
artifacts.description: The approved top-level policy governing IT operations, with management approval evidence and its review records. ADHICS requires it to cover all twelve specified management demand areas; DORA requires it to sit within the ICT risk management framework; NIST AI RMF expects the equivalent approved organisational policies for AI operations.

artifacts.name: Operating Procedures Library
artifacts.description: The central library of standard operating procedures and runbooks for routine operational activities (backup, patching, restart), with version control log, review records, the on-call and shift handover procedure, and the records showing procedures were distributed to and acknowledged by operators.

artifacts.name: Domain Security Policy Set
artifacts.description: The set of approved topic policies with their supporting operational procedures, one per security domain: network security, secure configuration, data protection, transmission cryptography, anti-malware, secure development, access control, authentication, physical access, logging and monitoring, and security testing. PCI DSS requires each to cover all activities in its corresponding requirement; DORA requires equivalent coverage of access control, authentication, encryption and network security architecture.

artifacts.name: Policy Review, Dissemination and Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Annual review records for each policy, evidence of dissemination to affected parties, and personnel acknowledgements confirming awareness and currency. PCI DSS tests these separately from the policies themselves and requires them per requirement area; ADHICS and ISO 27001 expect the same review and distribution trail.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Policy Set
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures governing AI operations, covering the documented AI risk tolerance statement with its approval records, the RACI matrix defining AI risk management roles, the risk treatment plan with prioritisation, and the implementation records evidencing each outcome within the AI lifecycle.

artifacts.name: AI Impact and Safety Assessment Records
artifacts.description: AI impact assessments, context documentation covering intended purposes, safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, the stakeholder engagement and feedback log, and the human oversight and human-AI configuration design.

artifacts.name: AI Third-Party and Regulatory Register
artifacts.description: The legal and regulatory requirements register mapping applicable AI laws to the organisation's obligations, together with the third-party AI and data risk assessments and the policies governing them.

artifacts.name: Documented Information Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The document control policy and procedure covering availability, protection, distribution, version control, retention and disposition, the retention and disposition schedule, the register of external-origin documents, and the document management system access control settings and audit logs.

artifacts.name: Data Operations Plan and Controls
artifacts.description: The documented data operations plan with the approved data management and personal data protection strategy behind it, the data security control evidence (access controls and equivalents), the privacy artifacts, and the compliance records held under the national regulator's regime.

artifacts.name: Security Monitoring Tooling and Reports
artifacts.description: The inventory of ICT security monitoring tools, the continuous monitoring reports they produce, and the documented measures by which ICT risk impact is minimised.

artifacts.name: Visitor Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for authorising visitor access including pre-approval, identification verification and escort, the badge standard distinguishing visitors from personnel, and sample identification-verification and escorted-access records.

artifacts.name: Internal Security Communication and Awareness Evidence
artifacts.description: Internal security communication procedures, security awareness programme materials, the board reporting packages on internal controls and security, and the whistleblower or anonymous reporting mechanism documentation.

OPS-01.notes: 109 asks across 8 frameworks. PCI DSS contributes one near-identical policy-and-procedure pair per requirement area (Req 1 through 11); those are merged into a single domain policy set rather than kept as eleven artifacts, with the review and dissemination records held separately because PCI DSS tests them as their own control.

artifacts.name: SOP Register
artifacts.description: A single register/index of every operating procedure in force, with procedure name, owner, current version, approval date, last review date and next review date, plus the storage location. Must cover all technology operations areas and be reconcilable to the procedure documents actually produced; several frameworks require the register itself to be maintained under version control and to list documented information additionally deemed necessary for the management system's effectiveness.

artifacts.name: Approved Standard Operating Procedures
artifacts.description: The current, approved, signed procedure documents themselves - step-by-step instructions with responsible roles, control points and exception handling, each referencing its parent policy. Coverage must span the operational areas the frameworks enumerate: network security control administration and ruleset review; logging, log protection, review, retention and time sync; security testing (scanning, penetration testing, IDS/IPS, FIM, tamper detection); secure configuration management; account/sensitive data protection, retention, disposal and masking; cryptographic key generation, distribution, storage, retirement/destruction, split-knowledge/dual control and substitution prevention; transmission security and certificate lifecycle; anti-malware operation; secure SDLC and code review; change control including back-out; access provisioning/modification/review/revocation; authentication and account lifecycle; physical entry, visitor management and secure areas; workstation use and acceptable use; system-access SOPs by user type; CERT/escalation coordination; and end-to-end transaction traceability. Procedures must be available to the operations personnel who perform the work.

artifacts.name: Governing Policy Library
artifacts.description: The approved parent policies the SOPs implement, each documented, management-approved, current and disseminated to affected parties: network security, logging and monitoring, security testing, secure configuration, data protection, transmission security, anti-malware, secure development, access control, authentication, physical access, workstation use, ICT security strategy and, where applicable, AI trustworthiness and third-party risk. Each must state scope, applicability, roles and responsibilities, review frequency and carry an approval signature with version history.

artifacts.name: Document Control Procedure, Templates & Repository
artifacts.description: The procedure governing how documented information is created, identified, formatted, reviewed, approved, distributed, version-controlled, protected, retained and disposed of; the approved template library that enforces title, date, author, reference and review fields; the controlled repository (DMS) holding the documents with its folder structure; the retention and disposition schedule; and the register controlling documents of external origin. Include the DMS access-control settings that restrict who can alter a controlled procedure.

artifacts.name: Procedure Review & Version Control Records
artifacts.description: Evidence each procedure is kept current: version history per document showing what changed and when, periodic review records naming reviewer, date, observations and corrective actions, and review/approval workflow logs or signatures. Review must be at least annual where the framework specifies a cadence, and must additionally be triggered by material change; records must show re-approval by the authorised approver after each change.

artifacts.name: Procedure Dissemination & Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that current procedures reached the people who must follow them and that those people confirmed receipt: distribution or publication records (email, intranet, DMS notification), staff acknowledgement records tied to the applicable SOP and version, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the requirement. Where user-facing policies are in scope (e.g. authentication guidance), include the communication to all users plus their acknowledgements.

artifacts.name: Roles, Responsibilities & Segregation of Duties Matrix
artifacts.description: Documented assignment of who performs, approves and oversees each operational process: RACI matrices for IT and AI risk processes, organisational structure charts showing operations roles and reporting lines, the segregation-of-duties matrix with conflict analysis, and role-specific registers such as designated key custodians with their assigned components and signed custodian acknowledgements. Must identify owners, cover all relevant processes and carry a last-updated date.

artifacts.name: Procedure Execution Records
artifacts.description: Sampled records proving the SOPs are actually followed in practice, not just written: completed change tickets showing reason, impact, authorised approval, testing that verified control integrity and back-out plan; change advisory board minutes; test/UAT evidence for sampled changes; signed key generation and key ceremony records under dual control; key distribution and destruction records with method and witness sign-off; visitor identification verification and escort records; and on-call/shift handover records. Each must be traceable to the procedure that mandates it.

artifacts.name: System Logs Evidencing Procedure Execution
artifacts.description: System-generated, tamper-protected logs that corroborate the procedural records: HSM/KMS audit logs of key generation, import and replacement with operator, timestamp, approver and integrity-check result; document management system audit logs; infrastructure and operations monitoring/event logs; AI lifecycle event logs with the time of use, input data and out-of-range outputs; and end-to-end transaction audit trails demonstrating traceability across tiers. Retention must match the stated log retention policy.

artifacts.name: System & Architecture Documentation Referenced by Procedures
artifacts.description: The current, version-controlled, dated and approved reference documentation the SOPs point to: system and network architecture diagrams showing components, interconnections, trust zones and data flows; security architecture and secure design principles; escalation/communication flow diagrams between response tiers; site security plans; asset and protection-tool inventories; AI system technical documentation (purpose, assumptions, limitations, monitoring, design, development data); intended-use context documentation; and non-repudiation control documentation. Diagrams must be updated when the environment changes.

artifacts.name: Configuration Evidence Supporting Procedures
artifacts.description: Live configuration extracts showing the procedural controls are technically enforced: key wrapping/transport configuration, HSM/KMS configuration including FIPS validation level and tamper response, access-control configuration restricting key storage and key import/replacement to designated custodians under dual control, access control and authentication mechanism configuration, and encryption implementation evidence. Each export must carry the date, system identifier and reviewer.

artifacts.name: SOP Compliance Audit & Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: Independent assessment that documented procedures are adhered to and complete: internal audit reports testing SOP adherence in practice, documentation-completeness audits confirming required documentation was produced at each project phase, capability/maturity assessments with improvement plans, security engineering review records, outsourced-service compliance reports, and regulator or external assessment records. Findings must be tracked to closure with owners and dates.

artifacts.name: Exception & Deviation Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented process for handling departures from procedure and the records it produced: the policy/procedure exception management process with approvals and expiry, failure and rollback management plans covering feature toggling, update process and user notification, human override and appeal mechanisms where automated processing is in scope, and safety/fail-safe evaluation records with residual risk. Each exception record must name the approver, the justification and the review date.

artifacts.name: Control-to-Risk Mapping & Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The documentation tying the procedure set back to the risks and obligations it exists to satisfy: the inventory of control activities mapped to risks, the risk-control mapping matrix and control design documentation, the legal and regulatory requirements register with owner and review dates, the documented risk tolerance/appetite statement with approval records, and the risk treatment plan with prioritisation, response options and tracking. Must show coverage of all in-scope processes and a last-review date.

OPS-01.1.notes: 168 entries collapse to 14 artifacts. The bulk of the input is the same ask restated per subject area (PCI restates 'policy + operational procedures' for each of Requirements 1-9; DORA, COBIT, QCB, HIPAA and SL CSF restate it for their own domains). Those collapse into the procedure library plus its governing policy library, with the domain list carried in the descriptions.

artifacts.name: IT Service Management Framework
artifacts.description: The documented ITSM framework covering preventive maintenance, incident and problem management, patch management and service delivery, with management approval, the detailed process documents for each component (ITIL-aligned where applicable), the tool screenshots evidencing operationalisation, and the KPI dashboard measuring performance across them.

artifacts.name: Operating Procedures Library
artifacts.description: The central library of standard operating procedures for IT operations, operational runbooks for routine activities such as backup, patching and restart, the on-call and shift handover procedure, the version control log, review records, and the records showing procedures were distributed to and acknowledged by operators.

artifacts.name: Service Level Agreements and Performance
artifacts.description: The service level and operational level agreements including the signed internal SLAs between IT and the business units covering availability, performance, capacity and support, the periodic SLA performance reports, the breach register with remediation actions, the review meeting minutes, and the compliance reports. COBIT additionally expects the service catalogue and customer satisfaction reporting.

artifacts.name: Help Desk Operations Records
artifacts.description: The help desk charter and standard operating procedure, the defined KPIs for resolving each problem category, the ticket logs showing incoming reports recorded and tracked, and the periodic performance reports against those KPIs including first-contact resolution, average handling time and satisfaction.

artifacts.name: Continual Service Improvement Records
artifacts.description: The documented improvement programme with KPIs linked to organisational objectives, the KPI framework and measurement reports showing improvement outcomes, the improvement initiative register with status and benefits realised, and the continuous improvement plans with corrective action reports.

artifacts.name: IT Operating Environment Reporting
artifacts.description: The periodic report on operating environment efficiency covering uptime, performance and incident counts against institutional targets, the IT KPI dashboard, the steering committee minutes reviewing it, and the action log tracking the improvements they mandate.

artifacts.name: Batch and Scheduled Job Controls
artifacts.description: The job schedule documentation with its authorisation, the monitoring dashboard or alert configuration, sample evidence of successful completion, failure logs with resolution documentation, and for period-end the processing schedule and checklist, cutoff control configuration, period lock evidence and batch completion evidence for close processes.

artifacts.name: Quality Management Records
artifacts.description: The quality management system documentation and policies, the quality standards and procedures for IT processes, and the quality monitoring reports with defect tracking records.

artifacts.name: IT Governance Structure Records
artifacts.description: The IT management framework documentation and policies, organisational structure charts with IT roles, RACI matrices for IT processes, capability maturity assessments with improvement plans, the business relationship management framework, business requirements documentation with prioritisation, and the IT-business alignment meeting minutes with action items.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Evidence
artifacts.description: The data processing specifications and documentation, input validation and output reconciliation procedures, processing accuracy monitoring reports, data quality management procedures and metrics, information classification policy, information flow diagrams for critical processes, and the system-generated reports demonstrating data integrity.

artifacts.name: Security Configuration and Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The access control policies and configurations, authentication mechanism documentation, encryption standards and implementation evidence, network security architecture documentation, the ICT security monitoring tools inventory, continuous monitoring reports, and the documented measures minimising ICT risk impact.

artifacts.name: Transmission Security Evidence
artifacts.description: The transmission encryption policy, email encryption implementation evidence, the certificate inventory, and the VPN configuration documentation covering protected transmission.

artifacts.name: Workstation Use and Placement Controls
artifacts.description: The workstation use policy with acceptable use guidelines, the workstation placement and screen privacy requirements, the workstation inventory with its security controls, and the workstation security standards.

artifacts.name: Responsible AI Use Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for responsible use of AI systems including required approvals, cost and approved sourcing, the approval records evidencing it was applied before use, the documented objectives covering fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, reliability and safety, the intended-use conformance procedure, the misuse and concern escalation records to internal personnel and suppliers, and the use event logs supporting them.

artifacts.name: Human Oversight Records
artifacts.description: The plan defining where and how meaningful human oversight is incorporated across the AI system life cycle, and the training records and instructions for the personnel performing that oversight.

artifacts.name: AI System Technical Documentation
artifacts.description: The technical documentation pack covering general description, intended purpose, usage instructions and technical assumptions, the failure management plan covering rollback, feature toggling, update process and user notification, the documentation of operations personnel roles and accountability especially for handling failures or updates, the AI event logging standard covering traceability across life-cycle phases, sample event logs, and the retention policy aligned to intended use and legal requirements.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Service Delivery Records
artifacts.description: The outsourcing agreements containing the required provisions, the evidence of third-party adherence to change management, the service-quality monitoring records, and the incident and downtime logs with root cause analysis and interface availability monitoring.

OPS-03.notes: 96 asks across 11 frameworks. ISO 42001 contributes a distinct block on responsible AI use, human oversight and AI event logging that has no counterpart in the IT service management demands around it, so it is kept separate rather than folded into operating procedures.

artifacts.name: Physical & Environmental Security Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy covering facility access control, physical perimeter protection, environmental safeguards and equipment protection, with evidence of top-management approval, the roles and responsibilities it assigns, distribution and user acknowledgement records, awareness communications, and the periodic review record naming the reviewer. Regulated entities in scope of ICT resilience rules must also show the risk management framework, proportionately scoped, under which these controls sit.

artifacts.name: Physical Security Procedures & Facility Security Plan
artifacts.description: The operating procedures implementing the policy: the facility security plan, data centre physical access procedures, physical security operations documentation, IT operations SOPs covering the facility, environmental protection procedures, hazardous material storage handling, the catalogue of physical, human and procedural controls, and records of procedure review and update.

artifacts.name: Facility Site Plan, Perimeter & Barrier Documentation
artifacts.description: Site plans showing the defined security perimeters and the specification of the physical barriers deployed at each, the list of facilities covered, evidence of physical isolation for sensitive systems, and the tamper and theft prevention measures protecting equipment.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control System Documentation
artifacts.description: Documentation of the badge, biometric and lock systems controlling entry, and the documented physical access rules stating which zones require which authorisation level — the configuration side of physical access, as distinct from the logs it produces.

artifacts.name: Physical & Data Centre Access Logs
artifacts.description: Badge, biometric and manual access logs for facilities and data centres covering the review period, including the physical access control records for secure zones such as the SWIFT environment, with evidence that the logs are reviewed rather than merely retained.

artifacts.name: Visitor Management Procedures & Logs
artifacts.description: The visitor handling procedure (identification, authorisation, escort and badge return) and the completed visitor register or logs for the period, covering data centre and other restricted areas.

artifacts.name: CCTV / Surveillance Deployment & Retention Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of surveillance camera coverage over entry points and sensitive areas, the recording and retention configuration, and sample footage or system records demonstrating the cameras were operating during the period.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Provisioning, De-provisioning & Review Records
artifacts.description: The access request and approval workflow evidence, role-based access matrix and logical access rules standard as applied to facilities, the modification log, the removal SLA report showing timely revocation on departure or role change, privileged access requests, the exception register, and the periodic access review reports with reviewer sign-off. Review frequency varies by framework, so evidence should show at least the most frequent applicable cadence.

artifacts.name: Environmental & Physical Threat Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The risk assessment covering environmental and physical threats — fire, flood, power loss, natural hazards, intrusion — including the perimeter risk assessment and the facility security assessment, the proportionality assessment where a simplified framework is applied, the risk treatment measures selected, and evidence of insurance coverage carried against residual risk.

artifacts.name: Environmental Control Design, Monitoring & Test Records
artifacts.description: Design documentation and operating evidence for environmental protections: fire detection and suppression with current certificates, temperature and humidity monitoring configuration and readings, flood protection measures, power and cooling arrangements, data centre monitoring system documentation, fire drill records and periodic environmental test or inspection reports.

artifacts.name: Facility Maintenance & Repair Records
artifacts.description: Logs of maintenance, repairs and modifications to the physical components of the facility — walls, doors, locks, perimeter, environmental plant — with the approvals for security-relevant changes, and the facilities/environmental management records evidencing planned upkeep rather than reactive fixes only.

artifacts.name: Physical & Environmental Incident Records and Operations Monitoring
artifacts.description: The log of environmental and physical security incidents (fire, flood, power, intrusion, tampering) with response and outcome, the data centre incident response plans, infrastructure operations monitoring logs and security event records, and evidence that the facility protection controls are demonstrably operating during the period.

artifacts.name: Data Centre Standards, Certification & Audit Reports
artifacts.description: For owned or provider-operated data centres: the data centre standards document and operations manual, evidence of certification against the applicable tier or standard, internal and external audit reports, environmental audit records, physical security survey reports, walkthrough photographs, and provider service management reports where the facility is outsourced.

artifacts.name: Backup & Disaster Recovery Evidence for Facility Loss
artifacts.description: The backup policy and schedule with completion logs, the disaster recovery plan covering loss of the facility, and the results of restoration and DR tests — the availability controls that stand behind the physical and environmental protections.

artifacts.name: Secure Media Transfer & Equipment Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The information transfer policy and secure transfer procedures, transfer agreement templates, managed file transfer logs, courier chain-of-custody receipts and encryption applied to transferred media, together with the off-site equipment disposal policy and the records evidencing secure disposal or sanitisation of equipment leaving the facility.

PES-01.notes: 111 asks collapse to 15 artifacts. Only two cloud-provider collectors are attached and physical security for hosted infrastructure is largely inherited, so most items are manual, with badge/visitor logs and access reviews hybrid (system exports plus reviewer sign-off). Where the data centre is a provider's, the certification and audit report item is the practical substitute for the site-level artifacts.

artifacts.name: Physical Zoning Plan
artifacts.description: The physical zoning plan, the security zone definitions, the security zone documentation, the site plans showing security perimeters, the floor plans showing demarcation of public and work areas, the facility security plan, the perimeter security documentation, and the secure area identification and perimeter documentation. HITRUST requires the approved physical security perimeter and securing offices policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Physical Barrier Specifications
artifacts.description: The physical barrier specifications, the physical barriers between public and restricted areas, the perimeter security design, the security countermeasures documentation, the physical access controls, and the physical separation of card production and identification-number generation areas.

artifacts.name: Per-Zone Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The per-zone risk assessment and the risk-based perimeter assessment records determining the controls each zone warrants.

artifacts.name: Signage Controls
artifacts.description: The signage policy with its review evidence, governing what a sign reveals about the zone behind it.

artifacts.name: Zone Access Controls
artifacts.description: The card data storage access controls and the perimeter monitoring records covering the zone boundaries.

artifacts.name: Facility Access and Review Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the zoning rules, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PES-01.2.notes: 31 asks across 4 frameworks. The zoning plan, the barriers that realise it and the per-zone risk assessment behind it are three proofs; signage is kept separate because it is the control that reveals or conceals a zone's purpose.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The authorised access list with approvals, the sample authorisation records for restricted areas, the identification verification procedure applied before access is granted, and the list of authorised personnel per secure area with its ownership register. PCI DSS requires authorisation to be based on individual job function; NIST 800-53 requires a maintained physical access authorisation list.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control System Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export from the access control system showing area restrictions, the inventory of facility entry controls deployed at each entry point, the badge or credential records, the door alarm and locking configuration, and the facility layout diagram they map to.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: The badge or biometric entry logs from controlled areas, the data centre access logs, and the securely stored facility entry and exit records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of documented procedures for limiting physical access.

artifacts.name: Access Provisioning and Revocation Records
artifacts.description: The provisioning workflow showing request, approval and issue, the modification log for role changes, the revocation records on termination or role change with the removal SLA report, and the reconciliation reports confirming the live authorised set matches the approved list.

artifacts.name: Periodic Physical Access Review
artifacts.description: The completed access list review documentation signed off by area owners, the quarterly review of access logs and surveillance, and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls. Cadence differs: ADHICS quarterly, ISO 27001 quarterly or bi-annual, SOX and NIST 800-53 periodic against a documented schedule.

artifacts.name: Visitor Management Records
artifacts.description: The visitor sign-in logs and management records, the contractor escort records, and the visitor management procedures governing identification, authorisation and supervision.

artifacts.name: Emergency Access Procedure and Records
artifacts.description: The emergency facility access procedures, the list of personnel authorised to invoke them, and the emergency access log records showing each invocation with justification.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Physical Access Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping roles to the physical areas each may enter, the access validation procedures applied against it, and the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping.

artifacts.name: Physical Key and Badge Inventory
artifacts.description: The physical key inventory with issue and return records, the identification badge issuance records, and the reconciliation of issued credentials against the authorised list.

artifacts.name: Token and Certificate Assignment Records
artifacts.description: The procedure assigning tokens, smart cards or certificates to named individuals with no sharing permitted, the assignment records, the revocation and replacement records following loss, theft or malfunction, and sample audit logs of authentication using them.

artifacts.name: Surveillance and Perimeter Evidence
artifacts.description: The camera deployment evidence with footage retention policy and storage records, the perimeter protection evidence covering fencing, bollards and gates, and the security barrier and entry control evidence for the most restricted areas. ADHICS requires surveillance to meet the local monitoring authority's requirements.

artifacts.name: Physical Security Policy and Perimeter Design
artifacts.description: The physical security policy defining perimeters and zoning, the site and floor plans marked with security zones, the barrier specification, the perimeter risk assessment with residual risk determination, the maintenance and inspection records, and the physical security survey report.

artifacts.name: Logical Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy defining least privilege, the logical access rules standard, the role-based access matrix for business applications, the quarterly access review results, and the privileged access request records — the logical counterpart the physical authorisations are aligned to.

artifacts.name: Entry Control Procedures and Audit
artifacts.description: The documented entry control procedures and the entry control audit reports testing whether they are followed in practice.

artifacts.name: Secure Asset Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The records of secure destruction or re-use of physical assets holding classified information, held with physical access because the same controlled areas govern their handling.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configuration, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, and the malware protection deployment records reviewed alongside the physical controls.

PES-02.notes: 94 asks across 16 frameworks. Authorisation, entry logging and periodic review are the three demands every framework makes; the rest are specialisations — HIPAA emergency access, PCI DSS token assignment, ADHICS local surveillance compliance — and are kept separate.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Physical Access Matrix
artifacts.description: The rules and zoning document for physical areas covering offices, data centres and restricted labs; the role-based access matrix mapping roles to permitted functions; the topic-specific access control policy defining least privilege and need-to-know; the standard defining authentication, authorisation and session rules; the role-based facility access procedure; and the procedure for authorising and managing personnel physical access based on individual job function. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limit-physical-access requirement.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Authorisation List
artifacts.description: The physical access authorisation list, the access badge and credential records, the access list review documentation, the sample authorisation records for protected-area access, the procedure requiring verification of identification before granting access, and the physical access provisioning and de-provisioning records.

artifacts.name: Access Control System Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration export from the access control system showing protected-area access restrictions, the inventory of facility entry controls deployed at those entry points, the facility layout diagram, and the physical access control system documentation.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: The sample physical access logs from protected-area entry points, the data centre access logs with their reviews, the physical access control records, the visitor management logs and procedures, and the visitor control logs with badge records.

artifacts.name: Access Review and Revocation Records
artifacts.description: The quarterly access review results signed off by data and system owners, the evidence of completed access recertification signed by managers, the records of physical access revocation upon termination or change of role, the audit log showing role changes processed for movers with approvals, the metrics showing access removed within the target service level for leavers, the provisioning workflow screenshots, and the register of approved access exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Emergency Access Records
artifacts.description: The emergency facility access procedures, the authorised emergency personnel list, and the emergency access log records.

artifacts.name: Physical Authentication Token Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure assigning tokens, smart cards or certificates to individuals with no sharing and covering revocation and replacement on loss; the records of those assignments; the revocation and replacement records following loss, theft or malfunction; and the sample audit logs of authentication using them.

artifacts.name: Privileged Physical Access Records
artifacts.description: The privileged access requests and approvals from the management platform covering the elevated physical rights a role may carry.

artifacts.name: Surveillance Records
artifacts.description: The security camera evidence covering the areas the role model admits access to.

artifacts.name: Test Environment Access Controls
artifacts.description: The software testing and revision access controls governing physical and logical reach into the non-production estate.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Records
artifacts.description: The access control lists with the user access review documentation, the security operations procedures and monitoring configurations, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, and the malware protection deployment and update records covering the access control systems.

PES-02.1.notes: 46 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps PES-03.1 and PES-06; what is distinct here is that physical access is granted by role rather than by individual approval, so the role matrix and its recertification are the primary artifacts.

artifacts.name: Physical Security Policy and Entry Control Procedures
artifacts.description: The approved physical and environmental security policy plus the entry control procedures implementing it: scope and applicability across facilities, security zoning principles, least-privilege and need-to-know rules for physical areas, authorisation and escort requirements, roles and responsibilities, and review frequency. Frameworks variously require board or management approval with version control, a documented facility security plan, procedures specific to data centres, server rooms and restricted areas, rules for what is publicly accessible, and a minimal-signage requirement so sensitive facilities are not advertised. Include the linked access control policy where physical and logical access rules are governed together.

artifacts.name: Facility Site Plans, Security Zones and Perimeter Design
artifacts.description: Site and floor plans marking security zones (public, reception, office, restricted, data centre, PIN room) with the entry and exit points that separate them, the secure area identification documentation, physical barrier specifications (walls, doors, fences, bollards, reception design, turnstiles), the data centre physical security design, and evidence of physical isolation of sensitive systems. PCI DSS requires the layout to show the cardholder data environment and the entry controls protecting it.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control System Configuration and Device Inventory
artifacts.description: Evidence of the deployed access control mechanisms: inventory of entry-control devices (badge readers, biometric readers, keypads, key locks, door alarms) per entry point with location and status, the access control system documentation and configuration export showing which credentials open which doors and areas, door alarm and locking configuration, equipment identification arrangements, and records of physical key issue and lock/combination changes (including changes on personnel departure or key loss). Configuration and device data can be exported from the access control platform; key and lock change records are manual.

artifacts.name: Authorized Personnel List and Physical Access Authorization Records
artifacts.description: The current list of personnel authorised to each secure area, showing role, business justification, approver and date of last review, together with the role-to-area access matrix and the underlying authorisation records: access requests with approvals, badge issuance records, modifications when people change role, timely removal for leavers against the defined SLA, temporary and privileged access grants with expiry, and the register of approved exceptions with compensating controls. Request and provisioning workflow data can be exported from the ITSM/PAM platform; the authorised list and approvals require owner attestation.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: Badge, biometric and manual entry/exit logs for controlled entry points, including data centres, server rooms and cardholder data environment areas, showing identity, timestamp, door/zone and grant or deny outcome, plus access control system audit logs for administrative changes. Frameworks require the logs to be retained for the defined period, protected from tampering, and available for investigation; provide a representative sample with the retention configuration.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Review and Recertification Records
artifacts.description: Completed periodic reviews of who holds physical access to each secure area, signed off by the area or system owner, with the resulting removals and corrections evidenced. Review cadence differs by framework — quarterly recertification is expected by some, at least annual by others — so state the cadence applied and show the reviews for the period. Include entry-control audit reports covering the operation of the controls themselves.

artifacts.name: Visitor and Contractor Escort Records
artifacts.description: The visitor management procedure (identification, registration, badge issue and return, escort requirements and the circumstances requiring escort) with completed visitor sign-in/sign-out logs and contractor escort records showing host, purpose, areas entered, times and escorting personnel, retained for the required period.

artifacts.name: CCTV and Surveillance Coverage Evidence
artifacts.description: Documentation of the surveillance capability protecting entry points and secure areas: system design covering camera placement, resolution, coverage and monitoring arrangements, the coverage map or floor plan showing fields of view, deployment evidence for data centre and sensitive areas, footage retention period and secure storage evidence, and — where local law requires — the notice informing employees and visitors that the area is monitored. Some jurisdictions impose specific surveillance compliance requirements (e.g. Abu Dhabi MCC) that must be evidenced.

artifacts.name: Intrusion Detection, Alarm and Guard Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that physical access attempts are detected and responded to: intrusion detection and alarm system configuration (sensors, zones, response actions), the alarm log showing events raised, response taken and false-positive analysis, guard patrol and shift incident logs, perimeter monitoring records, and periodic physical access monitoring reports with investigation of anomalous or out-of-hours access. Includes the security operations monitoring procedures governing this activity.

artifacts.name: Physical Security Risk Assessments and Site Surveys
artifacts.description: Risk assessments supporting the design of the physical access controls: per-perimeter and per-secure-area risk assessment with residual risk determination, facility security assessments or third-party physical security survey reports for key sites, and the site risk assessment addressing environmental and location threats for data centres.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Roles, Responsibilities and Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: Documented allocation of responsibility for operating physical access controls — the roles and responsibilities document and RACI mapping named personnel or roles to each physical access management activity — together with acknowledgement records evidencing those personnel are aware of and accept their responsibilities.

artifacts.name: Facility Maintenance and Environmental Control Records
artifacts.description: Records evidencing the physical controls remain effective: inspection and maintenance records for barriers, doors and locks; environmental monitoring logs (temperature, humidity, water, smoke) for data centres; UPS, generator and electrical equipment maintenance and testing records; and dated walkthrough photographs evidencing barriers, CCTV, biometric entry and environmental controls in place.

artifacts.name: Workstation and Media Physical Protection Records
artifacts.description: Standards and evidence for physical protection outside controlled entry points: workstation security standards specifying permitted locations and physical safeguards for devices accessing sensitive data, the workstation inventory recording the physical controls applied to each, and records of secure destruction or authorised re-use of physical assets and media holding classified information.

PES-03.notes: 129 entries collapse to 13 artifacts. Policy restatements (17 entries) and physical access system/device evidence (18) dominate; badge logs and authorisation lists are asked for by twelve and eight frameworks respectively in different wording. No collectors exist for this control today, but badge-system exports, access-control configuration and provisioning records are connector-addressable, hence hybrid.

artifacts.name: Physical Security Policy and Zoning
artifacts.description: The policy defining security perimeters and zoning principles across facilities, the site and floor plans marked with security zones, the facility layout diagram, the security zone documentation, the perimeter security design, and the perimeter risk assessment for each perimeter type with its residual risk determination. HITRUST requires the approved physical security perimeter policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Physical Barrier Specifications
artifacts.description: The technical specifications for walls, doors, fences, bollards and reception design; the physical barrier specifications; the security barrier and entry control evidence for the data centre and secure processing rooms; the maintenance and inspection records for the physical barriers; the minimal signage policy; and the third-party or internal physical security survey of key sites.

artifacts.name: Entry Control Inventory and Configuration
artifacts.description: The inventory of facility entry controls deployed at protected-area entry points, the physical access control system configuration with its zones and schedules, the entry control procedures, the access card system records, and the equipment identification records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented equipment identification requirement.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for authorising and managing personnel physical access based on individual job function, the procedure for granting, modifying and revoking physical access rights, the sample authorisation records for protected-area access, the procedure requiring verification of identification before granting access, the access list review records, the periodic review of badge holders confirming continued need, and the records of physical access revocation upon termination or change of role.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: The access log export showing entries and exits with names, timestamps and readers; the sample physical access logs from protected-area entry points; the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register; the entry control audit reports; the perimeter monitoring records; and the log of lost or stolen badges with their deactivation timestamps.

artifacts.name: Visitor Management Records
artifacts.description: The visitor log showing registration, escort assignment, badge issue and return; the visitor management logs; and the tailgating awareness posters, signage and reminders.

artifacts.name: Delivery and Loading Area Controls
artifacts.description: The delivery area procedures, the loading dock security measures, the isolation control documentation separating the delivery area from the interior, and the access point monitoring covering it.

artifacts.name: Surveillance Records
artifacts.description: The surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records and the monitoring and camera evidence covering the ingress and egress points.

artifacts.name: Public Access Controls
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the access control lists with the user access review documentation covering the publicly reachable areas. HITRUST requires the approved public access policy and standard with its implementing procedure, its awareness communications and its periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configurations, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, and the malware protection deployment and update records covering the systems that run the entry controls.

PES-03.1.notes: 55 asks across 7 frameworks. The perimeter design, the entry control at each point and the delivery or loading area are three proofs; the delivery area is kept separate because it is the ingress point most often left outside the badge system.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: The access log export showing entries and exits with names, timestamps and readers; the sample physical access logs from protected-area entry points; the physical access control logs; the secure area access logs; the access logs; the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register; and the access authentication records. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented maintain-physical-access-logs requirement.

artifacts.name: Visitor Log Records
artifacts.description: The visitor log showing registration, escort assignment, badge issue and return; the visitor log records; the visitor log samples; the visitor badge procedures; the identification badge issuance records; the contractor escort records; and the visitor record review documentation.

artifacts.name: Access Control System Configuration
artifacts.description: The physical access control system configuration with its zones and schedules, the inventory of facility entry controls deployed at protected-area entry points, the facility layout diagram, the access control systems documentation, the door alarm and locking configuration, and the physical access control policy covering data centres, server rooms and the segments hosting the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Authorised Access List
artifacts.description: The list of personnel authorised for physical access to the sites with role, justification and review date; the list of authorised personnel for secure areas; the authorised access list with its approvals; the procedure for granting, modifying and revoking physical access rights; the physical access controls documentation; and the physical access policy.

artifacts.name: Access Log Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic monitoring reports of physical access events with their anomaly investigation, the periodic review of badge holders confirming continued need, the periodic physical access review documentation, the facility security assessment, and the log of lost or stolen badges with their deactivation timestamps. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented failures and anomalies reporting requirement.

artifacts.name: Surveillance Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of camera coverage and retention for the data centre and server-room areas, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the deployment evidence meeting the local authority's requirements, and the retention policy with its footage storage records.

artifacts.name: Environmental Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The building management and environmental monitoring dashboards and the service availability alerting covering the monitored facility.

artifacts.name: Access Control and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the tailgating awareness posters, signage and reminders. HITRUST requires the approved physical entry controls policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

PES-03.3.notes: 50 asks across 12 frameworks. Distinct from PES-06 in that the object is the log rather than the visitor; the review of access events for anomalies is kept separate from the log itself because that is the control most often absent.

artifacts.name: Physical Security Policy and Zoning
artifacts.description: The policy defining security perimeters and zoning principles across facilities, the physical access rules and zoning document for offices, data centres and restricted areas, the site and floor plans marked with security zones, and the per-zone risk assessment. ADHICS requires site plans showing the perimeters with secure-area identification; QCB requires a physical zoning plan with a per-zone risk assessment.

artifacts.name: Perimeter Design and Maintenance Records
artifacts.description: The technical specification for walls, doors, fences, bollards and reception design, the physical barriers between public and restricted areas, the risk assessment for each perimeter type with its residual risk determination, the maintenance and inspection records for the barriers, and the physical security survey report over key sites.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The badge or biometric access logs with the visitor register, the access list and its periodic review records, the entry control evidence for restricted areas, and the physical access control records evidencing the barriers are enforced rather than only installed.

artifacts.name: Surveillance System Evidence
artifacts.description: The CCTV deployment evidence with footage retention records, the camera coverage over controlled areas, and the surveillance system documentation. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented surveillance policy.

artifacts.name: Visitor Management Records
artifacts.description: The visitor logs and management records for controlled facilities, held separately from staff access because the identification, escort and authorisation requirements differ.

artifacts.name: Secure Room Design and Discretion Evidence
artifacts.description: The design specification for secure rooms covering walls to deck, absence of external windows and sound attenuation, the facility signage audit confirming no public-facing signage reveals sensitive locations, the internal directory access restriction, the office layout privacy assessment covering screen visibility and confidential conversation risk, the designated private discussion areas with soundproofing evidence, and the secure area inspection reports.

artifacts.name: Physical Key and Access Device Management
artifacts.description: The log of physical keys and combinations issued, returned and changed, the lock and key management records, and the documented procedure or configuration evidence for managing physical access devices.

artifacts.name: Clear Desk and Clear Screen Evidence
artifacts.description: The policy with its requirements, timing rules and enforcement mechanisms, the screen lock configuration enforcing auto-lock and timeout, evidence that staff have lockable storage, the map of confidential waste bin placement, the awareness material and signage, the privacy screen deployment, and the results of periodic walkthrough audits with compliance rate and findings.

artifacts.name: Environmental Threat Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The environmental threat risk assessment covering fire, flood, earthquake, power and civil unrest, the building management system configuration for temperature, humidity, leak and smoke monitoring with its logs, fire detection and suppression commissioning and annual inspection certificates, fire drill records, flood protection documentation, the environmental incident log, and the insurance certificates covering environmental risk.

artifacts.name: Power Resilience Maintenance Records
artifacts.description: The records of uninterruptible power supply, generator and electrical stabiliser maintenance and testing, and the data centre resiliency design they support.

artifacts.name: Data Centre Security Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented physical controls for the data centre covering access, perimeter, video surveillance and visitor management, the access register with the authorised-personnel list and its review records, the site risk assessment addressing environmental threats considered in location selection, and the walkthrough photographs evidencing barriers, cameras, biometric entry and environmental controls.

artifacts.name: Workstation Security Records
artifacts.description: The workstation use policy with acceptable use guidelines, the placement and screen privacy requirements, the workstation inventory with its security controls, the workstation security standards, and the work area security procedures.

artifacts.name: Logical Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The access control policy defining least privilege and need-to-know, the logical access rules standard for each system type, the role-based access matrix, and the quarterly access review results signed off by owners — the logical counterpart the physical zoning is aligned to.

artifacts.name: Secure Media Transportation Records
artifacts.description: The secure media transportation policy and procedures with the records demonstrating they operate in the environment covered, addressing media leaving the secured facility.

artifacts.name: Security Operations Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The security operations procedures and monitoring configuration, the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, and the malware protection deployment records that sit alongside the physical controls in the same operational review.

artifacts.name: Signage and Awareness Review Records
artifacts.description: The signage policy with its review evidence, the minimal signage practice, the floor plans demarcating public from work areas, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the physical security requirements.

PES-04.notes: 97 asks across 13 frameworks. Perimeter design, secure-room design and clear-desk practice are kept apart because ISO 27001 tests them as three separate controls (A.7.1, A.7.3, A.7.7) and an assessor asks for each on its own.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Working Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for personnel working in secure areas covering device restrictions and dual-working requirements, the secure area working guidelines, the secure area work guidelines, the prohibited activities list, the supervision requirements, the supervision records for secure area activities, and the work authorisation records. HITRUST requires the approved working in secure areas policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Authorisation Register
artifacts.description: The register of personnel authorised to access secure areas with expiry dates, the secure area entry and exit log showing supervised and time-bound access, the periodic inspection records confirming vacant secure areas are locked and verified, and the physical access review report confirming continued need for each badge holder.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for granting, modifying and revoking physical access rights; the physical access control system configuration with its zones and schedules; the access log export showing entries and exits with names, timestamps and readers; the physical access control records; the data centre access logs; the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register; and the log of lost or stolen badges with their deactivation timestamps.

artifacts.name: Visitor Management Records
artifacts.description: The visitor log showing registration, escort assignment, badge issue and return; the records of escorts assigned for visits into secure areas; the visitor management logs; and the tailgating awareness posters, signage and reminders.

artifacts.name: Device Entry Controls
artifacts.description: The device check-in and check-out procedures, the mobile and portable device entry control logs, and the photographs of signage prohibiting photography and recording in secure areas.

artifacts.name: Secure Room Design Records
artifacts.description: The design specification for secure rooms covering walls to deck, absence of external windows and sound attenuation; the floor plans showing designated private areas; the designated private discussion areas; the soundproofing and privacy controls evidence; the assessment of screen visibility and confidential conversation risk in open offices; the privacy screen deployment; the facility signage audit confirming no public-facing signage reveals sensitive locations; the evidence that internal directories do not expose those locations; and the inspection reports of secure office areas for security weaknesses.

artifacts.name: Key and Combination Management
artifacts.description: The log of physical keys and combinations issued, returned and changed, covering the areas the badge system does not.

artifacts.name: Surveillance Records
artifacts.description: The security camera evidence, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, and the surveillance system documentation. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented surveillance system requirement.

artifacts.name: Workstation Security Standards
artifacts.description: The workstation security standards, the workstation inventory with its security controls, the physical security measures for workstations, the clean desk policy, and the work area security procedures governing what may sit on a desk inside the area.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Production Area Controls
artifacts.description: The card data storage access controls, the physical separation of card production and personal identification number generation, and the storage security for sensitive instrument information within the secure area.

artifacts.name: Access Control Policy and Review
artifacts.description: The topic-specific policy defining principles of least privilege and need-to-know, the standard defining authentication, authorisation and session rules for each system type, the rules and zoning document for physical areas, the role-based access matrix, and the quarterly access review results signed off by data and system owners.

artifacts.name: Media Transport Controls
artifacts.description: The secure media transportation policy and procedures governing media carried into and out of the secure area. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the secure area working requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PES-04.1.notes: 58 asks across 9 frameworks. The working rules inside a secure area, the entry controls that gate it and the room's physical design are three distinct proofs; ISO 27001 A.7.3 securing offices and rooms is design, A.7.6 is behaviour, and they stay apart.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Monitoring Reports
artifacts.description: The periodic monitoring reports of physical access events with their anomaly investigation, the monitoring review records, the physical access incident reports, the physical access monitoring procedures, the log of alarms raised with response actions and false-positive analysis, and the security guard patrol and incident log entries. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-and-monitor-the-facility requirement.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: The physical access logs, the physical access control records, the data centre access logs, and the visitor management logs and records forming the monitored event stream.

artifacts.name: Surveillance System Records
artifacts.description: The surveillance system documentation, the design documentation covering camera coverage, resolution, retention and monitoring, the map showing camera locations and fields of view, the evidence of camera coverage and retention for the data centre and server-room areas, the security camera evidence, the monitoring evidence, and the evidence of retention period compliance and secure storage of footage. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented surveillance system requirement.

artifacts.name: Intrusion Detection Configuration
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and alarm configuration including sensors, zones and response actions, and the perimeter security design it protects.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Policy and Authorisation
artifacts.description: The approved physical access control policy covering data centres, server rooms and the segments hosting the systems in scope; the list of personnel authorised for physical access with role, justification and review date; the secure area standard operating procedures covering each required element; and the site security plan.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Privacy Notice
artifacts.description: The notice informing employees and visitors that areas are monitored, as required by law.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Access Response Training
artifacts.description: The unauthorised access response training records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

PES-05.notes: 31 asks across 7 frameworks. Overlaps PES-05.1; what is distinct here is the monitoring of access events rather than the equipment doing the monitoring, so the review reports and anomaly investigation carry the weight.

artifacts.name: Surveillance System Design
artifacts.description: The design documentation covering camera coverage, resolution, retention and monitoring; the map showing camera locations and fields of view across facilities; the surveillance system documentation; the deployment evidence meeting the local authority's requirements; the camera and access control deployment with recording retention at the data centre; the documented physical controls covering access, perimeter, video surveillance and visitor management; and the specifications for cameras at self-service terminals covering angle, illumination, resolution and retention.

artifacts.name: Intrusion Alarm Configuration
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and alarm configuration including sensors, zones and response actions; the door alarm and locking configuration; the alarms at self-service terminals; the anti-skimming deployment; and the encrypting entry pads protecting the interfaces those terminals expose.

artifacts.name: Alarm and Footage Review Records
artifacts.description: The log of alarms raised with response actions and false-positive analysis, the monitoring review records, the physical access incident reports, the physical access monitoring procedures, the quarterly access log and surveillance review records, and the reconciliation reports of authorised users. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented protect-and-monitor-the-facility requirement.

artifacts.name: Footage Retention Records
artifacts.description: The retention policy with its footage storage records and the evidence of retention period compliance and secure storage of footage.

artifacts.name: Guard and Patrol Records
artifacts.description: The security guard patrol and incident log entries and the evidence of access-control mechanisms and surveillance for sensitive areas covering biometric, card, keypad and guarded entry.

artifacts.name: Perimeter Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of perimeter protection covering fencing, bollards and special-purpose gates, and the evidence of video surveillance and controlled physical access in operation.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Access Records
artifacts.description: The secure area access logs, the access authentication records, the list of authorised personnel for secure areas, the secure area ownership register, the physical key inventory, the identification badge issuance records, the contractor and vendor escort records, the third-party access agreement, the securely stored facility entry and exit records, and the visitor management records for the data centre.

artifacts.name: Environmental Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The building management and environmental monitoring dashboards and the service availability alerting covering the monitored facility.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Privacy Notice
artifacts.description: The notice informing employees and visitors that areas are monitored, as required by law.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Access Response Training
artifacts.description: The unauthorised access response training records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Media Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The records of secure destruction or re-use of physical assets holding classified information within the monitored facility.

PES-05.1.notes: 43 asks across 7 frameworks. The camera estate, the alarm system and the review of what both produce are three proofs; the privacy notice for monitoring is kept separate because it is a legal precondition rather than a security control.

artifacts.name: Visitor Access Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for authorising visitor access including pre-approval, identification verification and escort or supervision; the visitor management policy alignment; the role-based facility access procedure; the access validation procedures; the access approval records; and the vendor visit approvals for the data centre. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented escort-and-monitor-visitors requirement. HITRUST requires the approved physical entry controls policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Visitor Log Records
artifacts.description: The visitor log showing registration, escort assignment, badge issue and return; the sample visitor logs containing visitor name, company, escorting personnel and date and time of entry; the visitor control logs with badge records; the visitor sign-in logs; the visitor management logs; the visitor log samples; and the documentation of the visitor log retention period.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Area Visitor Log
artifacts.description: The sample sensitive-area visitor logs kept separate from the general facility logs, evidencing that entry to the protected zone is recorded on its own.

artifacts.name: Visitor Escort Records
artifacts.description: The escort standard operating procedure, the escort logs, the records of escorted visitor access in the protected area, and the secure-area access records showing who accompanied each visitor.

artifacts.name: Visitor Identification and Badging
