artifacts.name: Visitor Badge Surrender Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for surrendering or deactivating visitor badges before exit or at expiration, the sample sign-out and badge surrender records, and the sample badge deactivation logs from the access control system.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The physical access control system configuration with its zones and schedules, the access log export showing entries and exits with names, timestamps and readers, the badge or key card access records, the physical access control records and logs, the data centre access logs, the physical access logs with the visitor register, the procedure for granting, modifying and revoking physical access rights, the log of lost or stolen badges with their deactivation timestamps, and the role-based physical access matrix.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic review of badge holders confirming continued need, the periodic physical access review documentation, the authorised access list with its approvals, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Surveillance Records
artifacts.description: The documented physical controls covering access, perimeter, video surveillance and visitor management; the evidence of video surveillance and controlled physical access in operation; the security camera evidence; and the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records.

artifacts.name: Test Environment Access Controls
artifacts.description: The software testing and revision access controls governing visitor and contractor access to the non-production estate.

PES-06.notes: 51 asks across 10 frameworks. The visitor log, the escort and the badge surrender at exit are three proofs; PCI DSS separates its sensitive-area visitor log from the general facility log and that distinction is preserved.

artifacts.name: Unescorted Access Authorisation List
artifacts.description: The physical access authorisation list, the access badge and credential records, the authorised access list with its approvals, the access approval records, the access list review documentation, and the periodic physical access review documentation confirming continued need.

artifacts.name: Escort Records
artifacts.description: The escort standard operating procedure, the escort logs, the records of escorted visitor access in the protected area, the secure-area access records, and the vendor visit approvals for the data centre. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented escort-and-monitor-visitors requirement. HITRUST requires the approved working in secure areas policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Visitor Access Controls
artifacts.description: The procedure for authorising visitor access including pre-approval, identification verification and escort or supervision; the standard for visitor badges clearly distinguishing visitors from personnel; the sample records of visitor identification verification; the visitor badge inventory; the visitor log; the visitor log samples; and the visitor management policy alignment.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Logs
artifacts.description: The physical access control logs, the physical access control records, the data centre access logs, the physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, and the visitor management logs.

artifacts.name: Power Backup Infrastructure
artifacts.description: The documentation of uninterruptible power supply, generator, battery backup and fuel arrangements for technology service areas; the design records for backup generators and redundant power distribution; the deployment and capacity evidence for each; the deployment at each data centre; the matrix confirming backup power coverage across all service delivery, support and operations areas; the specifications for the deployed equipment; the evidence of diverse utility feeds or power distribution redundancy in critical facilities; and the utility redundancy documentation.

artifacts.name: Power System Testing and Maintenance
artifacts.description: The records of generator test runs, fuel levels and refuelling contracts; the maintenance, battery replacement and load test records for the uninterruptible supplies; the maintenance and fuel-level logs; the records of periodic testing of the supplies and generators; the generator maintenance records; the generator backup records; the power continuity test results; the power protection testing records; the test and maintenance records for the resilience equipment; the test schedules; and the maintenance and testing records for the electrical stabilisers.

artifacts.name: Environmental Controls Records
artifacts.description: The heating, ventilation and air conditioning maintenance records with the environmental monitoring logs, the environmental monitoring system configurations covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression, the environmental monitoring logs from the data centre covering temperature, humidity, water and smoke, the environmental controls documentation, and the protection assessments over them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented secure utilities and equipment location requirements.

artifacts.name: Cabling Security Records
artifacts.description: The diagrams of power, data and telecommunications cabling paths and patch panels; the specifications for conduits, armoured cables and separation of power and data; the evidence that cable access points such as risers and closets are locked and monitored; the photographs showing proper cable labelling at patch panels; the installer certification of the structured cabling installation and testing; and the inspection report of cable pathways for damage, interception risk and housekeeping.

artifacts.name: Utility Dependency Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment of dependencies on power, telecommunications, air conditioning and water; the service level agreements and contracts with utility providers; the site risk assessment addressing environmental threats considered in data centre location selection; and the utility failure response procedures.

artifacts.name: Facility Physical Security Records
artifacts.description: The physical and environmental security policy covering physical access controls, environmental monitoring and power protection for technology facilities; the access register for data centres and network equipment rooms with the authorised-personnel list and review records; the photographs evidencing physical security barriers, surveillance, biometric entry and environmental controls; the physical security measures; the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records; and the physical access logs with the visitor register.

artifacts.name: Operations Management Records
artifacts.description: The facilities and environmental management records, the standard operating procedures for technology operations, the operations monitoring logs and infrastructure event records, and the outsourced service management reports and compliance evidence covering utilities delivered by third parties.

artifacts.name: Continuity and Backup Records
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery plan and procedures, the backup policy and schedule with its successful completion logs, and the restoration test results and reports covering the failure the utilities are meant to prevent.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the supporting utilities requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved supporting utilities policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

PES-07.notes: 57 asks across 11 frameworks. Power, environmental conditioning and cabling are three separate utility dependencies with different failure modes and different maintenance records; ISO 27001 A.7.12 cabling security is kept distinct from A.7.11 supporting utilities.

artifacts.name: Emergency Power Infrastructure
artifacts.description: The documentation of uninterruptible power supply, generator, battery backup and fuel arrangements for technology service areas; the design records for backup generators and redundant power distribution; the deployment and capacity evidence for each; the deployment at each data centre; the deployment evidence; the configuration; the specifications; the matrix confirming backup power coverage across all service delivery, support and operations areas; the evidence of diverse utility feeds or power distribution redundancy in critical facilities; and the utility redundancy documentation.

artifacts.name: Power System Testing Records
artifacts.description: The records of generator test runs, fuel levels and refuelling contracts; the maintenance, battery replacement and load test records for the uninterruptible supplies; the maintenance and fuel-level logs; the records of periodic testing; the generator maintenance and backup records; the power continuity test results; the power protection testing records; the test and maintenance records for the resilience equipment; and the test schedules.

artifacts.name: Redundancy Assessment
artifacts.description: The redundancy assessment covering power, air conditioning, fire suppression and communications, and the utility support risk assessment of dependencies on power, telecommunications, air conditioning and water.

artifacts.name: Environmental Controls Records
artifacts.description: The heating, ventilation and air conditioning maintenance records with the environmental monitoring logs, the environmental monitoring system configurations covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression, and the disaster protection measures documentation. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented secure utilities requirement.

artifacts.name: Utility Provider Agreements
artifacts.description: The service level agreements and contracts with utility providers and the utility failure response procedures invoked when they are not met.

artifacts.name: Continuity and Backup Records
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery plan and procedures, the backup policy and schedule with its successful completion logs, the restoration test results and reports, and the off-site backup location records covering the failure emergency power is meant to prevent.

artifacts.name: Operations Management Records
artifacts.description: The facilities and environmental management records, the standard operating procedures for technology operations, the operations monitoring logs and infrastructure event records, and the outsourced service management reports and compliance evidence covering power delivered by third parties.

artifacts.name: Facility Access and Review Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the supporting utilities requirements, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved supporting utilities policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

PES-07.3.notes: 45 asks across 10 frameworks. Overlaps PES-07; what is distinct here is emergency power specifically, so the uninterruptible supply and generator artifacts carry the weight and the wider utility asks are kept subordinate.

artifacts.name: Fire Detection and Suppression Systems
artifacts.description: The design of early-warning smoke detection, automatic suppression and evacuation mechanisms; the fire detection and suppression system documentation; the fire detection system records; the fire suppression system documentation; the fire detection and suppression system specifications; the fire protection systems; and the evidence of those controls with their inspection records.

artifacts.name: Fire System Inspection and Maintenance
artifacts.description: The regular inspection, testing and maintenance records for the fire systems; the fire system inspection and maintenance records; and the fire marshal inspection reports.

artifacts.name: Fire Drill and Training Records
artifacts.description: The records of employee fire-response training and evacuation drills and the fire drill records.

artifacts.name: Environmental Protection Measures
artifacts.description: The environmental controls documentation, the environmental protection measures, the environmental monitoring system configurations covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression, the disaster protection documentation, the flood protection measures, the physical security measures, and the protection assessments over them. HITRUST requires the approved policy and standard on protecting against external and environmental threats with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Redundancy Assessment
artifacts.description: The redundancy assessment covering power, air conditioning, fire suppression and communications.

artifacts.name: Continuity and Backup Records
artifacts.description: The disaster recovery plan and procedures, the backup policy and schedule with its successful completion logs, and the restoration test results and reports covering the loss a fire would cause.

artifacts.name: Operations Management Records
artifacts.description: The facilities and environmental management records, the standard operating procedures for technology operations, the operations monitoring logs and infrastructure event records, and the outsourced service management reports and compliance evidence.

artifacts.name: Facility Access and Review Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, the awareness communications informing personnel of the environmental protections, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PES-08.notes: 33 asks across 9 frameworks. The detection and suppression system, its inspection and maintenance, and the drill that exercises the human response are three proofs.

artifacts.name: Equipment Siting Standards
artifacts.description: The standards for positioning critical equipment away from entrances, windows and water sources, the equipment placement plans and diagrams, the siting guidelines, and the risk assessment driving protection choices for specific locations. ADHICS requires an environmental risk assessment for placement and compliance with manufacturer environmental recommendations.

artifacts.name: Data Centre Layout and Rack Security
artifacts.description: The data centre rack layout with cooling, power and access paths documented, the evidence of locked racks with rack-level access controls and seals, the cage access controls, and the tape vault security.

artifacts.name: Environmental Controls and Monitoring
artifacts.description: The documented environmental controls protecting facilities and equipment, the building management system configuration for temperature, humidity, leak and smoke monitoring, the equipment cooling, humidity and dust controls, the maintenance evidence, and the environmental incident log with responses.

artifacts.name: Fire and Flood Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The environmental threat risk assessment covering fire, flood, earthquake and power, the fire detection and suppression commissioning and annual inspection certificates, the fire drill records, the flood protection documentation, the hazard mitigation design evidence such as raised flooring and leak detection, the leak detection test records, and the insurance certificates covering environmental risk.

artifacts.name: Power Resilience Evidence
artifacts.description: The uninterruptible power supply and battery backup configuration, the generator and backup power testing records, and the off-site backup location records that depend on them.

artifacts.name: Cabling Security Evidence
artifacts.description: The diagrams of power, data and telecommunications cabling paths and patch panels, the protection specifications for conduits, armoured cable and separation of power from data, the evidence that cable access points such as risers and closets are locked and monitored, the labelling photographs at patch panels, the installer certification of the structured cabling installation, and the pathway inspection report covering damage, interception risk and housekeeping.

artifacts.name: Network Jack Restriction Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented standard requiring physical or logical restriction of publicly accessible network jacks, photographs or inspection records of physically disabled or locked jacks, and the switch port, port-based authentication or network access control configuration preventing unauthorised use.

artifacts.name: Networking Hardware Location Controls
artifacts.description: The inventory of wireless access points, gateways, networking and communications hardware and telecommunication lines, the evidence showing them in locked rooms or cabinets with restricted access, and the sample physical access logs to those areas.

artifacts.name: Console Locking Evidence
artifacts.description: The standard requiring console locking in sensitive areas when not in use, the configuration evidence for screen-saver or inactivity locking on those consoles, and the periodic inspection records confirming compliance.

artifacts.name: Physical Access Controls for Equipment
artifacts.description: The physical access controls protecting equipment areas, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the badge or biometric access logs with visitor register, the physical access control records, and the security camera evidence over them.

artifacts.name: Workstation Physical Safeguards
artifacts.description: The workstation use policy, the physical safeguard evidence for workstations, the acceptable use and functions documentation, the access rights enforcement configuration, the screen privacy measures such as filters and partitions, and the office layout privacy assessment covering shoulder-surfing risk.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Design and Discretion Evidence
artifacts.description: The secure room design specification, the facility signage audit confirming no public signage reveals sensitive locations, the internal directory access restriction, the secure area inspection reports, the key and combination management log, and the security zone definitions.

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Configuration
artifacts.description: The network boundary protection documentation, the DMZ architecture documentation, the firewall and proxy configurations, and the boundary protection monitoring logs — the logical perimeter alongside the physical one.

artifacts.name: Backup and Recovery Assurance
artifacts.description: The backup policy, schedule and successful completion logs, the restoration test results and reports, and the disaster recovery plan and procedures that the sited equipment supports.

artifacts.name: Equipment Transport and Off-Site Movement Controls
artifacts.description: The transportation security procedures, the equipment security procedures, and the data protection procedures applied during maintenance or off-site movement of equipment.

artifacts.name: Multifunction Device Physical Controls
artifacts.description: The physical security controls for multifunction devices including cable locks and placement in restricted areas, held separately because these devices sit outside the controlled equipment rooms.

PES-12.notes: 90 asks across 14 frameworks. Equipment siting, cabling security and environmental protection are three distinct ISO 27001 controls (A.7.8, A.7.12, A.7.5) that land together here; PCI DSS adds a separate concern about publicly accessible network jacks and console locking.

artifacts.name: Cabling Infrastructure Documentation
artifacts.description: The diagrams of power, data and telecommunications cabling paths and patch panels, the cabling architecture diagrams, the cable routing diagrams, the cable run diagrams, the cabling infrastructure documentation, the cable management standards, the physical cabling segregation documentation, and the cable segregation documentation. HITRUST requires the approved cabling security policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Cable Protection Measures
artifacts.description: The specifications for conduits, armoured cables and separation of power and data; the cable protection measures; the conduit installation evidence and photographs; the evidence that cable access points such as risers and closets are locked and monitored; the photographs showing proper cable labelling at patch panels; and the installer certification of the structured cabling installation and testing.

artifacts.name: Cable Inspection Records
artifacts.description: The inspection report of cable pathways for damage, interception risk and housekeeping; the cable inspection records; the physical inspection records; and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Network Jack Restriction
artifacts.description: The documented standard requiring physical or logical restriction of publicly accessible network jacks, the photographs or inspection records of physically disabled or locked public jacks, and the configuration evidence through port shutdown, address filtering, port-based authentication or network access control preventing unauthorised use.

artifacts.name: Networking Hardware Physical Security
artifacts.description: The inventory of wireless access points, gateways, networking and communications hardware and telecommunication lines; the photographs or configuration showing devices in locked rooms or cabinets with restricted access; and the sample physical access logs to the areas containing that hardware. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limit-physical-access requirement.

artifacts.name: Boundary Protection Documentation
artifacts.description: The network boundary protection documentation, the demilitarised-zone architecture documentation, the firewall and proxy configurations, and the boundary protection monitoring logs.

artifacts.name: Environmental Systems Records
artifacts.description: The environmental systems records covering the conditions the cabling runs through. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Facility Access and Surveillance Records
artifacts.description: The physical access logs from badge or biometric systems with the visitor register, the surveillance deployment evidence with its footage retention records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the cabling security requirements.

PES-12.1.notes: 38 asks across 9 frameworks. Cable protection, network jack restriction and the physical security of networking hardware are three proofs; the jack restriction is kept separate because it addresses an attacker already inside the building.

artifacts.name: Privacy Policy
artifacts.description: The approved privacy policy embedding the privacy principles, with the mapping of policy clauses to each principle, the documented lawful basis, the transparency notices, and the personal information handling procedures. HITRUST requires the approved data protection and privacy standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Privacy Governance Charter
artifacts.description: The documented privacy governance structure with defined roles, responsibilities and accountability; the assignment records for the data protection role; the appointment letter for the data protection officer or equivalent; and the approved governance standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Records of Processing Activities
artifacts.description: The processing register documenting purposes, legal basis, data categories, retention and transfers, with the special category data inventory and the additional safeguards applied to it.

artifacts.name: Privacy Notices
artifacts.description: The privacy notice or statement published to data subjects with its version history, the communication templates, and the accessibility measures ensuring the notice is intelligible to its audience.

artifacts.name: Consent and Data Subject Rights Records
artifacts.description: The consent management records showing valid capture, the opt-out tracking, the data subject request logs, and the documented procedure for handling access, rectification, erasure and portability requests.

artifacts.name: Complaint Handling Records
artifacts.description: The evidence of an operational complaint-handling mechanism with the log of complaints received, and the assessment demonstrating the implemented safeguards ensure compliance and protect the rights they exist for.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Mechanisms
artifacts.description: The contractual clauses, binding corporate rules or adequacy decisions evidencing lawful international transfers, held as part of the privacy programme rather than only in the transfer control.

artifacts.name: Data Protection Impact Assessments
artifacts.description: The completed impact assessments for high-risk processing, and the privacy impact assessment for the personnel data the organisation holds about its own workforce.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The approved retention and disposal policy aligned to legal, regulatory and sectoral requirements, the retention schedule, and the evidence of the personal data protection controls applied across the lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Information Security Policy Framework
artifacts.description: The master policy document signed and dated by top management stating objectives, scope and commitments; the register of subordinate topic-specific policies with owners, versions and review dates; the approval records; the communication evidence; the acknowledgement log with timestamps; and the annual review minutes.

artifacts.name: Data Loss Prevention Deployment
artifacts.description: The data loss prevention deployment covering personal data, and the executed agreements with the required security clauses and signature records that extend the protection to third parties.

artifacts.name: AI Privacy Risk Records
artifacts.description: The privacy risk assessment for the AI system, the elicited system requirements with socio-technical design decision records, the documented evidence of the outcome, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Innovation and Technology Watch Records
artifacts.description: The innovation strategy and programme documentation, the portfolio tracking with benefits reports, the proof-of-concept evaluation results, and the technology watch reports that surface emerging privacy exposures.

artifacts.name: Data Management Programme Records
artifacts.description: The documented data management and personal data protection strategy and plan with their compliance evidence, the approved policy or standard, the data security control evidence, the privacy artifacts, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, the performance metrics dashboard, and the compliance audit reports.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the privacy obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-01.notes: 70 asks across 10 frameworks. The privacy programme's governance instruments (charter, roles, policy) are separated from its operating records (processing register, consent, rights requests) because an assessor tests the second to confirm the first is real.

artifacts.name: Technical Security Measures
artifacts.description: The security measures documentation, the encryption implementation, the access controls, the data loss prevention deployment, the personal information protection control inventory, the privacy and security control register, and the threat protection control evidence. HITRUST requires the approved data protection and privacy policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Privacy by Design Records
artifacts.description: The privacy by design procedures, the default settings documentation, and the design review records evidencing privacy considerations were built in rather than added.

artifacts.name: Privacy Governance Framework
artifacts.description: The governance framework, the policies and procedures, the compliance evidence, the privacy policy, the appointment of the data protection officer or equivalent function, the personal data handling procedure, and the policies and procedures covering confidentiality, integrity and availability of personal data.

artifacts.name: Risk and Impact Assessments
artifacts.description: The risk assessments, the completed data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing activities, and the privacy impact assessment for personnel data.

artifacts.name: Processing Records and Transfers
artifacts.description: The records of processing activities documenting purposes, legal basis, categories, retention and transfers; the cross-border transfer mechanisms evidencing lawful international transfers; the retention schedule; and the procedure for handling access, rectification, erasure and portability requests.

artifacts.name: Disclosure Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The disclosure monitoring records and the misuse prevention procedure documentation covering how the protected data is watched in use.

artifacts.name: Provider Responsibility Acknowledgment
artifacts.description: The standard contract clause embodying the required written acknowledgment of responsibility, the sample executed customer agreements containing it, and the repository of executed customer agreements.

artifacts.name: Consent and Notice Records
artifacts.description: The records from the consent management platform showing valid consent capture, the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, the privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, and the executed agreements with required security clauses and signature records.

PRI-01.6.notes: 38 asks across 6 frameworks. Technical measures, privacy-by-design and the governance framework behind both are three proofs; PCI DSS 12.9.1's written acknowledgment of responsibility is a contractual instrument and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Privacy Notice
artifacts.description: The privacy notice and policy published to data subjects, the privacy notice published on the website and in applications, the current notice of privacy practices, the collection notices, the published privacy notices stating purpose, legal basis and use of personal data, the third-party data notices, and the privacy policy behind them. HITRUST requires the approved privacy notice and openness and transparency policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Notice Delivery Records
artifacts.description: The notice delivery mechanisms, the evidence of notice communication to data subjects, the distribution and acknowledgment records, the notice timing evidence, the information provision timing, the information provided at collection, the website posting of the notice, the accessibility measures, the communication templates, and the accessibility and language review records.

artifacts.name: Notice Version History
artifacts.description: The privacy notice update and version history records, the notice revision history, the privacy notice update records, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Consent Records
artifacts.description: The records from the consent management platform showing valid consent capture, the records of consent captured where required, the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, and the consent form explanation procedure.

artifacts.name: Lawful Basis Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping each processing activity to its lawful basis and to consent where required, the records of processing activities documenting purposes, legal basis, categories, retention and transfers, and the source disclosure for personal data not obtained from the data subject.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Rights Procedure
artifacts.description: The procedure for handling access, rectification, erasure and portability requests, with the request logs evidencing it operates.

artifacts.name: Privacy Governance Records
artifacts.description: The appointment of the data protection officer or equivalent function, the completed data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing activities, and the cross-border transfer mechanisms evidencing lawful international transfers.

artifacts.name: Patient Communication Materials
artifacts.description: The patient communication materials about the exchange, the patient information leaflets and posters, the patient education materials on health information sharing, and the records of patient briefing sessions.

artifacts.name: Customer Security Communications
artifacts.description: The customer security education materials and the security advisory distribution records to customers.

artifacts.name: Disclosure Notification Records
artifacts.description: The disclosure notification records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented disclosure notification requirement.

artifacts.name: Privacy Notice Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented privacy notice and consent management specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures implementing it, the data lifecycle records covering retention schedules, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the notice obligations.

PRI-02.notes: 58 asks across 11 frameworks. The notice itself, its delivery and its version history are one artifact set; consent capture and the lawful-basis register are separate because a notice can be published without either.

artifacts.name: Purpose Documentation
artifacts.description: The purpose documentation, the data processing records, the privacy impact assessment, and the records of processing activities documenting purposes, legal basis, categories, retention and transfers. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limitation of purpose in personal data processing requirement. HITRUST requires the approved purpose legitimacy and purpose specification policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Lawful Basis Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping each processing activity to its lawful basis and to consent where required, and the published privacy notices stating purpose, legal basis and use of personal data.

artifacts.name: Collection Notices
artifacts.description: The collection notices, the information provided at collection, the notice timing evidence, the information provision timing for data not obtained from the subject, the source disclosure, the third-party data notices, and the privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history. HITRUST requires the approved privacy notice policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The authorisation form templates with their required elements, the authorisation tracking and management system, the procedures for verifying valid authorisations, and the revocation handling procedures.

artifacts.name: Consent Records
artifacts.description: The records from the consent management platform showing valid consent capture, the records of consent captured where required, the signed patient consent records, the consent form covering all participating facilities, the updated consent form with the exchange-specific clauses, the consent form explanation procedure, and the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs.

artifacts.name: Patient Communication Materials
artifacts.description: The patient communication materials about the exchange, the patient information leaflets and posters, the patient education materials on health information sharing, the records of patient briefing sessions, and the consent training records for the front-desk staff who obtain it.

artifacts.name: Privacy Governance Records
artifacts.description: The privacy policy, the appointment of the data protection officer or equivalent function, the completed data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing activities, the procedure for handling access, rectification, erasure and portability requests, and the cross-border transfer mechanisms evidencing lawful international transfers.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the purpose specification requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-02.1.notes: 49 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps PRI-02; what is distinct here is the statement of purpose and its lawful basis rather than the notice that carries it, so the processing register and authorisation forms stay separate from the notice artifacts.

artifacts.name: Consent Mechanisms
artifacts.description: The consent mechanisms and their documentation, the consent management platform and configuration, the opt-in and opt-out mechanism documentation, and the authorisation form templates with their required elements and tracking system.

artifacts.name: Consent Capture Records
artifacts.description: The consent records, the consent collection records with their audit trail, the records of consent captured where required, the records of explicit consent obtained before collection, the signed patient consent records, the consent form covering all participating facilities, the updated consent form with the exchange-specific clauses, and the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs. HITRUST requires the approved consent policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Consent Withdrawal Records
artifacts.description: The withdrawal procedures, the consent revocation procedures, the revocation handling procedures, the records of consent withdrawal requests and their processing, the objection procedures, the marketing opt-out mechanisms, and the processing cessation records evidencing withdrawal took effect.

artifacts.name: Special Category Consent Records
artifacts.description: The lawful basis for special category data, the special category data inventory, the additional safeguards applied to it, and the explicit consent forms and mechanisms for that data.

artifacts.name: Consent Change Management
artifacts.description: The process for managing consent for new data uses and the communication records informing data subjects of the consent requirements.

artifacts.name: Lawful Basis Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping each processing activity to its lawful basis and to consent where required, the published privacy notices stating purpose, legal basis and use of personal data, the privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, and the procedures for verifying valid authorisations.

artifacts.name: Consent Training Records
artifacts.description: The consent training records for the front-desk staff who obtain it and the awareness communications informing personnel of the consent requirements.

artifacts.name: Records Management Controls
artifacts.description: The policy on creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal of records; the retention schedule listing record types, period, legal basis and disposal method; the documentation of storage, encryption and access controls for protected records; the retention automation configuration; the archive access logs; and the destruction log with method and witness — the controls holding the consent record itself.

artifacts.name: Consent Management Accountability
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the documented privacy notice and consent management specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures implementing it, the data lifecycle records covering retention schedules, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-03.notes: 49 asks across 9 frameworks. Consent capture, consent withdrawal and the special-category uplift are three proofs; withdrawal is kept separate because a consent platform can record collection perfectly and still not honour a withdrawal.

artifacts.name: Purpose Documentation and Compatibility Assessment
artifacts.description: The documented purpose for each processing activity, the records of processing activities, and the compatibility assessment performed where data is to be used for a purpose beyond the original one. HITRUST requires the approved purpose legitimacy standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Collection Limitation Records
artifacts.description: The data collection inventory mapped to the purposes stated in the privacy notice, the collection method review and approval records, the approved collection limitation standard with its implementing procedure, and the third-party data source agreements with their reliability assessments.

artifacts.name: Data Minimisation Assessment
artifacts.description: The data inventory with the field-level justification showing each attribute is necessary for the stated purpose, the necessity assessments, the minimisation assessment documentation, and the approved minimisation standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Legal Basis and Authority Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented legal authority for the processing, the justification for handling personal information, the privacy law compliance records, and the applicable-laws compliance mapping.

artifacts.name: Purpose-of-Use Enforcement Records
artifacts.description: The procedures enforcing that access is exercised only for a permitted purpose, the permitted purpose audit logs, the user attestation records captured at point of access, and the logs recording permitted and non-permitted access flags.

artifacts.name: Minimum Necessary Disclosure Records
artifacts.description: The minimum necessary disclosure and request procedures, the defined minimum data set, the disclosure scope review records, the request scope justification records, and the documented exemption where the request is for a treatment purpose.

artifacts.name: Use Restriction Controls
artifacts.description: The procedures restricting use to the permitted operational purposes, the acceptable use policy referencing the exchange, the data-loss prevention rules preventing ingestion into unauthorised local systems, the cloud-storage prohibition controls, the data residency enforcement records, and the unauthorised disclosure prevention procedures.

artifacts.name: Privacy Policy and Principle Mapping
artifacts.description: The approved privacy policy embedding the stated privacy principles, the mapping of policy clauses to each principle, the personal information handling procedure, and the published privacy notice.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Purpose Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping every transfer or disclosure outside the jurisdiction to a permitted purpose, the documented legal basis assessment per transfer, the memo justifying that a transfer is necessary for central processing operations, and the extract from the processing records evidencing purpose, recipient, destination and data category for each outbound transfer.

artifacts.name: Research Transfer Minimisation Records
artifacts.description: The assessment documenting the scientific research purpose and confirming the data is not sensitive, the record evidencing the transfer is limited to the minimum data required, and the executed contractual clauses or recipient approval certificate relied on.

artifacts.name: Transfer Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The completed transfer risk assessment covering all required elements with the standard template enumerating them, the coverage matrix confirming each element is addressed, and the risk treatment plan documenting the measures applied to mitigate risks to data subjects.

artifacts.name: Records Retention and Destruction Controls
artifacts.description: The records management policy covering creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal; the retention schedule listing record types, period, legal basis and disposal method; the protection controls documentation; the retention automation configuration; the archive access logs; and the destruction log with method and witness.

artifacts.name: Privacy Impact Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The privacy impact assessment for the processing in question, the business intelligence use case validation with its compliance evidence, the data quality profiling reports, and the privacy artifacts supporting them.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Purpose Controls
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records, extending the purpose restriction to parties the data reaches.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the purpose, collection and minimisation obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-04.notes: 72 asks across 10 frameworks. Purpose limitation, collection limitation and data minimisation are three separate HITRUST standards and three separate GDPR obligations; they are kept as distinct artifacts because each is evidenced differently.

artifacts.name: Lawful Basis Documentation
artifacts.description: The lawful basis documentation, the basis justification, the processing records, the register mapping each processing activity to its lawful basis and to consent where required, the legal authority documentation, the personal data processing justification, and the privacy compliance records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limitation of purpose requirement. HITRUST requires the approved purpose legitimacy policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Collection Limitation Records
artifacts.description: The data collection inventory mapped to the privacy notice purposes, the data minimisation assessment documentation, the collection method review and approval records, and the third-party data source agreements with their reliability assessments. HITRUST requires the approved collection limitation policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Special Category Basis Records
artifacts.description: The lawful basis for special category data, the special category data inventory, and the additional safeguards applied to it.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Purpose Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping every transfer or disclosure of personal data outside the jurisdiction to a permitted purpose, the documented legal basis assessment tying each transfer to the relevant statutory subparagraph, the memo justifying that the transfer is necessary for central processing operations, and the processing-activities extract evidencing the transfer purpose, recipient, destination and data category for each outbound flow.

artifacts.name: Internal Sharing Authorisation
artifacts.description: The internal authorisation records, the process documentation for sharing legacy or non-consented data under regulatory mandate, and the records of data shared under that mandate.

artifacts.name: Restricted Subject Data Controls
artifacts.description: The high-profile patient data sharing procedure aligned with the regulator's directions, the participation criteria compliance evidence, and the access control configuration records for that data.

artifacts.name: Consent and Notice Records
artifacts.description: The records of consent captured where required, the published privacy notices stating purpose, legal basis and use of personal data, the awareness communications informing personnel of the collection rules, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-04.1.notes: 36 asks across 8 frameworks. The lawful basis, the collection limitation it imposes and the cross-border purpose register are three proofs; the special-category uplift is kept separate because it demands a second basis.

artifacts.name: Retention Schedule
artifacts.description: The documented retention schedule listing each data category with owner, legal or regulatory basis, retention trigger and period, and storage location. Periods differ materially and the schedule must satisfy the longest applicable: QCB requires fifteen-year retention for financial records; PCI DSS requires twelve months for logs with three immediately available.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Policy
artifacts.description: The approved retention and disposal policy aligned to legal, regulatory and sectoral requirements; the information deletion policy defining when and how information must be removed; the records management policy covering creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal; and the procedure operationalising consistent classification, retention and disposal. HITRUST requires the approved retention and disposal standard with its implementing procedure; CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence.

artifacts.name: Retention Automation Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration of retention policies in the content management and messaging platforms, the storage lifecycle policy export, and the automated purge and archival procedures with their logs.

artifacts.name: Retention Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The audit or report verifying that the age of the oldest retained data actually meets the required period, the retention compliance verification records, the archive restoration test demonstrating archived data can be recovered, and the archive access logs.

artifacts.name: Periodic Retention Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic review of retained personal information, the data minimisation reviews and assessments, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer, evidencing data is not held beyond its purpose by default.

artifacts.name: Logical Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The procedures for secure deletion across database, file, cloud and backup systems; the deletion log executed against the retention schedule with verification; the backup deletion records showing expired backups purged; the provider deletion attestations on termination; and the log of erasure requests fulfilled and verified.

artifacts.name: Electronic Media Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for destruction of electronic media by degaussing, secure wiping or physical destruction such that data cannot be reconstructed; the wiping tool configuration and execution logs; the destruction tool configurations; and the wiping and destruction verification evidence.

artifacts.name: Hard-Copy Destruction Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for destroying hard-copy material by cross-cut shredding, incineration or pulping such that it cannot be reconstructed; the physical document shredding procedures and records; and the evidence that material awaiting destruction is held in secure containers until then.

artifacts.name: Destruction Certificates
artifacts.description: The certificates of destruction from internal destruction or a third-party vendor, the disposal certificates and records, the media sanitisation records, and the disposal verification and audit trail tying each disposal to its certificate.

artifacts.name: Hardware Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The hardware decommissioning procedures, the media sanitisation and disposal policy, and the asset disposal records tying each retired asset to its destruction evidence.

artifacts.name: Records Protection Controls
artifacts.description: The documentation of storage, encryption and access controls protecting records through their retention period, and the destruction log recording method and witness at the end of it.

artifacts.name: Privacy Law Alignment Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence that the retention schedule aligns with applicable privacy law, the mapping of policy clauses to each privacy principle, and the evidence of the personal data protection controls applied.

artifacts.name: Data Flow and Segmentation Documentation
artifacts.description: The data flow diagrams, the information flow control policies, the network segmentation documentation and the boundary protection configurations that determine where retained data resides and what must be reached to dispose of it.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the retention and disposal obligations and the handling that follows from them.

PRI-05.notes: 69 asks across 10 frameworks. Retention (how long) and disposal (how it ends) are separated, and hard-copy destruction is kept apart from electronic because PCI DSS 9.4.6 and 9.4.7 test them as different requirements with different methods.

artifacts.name: Purpose Limitation for Internal Use
artifacts.description: The purpose limitation policy with its enforcement documentation, the purpose documentation, the data processing records, the privacy impact assessment, the legal authority documentation, the personal data processing justification, and the privacy compliance records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limitation of purpose requirement.

artifacts.name: Test Data Controls
artifacts.description: The approved policy prohibiting live regulated data in pre-production environments unless those environments are in scope, the configuration of data masking or synthetic data generation tooling, the data discovery scan of pre-production environments confirming no live data is present, and the evidence of full protection coverage where the pre-production environment is itself in scope.

artifacts.name: Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The authorisation form templates with their required elements, the authorisation tracking and management system, the procedures for verifying valid authorisations, and the revocation handling procedures.

artifacts.name: Research Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The assessment documenting the scientific research purpose and confirming the data is not sensitive, the record evidencing the transfer is limited to the minimum data required, and the executed standard contractual clauses or the recipient body's approval certificate from a licensed entity.

artifacts.name: Data Use Monitoring
artifacts.description: The data use monitoring and audit reports evidencing internal use stayed within the authorised purpose.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The personal information retention schedule, the data retention policy, the record retention schedule, the data disposal procedures with their evidence, and the retention compliance verification records.

artifacts.name: Records Management Controls
artifacts.description: The policy on creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal of records; the retention schedule listing record types, period, legal basis and disposal method; the documentation of storage, encryption and access controls for protected records; the retention automation configuration; the archive access logs; and the destruction log with method and witness.

artifacts.name: Data Location Records
artifacts.description: The data location controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

PRI-05.1.notes: 35 asks across 7 frameworks. Overlaps PRI-05.4 and TDA-10; what is distinct here is internal use for testing, training and research specifically, with the research-transfer exemption kept as its own artifact.

artifacts.name: Purpose Limitation Policy
artifacts.description: The purpose limitation policy with its enforcement documentation, the legal authority documentation, the personal data processing justification, the privacy compliance records, and the purpose-of-use enforcement procedures. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented limitation of purpose in personal data processing requirement. HITRUST requires the approved purpose specification and use and disclosure policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Permitted Purpose Enforcement
artifacts.description: The permitted purpose audit logs, the user attestation records confirming the purpose of each access, and the data use monitoring and audit reports.

artifacts.name: Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The authorisation form templates with their required elements, the authorisation tracking and management system, the procedures for verifying valid authorisations, and the revocation handling procedures.

artifacts.name: Restriction Request Records
artifacts.description: The restriction request procedures, the restriction request log with its tracking, the confidential communication accommodation procedures, and the staff training on individual rights.

artifacts.name: Retention and Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The personal information retention schedule, the data disposal and destruction procedures with their evidence, the retention schedule listing record types, period, legal basis and disposal method, the retention automation configuration, the archive access logs, and the destruction log with method and witness.

artifacts.name: Records Management Controls
artifacts.description: The policy on creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal of records and the documentation of storage, encryption and access controls for protected records.

artifacts.name: Test Data Restrictions
artifacts.description: The approved policy prohibiting live regulated data in pre-production environments unless those environments are in scope, the configuration of data masking or synthetic data generation tooling, the data discovery scan of pre-production environments confirming no live data is present, and the evidence of full protection coverage where the pre-production environment is itself in scope.

artifacts.name: AI Privacy Risk Records
artifacts.description: The privacy risk assessment for the AI system, the elicited system requirements with their socio-technical design decision records, the documented evidence demonstrating the outcome, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Data Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The sensitive data transfer controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented sensitive data transfer requirement.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the usage restrictions and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-05.4.notes: 44 asks across 9 frameworks. The purpose limitation, its technical enforcement and the individual's right to request a further restriction are three proofs; PCI DSS 6.5.5's prohibition on live data in test arrives here and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Rights Procedure
artifacts.description: The data subject access request procedures, the subject access request procedures, the rectification procedures, the erasure procedures, the restriction procedures, the access request procedures and forms, the patient data access procedure documentation, the response templates and communication templates, and the accessibility measures making the process usable. HITRUST requires the approved principle access policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Identity Verification Records
artifacts.description: The identity verification process for data subjects and the personal representative authorisation records evidencing a request was made by someone entitled to make it.

artifacts.name: Request Fulfilment Records
artifacts.description: The request handling records, the fulfilment records, the access request tracking log with response timelines, the records of patient access requests fulfilled, the deletion confirmation, the update confirmation, the processing flags applied for restriction, the sample responses demonstrating completeness, and the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs.

artifacts.name: Request Response Metrics
artifacts.description: The request tracking and response time metrics evidencing the statutory clocks are met rather than merely acknowledged.

artifacts.name: Designated Record Set Definition
artifacts.description: The designated record set definition scoping what a subject may reach and the fee schedule for copies where one applies.

artifacts.name: Privacy Notice and Rights Communication
artifacts.description: The privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, the privacy notices, the patient rights and responsibilities policy document, the patient information materials and posters, the regulatory compliance evidence for them, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved openness and transparency policy and standard with its implementing procedure and its awareness communications.

artifacts.name: Access Enforcement Records
artifacts.description: The role-based access control documentation, the access control list configurations, and the access enforcement testing results confirming the rights granted are the rights enforced.

artifacts.name: Sub-Processor Disclosure Records
artifacts.description: The disclosure of data sub-processors. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Rights Accountability
artifacts.description: The documented data subject rights specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the data security control evidence including access controls, the privacy artifacts, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability.

PRI-06.notes: 51 asks across 8 frameworks. The rights procedure, the identity verification that gates it and the fulfilment record are three proofs; the several GDPR articles each name a different right but are answered by one request-handling process and are merged accordingly.

artifacts.name: Complaint Handling Procedure
artifacts.description: The complaint resolution documentation with its response records, the privacy complaint and inquiry tracking system, the evidence of an operational complaint-handling mechanism with a log of complaints, the patient inquiry routing procedure, the inquiry handling logs and case records, and the facility contact directory routing them. HITRUST requires the approved complaint management policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Correction Request Records
artifacts.description: The amendment request procedures and forms, the amendment request tracking log, the amendment notification procedures, the denial and statement of disagreement records, the data correction and amendment request procedures, the records of corrections made to personal information, the third-party notification procedures for corrections, the erroneous information correction logs, and the operator notification records of corrections made.

artifacts.name: Access Denial Appeal Process
artifacts.description: The appeal process documentation for denied access requests, giving a data subject a route beyond the initial refusal.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Request Records
artifacts.description: The data subject access request procedures, the identity verification process for data subjects, the request tracking and response time metrics, the sample responses demonstrating completeness, and the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs.

artifacts.name: Restriction Request Records
artifacts.description: The restriction request procedures, the restriction request log with its tracking, the confidential communication accommodation procedures, and the staff training on individual rights.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Complaint Records
artifacts.description: The procedure ensuring data subject rights are upheld in cross-border transfers including the right to complain and the assessment demonstrating the implemented safeguards ensure compliance and protect the data.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Feedback Loop
artifacts.description: The approved data quality policy and procedures, the standardised data entry field definitions, the real-time validation and feedback loop configuration, the interface development best practices documentation, and the patient feedback intake records.

artifacts.name: Privacy Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The privacy compliance monitoring reports and audit results, the privacy noncompliance incident reports with their corrective action plans, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Privacy Notice and Communication
artifacts.description: The privacy notices, the privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, the communication templates, the accessibility measures, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the complaint management obligations.

PRI-06.4.notes: 42 asks across 6 frameworks. Complaints, correction requests and access-denial appeals are three distinct channels with different obligations; the appeal process is kept separate because it is what a denied request escalates into.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing Agreements
artifacts.description: The third-party data sharing agreements with their privacy addenda, the data sharing agreements with their interoperability standards and integration documentation, the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, and the documented external data sharing agreements specification with its compliance evidence and implementation records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented personal data sub-processing requirement. HITRUST requires the approved privacy requirements and use and disclosure policies and standards with their implementing procedures.

artifacts.name: Disclosure Authorisation Records
artifacts.description: The authorisation form templates with their required elements, the authorisation tracking and management system, the procedures for verifying valid authorisations, the revocation handling procedures, and the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs.

artifacts.name: Disclosure Logs
artifacts.description: The data disclosure logs recording purpose and consent basis for each disclosure and the disclosure audit reports drawn from them.

artifacts.name: Downstream Compliance Verification
artifacts.description: The compliance verification procedure for downstream disclosures and the legal and regulatory compliance attestation obtained from the recipient.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Privacy Assurance
artifacts.description: The third-party due diligence assessment records, the third-party privacy compliance monitoring reports, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The approval certificate held by the recipient party issued by a body licensed by the competent authority, the record confirming the data transferred is not sensitive, and the assessment evidencing the transfer provides a service or benefit directly to the data subject in a manner they would expect.

artifacts.name: Records Management Controls
artifacts.description: The policy on creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal of records; the retention schedule listing record types, period, legal basis and disposal method; the documentation of storage, encryption and access controls for protected records; the retention automation configuration; the archive access logs; and the destruction log with method and witness.

artifacts.name: Privacy Notice and Review Records
artifacts.description: The privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, the awareness communications informing personnel of the disclosure rules, the periodic review records naming the reviewer, and the organisational artifacts and periodic review records covering the sharing arrangements.

PRI-07.notes: 37 asks across 8 frameworks. The sharing agreement, the authorisation to share, and the log of what was actually disclosed are three proofs; the last is what an assessor samples and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Data Processing Agreements
artifacts.description: The data processing agreements with their contract provisions, the executed agreements with the required security clauses and signature records, the sample contract clauses and security requirements checklist, the contract review records, and the processor assessments performed before signature. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented personal data sub-processing and data portability contractual obligation requirements.

artifacts.name: Standard Contractual Clauses
artifacts.description: The signed standard contractual clauses in the standard form issued by the competent authority for the relevant transfer type, the executed clauses or the recipient body's approval certificate where that alternative is relied on, and the standard contractual clauses used for transfers under the general regime.

artifacts.name: Binding Corporate and Common Rules
artifacts.description: The binding corporate rules, the approved binding common rules adopted by the controller and applicable across the multinational group, the intra-group data transfer agreement, the memo evidencing the controller is part of a multinational group and the transfer is necessary to its central operations, and the recipient's certificate of approval from a licensed body where that alternative applies.

artifacts.name: Transfer Impact Assessments
artifacts.description: The transfer impact assessments, the assessment demonstrating the implemented safeguards ensure compliance and protect the data, and the certificate of accreditation held where accreditation is the chosen route.

artifacts.name: Transfer Safeguards Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping each exempt cross-border transfer to the safeguard implemented with its status and validity dates, the documented selection of the appropriate safeguard per exempt transfer, the evidence that safeguards remain in place notwithstanding the exemption, and the register recording each exempt transfer with the conditions exempted and the applicable case.

artifacts.name: Transfer Exemption Assessments
artifacts.description: The assessment confirming the transfer qualifies for exemption from the transfer conditions, the documentation evidencing the transfer is non-recurring or for a limited period involving a limited number of data subjects, the sensitivity screening record where the approval-certificate alternative is relied on, the assessment documenting the scientific research purpose and confirming the data is not sensitive, and the record evidencing the research transfer is limited to the minimum data required.

artifacts.name: Public Body Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The executed inter-governmental agreement or memorandum of understanding containing the standard personal data protection provisions, the authorisation record confirming the public-body-to-public-body transfer implements that agreement, and the mapping confirming the required standard provisions are present in each relevant agreement.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Rights and Complaints
artifacts.description: The procedure ensuring data subject rights are upheld in cross-border transfers including the right to complain, the evidence of an operational complaint-handling mechanism with a log of complaints relating to transfers, and the consent records, opt-out tracking and data subject request logs behind them.

artifacts.name: Disclosure Accounting Records
artifacts.description: The disclosure limitation policies aligned to the privacy notice, the data flow mapping showing disclosure recipients, the approval process for new disclosure purposes, the periodic review of disclosure practices, and the privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history. HITRUST requires the approved accounting of disclosures policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Legal Obligations Register
artifacts.description: The register of applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations with requirements mapped to controls; the matrix mapping each obligation to responsible owner, controls and evidence; the periodic compliance monitoring reports; the horizon scanning report on upcoming changes with readiness status; the advisory notes from counsel on new or changed requirements; and the legal review of cryptographic use across jurisdictions.

artifacts.name: Records Management Controls
artifacts.description: The policy on creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal of records; the retention schedule listing record types, period, legal basis and disposal method; the documentation of storage, encryption and access controls for protected records; the retention automation configuration; the archive access logs; and the destruction log with method and witness.

artifacts.name: Provider Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records covering the contractors and service providers handling personal data, with the awareness communications and periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved privacy requirements policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

PRI-07.1.notes: 65 asks across 7 frameworks. The KSA cross-border transfer regulation contributes eight separate legal pathways; these are grouped by instrument (contractual clauses, binding rules, exemption records) rather than by regulation article, because an assessor asks which pathway each transfer relies on.

artifacts.name: Privacy Control Testing
artifacts.description: The schedule of manager-led compliance reviews by area, the completed self-assessment forms from department managers, the automated compliance scan output against internal standards, the log of non-compliances detected with root cause and corrective action, and the evidence of actions taken to address them.

artifacts.name: Privacy Training Records
artifacts.description: The documented personal data protection training specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures behind it, the training and awareness records covering curriculum, attendance, completion and schedule, and the training attendance records with dates. HITRUST requires the approved privacy protection awareness policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Privacy Monitoring and Audit
artifacts.description: The documented compliance monitoring and audit specification with its compliance evidence, the audit plan and reports with scope, findings and remediation tracking, the audit logging configuration evidence, the log review records with their follow-up case documentation, the compliance monitoring dashboard showing indicator trends across control families, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records. HITRUST requires the approved privacy monitoring and auditing policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Technical Vulnerability Records
artifacts.description: The vulnerability management policy covering scanning cadence, service levels, prioritisation and exception handling; the periodic scan reports covering internal and external assets; the remediation tracker showing open vulnerabilities with owners, service levels and closure status; the metrics showing remediation performance against those service levels; the annual penetration test reports with findings and remediation evidence; the records of patches deployed per system with success or failure and rollback; and the documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated immediately.

artifacts.name: Privacy Programme Accountability
artifacts.description: The privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, the data sharing agreements with their interoperability standards and integration documentation, the business intelligence dashboards and analytics use-case register, the privacy artifacts, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-08.notes: 37 asks across 3 frameworks. Control testing, training and monitoring are three named obligations in the control title and are kept as three artifact groups rather than merged into a privacy programme pack.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Plan
artifacts.description: The documented data quality plan and data quality prioritisation specifications with their compliance evidence, the initial data quality assessment, the approved data management and personal data protection strategy behind them, the data quality management procedures for personal information, the documented controls maintaining accuracy, completeness and consistency across the lifecycle, and the registers evidencing prioritisation with a named owner. HITRUST requires the approved accuracy and quality policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Rules
artifacts.description: The documented data quality rules development specification with its compliance evidence, the register evidencing those rules with a named owner, the data accuracy verification and validation processes, and the evidence of validation and reconciliation activities.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Reports
artifacts.description: The data quality profiling reports, the data quality metrics and monitoring reports, the performance metrics dashboard with targets, measurements and review records, the business intelligence dashboards and analytics use-case register, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, and the data value realisation records.

artifacts.name: Master and Reference Data Records
artifacts.description: The master and reference data register with golden-record definitions and stewardship records and the documented reference and master data requirements specification with its compliance evidence, implementing procedures and process workflows, and the register evidencing it with a named owner.
