artifacts.name: Metadata Quality Records
artifacts.description: The approved metadata quality policy or standard with its documented specification, compliance evidence, implementing procedures and process workflows; the documented metadata quality indicators specification with its compliance evidence; the metadata repository or data catalog export; and the register evidencing metadata quality with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Patient Identity Reconciliation
artifacts.description: The master patient index design and documentation, its maintenance records, and the cross-system patient identifier reconciliation evidence.

artifacts.name: Data Relevance Assessment
artifacts.description: The data relevance assessment documentation confirming the personal information held is still necessary for the purpose it was collected for.

artifacts.name: Data Quality Governance Records
artifacts.description: The organisational artifacts covering role mandates, responsibility matrices, job descriptions and committee charters; the data security control evidence including access controls; the privacy artifacts; the awareness communications informing personnel of the accuracy and quality requirements; and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRI-10.notes: 49 asks across 5 frameworks. NDMO contributes eight separate data-quality specifications that collapse into a plan, a rule set and a measurement; the master patient index and metadata quality are kept separate because they are distinct data domains.

artifacts.name: Project and Programme Management Framework
artifacts.description: The documented methodology with its management approval, the playbook operationalising it across projects, the programme management standards, and sample project artifacts evidencing the framework is applied rather than only published.

artifacts.name: Project Portfolio Register and Dashboard
artifacts.description: The centralised registry of all technology projects maintained by the programme office, the portfolio-level dashboard monitoring progress with status, milestones and resource allocation, the programme status reports, and the project completion reports.

artifacts.name: Programme Office Governance Records
artifacts.description: The programme office charter and operating procedures, the periodic reports submitted to the steering committee on project status, the steering committee charter and terms of reference, and the meeting minutes documenting implementation reviews and directions.

artifacts.name: Project Security Integration Records
artifacts.description: The project management methodology explicitly integrating security checkpoints and gate criteria, the security risk assessment template used at initiation, a sample project charter showing security objectives and owners captured upfront, the portfolio security tracker with assessment status and outstanding actions, and the gate review sign-offs confirming security reviews completed before design and go-live.

artifacts.name: Investment Portfolio and Business Cases
artifacts.description: The IT investment portfolio documentation with its prioritisation criteria, the business case documentation per initiative, the investment decision and funding allocation records, the portfolio performance metrics and return analysis, and the benefits realisation tracking with post-implementation reviews of IT-enabled initiatives.

artifacts.name: Resource Allocation and Capacity Records
artifacts.description: The IT budget and cost optimisation reports, resource allocation plans and capacity assessments, resource utilisation metrics and workforce planning reports, the sourcing strategy documentation with vendor assessments, and the records of resource allocation of people and budget to each project.

artifacts.name: Requirements Definition and Sign-off
artifacts.description: The business requirements documentation with traceability matrices, the feasibility study reports and solution option analyses, the requirements risk assessment documentation, and the sign-off and approval records.

artifacts.name: Project Monitoring and Escalation Records
artifacts.description: The documented project monitoring procedure covering status reporting, escalation and resource checks, the issue escalation procedures, the register of project escalations addressed by the steering committee, and the records of escalated issues with their resolutions.

artifacts.name: IT Risk Register and Treatment
artifacts.description: The IT risk management policy and framework, the risk register with assessments and treatment plans, the risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact, and the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Security Planning Policy
artifacts.description: The security planning policy and its planning procedures, with the policy review records evidencing it is maintained.

artifacts.name: Objectives, Risk Tolerance and Compliance Inventory
artifacts.description: The documented security and operational objectives with the objective-setting methodology, the risk tolerance statements, and the inventory of compliance requirements the portfolio must satisfy.

artifacts.name: Control Framework and Lifecycle Documentation
artifacts.description: The IT general controls framework documentation, the security management process documentation, the technology acquisition and development lifecycle controls, and the technology infrastructure control inventory.

artifacts.name: Change Impact and Environmental Scanning
artifacts.description: The management of change procedures for significant organisational changes, the business model change impact assessments, the change management risk assessment process, and the environmental scanning and threat intelligence reports that trigger them.

artifacts.name: Management Commitment and Direction Records
artifacts.description: The signed leadership statement committing to enforce security policies and provide resources, the management review meeting minutes with directives, the guidance issued to line managers on enforcing policy in their teams, the employment contract security clauses, and the new joiner security briefing records.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Objectives
artifacts.description: The documented continuity objectives, the plan for achieving them, the KPIs and measurement criteria attached, and the monitoring and review records.

artifacts.name: AI Management System Resource Records
artifacts.description: The plan identifying financial, human, infrastructure and tooling resources required across establishment, implementation and improvement of the AI management system, the budget approvals and allocation records confirming provisioning, and the periodic utilisation reports against plan with variances and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: AI System Resource Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of resources per AI life-cycle stage covering system components, data, tooling, computing and human resources, the architecture and data-flow diagrams documenting them, and the assessment of resource availability with any required changes to design or deployment.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Management Oversight Records
artifacts.description: The documented evidence of the risk management outcomes, the AI impact assessment, the management oversight records confirming the outcome is resourced and operating, the implementation records and artifacts within the AI lifecycle, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Internal Communication and Reporting Channels
artifacts.description: The board reporting packages on internal controls and security, internal security communication procedures, security awareness programme materials, and the whistleblower or anonymous reporting mechanism.

PRM-01.notes: 91 asks across 9 frameworks. COBIT contributes five separate governance and management practices (EDM02 value, EDM04 resources, APO05 portfolio, APO12 risk, BAI01/02 programmes) that all land here; they are kept distinct because each has its own decision forum.

artifacts.name: Board-Approved IT and Digital Strategy
artifacts.description: The current IT and Digital Strategy documents covering vision, mission, stakeholder map, business workflow, data processing, system access, security practices and IT resource availability, with board approval signatures and dates. QCB and COBIT expect the strategy to be explicitly aligned to business strategy; SBP ETGRMF expects both the IT and the Digital Strategy to exist and to be pre-reviewed by the board IT committee before adoption.

artifacts.name: Board Approval Records and Minutes
artifacts.description: The signed board resolution approving the strategy with effective and next-review dates, the minutes capturing deliberation and questions, the presentation deck tabled at approval, and the board resolutions for each subsequent update or refresh.

artifacts.name: Strategy Implementation Roadmap and Tracker
artifacts.description: The multi-year roadmap breaking the strategy into initiatives with timelines, owners, budgets and KPIs, the detailed implementation plan operationalising it, the execution dashboard tracking initiatives against milestones, and the management progress reports and steering committee minutes evidencing oversight of that execution.

artifacts.name: Strategy Review and Update Records
artifacts.description: The documented strategic review procedure specifying frequency, participants, triggers and outputs, the minutes of periodic strategic reviews assessing continued relevance, and the change log capturing each update with its rationale. ISO 22301 scopes the equivalent to monitoring and review of business continuity objectives; NIST AI RMF expects periodic review records for the AI context.

artifacts.name: Cyber Security Strategy and Action Plan
artifacts.description: The board-approved cyber security strategy and action plan addressing anticipation of, withstanding of, detection of and response to cyber attacks, its implementation tracker and status dashboard, the periodic board reports on progress, the annual cyber security budget with contingency lines, and the mapping of the plan to international frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls).

artifacts.name: Digital Operational Resilience Strategy
artifacts.description: The digital operational resilience strategy document with ICT objectives aligned to risk appetite, the mapping of key dependencies, and the multi-vendor strategy documentation.

artifacts.name: Data Management and Personal Data Protection Strategy and Plan
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy and its implementing plan, with the per-domain plans derived from it (business intelligence, data architecture, catalog, classification, document and content management, personal data protection), the supporting procedures, and the register or inventory evidencing each with a named owner.

artifacts.name: AIMS Context and Scope Analysis
artifacts.description: The documented analysis of external and internal issues relevant to the AI management system, the PESTLE or equivalent worksheet capturing the factors driving it, the record determining the organisation's role for each AI system (provider, producer, customer, partner, subject), and the inventory of in-scope AI systems with their intended purpose.

artifacts.name: Interested Parties Register
artifacts.description: The register of interested parties (including AI subjects, customers, regulators, employees and suppliers) with their requirements and how each is addressed, the records of consultations and surveys used to elicit those requirements, and the mapping linking them to the processes and controls that satisfy them.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity Objectives
artifacts.description: The documented business continuity objectives, the plan for achieving them, the KPIs and measurement criteria attached to them, and the monitoring and review records.

artifacts.name: IT Governance Framework and Structure
artifacts.description: The IT management framework documentation and policies, organisational structure charts with IT roles and responsibilities, RACI matrices for IT processes, capability maturity assessments with improvement plans, committee charters for IT strategy, steering and technology risk, the committee minutes, and the IT policy, standard and procedure register.

artifacts.name: Strategic Constraints and Gap Analysis
artifacts.description: The current-versus-future-state technology assessment with gap analysis mapped to business objectives, the SWOT or PESTEL-style analysis of organisational, environmental and cultural constraints and enablers, gap analysis reports with prioritised initiatives, and the current-state and target-state architecture documentation behind them.

artifacts.name: AI Context Documentation
artifacts.description: Context documentation covering the intended purposes of each AI system, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing that the context has been established, and the periodic reviews confirming it remains accurate.

artifacts.name: Resource, Policy and Exception Registers
artifacts.description: The IT resource management plan covering people, process, technology and portfolio capacity, the IT value delivery dashboard, the IT-business strategic alignment traceability matrix, the master register of approved technology plans and policies with owner and review dates, the exception and deviation log with compensating controls and expiry, and the quarterly policy compliance monitoring report.

PRM-01.1.notes: 115 asks across 8 frameworks. NDMO restates the same strategy-and-plan artifact once per data domain; those are merged. Board approval evidence is held separately from the strategy document because several frameworks test the approval, not the document.

artifacts.name: Security Budget Approval
artifacts.description: The board or management-approved annual budget with dedicated line items for security solutions, training and certifications; the annual cyber security budget with its contingency line items; the annual awareness budget approval; the board approval minutes; the minutes evidencing approval of the dedicated budget; the register mapping allocated funds to security initiatives with spend tracking; and the evidence of adequate funding allocated to critical infrastructure security.

artifacts.name: Resource Allocation Plan
artifacts.description: The plan identifying financial, human, infrastructure and tooling resources required across the management system's establishment and implementation; the resource allocation approvals confirming provisioning; the periodic reports showing actual utilisation against plan with variances and corrective actions; the continuity management resource allocation records with their budget allocation and resource gap analysis; and the budget and resource allocations provisioned for the management system.

artifacts.name: Workforce and Succession Planning
artifacts.description: The technology workforce plan, the documented succession plan for key positions, the succession planning documentation for key technology and security roles, the resource utilisation metrics and workforce planning reports, and the resource allocation plans with their capacity assessments.

artifacts.name: Capacity Budget Integration
artifacts.description: The capacity plan integrated with the annual budgeting process and the reconciliation showing capacity requirements reflected in the budgets.

artifacts.name: Competence and Training Records
artifacts.description: The competency assessment records, the hiring and onboarding procedures including background checks, the training programme documentation with its completion records, the sample redacted contract showing security and confidentiality clauses, and the induction attendance or checklist signed by new hires confirming a security briefing before access.

artifacts.name: Leadership Commitment Records
artifacts.description: The signed leadership statement committing to enforce security policies and provide resources; the signed top-management statement of commitment to the management system, its policy and objectives; the management review meeting minutes; the minutes of executive meetings where performance, decisions and continual improvement are discussed; the guidance issued to line managers on enforcing policy; the log of internal communications by top management; and the records of top-management decisions on critical security matters.

artifacts.name: Investment Portfolio Records
artifacts.description: The technology investment portfolio with its business case documentation, the budget and cost optimisation reports, the benefits realisation tracking reports and dashboards, the value optimisation metrics and performance reports, the post-implementation reviews of technology-enabled initiatives, and the sourcing strategy documentation with its vendor assessments.

artifacts.name: Project Risk Records
artifacts.description: The project risk management procedures and the project risk registers with their mitigation plans.

artifacts.name: AI System Requirements Records
artifacts.description: The documented requirements and specifications for new AI systems or material enhancements including their rationale, and the traceability matrix linking requirements to design, development, testing and deployment artifacts.

artifacts.name: AI Resource Governance Records
artifacts.description: The AI impact assessment, the documented evidence demonstrating the resource management outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

PRM-02.notes: 49 asks across 10 frameworks. Budget, headcount and competence are three separable resource questions; the budget artifacts are kept apart from workforce planning because they are approved by different bodies and evidenced differently.

artifacts.name: Resource Gap Analysis
artifacts.description: The management-produced resource gap report identifying deficiencies across people, process and technology, submitted to the board or its committee, with the gap closure action plan naming owners, timelines and budgets.

artifacts.name: Gap Closure Tracking Records
artifacts.description: The tracking log showing status and timelines for each identified resource gap, updated periodically, evidencing that identified deficiencies are closed rather than only reported.

artifacts.name: Budget Approval Records
artifacts.description: The board resolutions approving budgets and resources to close identified gaps, the approved headcount plans and budgets, the budget allocation records, the budget line items for security specifically, and the budget documentation with its approval records.

artifacts.name: Resource Allocation Records
artifacts.description: The resource allocation plans with capacity assessments, the records of people and budget allocated to each project, the security resource allocation documentation, the resource planning records, and the sourcing strategy documentation with vendor assessments where capability is bought rather than built.

artifacts.name: Resource Utilisation Reports
artifacts.description: The periodic reports showing actual utilisation against plan with variances and corrective actions, the resource utilisation metrics and workforce planning reports, and the budget variance analysis and cost management reports.

artifacts.name: IT Financial Management Records
artifacts.description: The financial management policies and procedures, the cost allocation models with chargeback or showback reports, the budget and cost optimisation reports, and the value optimisation metrics.

artifacts.name: Investment Portfolio and Benefits Records
artifacts.description: The investment portfolio with business case documentation, the benefits realisation tracking reports and dashboards, and the post-implementation reviews of the initiatives the resources funded.

artifacts.name: Programme Plans and Status Reports
artifacts.description: The programme management methodology and standards, the charters with business cases and authorisation records, the plans with milestones, timelines and resource allocations, the status reports with benefits tracking, the portfolio dashboard, the project monitoring procedure covering resource checks, and the completion reports.

artifacts.name: Project Risk Records
artifacts.description: The project risk management procedures and the project risk registers with mitigation plans, covering the risks that arise when resources are constrained.

artifacts.name: IT Strategy and Roadmap Records
artifacts.description: The board-approved IT strategy with the resolution and minutes recording its approval, the presentation tabled at approval, and the multi-year implementation roadmap breaking it into initiatives with timelines, owners, budgets and targets.

artifacts.name: Workforce Capability Records
artifacts.description: The competency assessment records, the hiring and onboarding procedures including background checks, the training programme documentation with completion records, and the succession planning documentation for key technology and security roles.

artifacts.name: Control Implementation Prioritisation
artifacts.description: The risk and criticality-based control implementation plan with management or regulator approval, and the records prioritising resources to the assets that essential services depend on.

artifacts.name: AI Management System Resource Records
artifacts.description: The plan identifying financial, human, infrastructure and tooling resources required across establishment, implementation and improvement of the AI management system; the budget approvals confirming provisioning; the signed top-management commitment statement; the leadership communications log; and the executive minutes where performance and improvement are decided.

artifacts.name: AI System Resource Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of resources per AI life-cycle stage covering components, data, tooling, computing and human resources, the architecture and data-flow diagrams documenting them, and the assessment of resource availability with any required changes to design or deployment.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Resourcing Oversight
artifacts.description: The management oversight records confirming the risk management outcome is resourced and operating, the AI impact assessment, the documented evidence of the outcome, the implementation records within the AI lifecycle, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Independent Assurance over Resourcing
artifacts.description: The internal audit plan and schedule, the continuous monitoring programme documentation, the security control testing results, and the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports that reveal where under-resourcing has left gaps.

artifacts.name: Data Programme Resourcing Records
artifacts.description: The documented data classification and data management plans with their compliance evidence, the approved policy or standard behind them, the register with a named owner, the data security control evidence, and the privacy artifacts.

PRM-03.notes: 73 asks across 9 frameworks. The chain is gap identification → budget approval → allocation → utilisation against plan; SBP ETGRMF tests each link separately, so the gap analysis and the closure tracking are kept apart from the allocation records.

artifacts.name: Project Methodology with Security Gates
artifacts.description: The project management methodology explicitly integrating security checkpoints and gate criteria, the framework document covering structure, roles and activity breakdown, the playbook operationalising it, the management approval, and the sample project artifacts evidencing it is applied.

artifacts.name: Project Security Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The template used at project initiation to assess information security risks, the completed assessments per project, and the portfolio security tracker recording assessment status and outstanding actions across active projects.

artifacts.name: Security Requirements Specification
artifacts.description: The security requirements captured in the project's requirements documentation, the security specifications and business requirements with security included, the requirements review records, the sample charter showing security objectives and owners captured upfront, and the security-by-design requirements integrated into design and development. HITRUST requires the approved standard for security requirements analysis with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Requirements Traceability Matrix
artifacts.description: The traceability matrix linking each requirement through design, development, testing and deployment, the requirements specification documents, the change control records over requirements, and the business owner sign-off.

artifacts.name: Security Gate Sign-off Records
artifacts.description: The gate review sign-offs at design and go-live confirming security reviews were completed, the secure architecture review records for the systems in scope, and the approval authority matrix defining who may sign each gate.

artifacts.name: Project Initiation and Approval Records
artifacts.description: The standardised need assessment template used at initiation, the project management standards addressing need assessment, risk management and approval authorities with their management approval, the business case and feasibility analysis, the programme charters with authorisation records, and the project documentation repository with approval records.

artifacts.name: Project Governance and Status Records
artifacts.description: The project governance structure documentation, the plans with milestones, timelines and resource allocations, the status reports with schedule, cost and risk tracking, the stakeholder engagement documentation, and the closure reports with lessons learned and benefits assessment.

artifacts.name: Post-Implementation Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented methodology for post-implementation reviews, the schedule covering critical projects, the reports validating operational performance, and the evidence of results presented to management.

artifacts.name: Independent Project Quality Assurance
artifacts.description: The schedule of quality assurance reviews across major projects, the contracts engaging independent parties, the resulting review reports, and the reviewers' independence declarations.

artifacts.name: Solution Design and Test Records
artifacts.description: The development standards and quality assurance test plans, the high-level and detailed design documents, the procurement and build approval documentation, and the test results with defect tracking.

artifacts.name: Security Assessment Results
artifacts.description: The security assessment plan, the assessment results report, the plan of action and milestones, the security control testing results, and the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports covering the delivered system.

artifacts.name: Enterprise Risk Appetite Records
artifacts.description: The enterprise risk appetite and tolerance statements, the risk register with assessments and treatment plans, the risk committee minutes and escalation records, and the risk monitoring dashboards and trend reports that projects are assessed against.

artifacts.name: AI Project Resource and Requirements Records
artifacts.description: The documented requirements for new AI systems or material enhancements with their rationale, the traceability matrix, the resource inventory per life-cycle stage covering components, data, tooling, computing and human resources, the architecture and data-flow diagrams, and the resource availability assessment with any required design changes.

artifacts.name: Management System Communication Records
artifacts.description: The communication plan specifying what, when, with whom and how communications are made, the recurring communication schedule, and sample executed communications.

artifacts.name: Objectives and Control Framework Records
artifacts.description: The documented security and operational objectives with the objective-setting methodology, the risk tolerance statements, the compliance requirements inventory, the IT general controls framework, the security management process documentation, and the technology acquisition and development lifecycle controls.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The analysis of entity size and risk exposure, the assessment of incident likelihood and severity, and the justification for why the measures adopted in the project are proportionate.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the security requirements analysis obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

PRM-04.notes: 82 asks across 12 frameworks. Distinct from PRM-01 (portfolio) in that these demands concern security being present inside the project method — gates, requirements, sign-offs — rather than the portfolio being governed.

artifacts.name: Secure Development and Project Lifecycle Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented SDLC / project lifecycle methodology that governs new initiatives and significant changes, showing where security, compliance and resilience requirements are defined and where criticality analysis is performed. It must cover the phases (initiation, feasibility, business requirements, design, build, test, training, implementation, operation, maintenance, retirement), the mandatory security gate criteria and checkpoints at each decision point, the phase deliverable templates, need-assessment and approval authorities, and the system control standards for functional, security and automated control features. Frameworks expect management or board approval of the standards, evidence they are actually applied to development and acquisition, and coverage of both in-house build and acquired technology.

artifacts.name: Security, Compliance and Resilience Requirements Specifications
artifacts.description: The actual requirements artefacts produced for in-scope systems: the reusable security requirements catalogue (e.g. ASVS-based) and API security standard, plus per-project security requirement specifications, SRS/BRD sections capturing security requirements, non-functional requirements for performance and resilience, the regulatory requirements register feeding the specification, and — for AI systems — elicited system requirements with socio-technical design decision records, rationale and training/data requirements. Provide the catalogue plus sampled real project specifications.

artifacts.name: System Design Documents and Architecture Diagrams
artifacts.description: High-level and detailed design documentation for in-scope technology assets, applications and services: architecture, components, interfaces, data flows and functions, the application control design showing how security and automated controls are implemented, AI system and data-flow diagrams where applicable, and the records of secure-architecture reviews performed on those designs.

artifacts.name: Requirements Approval, Sign-off and Traceability Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that requirements were formally accepted and carried through: signed requirements approval records from security and architecture, security gate review sign-offs at design and go-live, the approval authority matrix showing who may approve at each project scale, management approval of the governing standards, and the traceability matrix linking each requirement to design, build, test and deployment artefacts. Also includes periodic review records confirming the requirements process remains effective.

artifacts.name: Technology Asset and System Inventory with Criticality Classification
artifacts.description: The inventory used to determine what is in scope and which components are critical: information asset register with owner, classification, location, custodian and retention; hardware, software and cloud resource inventories (CMDB and CSPM exports) reconciled against discovery scans; AI systems and AI resource inventories with intended purpose and lifecycle stage; and the technology infrastructure control inventory. Frameworks expect evidence of periodic reconciliation showing assets added, retired and verified, and formal asset owner assignment acknowledgements. Inventory exports are collector-friendly; classification, ownership and criticality determinations are manual.

artifacts.name: Project, Application and Proportionality Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: Risk assessments performed at defined decision points: the project security risk assessment template and completed assessments at initiation, application-level risk assessments driving security requirement selection, requirements risk assessments, operational risk assessments embedded in SDLC phases, privacy risk assessments for AI systems including data-minimisation and PETs, and the proportionality analysis (entity size, risk exposure, incident likelihood and severity, justification that the chosen measures are appropriate) required by NIS2.

artifacts.name: Project and Programme Governance Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that in-scope initiatives are actually governed through the methodology: programme and project charters with business cases and authorisation, project plans with scope, milestones, deliverables, timelines and resource allocation, status reports and benefits-realisation tracking, the project portfolio tracker showing security assessment status and outstanding actions per project, and sample project artefacts from each lifecycle phase of a real project.

artifacts.name: Technology Selection, Procurement and Third-Party Requirement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that security, compliance and resilience requirements are imposed before acquisition: the technology selection criteria framework and evaluation reports scoring candidates, signed selection decision records with rationale and TCO analysis, feasibility studies and solution option analyses, the procurement policy with RFP/ITT and BRD templates and their approval, issued RFP/ITT documents showing functional, operational and regulatory requirements, public procurement compliance records where applicable, security evaluations of acquired COTS/SaaS software, outsourcing agreements carrying security requirements with supporting third-party audit reports and provider assessments, and counterparty relationship authorisation and change records where required.

artifacts.name: Security Testing and Assurance Results
artifacts.description: Evidence that defined requirements are verified before and after deployment: the security testing policy defining test types (vulnerability assessment, penetration test, code review, configuration assessment), frequency and ownership; the annual testing calendar; QA and security test plans and results with defect tracking; vulnerability assessment and penetration test reports; security evaluation records at each SDLC phase; continuous monitoring and internal audit coverage of the lifecycle; and the remediation tracker following findings to closure. Scanner output can be collected automatically; test reports and remediation sign-off are manual.

artifacts.name: Stakeholder and Business Requirements Engagement Records
artifacts.description: Records showing whose requirements drive the definition: the interested-parties register with each party's requirements and how they are addressed, stakeholder requirements mapping to processes and controls, consultation, survey and meeting records used to elicit requirements, the organisational context analysis (internal/external issues, PESTLE, role determination relative to each system), business relationship management framework, IT-business alignment meeting minutes and actions, and service level agreements with satisfaction reporting.

artifacts.name: Governance Roles, RACI and Management Reporting
artifacts.description: Documentation of who is accountable for defining and approving requirements: organisational structure charts with technology roles, RACI matrices for the governing processes, project role and deliverable matrices, capability maturity assessments with improvement plans, internal communication procedures and reporting channels (including anonymous reporting), and board or management reporting packs covering the internal control and security position of the technology portfolio.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Training and Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Training and awareness records evidencing that developers, project managers and requirement owners understand the secure SDLC and security requirements obligations — attendee lists, delivery dates, module references and completion status, with effectiveness assessment where required.

artifacts.name: System Decommissioning and Retirement Records
artifacts.description: The decommissioning procedure and checklist applied at end of life, with completed records per retired asset confirming data retrieval or destruction, removal of access and dependencies, and sign-off that the retirement was executed as designed.

PRM-05.notes: 130 entries collapse to 13 artifacts. The two largest duplicate groups are the secure SDLC / project lifecycle methodology (19 entries across nine frameworks) and technology acquisition/procurement evidence (19 entries). No automated checks exist for this control, so only the inventory and testing artifacts are hybrid.

artifacts.name: Business Process and Mission Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented mission and business processes with the security considerations embedded in them and the risk impact analysis behind each, giving the definition against which controls are placed.

artifacts.name: Business Requirements and Traceability
artifacts.description: The business requirements documentation with prioritisation records, the traceability matrices linking requirement to solution, the feasibility study reports and solution option analyses, the requirements risk assessment, and the sign-off and approval records. MAS TRM requires non-functional requirements covering performance, resilience and security to be specified alongside the functional set.

artifacts.name: Programme and Project Management Records
artifacts.description: The programme management methodology and standards, programme charters with business cases and authorisation records, plans with milestones, timelines and resource allocations, status reports with benefits realisation tracking, sample project plans with scope and deliverables, and the documented project roles and responsibilities.

artifacts.name: Solution Design and Build Records
artifacts.description: The development standards and quality assurance test plans, high-level and detailed solution design documents, the procurement and build approval documentation, and the test results and defect tracking records.

artifacts.name: Capacity and Availability Management
artifacts.description: The availability and capacity management plans, the business impact analysis establishing availability requirements, capacity forecasting and planning documentation, and the performance baseline measurements with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: IT Management Framework and Structure
artifacts.description: The IT management framework documentation and policies, organisational structure charts with IT roles, RACI matrices for IT processes, capability maturity assessments with improvement plans, the business relationship management framework, IT-business alignment meeting minutes with action items, and the service level agreements with customer satisfaction reports.

artifacts.name: Organisational Roles and Segregation Evidence
artifacts.description: The organisation chart with reporting lines, job descriptions with defined authorities and responsibilities, the RACI matrix for key security functions, and the segregation of duties matrix with its analysis.

artifacts.name: Objectives, Risk Tolerance and Compliance Inventory
artifacts.description: The documented security and operational objectives with the methodology by which they were set, the risk tolerance statements, and the inventory of compliance requirements the processes must satisfy.

artifacts.name: Control Design and Risk Mapping
artifacts.description: The control activities inventory mapped to the risks they address, the control design documentation, the risk-control mapping matrix, the IT general controls framework, the security management process documentation, the technology infrastructure control inventory, and the acquisition and development lifecycle controls.

artifacts.name: Change Impact and Environmental Scanning
artifacts.description: The management of change procedures for significant organisational changes, the business model change impact assessments, the change management risk assessment process, and the environmental scanning and threat intelligence reports that trigger them.

artifacts.name: ICT Asset Register and Dependency Mapping
artifacts.description: The ICT asset register with asset classification, the mapping of business functions to the ICT assets that support them, and the dependency mapping showing what each function relies on.

artifacts.name: AI System Context and Scope Records
artifacts.description: The documented analysis of external and internal issues relevant to the AI management system, the PESTLE or equivalent worksheet behind it, the record determining the organisation's role for each AI system, the inventory of AI systems with intended purpose, the context documentation, AI impact assessments, defined AI risk metrics with methodology, and the TEVV test plans.

artifacts.name: Interested Parties and Communication Records
artifacts.description: The register of interested parties with their requirements and how each is addressed, the stakeholder engagement records used to elicit them, the requirements mapping to processes and controls, the communication plan specifying what, when, with whom and how, the communication schedule, and sample executed communications.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Evidence
artifacts.description: The data processing specifications and documentation, input validation and output reconciliation procedures, processing accuracy monitoring reports, and the data quality metrics and dashboards.

artifacts.name: Asset Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The decommissioning procedures and checklist, and the data retrieval or destruction confirmation showing the process was completed for each retired asset.

artifacts.name: Correspondent Relationship Management Records
artifacts.description: The correspondent authorisation documentation, the relationship management change logs, and the periodic review records over the authorised relationship set.

artifacts.name: Document Workflow Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The documented workflow prioritisation specification with its implementing procedures and process workflows, the implementation evidence, the register with a named owner, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Independent Assurance over Processes
artifacts.description: The internal audit plan and schedule, continuous monitoring programme documentation, security control testing results, and penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports that test whether the defined processes operate as designed.

PRM-06.notes: 98 asks across 10 frameworks. COBIT contributes four separate process areas (programme management, requirements, solution build, capacity) that all land here; they are kept as distinct artifacts because each is a different lifecycle stage with a different owner.

artifacts.name: Secure SDLC Policy and Framework
artifacts.description: The approved secure development lifecycle framework used for new initiatives and significant changes: the phases, the security and privacy activities and gates in each, the deliverables required to exit each phase, the roles accountable, and the development standards mandated. Must show that security and privacy considerations are built in by default rather than bolted on, and must cover both in-house and acquired technology. SOC 2 frames the same artefact as the IT general controls covering technology acquisition and development; CSA CCM expects records that it operates in the cloud environment; PISF 2026 expects implementation evidence alongside the defined requirements.

artifacts.name: Change Management Policy and Procedure
artifacts.description: Approved policy and the procedure beneath it defining change categories and their approval paths, how a change is requested, risk-assessed, approved, tested, implemented, verified and closed, the documentation required at each step, and the segregation between who requests, approves and implements. Must explicitly cover changes to applications, technology assets and services within the development lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Change Request, Approval and CAB Records
artifacts.description: Populated change records for the period showing the full lifecycle of representative changes: the request, the assessment, the named approver and approval date, implementation and verification, and closure. Include Change Advisory Board minutes evidencing review and approval of scheduled changes. Sampled from the change and source control platforms in use so that ticket, approval and merge evidence tie together for the same change.

artifacts.name: Emergency Change, Post-Implementation Review and Adoption Records
artifacts.description: The log of emergency or expedited changes for the period with the retrospective approval and post-implementation review for each, plus the effectiveness evidence for changes generally: change success and failed change metrics with analysis of failures, and for business-impacting changes the readiness assessment, communication plan, stakeholder engagement records and post-change adoption metrics.

artifacts.name: Rollback and Failure Management Plans
artifacts.description: Documented back-out or rollback plans for significant changes, stating the trigger conditions, the steps, the owner and the recovery point. For AI and continuously-updated systems, the wider failure management plan covering rollback, feature toggling, the update process, user and customer notification, and how updated failure information is captured.

artifacts.name: Change Impact and Security Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The assessment performed before a change or project is approved: the impact analysis including security and privacy considerations, the threat and risk assessment for the system, and the security requirements derived from it. Must show the risk assessment template or methodology used at initiation and completed instances for real changes. NIS2 additionally requires the proportionality justification, documenting entity size and risk exposure and why the measures chosen are appropriate given incident likelihood and severity.

artifacts.name: System Design Documents, Security Architecture and Threat Models
artifacts.description: The design-stage record for systems and significant changes: high-level and detailed design documents describing architecture, components, data flows and functions; the security architecture and the secure design principles applied; the threat models produced during design; and the security engineering review records. For AI systems, the architecture and data-flow diagrams documenting the components and data of each system.

artifacts.name: Requirements Specification and Traceability Matrix
artifacts.description: Documented business, technical and security requirements for each initiative with the rationale behind them (business case, customer request, regulatory driver), the feasibility or option analysis where solutions were compared, the formal requirements sign-off, and the traceability matrix linking each requirement through design, development, testing and deployment. ISO 42001 additionally requires training and data requirements to be specified for AI systems.

artifacts.name: Project Governance and Phase Security Sign-Off Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that projects are governed and that security signs off at each phase: the project or programme management methodology showing where security checkpoints and gate criteria sit, programme charters, business cases and authorisation records, project plans with milestones, deliverables and resource allocation, defined project roles and responsibilities including named security and privacy accountabilities, the security sign-off record for each SDLC phase, the release security gate approvals, and the portfolio-level tracker showing security assessment status and open actions across active projects. Includes programme status and benefits realisation reporting.

artifacts.name: Pre-Release Test, Quality Assurance and Defect Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that changes are validated before release: the quality management standards and metrics, the project quality plan, the QA test plans, the executed test results, and the defect tracking records with resolution status. Must demonstrate that the change was tested and validated prior to implementation and that outstanding defects were dispositioned before approval to deploy.

artifacts.name: Code Review and CI/CD Security Gate Evidence
artifacts.description: The pipeline configuration showing security scanning (SAST, DAST, SCA) embedded in the build with enforced pass conditions, together with code review records for merged changes showing an independent reviewer approved before merge. Collectable from the source control and scanning platforms already integrated.

artifacts.name: Developer Secure Coding Training Records
artifacts.description: Completion records for secure coding training taken by developers, showing individual, module, date and completion status, evidencing that the people executing the lifecycle are competent to meet its security requirements.

artifacts.name: AI System Lifecycle Documentation and Event Logging
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are in scope, the lifecycle documentation set: the technical documentation pack covering general description, intended purpose, usage instructions, technical assumptions and limitations, monitoring capabilities, design and architecture, development data and data quality assumptions, risk management activities and verification/validation results; documentation of operations personnel roles, accountability for handling failures and updates, and the management approvals; the event logging standard covering the lifecycle phases (as a minimum, in-use) with sample logs and the retention policy aligned to intended use and legal requirements; the concerns reporting procedure with confidential channels, investigation powers, escalation and protection from reprisal, plus the register of reported concerns and their resolution; and the periodic review, implementation and management oversight records showing the deployed system continues to deliver value and remains effective over time.

artifacts.name: Decommissioning and Phase-Out Procedure and Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure and checklist for retiring systems, components and services, and the completed records for decommissioning events: data retrieval or destruction confirmation, safe phase-out execution with date and performer, asset disposal records, and for AI systems the context documentation and safety evaluation (fail-safe behaviour, residual risk, monitoring) supporting the retirement decision.

artifacts.name: Technology Asset, Environment and Capacity Register
artifacts.description: The inventory underpinning lifecycle control: the IT asset register with lifecycle status and owner, identification of critical assets and their protection measures, software licence records, and for AI systems the inventory of components, data, tooling, computing and human resources per lifecycle stage with the availability assessment. Includes the availability and capacity management plans, performance baselines and monitoring reports, capacity forecasts, and the business impact analysis behind the availability requirements, which govern how pre-production and production environments are sized and protected.

PRM-07.notes: 108 manual entries across 12 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts. Nine evidence collectors are already wired (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, Render, Vercel, Semgrep, SonarCloud), so change tickets/approvals, code review and pipeline gates, and test/defect records are marked automated or hybrid accordingly. ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF contribute an AI-specific documentation and decommissioning strand that is kept separate because it only applies where AI systems are in scope. COBIT BAI01-BAI09 spreads across project governance, requirements, capacity and asset lifecycle rather than change control proper.

artifacts.name: Risk Management Framework and Programme Documentation
artifacts.description: The approved enterprise or ICT risk management framework and the risk management programme documentation implementing it - runbook or playbook level, showing how strategic, operational and tactical risk controls actually run. Must cover the risk taxonomy including technology and cyber risk, how the ICT/technology risk framework integrates with the overall enterprise risk management system, and the procedure by which technology risks are aggregated and reported into the ERM function. DORA permits a simplified framework for entities meeting the proportionality conditions and requires the comprehensive framework otherwise; MAS TRM and SBP require the framework to be board-approved with evidence of implementation across the organisation; SBP Cloud requires the ERM framework updated to cover cloud outsourcing risk including sub-contracting and location risk, with the management or board approval record. Include the risk assessment policy and procedures (NIST 800-53) and the policy/standard/procedure register (QCB).

artifacts.name: Risk Management and Operational Resilience Strategy
artifacts.description: The board-approved technology risk management strategy and the digital operational resilience strategy, showing how risk management aligns with strategic, operational and budgetary planning. Must set out ICT security objectives and how they align to risk appetite, the inventory of ICT security policies, protocols and procedures supporting the strategy, the multi-vendor strategy and key dependency mapping (DORA), the operational resilience strategy covering response to wide-scale disruption, cyber attack and critical infrastructure failure (SBP ETGRMF), and progress reports evidencing the strategy is being implemented rather than merely published.

artifacts.name: Risk Appetite and Tolerance Statement
artifacts.description: The documented, approved risk appetite and tolerance statement setting the thresholds against which risks are accepted, escalated or treated, together with the security and operational objectives it supports and the methodology used to set those objectives. ISO 42001 requires AI-specific risk criteria covering acceptance thresholds and assessment, treatment and impact-assessment criteria; NIST AI RMF requires the organisational AI risk tolerance statement with its approval records; COBIT requires enterprise-level appetite and tolerance statements.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented methodology for identifying, analysing, evaluating and prioritising risk: the identification approach, the analysis basis (consequences to the organisation, to individuals and to society for AI risk under ISO 42001), likelihood and impact scales, the severity rating system and how ratings drive remediation priority (CIS CSC), and the evaluation criteria for treatment decisions. HITRUST requires the methodology documentation with its approval records; ISO 42001 additionally requires evidence that repeated assessments produce consistent, valid and comparable results (calibration sessions or inter-rater checks).

artifacts.name: Risk Register
artifacts.description: The master risk register covering information security, technology and (where applicable) AI risks, with per-entry risk ID and description, owner, inherent and residual ratings, treatment status and link to the treatment plan. Must map risks to the enterprise risk categories and cover security, reliability, resiliency and interoperability dimensions (SBP ETGRMF), record opportunities alongside risks with planned actions and their effectiveness measures (ISO 42001), and include cloud service locations with risk ratings, onsite-audit feasibility and approval status (SBP Cloud). Include the log of actions taken to identify and address the entries.

artifacts.name: Completed Risk Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The executed risk assessment reports for the period, per system or per domain, showing consequence analysis, likelihood, resulting risk level and prioritisation for treatment. Must include the periodic information security risk assessment reports (SBP ETGRMF), risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact (COBIT), the GDPR-required assessments of risk to personal data, the jurisdictional risk assessment for each offshore cloud service location covering legal, regulatory, availability, security and connectivity risk (SBP Cloud), and the AI risk assessment reports per AI system (ISO 42001).

artifacts.name: Risk Treatment Plans and Residual Risk Acceptance
artifacts.description: The documented treatment process and the resulting plans: selected treatment option per risk, the controls determined necessary, owner, deadline, target residual risk, and the management approval accepting residual risk. ISO 42001 requires the Statement of Applicability listing all necessary controls with justification for inclusion and exclusion, comparison against Annex A, and records of communicating the necessary controls internally and to interested parties. NIS2 requires the treatment plan with prioritised actions; SOC 2 requires treatment plans specifically for identified business disruption risks; COBIT requires the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Risk Governance Roles and Committee Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of an established risk executive function that views risk organisation-wide: the appointment of the senior position accountable for risk management, the RACI or roles-and-responsibilities matrix defining risk management roles, responsibilities and communication lines, the charters for the IT strategy, IT steering and technology risk committees, and the minutes of those committees showing risk decisions and escalations. Include the board technology committee minutes evidencing oversight of resilience risk strategies (SBP ETGRMF) and the approved policies and procedures supporting defined risk management activity levels (NIST AI RMF).

artifacts.name: Risk Monitoring, Reporting and Framework Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the programme is reviewed and reported on at the defined frequency and after significant change. Must include: the schedule defining review intervals and the triggers for out-of-cycle review, the framework and strategy review records themselves, post-incident framework reviews, the annual framework review report and any regulatory submission of it (DORA requires submission to the competent authority), improvement action tracking, risk monitoring dashboards and trend reports, cybersecurity KPI metrics, consolidated risk reports tabled at the board showing technology risk within the enterprise view, management body briefing records on programme effectiveness (NIS2), and the continuous monitoring programme documentation (SOC 2). Cadence differs: DORA and NIS2 require at least annual review; NIST AI RMF requires ongoing monitoring with defined frequency and roles.

artifacts.name: Control Inventory and Risk-Control Mapping
artifacts.description: The inventory of control activities mapped to the risks they mitigate, the risk-control mapping matrix, control design documentation, the segregation of duties matrix with its analysis, the internal audit plan and schedule, and the security control testing results and reports. Required by SOC 2 as the evidence that identified risks are actually covered by designed and operating controls.

artifacts.name: Independent Assurance and Resilience Test Reports
artifacts.description: Third-party and independent testing results feeding the risk picture: independent audit review reports, security audit reports and findings, penetration test and vulnerability assessment reports, cyber-attack scenario test results, switchover and failover test documentation, and resilience scenario testing covering wide-scale disruption and multi-sector attack simulations. HITRUST additionally counts secure SDLC documentation with security checkpoints and the associated code review and security testing results as assurance evidence for this control.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery and Crisis Response Plans
artifacts.description: The ICT disaster recovery plans, business continuity plans, and the cyber crisis response plan for simulating and handling extreme disruption scenarios, together with the business disruption risk assessment and its mitigation plans, documentation of the quick-response capability, and the cyber insurance policy documentation where risk is transferred rather than treated.

artifacts.name: Physical and Environmental Risk Assessment and Controls
artifacts.description: For existing facilities, evidence that physical and environmental hazards are considered in the risk management strategy: the environmental threat risk assessment covering fire, flood, earthquake, power failure and civil unrest for each site, fire detection and suppression commissioning and annual inspection certificates, fire drill records with attendance and evaluation, building management system configuration for temperature, humidity, leak and smoke monitoring, flood protection documentation for at-risk or below-ground facilities, the log of environmental events and the response to each, insurance certificates covering environmental risk, and the physical infrastructure protection measures and asset protection tooling inventory required by DORA.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain and Third-Party Risk Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that supply chain risk is enforced through the programme: the supply chain security policy, supplier risk assessment records, the security requirements imposed contractually on suppliers, and the supplier security monitoring and audit reports that verify them. SBP Cloud additionally requires a documented alternate assurance mechanism for cloud locations where onsite assessment by the entity, the regulator or external audit is impractical.

artifacts.name: Compliance Obligations Inventory and Security Measures Evidence
artifacts.description: The inventory of legal, regulatory and contractual compliance requirements the risk programme must satisfy, together with the documented security measures implemented against them - encryption implementation and its risk management, access controls, and the documentation supporting the appropriateness of the measures chosen. GDPR requires the security measures documentation as the demonstration of appropriate technical and organisational measures; DORA requires the proportionality assessment and risk management measures documentation; CIS CSC requires the vulnerability prioritisation records showing risk ratings drive remediation order.

RSK-01.notes: 141 entries from 16 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts, all assigned exactly once. No automated collectors are listed and this is fundamentally documentary evidence, so most artifacts are manual; the risk register, control testing results, penetration test reports and environmental monitoring are marked hybrid because a GRC tool or connector holds part of them. Physical/environmental risk (ISO 27001, DORA) and supply chain risk (NIS2, SBP Cloud) are kept separate from the core risk artifacts because they are collected by different owners.

artifacts.name: Risk Management Framework
artifacts.description: The approved technology risk management framework, the risk management policy and framework, the risk assessment methodology and framework, the roles and responsibilities matrix, and the plan update history evidencing the framework is maintained.

artifacts.name: Risk Tolerance Statement
artifacts.description: The risk tolerance statements, the documented organisational risk tolerance statement with its approval records, the approved organisational policies and procedures setting it, and the periodic review records confirming it remains current.

artifacts.name: Risk Register
artifacts.description: The risk register with identified risks, likelihood and impact; the technology risk register; the risk register with its assessments and treatment plans; the annual risk assessment reports; the risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact assessments; the risk assessment reports; the risk register updates; and the threat landscape analysis reports and threat scenario documentation feeding it.

artifacts.name: Risk Treatment Records
artifacts.description: The risk treatment plans with their risk response decisions and the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Targeted Risk Analysis Library
artifacts.description: The library of targeted risk analyses for each requirement that specifies one, the documented methodology covering identification of assets, threats, impacted controls and the factors leading to likelihood and impact, the tracker of all analyses with last-review and next-review dates, and the management review and acceptance records for each.

artifacts.name: Customised Approach Risk Analyses
artifacts.description: The inventory of requirements met using the customised approach, the targeted risk analysis document for each with its reasoning, and the management review and approval records per analysis.

artifacts.name: AI Impact Assessment Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for AI system impact assessments covering deployment, intended use, foreseeable misuse and the technical context; the completed reports per AI system with consequences to individuals, groups and society; the schedule of assessments with planned intervals and change-driven triggers; the repository of executed results; the evidence that results feed into the AI risk assessment process; and, where appropriate, the records demonstrating results have been made available to relevant interested parties.

artifacts.name: Project Risk Framing Records
artifacts.description: The project management methodology explicitly integrating security checkpoints and gate criteria, the template used at project initiation to assess information security risks, the portfolio security tracker with outstanding actions, the gate review sign-offs, and a redacted charter from a real project showing security objectives and owners captured upfront.

artifacts.name: Remediation Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The remediation priority guidelines, the severity rating system documentation, and the vulnerability prioritisation records applying the framing to fix order. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remediation of audit findings and encryption risk management requirements.

RSK-01.1.notes: 50 asks across 11 frameworks. Risk framing is the statement of tolerance and scope that precedes assessment; PCI DSS's targeted and customised-approach analyses and ISO 42001's AI impact assessment are separate framing instruments and stay apart.

artifacts.name: Risk Appetite and Tolerance Statement
artifacts.description: The board-approved risk appetite and tolerance statement for information security, the documented organisational risk tolerance statement with its approval records, the risk tolerance statements, and the approved organisational policies and procedures setting them.

artifacts.name: Residual Risk Tracking
artifacts.description: The residual risk tracker measured against the tolerance levels post-treatment, the residual risk assessment documentation, and the risk acceptance approvals from management for what sits above tolerance.

artifacts.name: Risk Treatment Records
artifacts.description: The treatment plans for identified risks aligned with asset value and risk tolerance, the risk treatment plans with their risk response decisions, the risk treatment plans, and the evidence of treatment control implementation through technical configurations and process artifacts.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment and Register
artifacts.description: The risk assessment methodology and framework, the risk assessment methodology documentation with its approval records, the annual risk assessment reports, the risk assessment reports, the risk register with identified risks, likelihood and impact, the risk register with entries, owners, ratings and treatment plans, the risk register updates, and the threat scenario documentation. HITRUST requires the approved risk management programme development policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Tolerance Records
artifacts.description: The AI impact assessment, the incident response plan with the AI incident or error register, the documented evidence demonstrating each governance and mapping outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing them within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Development Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The secure development lifecycle documentation with its security checkpoints and the code review records with their security testing results.

RSK-01.3.notes: 33 asks across 6 frameworks. Overlaps RSK-01.1; what is distinct here is the tolerance statement itself and the residual risk measured against it, kept separate from the framework that produces the numbers.

artifacts.name: Categorisation Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented methodology for assessing and classifying asset criticality, the asset criticality criteria, the framework classifying assets by severity into criticality tiers, the guidance operationalising confidentiality, integrity and availability-based classification, the approved classification policy defining the tier criteria, the methodology used to derive classifications including importance, threat and vulnerability factors, the security categorisation documentation, the categorisation analysis, the information asset protection policy, and the formal policy specifying the criticality assessment methodology and protection planning.

artifacts.name: Categorised Asset Register
artifacts.description: The register of information system assets with criticality ratings and justifications, the inventory of critical infrastructure assets with assigned criticality levels, the register classifying each sensitive system, payment data set and application by tier, the mapping of assets to impact levels, the per-asset threat and vulnerability matrix, and the system categorisation approval.

artifacts.name: Protection Plans by Criticality
artifacts.description: The differentiated protection plans mapped to each criticality tier, evidencing the categorisation changes what is done rather than only what is recorded.

artifacts.name: Classification Review Records
artifacts.description: The records of periodic review and re-classification by data and system owners and the documented data classification review specification with its compliance evidence and implementing procedures and process workflows.

artifacts.name: Media Classification Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for classifying all media holding regulated data according to sensitivity, the register of media items with their classification labels, and the sample photographs of physical media with the labelling applied.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The annual risk assessment reports, the risk assessment methodology and framework, the risk register with identified risks, likelihood and impact, and the risk treatment plans with their risk response decisions. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented risk assessment and impact analysis requirement.

artifacts.name: Remediation Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The remediation priority guidelines, the severity rating system documentation, and the vulnerability prioritisation records applying the categorisation to fix order.

artifacts.name: Data Register and Impact Records
artifacts.description: The documented data register and impact assessment specifications with their compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing them, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the register or inventory evidencing the data register with a named owner, the compliance audit reports and assessment records, the formal approval and socialisation records, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability.

RSK-02.notes: 45 asks across 10 frameworks. Overlaps RSK-02.1; here the object is the categorisation scheme and its application to assets, with the differentiated protection plans it drives kept as their own artifact.

artifacts.name: Asset Criticality Classification Scheme
artifacts.description: The framework classifying assets by severity into criticality tiers, the documented criteria for asset prioritisation based on operational sensitivity, the documented methodology for identifying and prioritising critical information system assets, the approved classification policy defining the criteria for sensitive systems, payment data and applications, the methodology used to derive classifications including importance, threat and vulnerability factors, the service provider classification criteria and risk tier documentation, the security categorisation documentation, the categorisation analysis, and the board-approved security management framework containing the prioritisation component.

artifacts.name: Classified Asset Register
artifacts.description: The enterprise information asset inventory classified by criticality with owner, confidentiality-integrity-availability rating and location; the inventory of critical infrastructure assets with assigned criticality levels; the register classifying each sensitive system, payment data set and application by tier with threat factors; the prioritised asset list with operational sensitivity ratings; the application risk classification; the classification records; and the system categorisation approval.

artifacts.name: Classification Review Records
artifacts.description: The log evidencing periodic reviews and updates to the critical asset register, the records of periodic review and re-classification by data and system owners, and the records of periodic priority reviews.

artifacts.name: Impact Analysis Records
artifacts.description: The impact analysis reports, the risk scoring records, the risk heat map or matrix, the inputs from incidents, audits and regulatory observations feeding the ratings, and the risk-rated audit cycle plan derived from them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented risk assessment and impact analysis requirement.

artifacts.name: Disruption Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The matrix prioritising potential business disruptions by severity, the documented severity rating criteria applied to them, the risk ranking methodology and outcomes, and the continuity documentation reflecting the prioritised disruption scenarios.

artifacts.name: Control Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The risk and criticality-based control implementation plan with its management or regulator approval and the records prioritising resources to the assets critical to essential services.

artifacts.name: Remediation Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The remediation priority guidelines, the severity rating system documentation, and the vulnerability prioritisation records applying the asset criticality to fix order. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remediation of audit findings requirement.

artifacts.name: Maintenance Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The approved preventive maintenance plan listing prioritised assets, the list of assets included with their prioritisation rationale, the cost-effectiveness analysis behind the selection, the management approval of the plan, and the monitoring reports showing asset performance against operational goals.

artifacts.name: Encryption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The documented encryption risk management with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered, applying the criticality rating to cryptographic protection decisions. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Data Impact Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The documented impact assessment specification with its compliance evidence, the data classification scheme and labelled dataset register, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the compliance audit reports and assessment records.

artifacts.name: AI Impact Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The AI impact assessment, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the risk treatment plan with its prioritisation, the incident response plan with the incident or error register, the stakeholder engagement and feedback log, the documented evidence demonstrating the outcomes, and the periodic review records.

RSK-02.1.notes: 56 asks across 9 frameworks. The classification scheme, the classified inventory and what the classification then drives are three proofs; SBP ETGRMF's preventive maintenance prioritisation is a genuinely different consequence of the same rating and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented methodology covering asset and threat identification, likelihood and impact factors, and rating scales, with the risk management policy and framework behind it and the management review and approval of the methodology.

artifacts.name: Risk Register
artifacts.description: The risk register with identified risks, likelihood, impact and treatment plans, the technology risk register, the completed risk assessment reports, and the register update records evidencing it is maintained rather than written once.

artifacts.name: Threat and Vulnerability Register
artifacts.description: The register mapping identified threats to vulnerabilities with risk rating, the documented threat analysis methodology, the prioritised list of risks that may cause severe harm with impact assessment, the review log for that list, the threat scenario documentation, and the threat landscape analysis reports.

artifacts.name: Threat-to-Asset Mapping
