artifacts.description: The threat assessment report covering the assets in scope, the matrix mapping each identified threat or vulnerability to the affected assets, the vulnerability assessment report supporting it, and the threat intelligence feed subscriptions feeding the assessment.

artifacts.name: Targeted Risk Analysis Library
artifacts.description: The library of targeted risk analyses for each requirement that specifies one, the documented methodology covering assets, threats, impacted controls and the factors leading to likelihood and impact, the tracker with last and next review dates, and the management review and acceptance records for each.

artifacts.name: Customised Approach Risk Analyses
artifacts.description: The inventory of requirements met using the customised approach, the targeted risk analysis document for each with the reasoning, and the management review and approval records per analysis.

artifacts.name: Fraud Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The documented assessment of identity theft and identity fraud risks specific to the channel — account takeover, subscriber-identity swap, phishing, social engineering, synthetic identity, mule accounts and document forgery — with the treatment plan listing controls implemented or planned and the periodic loss statistics with trends and lessons learned.

artifacts.name: Gap Analysis and Remediation Roadmap
artifacts.description: The periodic gap analysis reports with the risk categorisation applied, and the remediation roadmap addressing the gaps identified.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance documentation informed by them.

artifacts.name: Availability and Environmental Risk Records
artifacts.description: The backup policy, schedule and completion logs; the restoration test results; the disaster recovery plan and procedures; and the environmental monitoring configuration covering temperature, humidity and fire suppression — the operational risks the assessment must consider.

artifacts.name: Detection and Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The security information platform monitoring and alerting evidence, the anomaly detection tool configuration and tuning records, the alert triage and escalation procedures, and the security operations procedures through which emerging risk is identified.

artifacts.name: Project Risk Identification Records
artifacts.description: The project management methodology integrating security checkpoints, the security risk assessment template used at initiation, the portfolio security tracker with outstanding actions, the gate review sign-offs, and a sample project charter showing security objectives captured upfront.

artifacts.name: Encryption Risk Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented encryption risk management with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Identification Records
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures, the incident response plan with the incident or error register, the documented evidence of the outcome, and the periodic review records covering AI risk identification.

RSK-03.notes: 66 asks across 13 frameworks. PCI DSS 12.3.1 and 12.3.2 contribute two named instruments — the targeted risk analysis and the customised-approach analysis — that are separate from the general risk register and are tested with their own evidence.

artifacts.name: Risk Management Policy & Risk Assessment Methodology
artifacts.description: The approved risk management policy plus the documented methodology: scope, asset and threat sources considered, likelihood and impact scales, scoring/aggregation rules, risk acceptance criteria and the definition of the assessment cadence. Must be repeatable — ISO 42001 asks for evidence that the same inputs yield consistent results; HITRUST 03.b asks for both the methodology and its approval record.

artifacts.name: Cybersecurity & Technology Risk Assessment Report
artifacts.description: The completed recurring risk assessment covering the in-scope technology assets, applications, services and data, stating for each identified risk the threat, vulnerability, likelihood, magnitude of harm and resulting rating, with quantified or scored prioritisation. HIPAA requires it to cover every system that creates, receives, maintains or transmits ePHI; DORA requires cyber-threat scenarios; SBP expects an executive summary and board-visible version. Report must be dated and approved.

artifacts.name: Risk Register with Treatment Plans & Remediation Tracking
artifacts.description: The live risk register: each risk with owner, inherent and residual rating, chosen treatment, the treatment/remediation plan with target dates, and the tracker showing progress and closure. Must include the risk-prioritised control plan and mapped controls (including risks retained where a service is outsourced), and evidence that management reviews and accepts residual risk.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Schedule, Review & Results Dissemination Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of cadence and communication: the defined assessment frequency and schedule, records of each scheduled and ad-hoc execution with the trigger that prompted it, management review minutes, and proof the results reached the defined roles — dissemination lists, risk dashboards and metrics, and awareness communications. Cadence differs by framework: annual review and update is the common floor (DORA, SBP Internet Banking, NIST 800-53), with event-driven reassessment on significant change or breach.

artifacts.name: Threat & Vulnerability Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The technical inputs to risk: vulnerability scan and assessment reports across the defined scope, threat assessments and the threat-to-asset mapping, current threat-intelligence feed subscriptions and how their output is consumed, and periodic threat-landscape reviews. SBP ETGRMF expects an annual vulnerability identification plan with a scope register; DoH ADHIE expects scan results tied to a remediation action plan.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Scope Statement & Asset Inventory
artifacts.description: The documented scope of the assessment and the asset population it covers: the scope statement listing the elements in scope, the asset inventory with named owners (including ePHI-holding systems and end-user-developed applications), and the vulnerability assessment scope register showing nothing in scope was silently excluded.

artifacts.name: AI Risk & Impact Assessment Records
artifacts.description: For AI systems: the AI risk assessment methodology and completed assessments, the AI risk register, and impact assessments on individuals, groups and society — covering environmental sustainability, potential misuse and historical bias — with expert consultation records, the results repository and its retention rule, and the RACI defining who owns AI risk decisions.

artifacts.name: Physical & Environmental Threat and Vulnerability Assessment
artifacts.description: Site and data-centre threat/vulnerability risk assessment (TVRA) covering fire, flood, power, climate and perimeter/surrounding threats, with the supporting evidence of the mitigations assessed: fire detection and suppression certificates, drill records, environmental monitoring configuration, flood protection measures, the environmental incident log, insurance coverage, and effectiveness reviews of the physical controls.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis & Continuity Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The BIA identifying critical processes with their RTO/RPO targets, the continuity risk assessment, and the dependency analysis behind it: resource requirements, ICT dependencies and the critical supplier/partner register. HITRUST 12.b additionally requires the business continuity plan carrying those targets and its test and post-test review records.

artifacts.name: Backup & Disaster Recovery Test Evidence
artifacts.description: Backup policy and schedule with completion logs, backup configuration and access controls, and restoration/recovery test results proving the recovery targets used in the risk assessment are achievable. SWIFT CSCF 7.4 requires verification logs alongside the test results.

artifacts.name: Incident Analysis & Post-Incident Risk Review Records
artifacts.description: Incident response plan and classification/prioritisation criteria, incident investigation and analysis reports, post-incident review and lessons-learned records, and the root cause analysis performed after a breach — with the resulting feedback into the risk assessment and register.

artifacts.name: Targeted & Customized Approach Risk Analyses (PCI DSS)
artifacts.description: The library of PCI DSS targeted risk analyses justifying each organization-defined frequency, plus the risk analyses supporting any customized-approach implementations with the inventory of controls using that approach, the documented methodology, and dated management approval and review records.

artifacts.name: Project & System Change Security Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: Evidence that risk is assessed for new projects and changes, not only periodically: the project methodology with security gates, the project risk assessment template and completed examples, sample project charters carrying security requirements, security sign-off records and the portfolio tracker showing coverage.

artifacts.name: Channel, Cloud & Network Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: Scoped risk assessments for specific delivery channels and platforms: per-channel fraud vulnerability assessments (internet, mobile, corporate/institutional banking) with the counter-fraud measures adopted, the cloud risk register with controls retained despite outsourcing, trusted-connectivity and cascading-risk evaluations, virtualization risk assessments, network component assessments, and encryption/key risk management records.

artifacts.name: Legal & Regulatory Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment of legal and regulatory exposure feeding the risk process: the annual legal-risk impact assessment with board approval of remedial actions, and the legal-environment assessment addressing specific statutory exposures (documentation and proof, burden of proof, liability, secrecy and privacy) with legal function sign-off.

RSK-04.notes: 158 entries reduce to 15. Most sources restate one thing: methodology, report, register, cadence. The connectors available (GuardDuty, ServiceNow, Opsgenie, DigitalOcean/Neon/Qovery) cover threat detection, incident records and backup state, so those clusters are hybrid; the assessments and their approval remain human work.

artifacts.name: Risk Register
artifacts.description: The technology risk register prioritising and closely monitoring high-risk activities, the risk register with its assessments and treatment plans, the risk register with risk ratings and mitigation plans, the technology risk register with identified risks, the risk register, and the risk heat map or matrix drawn from it.

artifacts.name: Register Maintenance Records
artifacts.description: The log evidencing periodic risk register updates, the periodic update evidence, the documented procedure for continuous risk assessment and treatment, and the inputs from incidents, audits and regulatory observations feeding those updates.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Methodology
artifacts.description: The technology risk assessment methodology, the completed risk assessment report, the risk management policy and framework, the risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact assessments, and the risk assessment review and approval by management.

artifacts.name: Residual Risk Register
artifacts.description: The residual risk register and the risk treatment plan with its prioritisation, recording what remains after treatment.

artifacts.name: Mitigation Tracking Records
artifacts.description: The mitigation action progress reports, the regular reports on mitigation actions for high-risk items, and the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Risk Reporting to Governance
artifacts.description: The risk reports submitted to the board and senior management drawn from the register.

artifacts.name: Targeted Risk Analysis Library
artifacts.description: The library of targeted risk analyses for each requirement that specifies one, the documented methodology covering assets, threats, impacted controls and the factors leading to likelihood and impact, the tracker with last-review and next-review dates, the inventory of requirements met using the customised approach with an analysis for each, and the management review and approval records for both sets.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Register
artifacts.description: The documented AI risk assessment methodology covering identification and analysis of consequences to the organisation and individuals; the completed assessment reports per AI system with consequence analysis, likelihood, level and prioritisation; the master AI risk register with identifiers, descriptions, analysis results, evaluation and prioritisation; and the records demonstrating repeated assessments produce consistent results.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Measurement Records
artifacts.description: The defined AI risk metrics and measurement methodology, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the validity and reliability demonstration with generalisability limitations documented, the responsibility matrix defining AI risk management roles, the documented evidence demonstrating the outcomes, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing them within the AI estate, and the ongoing monitoring and periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Encryption and Audit Finding Risk Records
artifacts.description: The documented encryption risk management and remediation of audit findings with the records demonstrating each operates in the environment covered. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of both documented requirements.

RSK-04.1.notes: 50 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps RSK-01.1; what is distinct here is the register as a maintained artifact — its update cadence, its residual entries and the reporting drawn from it — rather than the framing behind it.

artifacts.name: Reassessment Trigger Procedure
artifacts.description: The reassessment trigger procedure, the reassessment triggers and their outputs, the change-triggered risk assessment records, the change risk analysis records, the log of ad-hoc reviews triggered by major security breaches or significant infrastructure changes, and the process-integration evidence showing the triggers are wired into the change and incident processes. HITRUST requires the approved risk evaluation policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Periodic Review Schedule
artifacts.description: The schedule and historical records evidencing the at-least-annual review cycle of the risk assessment, the board meeting minutes recording review of the assessment and any subsequent updates, the reassessment reports, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

artifacts.name: Formal Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The comprehensive security risk assessment for the channel identifying, estimating and prioritising risks; the risk register listing identified risks with probability, impact, residual rating and treatment plan; the risk assessment reports; the risk register; and the risk treatment plans.

artifacts.name: Authentication Risk Reviews
artifacts.description: The periodic risk assessment report focused on authentication controls with threats, vulnerabilities and treatments; the records evidencing reviews triggered by changes in the internal or external environment; the records evidencing reviews triggered by application functionality changes; the records driven by changes in customer preferences; the sample post-incident authentication risk review reports following actual breaches; and the post-breach root cause analysis report demonstrating the review included it.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: The register logging when a transfer risk assessment is required, the inventory identifying transfers of sensitive data outside the jurisdiction carried out on a continuous or wide-scale basis, and the completed assessments evidenced to have been performed before the transfer or disclosure took place.

artifacts.name: Connection and Access Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: The per-application network access risk assessments, the risk assessment for trusted network connectivity, the cascading-risk evaluation, the connection termination evidence where the assessment did not support the connection, the risk assessment per remote access request with its approval workflow, the data-exchange risk assessments with the confidentiality agreement library supporting them, and the virtualisation risk assessment report.

artifacts.name: Fraud and Product Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: The mobile fraud risk assessment with its counter-fraud measures, the new product fraud assessments, and the fraud-loss limit mandates derived from them.

artifacts.name: Continuity Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The continuity management risk assessment, the business impact analysis, the critical process identification, and the recovery time objectives arising from them.

artifacts.name: Project Initiation Risk Records
artifacts.description: The documented project management standards addressing need assessment, risk management and approval authorities; the management approval of those standards; the standardised need assessment template used in project initiation; and the approval authority matrix.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the circumstances that oblige a fresh risk assessment.

RSK-04.3.notes: 48 asks across 7 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is the trigger — what events oblige a fresh assessment — so the trigger register is kept separate from the assessments themselves and from the domain-specific reassessments each framework names.

artifacts.name: Risk Management Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented methodology covering risk identification, assessment and treatment, the risk management policy and framework, and the approved standard addressing risk mitigation with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Risk Register with Treatment Status
artifacts.description: The risk register with inherent and residual ratings, owners and treatment status; the risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact; and the periodic risk assessment reports feeding it.

artifacts.name: Risk Treatment Plans
artifacts.description: The treatment plans for identified risks with controls, owners, deadlines and residual risk targets, the documentation of the treatment decision and its rationale, and the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Remediation Tracking Records
artifacts.description: The remediation tracking records with timeline compliance, the retest verification results confirming closure, the control deficiency tracking and remediation log, and the corrective action plans with timelines and status. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement to remediate vulnerabilities by risk.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance and Exception Records
artifacts.description: The management approval records for the treatment plan and the formal acceptance of residual risk, evidencing that what was not remediated was consciously accepted by a named owner.

artifacts.name: Targeted Risk Analysis Library
artifacts.description: The library of targeted risk analyses for each requirement that specifies one, the documented methodology covering identification of assets, threats and impacted controls and the factors leading to likelihood and impact, the tracker of all analyses with last and next review dates, and the management review and acceptance records for each.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The alert configuration covering failure of every critical security control system, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, sample failure alerts with triage, the documented response procedure covering restoration, cause and duration documentation and root-cause remediation, sample response records for past failures, mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Control Deficiency Reporting
artifacts.description: The management reporting on control exceptions and the board reporting on significant control deficiencies, evidencing unremediated risk reaches the level that can decide about it.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Treatment Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI risk treatment process covering option selection, control determination, comparison against the reference control set and additional controls; the treatment plan; the statement of applicability listing necessary controls with justification; the control communication records; the implementation tracker with effectiveness verification; the records applying the process to newly identified risks; and the revalidation records where a treatment proved ineffective.

artifacts.name: Nonconformity and Root Cause Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining how nonconformities are handled including reaction, root-cause analysis and corrective action; the log of nonconformities with cause analysis and checks for similar occurrences; the root cause analyses for material nonconformities; and the effectiveness review of the actions taken.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Prioritisation Records
artifacts.description: The AI risk treatment plan with prioritisation, the AI impact assessment, the documented evidence of the risk management outcome, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Readiness Records
artifacts.description: The incident response plan with defined roles and escalation procedures, the team roster and contact information, the tabletop exercise records, and the communication templates and notification records — the response capability that treats a risk that has materialised.

artifacts.name: Project Security Gate Records
artifacts.description: The project management methodology integrating security checkpoints and gate criteria, the security risk assessment template used at initiation, the portfolio security tracker with outstanding actions, the gate review sign-offs, and a sample project charter showing security objectives captured upfront.

artifacts.name: Standards Gap Analysis Records
artifacts.description: The gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards mapping and alignment documentation, the compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

artifacts.name: Encryption Risk Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented encryption risk management with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Risk Management Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented information security risk management artifacts held under the national regulator's regime, the evidence of compliance, and the regulator's own assessment records.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the risk mitigation requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

RSK-06.notes: 77 asks across 15 frameworks. Distinct from IAO-05 in that this control covers treating an identified risk rather than tracking an audit finding. PCI DSS 12.3.1's targeted risk analysis is kept separate because it is a named, per-requirement instrument rather than a general treatment plan.

artifacts.name: Risk Response Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented risk response procedures with the risk management policy and framework behind them, and the senior-management-approved follow-up procedure for timely implementation of recommendations with its approval records and evidence of application.

artifacts.name: Risk Register with Response Actions
artifacts.description: The risk register with assessments and treatment plans, the risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact, and the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Finding Tracking and Closure Records
artifacts.description: The records of tracking and closure of significant findings, the follow-up tracker, the recommendation timeline register measured against the approved procedure, the open findings register with ageing analysis, and the follow-up reports on remediation status.

artifacts.name: Independent Closure Validation
artifacts.description: The records of independent closure validation by the audit function, the corrective action monitoring records, and the evidence that findings are integrated back into risk management practice rather than closed in isolation. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remediation-of-findings requirement.

artifacts.name: Overdue Escalation Records
artifacts.description: The log of overdue significant findings escalated to senior management or committee, and the impairment disclosure and independence assessment records supporting the escalation route.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The plan of action and milestones entries, the documented risk acceptance where a response is to accept rather than treat, and the management approval attached to it.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Response
artifacts.description: The alert configuration covering failure of every critical security control system, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, sample failure alerts with triage, the documented response procedure covering restoration, cause and duration documentation and root-cause remediation, sample response records for past failures, mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Contingency Test Response Records
artifacts.description: The library of contingency test scenarios with coverage mapped against threats, the annual test report, the collaborative test evidence with the provider, the sign-off records confirming completion and acceptance, and the deficiency register with corrective action status and closure evidence.

artifacts.name: Continuity Plan Revision Records
artifacts.description: The change log of continuity plan updates with rationale, the revision records responding to operational changes, audit recommendations and test results, the records linking each update to its triggering event, and the version control records.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Treatment Records
artifacts.description: The documented AI risk treatment process covering option selection, control determination, comparison against the reference control set and additional controls; the treatment plan; the statement of applicability with justification; the control communication records; the implementation tracker with effectiveness verification; the records applying the process to newly identified risks; the revalidation records where a treatment proved ineffective; and the management approval of the plan and acceptance of residual risk.

artifacts.name: AI Incident and Decommissioning Response
artifacts.description: The incident response plan with the incident or error register, the approved organisational policies and procedures, the risk treatment plan with prioritisation, the decommissioning and deactivation procedure, the demonstration of validity and reliability with limitations documented, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Project Security Gate Records
artifacts.description: The project management methodology integrating security checkpoints and gate criteria, the security risk assessment template used at initiation, the portfolio security tracker with outstanding actions, the gate review sign-offs, and a sample project charter showing security objectives captured upfront.

artifacts.name: Encryption Risk Management Records
artifacts.description: The documented encryption risk management with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered.

RSK-06.1.notes: 74 asks across 11 frameworks. Overlaps RSK-06; what is distinct here is the response once a risk or finding is live — the follow-up procedure, closure validation, escalation of overdue items — rather than the treatment decision itself.

artifacts.name: Compensating Control Register
artifacts.description: The compensating control register, the compensating controls, the compensating control documents recorded when patches cannot be applied, the register of insecure services, protocols and ports in use with the specific compensating security features applied to each, and the documented business justification and risk acceptance for retaining each insecure service.

artifacts.name: Compensating Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration evidence of the implemented compensating controls, the service hardening evidence, the hardening baseline configuration showing unnecessary services and functions removed or disabled, the service inventory per system component showing only necessary services enabled, and the sample command or script output confirming removal or disablement.

artifacts.name: End-of-Life System Records
artifacts.description: The end-of-life and end-of-support tracker, the end-of-life software tracking, the supported software verification records, the risk acceptance for unsupported software, and the risk assessment for retained end-of-life systems with their compensating controls.

artifacts.name: Customised Approach Risk Analyses
artifacts.description: The inventory of requirements met using the customised approach, the targeted risk analysis document for each with its reasoning, the library of targeted risk analyses for each requirement that specifies one, the documented methodology behind them, the tracker with last-review and next-review dates, and the management review and approval records for each.

artifacts.name: Control Selection Analysis
artifacts.description: The evaluation reports comparing alternative controls for risk mitigation, the cost-benefit analyses for candidate controls showing cost against effectiveness, the return-on-security-investment analysis for material control decisions, and the management approvals recording the rationale linking control choice to cost and effectiveness.

artifacts.name: Risk Treatment Records
artifacts.description: The risk treatment plans for identified risks and the documentation of risk treatment decisions with their rationale.

artifacts.name: Segregation of Duties Compensating Controls
artifacts.description: The segregation of duties policy and framework, the conflict matrix documentation, the exception and compensating control documentation, the technical enforcement configuration evidence, the periodic review reports, the conflict identification and remediation tracking, the management sign-off on review results, and the trend analysis of conflicts over time.

artifacts.name: Patch Testing Records
artifacts.description: The test environment patch test records evidencing that a compensating control was chosen because the patch failed rather than in place of trying it.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Treatment Records
artifacts.description: The tracker showing implementation status and effectiveness verification of AI risk treatment plan items, the records evidencing the treatment process was applied to newly identified risks, and the records of review and revalidation of ineffective treatment options with the corresponding plan updates.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Management Records
artifacts.description: The AI impact assessment, the documented evidence demonstrating the management outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

RSK-06.2.notes: 44 asks across 8 frameworks. A compensating control is a deliberate acceptance with an offsetting measure; the register of what is being compensated for is kept separate from the measures themselves, because the first is what makes the second auditable.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis Report
artifacts.description: The completed BIA covering every business function and process in scope: the impact of disruption assessed across financial, operational, reputational and regulatory dimensions, functions prioritised by criticality, and the analysis linking each to the systems and third parties it depends on. Frameworks differ on cadence and trigger - PISF 2026 requires it annually, ISO 22301 expects completed reports per business unit, and SCF additionally requires a BIA for proposed significant changes - so state which applies and show the report is current. Must be dated and identify who performed it.

artifacts.name: Risk Register and Risk Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The risk register capturing identified risks with owner, likelihood and impact ratings, treatment decision and status, together with the periodic risk analysis reports and the treatment plans and monitoring records that follow from them. Must show the linkage in both directions with the BIA: continuity risks ranked by the BIA appear in the register, and register entries inform the BIA's assumptions. Several frameworks require an annual refresh.

artifacts.name: BIA and Risk Assessment Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented methodology and process governing how impact analysis is performed: the impact criteria and severity rating scales, how likelihood and impact are combined, the process steps and roles, and the approval of the methodology itself. Must be board- or management-approved and current, and cover both the business continuity impact assessment and the underlying risk assessment approach.

artifacts.name: Business Process Dependency Map
artifacts.description: The mapping of critical business activities to their upstream and downstream dependencies - workflows, supporting systems, facilities, people and suppliers - and the interdependencies between business functions. This is what allows the BIA's criticality ratings to be defended; it must identify the critical processes explicitly and carry a last-updated date.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objectives and Tolerance Register
artifacts.description: The register of recovery parameters derived from the BIA: RTO, RPO and maximum tolerable period of disruption / maximum tolerable downtime per critical service or function, with the acceptable loss levels the business will bear, the worksheets showing how each was determined, and management approval of the MTD thresholds. Include the availability and capacity requirements supporting those objectives - capacity plans, performance baselines and forecasting - where the framework requires them.

artifacts.name: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plans
artifacts.description: The enterprise business continuity plan and the ICT/disaster recovery plans built on the BIA's findings: invocation conditions and immediate response steps, tiered recovery sequences honouring the documented RTO/RPO, alternate sites and remote-working arrangements, supply-chain resilience, crisis management roles and escalation, communication protocol, DR runbooks per critical system and the failover architecture. Must be traceable to the BIA - showing which BIA-identified threats and recovery objectives drove each DR specification and the justification for the recovery approach chosen - and evidence of dissemination across the organisation. Where AI systems are in scope, include the incident response plan and incident/error register covering them.

artifacts.name: AI Impact Assessment Methodology and Schedule
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are in scope: the documented procedure for AI system impact assessments - what must be considered (deployment context, intended use, reasonably foreseeable misuse, technical and societal context, jurisdictions), the defined AI risk metrics and measurement methodology, the schedule of assessments with planned intervals and the change-driven triggers that force a reassessment, and the retention policy for the results.

artifacts.name: AI System Impact Assessment Results
artifacts.description: The repository of completed AI system impact assessments, one per system, documenting intended purpose and deployment context, users and assumptions, the likelihood and magnitude of both beneficial and harmful impacts, predictable failure modes, demographic applicability, system complexity and the human oversight role. Must cover impacts to individuals and groups (fairness, accountability, transparency and explainability, security and privacy, safety and health, financial consequences, accessibility, human rights, including protection needs of children, impaired or elderly persons and workers) and to society (environmental sustainability, economic, government, health and safety, and cultural norms), plus analysis of misuse risk and reinforcement of historical bias. Include the test and evaluation plans and result reports supporting the conclusions, the expert and stakeholder consultation records with how feedback was adjudicated, evidence that results feed the risk assessment process, and where appropriate the records of disclosure to interested parties.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Monitoring and Review Records
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are in scope: the RACI matrix defining AI risk management roles, responsibilities and communication lines, and the records of ongoing monitoring and periodic review at the defined frequency showing the impact assessment conclusions are still valid, with performer, date and reference to the AI system reviewed.

artifacts.name: Critical System and Control Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of critical ICT services and technology infrastructure in scope, with owner, recovery tier and the controls relied on, together with the IT general controls framework documentation and the security management process description that governs them. This is what the BIA's function-to-system mapping is checked against.

artifacts.name: Continuity and Recovery Test Records
artifacts.description: The BCP/DR testing programme and the evidence of its execution: test scenarios traceable to the BIA findings and risk assessment outcomes, the BIA-to-test-case mapping, the most recent test reports showing whether documented RTO and RPO targets were actually achieved, and the post-test review with corrective actions. Frameworks generally expect at least annual exercising.

artifacts.name: Disruption Scenario Register and Scenario Analysis
artifacts.description: The library or register of disruption and threat scenarios considered - including uncontrolled and non-specific events - with the severity rating criteria applied, the prioritisation matrix ranking them, and the records of the scenario evaluation (including workshop minutes) confirming the BIA's assumptions hold when tested against those scenarios.

artifacts.name: Management Approval and Accountability Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the BIA and the plans built on it were formally approved by the accountable body: BIA approval records, board approval of the BCP/DRP (annually where required, and by the sector regulator where applicable), and the appointment letter for the person accountable for business continuity management.

RSK-08.notes: 113 entries collapse to 13. The BIA itself, its methodology, and the recovery objectives it produces are restated by nine frameworks; the BCP/DR plans it feeds are restated by seven (21 entries, one artifact). ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF contribute a parallel AI impact-assessment track that is genuinely a different document set, so it is kept as three items rather than forced into the business BIA. No connectors are configured for this control - everything here is produced by people.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
artifacts.description: The documented plan addressing risks from hardware, software and cloud vendors across the chain, with its review and update records and the evidence that the processes are implemented rather than only defined. DORA requires the third-party risk strategy to be a distinct document integrated with the ICT risk framework.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Register
artifacts.description: The register tracking supply chain risks including fourth-party exposure, geopolitical concentration and single points of failure, with the risk assessment behind each entry and the treatment plans.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Arrangements Register
artifacts.description: The register of ICT third-party arrangements with the critical versus non-critical classification, the consolidated group-level register, the update procedures and records, and the provider categorisation documentation. DORA requires this register to be maintained continuously and submitted to the competent authority.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Submission Records
artifacts.description: The annual reports on third-party arrangements, the competent authority submission records, and the tracking of new arrangements entered during the period.

artifacts.name: Concentration Risk Analysis
artifacts.description: The ICT concentration risk assessment methodology, the monitoring reports produced under it, the mitigation measures adopted where concentration is material, the multi-vendor strategy documentation, and the pre-contract risk assessments feeding it.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy governing third-party and critical service provider engagement, the responsibility assignment for third-party oversight, the regulatory compliance obligations mapping, the service provider management policy, and the policy review records.

artifacts.name: Enterprise Risk Framework Coverage
artifacts.description: The enterprise risk management framework updated to explicitly cover outsourcing risks including subcontracting, the management or board approval records for that update, the risk assessment methodology and framework, the risk register with likelihood and impact, and the risk treatment plans with response decisions.

artifacts.name: Location and Jurisdictional Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The jurisdictional risk assessment for each offshore service location covering legal, regulatory and availability exposure, the risk register of locations with ratings and onsite-audit feasibility, and the documented alternate assurance mechanism for locations where onsite assessment is impractical.

artifacts.name: Vendor Due Diligence Records
artifacts.description: The completed due diligence assessments covering financial and security review, the supplier security audit and assurance reports, the risk assessment questionnaires and results, and the third-party security assessments.

artifacts.name: Supplier Contract Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The contractual security requirements imposed on suppliers, the vendor contracts with security requirements and service levels, the external service provider agreements, and the supply chain security policy setting the baseline for them.

artifacts.name: Software Bill of Materials Records
artifacts.description: The software bill of materials requested from and received from vendors, with the analysis of the components it discloses.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Assurance
artifacts.description: The development supplier contracts including security, intellectual property and testing obligations, the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses, the source code escrow arrangement for critical software, the assessment of supplier development maturity, the security test results from deliverables, the organisation-side code review, and the periodic vendor quality reports.

artifacts.name: Critical Vendor Contingency Plan
artifacts.description: The plans for replacing or mitigating loss of critical suppliers, the business impact analysis categorising critical functions and interdependencies, and the continuity plan covering supply-chain resilience.

artifacts.name: Ongoing Vendor Performance Review
artifacts.description: The annual vendor performance review documentation, the supplier security monitoring and audit reports, and the continuous monitoring of external services once engaged.

artifacts.name: AI Supplier Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for selecting AI suppliers of datasets, models, libraries or complete systems, the supplier register with risk assessments, evidence that suppliers delivered adequate documentation, the corrective action records where components do not align, the life-cycle responsibility allocation, and the controller or processor determination where personal information is processed.

artifacts.name: Objectives and Compliance Inventory
artifacts.description: The documented security and operational objectives with the objective-setting methodology, the risk tolerance statements, the compliance requirements inventory, and the independent assurance — audit plan, control testing and penetration test reports — that tests them.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The analysis of entity size and risk exposure, the assessment of incident likelihood and severity, and the justification for why the supply chain measures adopted are proportionate.

RSK-09.notes: 86 asks across 10 frameworks. Overlaps TPM-03; what is distinct here is the plan and register as risk-management instruments — DORA Article 28's register of arrangements, concentration risk methodology and regulator submissions — rather than the supplier controls themselves.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented methodology for supply chain risk classification, the risk assessment methodology, the vendor risk management policy and procedures, the risk management policy and framework, and the assessment schedule governing when reassessment falls due.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Register
artifacts.description: The register identifying, assessing and classifying supply chain risks by category; the risk register with its assessments and treatment plans; the risk assessment report; the risk assessment update records; the threat and vulnerability analysis; the risk analysis reports with likelihood and impact assessments; and the risk response actions with their monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: Supplier Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The service provider assessment reports, the assurance report reviews, the vendor risk assessment questionnaires and results, the periodic supplier review reports with their risk assessments, the annual vendor performance review documentation, the supplier performance indicator dashboard, and the vendor contracts with their security requirements and service levels.

artifacts.name: Sub-Contractor Risk Records
artifacts.description: The up-to-date list of provider sub-contractors with scope of services, locations and criticality; the map of the provider supply chain visualising sub-contractor dependencies; the log of sub-contractor list updates received and reviewed; the assessment of large or complex sub-contracting and its impact on operational resilience; and the evaluation of the organisation's capacity to oversee and monitor emerging risks from those chains.

artifacts.name: Procurement Security Testing
artifacts.description: The records of security testing and evaluation performed during procurement and the supply chain risk assessments for critical infrastructure procurement.

artifacts.name: Development Supplier Controls
artifacts.description: The contracts with development suppliers including security, intellectual property and testing obligations; the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses; the assessment of the supplier's development lifecycle maturity and security practices; the security test results from vendor deliverables; the evidence of organisation-side code review of vendor-delivered code; the periodic quality and security reports from development vendors; and the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software.

artifacts.name: AI Supply Chain Risk Records
artifacts.description: The third-party AI and data risk assessments, the AI impact assessment, the documented evidence demonstrating the management outcome, and the ongoing monitoring and periodic review records.

RSK-09.1.notes: 37 asks across 8 frameworks. Overlaps TPM-02; what is distinct here is the risk assessment as a repeated activity with a schedule, and the sub-contractor layer beneath the direct supplier.

artifacts.name: Impact Assessment Methodology and Trigger Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented methodology defining how an assessment is performed, the template used, and the procedure defining what triggers one — high-risk processing, a new system, a material change. GDPR requires the high-risk processing identification behind the trigger; PISF 2026 requires the template and trigger procedure as a distinct artifact.

artifacts.name: Completed Privacy Impact Assessments
artifacts.description: The completed assessments per system, project or process, with the identified risks, the mitigation measures adopted, and the residual risk position. NDMO requires the initial personal data protection assessment and the risk assessments to be evidenced as separate documented specifications.

artifacts.name: Privacy Risk Mitigation Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker of privacy risks identified in assessments with mitigation status and closure, evidencing the assessment drives action rather than terminating as a document.

artifacts.name: Supervisory Authority Consultation Records
artifacts.description: The consultation procedures for cases where residual high risk remains, and the communication records with the authority, held separately because the obligation arises only when mitigation is insufficient.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The completed transfer risk assessment covering all required elements — purpose and legal basis, nature and volume of data, recipient safeguards, destination legal regime, risks to data subjects and mitigation — with the standard template enumerating them and the coverage matrix confirming each element is addressed in every assessment.

artifacts.name: Transfer Risk Trigger Register
artifacts.description: The register logging when a transfer risk assessment is required, the inventory identifying continuous or wide-scale transfers of sensitive data outside the jurisdiction, and the evidence that assessments were completed before the transfer took place rather than after.

artifacts.name: Transfer Risk Treatment Plan
artifacts.description: The plan documenting the measures or controls applied to prevent or mitigate the identified risks to data subjects, with the owner and the status of each measure.

artifacts.name: AI System Impact Assessment Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for AI system impact assessments covering deployment context, intended use, foreseeable misuse and the consequences to individuals, groups and society, with the schedule defining planned intervals and change-driven triggers.

artifacts.name: AI Impact Assessment Results Repository
artifacts.description: The repository of completed AI system impact assessments recording intended use, positive and negative impacts and predictable consequences, with the retention policy defining how long results are kept and the records showing results were made available to relevant interested parties where appropriate.

artifacts.name: Individual and Societal Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The assessments covering fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, security, privacy and safety for individuals and groups; the societal impact assessment covering environmental sustainability, economic and health effects; the misuse and historical bias analysis; and the records of consultation with researchers, subject-matter experts and users used to understand potential impacts.

artifacts.name: Impact-to-Risk Integration Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence that impact assessment results feed the risk assessment process through linked entries or a documented method, so an identified impact becomes a managed risk rather than a filed report.

artifacts.name: AI Privacy Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The privacy risk assessment for the AI system, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the AI impact assessment, the defined AI risk metrics with measurement methodology, the test and evaluation plans, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Framework and Register
artifacts.description: The risk assessment methodology and framework, the annual risk assessment reports, the risk register with identified risks, likelihood and impact, the risk treatment plans with response decisions, and the risk analysis reports.

artifacts.name: Records Management and Retention Controls
artifacts.description: The records management policy covering creation, storage, retrieval, protection and disposal; the retention schedule listing record types, retention period, legal basis and disposal method; the protection controls documentation covering storage, encryption and access; the retention automation configuration; the archive access logs; and the destruction log with method and witness.

artifacts.name: Data Subject Rights Records
artifacts.description: The consent records, opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, and the published privacy notice with its version history.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Evidence
artifacts.description: The data processing specifications and documentation, input validation and output reconciliation procedures, processing accuracy monitoring reports, and the data quality metrics and dashboards the assessment relies on.

artifacts.name: Data Protection Control Evidence
artifacts.description: The data security control evidence including access controls, the privacy artifacts, the documented procedures, the approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the compliance audit reports.

artifacts.name: Control Framework Documentation
artifacts.description: The IT general controls framework documentation, the security management process documentation, the technology acquisition and development lifecycle controls, and the technology infrastructure control inventory.

RSK-10.notes: 86 asks across 11 frameworks. Three distinct assessment regimes converge here and are kept apart because each has its own trigger, template and retention rule: the privacy impact assessment (GDPR, PISF 2026, NDMO), the cross-border transfer risk assessment (KSA PDP), and the AI system impact assessment (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF).

artifacts.name: Continuous Monitoring Strategy
artifacts.description: The continuous monitoring strategy, the procedure defining proactive monitoring of information assets and security controls, the documented procedure for continuous risk assessment and treatment, and the procedures defining how risks are monitored and reported at tactical, management and board levels.

artifacts.name: Monitoring Tooling Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration evidence of monitoring tooling for assets and controls and the continuous monitoring records evidencing it operates.

artifacts.name: Risk Monitoring Dashboards
artifacts.description: The dashboard showing real-time or periodic risk metrics, the dashboard reporting continuous posture and risk profile to management, the monitoring metrics and dashboards, the security status reports, the ongoing assessment reports, and the monitoring evidence for the threats on the register.

artifacts.name: Control Testing Records
artifacts.description: The control testing programme with its test results, the records of risk review of controls, and the reports from testing methodologies evaluating the risk processes themselves.

artifacts.name: Risk Register and Updates
artifacts.description: The maintained risk register prioritising and closely monitoring high-risk activities, the current register evidencing ongoing monitoring and status updates, the risk register, the log evidencing periodic updates, the periodic update evidence, the threat register, and the mitigation action progress reports.

artifacts.name: Risk Reporting to Governance
artifacts.description: The reports of major risks submitted to the governing committee, the regular reports on mitigation actions for high-risk items, the templates for periodic monthly, quarterly and annual risk reports, the management-approved procedures defining the format and contents of management information, the technical specification of data sources, frequency, report templates and distribution list, the periodic management reports monitoring framework implementation, and the minutes of senior management meetings reviewing those outputs.

artifacts.name: Security Function Accountability
artifacts.description: The formal head of information security job description covering enterprise-wide security risk management, the defined performance indicators covering risk management and mitigation effectiveness, the periodic reports produced on security risk posture, strategies and emerging risks, and the enterprise security strategy devised to monitor and address current and emerging risks.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Monitoring
artifacts.description: The records of continuous supply chain monitoring and review at defined intervals or on change and the log of escalations and remediation actions for supply chain risks.

RSK-11.notes: 37 asks across 4 frameworks. Overlaps RSK-04.1; what is distinct here is continuous monitoring — the strategy, the tooling and the security status reports — rather than the register being updated.

artifacts.name: Security Awareness Programme
artifacts.description: The documented and approved awareness programme covering the information security policy, each person's role in protecting information, and the threats they face. PCI DSS requires the curriculum to cover phishing and social engineering and to include role-specific content; PISF 2026 requires a structured programme with priorities, topics, schedules, resources, methods and audiences; CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented programme.

artifacts.name: Annual Training Plan and Schedule
artifacts.description: The annual plan covering target audiences, topics, delivery methods and frequency, the training calendar, and the mapping of programme content to sector-regulator recommendations where required.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The learning management system export showing per-user completion of mandatory modules, with completion rates by department. PCI DSS requires training on hire and at least once every twelve months; HIPAA requires records for all workforce members.

artifacts.name: Training Content Library
artifacts.description: The training materials — decks, videos, quizzes, e-learning modules and posters — used in the programme, with the role-specific content for audiences whose exposure differs.

artifacts.name: Awareness Campaign Collateral
artifacts.description: The posters, newsletters, intranet articles and campaign materials used in ongoing awareness activity between formal training cycles.

artifacts.name: Phishing Simulation Results
artifacts.description: The simulation reports showing click rates, reporting rates and repeat offenders, and the follow-up applied to those who repeatedly fail.

artifacts.name: Training Effectiveness Measurement
artifacts.description: The metrics showing behavioural change rather than attendance — incident reporting rates, simulation click rates, quiz scores and behaviour surveys — and the effectiveness assessments drawn from them.

artifacts.name: Programme Review and Currency Records
artifacts.description: The annual review records of the programme with reviewer and findings, the update records reflecting newly identified threats and vulnerabilities, and the documentation evidencing the content reflects the current threat landscape rather than the year it was written.

artifacts.name: Policy Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: The personnel acknowledgements confirming they have read and understood the security policies and procedures, the acceptable use acknowledgements, and the records of communication of the policies to all users.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Training Records
artifacts.description: The records for specialised training beyond general awareness — secure coding for developers, privileged access management for administrators, protection training for executives — showing each audience received what its exposure requires.

artifacts.name: Payment Device Tamper Training and Inspection
artifacts.description: The inventory of point-of-interaction devices with make, model, serial number, location and responsible person; the inspection procedure with its cadence and methods; the records of personnel training on detecting tampering and unauthorised substitution; the periodic inspection records; and the investigation outcomes for any reported tampering.

artifacts.name: Hiring and Onboarding Records
artifacts.description: The approved hiring policy governing recruitment with selection criteria, vetting and onboarding; the standard operating procedures implementing it; the onboarding procedures including background checks; the competency assessment records; and the audit reports on adherence to the hiring and training policies.

artifacts.name: Management Responsibility Records
artifacts.description: The approved standard on management responsibilities with its implementing procedure, the tone-from-the-top communications on technology risk, the management report on implementation of each approved policy, and the awareness communications evidencing personnel were informed.

artifacts.name: Cyber Hygiene Practices Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented cyber hygiene policy and practices that the training programme teaches, with the curriculum covering them.

artifacts.name: Succession Planning Records
artifacts.description: The succession planning documentation for key technology and security roles, evidencing capability is retained beyond individual post-holders.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures covering AI, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the AI impact assessment, and the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour that the relevant workforce must be trained on.

artifacts.name: Programme Budget and Charter
artifacts.description: The awareness programme charter and the annual budget approval evidencing the programme is resourced rather than only mandated.

artifacts.name: Data Awareness Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented information security training and business intelligence awareness specifications with their compliance evidence, the training and awareness records covering curriculum, attendance, completion and schedule, the data sharing agreements the training covers, and the regulator's own assessment records.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Security Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses and the third-party risk assessment and monitoring records, held here because the awareness obligation extends to the personnel of providers with access.

SAT-01.notes: 85 asks across 17 frameworks. The core is one awareness programme with completion records and effectiveness measurement; the specialisations kept separate are role-based training (ISO 27001), payment-device tamper training (PCI DSS 9.5.1) and the hiring policy that precedes training (SBP ETGRMF 1.8.a).

artifacts.name: Training Programme Plan
artifacts.description: The documented structured training programme with priorities, topics, schedules, resources, methods and audiences; the training calendar aligned with organisational objectives and regulator recommendations; the annual training calendar; the awareness and training programme plan; the training programme documentation; the mandatory training policy; the course catalogue mapped to attack techniques; and the mapping of programme content to the applicable regulator's recommendations.

artifacts.name: Content Currency Records
artifacts.description: The log of regular content reviews and updates, the content change log, the annual update sign-off, the change history of the programme reflecting evolving threats, the training content and curriculum covering the required key topics, the training content and materials, the awareness materials, and the awareness campaign materials.

artifacts.name: Training Needs Analysis
artifacts.description: The needs analysis derived from risk assessments, audits, incidents and regulatory obligations, and the schedule evidencing at least annual refresh of specialised training.

artifacts.name: Ad-Hoc and Refresher Sessions
artifacts.description: The evidence of ad-hoc sessions triggered by emerging threats, incidents or regulatory change; the attendance and completion records for annual refresher sessions; and the records showing awareness completion prior to access provisioning.

artifacts.name: Delivery Format Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of multiple delivery formats covering e-learning, instructor-led training, webinars and tabletop exercises.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The training attendance and completion records, the training completion records, the learning management completion reports, and the training completion dashboard.

artifacts.name: Effectiveness Evaluation Records
artifacts.description: The reports from simulations, assessments and performance monitoring of the programme; the results of phishing and social-engineering simulations; the training effectiveness assessments; the training effectiveness assessment results; and the corrective and preventive actions derived from the evaluation outcomes.

artifacts.name: Feedback Incorporation Records
artifacts.description: The records showing employee, audit and incident feedback incorporated into the programme.

artifacts.name: Governance Review Records
artifacts.description: The committee minutes evidencing review of training plan adequacy including cyber security coverage and the training budget allocations demonstrating investment in that training.

SAT-01.1.notes: 38 asks across 6 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is that the programme stays current — the content review log, the ad-hoc sessions triggered by emerging threats and the feedback loop — rather than that training happened.

artifacts.name: Security Awareness & Training Program Plan
artifacts.description: The approved awareness and training program document: scope covering all employees and contractors, mandated topics, delivery methods, frequency, ownership and management approval. HITRUST and ADHICS expect both the approved policy/standard and the procedure implementing it; PISF 2026 and SBP ETGRMF expect an approved program with an annual plan; QCB requires the mandatory-training policy making completion obligatory.

artifacts.name: Training Curriculum & Content Library
artifacts.description: The actual training materials: modules, decks, LMS courses and the curriculum showing topic coverage — acceptable use, authentication and password practice, phishing and social engineering, email and internet hygiene, malware, patching, data labelling and handling, incident reporting, remote access/VPN, and platform-specific operating procedures. Content must be traceable to current threats and to the policies it teaches; PISF 2026 also asks for evidence of the delivery formats used.

artifacts.name: Training Completion & Attendance Records
artifacts.description: Per-person completion evidence for the whole in-scope population — employees, contractors, managers and senior executives — from the LMS or attendance registers, with dates, and a reconciliation against the current headcount showing coverage and follow-up on non-completers. DoH ADHIE additionally requires the records repository to be maintained and authorised-user status to be tied to training currency.

artifacts.name: New-Hire & Pre-Access Training Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that users complete awareness training as part of initial onboarding and, where required, before access is granted: induction training records, pre-access completion records, and the timeline showing training preceded or immediately followed account provisioning.

artifacts.name: Annual Refresher Plan, Calendar & Completion Records
artifacts.description: The recurring training schedule and its completion evidence. Frameworks converge on at least annual refresher training for all personnel (NIST 800-53, PISF 2026, DoH ADHIE, ADHICS, NIS2, QCB), with additional ad-hoc sessions triggered by system changes, policy updates or incidents — retain the trigger record alongside the ad-hoc session evidence.

artifacts.name: Phishing & Social Engineering Simulation Results
artifacts.description: Results of simulated phishing or social engineering exercises: scope, date, click and report rates, repeat-offender handling and the remedial training given to those who failed.

artifacts.name: Training Effectiveness Assessment & Metrics
artifacts.description: Evidence the program works, not just that it ran: knowledge assessment or quiz results, awareness measurement surveys, effectiveness metrics and trend reporting, post-campaign effectiveness reviews, and the actions taken where effectiveness fell short.

artifacts.name: Training Acknowledgement & Policy Communication Records
artifacts.description: Signed or logged acknowledgements that personnel received and understood the training and the policies it covers, together with the communications issued when policies or authentication practices change, and trainee acknowledgement of the specific topics covered.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Training Matrix & Topic Coverage Map
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping job roles to the training each must complete, and the topic coverage map showing every mandated subject (including attack techniques relevant to the organization) is assigned to at least one course and to the right audience — with the role-specific content and completion evidence for privileged and specialist roles.

artifacts.name: Awareness Campaign Materials & Participation Records
artifacts.description: Ongoing awareness activity beyond formal courses: campaign calendar, posters, newsletters, intranet and email communications, fraud-awareness campaigns, participation records and any incentive/recognition program records.

artifacts.name: Policies & Procedures Underpinning Awareness Content
artifacts.description: The approved policies and procedures the awareness program is required to convey — password/authentication use, malicious code controls, security event reporting, privacy protection — supplied as the source documents the training maps to, plus the in-house security controls policy and its coverage matrix. Requested here because several frameworks (HITRUST, PCI DSS 8.3.8, CIS CSC, NIST 800-171, CSA CCM) test awareness against the underlying documented rule.

artifacts.name: Supporting Control Evidence for Mapped Requirements
artifacts.description: Operating evidence for the controls that frameworks mapped into this requirement alongside awareness: anti-malware deployment, definition update logs, scan reports and malware incident records; access provisioning/review records and password configuration; physical access logs; incident response plan and incident register; business continuity plan and test records; privacy notice, consent and data subject request records; third-party agreements and monitoring. Collect from the control owners, not the training team.

artifacts.name: Training Governance, Needs Assessment & Budget Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the program is governed and resourced: training needs assessment, program and content review logs showing material is refreshed on a defined cycle and after triggering events, the committee or management review of training adequacy, completion dashboards reported to management, budget records, background/knowledge verification of trainers or trainees where required, and external assessment records where a regulator performs the check.

artifacts.name: POI Device Inspection & Tamper Awareness Records
artifacts.description: For card-present environments: the POI device inventory, the documented inspection procedure, periodic inspection records, training records for the personnel performing inspections, and investigation records for any reported tampering or substitution.

artifacts.name: Privacy Officer Designation & Complaint Handling Records
artifacts.description: Documentation designating the privacy officer and the contact person for complaints, their job description and authority, and the complaint handling procedure personnel are trained to use.

SAT-02.notes: 153 entries reduce to 15. Roughly half are the same four artifacts (program plan, content, completion records, effectiveness) restated by 21 frameworks. No connectors are configured for this control, so everything is manual — an LMS connector would move completion records and refresher tracking to automated and is the highest-value automation here. Two clusters (underpinning policies, supporting control evidence) exist because several frameworks map non-training controls into this requirement; they are kept separate so the training team is not handed malware and BCP evidence.

artifacts.name: Security & Privacy Training Program Document
artifacts.description: The approved, current policy/programme document governing role-based security, privacy and resilience training: scope and applicability, target audiences, mandatory topics, delivery methods, frequency (before access, on system/technology change, and at least annually), roles and responsibilities for owning and delivering the programme, and the procedure or work instruction that implements it. Must carry management approval, version history and a stated review frequency. Where privacy, AI risk or data-management training is in scope, the same document (or a named subordinate one) must cover it.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Training Matrix & Curriculum
artifacts.description: A matrix mapping every defined role - privileged/system administrators, developers, network and firewall administrators, incident responders, fraud and helpdesk staff, data stewards, executives, third-party users - to the specific training modules each must complete, with the approved curriculum for each track. Must show which roles require training as a precondition of access, and include the named accountable owners (e.g. designated privacy/security officer and complaint contact) whose duties the curriculum reflects. Several frameworks require the matrix to be formally approved and kept current as roles change.

artifacts.name: Training Needs Analysis & Annual Training Plan
artifacts.description: The documented needs analysis driving the curriculum - derived from risk assessments, audit findings, incidents/breaches, new or changed technology, and regulatory obligations - together with the resulting annual plan and schedule: audiences, topics, delivery method, dates, and the at-least-annual refresh cycle. Where capacity-building or certification budgets are mandated, the plan must show skills targets, budget allocation and the link to service-delivery objectives.

artifacts.name: Training Content Library
artifacts.description: The actual delivered materials for every module in the curriculum - decks, e-learning modules, videos, quizzes, manuals and job aids - covering at minimum the topics the frameworks name: authentication and strong-factor selection, data handling and classification/labelling, secure coding for the technologies in use, network and VPN/remote-access use, patching and how to report issues, phishing and social engineering, acceptable use, breach notification and sanctions, supply-chain risk for procurement staff, cloud and privileged administration, AI risk, and platform-specific operation. Materials must be version-identified and traceable to the module recorded in completion records.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: Per-person completion evidence for every mandatory and role-specific module - LMS export or attendance register showing name, role, module/content reference, delivery date and completion status. Must evidence the three required triggers: completion on hire/before duties, completion after system or technology changes, and recurring completion at least every 12 months (some frameworks require more frequent refreshers for fraud, privileged and CII roles). Records must be retained for the applicable retention period and be tamper-protected.

artifacts.name: Pre-Access Training Gate Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that training completion is enforced as a precondition of access, not merely tracked: induction/new-joiner briefing records signed before access, access request forms carrying manager sign-off and a training-completion check, the provisioning workflow or go-live checklist showing training as a mandatory gate, and per-authorized-user training documentation for regulated platforms. Must show the training date precedes the access-grant date.

artifacts.name: Policy & Training Acknowledgement Records
artifacts.description: Signed or electronically captured acknowledgements from personnel confirming they received and understood the security policies, acceptable use terms and role responsibilities covered in training - including specific acknowledgements where required for authentication/password policy, network security control responsibilities, and acceptable use before access. Acknowledgements must be dated, attributable to a named individual and tied to the policy version acknowledged.

artifacts.name: Training Assessment & Effectiveness Results
artifacts.description: Evidence that training works, not just that it was delivered: post-training quizzes and pass/fail results, pre- and post-assessment scores for specialized audiences, skills and data-handling assessments, phishing and social-engineering simulation campaign results with remediation actions, and behavioural metrics (phishing click-rate trend, incident reporting rate). Several frameworks additionally require a documented post-campaign or programme effectiveness review with conclusions and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Certification & Competency Register
