artifacts.description: Register of professional security, IT and service-management certifications held by relevant staff, with holder, certification name, issue and expiry dates, plus copies of the certificates and any competency assessments validating role capability. Where budget for certification is mandated, include the allocation and the certifications actually obtained against it.

artifacts.name: Board & Executive Training Records
artifacts.description: Completion evidence for training delivered specifically to the management body, board members and senior officials on cybersecurity and technology risk - session evidence, attendance, and completion certificates. At least one framework makes management-body training an explicit, separately auditable obligation, so this must be presentable independently of the workforce-wide records.

artifacts.name: Privileged & High-Risk Role Training Records
artifacts.description: Specialized training evidence for the populations that carry elevated risk: a register of staff holding privileged access or sensitive business functions, the additional curriculum built for them (secure administration, insider threat, advanced phishing, cloud administration, payment-device tamper detection), completion records with assessment scores, and - where applicable - the operational records showing trained personnel actually performed the duty (e.g. device inspection records naming the trained inspector and the investigation of any reported tampering).

artifacts.name: Awareness Campaign Collateral & Communications
artifacts.description: The ongoing-awareness output that sits alongside formal training: posters, newsletters, intranet articles, emails and town-hall material; the annual campaign schedule and participation/incentive records; and the communication records evidencing that policy changes, new authentication requirements and reporting channels (e.g. the dedicated fraud reporting email and phone line) were actually pushed to staff and customers where required.

artifacts.name: Training Content Review & Update Records
artifacts.description: Evidence the programme is maintained: periodic (at least annual, more often where specified) review of the programme and its content with reviewer, date, observations and changes made; content updates triggered by incidents, breaches or emerging threats with lessons learned incorporated; ad-hoc sessions run in response to threats, incidents or regulatory change; and pre-deployment training built and delivered before each major new technology goes live.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Training Requirements & Contract Clauses
artifacts.description: Evidence that the training obligation extends to contractors, vendors and third-party personnel with access: the training-requirement clauses in third-party agreements, employment/contract security and confidentiality clauses, and the completion or attestation records obtained from those parties. Where right-to-audit and monitoring provisions apply, include the assessment records confirming the third party met the training requirement.

SAT-03.notes: 172 entries collapse to 14 artifacts. Several crosswalk entries are mis-mapped in the source data (SWIFT CSCF 7.2 lists anti-malware artifacts, CSA CCM DCS-12 lists cabling security, SBP Cloud 18.1 lists capacity management, PCI DSS 9.5.1 lists POI inventory/inspection) - those frameworks are still cited against the nearest genuine training artifact rather than dropped.

artifacts.name: Awareness Programme Plan
artifacts.description: The annual awareness programme plan with audience segmentation, content and delivery mechanisms; the training programme documentation; the security awareness training programme materials; the library of awareness materials covering e-learning, posters, videos and infographics; the awareness campaign materials; and the training needs assessment behind them.

artifacts.name: Role-Based Training Curriculum
artifacts.description: The role-based training curriculum, the specialised training on data exposure and handling of regulated information, and the certification and qualification records for the roles requiring them.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The training completion records for all staff, the records of staff completion of awareness training across the organisation, the specialised training completion records, the training attendance records with dates, and the training documentation held per authorised user.

artifacts.name: Access Gated on Training
artifacts.description: The access provisioning gate linked to training completion and the pre-access privacy and security training records evidencing training precedes access rather than following it.

artifacts.name: Training Effectiveness Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment results measuring security awareness, the training effectiveness assessments, the metrics measuring awareness effectiveness through phishing click trend, reporting rate and quiz scores, and the reports of periodic phishing simulations with their click and report rates.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data Handling Controls
artifacts.description: The documented access criteria for the regulated information, the protection orientation records for personnel handling it, the unattended-information detection controls, the print and share privilege restrictions with local-printer-only configuration, the hardcopy shredding records with shredder logs, the clear desk and screen audit records in the areas holding it, the cleaning staff access monitoring records, the professional licence verification records, and the breach notification procedure to the regulator.

artifacts.name: Handling Procedure Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The compliance monitoring records for the handling procedures, the internal audit reports on adherence to them, and the incident records related to handling violations.

artifacts.name: Secure Area Conduct Records
artifacts.description: The secure area orientation and training records, the posters and communications on discussion etiquette for regulated information, and the signed rules acknowledgements from personnel working in those areas.

artifacts.name: Payment Device Inspection Training
artifacts.description: The inventory of point-of-interaction devices including make, model, serial number, location and responsible personnel; the procedure governing inspection cadence, methods and reporting; the records of personnel training on detecting tampering and unauthorised substitution; the periodic inspection records; and the records of reported tampering with their investigation outcomes.

artifacts.name: Data Sharing Training Records
artifacts.description: The documented data sharing training specification with its compliance evidence, the documented procedures and process workflows implementing it, the training and awareness records covering curriculum, attendance, completion and schedule, the data sharing agreements with their interoperability standards and integration documentation, and the organisational artifacts carrying accountability.

artifacts.name: Sensitive Data Transfer Records
artifacts.description: The sensitive data transfer controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented sensitive data transfer requirement.

artifacts.name: Privacy Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The privacy notice published to data subjects with its version history, the consent records with opt-out tracking and data subject request logs, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer. HITRUST requires the approved privacy protection awareness policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

SAT-03.3.notes: 55 asks across 11 frameworks. The general awareness programme is kept separate from the role-specific training on handling regulated data, and both from the access gate that ties provisioning to training completion — that gate is the control an assessor actually tests.

artifacts.name: Threat Awareness Programme
artifacts.description: The security awareness training materials, the approved awareness training curriculum covering threats and vulnerabilities including phishing and social engineering, the training programme documentation, the awareness campaign materials, the awareness materials, the campaign materials, the annual awareness campaign schedule, the annual training schedule, the mandatory training policy, and the course catalogue mapped to attack techniques.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The training completion records, the learning management records evidencing personnel receive training upon hire and at least once every twelve months, the campaign participation records, the learning management completion reports, and the personnel acknowledgments confirming understanding of the policies and procedures.

artifacts.name: Awareness Effectiveness Measurement
artifacts.description: The phishing simulation campaign results with their remediation activities, the phishing simulation results, the post-campaign effectiveness reviews, the training effectiveness assessments, and the incentive programme records driving participation.

artifacts.name: Ongoing Threat Communications
artifacts.description: The security reminder distribution records, the newsletter or mail communications, and the security bulletin archives keeping the threat picture current between formal training cycles.

artifacts.name: Insider Threat Awareness
artifacts.description: The documented insider-threat awareness training with the records demonstrating it is delivered and operating. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented requirement.

artifacts.name: Payment Device Tamper Training
artifacts.description: The inventory of point-of-interaction devices including make, model, serial number, location and responsible personnel; the procedure governing inspection cadence, methods and reporting; the records of personnel training on detecting tampering and unauthorised substitution; the periodic inspection records; and the records of reported tampering with their investigation outcomes.

artifacts.name: External Threat Monitoring
artifacts.description: The media monitoring service documentation and the online misinformation monitoring procedures covering the reputational threat environment.

artifacts.name: AI Risk Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The AI risk management training records with their attendees, the approved organisational policies and procedures, the documented evidence demonstrating the outcome, and the periodic review records.

SAT-03.6.notes: 39 asks across 10 frameworks. Threat-environment awareness is the training topic; the campaign, its measurement and the domain-specific tamper training are three proofs, with PCI DSS 9.5.1 kept separate because it trains a specific physical inspection skill.

artifacts.name: Training Completion Records
artifacts.description: The learning management records evidencing personnel receive training upon hire and at least once every twelve months, the individual training transcripts, the completion reports, the training attendance and completion records with dates, the training completion records and tracking, the completion records for annual training, the attendance and acknowledgement records, and the baseline and security-focused training completion records.

artifacts.name: Training Record Retention
artifacts.description: The training record retention policy, the training tracking system records, the hard copy and electronic training records repository, the evidence of secure storage, backup and retention of training records, the certification storage and retention evidence, and the records capturing attendee, dates, modules and assessment outcomes.

artifacts.name: Training Acknowledgements and Certifications
artifacts.description: The signed training certifications, the acknowledgement records, the personnel acknowledgments confirming understanding of the policies and procedures, and the authorised user status maintenance log tied to training currency.

artifacts.name: Access Gated on Training
artifacts.description: The access provisioning gate linked to training completion, the pre-access privacy and security training records, and the training documentation held per authorised user evidencing training precedes access.

artifacts.name: Training Programme Plan
artifacts.description: The documented and approved security awareness programme covering the information security policy and each person's role, the awareness and training programme plan, the annual training calendar, the annual refresher training schedule, the mandatory training policy, the course catalogue mapped to attack techniques, the role-specific awareness content, the awareness content library, the training content and materials, the approved curriculum, and the records of programme review and updates.

artifacts.name: Training Effectiveness Records
artifacts.description: The post-training assessments and quizzes, the training effectiveness assessment results, and the phishing simulation campaign results with their remediation activities.

artifacts.name: Leadership and Specialised Training Records
artifacts.description: The board and senior management training session evidence, the specialised regulatory training documentation, the developer training programme documentation, and the non-compliance escalation evidence for personnel who do not complete mandatory training.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Training Records
artifacts.description: The training requirements written into third-party agreements, the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records covering provider training obligations. HITRUST requires the approved information security awareness policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

SAT-04.notes: 50 asks across 9 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is the record rather than the training: the transcript, its retention and the access gate that depends on it. The programme content artifacts are kept separate because they answer SAT-02 rather than this control.

artifacts.name: Secure Engineering & Architecture Principles Standard
artifacts.description: The approved document that states the organisation's secure design and data-privacy engineering principles (defence in depth, least privilege, zero trust, secure defaults, privacy by design) and how they are applied when specifying, designing, building and modifying systems. Must include the reference architectures and approved security pattern library that operationalise the principles, name the owner and approver, and show a current version with a defined review cycle. PISF 2026 additionally expects the principles to be explicitly applied to critical information infrastructure projects.

artifacts.name: Secure SDLC Standard & Secure Coding Standards
artifacts.description: The approved secure software development lifecycle standard showing security is embedded at every stage (requirements, design, build, test, deploy, retire), together with the secure coding standards it mandates (OWASP Top 10 / ASVS alignment and language-specific guidance). PCI DSS requires the standard to be based on industry-accepted practice; SOC 2 wants technology acquisition and development lifecycle controls covered; ADHICS requires a management-approved information systems acquisition, development and maintenance policy; NDMO expects the design, development and testing artefacts to be produced and retained.

artifacts.name: Application Security Requirements Catalogue
artifacts.description: The reusable catalogue of security requirements applied to applications (ASVS-derived), the API security requirements standard, sample redacted requirement specifications from live projects, and the pre-acquisition security evaluation applied to COTS/SaaS software. Should show how requirements are selected per application and that the same catalogue is used for both built and bought software.

artifacts.name: Architecture & Design Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that designs are actually reviewed against the principles before build: architecture review board minutes and decisions, security engineering and secure design review records, threat models for in-flight projects, requirement sign-off by security/architecture, SDLC stage-gate approvals, and the system design documents for a sample of systems. Should be sampled across recent projects with dates, reviewers and outcomes; PISF 2026 and NIST 800-171 expect the reviews to be demonstrably operating, not just defined.

artifacts.name: Enterprise & Network Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: Current-state architecture documentation across business, data, application and technology layers, including network architecture and segmentation diagrams, DMZ/boundary design, virtual network design, and the architecture roadmap and transition plans. Diagrams must be dated and show the security boundaries and trust zones actually in place.

artifacts.name: Architecture Deviation & Control Exception Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved departures from reference architectures and standard controls, including authorised control bypasses (e.g. time-limited MFA bypass with manager approval) and any alternate/compensating controls accepted in their place, each with the risk assessment, approver, expiry and review status.

artifacts.name: Boundary, Protocol & Virtualisation Configuration Evidence
artifacts.description: Live configuration evidence that the engineered protections are in effect: firewall/proxy and boundary-protection rule sets with monitoring output, evidence that insecure protocols are removed or remediated with the supporting compliance scan results, hypervisor hardening and VM isolation settings, and the MFA implementation configuration showing replay resistance, no user or admin bypass, at least two distinct factor types and all factors required to succeed. The infrastructure and virtualisation security policy that governs these settings must accompany the extracts.

artifacts.name: Cybersecurity & Data Privacy Policy Set
artifacts.description: The approved policy layer sitting above the engineering standards: system and communications protection policy, system and information integrity policy, privacy policy with the PII handling procedures beneath it, and the policy framework that ties them together. Each must be current, management-approved, and state scope, roles and responsibilities, control objectives and review frequency. NIST AI RMF additionally expects trustworthy-AI characteristics to be reflected in these approved policies and their supporting procedures.

artifacts.name: Data Protection by Design & DLP Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that data protection by design and default is engineered into systems: the DLP policy defining scope, detection strategy and response; the active DLP rule set covering email, endpoint, web and cloud channels; the alert and investigation log; platform dashboard showing coverage; removable-media and cloud-storage control configuration; and the playbook for confirmed leakage events. CSA CCM expects the equivalent records for the cloud environment specifically.

artifacts.name: Risk Assessment Methodology, Register & Treatment Plans
artifacts.description: The documented risk assessment methodology, the risk register with likelihood and impact ratings, risk treatment decisions, and the most recent assessment report. Application-level risk assessments that drive which security requirements apply must be included. SOC 2 expects an annual cycle; MAS TRM additionally requires security and risk/control assessments for online services and assessment of controls at corporate customers, with any alternate controls risk-assessed.

artifacts.name: Control Inventory & Risk-Control Mapping
artifacts.description: The inventory of control activities mapped to the risks they address, the ITGC framework documentation and technology infrastructure control inventory, the segregation of duties matrix and its analysis, and the control design documentation showing how each control was designed to meet its objective.

artifacts.name: Security Communication & Awareness Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that engineering and security expectations are communicated internally: the internal security communication procedures, awareness programme materials, the anonymous/whistleblower reporting mechanism documentation, board reporting packages covering internal controls and security, and stakeholder acknowledgement records for the governing policy.

artifacts.name: Innovation & Emerging Technology Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The innovation strategy and programme documentation, technology watch and emerging-technology assessment reports, proof-of-concept evaluation results with their business cases, and the innovation portfolio tracking and benefits reports — showing new technology is assessed before it enters the architecture.

artifacts.name: Policy Approval & Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: Dated records showing the engineering policies and standards were formally approved and are reviewed on the defined cycle: management approval evidence, policy review records, and implementation/assessment records confirming the outcomes hold over time. NIST AI RMF expects periodic review plus lifecycle implementation artefacts; NDMO expects compliance evidence and the NCA-conducted assessment records for design, development and testing.

SEA-01.notes: 105 framework evidence asks collapse to 14 artifacts. No automated collectors are attached to this control, so nothing is fully automated today; boundary/DLP configuration items are marked hybrid because a connector could pull the config state but the governing design documents must be produced by engineering.

artifacts.name: Control Activities Inventory
artifacts.description: The control activities inventory mapped to the risks they address, the control design documentation, the risk-control mapping matrix, and the segregation of duties matrix with its analysis.

artifacts.name: Control Failure Detection
artifacts.description: The procedure for detecting and addressing failures of each listed critical security control system, the service-provider variant of that procedure, the alert configuration covering network security controls, intrusion detection, integrity monitoring, anti-malware and physical access controls, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, the sample failure alert logs, and the sample failure alerts with their triage and resolution records.

artifacts.name: Control Failure Response
artifacts.description: The documented response procedure covering restoring security functions, identifying and documenting cause and duration, and resuming monitoring; the response records demonstrating prompt addressing of failures; the sample incident response records for past failures; the mean-time-to-restore metrics; and the lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Enterprise Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The enterprise architecture documentation covering business, data, application and technology layers; the architecture principles and standards documentation; the architecture roadmap and transition plans; the architecture review board meeting minutes and decisions; the security architecture documentation; the security design principles checklist; and the design review records.

artifacts.name: Centralised Data Leakage Controls
artifacts.description: The policy defining scope, detection strategy and response; the rule export covering mail, endpoint, web and cloud channels; the cloud storage configuration; the platform dashboard showing coverage; the endpoint control preventing or monitoring transfers to removable media; the log of alerts triggered, triaged and investigated; and the playbook defining response steps for confirmed leakage events.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Records
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures, the documented evidence demonstrating the governance outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

SEA-01.1.notes: 34 asks across 6 frameworks. Overlaps SEA-03 and MON-01.4; what is distinct here is centralised management of the control estate, with PCI DSS 10.7's control-failure detection as the proof that centralisation actually sees everything.

artifacts.name: Enterprise Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The enterprise architecture across business, data, application and technology layers, the current-state and target-state architecture, the architecture principles and standards, and the roadmap and transition plans between them.

artifacts.name: Architecture Governance Records
artifacts.description: The architecture review board meeting minutes and decisions, the architecture review records, and the design review records evidencing that changes are assessed against the architecture rather than around it.

artifacts.name: Architecture Gap Analysis
artifacts.description: The gap analysis reports with prioritised initiatives, the documented future-state gap assessment, the IT strategic plan aligned to business strategy, and the strategy communication and roadmap material.

artifacts.name: Data Architecture and Modelling Records
artifacts.description: The data architecture artifacts covering models, entity-relationship diagrams and design documentation, the approved data architecture policy and standard, the documented current-state and target-state data architecture with their implementing procedures and process workflows, the register with a named owner, and the performance metrics dashboard.

artifacts.name: Data Integration Architecture Records
artifacts.description: The documented data integration plan and target integration architecture with their compliance evidence, the data sharing agreements, interoperability standards and integration documentation, and the register evidencing each with a named owner.

artifacts.name: Security Requirements Catalogue
artifacts.description: The catalogue of reusable security requirements applied to applications, the API security requirements standard covering authentication, authorisation, validation and rate limiting, the security evaluation of acquired software before purchase, the application risk assessment driving requirement selection, sample requirements specifications from real projects, and the sign-off records showing they were approved by security or architecture.

artifacts.name: Project Security Gate Records
artifacts.description: The project management methodology explicitly integrating security checkpoints and gate criteria, the security risk assessment template used at initiation, a sample project charter showing security objectives captured upfront, the portfolio security tracker with assessment status, and the gate review sign-offs confirming security reviews completed.

artifacts.name: Network Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The network architecture documentation and segmentation diagrams with the records demonstrating the architecture is implemented in the environment it describes. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented architecture.

artifacts.name: Security Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The security architecture documentation and the security design principles checklist applied when a design is reviewed.

artifacts.name: Innovation and Technology Watch Records
artifacts.description: The innovation strategy and programme documentation, the portfolio tracking with benefits reports, the proof-of-concept evaluation results with business cases, and the technology watch and emerging technology assessment reports.

artifacts.name: Security Function Leadership Records
artifacts.description: The security function lead's job description covering the full set of responsibilities, the annual performance review, and the programme and budget presentations made to the executive.

artifacts.name: Control Design and Risk Mapping
artifacts.description: The control activities inventory mapped to risks, the control design documentation, the risk-control mapping matrix, and the segregation of duties matrix with its analysis.

artifacts.name: Objectives and Compliance Inventory
artifacts.description: The documented security and operational objectives with the objective-setting methodology, the risk tolerance statements, and the compliance requirements inventory the architecture must satisfy.

artifacts.name: Independent Assurance over Architecture
artifacts.description: The internal audit plan and schedule, the continuous monitoring programme documentation, the security control testing results, and the penetration testing and vulnerability assessment reports that test whether the architecture holds in practice.

artifacts.name: Data Security and Privacy Controls
artifacts.description: The data security control evidence including access controls, the privacy artifacts, the approved data management and personal data protection strategy, the compliance audit reports, and the regulator's own assessment records.

SEA-02.notes: 84 asks across 7 frameworks, dominated by NDMO restating the same architecture artifact once per specification. Those are merged. The distinct demands kept separate are the architecture governance function (COBIT), security requirements in the design (ISO 27001) and the data architecture itself (NDMO).

artifacts.name: Enterprise Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The enterprise architecture documentation covering business, data, application and technology layers; the architecture principles and standards documentation; the architecture roadmap and transition plans; and the architecture review board meeting minutes and decisions. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented employ-secure-architecture-and-engineering requirement.

artifacts.name: Defence-in-Depth Design
artifacts.description: The network design document covering defence in depth, the multi-layer security architecture diagram showing firewalls, secure sign-on, dual authentication with triangulation and real-time event monitoring, the defence-in-depth controls inventory, the matrix showing multi-layer control coverage across assets, and the single-point-of-failure review.

artifacts.name: Perimeter Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The architecture diagram showing network security control deployment at every boundary between trusted and untrusted networks, the configuration export of those perimeter controls, the register classifying every network as trusted or untrusted with its enforcement point, the approved configuration standard defining ruleset baselines and review cadence, the sample configurations from production controls, the version history and maintenance records of that standard, the firewall rulebase with its periodic review evidence, and the quarterly configuration review. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented network defence requirement.

artifacts.name: Access Layer Configuration
artifacts.description: The port-based authentication and network access control configuration, the authentication, authorisation and accounting server deployment, the port security and address filtering configurations, the management network segregation diagram, the secure management access configuration with multi-factor, and the dual authentication configuration with triangulation of access.

artifacts.name: Detection Layer Configuration
artifacts.description: The intrusion detection and prevention deployment, the operations centre roster covering continuous coverage, and the real-time security event monitoring dashboard screenshots.

artifacts.name: Innovation and Technology Watch
artifacts.description: The innovation strategy and programme documentation, the innovation portfolio tracking and benefits reports, the proof-of-concept evaluation results with their business cases, and the technology watch and emerging technology assessment reports feeding the architecture roadmap.

artifacts.name: Architecture Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The documented information security architecture artifacts addressed under the national authority's regulations, the evidence of compliance with them, and the assessment or compliance records held by that authority.

SEA-03.notes: 37 asks across 7 frameworks. Overlaps NET-02 on network layering; what is distinct here is the enterprise architecture discipline behind it — the principles, the review board and the roadmap — which is kept separate from the deployed controls.

artifacts.name: Time Synchronisation Policy
artifacts.description: The policy mandating time synchronisation and approved time sources across all systems, the standard date and time format policy, and the documented standard specifying authoritative internal time sources traceable to a reliable external source. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented clock synchronisation requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the synchronise-clocks requirement. HITRUST requires the approved clock synchronisation policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Time Source Documentation
artifacts.description: The documentation of primary and secondary time sources used, the list of authorised internal and external sources accepted by in-scope systems, the source list naming the reference clock, and the design showing redundant time sources to prevent a single point of failure.

artifacts.name: Synchronisation Configuration
artifacts.description: The time protocol configuration export from sample components, the time service configuration documentation, the server configuration, the architecture document showing the synchronisation technology deployed to all in-scope components, the configuration evidence showing all systems set to the correct and consistent time, the sample output demonstrating active synchronisation, the output from the verification script showing time alignment across sample hosts, and the specialised device clock synchronisation records.

artifacts.name: Drift Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The monitoring report showing clock offset across systems stays within tolerance, the time drift monitoring records, the clock variation monitoring, the time synchronisation monitoring, and the synchronisation status reports.

artifacts.name: Time Setting Access Controls
artifacts.description: The access control configuration restricting modification of time-synchronisation settings to authorised personnel and the audit logs of any modifications to those settings.

artifacts.name: Timestamped Audit Records
artifacts.description: The sample time-stamped audit records demonstrating the synchronised clock reaches the log entries that depend on it.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the clock synchronisation requirements and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

SEA-20.notes: 32 asks across 8 frameworks. The time source, the synchronisation configuration and the drift monitoring proving it holds are three proofs; access control over the time settings is a fourth, because a modifiable clock defeats every audit trail.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Programme Documentation
artifacts.description: The programme-level documentation for how software is built securely - runbook, playbook or equivalent - covering the secure software development principles, the secure engineering and data privacy programme, and the SDLC policy embedding security activities in each phase with the deliverables and gates for each. Must be approved, current, and specific enough that a developer can follow it rather than restating the policy.

artifacts.name: Secure Engineering Principles, Coding Standards and Threat Models
artifacts.description: The defined secure engineering principles ensuring confidentiality, integrity, availability and safety are addressed in design and implementation, the secure coding standards applied (aligned to OWASP ASVS / Top 10 and the languages in use), the template used to capture security requirements in specifications and user stories, threat models produced during design for a sample of projects, and the developer secure-coding training completion records showing the standards are actually taught.

artifacts.name: System and Solution Design Documentation
artifacts.description: Design documentation for systems built or acquired: high-level and detailed solution designs, component and interface specifications, and the final system architecture including the security threat model. Where AI systems are in scope, the design must additionally cover the machine learning approach, learning algorithm and model, training plan and training-data quality expectations, evaluation and refinement approach, hardware and software components, the AI-specific security threats considered (data poisoning, model stealing, model inversion), human interaction points and interoperability.

artifacts.name: Enterprise Architecture and Architecture Review Records
artifacts.description: The enterprise architecture documentation across business, data, application and technology layers, the architecture principles and standards that constrain new development and acquisition, the technology infrastructure control inventory, the architecture review board minutes and decisions, and the architecture roadmap and transition plans.

artifacts.name: Technology Strategy, Evaluation and Business Case Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that technology choices are made deliberately rather than ad hoc: the innovation and technology strategy, technology watch and emerging technology assessments, proof-of-concept evaluation results with business cases, the documented selection criteria framework ensuring strategic fit and optimal resource use, technology evaluation reports scoring candidates against strategic requirements, total cost of ownership analyses for major selections, the checklist used to confirm requirements documents align with IT strategy, and innovation portfolio benefit tracking.

artifacts.name: Development Standards, QA Test Plans and Results
artifacts.description: The development standards and quality assurance test plans applied to solutions being built, with the executed test results and the defect tracking records showing what was found and how it was closed before acceptance.

artifacts.name: Procurement and Selection Records
artifacts.description: The acquisition file for a sample of technology procurements: the RFP/ITT or business requirements document capturing functional, operational, security and regulatory requirements; the requirements traceability matrix from business need through to specification; the register of regulatory requirements fed into the RFP; the review and sign-off records confirming the requirements are comprehensive and aligned to strategy; the formal system selection analysis with the scoring against the selection criteria; the compliance matrix confirming the selected system meets user, business, legal and regulatory requirements; and the signed selection and build/buy approval with its rationale. Public-sector entities must also evidence compliance with applicable public procurement rules.

artifacts.name: Acquisition and Security Planning Policy
artifacts.description: The approved system and services acquisition policy and the procedures implementing it, plus the security planning policy where held separately. Must define scope and applicability, the roles and the official who owns the policy, the personnel to whom policy and procedures are disseminated, the level at which it applies (organisation, mission/business process or system), the review and update frequency and the events that trigger an off-cycle update. Evidence must include management approval, stakeholder acknowledgement records and the policy review records themselves. Includes the acquisition and development lifecycle controls documented in the IT general controls framework.

artifacts.name: Supplier Contracts with Security, IP and Escrow Clauses
artifacts.description: Executed contracts and agreements for outsourced development and acquired technology, showing the security requirements incorporated into the contract, testing obligations placed on the supplier, intellectual property ownership and confidentiality clauses, service levels with their security provisions and the review of those SLAs, and the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software. Signed by both parties, with term and right-to-audit provisions.

artifacts.name: Vendor Security Assessment and Performance Reports
artifacts.description: Assessments performed on suppliers before and during engagement: the vendor security assessment results, the evaluation of the supplier's secure SDLC maturity and development practices, the periodic quality and security reports received from development vendors, and records of monitoring vendor access to the environment.

artifacts.name: AI Development Governance Records
artifacts.description: Where AI systems are developed or acquired: the documented AI design and development process covering lifecycle stages, testing requirements and methods, human oversight requirements, impact assessment stages, training-data expectations, required expertise and training, release criteria, approvals and sign-offs, change control and usability considerations; the supporting SOPs for each stage; the organisational policies embedding trustworthy AI characteristics; the AI impact assessment documenting likelihood and magnitude of beneficial and harmful impacts; the team composition records evidencing demographic, disciplinary and domain diversity in decision-making; and the periodic review records showing these remain effective.

artifacts.name: Application Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: Documentation and evidence for the controls that keep data correct through the systems built or acquired: input validation and error handling design, transaction authorisation procedures with the supporting logs, input-to-output reconciliation reports, exception and error detection monitoring output, error correction, resubmission and reprocessing procedures, the automated validation and quality-check configurations, and root cause analysis for recurring processing errors.

artifacts.name: Pre-Deployment Security Testing and Gate Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that security is verified before a system reaches production: the security review gate approvals at each SDLC stage, the CI/CD pipeline configuration with embedded SAST, DAST and SCA scanning, security test results for systems and for vendor-delivered code, organisation-side code review of vendor deliverables, security testing and evaluation performed during procurement, and - where connecting to an external platform - the completed readiness assessment and interface standards conformance evidence. Include the vulnerability handling and disclosure policy governing what happens to what the testing finds.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain and Proportionality Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: Assessments of the risk carried by the acquisition itself: supply chain risk assessments for critical infrastructure procurement identifying, and documenting mitigation of, supplier-borne risk; and the proportionality assessment justifying that the measures adopted are appropriate to the entity's size, risk exposure, and the likelihood and severity of incidents it faces.

artifacts.name: Technology Lifecycle: Refresh, Maintenance and Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The management-approved technology refresh policy and the refresh roadmap showing when systems reach end of support and how they will be replaced, the maintenance records for systems in service, and the decommissioning procedure and checklist with confirmation for each retired asset that data was retrieved where needed and securely destroyed otherwise.

TDA-01.notes: 113 entries collapse to 15. Procurement (14 entries) and the acquisition policy (12) are the core of this control and were spread across five frameworks in near-identical words. Kept separate because the deliverable genuinely differs: enterprise architecture (COBIT APO03), technology strategy and business cases (APO04, SBP 1.4.2), AI development governance (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001), processing integrity (SOC 2 PI1.x) and lifecycle refresh/decommissioning (CIS 15.7, QCB 8.8.1). No connectors are configured, so only pipeline-derived testing evidence is partly automatable.

artifacts.name: Product and Project Lifecycle Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented lifecycle methodology covering initiation, feasibility, requirements, design, development, testing and deployment, with the templates for each phase deliverable, the matrix of roles and deliverables per phase, and sample project artifacts evidencing the methodology is applied.

artifacts.name: Requirements Specification and Traceability
artifacts.description: The documented requirements for new products or material enhancements including the business, technical and regulatory rationale, and the traceability matrix linking each requirement through design, development, testing and deployment.

artifacts.name: Solution Design and Build Records
artifacts.description: The development standards and quality assurance test plans, the high-level and detailed design documents, the procurement and build approval documentation, and the test results with defect tracking.

artifacts.name: Security Requirements from Threat Assessment
artifacts.description: The system threat and risk assessment reports and the security requirements derived from them, evidencing that security requirements are driven by assessed threat rather than by checklist.

artifacts.name: Release and Deployment Records
artifacts.description: The release and deployment plans with rollback procedures, the production promotion checklists and authorisation records, the user acceptance testing results with sign-off, and the post-implementation review reports with lessons learned.

artifacts.name: Change Management Records
artifacts.description: The change management policy and procedures, the change advisory board minutes and decisions, the change request logs with assessment, authorisation and implementation records, and the post-implementation and emergency change documentation.

artifacts.name: Organisational Change Management Records
artifacts.description: The organisational change management plans and strategies, the change readiness assessment reports, the communication plans and stakeholder engagement records, and the post-change effectiveness reviews with adoption metrics.

artifacts.name: Enterprise Architecture Alignment
artifacts.description: The enterprise architecture documentation across business, data, application and technology layers, the architecture principles and standards, the architecture review board minutes, and the roadmap and transition plans the product must fit.

artifacts.name: Capacity and Availability Planning
artifacts.description: The availability and capacity management plans, the business impact analysis establishing availability requirements, the capacity forecasting documentation, and the performance baseline measurements with monitoring reports.

artifacts.name: AI System Technical Documentation
artifacts.description: The technical documentation pack covering general description, intended purpose, usage instructions and technical assumptions; the failure management plan covering rollback, feature toggling, update process and user notification; and the documentation of operations personnel roles and accountability for handling failures and updates.

artifacts.name: AI Event Logging Records
artifacts.description: The logging standard specifying what is captured across AI life-cycle phases covering traceability and detection, sample event logs showing time of use, input production data and out-of-range outputs, and the retention policy aligned to intended use and legal requirements.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Records
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures for AI, the documented evidence for each governance outcome, the AI impact assessments, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the risk treatment plan with prioritisation, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, the team composition records evidencing diversity, the stakeholder engagement and feedback log, the management oversight records confirming the outcome is resourced, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Mobile Application Distribution Controls
artifacts.description: The mobile application distribution policy, the official app store listing verification, the device integrity checking implementation, and the jailbreak or root detection mechanism documentation.

artifacts.name: Product Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The decommissioning procedures and checklist, and the data retrieval or destruction confirmation showing the process was completed for each retired product.

artifacts.name: Knowledge Management Records
artifacts.description: The knowledge management strategy and policies, the knowledge repository with maintained documentation, and the knowledge sharing activity records and training materials supporting the product through its life.

TDA-01.1.notes: 83 asks across 6 frameworks. NIST AI RMF restates the same governance evidence across eight outcomes; those are merged. What remains distinct is the product lifecycle methodology (SBP ETGRMF, COBIT), the AI system documentation pack (ISO 42001) and mobile application distribution (MAS TRM).

artifacts.name: Security Requirements Specification
artifacts.description: The documented security requirements for new or materially changed systems, the requirements specification documents with their security section, the business and technical requirement documents, the security specifications, and the risk assessment outputs the requirements are linked to. HITRUST requires the approved standard for security requirements analysis with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Security Requirements Template
artifacts.description: The template used to capture security requirements in user stories and specifications, the security controls checklist for each development phase, and the system control standards covering functional, security and automated control features.

artifacts.name: Requirements Traceability Matrix
artifacts.description: The traceability matrix linking each requirement through design, development, testing and deployment; the requirements change control records; the requirements review records; and the business owner sign-off.

artifacts.name: Requirements Approval Records
artifacts.description: The business and information security approval records for the requirements, the management approval, the evidence that control standards were applied during development, and the documented system acceptance criteria the requirements are tested against.

artifacts.name: Threat Model and Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The threat models created during the design phase for sample projects, the system threat and risk assessment reports, and the security requirements derived from them rather than from a generic checklist.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Documentation
artifacts.description: The secure development policy embedding security activities throughout the lifecycle, the documentation of each phase with its security gates and deliverables, the security review gate records before release, and the developer secure coding training records.

artifacts.name: Pipeline Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The continuous integration and delivery pipeline configuration with embedded static, dynamic and composition security scanning, evidencing the requirements are enforced automatically rather than only reviewed.

artifacts.name: Software Composition Records
artifacts.description: The software bill of materials, the third-party component inventory, and the component vulnerability tracking showing which incorporated components carry known weaknesses.

artifacts.name: Security Testing Records
artifacts.description: The security testing strategy defining types and coverage across the release cycle, the test plans per release with security test cases, the security acceptance test results before go-live, the penetration test reports, the bug bounty programme reports, the retest and closure evidence, and the documentation of the isolated test environments used.

artifacts.name: Solution Design and Test Records
artifacts.description: The development standards and quality assurance test plans, the high-level and detailed solution design documents, the procurement and build approval documentation, and the test results with defect tracking.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Assurance
artifacts.description: The development supplier contracts including security, intellectual property and testing obligations, the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses, the source code escrow arrangement, the assessment of the supplier's development maturity, the security test results from deliverables, the organisation-side code review, and the periodic vendor quality and security reports.

artifacts.name: Acquisition Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The acquisition documentation, the security requirements written into contracts, and the vendor security assessment results for components brought in rather than built.

artifacts.name: AI System Requirements Records
artifacts.description: The documented requirements and specifications for new AI systems or material enhancements including the business, technical and regulatory rationale, with the traceability matrix linking them through to deployment artifacts.

artifacts.name: Control Framework Documentation
artifacts.description: The IT general controls framework documentation, the security management process documentation, the technology acquisition and development lifecycle controls, and the technology infrastructure control inventory the requirements are drawn from.

artifacts.name: Integration and Data Requirements Records
artifacts.description: The documented integration requirements and data hub technical requirements specifications with their compliance and implementation evidence, the data architecture artifacts, the data sharing agreements and interoperability standards, the register with a named owner, the organisational artifacts carrying accountability, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the security requirements analysis obligations and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

TDA-02.notes: 76 asks across 14 frameworks. Overlaps PRM-04; the distinction kept here is that these demands concern the security requirements themselves — how they are specified, approved and tested against — rather than the project governance around them.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Standard
artifacts.description: The approved secure software development lifecycle standard incorporating industry standards and best practices, the policy embedding security activities throughout the lifecycle, the secure development lifecycle documentation, the documentation of each phase with its security gates and deliverables, the security gate definitions, the evidence of security gates in each stage, the records of security gate approvals before release, and the process review records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented secure application design and development requirement.

artifacts.name: Secure Coding Standards
artifacts.description: The documented secure coding standards aligned to a recognised application security verification standard with language-specific guides, the secure coding policy, the template used to capture security requirements in user stories and specifications, and the training records for secure coding completion by developers.

artifacts.name: Design Review and Threat Modelling
artifacts.description: The threat models created during the design phase for sample projects, the sample secure design review and threat model artifacts for in-flight projects, and the high-level and detailed solution design documents they review.

artifacts.name: Security Testing Records
artifacts.description: The strategy defining testing types and coverage across the release cycle, the test plans for each release including security test cases, the continuous integration pipeline configuration with embedded static, dynamic and composition scans, the evidence of security acceptance testing prior to go-live, the penetration test reports, the bug bounty platform reports with valid findings, the retest and closure evidence after remediation, the documentation of isolated test environments used for security testing, and the source code review reports.

artifacts.name: Quality Assurance Standards
artifacts.description: The quality assurance standards covering validation of project assumptions, standards adherence and product performance testing; the management approval of those standards; the quality assurance checklist; the quality assurance review reports; the quality assurance process documentation; the development standards and quality assurance test plans; and the test results with the defect tracking records.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Controls
artifacts.description: The outsourced development agreements with the required clauses, the outsourcing agreements, the right-to-audit clauses in those agreements, the vendor supervision records, the staff rotation and termination records for outsourced work, the code ownership documentation, and the licensing documentation covering what was produced.

artifacts.name: Acquisition Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The acquisition documentation, the security requirements written into contracts, the vendor security assessment results, the supply chain assessment procedures, the weakness identification records, the remediation tracking documentation, and the solution procurement and build approval documentation.

artifacts.name: AI Development Process
artifacts.description: The documented AI design and development process covering lifecycle stages, testing requirements and means, and human oversight; the standard operating procedures supporting each stage of the responsible development process; the design documentation covering the machine learning approach, learning algorithm and model, training plan and data quality, and evaluation; and the final system architecture.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Records
artifacts.description: The approved organisational policies and procedures covering AI, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the AI impact assessment, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, the documented evidence demonstrating the outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

TDA-02.3.notes: 60 asks across 11 frameworks. The development methodology, the quality assurance function and the outsourced-development controls are three separable proofs; ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF contribute an AI-specific development process kept distinct from the general one.

artifacts.name: System Documentation Set
artifacts.description: The application documentation, the user manuals, the programming flowcharts, the documented workflow processes for applications, the system documentation, the templates for development, testing, training and operational documentation, and the procedures covering all system development documentation.

artifacts.name: Documentation Repository Controls
artifacts.description: The structure of the document repository showing organised storage per procedure, the evidence of access controls on documentation libraries, the documentation security controls preventing unauthorised access, the access rights records, the access logs, the version control records, and the audit report on library access controls. HITRUST requires the approved security of system documentation policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Documentation Completeness Review
artifacts.description: The audit evidence that documentation was produced per procedure for each project phase and the records of periodic documentation completeness reviews.

artifacts.name: AI Technical Documentation
artifacts.description: The technical documentation covering general description, intended purpose, usage instructions and technical assumptions; the plan for managing failures including rollback, feature toggling, update process and user notification; and the documentation of operations personnel roles, accountability for handling failures or updates, and management approvals.

artifacts.name: AI Event Logging Records
artifacts.description: The standard specifying logging across AI lifecycle phases covering traceability and detection, the sample event logs demonstrating that logging is implemented, and the retention policy aligned with intended use, organisational retention policies and applicable legal requirements.

artifacts.name: Data Architecture Documentation
artifacts.description: The documented data architecture and modelling register specification with its compliance evidence, the data architecture artifacts covering data models, entity relationship diagrams and design documentation, the implementation evidence demonstrating the outcome, the register or inventory evidencing the architecture register with a named owner, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: AI Governance Documentation Records
artifacts.description: The AI impact assessment, the documented evidence demonstrating the governance outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

artifacts.name: Documentation Access Review
artifacts.description: The access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, the user access provisioning, modification and review records, and the awareness communications informing personnel of the documentation security requirements.

TDA-04.notes: 36 asks across 5 frameworks. The documentation set, the access controls over it and the completeness review are three proofs; ISO 42001's AI technical documentation and event logging are separate obligations with their own content requirements.

artifacts.name: Secure Architecture Principles
artifacts.description: The documented secure architecture principles covering defence in depth, least privilege and zero trust; the reference architectures; the library of approved security patterns; the security design principles checklist; and the security architecture documentation.

artifacts.name: System Design Documents
artifacts.description: The design documents for sample systems showing application of the principles, the design specification documents, the system documentation, the database specification documents, and the data flow diagrams.

artifacts.name: Design Review Records
artifacts.description: The architecture review board minutes showing security review of architectures, the design review records, the design review meeting minutes, the security review checklist completion, the sample secure design review and threat model artifacts for in-flight projects, the issue tracking and resolution records, and the records of periodic documentation reviews.

artifacts.name: Architecture Deviation Register
artifacts.description: The register of approved deviations from the reference architectures, recording where a design departed from the standard and why.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Standards
artifacts.description: The approved secure software development lifecycle standard, the secure development lifecycle documentation, the documented secure coding standards, the evidence of security gates in each stage, the security gate definitions, and the process review records.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Controls
artifacts.description: The contracts with development suppliers including security, intellectual property and testing obligations; the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses; the assessment of the supplier's development lifecycle maturity and security practices; the security test results from vendor deliverables; the evidence of organisation-side code review of vendor-delivered code; the periodic quality and security reports from development vendors; and the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software.

artifacts.name: Solution Design Accountability
artifacts.description: The documented solution design specification with its compliance evidence, the implementation evidence demonstrating the outcome, the data architecture artifacts covering data models, entity relationship diagrams and design documentation, the data sharing agreements with their interoperability standards and integration documentation, and the periodic review records naming reviewer, date and corrective actions.

artifacts.name: AI Design Governance Records
artifacts.description: The AI impact assessment, the documented evidence demonstrating the governance outcome, the implementation records and artifacts evidencing it within the AI estate, and the periodic review records.

TDA-05.notes: 40 asks across 7 frameworks. Architecture principles, the design that applies them and the review that signs it off are three proofs; ISO 27001 A.8.30 outsourced development arrives here and is kept as its own artifact set.

artifacts.name: Secure SDLC Policy and Methodology
artifacts.description: The approved secure software development lifecycle policy and the methodology document implementing it, covering every lifecycle phase from requirements to retirement with the security activities, deliverables and quality-control processes at each. Must identify the development standards, tools and specific tool configurations used, state the security and privacy requirements the process must satisfy, define the testing, evaluation, verification and validation methods, and state the frequency at which the process, standards and tooling are reviewed - with the review records for the period. PCI DSS requires the standard to incorporate recognised industry standards and to show information security is embedded throughout; MAS TRM requires the agile variant with defined security integration points; ISO 42001 requires the equivalent for AI development including human oversight requirements. Include the documented secure engineering principles and any software assurance maturity model used (SCF).

artifacts.name: Secure Coding Standards and Code Review Checklist
artifacts.description: The organisation's secure coding standards, by language where applicable, referencing OWASP, CERT and CWE (explicitly required by QCB and MAS TRM), together with the security checklist used during peer code review. PCI DSS additionally requires a documented statement of the engineering techniques used to prevent each named attack category - injection flaws, attacks on data and data structures, cryptography misuse, business logic abuse, access control attacks - so the standard must address them individually rather than by general reference.

artifacts.name: Application Security Requirements and Acceptance Criteria
artifacts.description: The reusable catalogue of application security requirements (ASVS-based or equivalent) and the template used to capture security requirements in specifications and user stories, plus, for a sample of real projects, the completed security requirements specification, the system acceptance criteria, the business and technical requirement documents, and the sign-off showing security or architecture approved them. Must include the API security standard covering authentication, authorisation, input validation and rate limiting (ISO 27001) and, for ADHICS, the business and information security approval records for new-system security requirements.

artifacts.name: Threat Models and Secure Design Documentation
artifacts.description: Design-phase security artifacts for a sample of systems: threat models (STRIDE or equivalent), the documented secure architecture principles (defence in depth, least privilege, zero trust) and the design-principles checklist applied against them, reference architectures with security built in, the security pattern library for common flows such as authentication and data protection, system design documents showing the principles were applied, architecture review board minutes recording security review of designs, and the register of approved deviations from reference architecture. Include the enterprise architecture documentation and roadmap (COBIT), the final AI system architecture with its security threat model (ISO 42001), and the secure design documentation covering TLS configuration for data in transit and the authentication and session management controls (PISF 2026).

artifacts.name: SDLC Security Gate and Release Approval Records
artifacts.description: The definition of the security gates at each SDLC stage and the records showing each gate was actually passed for a sample of releases: security review approvals before release, build pipeline gates configured to break the build on critical findings, code security validation and approval prior to deployment, sprint security review records for agile teams, and evidence that the SDLC methodology was applied to both in-house development and acquired software. PISF 2026 additionally requires independent third-party testing records for critical software before release.

artifacts.name: CI/CD Pipeline Security Configuration
artifacts.description: The pipeline configuration showing security scanning embedded in the build and deployment path - SAST, DAST, IAST and SCA tooling integrated and enforced - together with evidence of environment separation between development, test and production and the access controls on source code and artifact repositories. CSA CCM requires records demonstrating that automated secure application deployment is actually operating in the cloud environment, not merely configured.

artifacts.name: Application Security Test Reports (SAST, DAST, SCA, Penetration)
artifacts.description: Scan and test reports covering the period: static analysis per release, dynamic testing for web-facing applications, software composition analysis identifying vulnerable dependencies, and vulnerability assessment and penetration test reports with remediation tracking to closure. PCI DSS additionally requires a mapping of SAST and DAST rule sets to each named attack category to demonstrate coverage; MAS TRM requires the agile-cadence security testing records; HITRUST requires the code review records alongside the SAST/DAST/penetration results as one body of evidence.

artifacts.name: Code Review Records
artifacts.description: A sample of pull requests or merge requests showing security-relevant review comments raised and resolved before merge, with reviewer identity and date. PCI DSS additionally requires sample code or library evidence of the mitigations themselves in place - parameterised queries, output encoding, CSRF tokens, role-based access checks - not just the review that approved them.

artifacts.name: Developer Secure Coding Training Records
artifacts.description: Completion records for secure coding and secure SDLC training by developers and engineers, showing who was trained, on what module, and when. SBP ETGRMF requires the training to evidence developer awareness of the organisation's Secure SDLC requirements specifically; HITRUST requires awareness communications with attendee list, delivery dates and content demonstrating personnel were informed of the requirement.

artifacts.name: Application Risk Assessment and Acquisition Security Evaluation
artifacts.description: The risk assessment performed per application that drives which security requirements apply, and the security evaluation performed on COTS and SaaS software before acquisition, with the acquisition documentation and vendor security assessment results. Must link risk assessment outputs to the security requirements selected (ADHICS) and show operational risk assessments embedded within the SDLC phases (SBP ETGRMF). NIS2 requires the proportionality assessment justifying that the measures chosen are appropriate to entity size and risk exposure, with the incident likelihood and severity analysis behind it.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Contracts and Vendor Assurance Evidence
artifacts.description: For development performed by suppliers: the development agreement including security, testing, IP ownership and confidentiality obligations, the assessment of the supplier's own SDLC maturity and security practices, evidence of organisation-side code review of vendor-delivered code, the vendor's security test results (SAST, DAST, penetration) for its deliverables, periodic vendor quality and security reports, and the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software. NIST 800-53 requires the security requirements to appear in the contracts themselves.

artifacts.name: Approved Component Inventory and Provenance Verification
artifacts.description: The list of approved, vetted security components and libraries developers may use, the vetting records behind approvals, documented justification wherever a team implemented its own instead of using an approved component, records showing components are kept current, and verification that components are obtained from trusted sources with dependency scan results supporting it. Required by CIS CSC as the counterpart to secure coding standards.

artifacts.name: Input, Processing and Output Validation Controls Documentation
artifacts.description: The application-control layer that makes processing complete, accurate and authorised: documented data processing specifications, input validation controls with error handling, internal processing validation requirements and controls, output validation and reconciliation procedures, input-to-output reconciliation reports, transaction authorisation procedures and their logs, automated validation and quality-check configurations, output delivery verification and acknowledgement logs, output distribution access controls, and report generation completeness and accuracy validation. HITRUST requires an approved policy plus an implementing procedure for each of input validation, control of internal processing and output validation separately, along with periodic review records; ADHICS requires developer compliance evidence and reviews of validation check effectiveness.

artifacts.name: Processing Error Monitoring and Correction Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that processing failures are detected, corrected and prevented from recurring: processing accuracy monitoring reports, data quality metrics and dashboards, exception and error detection reports, the documented error correction, reprocessing and resubmission procedures, and root cause analysis for recurring processing errors. Required by SOC 2 processing integrity criteria.

artifacts.name: Data Storage Integrity and Retention Controls
artifacts.description: Controls protecting stored and archived data used by the application: storage integrity controls including checksums, database integrity monitoring configuration, storage access control configuration, application and database hardening evidence (QCB requires this for core banking systems specifically), and the documented archival and retention procedures covering both output and stored data.

TDA-06.notes: 142 entries from 16 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts, all assigned exactly once. The control's automated list is empty, but the platform has SAST/SCA connectors (Semgrep, SonarCloud) and repo connectors, so scan reports, pipeline configuration and code review records are marked automated or hybrid on the basis that a connector can genuinely produce them. The large SOC 2 and HITRUST processing-integrity block (input validation, error handling, output validation, storage integrity) is kept as three separate artifacts rather than folded into the SDLC ones - they are application-control evidence a different team produces.

artifacts.name: Environment Separation Standard
artifacts.description: The standard defining required separation between development, test and production; the environment separation documentation; the environment inventory; the architecture diagram showing separation between production and pre-production; the environment architecture diagram showing segregation; the environment topology diagram; the test environment architecture documentation; and the environment configuration management documentation. HITRUST requires the approved separation of development and production policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Environment Network Segmentation
artifacts.description: The firewall rules or cloud security group configurations enforcing separation between environments, the network security control configuration evidence, and the environment isolation evidence.

artifacts.name: Environment Access Controls
artifacts.description: The matrix showing who has access to each environment and for what purpose, the access control configuration, the access control records for test environments, the access privilege reports per environment, the environment access controls, the access approvals for non-production, the non-production access records for third-party developers, the third-party change request records, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Developer Production Access Review
artifacts.description: The review of any developer access to production with its justification and expiry, evidencing the separation is not routinely bypassed.

artifacts.name: Non-Production Data Controls
artifacts.description: The evidence that production data is not used in development or test without masking, the data masking procedures for non-production use, and the data sanitisation procedures applied to lower environments.

artifacts.name: Promotion Pipeline Controls
artifacts.description: The deployment pipeline configuration enforcing environment promotion controls, the change approval records required before promoting code to production, the production promotion checklists and authorisation records, the release and deployment plans with their rollback procedures, the user acceptance testing results with their sign-off documentation, the post-implementation review reports with lessons learned, the change management procedure with advisory board approvals and back-out plans, and the change records with their risk classification.
