CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented automated secure application deployment requirement.

artifacts.name: Segmentation Penetration Testing
artifacts.description: The inventory of segmentation controls in scope of testing, the latest segmentation penetration test report at least annually and after changes to those controls, the test evidence confirming all out-of-scope networks remain isolated, and the remediation records for what the test found.

artifacts.name: Service Provider Segmentation Testing
artifacts.description: The service-provider segmentation penetration test reports at least every six months and after changes, the schedule and history of that six-monthly testing, the evidence of coverage of all isolation and segmentation mechanisms, and the remediation records arising.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The policy embedding security activities throughout the development lifecycle, the documentation of each phase with its security gates and deliverables, the lifecycle documentation with security gates, the security requirements written into each phase, the security role assignments in projects, the template used to capture security requirements in specifications, the records of security gate approvals before release, the threat models created during design, the pipeline configuration with embedded security scans, and the developer secure coding training records.

TDA-07.notes: 55 asks across 10 frameworks. Environment separation, the data used in the lower environments and the promotion path between them are three proofs; PCI DSS 11.4.5 and 11.4.6 segmentation testing sit here and are kept as their own artifacts because they are periodic tests rather than standing configuration.

artifacts.name: Environment Separation Standard
artifacts.description: The standard defining the required separation between development, test and production, the approved policy and its implementing procedure, and the environment inventory listing each environment with its purpose and controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented production and non-production separation.

artifacts.name: Environment Architecture Diagram
artifacts.description: The architecture and topology diagrams showing the separation between production and pre-production, the test environment architecture documentation, and the segregation architecture for each environment tier.

artifacts.name: Network Segmentation Configuration
artifacts.description: The firewall rules or cloud security group configuration enforcing separation between environments, the network security control configuration evidencing it, and the environment isolation evidence.

artifacts.name: Environment Access Control Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix showing who has access to each environment and for what purpose, the access control configuration and approvals for non-production, the access privilege reports per environment, and the access provisioning, modification and review records.

artifacts.name: Developer Production Access Evidence
artifacts.description: The segregation-of-duties policy prohibiting developer access to production, the access review records showing no developer holds it, the review of any exception with justification and expiry, and the internal audit report confirming compliance.

artifacts.name: Test Data Masking Evidence
artifacts.description: The data masking procedures for non-production use, the evidence that production data is not used in development or test without masking, the data handling procedures between environments, the test data management records, and the data sanitisation procedures and records for test environments.

artifacts.name: Test Data and Account Removal Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for removing test data and test accounts before production release, the production deployment checklist covering it, sample sign-off records confirming removal for recent deployments, and the periodic scan of production for residual test accounts.

artifacts.name: Deployment Pipeline Configuration
artifacts.description: The CI/CD pipeline configuration enforcing environment promotion controls with embedded security scanning, the automated secure application deployment records, the inter-environment transfer procedures, and the release and deployment plans with rollback procedures.

artifacts.name: Production Promotion Approval Records
artifacts.description: The change approval records required before promoting code to production, the promotion checklists and authorisation records, the change records with risk classification, and the change management procedure with board approvals and back-out plans.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Documentation
artifacts.description: The secure development policy embedding security activities throughout the lifecycle, the documentation of each phase with its security gates and deliverables, the security requirements template used in specifications, the threat modelling artifacts created during design, the security review gate records, and the developer secure coding training records.

artifacts.name: Pre-Release Testing Records
artifacts.description: The test plans and cases, the test execution results with sign-off, user acceptance testing results and approval documentation, the pre-implementation testing results, the system acceptance criteria with sign-off, and the independent testing records for critical software before release.

artifacts.name: Change Security Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The security impact analysis reports and change risk assessment documentation performed before a change is promoted, evidencing the effect on the production environment was assessed.

artifacts.name: Production Environment Controls
artifacts.description: The policy prohibiting testing in the production environment, the production system software inventory, the test user account inventory, and the non-production environment configuration documentation.

artifacts.name: Post-Implementation Review Records
artifacts.description: The post-implementation review reports with lessons learned, evidencing the promotion achieved its intent and the environments remained separated through it.

artifacts.name: Integration Testing and Data Architecture Records
artifacts.description: The documented integration solution testing and business intelligence use case plan specifications with their compliance evidence, the data architecture artifacts and models, the data quality profiling reports, the data sharing and integration documentation, the register with a named owner, and the performance metrics dashboard.

TDA-08.notes: 92 asks across 16 frameworks. Three distinct demands: the environments must be separated (architecture, network, access), production data must not appear in them unmasked, and test artifacts must not survive into production. The third is PCI DSS 6.5.6 and is easy to lose inside the first two, so it is kept apart.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Policy and Standard
artifacts.description: Approved, current policy and supporting standard that embeds security, compliance and resilience activities into every SDLC phase, naming the phases, the security gate at each, deliverables, and the roles that must be consulted (security, compliance, resilience personnel). Must show management approval, version history, review cadence and the development/coding standards it mandates. CSA CCM additionally expects records that the design and development practice is actually operating in the cloud environment, and HITRUST expects a separate step-by-step procedure or work instruction beneath the policy.

artifacts.name: Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) Plan and Testing Schedule
artifacts.description: Documented plan or strategy defining the types of security testing performed (SAST, DAST, IAST, SCA, penetration testing, configuration assessment, code review), the breadth, depth and coverage of each, who owns them, and at what point in the lifecycle and at what frequency they run. Must be accompanied by the forward schedule or annual testing calendar showing planned assessments per system or software module. NIST 800-53 frames this as the developer's own security testing plan; SBP ETGRMF requires it as an approved policy plus a dated annual calendar; ISO 27001 expects release-level test plans containing the specific security test cases.

artifacts.name: Application Security Testing Reports and Pipeline Scan Configuration
artifacts.description: Output of the automated application security testing tooling plus the configuration proving it runs at the right point: SAST, DAST, IAST, SCA and fuzzing reports for in-scope applications, and the CI/CD pipeline configuration showing the scans are wired into the build with their pass/fail thresholds. Reports must identify the scanned application, version, scan date, tool and findings by severity. PCI DSS accepts equivalent manual review where automated tooling is not used; SBP ETGRMF requires scan outputs per software module; QCB requires reports mapped to each lifecycle stage.

artifacts.name: Penetration Test and Bug Bounty Reports
artifacts.description: Independent penetration test and vulnerability assessment reports covering in-scope applications, with scope, methodology, tester, dates, findings by severity and retest verification. ISO 27001 expects these prior to major releases; SBP ETGRMF expects sample VA and PT reports with remediation status attached. Where a bug bounty or crowd-sourced testing programme runs, include the platform reports covering the period with the valid findings accepted.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Disclosure Process Records
artifacts.description: The published vulnerability disclosure policy or channel through which external parties report weaknesses, together with the intake records for reports received in the period and evidence that each was acknowledged, triaged and responded to within the committed timeline. Sourced from CIS CSC, which is the only framework here asking for the external intake path as distinct from the organisation's own testing.

artifacts.name: Peer Code Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented code review procedure plus a sample of completed reviews for recent releases. The procedure must require review by a knowledgeable individual other than the originating developer, application of the secure coding guidelines, and management review and approval of results. Samples should be pull-request or merge-request approvals from the source control platform showing reviewer identity distinct from author, date, and the reviewer checklist applied. HITRUST and SL CSF accept the same review records as evidence of the SDLC checkpoint operating.

artifacts.name: Secure Coding Standard and Attack-Category Coverage Mapping
artifacts.description: Documented engineering techniques the organisation requires developers to apply for each category of common software attack, and the mapping showing how the review checklist and the SAST/DAST rule sets cover each category. PCI DSS enumerates the categories that must each be addressed: injection, data and data-structure attacks, cryptographic misuse, business logic flaws including cross-site scripting and request forgery, access control bypass, and any other high-risk vulnerability identified by the organisation. Include sample implementation evidence such as parameterised queries, output encoding, anti-CSRF tokens or authorisation checks.

artifacts.name: Security Requirements, Threat Models and Design Analysis
artifacts.description: Design-stage artefacts showing security was engineered in before testing: the documented security and privacy requirements for the system (with the risk assessment output they derive from), the threat models or attack surface reviews produced during design, and any structured failure analysis such as FMEA. Must show business and information security approval of the requirements, the acceptance criteria the system will be tested against, and for data-centric systems the data models, ERDs and design documentation. ADHICS is most prescriptive here, requiring business plus security sign-off on the requirements set.

artifacts.name: System Test Plans and Test Execution Results
artifacts.description: Functional, regression, integration and acceptance test plans with the corresponding execution records and results. Plans must cover predetermined test data, expected processing problems and realistic business scenarios; results must show scope, methodology, executor, date, pass/fail outcome, defects raised and re-test evidence. Includes change-related and regression testing before deployment (MAS TRM), the QA test plans and defect records (COBIT), security acceptance test results prior to go-live (ISO 27001), and the data quality/profiling and integration testing records demanded for data platforms (NDMO).

artifacts.name: Security Defect and Flaw Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: A single tracker demonstrating the verifiable flaw remediation loop: every weakness found by testing, scanning, code review or disclosure, with severity, owner, target date, remediation action, retest result and closure date. Must show that identified vulnerabilities were corrected and re-verified before release (PCI DSS), that major issues were escalated to management (MAS TRM), that root cause analysis and lessons learned were recorded for significant defects (CIS CSC), and that findings from formal security assessments are tracked to closure (SBP ETGRMF, QCB, NIST 800-53).

artifacts.name: Pre-Release Security Gate and Acceptance Sign-Off Records
artifacts.description: Records of the formal go/no-go decision before release: security gate approvals showing the required testing was completed and findings closed or accepted, and system acceptance sign-off against the documented acceptance criteria. Each record must carry the date, the approver, the system and release being approved, and reference to the test evidence relied on.

artifacts.name: Test Environment and Test Data Controls Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that testing happens in controlled environments and leaves nothing behind in production: documentation of the isolated test/UAT environments used, the policy prohibiting testing in production, the documented procedure for removing test data and test accounts before go-live, the deployment checklist enforcing it, and sample sign-off records confirming removal for recent releases. Supporting inventories: test user accounts held, and production software inventory showing development tools are not present. PCI DSS additionally expects a periodic scan of production for residual test accounts.

artifacts.name: Independent Quality Assurance Function Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that quality assurance of in-house development is performed independently of the development team: the QA charter establishing the function, organisational evidence of its reporting line separate from development, the documented QA methodology showing security and vulnerability testing coverage, and the QA review reports issued for in-house developments. Required specifically by SBP ETGRMF.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Security Assurance Pack
artifacts.description: Where development is outsourced, the evidence that the same testing rigour applies to supplier deliverables: the development contract clauses covering security, testing obligations, intellectual property and confidentiality; the assessment of the supplier's own secure SDLC maturity; the organisation-side code review of delivered code; the supplier's security test results (SAST, DAST, penetration); periodic quality and security reports; and any source code escrow arrangement for critical software. PISF 2026 adds supply chain risk assessment and records of security testing performed during procurement; NDMO adds the data sharing, interoperability and API documentation governing integrated deliverables.

artifacts.name: Developer Secure Coding Training Records
artifacts.description: Training completion records for developers covering secure coding, showing who was trained, on what module, when, and completion status; plus the awareness communications evidencing that engineering personnel were informed of the testing and remediation requirements they must follow.

TDA-09.notes: 109 manual entries across 14 frameworks collapsed to 15 artifacts. No evidence collectors are wired to this control, so nothing is marked fully automated; scan-report and defect-tracker items are hybrid because the tooling exists platform-wide (SAST/DAST/CI) but coverage and sign-off must be attested. Frameworks split into three recurring asks: the plan (ST&E strategy), the execution (scans, pen tests, code reviews, system tests), and the closure loop (flaw remediation, retest, gate sign-off). PCI DSS is the only source demanding attack-category coverage mapping and test-data removal; SBP ETGRMF is the only source demanding an independent QA function; ISO 27001 A.8.30 carries almost the whole outsourced-development ask.

artifacts.name: Test Data Policy
artifacts.description: The policy on sourcing, protecting and disposing of test data; the approved policy prohibiting live regulated data in pre-production environments unless those environments are in scope; the policy prohibiting use of non-desensitised production data in testing; the test data management policy; the documented testing programme covering internal and external stakeholder participation and data-masking requirements; and the inter-environment transfer procedures. HITRUST requires the approved protection of system test data policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Data Masking Configuration
artifacts.description: The configuration of data masking or synthetic data generation tooling used to provide pre-production data, the configuration of masking tools for producing safe test data, the procedure for generating synthetic data where real data is unsuitable, the data masking procedures, the standard operating procedure for masking production data when external parties are involved, and the sample masking tool output evidencing desensitisation.

artifacts.name: Masking Verification Records
artifacts.description: The data discovery scan of pre-production environments confirming no live regulated data is present, the records of data desensitisation before use in testing, the evidence of masking validation before external testing, and the anonymisation evidence for personal data.

artifacts.name: Test Data Use Approval Records
artifacts.description: The approval records required before using any data copied from production, the production data usage authorisation records, and the information owner approvals when desensitised production data is used in testing.

artifacts.name: Test Data Disposal Records
artifacts.description: The records of test data deletion after testing completes, the post-test data erasure confirmation, the data sanitisation records for test environments, the test data lifecycle records, and the test data management records.

artifacts.name: Test Data Access Controls
artifacts.description: The access controls applied to test data stores equivalent to production sensitivity, the test data access controls, the access privilege reports per environment, and the data protection records covering the test estate.

artifacts.name: Environment Segregation Records
artifacts.description: The environment segregation architecture diagrams, the environment architecture diagram showing segregation, the environment configuration management documentation, and the evidence of full protection coverage where the pre-production environment is itself in scope.

artifacts.name: Test Execution Records
artifacts.description: The reports from the testing programme exercises with results and improvement actions, the log showing participation of business line management, incident response and crisis teams and other functions, and the sample test data sets used.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Lifecycle Records
artifacts.description: The lifecycle documentation with its security gates, the security requirements written into each phase, and the security role assignments in projects.

artifacts.name: Data Location Records
artifacts.description: The data location controls. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented data location requirement.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the test data restrictions and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

TDA-10.notes: 45 asks across 9 frameworks. The prohibition, the masking that makes compliance possible, and the discovery scan that proves it are three proofs; the discovery scan is what an assessor actually samples and is kept separate.

artifacts.name: Independent Quality Assurance Function
artifacts.description: The charter establishing an independent quality assurance function for in-house developments, the organisational evidence showing that function reports independently of development, the documented quality assurance methodology including security and vulnerability testing coverage, and the reports of quality assurance reviews of in-house developments for vulnerabilities posing risk.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Disclosure Programme
artifacts.description: The vulnerability disclosure policy, the vulnerability intake records, and the response timeline documentation committing to how quickly a reported flaw is triaged and fixed.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Standards
artifacts.description: The approved secure software development lifecycle standard incorporating industry standards and best practices, the evidence of security gates in each stage, the documented secure coding standards aligned to a recognised application security verification standard, the documented engineering techniques addressing each common attack category, the sample code or library evidence of the mitigations implemented, and the sample secure design review and threat model artifacts.

artifacts.name: Developer Security Training Records
artifacts.description: The approved secure coding training curriculum covering software security relevant to the technologies in use, the learning management records of completion at least once every twelve months for all developers of bespoke and custom software, and the sample completion certificates and acknowledgments.

artifacts.name: Code Review Records
artifacts.description: The procedure mandating pre-release reviews by knowledgeable individuals other than the originating developer, the code review checklist, the sample pull-request approvals showing reviewer sign-off, the static application security testing reports, the mapping of scanner rule sets to each attack category demonstrating coverage, and the evidence of identified vulnerabilities corrected prior to release with re-review confirmation.

artifacts.name: Flaw Remediation Records
artifacts.description: The flaw remediation documentation, the developer security testing plan, the testing results and reports, and the application vulnerability remediation records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented application vulnerability remediation requirement.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Intelligence and Tracking
artifacts.description: The inventory of vulnerability intelligence sources subscribed to, the documented risk ranking methodology aligned with industry sources, the documented vulnerability management procedure covering identification and ranking, and the tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status.

artifacts.name: Penetration Testing Programme
artifacts.description: The documented penetration testing methodology covering industry-accepted approaches and critical system coverage, the periodic review and update records for that methodology, the documentation of tester qualifications and organisational independence, the finding tracker with risk ranking, owner and remediation status, the documented risk-based remediation plan with timelines per severity, and the retest or rescan records demonstrating remediation.

artifacts.name: Public Web Application Protection
artifacts.description: The annual security assessment report covering each public-facing web application, the post-change reassessment records, the tracker of identified vulnerabilities with correction status and reassessment confirmation, the configuration export of the web application firewall or runtime protection deployed in front of those applications, the evidence it operates in blocking mode or that its alerts are promptly investigated, the rule-set currency records, and the sample audit logs showing detection and blocking.

artifacts.name: Nonconformity and Corrective Action Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining handling of nonconformities including reaction, root-cause analysis, corrective action and effectiveness review; the log of nonconformities with cause analysis, similar-nonconformity checks and actions taken; the root cause analyses for material nonconformities; the control deficiency tracking and remediation log; the corrective action plans with timelines and status; the management reporting on control exceptions; the board reporting on significant deficiencies; and the records reviewing the effectiveness of corrective actions.

artifacts.name: Standards Alignment Records
artifacts.description: The standards mapping and alignment documentation, the gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation, and the segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records.

TDA-15.notes: 61 asks across 9 frameworks. Overlaps IAO-04 substantially; what is distinct here is the developer-side obligation — the independent quality assurance function and the vulnerability disclosure intake — rather than the assurance programme that tests the result.

artifacts.name: End-of-Life Inventory
artifacts.description: The register tracking end-of-life software with its remediation and replacement plans, the end-of-life component inventory, the end-of-life software tracking, the end-of-life and end-of-support tracker, the out-of-support inventory monitoring, the inventory of installed software with versions compared against vendor-supported versions, the technology systems inventory with its currency assessment, the technology lifecycle tracking records, the end-of-support monitoring reports and dashboards, and the supported software verification records.

artifacts.name: Replacement and Refresh Plans
artifacts.description: The replacement and migration plans, the annual refresh plan with its milestones, and the technology resilience assessment informing the sequencing.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance for Unsupported Components
artifacts.description: The risk acceptance for unsupported components, the risk acceptance for unsupported software, and the risk assessment for retained end-of-life systems with the compensating controls applied to them.

artifacts.name: Dispensation Records
artifacts.description: The management dispensation records for end-of-support systems and the periodic dispensation review records confirming the exception is still warranted.

artifacts.name: Patch and Version Management
artifacts.description: The policy mandating installation of updated software versions with a defined cadence, the patch compliance report showing the compliance rate across the estate, the system update and maintenance records, the configuration baseline documentation with its hardening standards, and the capacity planning documentation supporting the upgrades. HITRUST requires the approved control of operational software policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: AI Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The decommissioning and deactivation procedure, the approved organisational policies and procedures, the context documentation covering intended purposes, the safety evaluation records including fail-safe behaviour, and the documented evidence demonstrating the outcome.

artifacts.name: Data Platform Versioning Records
artifacts.description: The approved data management and personal data protection strategy; the documented database management system versioning and tool versioning specifications with their compliance evidence; the metadata repository or data catalog export; the register or inventory evidencing tool versioning with a named owner; the compliance audit reports and assessment records; the data security control evidence including access controls; and the privacy artifacts.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the operational software controls and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

TDA-17.notes: 42 asks across 9 frameworks. The end-of-life inventory, the replacement plan and the risk acceptance for what stays are three proofs; the dispensation record is kept separate because it is the named authority behind each retained unsupported system.

artifacts.name: Input Validation Rules
artifacts.description: The input validation criteria and rules documentation, the input validation configuration documentation, the input validation procedures, the input validation controls, the input validation rule configuration, and the application code or configuration implementing the validation. HITRUST requires the approved input data validation policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Validation Test Evidence
artifacts.description: The application input validation testing, the invalid input handling test results, the test plans covering all testing phases, the test execution results with defect tracking, the user acceptance sign-off from business users, and the code review records with their security testing results.

artifacts.name: Error Handling and Correction Records
artifacts.description: The error handling documentation, the input error correction records, the source data reconciliation evidence, the data feed documentation with its verification, and the output verification and processing controls documentation.

artifacts.name: Secure Development Records
artifacts.description: The secure development lifecycle documentation with its security checkpoints and the coding standards documentation defining how validation is to be written.

artifacts.name: Journal Entry Controls
artifacts.description: The journal entry application security configuration, the exception reporting configuration for unusual entries, the journal entry audit trail reports, and the preparer and approver segregation evidence.

artifacts.name: Integrity Verification Records
artifacts.description: The file integrity monitoring configuration, the integrity verification tool reports, and the unauthorised change detection records covering the code that performs the validation.

artifacts.name: Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The role-based access control documentation, the access control list configurations, the access enforcement testing results, the account management procedures, the account review documentation, the user access authorisation records, the terminated user account records, the separation of duties matrix, the role definitions with incompatible duties identified, and the system access authorisation records.

artifacts.name: Malware and Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The anti-malware solution documentation with its definition update records, scan reports and incident records; the intrusion detection and prevention configuration; the security information platform deployment documentation; the system monitoring strategy; the monitoring alert review records; the security alert subscription records; the internal security advisory procedures; and the advisory review and response records.

artifacts.name: Awareness Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the input validation requirements that bind them.

TDA-18.notes: 51 asks across 5 frameworks. The validation rules, the test that proves invalid input is rejected and the handling of what fails are three proofs; NIST 800-53 contributes a wide adjacent set covering access, malware and monitoring that is kept separate from input validation itself.

artifacts.name: Source Code Access Policy
artifacts.description: The policy governing read and write access to repositories and build systems, the source code access authorisation records, and the source code repository access control list. HITRUST requires the approved access control to program source code policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Repository Access Records
artifacts.description: The repository export showing members and permissions, the access logs to source code repositories, the repository audit log showing access, pushes, merges and setting changes, the log of developer account creation and removal aligned to employment status, and the non-production access records for third-party developers with their change request records.

artifacts.name: Repository Protection Configuration
artifacts.description: The branch protection rules requiring reviews and status checks, the secrets scanning configuration in repositories, and the code signing certificate management showing certificates held in a hardware security module with restricted access.

artifacts.name: Secured Migration Library
artifacts.description: The documentation of the secured library or quarantine area for pre-migration programs, the configuration screenshots showing restricted access to it, the access control records for the library, and the records of migration processes using it.

artifacts.name: Code Integrity Verification
artifacts.description: The software code integrity verification records and the release traceability documentation.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Controls
artifacts.description: The contracts with development suppliers including security, intellectual property and testing obligations; the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses; the assessment of the supplier's development lifecycle maturity and security practices; the security test results from vendor deliverables; the evidence of organisation-side code review of vendor-delivered code; the periodic quality and security reports from development vendors; and the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software.

artifacts.name: Acquisition Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The acquisition documentation, the security requirements written into contracts, and the vendor security assessment results for acquired code.

artifacts.name: Development Lifecycle and Access Review
artifacts.description: The secure development lifecycle documentation with its security checkpoints, the code review records with their security testing results, the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping, and the user access provisioning, modification and review records covering the repository population.

TDA-20.notes: 34 asks across 7 frameworks. Repository access control, the audit log over it and the secured pre-migration library are three proofs; outsourced development arrives through ISO 27001 A.8.30 and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Threat Intelligence Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented process for collecting, analysing, disseminating and retiring threat intelligence, the gathering procedure covering participants, service providers and ecosystem sources, and the capability documentation. CSA CCM and NIST 800-171 accept configuration evidence in place of the documented process.

artifacts.name: Threat Intelligence Source Register
artifacts.description: The register of intelligence feeds — commercial, open source, sector body, government — with coverage, frequency and cost; the subscriptions held; and the register of sources including peers and ecosystem participants.

artifacts.name: Indicator Ingestion Evidence
artifacts.description: The log of indicators pushed into detection tooling with their correlation results, the intelligence platform dashboard showing active indicators and feeds, the technical feed integration evidence, the consumption and action records, and the detection update records.

artifacts.name: Threat Landscape Reporting
artifacts.description: The periodic analyst-produced report on threats relevant to the organisation's sector and assets, the threat intelligence reports distributed internally, the ecosystem attack indicator log, and the evidence of regular threat briefings delivered to leadership and operations teams.

artifacts.name: Information Sharing Arrangements
artifacts.description: The information sharing agreements or arrangements, the governance framework for the sharing, the documented participation conditions, the trusted community membership documentation, and the protocols for public authority involvement. NIS2 and DORA both require the arrangement to be documented before sharing begins.

artifacts.name: Sharing Community Membership Records
artifacts.description: The membership evidence for sector response and information sharing platforms, the participation logs recording downloads, submissions and contributions, the records of national and international cooperation linkages, and the technical connector evidence for the exchange feeds.

artifacts.name: Shared Indicator Records
artifacts.description: The log of threat intelligence received from and shared with peers, the shared indicator and compromise records, and the information exchange records with the industry platform.

artifacts.name: Data Protection for Shared Information
artifacts.description: The documented data protection measures applied to information before it is shared and the compliance records for them, evidencing that sharing does not itself create an exposure.

artifacts.name: Regulator Notification Records
artifacts.description: The competent authority notification records for participation in sharing arrangements, the membership validation documentation, the membership change notifications, and the withdrawal notifications.

artifacts.name: Escalation Criteria to Sector Response Body
artifacts.description: The documented mechanism for sharing threat, incident and breach data with the sector response body, with the defined criteria for when escalation is required.

artifacts.name: Cyber Security Action Plan
artifacts.description: The board-approved action plan addressing anticipation, withstanding, detection and response, the board resolution approving it, the implementation tracker and status dashboard, the periodic board reports on progress, and the mapping to international frameworks.

artifacts.name: Threat-to-Control Mapping
artifacts.description: The indicator and severity matrix, the inventory of preventive controls mapped to the threats they address, the incident response playbooks and quarantine procedures for the threats identified, and the phishing monitoring procedures with the incident response records arising from them.

artifacts.name: Continuous Control Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence for monitoring security alerts and advisories and for monitoring security controls continuously, with the records demonstrating each is implemented and operating.

artifacts.name: Post-Incident Improvement Records
artifacts.description: The post-incident review reports, the lessons learned documentation, and the framework improvement action plans arising from them, evidencing intelligence and incidents feed the programme back.

artifacts.name: Fraud and Insider Threat Records
artifacts.description: The fraud risk assessment documentation, the anti-fraud controls inventory, the background check and screening procedures, and the insider threat programme documentation — the internal counterpart of external threat intelligence.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance documentation informed by the threat picture.

THR-01.notes: 79 asks across 11 frameworks. Consuming intelligence and sharing it are different obligations with different evidence, and DORA Article 45 and NIS2 Article 29 govern the sharing arrangement specifically — including data-protection compliance for what is shared. Those are kept separate.

artifacts.name: Threat Intelligence Source Register
artifacts.description: The register of intelligence feeds — commercial, open source, sector body, government — with coverage, frequency and cost; the subscriptions held; the monitoring service agreements; the register of sources including peers and ecosystem participants; and the register of best-practice sources maintained.

artifacts.name: Indicator Ingestion Evidence
artifacts.description: The log of indicators pushed into detection tooling with their correlation results, the intelligence platform dashboard showing active indicators and feeds, the consumption and action records, and the ecosystem attack indicator log.

artifacts.name: Threat Intelligence Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented process for collecting, analysing, disseminating and retiring threat intelligence; the gathering procedure covering participants, service providers and ecosystem sources; the priority information identification process; and the capability documentation. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented monitoring requirement.

artifacts.name: Threat Analysis and Briefing Records
artifacts.description: The periodic analyst-produced report on threats relevant to the organisation's sector and assets, the threat intelligence analysis reports, the intelligence reports distributed internally, and the evidence of regular briefings delivered to leadership and operations teams.

artifacts.name: Security Advisory Subscription and Response
artifacts.description: The security alert subscription records, the internal security advisory procedures, the advisory review and response records, the vendor advisory monitoring records, and the records demonstrating alerts and advisories are monitored and acted upon.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Intelligence Records
artifacts.description: The inventory of vulnerability intelligence sources subscribed to, the documented risk ranking methodology aligned with industry sources for newly discovered vulnerabilities, the vulnerability management procedure covering identification from those sources, and the tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status.

artifacts.name: Emergency Patch Records
artifacts.description: The emergency patch standard operating procedure and examples of emergency patches deployed in response to intelligence, evidencing the feed drives action within a compressed timeframe when it needs to.

artifacts.name: External Event Analysis and Lessons
artifacts.description: The briefs analysing significant external cyber events and the lessons applicable to the organisation, the lessons-learned register capturing them alongside internal events, the improvement action plans implementing them, and the post-incident review reports.

artifacts.name: Sharing Community Membership Records
artifacts.description: The membership evidence for sector response and information sharing platforms, the participation records in threat information sharing, the coordination records with the sector regulator, and the records of national and international cooperation linkages.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Records
artifacts.description: The vulnerability management policy, the scanning reports with remediation tracking and timing, the patch management records with deployment evidence and exception register, and the remediation tracking showing intelligence closed the loop.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Component Intelligence
artifacts.description: The documented handling of vulnerabilities in external libraries and the penetration testing requirement, with the records demonstrating each operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Risk Register Updates from Intelligence
artifacts.description: The risk assessment reports, the risk register updates, the risk treatment plans and the threat scenario documentation showing intelligence feeds the risk picture rather than terminating in the security operations centre.

artifacts.name: Continuous Control Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence for monitoring security controls continuously, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the technical vulnerability controls and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

THR-03.notes: 68 asks across 14 frameworks. Distinct from THR-01 in that the demand here is the feed itself — sources subscribed, indicators ingested, advisories acted on — rather than the programme that governs it. PCI DSS 6.3.1's vulnerability intelligence is kept separate because it drives patching rather than detection.

artifacts.name: Threat Assessment Report
artifacts.description: The threat assessment report covering customer information, payments data, systems and applications; the threat register; the threat and vulnerability matrix; the risk assessment programme covering each required area; the threat impact analysis based on impact to the institution, customers and stakeholders; the risk assessment report; the stakeholder impact assessment; the register of customer impacts by threat scenario; and the prioritisation outputs derived from them.

artifacts.name: Threat to Asset Mapping
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping each identified threat or vulnerability to the affected assets, the latest vulnerability assessment report covering the infrastructure and applications in scope, and the monitoring evidence for the listed threats.

artifacts.name: Threat Scenario Library
artifacts.description: The library of threat scenarios used to evaluate business impact analysis assumptions, the threat scenario documentation, the workshop minutes where those assumptions were evaluated against scenarios, the records of threat scenarios evaluated against them, and the documentation confirming the assumptions were validated through scenario analysis.

artifacts.name: Threat Intelligence Inputs
artifacts.description: The evidence of threat intelligence feed subscriptions feeding the assessment, the register of intelligence sources including peers and ecosystem participants, the procedure for collecting and interpreting intelligence from participants, service providers and ecosystem sources, the threat intelligence reports, and the log of attack indicators relevant to ecosystem entities.

artifacts.name: Identity Theft Prevention Programme
artifacts.description: The approved identity theft prevention programme covering identification of protected information and theft and fraud detection; the procedure for identifying the information to be protected; the catalogue of identity theft and fraud threats considered; the configuration of detection rules supporting proactive identification; the response playbook detailing methods for responding; and the periodic statistics of identified cases with response times and outcomes.

artifacts.name: Identity Fraud Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The documented assessment of identity theft risks specific to the channel, the documented assessment of identity fraud risks covering synthetic identity, mule accounts and document forgery, the treatment plan listing controls implemented or planned, and the periodic loss statistics with trends, categories and lessons learned.

artifacts.name: Cloud Threat Testing
artifacts.description: The test case library covering hypervisor escape, weak interfaces, denial-of-service, wrapping attacks and other cloud-specific scenarios; the penetration testing reports explicitly exercising those scenarios with results and residual risk; the interface-specific testing evidence for all cloud-exposed interfaces with tool output and fix verification; and the mapping of each cloud-specific threat to implemented controls and test coverage. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented vulnerability management metrics requirement.

artifacts.name: Insider Threat Analysis
artifacts.description: The insider risk register, the threat-modelling outputs, and the mitigating control mapping against them.

artifacts.name: Availability Threat Analysis
artifacts.description: The network design denial-of-service analysis and the single-point-of-failure inventory arising from it.

artifacts.name: Facility Threat Assessment
artifacts.description: The data centre threat, vulnerability and risk assessment reports and the data centre protection measures documentation responding to them.

artifacts.name: Risk Register Updates
artifacts.description: The risk assessment reports, the risk register updates and the risk treatment plans showing the threat analysis fed the risk picture.

THR-10.notes: 49 asks across 7 frameworks. Distinct from THR-03 in that the demand is the analysis rather than the feed. Identity-theft threat analysis and cloud-specific threat testing are kept as their own artifacts because they are separately-scoped programmes.

artifacts.name: Third-Party and Outsourcing Security Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy set governing third-party, supplier, cloud outsourcing and supply chain risk: scope and applicability, supplier categorisation/tiering, minimum security expectations per tier, the end-to-end process from selection through onboarding, monitoring, renewal and exit, and defined roles and responsibilities. Frameworks require board or senior management approval (with cloud outsourcing policy specifically board-approved), a version-controlled review log evidencing periodic review, evidence of dissemination to relevant stakeholders with acknowledgements, and third-party representative acknowledgement of the framework.

artifacts.name: Board and Management Approval and Oversight Records
artifacts.description: Governance records evidencing senior oversight of third-party arrangements: board or committee minutes approving the outsourcing/third-party policy and its revisions, board approvals for individual material or critical outsourcing arrangements, management approval evidence for the third-party security framework, and the record of board-level oversight of the outsourcing portfolio.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Register
artifacts.description: The inventory of all third parties, suppliers and service providers, recording for each: services provided, data and systems accessed, tier or materiality rating, whether the arrangement is a material/critical outsourcing, risk rating, assessment status and dates, and contract references. PCI DSS additionally requires the register to show which providers receive account data and through which channels, with evidence that the list is maintained and updated when new providers are engaged; separate registers or register views are expected for AI suppliers (what they supply and how it is integrated), business associates handling health data, and outsourcing risk with ratings and controls.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Due Diligence and Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Completed pre-engagement and periodic risk assessments per third party: security questionnaire responses (SIG, CAIQ or equivalent), independent assurance collected (SOC 2, ISO 27001 certificates, third-party audit reports), the organisation's own assessment of the provider's controls, and the resulting risk rating and treatment decisions. Also covers the criticality-related analysis several regimes demand — designation criteria for critical ICT providers, systemic impact and substitutability analysis, concentration and supervisory monitoring — and the proportionality justification recording why the measures imposed suit the entity's size and risk exposure. Reassessment cadence varies (annual for most, more frequent for critical or material providers); state the cadence applied.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Contracts and Security Clauses
artifacts.description: Executed agreements with third parties carrying the required protections, plus the standard clause library and templates behind them: information security obligations and control requirements, confidentiality/NDA and IP terms, data protection and processing terms, incident notification obligations, right-to-audit and subprocessor approval rights, service levels, and termination and exit provisions. Includes signed business associate agreements where health data is involved, outsourcing agreements with security requirements, outsourced development contracts covering security, IP and testing obligations, source code escrow for critical software, and the contract compliance tracker showing which suppliers are on current clause versions.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Performance and Service Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence of ongoing oversight after onboarding: the formal periodic (at least annual) stakeholder review of each external service provider, vendor performance scorecards and service reports against SLAs, supplier security monitoring and audit reports, compliance verification of business associates, records of corrective action required of suppliers where delivery did not meet the organisation's requirements, management information reporting on outsourcing risk, performance and incidents, and the operating procedures under which outsourced services are managed day to day.

artifacts.name: Shared Responsibility and Role Allocation Documentation
artifacts.description: Documentation splitting responsibility between the organisation and its third parties: the shared security responsibility model and its supporting procedures, allocation of AI lifecycle responsibilities across provider, producer, customer and partner roles (data, models, development and use), determination of controller / joint controller / processor roles where personal data is processed, and records evidencing that required technical and user documentation was delivered to and received from the relevant parties. Where the organisation is itself the provider, include the procedure and samples for responding to customer requests for compliance information, with the request tracker and response timelines.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Access Control and Privileged Access Approval Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that third-party and cross-tenant access is restricted and approved: customer or system-owner approval records for agreed privileged access roles, the authentication policy and identity verification procedures applied to third-party personnel, multi-factor authentication implementation evidence, configuration showing unique per-customer or per-environment credentials for remote support access with the supporting credential register, and audit logs of third-party remote access showing which credentials were used and when. Configuration and log evidence is connector-addressable; the approvals and policy are manual.

artifacts.name: Customer Agreements and Service-Provider Responsibility Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: Where the organisation acts as a service provider: executed customer agreements containing the written acknowledgement that it is responsible for the security of customer data it holds, processes or can affect, the standard clause embodying that acknowledgement, and the repository of executed agreements demonstrating the clause is consistently applied.

artifacts.name: Vendor Selection and Secure Procurement Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that security requirements are imposed before commitment: the supplier selection and evaluation criteria, the due diligence procedure defining depth of assessment by tier and data access, the secure procurement policy with security requirements embedded in RFPs, acquisition documentation showing security requirements were specified, and the AI supplier selection procedure covering datasets, models, libraries and complete systems with the requirements and monitoring set at selection.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Security Assurance
artifacts.description: Assurance evidence for software and components built or supplied by third parties: assessment of the vendor's secure development lifecycle and practices, the organisation's own review of vendor-delivered code, security test results for supplied components (SAST, DAST, penetration testing) before deployment, periodic vendor quality and security reports, and the vulnerability handling and coordinated disclosure arrangements covering supplied products.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Resilience and Continuity Evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence that dependency on third parties is covered by continuity planning: business disruption risk assessments and treatment plans covering supplier failure, business continuity and disaster recovery plans referencing critical providers, assessments of each critical provider's own DR capability, results of joint recovery testing performed with providers, cyber insurance documentation, and facilities/environmental management records for outsourced hosting.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Personnel Screening and Fraud/Insider Risk Controls
artifacts.description: Evidence that people acting on behalf of third parties are vetted and monitored: background check and screening procedures and their application to third-party personnel, the fraud risk assessment covering third-party-enabled fraud, the inventory of anti-fraud controls, and the insider threat programme documentation extending to contractors and service provider staff.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Compliance Mapping and External Assessment Records
artifacts.description: Where a national regulator prescribes third-party or outsourcing requirements: the mapping of each regulatory requirement to the corresponding policy clause, control and evidence, the compliance document addressing the applicable circular or regulation, and the records of regulator-conducted assessments or compliance reviews of third-party supplier security together with any resulting remediation.

TPM-01.notes: 129 entries collapse to 14 artifacts. The policy/framework group (18 entries) and the due diligence group (19) are the largest sets of restatements; contract evidence is asked for by eight frameworks in eight different wordings. No collectors are configured, so only third-party access configuration and logs are hybrid.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Inventory
artifacts.description: The service provider inventory, the third-party service provider inventory, the register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating, the register of suppliers documented and classified by criticality, the supply chain element inventory with its interdependencies, the provider classification records, the criteria used to classify supplier criticality, and the inventory review records evidencing it is maintained.

artifacts.name: Regulated Data Sharing Inventory
artifacts.description: The list of all third-party service providers with which account data is shared or that could affect the security of account data with a description of the service provided, the documentation of which providers receive what data and through which channels, and the records evidencing list maintenance and updates upon engagement of new providers.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Arrangements Register
artifacts.description: The technology third-party arrangements register, the consolidated group-level register, the critical versus non-critical classification, and the register update procedures and records maintaining it.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk Strategy
artifacts.description: The technology third-party risk strategy document, the critical service provider policy, the multi-vendor strategy documentation, the third-party risk management policy, the strategy review and update records, the documentation integrating the register with the technology risk framework, the responsibility assignment for third-party oversight, and the regulatory compliance obligations mapping.

artifacts.name: Concentration Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The technology concentration risk assessment methodology, the concentration risk monitoring reports, the mitigation measures for the concentration risk identified, and the pre-contract risk assessments feeding it.

artifacts.name: Sub-Contractor Register
artifacts.description: The up-to-date list of provider sub-contractors with scope of services, locations and criticality; the map of the provider supply chain visualising sub-contractor dependencies for the outsourced workload; the log of sub-contractor list updates received and reviewed; the assessment of large or complex sub-contracting and its impact on operational resilience; and the evaluation of the organisation's capacity to oversee and monitor emerging risks from those chains.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Outsourcing Approvals
artifacts.description: The regulator's pre-outsourcing approvals and the scope submissions made to obtain them.

artifacts.name: Supplier Assessment Procedure
artifacts.description: The supplier information security policy setting security expectations for all supplier categories, the supplier risk assessment procedure for onboarding due diligence based on tier and data access, the completed due diligence questionnaires from critical suppliers, the certifications collected from key suppliers, the supply chain assessment and audit reports, the issue tracking records for supply chain elements, and the vendor risk assessment records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented supply chain risk management requirement.

artifacts.name: Provider Contracts and Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: The contract provisions covering audit rights and control requirements, the assurance report review documentation with its assessment of complementary user entity controls, the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, and the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records. HITRUST requires the approved service delivery policy and standard with its implementing procedure and its awareness communications.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

TPM-01.1.notes: 54 asks across 12 frameworks. DORA Article 28 imposes a formal register with a prescribed structure that is distinct from an ordinary supplier list, and SBP Cloud adds a sub-contractor layer beneath it; both stay separate from the general inventory.

artifacts.name: Supplier Criticality Criteria
artifacts.description: The criteria used to classify supplier criticality, the documented methodology for supply chain risk classification, the service provider classification criteria with the risk tier documentation, the supplier risk assessment procedure for onboarding due diligence based on tier and data access, the supplier information security policy setting expectations by category, the vendor evaluation criteria and procedures, and the vendor selection criteria and evaluation documentation.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register with Criticality
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating; the register of suppliers documented and classified by criticality; the inventory of service providers supporting the channel with services, criticality and access scope; the supply chain element inventory with its interdependencies; the classification records; and the supply chain risk register identifying, assessing and classifying risks by category.

artifacts.name: Due Diligence Records
artifacts.description: The standardised due diligence checklist covering security, legal and regulatory requirements; the pre-engagement risk-based due diligence assessments per supplier; the pre-contract supplier review records; the supplier evaluation process documentation; the completed due diligence questionnaires from critical suppliers; the certifications collected from key suppliers; the data centre and technology provider due diligence reports; the vendor selection assessment reports; the third-party security assessments; and the vendor risk assessment reports and due diligence records.

artifacts.name: Provider Due Diligence Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for conducting provider due diligence covering every criterion in the framework's due diligence section, the completed due diligence reports for each engaged provider with findings, risk rating and go or no-go decision, the risk register covering provider-specific risks, sub-contracting risks, residual risks and treatment plans, and the dedicated sub-contracting risk assessment for each provider's supply chain with visibility, depth and mitigation.

artifacts.name: Provider Financial Viability Assessment
artifacts.description: The provider's latest audited financial statements obtained during due diligence, the assessment report covering those statements with credit rating, liquidity and going-concern indicators, the corporate profile, client reference list and verified track record documentation, and the financial viability assessments held on file.

artifacts.name: Engagement Feasibility Study
artifacts.description: The feasibility study covering cost-effectiveness, service quality and legal, regulatory and compliance risks of the arrangement; the cost-benefit analysis; and the assessment of the provider's ability to meet the applicable local legal and regulatory requirements for the outsourced workload.

artifacts.name: Concentration Risk Analysis
artifacts.description: The analysis identifying single-source and highly-dependent supplier concentration risks and the plan to manage the concentration risks identified.

artifacts.name: Business Impact Analysis
artifacts.description: The business impact analysis documentation, the application criticality classification, and the data criticality analysis report determining which supplier failures matter most.

artifacts.name: Provider Contracts and Responsibility Matrix
artifacts.description: The sample executed service provider contracts highlighting security obligations and clauses, the matrix documenting the security and contractual responsibilities of each service provider, the external service provider agreements, the service level agreements with security requirements, the vendor contracts and service level agreements, and the inventory of customer entities with access to organisational systems and data with their access rationale.

artifacts.name: Ongoing Provider Monitoring
artifacts.description: The continuous monitoring of external services, the periodic supplier compliance reviews, the vendor performance monitoring reports and scorecards, and the federal or local government compliance verification for the providers subject to it.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance policy documentation.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

TPM-02.notes: 57 asks across 13 frameworks. Criticality tiering, financial viability and concentration risk are three different questions about the same supplier; SBP Cloud's provider feasibility study is a distinct pre-engagement instrument and stays separate.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Management Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy addressing risks from hardware, software and cloud vendors across the supply chain, the supply chain risk management plan with its review and update records, and the evidence that the processes are implemented rather than only defined.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Register
artifacts.description: The register tracking supply chain risks including fourth-party exposure, geopolitical concentration and single points of failure, with the supply chain risk assessment and evaluation reports behind it.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register and Tiering
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating, and the risk assessment procedure defining onboarding due diligence by tier and data access.

artifacts.name: Vendor Due Diligence Records
artifacts.description: The completed due diligence assessments covering financial and security review, the security questionnaire responses from critical suppliers, the certifications collected, the supplier security audit and assurance reports, the outsourcing risk assessment, and the jurisdiction matrix where data location matters.

artifacts.name: Supplier Contract Security Clauses
artifacts.description: The contracts containing the required security control measures, the flow-down clauses obligating suppliers to impose equivalent requirements on their own subcontractors, the contractual security requirements, and the supplier-agreed control measures documentation.

artifacts.name: Subcontractor Visibility Records
artifacts.description: The up-to-date list of the provider's subcontractors with scope of services, locations and criticality, the map visualising those dependencies for the outsourced workload, the log of list updates received and reviewed, the subcontractor assessments, and the impact assessment of large or complex subcontracting on operational resilience.

artifacts.name: Subcontracting Permission and Oversight Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for evaluating and permitting subcontracting based on operational risk acceptability, the assessment of the provider's capability to oversee its own material subcontractors, the evaluation of the organisation's own capacity to oversee complex chains, the review reports on material subcontracting agreements, the rights flow-down clause obligating the provider to pass through audit and access requirements, the subcontractor compliance attestations, and the risk acceptance decisions for each arrangement.

artifacts.name: Cloud Provider Due Diligence Records
artifacts.description: The documented procedure for conducting provider due diligence against every criterion in the applicable framework, the completed due diligence reports for each engaged provider with findings, risk rating and go or no-go decision, the outsourcing risk register covering provider-specific, subcontracting and residual risks with treatment plans, and the dedicated subcontracting risk assessment for each provider's chain.

artifacts.name: Software Bill of Materials Records
artifacts.description: The software bill of materials requested from and received from vendors, with the analysis of the components it discloses.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Assurance
artifacts.description: The development supplier contracts including security, intellectual property and testing obligations, the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses, the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software, the assessment of the supplier's secure development maturity, the security test results from vendor deliverables, the organisation-side code review of vendor-delivered code, and the periodic vendor quality and security reports.

artifacts.name: Supplier Performance and Review Records
artifacts.description: The periodic supplier review reports covering service levels, security KPIs and incidents, the SLA compliance dashboard, the supplier scorecard, the audit reports with management responses, the governance meeting minutes, the change notification records with impact assessment, and the vendor performance monitoring reports and scorecards.

artifacts.name: Critical Vendor Contingency Plan
artifacts.description: The plans for replacing or mitigating loss of critical suppliers, the business continuity and disaster recovery plans covering that scenario, the business disruption risk assessment with mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans, and the cyber insurance documentation.

artifacts.name: Product Acquisition and Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The product and service acquisition policy, the supply chain protection policy, the product compliance verification records, and the documented system acceptance criteria applied before a supplied component enters service.

artifacts.name: Vendor Selection Records
artifacts.description: The vendor selection criteria and evaluation documentation, the contracts and service level agreements resulting from it, and the continuous monitoring of the external services once engaged.

artifacts.name: AI Supplier Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for selecting AI suppliers of datasets, models, libraries or complete systems, the supplier register with what each supplies and its risk assessment, evidence that suppliers delivered adequate documentation, the corrective action records where supplied components do not align, the life-cycle responsibility allocation between the organisation and its suppliers, and the controller or processor determination where personal information is processed.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Approval for Providers
artifacts.description: The documented approval for the privileged access roles agreed with the provider, with the records demonstrating the approval operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The analysis of entity size and risk exposure, the assessment of incident likelihood and severity, and the justification for why the supply chain measures adopted are proportionate.

TPM-03.notes: 87 asks across 12 frameworks. Distinct from TPM-04 (third-party services) in that the demands here reach past the direct supplier into the chain behind it — sub-contractors, fourth parties, software bills of materials, flow-down clauses.

artifacts.name: Procurement Policy
artifacts.description: The technology procurement policy covering request-for-proposal and business-requirement formulation with defined content requirements, the comprehensive procurement policy covering asset types, vendor types, selection criteria, acquisition process and payment and monitoring, the product and service acquisition policy, the procurement security procedures, the acquisition strategy documentation, and the board or management approval of the policy.

artifacts.name: Procurement Templates and Approval Matrix
artifacts.description: The standardised request-for-proposal template and business requirement document template, the approval matrix defining authorities at different procurement scales, the delegation of authority register referencing the approval thresholds, the policy document containing the matrix, and the sample approval records following it.

artifacts.name: Strategy and Business Plan Alignment
artifacts.description: The procurement policy sections referencing strategy compliance requirements, the technology procurement register with alignment status for each major procurement, the committee review records confirming procurements align with the board-approved technology strategy, the current business plan referenced when assessing alignment, the matrix linking each major procurement to specific business plan objectives, the committee minutes documenting the review, and the approval memos citing that alignment.

artifacts.name: Vendor Selection Records
artifacts.description: The vendor selection criteria matrix with its scoring methodology, the register of approved vendors categorised by asset type, the vendor selection criteria and evaluation documentation, and the completed due diligence assessments for technology vendors including financial and security review.

artifacts.name: Contract Security Requirements
artifacts.description: The contract security requirements, the supplier contracts with the required clauses, and the system acceptance criteria documentation against which delivery is judged.

artifacts.name: Delivery Verification Records
artifacts.description: The delivery assurance and verification checklist and the product compliance verification records evidencing what was received matched what was specified.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Management
artifacts.description: The policy addressing risks from hardware, software and cloud vendors across the supply chain; the supply chain protection policy; the risk register tracking supply chain risks including fourth-party, geopolitical and single points of failure; the supply chain assessment procedures; the weakness identification records with their remediation tracking; the plans for replacing or mitigating loss of critical suppliers; the software bills of materials received from vendors with their component analysis; and the audit or assurance reports received from technology suppliers.

artifacts.name: Supplier Performance Management
artifacts.description: The periodic supplier review reports covering service levels, security indicators and incidents; the supplier scorecard rating suppliers across security, performance and compliance; the service level attainment dashboard; the minutes of regular governance and service review meetings; the on-site or remote supplier audit reports with management responses; the supplier change notification records with their impact assessments; and the vendor contracts, service level agreements and performance monitoring reports behind them.

artifacts.name: Solution Design and Testing Records
artifacts.description: The high-level and detailed solution design documents, the development standards and quality assurance test plans, the solution procurement and build approval documentation, and the test results with the defect tracking records.

artifacts.name: Registered Security Service Provider Records
artifacts.description: The bidding and procurement records demonstrating compliance with the public procurement rules for security service outsourcing, the contracts with firms registered with the national or sectoral response team or the regulator, and the evidence that the engaged firm holds that registration.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
