artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption and Fraud Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, the cyber insurance policy documentation, the fraud risk assessment documentation, the anti-fraud controls inventory, the insider threat programme documentation, and the background check and screening procedures.

TPM-03.1.notes: 62 asks across 8 frameworks. The procurement policy, the templates it mandates and the approval thresholds are one instrument in SBP ETGRMF and are merged; supplier performance management arrives through ISO 27001 A.5.22 and is kept separate because it is post-award.

artifacts.name: Supplier Diversity Records
artifacts.description: The diverse supplier engagement records for critical products, evidencing the organisation is not dependent on a single source for anything it cannot survive losing.

artifacts.name: Information Sharing Restrictions
artifacts.description: The information sharing restrictions documentation and the secure information sharing channel evidence limiting what a supplier receives and how.

artifacts.name: Supplier Agreements and Clauses
artifacts.description: The executed supplier contracts showing information security and incident reporting clauses, the library of standard security clauses and processing agreement templates, the extracts showing right-to-audit and sub-processor approval rights, the signed non-disclosure agreements with suppliers, the tracker showing which suppliers have updated contracts with current security clauses, the supplier contracts containing the agreed control measures, the supplier contracts with the required clauses, the contract security requirements checklist, the contract review records, and the sample contract clauses.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Records
artifacts.description: The supply chain protection policy, the supply chain risk evaluation reports, the supply chain assessment procedures, the weakness identification records with their remediation tracking, the supplier-agreed control measures documentation, and the product and service acquisition policy with its compliance verification records and system acceptance criteria.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register and Assessment
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating; the supplier information security policy setting expectations for all supplier categories; the supplier risk assessment procedure for onboarding due diligence; the completed due diligence questionnaires from critical suppliers; and the certifications collected from key suppliers.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance policy documentation.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

TPM-03.2.notes: 35 asks across 6 frameworks. The distinguishing demand is limiting the damage a compromised supplier can do — supplier diversity and information-sharing restrictions — rather than assessing the supplier.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk Management Procedure
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure for identifying and addressing risks related to third parties, the risk assessment methodology with its classification scheme, and the third-party inventory it is applied to. HITRUST requires separate approved standards for identifying third-party risk and for addressing security in third-party agreements.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Agreements with Security Clauses
artifacts.description: The executed agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit provisions, the agreement repository with metadata covering effective date, renewal and owner, the contract templates and sample clauses, the non-disclosure agreements, and the records of renewals, amendments and supersessions. HIPAA requires signed business associate agreements with an inventory of them.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The completed due diligence and risk assessments per provider, the security questionnaire responses, the certifications collected, the provider suitability evaluation, the concentration risk analysis, and the compliance verification records for the provider's own controls.

artifacts.name: Ongoing Provider Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The assessment schedule with the periodic reassessment records, the assurance report reviews, the service level monitoring reports, the security monitoring and audit reports over the provider, and the continuous monitoring of the external services.

artifacts.name: Vendor Access Control Records
artifacts.description: The written procedure governing vendor access to sensitive data and systems with its approval workflow, the log of access requests with approvals and access periods, the non-disclosure and data-handling clauses in the agreements, the documentation of what information type each third party may reach, and the session monitoring or recording logs for vendor access.

artifacts.name: Per-Customer Provider Credentials
artifacts.description: For providers with remote access into multiple customer environments: the register of customer-specific credentials or keys, the configuration evidence showing unique authentication factors per environment, and sample audit logs demonstrating credentials are not shared across customers.

artifacts.name: Customer-Facing Responsibility Documentation
artifacts.description: For the organisation acting as the provider: the repository of executed customer agreements containing the written acknowledgment of responsibility, the standard clause embodying it, the procedure for supporting customer requests for the information they need to meet their own obligations, the request tracker with response timelines, and samples of the responsibility documentation provided.

artifacts.name: Selection and Onboarding Process Records
artifacts.description: The documented selection and assessment process, the contract review records, the contract security requirements checklist applied during review, and the due diligence assessment reports supporting the engagement decision.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Assurance
artifacts.description: The development supplier contracts including security, intellectual property and testing obligations, the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses, the source code escrow arrangement for critical software, the assessment of the supplier's secure development maturity, the security test results from deliverables, the organisation-side code review, and the periodic vendor quality and security reports.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register and Security Policy
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating, the supplier information security policy setting expectations by category, the third-party relationship management roles, and the risk mitigation controls documentation.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Register
artifacts.description: The register identifying, assessing and classifying supply chain risks by category, with the documented methodology for that classification.

artifacts.name: AI Supplier Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for selecting AI suppliers of datasets, models, libraries or complete systems, the supplier register with risk assessments, evidence that suppliers delivered adequate documentation, the corrective action records where components do not align, the life-cycle responsibility allocation, and the controller or processor determination where personal information is processed.

artifacts.name: Privileged Access Approval for Providers
artifacts.description: The documented approval for the privileged access roles agreed with the provider, with the records demonstrating that approval operates in the environment covered.

artifacts.name: Fraud and Insider Risk Controls
artifacts.description: The fraud risk assessment documentation, the anti-fraud controls inventory, the background check and screening procedures applied to provider personnel where relevant, and the insider threat programme documentation.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The analysis of entity size and risk exposure, the assessment of incident likelihood and severity, and the justification for why the third-party measures adopted are proportionate.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the third-party security requirements and how to apply them when engaging providers.

TPM-04.notes: 89 asks across 15 frameworks. Distinct from TPM-03 in that the demands here concern the direct engagement — the agreement, the assessment, the access the provider holds — rather than the chain behind it. PCI DSS's customer-facing obligations for an organisation acting as the provider are kept separate from its obligations as a customer.

artifacts.name: Third-Party & Outsourcing Risk Management Policy
artifacts.description: The approved policy governing acquisition and outsourcing of technology assets, applications and services, setting security expectations for each supplier category and defining who may approve an engagement. Must state scope, applicability, roles and responsibilities, and be current-version with management approval. Frameworks add specific policy coverage: a procurement policy covering asset types, vendor types, selection criteria and acquisition process; a cloud computing policy governing use of cloud services; and an outsourcing risk management policy covering identification, measurement, monitoring and control of outsourcing risk. Evidence that personnel were informed of the requirement is also requested.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Due Diligence & Risk Assessment Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented, repeatable procedure for assessing a third party before engagement: the tiering or criticality criteria that determine assessment depth, the questionnaire or checklist used, the scoring methodology, the risk acceptance thresholds and the go/no-go decision rights. Must cover the full engagement lifecycle from selection criteria through to approval. Specific variants demanded: a vetting procedure for third-party API access, a cloud service provider due diligence procedure covering the regulator's full criteria list, a standardised due diligence checklist covering security, legal and regulatory requirements, and a customer/vendor screening procedure.

artifacts.name: Pre-Engagement Third-Party Risk Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The completed risk assessment for each proposed acquisition or outsourcing arrangement, produced before the contract is signed, with the risks identified, their likelihood and severity, the residual risk and the named approver of the decision to proceed. Must cover the risk categories the frameworks collectively name: compliance, concentration, operational, country/geopolitical and legal risk; supply chain risk for critical infrastructure procurement; sub-contracting risk down the provider's own supply chain; risk from data sensitivity where APIs exchange data; and, for AI services, a third-party AI and data risk assessment plus an impact assessment covering the likelihood and magnitude of both beneficial and harmful impacts. One framework requires the assessment to justify that the measures chosen are proportionate to the entity's size and risk exposure. Assessments triggered by significant changes to the business model or operating environment fall in scope here too.

artifacts.name: Supplier Due Diligence & Security Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The evidence gathered from and about the supplier during due diligence: completed security questionnaires (SIG, CAIQ or equivalent) with the supplier's responses, the security assessment performed against them, the assessment of their physical security and internal controls against the intended workload's confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience requirements, and the findings with any conditions imposed. Must include due diligence on data centre and technology providers, on cloud providers across the regulator's full list of security domains, and ethical conduct or background screening records where required. Reviews must be repeated pre-contract and periodically thereafter.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Assurance Reports & Certifications
artifacts.description: Independent assurance artifacts collected from the provider and the record of their review: SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO 27001, PCI DSS and CSA STAR certificates, and third-party audit reports, together with a register tracking each certificate's issue date, expiry date and scope of coverage so lapsed or out-of-scope certifications are visible. The review itself must be evidenced, not just the certificate on file - one framework explicitly asks for the SOC report review, including how carve-outs and complementary user entity controls were handled.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Inventory & Criticality Register
artifacts.description: The master register of third parties, suppliers and service providers, each with the service supplied, the data or systems they access, their criticality or tier, their risk rating and the date of last assessment. Must be complete for the in-scope environment. Frameworks add: a register of approved vendors categorised by asset type, a catalogue of approved cloud applications, a register of outsourced IT activities mapped to the applicable regulatory instructions, a matrix of each provider's security and contractual responsibilities, and an inventory of customer entities that hold access to the organisation's systems or data with the rationale for that access.

artifacts.name: Outsourcing Risk Register & Treatment Records
artifacts.description: A risk register covering all technology outsourcing and cloud arrangements, showing per-provider risks with ratings, the controls or mitigations applied, treatment status and residual risk. Must include cloud-provider-specific and sub-contracting risks, and the documentation of the mitigating controls relied upon.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Contracts, SLAs & Right-to-Audit Clauses
artifacts.description: Executed agreements with each in-scope third party carrying the cybersecurity and data privacy obligations, the security requirements and service levels, and the right-to-audit clause with its scope and methodology. Must evidence that security obligations were contracted before or at engagement, not retrofitted. Framework-specific additions: outsourcing agreements compliant with the applicable central bank circular, SLA review records forming part of the selection analysis, and intellectual property clauses where AI services are procured.

artifacts.name: Ongoing Third-Party Monitoring & Service Review Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that the relationship is monitored after onboarding, not just assessed once: the formal stakeholder review of each provider's services (annual is the common cadence), performance monitoring reports and scorecards against the agreed service levels, continuous monitoring of the external service, monitoring of the provider's access to systems and data, periodic compliance reviews, and the management information pack reporting outsourcing risk, performance and incidents to senior management. Monitoring frequency and the roles responsible must be defined, and for AI services the periodic review of third-party risks and benefits is explicitly required.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Approval, Jurisdiction & Data Residency Verification
artifacts.description: Evidence that the arrangement satisfies the applicable regulatory regime: assessment of the provider's ability to meet local legal and regulatory requirements with a gap analysis, prior regulatory approval for the outsourcing where the regulator requires it, verification of the provider's legal authorisations, and confirmation of federal or local government compliance obligations. Must include the jurisdiction matrix showing where data will be stored and processed and which laws apply, the assessment of the provider's data residency capability including the ability to move between preferred data centre regions, and configuration evidence (portal screenshots showing region restrictions) that residency controls are actually enforced. National regulator assessment or compliance records are requested where a national authority conducts them.

artifacts.name: Provider Financial Viability & Track Record Assessment
artifacts.description: Assessment of the provider as a going concern before engagement: their latest audited financial statements, the analysis of credit rating, liquidity and going-concern indicators, and the review of their corporate governance, board composition and entity-level controls. Track record must be verified through corporate profile, client reference list and demonstrated operating experience - one framework sets a minimum five-year threshold.

artifacts.name: Acquisition Business Case, Feasibility & Selection Analysis
artifacts.description: The documented business case for the acquisition or outsourcing decision: the business requirements for the function being outsourced, the feasibility study covering cost-effectiveness, service quality and legal/regulatory/compliance risk, the cost-benefit analysis comparing the proposed arrangement against on-premise or alternative options, the formal system selection analysis for the hardware, software or service chosen, and the requirements compliance matrix confirming the selection meets user, business and regulatory requirements.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Continuity, Exit Strategy & DR Validation
artifacts.description: Evidence that dependency on the provider is survivable: the documented exit strategy for the arrangement, the multi-geography risk assessment where services span regions, pre-contract validation of the provider's disaster recovery capability, and recovery time objective verification test results proving the stated RTO is achievable. Scope documents for volumetric and application-layer DDoS protection services obtained from providers fall here as a continuity dependency.

artifacts.name: Secure Acquisition & Procurement Security Testing Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that security was built into how technology is acquired and developed rather than bolted on: the documented secure SDLC or equivalent methodology, records showing it was applied to both in-house development and acquired software, the operational risk assessments embedded in its phases, and developer training records evidencing awareness of its requirements. Also covers security testing and evaluation performed during procurement and the delivery assurance and verification checklist completed at handover.

TPM-04.1.notes: 140 entries across 19 frameworks collapsed to 14 artifacts. No automated collectors exist for this control, so every artifact is manual. The cloud and banking frameworks (SBP Cloud, SBP ETGRMF, QCB) drive most of the specialised buckets - financial viability, data residency, exit strategy - which do not appear in the general frameworks but cannot be merged away without losing a real ask.

artifacts.name: Processing Location Register
artifacts.description: The register listing every cloud outsourcing arrangement with provider classification, workload materiality and location; the jurisdiction matrix; the offshore hosting inventory of applications hosted outside the country; and the cloud data residency assessment behind them.

artifacts.name: Jurisdiction Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The jurisdiction risk register, the multi-geography risk assessment, the outsourcing risk assessment, the due diligence reports supporting it, and the legal and compliance memo confirming no provider data-centre location falls within an unfriendly or hostile jurisdiction.

artifacts.name: Onshore Preference and Provider Assessment
artifacts.description: The board-approved cloud outsourcing policy section articulating the preference for onshore providers with its rationale and criteria, the assessment report documenting why the selected onshore provider is deemed reputable including reference checks, and the configuration export restricting resource deployment to permitted regions.

artifacts.name: In-Country Location Evidence
artifacts.description: The contracts specifying in-country data centres and operations, the verification evidence that providers and all physical servers are located in-country across the service models, the provider site attestation confirming service location, the due diligence records confirming in-country operations, the data centre location attestations confirming residency, and the plan for migrating hosting into in-country data centres where it is not yet.

artifacts.name: Offshore Regulatory Submission
artifacts.description: The register distinguishing material from non-material workloads with the materiality criteria and classification rationale, the detailed risk assessment covering systemic, institution-specific, legal and strategic risks, the internal committee or board approval records authorising the pre-placement submission, the submission package covering every required area, and the signed regulatory approval letter authorising outsourcing of the material workload to the named offshore provider.

artifacts.name: Offshore Arrangement Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The licensing or authorisation documentation confirming the entity's regulatory classification, the checklist demonstrating the offshore arrangement complies with every section of the framework, the executed offshore provider contract meeting all framework requirements, and the exit strategy document for the arrangement.

artifacts.name: Scope Definition and Validation
artifacts.description: The annually-confirmed scope document including all data flows, the locations where regulated data resides and the identification of all connected components; the documented scoping validation methodology aligned with the standards body's guidance; the validation results from data discovery scans, network analysis and interviews; and the records of scope reviews performed upon significant changes.

artifacts.name: Data Location Discovery Results
artifacts.description: The results of data discovery scans confirming account data resides only where the scope document says it does, with the scanning tool configuration and the follow-up on any data found outside the expected locations.

artifacts.name: Retention and Secure Deletion Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy specifying retention periods with their business, legal and regulatory justification and the disposal methods; the register of retention periods per data element with documented justification; and the records of secure deletion or cryptographic erasure executed when retention periods are exceeded.

artifacts.name: Supplier Data Handling Assurance
artifacts.description: The contractual data-handling requirements aligned to the data protection and privacy policy, the assurance evidence through attestations or audits that suppliers meet them, the procedure defining supplier-change triggers requiring risk reassessment, and the records of reassessments performed following significant supplier changes.

artifacts.name: External Service Provider Agreements
artifacts.description: The external service provider agreements, the service level agreements with security requirements, the third-party security assessments, and the continuous monitoring records for the external services.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Risk Register
artifacts.description: The policy addressing risks from hardware, software and cloud vendors across the supply chain; the risk register tracking fourth-party, geopolitical and single-point-of-failure risks; the completed vendor due diligence reports; the audit or assurance reports from technology suppliers; the software bills of materials with their component analysis; the plans for replacing or mitigating loss of critical suppliers; and the vendor contracts, service level agreements, performance monitoring reports and due diligence records behind them.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance policy documentation.

TPM-04.4.notes: 63 asks across 10 frameworks. Four regulators impose distinct residency regimes with different tests and different filings; each stays its own artifact because the evidence is jurisdiction-specific and not interchangeable.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Contract Clause Library & Templates
artifacts.description: The approved standard security, compliance and resilience clause set used in third-party agreements, plus the contract and agreement templates that carry it. Must cover, at minimum: confidentiality and non-disclosure; the security requirements the provider must meet; data protection, location and handling; breach and incident notification; right-to-audit for the organization and, in regulated sectors, for the regulator; subcontracting approval and flow-down of the same obligations to fourth parties; secure data return and destruction on exit; compliance with named baselines or standards; liability, indemnification and penalties; governing law; and termination rights. Templates must exist in the variants actually used (services, cloud, outsourced development, information exchange, NDA).

artifacts.name: Executed Third-Party Agreements
artifacts.description: The signed contracts, service agreements and SLAs themselves, retrievable from a single repository, for the third parties in scope. Must be fully executed by an authorized signatory, current (not expired or superseded), and demonstrably contain the required security clauses. Evidence should include the repository or agreement register with execution and renewal dates, and, where a regulator's prior approval or notification of the outsourcing arrangement is required, that approval on file alongside the agreement. Sampling across provider tiers is acceptable where framework does not demand full population.

artifacts.name: Non-Disclosure Agreements
artifacts.description: Executed NDAs or confidentiality agreements with every third party that receives sensitive or regulated data, plus the master NDA template, the variant library, the NDA register with renewal/reissue dates, and legal review records. Must be in place before data is shared. Several frameworks additionally require signed employee/personnel NDAs and NDAs with assessors and auditors engaged on the organization's systems.

artifacts.name: Third-Party & Subcontractor Register
artifacts.description: The inventory of external parties: provider name, service supplied, business owner, criticality/materiality, data categories and system access granted, contract reference and dates, hosting/processing locations, and status. Must extend to declared subcontractors (fourth parties) where subcontracting is permitted, and to e-commerce and payment-service partners where those are used. The register is the population from which all other third-party evidence is sampled, so completeness against procurement and payables records matters.

artifacts.name: Contract Clause Coverage Checklist & Legal Review
artifacts.description: Per-agreement evidence that the required clauses are actually present: the completed clause checklist or coverage matrix mapping each mandated requirement to the clause and page in the executed contract, the contract review record, and sign-off by legal or the equivalent vetting function. Regulated-sector frameworks name the specific clause schedules that must be mapped (for example a cloud contract checklist against the regulator's enumerated items, or a legal vetting certificate confirming no lock-in and enforceable governing law).

artifacts.name: Shared Responsibility Matrix
artifacts.description: For each provider, the documented split of control ownership between the organization and the provider — which controls the provider operates, which the organization retains, and which are shared. Must be confirmed by the provider, not asserted unilaterally, and must be reconciled against the organization's own control set so that no in-scope requirement is left unowned. PCI DSS requires this per third-party service provider; cloud frameworks require it as the shared security responsibility model.

artifacts.name: Right-to-Audit Clauses & Audit Access Records
artifacts.description: The audit-rights provisions in executed agreements plus evidence they are usable and used: scope of the audit right, confirmation that the provider places no restriction on access, extension of the right to the organization's regulator and external auditors, and the log of audits or inspections actually requested and performed. Regulated-sector frameworks additionally require an audit-non-impedance clause, a documented access request procedure, and records of notifying the regulator if access is obstructed.

artifacts.name: Pre-Contract Due Diligence & Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment performed before the agreement was signed, showing that requirements were set from an understanding of the risk: vendor selection criteria and scoring, security questionnaires completed by the provider, supply chain and technology risk assessments, supplier certifications collected, SBOM requests where applicable, and — for AI or personal-data providers — impact assessments and controller/processor determination. Must cover concentration and country risk for offshore providers where the framework requires it, and record the residual risk accepted and by whom. NIS2 additionally expects a proportionality justification linking the measures required to entity size and risk exposure.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Assurance Reports & Attestations
artifacts.description: Independent assurance obtained about the provider: SOC/ISAE 3402 reports, ISO or equivalent certifications with scope statements, PCI DSS Attestations of Compliance, provider compliance attestations, and vulnerability assessment or penetration test reports supplied under contract. Must be current, in-scope for the services consumed, and accompanied by the organization's review of the report — including a reliance justification and treatment of any carve-outs, exceptions or complementary user entity controls.

artifacts.name: SLA Definitions & Compliance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The service level definitions and metrics agreed in contract — including quantitative targets for critical or material services — together with the monitoring output that shows they are tracked: SLA compliance reports, service delivery reports, breach registers, penalty or liquidated-damages application, and the governance minutes where provider performance is reviewed. Where a regulator must be notified of deviations or must receive a consolidated outsourcing report, those submissions belong here.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Management Policy & Supply Chain Risk Plan
artifacts.description: The governing documents: supplier/third-party information security policy, procurement and acquisition policy, supply chain risk management plan, outsourcing risk policy, and the procedures for onboarding, contracting, change management with third parties, and the AI-supplier management procedure where applicable. Must define who may sign, what security requirements attach at each provider tier, how subcontracting is approved, and how third-party-initiated changes are communicated and assessed.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Agreements & Assurance
artifacts.description: Where software development is outsourced: the development agreement carrying secure-coding, quality, licensing, IP and confidentiality obligations, plus the assurance the contract entitles the organization to — vendor secure SDLC assessment, source code review reports of delivered code, vendor security test results, source code access or escrow provisions, and records covering rotation or termination of vendor staff on the engagement.

artifacts.name: Data Exchange, Processing & Network Service Agreements
artifacts.description: The agreements that govern specific data flows and connections rather than the commercial relationship as a whole: business associate agreements for protected health information, information exchange agreements, health information exchange participant agreements, cross-border transfer instruments and standard data protection provisions, system connection and processing agreements, and network service agreements with their security specifications. Collect with the evidence that the connection implements what was agreed — encryption of the link, the access granted per connection, and data erasure or destruction certificates at the end of the engagement.

artifacts.name: Exit, Termination & Contingency Provisions
artifacts.description: Contractual and planning evidence that the organization can leave: termination rights and the scenarios they cover, minimum notice periods, continue-until-substitute obligations, data return and secure destruction on exit, and confirmation that no technical or commercial lock-in prevents transition. Supported by the exit strategy and transition plan, migration and rollback plans, contingency plans for critical vendors, and the risk treatment covering provider disruption — including cyber insurance where relied on.

artifacts.name: Customer-Facing Agreements & Responsibility Acknowledgements
artifacts.description: Where the organization is itself the service provider: customer agreements containing its written acknowledgement of responsibility for the security of customer data it holds, processes or can affect; the standard acknowledgement clause; the procedure and tracker for responding to customer requests for compliance information and for supplying that information; and, where customer environments are accessed, evidence of unique per-customer credentials with the supporting credential register and access logs.

TPM-05.notes: 334 entries collapse to 15. Roughly half of the input is the same two artifacts restated per clause: 'the contract template containing clause X' and 'the signed agreement evidencing clause X' — across confidentiality, right-to-audit, subcontracting, data destruction, breach notification, termination, liability and flow-down. Those become a clause template library plus an executed-agreement repository, with a clause coverage checklist as the third artifact that ties them together. Provider-side and org-as-service-provider asks (PCI DSS 12.9.x) are kept separate because a different team collects them. No automated collectors are mapped to this control; per-customer credential evidence is the only genuinely system-derived item and is marked hybrid.

artifacts.name: Flow-Down Contract Clauses
artifacts.description: The contract clauses obligating providers to impose equivalent requirements on their own subcontractors, the mapping of the organisation's controls to the vendor obligations written into contracts, the baseline clauses required by the sector regulator, and the subcontractor accountability clauses making the supplier answerable for parties behind it.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Agreements with Security Clauses
artifacts.description: The executed agreements carrying security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit; the repository of provider contracts containing the clauses that bind them to the applicable regulation; and the approved standard for addressing security in third-party agreements with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Audit and Access Rights Clauses
artifacts.description: The clauses granting audit and onsite assessment rights to the organisation's internal and external auditors, independent assessors and the regulator; the clauses covering every required information area — premises, data, devices, systems, networks; the contract coverage matrix confirming each area is present; the documented procedure for initiating and fulfilling access requests; the log of access actually exercised with dates, scope and outcomes; and the provider attestation confirming no restriction on that access.

artifacts.name: Subcontracting Approval and Oversight
artifacts.description: The subcontracting approval clause in the outsourcing contract, the procedure for evaluating and permitting subcontracting based on operational risk, the assessment of the provider's capability to oversee its own subcontractors, the review reports on material subcontracting agreements, the rights flow-down clause, the subcontractor compliance attestations, and the risk acceptance decisions per arrangement.

artifacts.name: Fourth-Party Register
artifacts.description: The register of subcontractors and fourth parties interacting with organisational systems or data, establishing visibility past the direct supplier.

artifacts.name: Provider Compliance Attestations
artifacts.description: The periodic attestations from providers confirming continued compliance with the applicable regulation, the compliance monitoring register tracking each provider against the controls flowed down to it, the provider compliance evidence, and the compliance verification records.

artifacts.name: Retained Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The internal memo or policy clarifying that outsourcing does not relieve the organisation of its own compliance responsibility, establishing that flow-down supplements rather than transfers the obligation.

artifacts.name: Business Associate Agreements
artifacts.description: The signed agreement templates with the inventory of executed agreements, the compliance verification records, and the security assessment documentation for each party holding regulated data on the organisation's behalf.

artifacts.name: Privacy Requirement Flow-Down
artifacts.description: The approved standard for privacy requirements with its implementing procedure, the consent records, opt-out tracking and data subject request logs the provider must support, and the published privacy notice with its version history.

artifacts.name: Onward Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The contractual provisions extending compliance obligations to any subsequent transfer by the recipient, the recipient attestation confirming onward transfers will comply, and the register tracking onward transfers performed by recipients with their destinations.

artifacts.name: Provider Certification and Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The register and copies of provider certifications covering service delivery, continuity and information security; the assessment of the provider's data security controls; the contingency, recovery and exit review; the subcontracting risk assessment; the support services agreement; and the provider-supplied security testing results reviewed by the organisation.

artifacts.name: Provider Auditor Interaction Records
artifacts.description: The records of interactions with the provider's external auditors including calls, walk-throughs and minutes, and the provider's company and financial information obtained under the contract.

artifacts.name: External Party Security Verification
artifacts.description: The security requirements implementation verification for external parties, the effectiveness review records, and the security briefing records for external party personnel.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Weakness Tracking
artifacts.description: The supply chain assessment procedures, the weakness identification records, and the remediation tracking documentation covering deficiencies found in the chain.

artifacts.name: Internal Compliance Testing Records
artifacts.description: The documented internal compliance testing with the records demonstrating it operates in the environment covered, and the access limitation evidence showing only authorised users reach the systems in scope.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The analysis of entity size and risk exposure, the assessment of incident likelihood and severity, and the justification for why the flow-down measures adopted are proportionate.

artifacts.name: Awareness Communications
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the third-party security requirements and their obligation to apply them when engaging providers.

TPM-05.2.notes: 75 asks across 14 frameworks. The single recurring demand is that obligations imposed on the organisation reach its providers and their subcontractors by contract; the artifacts are grouped by what is flowed down — security requirements, audit rights, privacy obligations, onward-transfer controls.

artifacts.name: Internal Security Responsibility Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping security activities — risk management, incident response, audit, asset ownership — to roles marked responsible, accountable, consulted and informed, with the organisation chart showing the security function's reporting line and independence, the job descriptions listing security duties explicitly, and the appointment letters formally assigning the named roles.

artifacts.name: Shared Responsibility Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix mapping control ownership between the organisation and each provider by service model, showing which requirements the provider manages, which the organisation manages and which are shared. PCI DSS requires one per third-party service provider with the entity's internal coverage mapping and the provider's own confirmation of the responsibilities it has assumed; CSA CCM requires the shared responsibility model to be documented, reviewed, owned and implemented as five separate demands.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Service Agreements
artifacts.description: The repository of executed written agreements with providers, including the acknowledgment of the provider's responsibility for the data it holds or processes, the agreement metadata (effective date, renewal, owner), and the records of renewals, amendments and supersessions. HIPAA requires signed business associate agreements with an inventory of them; ADHICS requires right-to-audit clauses and service-specific security requirements in the agreements.

artifacts.name: Provider Due Diligence and Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The due diligence reports and technology risk assessments performed before and during each engagement, the third-party security assessments, the vendor risk assessment records, and the compliance verification records for the provider's own controls.

artifacts.name: Provider Performance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The service level agreements with their security requirements, the SLA monitoring reports, service delivery reports, performance monitoring records, and the continuous monitoring of external services showing the arrangement is overseen rather than only contracted.

artifacts.name: Provider Assurance Report Review
artifacts.description: The third-party service provider inventory, the assurance reports received from each, the review documentation with the assessment of complementary user entity controls, and the contract provisions covering audit rights and control requirements.

artifacts.name: Customer-Facing Responsibility Documentation
artifacts.description: For the organisation acting as the provider: the repository of executed customer agreements containing the written acknowledgment of responsibility, the standard contract clause embodying it, the procedure for supporting customer requests for the information they need to meet their own obligations, the request tracker with response timelines, and samples of the responsibility documentation provided to customers.

artifacts.name: Executive Accountability Records
artifacts.description: The executive management charter establishing responsibility for the protection programme, the executive sign-off records, and the records of strategy and compliance reporting to executive management. SBP Cloud requires a board resolution acknowledging ultimate accountability for cloud-hosted assets; SBP ETGRMF requires a board-approved policy confirming the institution retains ultimate responsibility for data security.

artifacts.name: Cloud Security Posture and Exit Evidence
artifacts.description: The cloud security policy covering acquisition, use, data location, encryption and exit, the provider risk assessment including data residency and certifications, the configuration baseline applied, posture management scan results with remediation status, the tenant admin access review, the documented exit strategy for each provider, and the cloud risk register.

artifacts.name: Cloud Migration Responsibility Records
artifacts.description: The RACI matrix for the migration covering requirement analysis, performance testing, acceptance testing and data transfer, the migration runbook with role-by-role task assignment, the signed pre-transfer agreement of roles and responsibilities, and the pre-go-live sign-off records confirming those roles were executed before cut-over.

artifacts.name: Regulatory Readiness Records for Outsourcing
artifacts.description: The consolidated dossier of outsourcing arrangements maintained for regulator submission on demand, the log of information requests received with response dates and contents, the internal audit certification to the board confirming legal and regulatory compliance of the arrangements, and the readiness note evidencing capability to shift workloads to a designated onshore alternative.

artifacts.name: Data Ownership Evidence
artifacts.description: The cloud service contracts specifying data ownership terms, the register of hosted data with ownership attestation, and the due diligence records on the provider's data security practices.

artifacts.name: AI Management System Responsibility Charter
artifacts.description: The charter or terms of reference assigning AI management system responsibilities and authorities including conformity assurance, the RACI matrix across its processes, the performance reporting templates to top management, and the communications confirming assigned roles to staff including formal appointment letters.

artifacts.name: AI Life-Cycle Responsibility Allocation
artifacts.description: The document allocating AI life-cycle responsibilities between the organisation, partners, suppliers, customers and third parties, the determination of controller or processor roles where personal information is processed, the documentation delivery records to interested parties, the responsibility boundary document between provider and customer, the customer requirements capture records, and the risk information pack identifying limits of valid use.

artifacts.name: AI Supplier Management Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for selecting AI suppliers of datasets, models, libraries or complete systems, the supplier register with what each supplies and its risk assessment, evidence that suppliers delivered adequate documentation, and the records requiring corrective action where supplied components do not align with the organisation's approach.

artifacts.name: Supply Chain Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of the supply chain with the records demonstrating it is maintained in the environment it covers, and the governance responsibility model documenting who owns each governance activity across it.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The analysis of entity size and risk exposure, the assessment of incident likelihood and severity, the justification for why the measures adopted are appropriate, and the proportionality documentation supporting that judgement.

artifacts.name: Residual Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The signed acceptance forms showing named risk owners have formally accepted the residual risks arising from the responsibility allocation, and the third-party information access type documentation and relationship management roles behind them.

TPM-05.4.notes: 98 asks across 14 frameworks. Two different RASCI questions arrive under one control: who inside the organisation owns each security activity (ISO 27001, ISO 42001), and how responsibility divides between the organisation and its providers (CSA CCM shared responsibility model, PCI DSS TPSP matrix, SBP Cloud). They are kept apart because the second is contractual and the first is not.

artifacts.name: Provider Certification Register
artifacts.description: The register tracking provider certifications with issue dates, expiry dates and scope of coverage, copies of each certification document obtained and validated, and the certification pack evidencing adherence to the relevant international standards.

artifacts.name: Provider Assurance Reports
artifacts.description: The provider's service organisation control, standards certification and other control audit reports obtained and reviewed, the bridge letters covering the gap between report period and reliance date, and the expert security or compliance reports from outsourcing providers.

artifacts.name: Assurance Report Review Records
artifacts.description: The documented review of the provider reports with conclusions on security and resilience assurance, the review documentation with the complementary user entity control assessment, and the tracker of findings identified in those reports with the organisation's response and remediation monitoring.

artifacts.name: Certification Scope and Methodology Review
artifacts.description: The documented review of the certification's scope, methodology and the assessor's qualifications and ability, the memo documenting why an onsite audit is not feasible, and the justification for relying on the third-party certification instead.

artifacts.name: Scope Expansion Rights and Requests
artifacts.description: The contractual clause granting the right to request expansion of the scope of certifications, assessments or audits, and the log of scope-expansion requests submitted with the provider's responses and outcomes.

artifacts.name: Provider Audit Programme
artifacts.description: The rolling biennial audit schedule for providers carrying material workloads, the documented scope confirming coverage of the infrastructure and software delivering the service, the comprehensive audit report whether self, third-party or pooled, and the assessor engagement letter or pooled-audit agreement specifying independence, scope and deliverables.

artifacts.name: Contractual Audit Rights
artifacts.description: The clauses granting audit, access and information rights to the organisation, its regulator and its external auditors over the provider and its subcontractors, the contract clause checklist, sample contracts containing the required clauses, and the contract provisions covering audit rights and control requirements.

artifacts.name: Provider Controls Assessment
artifacts.description: The assessment of the provider's physical security and internal controls against the intended workload's confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience requirements; the data security controls assessment covering encryption, key management, loss prevention and classification; the corporate governance review covering board composition and entity-level controls; and the contingency, recovery and exit support review.

artifacts.name: Data Residency Capability Evidence
artifacts.description: The assessment of the provider's ability to give the organisation control over data residency including shifting between preferred locations, and the portal configuration screenshots showing residency controls and region restrictions in force.

artifacts.name: Independent Data Centre Assessment
artifacts.description: The independent threat and vulnerability assessment covering the provider data centres holding material workloads, the scope confirmation covering physical and environmental security, perimeter and access controls, the coverage list of every data centre in scope, the country risk report for each location, the findings remediation tracker, and the internal audit and information security review of the results.

artifacts.name: Subcontracting Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The assessment of the provider's subcontracting practices including the subcontractor inventory and risk mitigation, and the support services agreement covering response times, escalation tiers and availability.

artifacts.name: Vendor Assessment and Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: The pre-contract due diligence covering the required security domains, the annual vendor audit reports, the vendor self-assessment questionnaires, the periodic vendor security reviews, the vendor risk assessment records, the third-party service provider inventory, and the ongoing performance monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Compliance Register
artifacts.description: The register tracking third-party compliance status, the records verifying third-party legal authorisations and controls, and the supplier assessments and audits evaluating their security compliance posture.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Safeguards
artifacts.description: The documented selection of the appropriate safeguard for each exempt transfer, the executed standard contractual clauses in the form issued by the competent authority, the approved binding common rules applicable across the group, the certificate of accreditation, and the register mapping each transfer to its safeguard with status and validity dates.

artifacts.name: Recipient Approval Evidence
artifacts.description: The approval certificate held by the recipient issued by a body licensed by the competent authority, the record confirming the data is not sensitive where the approval-certificate route is relied on, and the assessment evidencing the transfer provides a service or benefit directly to the data subject.

artifacts.name: Intra-Group Transfer Evidence
artifacts.description: The intra-group data transfer agreement, the memo evidencing the controller is part of a multinational group and the transfer is necessary for its central operations, and the recipient's certificate of approval where required.

artifacts.name: Limited Transfer Justification
artifacts.description: The documentation evidencing that a transfer is non-recurring or for a limited period and involves a limited number of data subjects, where that exemption is relied on rather than a standing safeguard.

artifacts.name: Certification Scheme Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The assessment of applicable certification requirements, the inventory of certified products and services in use, the certification validity monitoring records, and the scheme compliance records.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Monitoring and Review Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy and procedure for monitoring and reviewing third-party services, the audit plan and reports with scope, findings and remediation tracking, the audit logging configuration evidence, the log review records with follow-up documentation, and the third-party agreements with security clauses and right-to-audit.

TPM-05.8.notes: 79 asks across 8 frameworks. Two different attestation regimes converge: assurance reports relied on in place of the organisation's own audit (SBP Cloud, SOX, QCB), and the cross-border transfer safeguards that must themselves be attested (KSA PDP). They are kept apart because the second is a legal instrument, not an assurance report.

artifacts.name: Provider Personnel Screening
artifacts.description: The background verification records for provider personnel per role sensitivity, the third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit, the third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records, and the data classification scheme determining which provider roles require screening. HITRUST requires the approved screening policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Provider Personnel Training
artifacts.description: The role-based training matrix and the training attendance records covering the personnel a provider assigns to the engagement.

artifacts.name: Supplier Off-Boarding Records
artifacts.description: The procedure for secure off-boarding covering data return or destruction, access revocation and exit audit, and the records evidencing completed off-boarding steps for exited suppliers.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register and Assessment
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating; the supplier information security policy setting expectations for all supplier categories; the supplier risk assessment procedure for onboarding due diligence based on tier and data access; the completed due diligence questionnaires from critical suppliers; the certifications collected from key suppliers; the vendor risk assessment and due diligence records; and the vendor selection criteria and evaluation documentation.

artifacts.name: Outsourced Development Personnel Controls
artifacts.description: The contracts with development suppliers including security, intellectual property and testing obligations; the intellectual property and confidentiality clauses; the assessment of the supplier's development lifecycle maturity and security practices; the security test results from vendor deliverables; the evidence of organisation-side code review of vendor-delivered code; the periodic quality and security reports from development vendors; and the source code escrow arrangement for critical outsourced software.

artifacts.name: Provider Performance Records
artifacts.description: The vendor contracts and service level agreements and the vendor performance monitoring reports and scorecards covering the personnel dimension of delivery.

artifacts.name: Security Role Appointments
artifacts.description: The letters or electronic appointments formally assigning security roles, the job descriptions explicitly listing security duties, the organisation chart showing reporting lines for the security function and its independence from technology operations, the responsibility matrix mapping security activities to roles, and the signed acceptance forms showing named risk owners have formally accepted residual risks.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance policy documentation.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

TPM-06.notes: 39 asks across 7 frameworks. Screening of provider personnel, their training and their off-boarding are three proofs; the security-role appointment asks arrive through an adjacent ISO crosswalk and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Monitoring & Review Procedure
artifacts.description: The documented process for ongoing oversight of external service providers: which providers are reviewed, at what depth and frequency by criticality tier, what is examined (security control compliance, service delivery, risk changes, subcontracting), who performs and who approves the review, and how findings are escalated. Must include the supplier evaluation criteria applied at review and the oversight framework or charter where a governance body owns the activity. Frequencies differ by framework — quarterly compliance review in PCI DSS for service providers, annual vendor audit in several banking frameworks, and at least annual or on significant change elsewhere.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Register with Review Status
artifacts.description: The provider inventory used to drive and evidence the review cycle: provider, service, criticality or materiality, contract reference, last review date, next review due, assurance report currency, open findings and current risk rating. Must be complete enough to show that no in-scope provider went unreviewed in the period, and to support concentration analysis where required.

artifacts.name: Periodic Supplier Review Reports & Scorecards
artifacts.description: The output of each completed review: supplier performance review reports, supplier scorecards and KPI dashboards, periodic security reviews, service review records and the meeting minutes where results were discussed with the provider. Must state the period covered, what was assessed, the conclusion on whether contracted security and service obligations are being met, and any actions agreed with the provider.

artifacts.name: SLA Compliance Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: Continuous monitoring evidence between formal reviews: SLA compliance and service-level performance reports, service delivery reports, SLA compliance dashboards, breach registers with the remedies applied, contractual obligation trackers and service-quality monitoring. Must be tied to the service levels actually agreed in contract, including quantitative targets for critical or material services, and show that breaches are recorded and pursued rather than merely observed.

artifacts.name: Provider Assurance Reports & Review Notes
artifacts.description: Independent assurance received from providers and the organization's assessment of it: SOC and ISO audit reports, ISAE 3402 or equivalent, PCI DSS Attestations of Compliance, certifications, and periodic compliance or security reports supplied under contract. The organization's own review record is as important as the report — scope and methodology assessment, reliance justification, treatment of carve-outs and complementary user entity controls, and findings extracted into a tracker. Reports must be current for the period under review.

artifacts.name: Right-to-Audit Exercise Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that contractual audit rights are exercised, not merely held: the audit plan and rolling schedule, scope documents, engagement letters where an external assessor is used, records of audits and inspections performed on the provider, access and inspection procedures, and the regulator's exercise of its own access rights where applicable. Some banking frameworks specify cadence explicitly — for example a biennial audit for material workloads with a two-year rolling schedule; others require it risk-based.

artifacts.name: Provider Security Assessments & Questionnaire Responses
artifacts.description: Assessment evidence the organization gathers directly: security questionnaires and provider control self-assessments, supplier security audit reports commissioned by the organization, vulnerability assessment and penetration test reports for the provider's environment (including sub-contractor testing results where obtained), security posture reports, and comparison of the provider's policies against the organization's own requirements. Must be current and cover the services actually consumed.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk Register & Ongoing Risk Assessments
artifacts.description: The risk view maintained across the relationship life cycle: the outsourcing or supply chain risk register, periodic re-assessments of provider risk, emerging-risk records, concentration risk analysis, country risk assessment for offshore providers, supply chain data security assessments and — where AI or personal data is involved — third-party AI, data and impact assessments. Must record mitigation strategies and formal residual risk acceptance with the accepting authority named. NIS2 additionally expects the proportionality of measures to be justified.

artifacts.name: Findings, Escalation & Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: What happened to everything the reviews surfaced: the findings tracker per provider, non-compliance escalation records, remediation plans with owners and due dates, overdue-finding escalation, follow-up correspondence with the provider, and performance improvement actions. Must show closure or a current, accepted status for each item rather than an open list carried forward indefinitely.

artifacts.name: Oversight Governance Minutes & Management Reporting
artifacts.description: Evidence that review results reach decision-makers: oversight committee or IT steering committee minutes covering provider performance, management sign-off on periodic review conclusions, evidence of reviewer independence where required, board or audit committee reporting, outsourcing management information packs, and consolidated outsourcing reports submitted to a regulator where mandated.

artifacts.name: Subcontractor & Fourth-Party Oversight Records
artifacts.description: Oversight extended beyond the direct provider: the subcontracting permission procedure and approval records, evidence that security obligations and audit rights flow down to subcontractors, subcontractor compliance attestations and assessments, review of material subcontracting agreements, and assessment of the primary provider's own capability to oversee its subcontractors.

artifacts.name: Provider Incident & Change Notification Records
artifacts.description: Records of events the provider was contractually required to report and how the organization responded: security incidents involving or reported by the provider, the provider's incident history, change notifications and evidence of the provider's adherence to agreed change management, provider change logs, and deviation reports made to authorities where a regulator must be told.

artifacts.name: Provider Access Monitoring Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that access granted to providers is controlled and watched during the relationship: the request-based access procedure, provider access request and approval records, access monitoring configuration, provider session and access logs, periodic access audit reports for provider accounts, and controls preventing unauthorized storage or removal of data by provider staff.

TPM-08.notes: 229 entries collapse to 13. The dominant duplication is 'get the provider's audit/assurance report' and 'monitor the provider against the SLA', each restated per regulator and per provider type (CSP, network service, outsourcing, processor). Contract-side items that appear here (clauses, NDAs, signed agreements) belong to TPM-05 and are folded into the smallest possible footprint — this control's evidence is the review activity, its output and what happened to the findings. No collectors are mapped, so everything is manual except provider access logs, which a connector could produce.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Finding Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker of audit findings on the provider with target dates, owner, remediation status and closure evidence; the issue tracking records for supply chain elements; the log of escalations and remediation actions for supply chain risks; the control deficiency tracking and remediation log; and the corrective action plans with timelines and status.

artifacts.name: Remediation Follow-Up Records
artifacts.description: The correspondence with the provider regarding finding remediation and status updates, the compliance verification records, the service review records, and the performance monitoring reports evidencing the deficiency was pursued rather than logged.

artifacts.name: Overdue Finding Escalation
artifacts.description: The records of escalations of overdue provider findings to the governing committee or management, the management reporting on control exceptions, and the board reporting on significant control deficiencies.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Audit Reports
artifacts.description: The third party audit reports, the supply chain assessment and audit reports, the audit plan and reports with scope, findings and remediation tracking, the third party monitoring reports and assessments, and the certifications collected from key suppliers.

artifacts.name: Provider Oversight Framework
artifacts.description: The documented framework for ongoing provider oversight covering performance, viability, cyber practices and location or sub-contracting changes; the oversight dashboard tracking service level performance, viability indicators, security metrics and change-event alerts; the minutes of periodic oversight reviews with decisions and actions; the register of emerging risks with response actions, owners and timelines; the log of notified provider changes with the organisation's response; and the records of continuous supply chain risk monitoring at defined intervals or on change.

artifacts.name: Provider Vulnerability Management
artifacts.description: The vulnerability management procedure for the cloud estate defining risk categorisation, rectification service levels, tracking and post-validation; the tracker showing categorisation, owner, rectification status and post-validation evidence; the scanner configuration and scan outputs; the reports evidencing closure of vulnerabilities after remediation through re-testing; and the document describing alternate assurance mechanisms where direct scanning is not permitted.

artifacts.name: Regulator Information Response
artifacts.description: The service level clause obligating the provider to timely provide any information requested by the regulator and the log of regulator information requests with the provider and organisation responses and their timeliness metrics.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register and Assessment Procedure
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating; the supplier information security policy setting security expectations for all supplier categories; the supplier risk assessment procedure for onboarding due diligence based on tier and data access; the completed due diligence questionnaires from critical suppliers; the vendor risk assessment and due diligence records; and the vendor selection criteria and evaluation documentation.

artifacts.name: Supplier Agreements and Service Levels
artifacts.description: The third-party agreements with security clauses, service levels and right-to-audit; the service level agreements with security requirements; the vendor contracts and service level agreements; and the vendor performance monitoring reports and scorecards. HITRUST requires the approved policy and standard on monitoring and review of third-party services with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Activity Logging
artifacts.description: The audit logging configuration evidence covering third-party activity and the log review records with their follow-up case documentation.

artifacts.name: Business Disruption Risk Records
artifacts.description: The business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans for the risks identified, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance policy documentation.

artifacts.name: Standards Alignment and Proportionality
artifacts.description: The standards mapping and alignment documentation, the gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards compliance assessment reports, the certification scheme participation records, the entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

TPM-09.notes: 57 asks across 10 frameworks. Distinct from TPM-02 in that the object is what happens after a deficiency is found in a supplier; the escalation of overdue provider findings is kept separate because the organisation cannot remediate directly and escalation is the only lever it holds.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Change Management Process
artifacts.description: The third party change management process, the change parameter documentation in agreements, the evidence of adherence to that change management process, the change management procedure with advisory board approvals and back-out plans, and the change records with their risk classification. HITRUST requires the approved policy and standard on managing changes to third-party services with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Jointly Agreed Change Procedure
artifacts.description: The change management procedure jointly agreed and signed by the organisation and the provider covering change request, approval and prioritisation; the provider-supplied documentation of its own change management controls as reviewed; the change request and approval workflow documentation with screenshots; and the documented timeframes for patching and software releases by criticality.

artifacts.name: Provider Change Notifications
artifacts.description: The advance change notification records received from the provider and acknowledged, the log of notified changes in ownership, service locations and sub-contracting with the organisation's response, the change communication records with third parties, and the notifications of material changes to supplier services with their impact assessments.

artifacts.name: Change Reassessment Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining supplier-change triggers requiring risk reassessment, the records of supply chain risk reassessments following significant supplier changes, the change management risk assessment process, and the management of change procedures for significant organisational changes.

artifacts.name: Unauthorised Change Detection
artifacts.description: The configuration of cloud change-detection tooling, the automated alerting rules for unauthorised configuration changes, and the sample unauthorised-change alerts with their triage and remediation records.

artifacts.name: Provider Oversight Framework
artifacts.description: The documented framework for ongoing provider oversight covering performance, viability, cyber practices and location or sub-contracting changes; the oversight dashboard tracking service level performance, viability indicators, security metrics and change-event alerts; the minutes of periodic oversight reviews with decisions and actions; the register of emerging risks with response actions, owners and timelines; and the service-quality monitoring records.

artifacts.name: Supplier Agreements and Clauses
artifacts.description: The executed supplier contracts showing information security and incident reporting clauses, the library of standard security clauses and processing agreement templates, the extracts showing right-to-audit and sub-processor approval rights, the signed non-disclosure agreements with suppliers holding confidential information, the tracker showing which suppliers have updated contracts with current security clauses, and the vendor contracts and service level agreements behind them. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented supply chain agreement review requirement.

artifacts.name: Supplier Performance Management
artifacts.description: The periodic supplier review reports covering service levels, security indicators and incidents; the supplier scorecard rating suppliers across security, performance and compliance; the service level attainment dashboard; the minutes of regular governance and service review meetings; the on-site or remote supplier audit reports with management responses; the vendor performance monitoring reports and scorecards; and the vendor risk assessment and due diligence records.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk Assessment Records
artifacts.description: The third-party risk assessment and ongoing monitoring records, the vendor selection criteria and evaluation documentation, the vendor security assessment results, the acquisition documentation, and the security requirements written into contracts.

artifacts.name: Service Decommissioning Records
artifacts.description: The decommissioning procedures, the decommissioning checklist, and the data retrieval and destruction confirmation closing out a terminated provider relationship.

artifacts.name: Business Change Impact Records
artifacts.description: The business model change impact assessments, the environmental scanning and threat intelligence reports informing them, the business disruption risk assessment with its mitigation plans, the risk treatment plans, the continuity and disaster recovery plans, and the cyber insurance policy documentation.

artifacts.name: Proportionality Assessment
artifacts.description: The entity size and risk exposure analysis, the incident likelihood and severity assessment, the proportionality assessment documentation, and the justification for the appropriateness of the measures selected.

TPM-10.notes: 61 asks across 12 frameworks. The provider's own change process, the notifications it must send, and the organisation's reassessment on receiving one are three separate proofs. SBP Cloud contributes a jointly-signed change procedure that is a distinct instrument from a supplier contract.

artifacts.name: Provider Disaster Recovery Plan
artifacts.description: The provider's disaster recovery plan covering scope, recovery objectives, recovery teams and procedures for the services in use, with the inventory of their recovery sites by type, capacity, location and activation procedure, and the contingency framework behind it.

artifacts.name: Recovery Objective Alignment Evidence
artifacts.description: The memo or matrix demonstrating the provider's recovery time and recovery point objectives align with the organisation's own business requirements, with the side-by-side comparison and the defined and measured objectives behind it. A provider plan that recovers slower than the business requires is a gap even when the provider meets its own targets.

artifacts.name: Provider Recovery Test Reports
artifacts.description: The periodic recovery test reports from the provider with results, gaps and corrective actions, the test records, and the supplier service level test reports.

artifacts.name: Joint Testing and Participation Records
