artifacts.description: The annual schedule for continuity drills conducted with third parties, the records of the organisation's participation in the provider's tests including offshore systems, the joint walkthrough or table-top exercise records, the collaborative test evidence, the third-party participation sign-offs, the observer sign-offs, and the drill results with lessons learned.

artifacts.name: Contingency Test Programme Records
artifacts.description: The library of contingency test scenarios with coverage mapped against threats, the annual contingency test report, the sign-off records by responsible heads confirming completion and acceptance, and the deficiency register with corrective action status and closure evidence.

artifacts.name: Provider Disruption Continuity Plan
artifacts.description: The continuity plan specifically addressing provider service disruption, the business resumption plans for that scenario, the fallback plans to an alternate provider or on-premise environment, and the testing records for those scenarios.

artifacts.name: Joint Incident Response Procedure
artifacts.description: The joint incident response mechanism agreed with suppliers, and the contractual incident detection, notification and coordination requirements with their timelines, establishing who does what and by when before an incident occurs.

artifacts.name: Incident Response Records
artifacts.description: The incident response plan and handling procedures, the classification and prioritisation criteria, the incident tracking system records, the investigation and analysis reports, the incident records related to third parties, and the post-incident review with lessons learned.

artifacts.name: Critical Control Failure Detection and Response
artifacts.description: The alert configuration covering failure of every critical security control system, the health-check or heartbeat configuration, sample failure alerts with triage, the documented response procedure covering restoration, cause and duration documentation and root-cause remediation, sample response records for past failures, mean-time-to-restore metrics and lessons-learned records.

artifacts.name: Third-Party Risk and Performance Monitoring
artifacts.description: The third-party risk assessments, compliance monitoring records, service performance reports and audit reports, evidencing the provider's capability is overseen continuously rather than only at onboarding.

artifacts.name: Supplier Register and Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The register of suppliers with tier, data accessed, last assessment date and risk rating; the supplier information security policy; the risk assessment procedure for onboarding due diligence; the security questionnaire responses; and the certifications collected from key suppliers.

artifacts.name: Supplier Continuity Assurance Evidence
artifacts.description: The documented and tested continuity and recovery plans held by suppliers of critical services, with the reports from their testing.

artifacts.name: Risk Mitigation and Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The documented risk-specific mitigation strategies covering diversification, contingency, contractual controls and audit, with the residual risk acceptance records showing risks reduced to acceptable levels and signed off.

artifacts.name: Cross-Border Transfer Controls
artifacts.description: The cross-border data transfer inventory and mapping, the standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules relied on, the transfer impact assessments, and the monitoring and compliance reports over those transfers.

artifacts.name: Legal Disclosure Request Records
artifacts.description: The procedures for evaluating legal and government disclosure requests, the tracking register of requests received, the legal counsel review documentation, and the records of information actually disclosed in response.

artifacts.name: Provider Asset Lifecycle Documentation
artifacts.description: The provider-supplied documentation covering acquisition, deployment, maintenance, refresh and disposal of the assets delivering the service, establishing whether the estate behind the service is being kept current.

artifacts.name: Stakeholder Communication Material
artifacts.description: The stakeholder communication and awareness campaign material prepared for a provider disruption, and the vendor security clauses that underpin the obligations being communicated.

TPM-11.notes: 83 asks across 10 frameworks. Two demands sit here: the provider must have a tested recovery capability, and the organisation must be able to respond jointly with it. Joint testing and joint incident response are kept as their own artifacts because a provider's own test report does not evidence either.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering scanning cadence, service levels, prioritisation and exception handling; the vulnerability management process document; the defined and approved vulnerability and patch management lifecycle; the documented procedure covering identification using industry-recognised sources and risk ranking; the vulnerability handling and disclosure policy; and the process review records. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented threat and vulnerability management policy requirement; NIST 800-171 likewise for the flaw identification and correction requirement.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Scanning Reports
artifacts.description: The periodic scan reports covering internal and external assets, the vulnerability assessment reports, the scan schedule documentation, the network security assessment results, and the software composition analysis and third-party software vulnerability tracking records.

artifacts.name: Remediation Tracking and Service Levels
artifacts.description: The remediation service level definitions by severity, the tracker showing open vulnerabilities with owners, service levels and closure status, the remediation tracking records, the vulnerability remediation tracking, the metrics showing remediation performance against the service levels, and the tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Intelligence and Risk Ranking
artifacts.description: The inventory of intelligence sources subscribed to and the documented risk ranking methodology aligned with industry sources for newly discovered vulnerabilities, with the gap analysis documentation supporting the ranking decisions.

artifacts.name: Patch Management Policy and Records
artifacts.description: The approved policy specifying installation of critical and high-risk patches within one month of release and other patches on a defined cycle, the patch management policy and procedures, the patch management process, the records of patches deployed per system with success or failure and rollback, the sample deployment records for the last review period, the patch compliance report, the patch testing documentation, the patch source validation procedures, and the rollback and redeployment playbooks.

artifacts.name: Post-Remediation Verification
artifacts.description: The post-patch vulnerability scan results confirming patched vulnerabilities are no longer detected, and the component version inventory evidencing the deployed versions are those the patches produced.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated immediately, with the risk acceptance records naming the accepting authority and the compensating controls applied.

artifacts.name: Penetration and Resilience Testing
artifacts.description: The annual penetration test reports with findings and remediation evidence, the annual testing plan for critical systems with the critical system identification behind it, the scenario-based test results, the test execution records, and the testing coverage reports.

artifacts.name: Secure Development and Procurement Records
artifacts.description: The secure development lifecycle documentation and procedures, the secure procurement policy with security requirements written into tender documents, and the security testing results for systems before deployment.

artifacts.name: Malware Protection Evidence
artifacts.description: The anti-malware solution documentation, the definition update records, the scan reports, the malware incident records, and the malware protection deployment and update records.

artifacts.name: Security Monitoring Evidence
artifacts.description: The security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports, the security operations procedures and monitoring configurations, the evidence of continuous monitoring and incident response tooling with at least twelve months of secure log retention, and the access control lists with the user access review documentation.

artifacts.name: Hardening and Perimeter Configuration
artifacts.description: The hardening and configuration baselines with unused ports and services disabled, and the configuration evidence for perimeter firewalls, web application firewalls, intrusion detection, denial-of-service protection and data loss prevention with segmentation and demilitarised zone placement.

artifacts.name: Backup and Recovery Test Reports
artifacts.description: The encrypted, access-controlled backups with their periodic restoration testing and offsite or geographically separate storage, with the tested restoration reports and the implementation evidence showing the lifecycle operates in production.

VPM-01.notes: 65 asks across 13 frameworks. This is the programme-level control, so the policy, the scanning cadence and the remediation service levels sit here; the malware and monitoring artifacts that arrive through COBIT DSS05 and PISF 9.2 are kept separate rather than folded into vulnerability management.

artifacts.name: Scan Scope Definition
artifacts.description: The annual plan covering enterprise-wide, risk-based vulnerability identification across critical systems and infrastructure; the register confirming coverage of all critical information systems and supporting infrastructure; the scope definition documentation; the scan configuration and coverage reports; the scanner configuration with authenticated scan credentials and scope coverage; the documentation of qualified internal personnel or qualified third party performing the scans; and the scan schedule documentation.

artifacts.name: Internal Vulnerability Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The latest four quarters of internal vulnerability scan reports, the scan reports performed after significant changes to the environment, the rescan reports, the periodic scan reports covering internal and external assets, the assessment reports covering the full scope with severity scoring and asset-criticality mapping, and the vulnerability assessment reports.

artifacts.name: External Approved-Vendor Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The engagement records and contracts with the approved scanning vendor, the latest four quarters of vendor scan reports showing passing results, the attestation, and the vendor rescan reports performed after significant changes to the external environment.

artifacts.name: Software Component Inventory
artifacts.description: The software bill of materials inventory of bespoke and custom software with the incorporated third-party components and their versions, the procedure governing maintenance of that inventory upon every release, the software composition analysis tool reports showing component coverage, the component version inventory, and the third-party software vulnerability tracking records.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering scanning cadence, service levels, prioritisation and exception handling; the documented vulnerability management procedure covering identification using industry-recognised sources; the inventory of vulnerability intelligence sources subscribed to; the documented risk ranking methodology; and the patch management policy. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented vulnerability remediation schedule requirement.

artifacts.name: Remediation Tracking Records
artifacts.description: The tracker showing open vulnerabilities with owners, service levels and closure status; the tracker of findings through to closure with retest evidence; the remediation tracking records; the tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status; the metrics showing remediation performance against the service levels; the records of patches deployed per system with success or failure and rollback; the patch deployment records; the flaw remediation documentation; and the documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated immediately.

artifacts.name: Penetration Testing Records
artifacts.description: The annual penetration test reports with findings and remediation evidence, the developer security testing plan, and the testing results and reports.

artifacts.name: Management System Scope Statement
artifacts.description: The formal documented scope statement defining boundaries, locations, systems, organisational units and products; the diagram showing in-scope units, systems, sites and interfaces to out-of-scope areas; and the top-management approval record authorising that scope.

VPM-01.1.notes: 48 asks across 8 frameworks. The demand is scope — that scanning covers everything it should. Internal scans, external approved-vendor scans and the software bill of materials are three different coverage proofs and are kept apart.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Policy and Remediation Procedure
artifacts.description: The policy covering scanning cadence, remediation service levels by severity, risk-based prioritisation criteria and exception handling, with the remediation management procedure implementing it. SBP Cloud requires risk categorisation into critical, high, medium and low with rectification SLAs and post-validation defined; NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the document.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker showing each open finding with owner, severity, service level and closure status, the action plan behind it, and the finding closure tracker. ISO 27001 requires SLA compliance metrics by severity; CIS CSC requires remediation timeline compliance reporting; MAS TRM requires severity and timelines on the tracking reports.

artifacts.name: Validated Closure Evidence
artifacts.description: The retest or rescan reports confirming each remediated vulnerability is no longer present, the post-validation closure reports, and the rescan records after significant change. SBP ETGRMF and SBP Cloud require closure to be evidenced by validation rather than by the owner marking it complete.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated within the applicable window, with the compensating controls, the named owner accepting the exposure, and the missing patch exception documentation.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The internal and external scan reports with criticality classification and the scanner configuration with authenticated credentials and scope coverage. PCI DSS requires the latest four quarters internally plus quarterly approved-vendor external scans with the attestation and engagement records, performed by personnel whose qualifications are documented.

artifacts.name: Patch Deployment and Compliance Records
artifacts.description: The patch management policy with its SLA definitions, patch assessment and testing records, deployment records with success or failure, deployment reports showing compliance with the SLAs, and the component version inventory the patches are applied against.

artifacts.name: Application Security Testing Records
artifacts.description: The application security testing reports per lifecycle stage, the software composition analysis reports, the third-party software vulnerability tracking records, and the annual penetration test reports with findings and remediation evidence.

artifacts.name: Cloud Vulnerability Assurance Records
artifacts.description: The scanner configuration and outputs for cloud workloads, the tracker showing categorisation, owner, rectification status and post-validation evidence, and the document describing alternate assurance mechanisms where the provider manages the layer — assurance reports, disclosure programmes, attestations — because the customer cannot scan it directly.

artifacts.name: Control Deficiency Tracking and Reporting
artifacts.description: The control deficiency tracking and remediation log, corrective action plans with timelines and status, management reporting on control exceptions, and the board reporting on significant deficiencies.

artifacts.name: Nonconformity and Root Cause Records
artifacts.description: The procedure defining how nonconformities are handled including reaction, root-cause analysis and corrective action, the log of nonconformities with cause analysis and checks for similar occurrences, the root cause analyses for material nonconformities, and the records reviewing the effectiveness of the actions taken.

artifacts.name: Standards Gap Analysis Records
artifacts.description: The gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards mapping and alignment documentation, the compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

artifacts.name: Hardening and Control Implementation Records
artifacts.description: The hardening standards applied, the control implementation records, and the compliance verification reports confirming the hardened state is maintained.

artifacts.name: Network Component Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The network component risk assessment report and the vulnerability scan results feeding it, establishing which components warrant priority remediation.

artifacts.name: Business Process Control Records
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, information processing validation and integrity check records, error and exception handling logs with corrective action, and the segregation of duties matrix with access privilege records.

artifacts.name: Awareness and Periodic Review Records
artifacts.description: The awareness communications informing personnel of the technical vulnerability controls, and the periodic review records naming the reviewer.

VPM-02.notes: 93 asks across 20 frameworks — the widest crosswalk in the catalogue. Overlaps VPM-06 (scanning); what is distinct here is the remediation process itself: prioritisation criteria, SLAs, validated closure and risk acceptance, rather than the discovery that feeds it.

artifacts.name: Risk Ranking Methodology
artifacts.description: The documented risk ranking methodology aligned with industry sources for newly discovered vulnerabilities, the categorisation and prioritisation matrix for security patches, the procedure defining risk categorisation with rectification service levels, and the patch management policy with its service level definitions.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering scanning cadence, service levels, prioritisation and exception handling; the vulnerability management policy; the documented procedure covering identification using industry-recognised sources; the patch management policy and procedures covering identification, categorisation, prioritisation and testing; and the inventory of intelligence sources subscribed to. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented vulnerability remediation schedule and vulnerability management reporting requirements. HITRUST requires the approved control of technical vulnerabilities policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Ranked Vulnerability Reports
artifacts.description: The regular vulnerability assessment reports with criticality classification, the periodic scan reports covering internal and external assets, the vulnerability scanning reports with their remediation tracking and timing, the vulnerability scan reports, the scanner configuration and outputs, and the vulnerability assessment reports.

artifacts.name: Remediation Tracking Against Service Levels
artifacts.description: The tracker showing open vulnerabilities with owners, service levels and closure status; the tracker showing categorisation, owner, rectification status and post-validation evidence; the remediation tracking records; the tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status; the metrics showing remediation performance against the service levels by severity; and the patch deployment reports showing compliance with those service levels.

artifacts.name: Patch Deployment Records
artifacts.description: The records of patches deployed per system with success or failure and rollback; the patch management records with deployment evidence and exception register; the change records for patch deployments with their approval workflow; the patch management tool reports; the patching records; the patch deployment records; the component version inventory; and the patch assessment and testing records.

artifacts.name: Patch Testing Evidence
artifacts.description: The evidence of patch testing in a segregated environment before production deployment, evidencing the ranking did not push an untested fix into production.

artifacts.name: Post-Remediation Validation
artifacts.description: The reports evidencing closure of vulnerabilities after remediation through re-testing and the document describing alternate assurance mechanisms where direct re-testing is not permitted.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated immediately, the risk acceptance records, and the missing patch exception documentation.

artifacts.name: Penetration Test and Review Records
artifacts.description: The annual penetration test reports with findings and remediation evidence and the periodic review records naming the reviewer, with the awareness communications informing personnel of the technical vulnerability controls.

VPM-03.notes: 48 asks across 11 frameworks. Overlaps VPM-01; what is distinct here is the ranking that drives fix order — the categorisation matrix and the service levels attached to each band — rather than the discovery or the fix.

artifacts.name: Remediation Timeline Compliance
artifacts.description: The remediation timeline compliance reports, the remediation timeline compliance records, the remediation tracking records, the vulnerability remediation records, the remediation tracking, the control deficiency tracking and remediation log, and the corrective action plans with their timelines and status. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented remediate-vulnerabilities-by-risk requirement; CSA CCM likewise for the vulnerability prioritisation and vulnerability management metrics requirements.

artifacts.name: Patch Management Programme
artifacts.description: The approved policy specifying installation of critical and high-risk patches within the required window and other patches on a defined cycle; the documented programme including pre-deployment testing, monitoring and rollback strategy; the patch management policy; the patch deployment records; the sample deployment records for the last review period; the patch compliance report; the patching records; and the patch and update records.

artifacts.name: Pre-Deployment Testing and Rollback
artifacts.description: The records of vulnerability testing before patch deployment and the defined rollback strategy for failed patches.

artifacts.name: Post-Remediation Verification
artifacts.description: The post-patch vulnerability scan results confirming patched vulnerabilities are no longer detected, the retest verification results, the vulnerability scan reports, the vulnerability assessment reports, and the scan schedule documentation.

artifacts.name: Version and Firmware Inventory
artifacts.description: The network device firmware inventory, the version compliance reports, and the component version inventory establishing what is currently deployed.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The risk acceptance documentation for unresolved vulnerabilities and the risk acceptance records naming the accepting authority.

artifacts.name: Management Reporting Records
artifacts.description: The management reporting on control exceptions and the board reporting on significant control deficiencies arising from unremediated vulnerabilities.

artifacts.name: Standards Alignment Records
artifacts.description: The standards mapping and alignment documentation, the gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

artifacts.name: Processing Integrity Controls
artifacts.description: The business process control documentation and procedures, the information processing validation and integrity check records, the error and exception handling logs with corrective action documentation, and the segregation of duties matrix with its access privilege records.

VPM-04.notes: 45 asks across 10 frameworks. Overlaps VPM-01 and VPM-03; what is distinct here is continuity — that remediation runs as an ongoing activity with timeline compliance measured — so the timeline metrics and rollback strategy carry the weight.

artifacts.name: Patch Management Policy and SLAs
artifacts.description: The approved policy covering identification, categorisation, prioritisation, testing and deployment of patches, with the remediation service levels by severity. PCI DSS requires critical or high-risk patches within one month of release and a defined window for the rest; SOX requires SLA definitions in the policy and documented exceptions for missing patches; SBP ETGRMF requires a defined cadence for installing updated software versions.

artifacts.name: Patch Deployment Records
artifacts.description: Records of patches deployed per system with success or failure status, rollback where it occurred, and the deployment timeline against the applicable SLA. CIS CSC expects operating-system and application patching to be evidenced separately; ADHICS expects firmware update logs alongside software patches.

artifacts.name: Patch Compliance Report
artifacts.description: The report or dashboard showing patch compliance rate across the estate, broken down by asset class. QCB requires coverage across asset classes including databases, virtual machines, remote-access servers and multifunction devices; PISF 2026 requires endpoint patch compliance evidence; SOX requires the report to demonstrate compliance with the stated SLAs.

artifacts.name: Patch Testing and Approval Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that patches were tested before production deployment, in a segregated environment where required, with the change records and approval workflow covering the deployment and the risk assessment performed for upgrades.

artifacts.name: Patch Categorisation and Prioritisation Matrix
artifacts.description: The matrix classifying patches by criticality and the prioritisation rules that determine deployment order and deadline, with sample records showing patches classified under it.

artifacts.name: Software Version and End-of-Life Register
artifacts.description: The inventory of installed software with versions compared against vendor-supported versions, the register tracking end-of-life software with replacement or remediation plans, the network device firmware inventory, and the version compliance reports.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Scanning Reports
artifacts.description: Periodic internal and external vulnerability scan reports with criticality classification, the annual penetration test reports with findings, and the post-patch rescan results confirming remediated vulnerabilities are no longer detected.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker showing open vulnerabilities with owner, severity, SLA and closure status, the SLA compliance metrics by severity, remediation timeline compliance, retest verification results, and the documented risk acceptance for vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated within the window.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering scanning cadence, remediation service levels, prioritisation by risk and exception handling, with the remediation procedures implementing it.

artifacts.name: Anti-Malware Deployment and Update Records
artifacts.description: The anti-malware or endpoint detection solution documentation, the coverage report showing no unprotected endpoints, the definition update records, scan reports and the malware incident records arising from them.

artifacts.name: Change Control Records for Patching
artifacts.description: The approved change control procedure covering patch deployment, the change records with risk classification and back-out plans, the change advisory board approvals, and the awareness communications informing affected personnel.

artifacts.name: Hardening Standards and Sign-off
artifacts.description: The hardening standards applied to systems and gateways, the hardening checklist covering each required element, the pre-production hardening sign-off, and the control implementation and compliance verification records.

artifacts.name: IT Service Management Framework
artifacts.description: The documented ITSM framework covering preventive maintenance, incident and problem management and patch management with management approval, the detailed process documents for each component, the tool screenshots evidencing the processes in operation, and the KPI dashboard measuring performance across them.

artifacts.name: Data Platform Versioning Records
artifacts.description: The documented database and tool versioning specifications with their compliance evidence, the metadata repository or catalog export, the register evidencing each with a named owner, the data security control evidence and privacy artifacts, and the compliance audit reports covering them.

artifacts.name: Removable Media Control Configuration
artifacts.description: The policy and configuration governing secure use of external and removable media, kept as its own artifact because it addresses a different infection vector from the patching that surrounds it in the same requirement.

VPM-05.notes: 100 asks across 16 frameworks. Patching and vulnerability management are adjacent but tested separately by ISO 27001 and PISF 2026, so the scanning and remediation-SLA evidence is kept apart from the deployment records. Anti-malware definition updates are a distinct artifact despite arriving under the same control.

artifacts.name: Centralised Patch Management
artifacts.description: The patch management policy specifying installation of critical and high-risk patches within the required window, the patch management policy and procedures, the application patch management configuration, the application patch deployment reports, the patch deployment records, the sample deployment records for the last review period, the patch compliance report, the application patching compliance, and the patch testing documentation.

artifacts.name: Software Component Inventory
artifacts.description: The software bill of materials inventory of bespoke and custom software with the incorporated third-party components and their versions, the procedure governing maintenance of that inventory upon every release, the composition analysis tool reports showing component coverage, and the component version inventory.

artifacts.name: Centralised Remediation Tracking
artifacts.description: The vulnerability tracking system records showing identification source, severity, owner and status; the tracker of identified vulnerabilities with correction status and reassessment confirmation; the vulnerability remediation tracking; the documented vulnerability management procedure covering identification using industry-recognised sources; the documented risk ranking methodology; and the inventory of intelligence sources subscribed to.

artifacts.name: Post-Remediation Verification
artifacts.description: The post-patch vulnerability scan results confirming patched vulnerabilities are no longer detected and the vulnerability assessment reports covering the remediated estate.

artifacts.name: Public Web Application Protection
artifacts.description: The annual security assessment report covering each public-facing web application, the post-change reassessment records, the configuration export of the web application firewall or runtime protection deployed in front of those applications, the evidence it operates in blocking mode or that its alerts are promptly investigated, the rule-set currency records, and the sample audit logs showing detection and blocking.

artifacts.name: Payment Page Script Inventory
artifacts.description: The inventory of all scripts loaded and executed in the consumer's browser on payment pages with source and purpose, the records demonstrating each script is authorised with documented business or technical justification, the configuration evidence of integrity assurance for each script, and the records of periodic inventory and authorisation reviews.

artifacts.name: Standards Alignment Records
artifacts.description: The standards mapping and alignment documentation, the gap analysis against relevant international standards, the standards compliance assessment reports, and the certification scheme participation records.

VPM-05.1.notes: 38 asks across 5 frameworks. Overlaps VPM-01 and VPM-04; what is distinct here is centralised management — one patch platform, one component inventory, one tracker — and PCI DSS 6.4.3's payment page script inventory is a separate object entirely.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Management Policy
artifacts.description: The policy covering scanning cadence, remediation service levels by severity, prioritisation and exception handling, with the remediation procedures implementing it. NIST 800-171 accepts configuration evidence in place of the document; SBP ETGRMF requires an annual enterprise-wide, risk-based vulnerability identification plan.

artifacts.name: Scan Schedule and Scope Coverage
artifacts.description: The documented scan schedule with the register confirming coverage of all critical systems and supporting infrastructure, the external asset inventory in scope, and the scanning tool configuration including authenticated scan credentials. CIS CSC requires internal and external coverage to be evidenced separately; SBP ETGRMF requires credentialed-scan coverage evidence.

artifacts.name: Internal Vulnerability Scan Reports
artifacts.description: The periodic internal scan reports with criticality classification and the rescan reports confirming closure. PCI DSS requires the latest four quarters plus scans after every significant change, performed by qualified personnel whose credentials are documented; QCB requires semi-annual reports for infrastructure and bi-annual reports following a recognised testing methodology.

artifacts.name: External Scan and Attestation Records
artifacts.description: The external vulnerability scan reports with their engagement records. PCI DSS requires the latest four quarters of passing scans from an approved scanning vendor with the attestation, the engagement contract, and rescans after significant changes to the external environment.

artifacts.name: Penetration Test Reports
artifacts.description: The penetration test reports with findings, severity and remediation status. QCB requires semi-annual tests with online and core banking scenarios including man-in-the-middle and man-in-the-browser; SBP Cloud requires an independent tester engagement letter confirming scope and independence, a methodology document aligned to a recognised standard, and the provider's pre-authorisation for customer-initiated testing.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Remediation Tracker
artifacts.description: The tracker showing open findings with owner, severity, service level and closure status, the year-over-year remediation evidence, the action plan behind it, and the retest or validation reports confirming closure. ISO 27001 requires SLA compliance metrics by severity; ADHICS requires mitigation effectiveness verification separate from mitigation tracking.

artifacts.name: Risk Acceptance Records
artifacts.description: The documented acceptance of vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated within the applicable window, with the compensating controls and the named owner accepting the residual exposure.

artifacts.name: Web Application Security Assessment
artifacts.description: The annual security assessment covering each public-facing web application using manual or automated techniques, the reassessment records following changes to those applications, the vulnerability correction tracker with reassessment confirmation, and where the alternative path is taken, the configuration evidence for the web application firewall or runtime protection deployed in front of them.

artifacts.name: Scenario-Based and Resilience Testing
artifacts.description: The scenario-based, red-team or purple-team testing reports covering realistic attack chains, the critical system identification behind the test scope, the annual testing plan for those systems, the test execution records and the coverage reports.

artifacts.name: Network and Component Risk Assessment
artifacts.description: The network security assessment results, the network component risk assessment report, and the gap analysis documentation identifying where the assessed posture falls short of the target.

artifacts.name: Patch Deployment Records
artifacts.description: The records of patches deployed per system with success or failure and rollback, evidencing that the vulnerabilities the scans identified were actually closed rather than only tracked.

artifacts.name: Security Monitoring and Detection Configuration
artifacts.description: The security information and event management configuration, infrastructure monitoring tool configuration and alert rules, configuration monitoring and baseline comparison reports, malware protection deployment and update records, and the security event monitoring logs and incident detection reports.

artifacts.name: Code Review Reports
artifacts.description: The application code review reports covering the systems in scope, held separately from the scan reports because the technique and the reviewer are different.

artifacts.name: Regulator Reporting Records
artifacts.description: The assessment reports shared with the sector regulator and the annual security assessment schedule under which they are produced.

artifacts.name: Access Control Review Documentation
artifacts.description: The access control lists and user access review documentation and the security operations procedures, evidencing the identity controls over the systems being scanned.

VPM-06.notes: 100 asks across 19 frameworks — the widest crosswalk after CHG-01. Scan cadence is the main divergence and is stated inside the scanning artifacts: PCI DSS quarterly internal and quarterly approved-vendor external, QCB semi-annual and bi-annual by system class, DORA annual for critical systems, PISF 2026 and SBP ETGRMF risk-based.

artifacts.name: Penetration Testing Policy, Methodology & Scope
artifacts.description: The approved penetration testing policy and methodology: the industry-accepted approach used (OWASP, PTES, NIST SP 800-115), what is in scope (networks, applications, people and processes; the cardholder data environment perimeter and critical systems for PCI DSS; critical or important functions for DORA threat-led testing), testing from both inside and outside, the tests used to validate segmentation and scope reduction, coverage of application-layer and network-layer threats from the last 12 months, and the retention of results and remediation. Include the developer security testing plan where testing is performed in the SDLC, the cloud testing scope and methodology agreed with the tester, and the justification showing scope and frequency are commensurate with system complexity and risk.

artifacts.name: Penetration Testing Schedule & Frequency Plan
artifacts.description: The forward schedule and completion history proving the required cadence is met. Frequencies differ by framework: at least annually and after significant change (PCI DSS, MAS TRM for internet-facing systems); every six months for service-provider segmentation testing (PCI DSS) and semi-annual VA/PT under QCB; at least twice yearly under QCB 9.4.3.3; quarterly wireless testing under QCB; annual assessment schedule under ADHICS; and an annual security testing plan covering self-assessments, pen tests and independent audits under SBP. Must also include the trigger log linking major updates and deployments to the tests they caused, and the risk-classification basis for how often each system is tested.

artifacts.name: External Penetration Test Report
artifacts.description: The most recent external penetration test report covering the internet-facing perimeter and critical externally-facing systems, with scope, methodology, findings, severity ratings, evidence references and recommendations. Required at least annually and after significant infrastructure or application change (PCI DSS), semi-annually or bi-annually under QCB, and covering internet banking and healthcare systems under SBP and ADHICS respectively; PISF 2026 expects VA and penetration test reports with remediation tracking attached.

artifacts.name: Internal Penetration Test Report
artifacts.description: The most recent internal penetration test report covering the internal network and critical systems, at least annually and after significant change. Where testing is performed against production, include the documented safeguards applied and the formal approval obtained before testing, together with the results.

artifacts.name: Segmentation Penetration Test Report
artifacts.description: Test evidence confirming that segmentation controls isolate the in-scope environment from out-of-scope networks: the inventory of segmentation and isolation mechanisms tested, the test results confirming isolation holds, and coverage evidence showing every mechanism was exercised. PCI DSS requires this at least every 12 months and after any change to segmentation controls, and at least every six months for service providers.

artifacts.name: Application & API Security Test Report
artifacts.description: Application-layer testing evidence: abuse-case, malformed and unexpected-input (fuzz) testing, attack surface analysis and vulnerability chaining; web application security assessment reports; API testing against the OWASP API Top 10 for all exposed APIs with tool output and fix verification; secure code review reports; and the security-testing approval recorded at the pre-deployment gate. QCB additionally requires online and core banking application testing covering man-in-the-middle and man-in-the-browser scenarios.

artifacts.name: Threat-Led / Scenario-Based Testing Evidence
artifacts.description: Red-team, purple-team and threat-intelligence-led testing that goes beyond routine pen testing: the threat scenarios used, the test case library for environment-specific attack chains (for cloud: hypervisor escape, insecure APIs, hyperjacking, wrapping attacks, malware injection, side-channel), execution reports with results and residual risk, and the mapping of each threat scenario to the controls and test coverage that address it. DORA requires testing on live production systems covering critical functions, with third-party providers included in scope.

artifacts.name: Vulnerability Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The automated scanning output that sits alongside manual testing: periodic vulnerability assessment reports (semi-annual or bi-annual under QCB, per the assessment schedule under ADHICS), wireless/rogue access point scan results, and the records demonstrating vulnerability identification is operating in the cloud environment.

artifacts.name: Findings Remediation Tracker & Retest Evidence
artifacts.description: The tracker carrying every finding from all of the above through to closure: finding, risk ranking, owner, target date driven by severity, and current status; the documented risk-based remediation plan; and the retest, rescan or post-validation records proving exploitable vulnerabilities and weaknesses were actually corrected. Include the flaw remediation documentation from development testing and the risk management procedures governing risks raised during threat-led testing, plus verification that the mitigation was effective.

artifacts.name: Tester Qualification & Independence Records
artifacts.description: Evidence that whoever performed the testing was competent and independent: certifications and qualifications (OSCP, CREST, CEH or equivalent), organisational independence from the teams that built or run the systems tested, the engagement letter or contract defining scope, independence and deliverables, and — under DORA — the tester rotation records and evidence of third-party participation in the test.

artifacts.name: Third-Party & Cloud Provider Testing Rights and Authorisations
artifacts.description: The contractual and coordination evidence for testing that crosses organisational boundaries: right-to-test clauses in cloud and outsourcing contracts (including the contractual right to third-level audit and pen test), the provider's pre-authorisation or notification records for customer-initiated testing, the reports received from provider-side testing, evidence that third-party service providers were included in the test scope, and — for multi-tenant service providers — the documented procedure and sample records for supporting customers' own external penetration testing, with the communication templates used.

artifacts.name: Methodology & Programme Review Records
artifacts.description: Dated records showing the testing methodology and the overall testing programme are reviewed and updated periodically, with what changed and who approved it.

artifacts.name: Independent Audit & Self-Assessment Reports
artifacts.description: The independent security audit report and the internal self-assessment reports covering the same systems, showing control coverage, plus the copies of assessment results submitted to the regulator where that is required (reports shared with DOH under ADHICS).

artifacts.name: System Integrity & Secure Configuration Verification Evidence
artifacts.description: Verification that the tested systems are running the software and settings they are supposed to: software integrity verification with hash or signature checks, file integrity monitoring output, the change control records for the verified components, and the secure configuration evidence exercised by the tests — TLS configuration for data in transit and the authentication and session management settings.

VPM-07.notes: 104 framework evidence asks collapse to 14 artifacts. No automated collectors are attached to this control; test reports and trackers are human deliverables, so only the configuration-verification artifact is marked hybrid. Frequency requirements differ sharply between frameworks and are called out in the descriptions.

artifacts.name: Client-Facing Service Inventory
artifacts.description: The electronic commerce service inventory, the service provider and partner details, the online services risk and control documentation, and the partner service agreements governing them. HITRUST requires the approved electronic commerce services policy and standard with its implementing procedure.

artifacts.name: Web Application Security Controls
artifacts.description: The web application security controls documentation, the electronic commerce security measures documentation, the communication channel encryption configuration, the digital signature implementation records, and the online transaction procedures.

artifacts.name: Web Application Security Testing
artifacts.description: The web application security testing reports and the online services security assessment.

artifacts.name: Customer Authentication Controls
artifacts.description: The online multi-factor implementation documentation, the login flow verification records, the adaptive authentication system documentation, the risk-based authentication rules and thresholds, and the authentication controls applied to the channel.

artifacts.name: Transaction Signing Controls
artifacts.description: The high-risk transaction classification criteria, the transaction signing implementation documentation, the segregation of duties matrix, and the transaction logging records.

artifacts.name: Credential Protection Records
artifacts.description: The credential storage security standards and the credential protection implementation assessment.

artifacts.name: Mobile Channel Controls
artifacts.description: The mobile application risk assessment, the mobile-specific security controls documentation, the mobile application data protection controls covering encryption and secure storage, and the mobile banking security controls inventory.

artifacts.name: Public System Data Controls
artifacts.description: The documented requirement or configuration evidence controlling regulated data on publicly accessible systems, with the records demonstrating it is implemented and operating.

artifacts.name: Network and Access Records
artifacts.description: The network architecture diagram showing segmentation, firewalls and trust zones; the network device configuration baselines with their ruleset review records; the access control matrix with role-to-permission mapping; and the user access provisioning, modification and review records covering the client-facing estate.

WEB-04.notes: 34 asks across 6 frameworks. The service inventory, the security controls applied to each and the testing that verifies them are three proofs; the mobile channel is kept separate because its threat surface differs from the browser channel.

artifacts.name: Customer Authentication Policy
artifacts.description: The approved authentication policy for customers covering enrolment, second-factor authentication, layered security, account lockout and session handling; the approved policy mandating two-factor authentication for all customer logins and transaction approvals; the documented architecture of customer authentication including the identity provider, authentication broker and risk-based engine; the authentication controls; and the matrix listing each authentication control with implementation status, owner and last review date. CSA CCM accepts configuration evidence in place of the documented identity and access management policy, strong authentication and uniquely identifiable users requirements.

artifacts.name: Second Factor Enforcement Evidence
artifacts.description: The configuration export from the authentication solution showing enforced second-factor authentication on the customer-facing application, the audit or report confirming every customer authentication path requires it with no bypass routes, the inventory of approved second-factor methods, the screenshots of login and transaction-approval flows demonstrating the prompts, the two-factor implementation, the login flow verification records, and the online multi-factor implementation documentation.

artifacts.name: Transaction Authorisation Controls
artifacts.description: The transaction-signing second-factor evidence, the separate transaction password configuration, the transaction value caps, the multi-channel payee registration workflow, the alerting on transactions, the token-based authorisation for corporate banking, the risk assessment for institutional and corporate channels, the online transaction procedures, the segregation of duties matrix, and the transaction logging records.

artifacts.name: Layered Security for High-Value Transactions
artifacts.description: The approved policy defining high-value transaction thresholds and the additional layered security required; the configuration of the layered controls applied to them; the rule set in the risk-based authentication engine triggering step-up for high-value or anomalous transactions; the walkthrough screenshots of a high-value transaction demonstrating activation of the additional layers; and the report showing effectiveness of the layered programmes including false positives, blocked fraudulent attempts and customer friction.

artifacts.name: One-Time Passcode Controls
artifacts.description: The one-time passcode security assessment documentation, the validity period configuration, and the passcode-based second-factor implementation for card-not-present transactions.

artifacts.name: Biometric Authentication Controls
artifacts.description: The biometric solution performance assessment, the false-accept and false-reject calibration records, the biometric data encryption configuration, and the biometric data storage security assessment.

artifacts.name: Device Binding and Token Provisioning
artifacts.description: The device binding implementation records and the soft token provisioning procedures governing how a factor is bound to a customer's device.

artifacts.name: Session Management Controls
artifacts.description: The session management configuration documentation and the session timeout and hijack detection settings protecting an authenticated session.

artifacts.name: Card Authentication Controls
artifacts.description: The card authentication protocol implementation and the cardholder enrolment and communication evidence supporting it.

artifacts.name: Mobile Channel Controls
artifacts.description: The mobile banking security controls inventory covering the authentication surface exposed on that channel.

artifacts.name: Customer Credential Guidance
artifacts.description: The guidance issued to customer users covering periodic change of credentials and how to recognise when credentials may be compromised, with the evidence of its distribution through portal publication or onboarding communications.

WEB-06.notes: 49 asks across 6 frameworks. Second-factor enforcement, step-up on high-value transactions and the specific factor technologies are three proofs; the factor-technology artifacts stay separate because each carries its own assurance requirements.
